title: 63-101 Household Concept
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Household Concept 63-101 1 of 8 Revision Date: 04/01/2023 Background: Household (HH) composition is used to determine which individuals will be included in the CalFresh HH. Purpose: This section details the effects HH composition has on determining eligibility. The section is being revised to include the CalFresh definitions of elderly and disabled along with clarification of the 165% elderly and disabled (E/D) separate HH determination rule. The section has been reformatted and is being updated due to sunset review. Policy: A CalFresh HH is an individual or group of individuals who live together and customarily purchase and prepare (P&P) meals together. A HH is determined by the relationship that exists among its members. Restricted relationships take priority when determining HH composition. The customer is responsible for providing complete and correct information to determine HH composition. Do not deny an application when an applicant applies separately but lives with others who must be included in the HH with the applicant. Continue processing the application and: •Inform the applicant that the other persons living with him/her must be included in the HH, and •Request information and verification of the other people in the home and continue processing the application for the entire HH following regulations as explained in 63-109. If the applicant fails to provide the information and verification on other HH members needed to determine eligibility, deny the application for failure to provide information. Note: An unaccompanied minor experiencing homelessness, who is not in the physical custody of a parent or guardian, is not living with an adult who has parental control over them, or in foster care may apply as their own HH even if there is no adult in the case. 1. Definitions: The following are definitions for terms that will be used throughout the section: Term Definition Elderly A HH member who is 60 years of age or older. Disabled A HH member who receives or meets any of the following: •Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits under Title XVI, or disability or blindness payments under Title II (Social Security Disability Insurance Program) of the Social Security Act. •Disability retirement benefits from a governmental agency because of a disability considered permanent under Section 221(i) of the Social Security Act. •Interim assistance benefits pending receipt of SSI, provided that the eligibility to receive those benefits is based upon disability or blindness criteria which County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Household Concept 63-101 2 of 8 are at least as stringent as those used under Title XVI of the Social Security Act. •Disability-related medical assistance under Title XIX (Medi-Cal) of the Social Security Act. •Disability-based general assistance benefits, provided that the eligibility to receive those benefits is based upon disability or blindness criteria which are at least as stringent as those used under Title XVI of the Social Security Act. •An annuity payment under Section 2(a)(1)(iv) of the Railroad Retirement Act of 1974 and is determined to be eligible to receive Medicare by the Railroad Retirement Board; or Section 2(a)(1)(v) of the Railroad Retirement Act of 1974 and is determined to be disabled based upon the criteria used under Title XVI of the Social Security Act. •Veteran’s benefits based on a service-connected or nonservice-connected disability rated by the Veteran's Administration (VA) as total or paid as total by the VA under Title 38 of the United States Code (this includes veterans considered by the VA to need regular aid and attendance or permanently housebound). •Is a surviving spouse of a veteran and considered by the VA to need regular aid and attendance or permanently housebound or a surviving child of a veteran and considered by the VA to be permanently incapable of selfsupport under Title 38 of the United States Code. •Is a surviving spouse or surviving child of a veteran and considered by the VA to be entitled to compensation for a service-connected death or pension benefits for a nonservice-connected death under Title 38 of the United States Code and has a disability considered permanent under Section 221(i) of the Social Security Act (entitled as used in this definition refers to those veterans' surviving spouses and surviving children who are receiving the compensation or pension benefits stated or have been approved for such payments, but are not yet receiving them). 2. Restricted HH: Restricted HH members are individuals who live together and must be considered as P&P meals together, even if they claim not to be. Restricted HH members are required to be included in the same HH. The following are restricted HH members in which separate HH status cannot be approved: •Spouses either married under applicable state law or who are living together and representing themselves to the community as married. •A person under 22 years of age who is living with their natural or adoptive parent(s) or stepparent(s). When the parents of a child have joint custody and there is equal (50/50) physical custody of a child and the living arrangements are that the child lives with each parent an equal number of days per month, HH composition will be determined as follows: If the child eats … then … the majority of meals in a month the child may participate with the parent providing the majority of the meals, unless the two custodial parents agree County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Household Concept 63-101 3 of 8 with one parent, otherwise. an equal number of meals with each parent monthly, the first custodial parent to apply may participate with the child, unless the two custodial parents agree otherwise. •A minor (other than a foster child) who lives with and is under the parental control of a HH member who is not his or her parent unless the minor meets one of the following conditions: Has entered a valid marriage Is on active duty in the U.S. armed forces Has been emancipated by a court order Note: A minor (other than a foster child) is not considered under the parental control of a HH member when one of the following occurs: The minor’s liquid resources and/or income is sufficient to economically self-support their own affairs The minor is approaching their 18th birthday in the calendar month prior to application The minor comes and goes without approval •Children who reside at a drug/alcohol treatment center with their parent. 3. Dependent Relationship: If there is a dependent relationship between any restricted HH members, they must all be included in the HH. A dependent relationship is established if any of the following apply: •Reside on the same parcel of land and do not live in separate and distinct living quarters. Separate and distinct living quarters include different buildings with self-contained living facilities, different units within the same building with self-contained living facilities, and mobile homes that are affixed to the land. •Repeatedly using the kitchen, bathroom or sleeping facilities of the other person, repeatedly is defined as a majority of usage of any such type of facility. 4. Non-HH Members: The following members should not be included as a member of the HH unless they P&P meals together. Non-HH members who are otherwise eligible, may participate as a separate HH from the individuals they live with. The following are considered non-HH members: •Individuals to whom a HH provides lodging but not meals, also known as roomers. •Live-in attendants or individuals who reside with a HH to provide medical, housekeeping, childcare or other similar personal services. •Individuals who share living quarters and are not restricted HH members. 5. Separate HH Status: Separate HH status may be approved for the following: •An individual living with others who customarily P&Ps meals separately from the other members in the home. Note: A disabled individual who is unable to P&P (who is not a restricted HH member) their own meals but has arranged to have their food P&P separately from those they live with, even if the County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Household Concept 63-101 4 of 8 person who shops for the food or prepares the meals for the disabled individual lives in the home, may claim separate HH status. Example Scenario HH consists of mom and her 30-year-old severely disabled son. Mom and son claim to P&P separately. Son states mom uses his money to shop for him and prepares his meals for him, since he is unable to. Outcome Son is considered a separate HH from mom and may have his own CalFresh case. •An individual (and their children if living with them) who is a temporary resident of a shelter for battered persons. 6. 165% Rule for Separate HH Status for E/D HH Members: Although all individuals living together who P&P meals together are considered to be one CalFresh HH, there is one exception. Refer to the table below for situations when an elderly person who suffers from a disability considered permanent under the Social Security Act or a non-disease related severe permanent disability may be considered a separate HH from those they P&P with. If an E/D person (and their spouse) reports… then the E/D person (and their spouse) … they are unable to P&P their own meals therefore they P&P meals together with the other HH members they live with, may be considered a separate HH from those they live with if the income of the other HH members (excluding the E/D individual and their spouse’s income) is less than 165% of the Federal Poverty Line (FPL). Note: The E/D person (and their spouse) may be a separate HH but are not required to be. Staff should process the case based on what is most beneficial to the HH. they P&P meals separately from the others in which they live, is considered a separate HH and the 165% FPL rule is not used. Note: If the E/D person states to P&P separately we are to accept their statement. See examples below: Example 1 Scenario HH consists of a mother, her 2 minor children and their 61-year-old grandma who is receiving Social Security Disability benefits. Grandma is unable to P&P her meals on her own and reports she P&P with the rest of the HH. The HH income including the grandma’s income is $3,200 per month. The grandma’s income is $524 per month. Outcome HHs total income $3,200 Grandma’s income - $524 HH gross income $2,676 165% FPL of a HH of 3 (mom and 2 children) = $3,167 Since the income does not exceed 165% FPL for a HH of 3 people, the grandma County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Household Concept 63-101 5 of 8 can be certified as her own HH consisting of just her, even if she reports to P&P with her daughter and grandchildren. Example 2 Scenario HH consists of a mother, her 2 minor children and their 61-year-old grandma who is receiving Social Security Disability benefits. Grandma is unable to P&P her meals on her own and reports she P&P together with the rest of the HH. The HH income including the grandma’s income is $8,624 per month. The grandma’s income is $524 per month. Outcome HHs total income $8,624 Grandma’s income - $524 HH gross income $8,000 165% FPL of a HH of 3 (mom and 2 children) = $3,167 Since the income exceeds 165% FPL for a HH of 3 people, the grandma cannot be certified as her own HH consisting of just her, the daughter and 2 grandchildren are required to be part of the CalFresh HH. Example 3 Scenario HH consists of a mother, her 2 minor children and their 61-year-old grandma who is receiving Social Security Disability benefits. Grandma reports she P&P her meals separate from the HH. The HH income including the grandma’s income is $7,000 per month. The grandma’s income is $524 per month. Outcome Since grandma reports to P&P on her own evaluate her as a separate HH and do not review for the 165% rule. 7. Residents of Institutions: Residents of institutions are ineligible to CalFresh. Individuals are considered residents of an institution when the institution provides them with the majority of their meals (over 50% of three meals a day) as part of the institution’s normal services. Examples of institutions include Job Corps, hospitals, jails, commercial boarding houses, and nursing homes. Any time staff become aware that a HH member is residing in an institution, they should verify the information and discontinue benefits for the individual if the stay has lasted or is expected to last over 30 days. The following individuals are not considered residents of institutions: •Residents of federally subsidized housing for the elderly. •Individuals residing in Drug or Alcoholic Treatment Centers (D/ATC), refer to 63-123. •Children of residents of D/ATC who reside with their parent(s) in the treatment center. •Disabled or blind individuals residing in Group Living Arrangements (GLA) receiving benefits under Title II of the Social Security Act, refer to 63-123. •Residents of temporary shelters for battered persons, refer to 63-124. •Residents of public or private nonprofit homeless shelters. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Household Concept 63-101 6 of 8 8. Boarders: Boarders are individuals or groups of individuals residing with a HH in a private home and paying reasonable compensation to the HH for lodging and meals. Boarders should not be confused with roomers who are only paying for lodging. Commercial boarding houses are establishments licensed as commercial enterprises offering meals and lodging for compensation with the intent of making a profit. Residents of commercial boarding houses are considered residents of institutions and are ineligible to CalFresh. The table below demonstrates reasonable compensation: If the board arrangement is for… the boarder shall pay an amount… more than 2 meals per day, equal to or that exceeds the max monthly CalFresh allotment for the appropriate number of boarders. 2 meals or less per day, equal to or that exceeds two-thirds of the max CalFresh allotment for the appropriate number of boarders. Note: If the boarder pays less than reasonable compensation, they would not be treated as a boarder, they would be considered a member of the HH they live with and would be required to be included in the same CalFresh HH. Boarders are ineligible to CalFresh when applying on their own. Boarders may only be eligible to CalFresh if the HH providing the boarding services applies for CalFresh and requests that the boarder be included in their HH. If the HH providing the boarding services applies for CalFresh and does not request the boarder be included in their HH, the income received from the boarder must be included in the budget as self-employment income. Refer to Section 63-225 for more information. The following individuals are considered boarders if they are placed by a federal, state, or local government program in the private home of a relative or other individual. If the HH providing the lodging and meals requests to include them, their assistance payment must be counted in the budget: •Foster Care or Approved Relative Caregiver (ARC) children. •Non-Minor Dependent (NMD) children receiving CalWORKs under the Extended Foster Care Program (AB 12). •Kinship Guardian Assistance Payment (Kin-GAP) children. Note: Children who participate in the "Foster Care Wraparound Services" program are not considered foster care children. 9. NMD Receiving Extended Foster Care Living in a Supervised Independent Living Placement (SILP) or a Transitional Housing Placement Program (THPP): The following individuals may apply for CalFresh as a separate HH, however if they report to P&P with others they live with, those individuals must be included in their CalFresh HH. NMD residing in SILPs and THPPs will have part of their Foster Care payment paid directly to the facility they live in, and the remainder paid directly to the NMD. The only portion of the foster care payment which should be included as unearned income is the portion paid directly to the NMD. Refer to How To #331 Entering THP/FC Benefits in CalFresh Case for instructions on how to enter the income. 10. Strikers: A striker is defined as anyone involved in a strike or concerted stoppage of work by employees or any concerted slowdown or interruption of operations by employees. Included in the definition of a County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Household Concept 63-101 7 of 8 concerted stoppage of work is a stoppage by reason of the expiration of a collective-bargaining agreement. HHs with striking members are ineligible to CalFresh unless the HH was eligible the day before the strike and is otherwise eligible at the time of application. The following people are not considered strikers: •Employees whose workplace is closed by an employer in order to resist demands of employees (a lockout). •Non–striking employees unable to work as a result of striking employees. •Employees not wanting to cross a picket line due to fear of personal injury or death. •Individuals exempted from work registration on the day prior to the strike, other than those exempt solely on the grounds that they are employed. •Employees whose employers have hired permanent replacements for the striking employees’ jobs. The fact that the striking employees are offered other jobs does not affect their status as they must be able to return to the same job. Refer to Processing Guide 101-01 for instructions on determining eligibility for strikers. 11. Head of HH: The head of HH is usually the person in whose name the application is made, however the HH may designate any responsible HH member to serve as the head of HH. Although an individual may be designated as the head of HH, any responsible HH member may apply, recertify, complete the semiannual report, or report changes. When there is no adult eligible to be included in the HH, the head of HH may be: •A non-HH member. •An excluded HH member. •Any adult responsible for the minor HH member(s). •A minor, if not living with an adult. 12. Ineligible HH Members: These individuals are required to be included in the HH but are ineligible to CalFresh benefits. When determining benefits ineligible HH members are excluded from the HH size as described in the table below: Reason for Ineligibility Exclude When Determining the HH Size for the Purposes of - Social Security Number (SSN) disqualified - Ineligible noncitizen - Individuals failing to meet Able Body Adults Without Dependents (ABAWD) work requirements - Assigning a benefit level - Assigning a standard deduction - Comparing the HH’s monthly income with the income eligibility standards - Comparing the HH’s resources with the resource eligibility limits - Determining the categorical eligibility of the HH - Intentional Program Violator (IPV) - Fleeing felon - Assigning a benefit level - Comparing the HH’s monthly income with the County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Household Concept 63-101 8 of 8 - Probation/parole violator - Work sanctioned income eligibility standards - Comparing the HH’s resources with the resource eligibility limits - Ineligible student - Excluded from the HH size count for everything References: ACL 11-05, 14-100, 17-09, 18-90, 19-51 ACIN I-02-82, I-39-13, I-68-17 MPP 63-402, 503.44-.45 CFR 273.1 FNS Memorandum, Separate Household Status for Disabled Persons (6/12/2006) Processing Guide 101-01 Household Concept Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 04/30/2026. Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-103 Filing an Application
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageFiling an Application 63-103 1 of 3 Revision: 06/01/2022 Background: To apply for CalFresh benefits an application must be submitted. CalFresh applicants must then complete an interview and provide verification of certain information. Purpose: This section provides guidance on acceptable application forms, determining the beginning date of aid, and the processing of combo applications. This section is being revised after sunset review, there are no changes due to state legislation. Policy: Any of the following forms may be used to apply for CalFresh: •Application for CalFresh Benefits (CF 285) •Initial Application for CalFresh, Cash-Aid, and/or Medi-Cal/Healthcare Programs (SAWS 1) •Application for CalFresh, Cash-Aid, and/or Medi-Cal/Healthcare Programs (SAWS 2 Plus) Application forms must be available to customers at each Family Resource Center (FRC) lobby. An application must be accepted as long as it contains the following minimum requirements: applicant’s name, address, and signature of a responsible household (HH) member or Authorized Representative (AR). Applications may be submitted in person, by mail, online, faxed, or by phone. Applications submitted with electronic or telephonic signatures are acceptable. Customers applying for multiple programs will only have to complete one application and one interview. 1. Public Assistance (PA) and CalFresh Application: An application submitted for PA shall be considered a request for both PA and CalFresh, unless it is determined otherwise during the interview. When processing a PA and CalFresh application, eligibility for CalFresh benefits will be based on CalFresh regulations, including Expedited Services (ES). If PA is denied, CalFresh must continue to be evaluated. 2. Establishing the Beginning Date of Aid (BDA): The date the application is received by the county establishes the BDA. The date the application is received must be recorded on the application. If an application is received outside of normal business hours, the beginning date of aid will be the next business day. If the application is submitted … then the date of application will be … within regular business hours, the date that the application is received by the county. after regular business hours, the next business day from the date that the application was received by the county. Example: Application was received on Monday at 5:30 PM. Date of application will be Tuesday. on a non-business day, the next business day from the date that the application was received by the county. Example: Application was submitted on Saturday at 9:30 AM. Date of application will be Monday. If Monday is a holiday and the office is closed, the date of application will be Tuesday. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageFiling an Application 63-103 2 of 3 Note: Regular business hours are 7AM – 5PM Monday through Friday. 3. Establishing the Semi-Annual Report (SAR) Payment Period: The BDA establishes the SAR payment period. The SAR payment period begins the first month the customer is eligible to receive benefits. If the customer is not eligible to receive benefits in the month of application, the SAR payment period will begin in the second month. Example: Establishing BDA and SAR Cycle Scenario Customer applies in January, is not eligible for benefits in January, but is approved for benefits in February and ongoing. Outcome February 1st is the BDA and the SAR cycle begins in February. 4. Month of Application: Eligibility in the month of application is determined by the HH circumstances as of the date of the interview. Exceptions to this include HH that consist of the following individuals: HH Types Refer to Strikers 63-101 Household Concept for guidance on determining eligibility for strikers Voluntary Quit 63-159 Voluntary Quit and the Reduction of Work Effort for guidance on determining eligibility for customers who have voluntary quit a job Resource Transfers 63-201 Resource Eligibility Determination for guidance on determining eligibility when there has been a transfer of resources Migrant and seasonal farmworkers that meet the destitute criteria 63-252 Household’s with Migrant or Seasonal Farmworkers for guidance on determining eligibility for Migrant or seasonal farmworkers that meet the destitute criteria in the month of application Categorically Eligible (CE) 63-120 Categorical Eligibility (CE) for guidance on determining CalFresh eligibility for CE HH 5. Proration of Benefits: Most of the time, a HH will not get a full month’s benefits in the month of application, this is also referred to as proration. CalFresh benefits are prorated from the date the application was received and customers will be issued benefits for the days remaining in the month. Refer to section 63-109 Time Limits and Delays for further guidance on timely processing. The table below describes proration of benefits in the month of application: If … Then … all required verifications are received timely, benefits will be prorated from the date the application is received. processing the application is delayed beyond 30 days due to the fault of the HH but is found eligible during the second 30-day period, benefits will be prorated from the date the customer submits all required verifications. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageFiling an Application 63-103 3 of 3 processing the application is delayed beyond 30 days due to the fault of the county, benefits will be prorated retroactive to the date of the application. Note: Migrant or seasonal farmworker HH’s that have a break in aid of 30 days or less will not have their benefits prorated, they will receive the full month’s benefit. 6. CalFresh Application Used to Apply for Medi-Cal: Upon the return of a CalFresh application, if the customer indicates interest in applying for Medi-Cal, the information captured on the CalFresh application will be used to complete an eligibility determination for Medi-Cal. If there is no active or pending Medi-Cal, collect the Request for Tax Household Information (RFTHI) from the customer. The Medi-Cal BDA will be established upon receipt of the RFTHI. Refer to MPG 04.02.13A for further guidance when processing a Medi-Cal eligibility determination using a CalFresh application. 7. Verification Procedure for Combo Applications: Verifications received for other programs can be used to help determine eligibility for CalFresh. Do not delay processing the CalFresh application while waiting for verifications for other programs. Approve CalFresh as soon as all verifications have been received, even if there are pending verifications for other programs. If other programs are denied, continue to evaluate CalFresh eligibility based on the original application. CalFresh cannot be denied for failure to provide before the 30 th day even if the PA application is denied sooner. Refer to 63-117 Verification and Documentation for guidance on mandatory CalFresh verifications. Other Program Impacts: CalWORKs, CAPI, GR, MC References: MPP 63-300.2; MPP 63-301.6; MPP 63-503; MPG 04.02.13A; ACWDL 01-10; ACL 15-84; AB 59; SB 493 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 06/30/2025. Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-105 Expedited Services
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageExpedited Services 63-105 1 of 3 Revision: 08/01/2020 Background: Expedited Services (ES) allows eligible customers to receive CalFresh benefits while their case is being processed. When found eligible to ES, benefits must be issued to the customer within the 3-day ES timeframe. There are no changes due to State legislation, this section is being re-formatted after sunset review. Purpose: This section describes the policies for evaluating ES. Policy: ES must be screened and evaluated even when the ES section of the application is not completed. Applications that do not contain enough information to determine ES eligibility will be processed under regular CalFresh timeframes. The screening and evaluation must be completed during the intake interview and anytime the household’s situation changes prior to granting the case. This includes customers being certified or reapplying after less than a one-month break in aid. Customers must be offered application assistance and informed of their right to ES. Evaluations must be completed, and benefits issued within the 3-day ES timeframe. Refer to CalFresh Expedited Services/Processing Timeframes Desk Aid. 1. ES Criteria: When determining ES, actual monthly income and liquid resources reported for the application month must be used to determine ES eligibility. To be eligible to ES, a customer must meet one of the following criteria: •Customers with less than $150.00 in monthly gross income and $100.00 or less in liquid resources. (liquid resources are counted during the ES evaluation) or •Customers whose combined gross monthly income and liquid resources are less than the monthly rent or mortgage and utilities or •Migrant or seasonal farm worker’s who are destitute and have liquid resources that are not more than $100.00 After ES eligibility criteria is determined to be met, the eligibility determination must be completed as follows: •Budget the income that can be reasonably anticipated over the certification period to determine the benefit amount •Evaluate for eligibility to the State Utility Assistance Subsidy (SUAS) •Exempt resources if the customer is determined Modified Categorical Eligible (MCE) 2. ES Ineligibility: Customers who are ineligible to ES will not be issued a denial Notice of Action (NOA). Customers disputing the ES ineligibility may request an agency conference. Refer to Processing Guide 105-01 for steps on conducting an agency conference. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageExpedited Services 63-105 2 of 3 3. Verifications Required for ES: The only verification required to issue ES is identity of the customer. If the household applies through an Authorized Representative (AR), both the AR and customer must provide identity verification. Refer to “Desk Aid Verification Requirement Chart” in Eligibility Essentials for a detailed listing of acceptable forms of identity verifications. When processing ES, attempt to obtain all required verifications to approve ES and CalFresh at the same time. Do not delay the issuance of ES while waiting for the mandatory verifications to be provided. 4. Processing Standards: ES evaluations must be completed, and benefits issued no later than the third calendar day following the date the application was received. A weekend (Saturday and Sunday) will be considered one calendar day. When the third calendar day is a nonworking day and benefits cannot be issued, the benefits must be made available the last working day prior to the third calendar day. Recertification or re-applications after less than a one-month break in aid must have ES benefits issued no later than the third calendar day following the date the application is filed or by the household's normal issuance cycle in the new certification period, whichever is later. ES regulations do not apply if the recertification is completed before the end of the certification period. The ES time frame for customers evaluated and determined eligible to ES during the initial interview will start from the date the county became aware of the household’s ES eligibility. Customers applying for both CalWORKs and CalFresh (PACF) are eligible to apply for both ES and Immediate Need (IN) benefits. Only one application and one interview are required for both programs. The only exception for conducting a separate CalFresh interview is to prevent a delay in the issuance of ES. Evaluate ES and IN independently of each other. ES evaluation will not be delayed while waiting for the CalWORKs IN request to be processed. 5. Customers with Postponed Verifications: Customers approved for ES who do not provide the postponed verifications within 30-days from the date the application was filed will be discontinued. Customers may have their ES eligibility reevaluated if the postponed verifications are received during the second 30-day period. Refer to 63- 109.6 for policy on processing customer caused delays. Customers who reapply are not entitled to ES again unless the postponed verifications have been provided. The “Notice of Approval for CalFresh Benefits” must be sent informing customers that no further benefits will be issued until the postponed verifications are provided and eligibility will discontinue if they fail to provide the postponed verifications. When the postponed verifications are provided, a re-evaluation must be completed for future and ongoing benefits. Postponed verifications must be processed within five working days from the date the verifications are received, or the first day of the second calendar month, whichever is later. There is no limit to the number of times a customer may apply for ES. Customers with postponed verifications will have benefits prorated and issued as follows: If the application is submitted … Then issue prorated ES benefits for the … on or before the 15th of the month month of application and the following month’s benefits will be “pending” until any postponed verifications are provided after the 15th of the month application month and issue the following month’s allotment at the same time County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageExpedited Services 63-105 3 of 3 Migrant farm worker households may postpone out of state verifications once each farm season. The out of state verification must be provided within 60-days following the date the application was filed. Migrant households eligible to ES will receive the prorated benefits for the application month and the following month if the only missing verification is from an out of state source. When the out of state verification is not received within 60 days, benefits will be discontinued. Procedure: CalFresh Processing Guide 105-01 References: MPP 63-301.5 All County Letter 16-14 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 08/31/2023 Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Eligibility Operations

title: 63-107 Household Cooperation
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Household Cooperation 63-107 1 of 3 Revision Date 12/01/2019 Background: Households or the designated authorized representative must cooperate in the application process and Quality Control (QC) review process. Refusal to cooperate in completing the application process will result in the application being denied. Households that refuse to cooperate with the QC review process will result in the household being sanctioned. This revision updates the section to the new format. There are no changes due to state legislation. Purpose: This section describes the CalFresh regulations for households failing to cooperate with the application and the QC review process. Policy: 63-107.1 Household Cooperation to Determine Eligibility: In order to determine eligibility to the CalFresh program, the household or its authorized representative must: •Complete and sign the application form •Be interviewed; and •Verify certain information on the application 63-107.2 Refusal to Cooperate: If the household, including excluded household members who are part of the CalFresh household, refuses to cooperate in completing the application process, the application will be denied at the time of refusal. In order to determine that a household has refused to cooperate, the household must have been able to cooperate and clearly demonstrated that the household chose not to take the actions required to complete the application process. If the household has merely failed to cooperate, as opposed to refuse to cooperate, the household will not be denied The household will also be determined ineligible when refusing to cooperate in any subsequent review of eligibility, including reviews generated by reported changes, recertifications, or as part of a QC review. Note: Refusal to disclose a Social Security Number (SSN) is an exception to the denial of the entire household. When an individual required to provide his/her SSN has refused to comply, the eligibility of the other household members will not be affected. If a noncitizen refuses to provide immigration documentation or the sponsor’s information (unless they meet an exception to sponsorship provisions found in 63-157.3), the noncitizen will be considered an excluded member of the CalFresh household and his/her income, resources and deductible expenses will be counted according to Sections 63-244 and 63-206. 63-107.3 Refusal to Cooperate with a QC review: The Quality and Eligibility Support Departments (QESD) and QC staff are responsible for conducting reviews as part of the County’s Performance Reporting System. For QC reviews, a statistical sample County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Household Cooperation 63-107 2 of 3 of households will be selected from active cases and denied, suspended, or terminated CalFresh cases. The QC review period extends from October 1st to September 30th of the next year. A household can be selected for a State or Federal review of CalFresh benefits authorized for a specific sample month. Cooperation is mandatory for both types of reviews. If a household refuses to cooperate, it is subject to State or Federal sanctions and it is ineligible to receive CalFresh. When a household member refuses to cooperate in a QC review, the entire household must be discontinued from the CalFresh program at the end of the month in which a timely and adequate notice can be provided. The QESD Eligibility Support staff are responsible for imposing the QC sanction on the CalFresh household, as specified in How To #335. Failure to cooperate with the QC review is a County initiated action. Therefore, the sanctioned household should be discontinued mid-period with timely notice. Refer to 63-285.1. Sanction Periods Once denied or discontinued for refusal to cooperate with the QC review, the household may reapply but will not be eligible until the household cooperates with the QC review during the review period. If the household does not cooperate during the review period, the household will be ineligible to participate for a specified period, depending on the review type (State or Federal). State The household is not eligible to reapply until at least 125 days after the end of the annual review period in which the refusal to cooperate with a State QC reviewer occurred. Federal The household is not eligible to reapply until 9 months after the end of the annual review period in which the refusal to cooperate with a Federal QC reviewer occurred. Refer to 63-1103 Definitions and Examples for examples of State and Federal sanctions. Note: An applicant’s household that has been sanctioned for not cooperating with QC will be required to provide verification of all eligibility requirements, including items that would normally be verified only if questionable, as specified in 63-117. 63-107.4 Cooperating with QESD: The QESD Eligibility Support staff are responsible for ending the QC sanction on the CalFresh household as follows: QC Sanctions will be removed and the CalFresh case will be re-opened when: •the sanctioned household cooperates and completes the review during the QC review period, and the household cooperates during the month of the discontinuance (sanction has not taken effect) QC Sanctions will be removed but the CalFresh household must re-apply for CalFresh when: •the sanctioned household cooperates and completes the review during the QESD review period, but they cooperate after the month of discontinuance (sanction is already in effect) County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Household Cooperation 63-107 3 of 3 63-107.5 Failure to Cooperate with QESD: The QESD Eligibility Support staff are responsible for assisting the QC reviewer in locating households that fail to cooperate during the QESD review period, by sending the CF 387 Request for Information (RFI) to the last known address, as outlined in 63-152.8. 63-107.6 Non-Cooperating Household Member: Non-Cooperating Household Member If a non-cooperating household member refuses to cooperate in a QC review, the entire household must be discontinued from the CalFresh program at the end of the month in which a timely and adequate notice can be provided. Non-Cooperating Household Member leaves the Household During the Sanction Period If the non-cooperating household member(s) leaves the household (household #1) during the sanction period, the sanction will follow the non-cooperating household member(s). If the remaining household members from the original household were not considered non-cooperating members, they will be eligible to reapply for CalFresh. Non-Cooperating Household Member leaves the Household and joins another CalFresh Household If the non-cooperating household member (from household #1) joins another CalFresh household (household #2), household #2 becomes ineligible until the sanction ends or the non-cooperating household member complies with the QC review during the QC review period and CalFresh household sanction is lifted. Refer to 63-1103 Definition and Examples for examples. Procedure: Required Actions EO staff are to refer the CalFresh household to the QC reviewer for cooperation in the QC review. Other Program Impacts None References: MPP 63-505; ACL 11-72; ACL 11-72E; How To #335 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 11/30/2022 Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Eligibility Operations

title: 63-109 Time Limits and Delays
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Time Limits and Delays Number Page 63-109 1 of 4 Revision Date: 11/01/2024 Background: Processing standards are set in place to ensure the application process is completed within state mandated timeframes. Purpose: This section outlines time limit guidelines for applications and processing delays. This section is being revised due to sunset review. Policy: All applications must be processed at the earliest extent possible upon receipt, but no later than the 30th day from the date of application. If eligibility is not determined and the opportunity to participate is not provided within 30 days of the application date, it will result in untimely processing. Processing guidelines for required actions during the initial 30 days of the application are outline d in CalFresh Processing Guide 109-01 Time Limits and Delays. 1. Exceptions to Denials on the 30th Day Exceptions to processing guidelines apply to applications where the 30th day from the file date falls on a non-business day. When this occurs, the application must be denied on the following business day. Refer to examples below: 2. Delayed Processing When processing a delayed action, first determine the cause. Eligibility determination delays will be categorized as either household (HH) or county caused. When the HH has failed to complete the application process despite the county’s actions to assist , establish a HH caused delay . When the county has failed to complete the required actions, establish a county caused delay. Refer to table below for HH caused reasons and county required actions. If the HH fails to… then the county required action is to… complete application forms, offer or attempt to offer, assistance in its completion. Example 1 Scenario The 30th day from the application file date falls on Wednesday, Christmas Day. Outcome Deny the application on Thursday, the next business day. Example 2 Scenario The 30th day from the application file date falls on a Sunday and Monday is a holiday. Outcome Deny the application on Tuesday, the next business day. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Time Limits and Delays Number Page 63-109 2 of 4 provide complete verification, provide the HH with a list of required verifications on the Request for Verifications (CW 2200) form and offer assistance in obtaining the verifications. Give the HH at least 10 days from the date of the initial request to provide missing verification. appear to their initial interview, issue a Notice of Missed Interview (NOMI) CF 386. If the HH requests to be rescheduled within the initial 30-day period, then schedule a second interview. If the HH… then… postpones the second interview or cannot be rescheduled until after the 20th day, but before the 30th day from the date of application, the HH must appear for their interview, provide verification, and register members for work by the 30th day. Otherwise, the delay is the fault of the HH. fails to appear to their initial interview and the second interview is postponed at the HH’s request until after 30th day from the date the application was filed, delay is fault of the HH. has missed both scheduled interviews and requests another interview, any delay is fault of the HH. Note: A denial action cannot be taken if the 10 days from the request for verification have not elapsed even if the due date is past the 30th day. 3. Delays Beyond 30th Day If the application cannot be processed by the end of the 30- day processing period due to the fault of the HH, deny the application on the 30 th day and the HH will lose their entitlement to benefits for the month of application. However, give the HH an additional 30 days from the date of denial to take the required action. When the application is denied, send the HH a denial NOA on the 30 th day notifying the HH of the action required to complete the application. If the HH takes the required action within the second 30- day period (within 60 days from the application file date), a new application is not required to make an eligibility determination. If the HH responds during the second 30-day processing period and is found to be… then… eligible, prorate benefits from the date the HH provided all required verifications and completed actions. ineligible, deny the application and provide the HH with a denial NOA. If the HH does not take the required action s within the second 30- day processing period, take no further action. The HH must re-apply. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Time Limits and Delays Number Page 63-109 3 of 4 When a delay in the initial 30- day application processing period is the fault of the county, take immediate corrective action. Do not deny the application unless otherwise ineligible. Process the application and send the DFA 377.1A NOA to inform the HH of the pending processing of their application by the 30th day of the application file date. • If the case documentation is insufficient to determine eligibility , inform the HH of any actions or verifications that are required to complete the application process. • If the HH fails to respond during the second 30- day processing period, deny the application and take no further action. If the HH is determined eligible during the second 30- day processing period, then p rovide benefits back to the date of the application file date. I f the HH is determined ineligible during the second 30- day processing period, then deny the application and send a denial NOA. 4. Delays Beyond 60 Days When processing delays beyond the initial and second 30- day processing period (beyond 60 days), the cause of delay(s) must first be reviewed to determine the HH ’s eligibility and benefit issuance date. Refer to table below for guidance on processing delays beyond 60 days. If at the end of the second 30-day processing period the… then… HH is at fault for not completing the application process, the HH must file a new application to participate. county is at fault for not completing the application process and the case documentation is sufficient to determine eligibility, continue to process the original application and any supplemental information provided by the HH until an eligibility determination is made. If the HH is determined eligible, benefit entitlement will be determined as follows: Initial 30- day Delay 2nd 30-day Delay Benefit Entitlement Date County caused County caused Application file date. HH caused County caused Date all required verifications were received and all actions completed. If the HH is ineligible, deny the application and send a denial NOA. county is at fault for not completing the application process and the case documentation is insufficient to determine eligibility, continue to process the original application and send the HH a DFA 377.1A NOA informing the HH of the pending status of the application. Inform the HH of the actions necessary to complete application process, allow at least 10 days to take required actions specified on the NOA. If the HH fails to take required action, deny the application. CalFresh Processing Guide 109-01 Time Limits and Delays. Other Program Impacts: None. References: All County Letter (ACL) 15-93, 17-55. All County Information Notice (ACIN) I-14-06, I-58-08. Manual of Policy and Procedures (MPP) Sections 63-301.3, 63-301.4. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 10/31/2027.
