title: 63-1103 Definitions and Examples
content: 63-1103 CalFresh Definitions and Examples Calculating Net Monthly Income of Households that Include and Elderly or Disabled Member The household consists of a mother, child and an elderly grandmother. The grandmother purchases and prepares meals with her daughter and grandchild. The total combined monthly unearned income is $2,121 (MCE household). The household pays $1,200 for rent and is entitled to the Standard Utility Allowance. The medical expenses are $235 per month, of which $200 is the medical deduction (the amount in excess of $35). The computation to determine benefits for the household is as follows: Step Action The household is exempt from the gross income test (130% of FPL) due to the elderly/disabled member 1 a.Add the total monthly unearned income of all household members that can be anticipated and b.Deduct the legal obligated child support paid ($2,121-$0): $2,121 2 a.Add the total gross earned income of all household members that can be anticipated: b.Subtract the earned income deduction (20%) and c.Deduct any remaining legal obligated child support paid $0 3 Adjusted Gross Income Add total unearned income plus the adjusted gross earned income (Step 1 + Step 2) [$2,121+$0] $2,121 4 Adjusted Net Income From the total adjusted gross income (Step 3) subtract: $2,121 a.The standard deduction: - $167 b.The excess medical expense [$235- $35=$200]: - $200 c.The monthly dependent care cost: - $0 d.The homeless shelter deduction: - $0 Adjusted Net Income: $1,754 Shelter Deduction Computation Rent: $1,200 SUA: + $397 a. Total Shelter Cost: $1,597 b. 50% of Adjusted Net Income ($1,754/2) = $877 c. Subtract from the total shelter cost 50% of Adjusted Net Income (5a – 5b) $1,597 - $877 5 d. Allowable shelter deduction: $720 Net Income Computation $1,754 - $720 Subtract the shelter cost from the adjusted net income: $1,034 The shelter deduction is not limited to the Maximum Shelter Deduction for households with elderly or disabled members, 6 Net Income: $1,034 7 Do not compute the Net Income Test because the household is MCE Refer to 63-254.6 to determine the household’s allotment CalFresh Allotment Computation Step Action 1 The total net income of a household of four (4) is $725 2 The maximum allotment for a household size of 4 (as of October 2019) is $646 3 Multiply the net monthly by 30%: $725 x 30%=$217.5 rounded up to $218 4 Subtract the amount in #3 above ($218) from the maximum allotment for a household size of 4 ($646): $646 - $218 = $428 Determining Allotment Level EXAMPLE: A CalFresh household of 4 has a net monthly income of $725. Under the “Monthly Net Income” column in the CalFresh Allotment Table ( 63- 1101.5) in page 7, find row “724 - 726.” The CalFresh allotment for 4 persons is $422. See “How to Use the CalFresh Allotment Tables” desk aid. Disabled Household Member A disabled CalFresh household member is a member of a household who is at least one of the following: •Receives disability retirement benefits from a governmental agency because of a disability considered permanent under Section 221(i) of the Social Security Act; or •Receives interim assistance benefits pending receipt of SSI, provided that the eligibility to receive those benefits is based upon disability or blindness criteria, which are at least as stringent as those used under Title XVI of the Social Security Act; or •Receives disability-related medical assistance under Title XIX (Medi-Cal) of the Social Security act; or •Receives disability-based general assistance benefits, provided that the eligibility to receive those benefits is based upon disability or blindness criteria which are at least as stringent as those used under Title XVI of the Social Security Act; or •Is a veteran: oWith a service-connected, or non-service-connected disability rated by the Veteran's Administration (VA) as total or paid as total by the VA under Title 38 of the United States Code; or oConsidered by the VA to be in need of regular aid and attendance or permanently housebound under Title 38 of the United States Code; •Is a surviving spouse of a veteran considered by the VA: oTo be in need of regular aid and attendance, or permanently housebound; oTo be entitled to compensation for a service-connected death or pension benefits for a non-service-connected death under Title 38 of the United States Code; and has a disability considered permanent under Section 221(i) of the Social Security Act; or •Is a surviving child of a veteran: oConsidered by the VA to be permanently incapable of selfsupport under Title 38 of the United States Code; or oConsidered by the VA to be entitled to compensation for a service-connected death or pension benefits for a nonservice-connected death under Title 38 of the United States Code; and has a disability considered permanent under Section 221(i) of the Social Security Act; "Entitled" as used in this definition, refers to those veterans' surviving spouses and surviving children who are receiving the compensation or pension benefits stated, or have been approved for such payments, but are not yet receiving them; or •Receives an annuity payment under Section 2(a)(1)(iv) of the Railroad Retirement Act of 1974 and is determined to be eligible to receive Medicare by the Railroad Retirement Board; or Section 2(a)(1)(v) of the Railroad Retirement Act of 1974 and is determined to be disabled based upon the criteria used under Title XVI of the Social Security Act; or •Receives Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits under Title XVI, or disability or blindness payments under Title II (Social Security Disability Insurance Program) of the Social Security Act; From 1974 to May 31, 2019, in California, SSI recipients were included as a member of the household for purposes of household composition. However, they were excluded from the household for the purpose of determining household size, eligibility or benefit level. Effective June 1, 2019, individuals receiving SSI/SSP in California are eligible for CalFresh, provided all other eligibility criteria are met. Elderly Household Member An elderly CalFresh household member is a member of a household who is 60 years of age or older. ICT INTER-COUNTY TRANSFER A transfer of responsibility for determination of eligibility and provision of social services (including CalFresh) from one county to another. SENDING COUNTY The county from which the household has moved. RECEIVING COUNTY The county to which the household has moved. TRANSFER PERIOD The period of time in which the sending county remains responsible for payment of benefits. 30-DAY TRANSFER PERIOD The 30-day transfer period begins the date the sending county informs the receiving county of the transfer, either via the postmarked date if mailed or the date of the electronic transfer of the notification of the ICT. When the 30th day falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, the first business day following the weekend or holiday is considered to be the last day of the 30-day transfer period. EXPIRATION OF THE TRANSFER PERIOD The expiration of the transfer period occurs at the end of the month following the 30-day transfer period after the sending county either mails or electronically transfers the notification of the ICT to the receiving county or the end of the month in which benefits are discontinued for other reasons, whichever is earlier. By mutual agreement of the counties involved, the transfer of responsibility may occur at an earlier date. Migrant Farm Worker Season A migrant farm season is defined as having a clear beginning point and ending point between which migrant farm workers travel. When they are not migrating to work they are residing at one location which they regard as home. In this case, the season would be the period during which the migrants are traveling to work. If a migrant farm worker travels constantly with no break period, the season will be considered the calendar year. SAR CONVERSION FACTOR A figure used to convert income paid on a weekly or bi-weekly basis to a monthly averaged figure. Weekly amounts are multiplied by 4.33 and bi-weekly amounts by 2.167. COUNTY INITIATED MID-PERIOD ACTIONS The changes in eligibility status based on case information that the worker is required to act upon mid-period in which timely and adequate notice can be provided, even if the action results in a decrease in benefits, such as sanctions, financial penalties, approval of benefits in another household, the end of an inter-county transfer, or cost-of-living changes. EXTENDED FILING DATE The final date by which the household must submit a complete Semi- Annual Report (SAR 7) including all required verification without termination of eligibility. In a SAR system, this is the first working day of the next payment period. FLUCTUATING INCOME Income is considered to be fluctuating when the amount varies significantly for each month of the certification period. This includes when the household has income for one or more months of the certification period and zero income for the remaining months of the certification period due to income starting or stopping. INCOME REPORTING THRESHOLD (IRT) The IRT is the level of income that triggers the requirement of a SAR CalFresh household who has been certified with gross income at or below 130% of the FPL to report a change during the certification period. Note: Households certified between 131% and 200% of the FPL will not be required to make any reports of income during the SAR payment period. These households will not have a CalFresh IRT. Refer to: Processing Guide 63-271-01 Refer to 63-1101.6 for CalFresh IRT. MID-PERIOD CHANGES Any change reported during the certification period that is outside the SAR 7 report or the recertification process. There are two types of midperiod reports: •Mandatory Mid-Period Reports: Under SAR, recipients are mandated to report specified changes within 10 calendar days of the date the change becomes known to the household. The mandatory reporting requirements for CalFresh are: oThe household’s income goes over the CalFresh IRT or when oWork hours for able-bodied adults without dependents (ABAWD) drop below 20 hours averaged monthly outside of the household’s initial certification/ recertification and SAR 7 reporting month. •Voluntary Mid-Period Reports: Reports made by the household during the certification period that are not mandatory. PROSPECTIVE BUDGETING Budgeting methodology that uses reasonably anticipated income for the determination of benefits for a household. REASONABLY ANTICIPATED INCOME AND EXPENSES Income and expenses that have been or will be budgeted for the upcoming certification period when: •The income has been or will be approved or authorized as of a date within the upcoming certification period, or the household is otherwise reasonably certain that the income will be received within the period; and •The amount of income is known. STABLE INCOME Income that is expected to remain at the same level and frequency throughout the certification period. Income could be considered stable when the amounts don’t vary significantly and the pattern of receipt is stable throughout the certification period. VERIFIED UPON RECEIPT (VUR) Information provided that is not questionable, where the provider is the primary source of the information and for which no further information is needed to take action. CalFresh Examples and Scenarios Alignment of CalFresh/CalWORKs Examples: Example 1: Aligning CalWORKs (CW) to Existing CalFresh (CF) with 12 month certification period Situation Ongoing regular NACF case with BDA of January 10, 2015 (cycle 1); the recertification month is December 2015. •The household applies for CW on August 15, 2015. Outcome Match CW redetermination to existing CF recertification. CW will be certified for five months (August 2015 to December 2015). In December 2015, CW/CF will have Redetermination/ Recertification. •Match CW cycle to CF cycle Example 2: Aligning CW to Existing CF earned income household with 24 month certification period Situation Ongoing E/D NACF case with BDA of January 10, 2015 (cycle 1); the recertification month is December 2016. •The household applies for CW on August 15, 2015. Outcome Match CW redetermination to existing CF 12 month SAR 7 Submit Month. CW case will be certified for five months (August 2015 to December 2015). At the December 2015 CF will submit a SAR 7 and CW will have 1 st redetermination. In June 2016 CW/CF will submit a SAR7. In December 2016, CW will have 2nd redetermination and CF will have 1st recertification •Match CW cycle to CF cycle Example 3: Aligning CW to Existing CF unearned income household with 24 months certification period Situation Ongoing E/D NACF case with BDA of January 10, 2015 (cycle 1); the recertification month is December 2016. The household applies for CW on August 15, 2015. Outcome Match CW redetermination to existing CF 12 month SAR 7 Submit Month. CW case will be certified for five months (August 2015 to December 2015). At the December 2015 CF will submit a SAR 7 and CW will have 1st redetermination. In June 2016 CW will submit a SAR7. In December 2016, CW will have 2nd redetermination and CF will have 1st recertification Match CW cycle to CF cycle Example 4: Aligning Regular CF with 12 months certification period household to Existing CW Situation Ongoing CW case with BDA of January 10, 2016, (cycle 1); the redetermination month is December 2016. The household applies for CF on August 15, 2016. Outcome •Match the CF recertification to the existing CW redetermination. CF case will be certified for 5 months (August 2016 to December 2016). In December 2016, CW/CF will have Redetermination/Recertification. •Match CF cycle to CW cycle Example 5: Aligning E/D CF with 24 month certification period and no earned income household to Existing CW Situation Ongoing CW case with BDA of January 10, 2016, (cycle 1); the redetermination month is December 2016. •The household applies for CF August 15, 2016. Outcome •Match CF recertification to existing CW redetermination. CF case will be certified for 17 months (August 2016 to December 2017). In December 2016 CF will submit a SAR 7 and CW will have 1 st redetermination. In June 2017 CW will submit a SAR7. In December 2017, CW will have 2nd redetermination and CF will have 1st recertification. •Match CW cycle to CF cycle Example 6: Aligning CF earned income household with 24 month certification period to Existing CW Situation Ongoing CW case with BDA of January 10, 2016, (cycle 1); the redetermination month is December 2016. •The household applies for CalFresh August 15, 2016. Outcome •Match CF recertification to the existing CW redetermination. CF case will be certified for 17 months (August 2016 to December 2017). In December 2016 CF will submit a SAR 7 and CW will have 1 st redetermination. In June 2017 CW/CF will submit a SAR 7. In December 2017, CW will have 2 nd redetermination and CF will have 1 st recertification. •Match CW cycle to CF cycle Alignment of CalFresh/CalWORKs Examples with Charts: How to align CW to existing CF case: Example 1: CF household with earned income and a 24 month certification period. The BDA is March 2016 (Cycle 3), CW application May 2016. Align CW to the existing CF as follows: Match CW cycle to CF Cycle 3. (If CalWIN does not correctly align the cycle, a supervisor can change it.) Match the CW RRR to CF existing RRR. Since CF has a RRR at 24 months, match the CW RRR to the CF SAR 7 due at 12 months. CF/CW will have an RRR at 24 months. See chart below: Month 1st 2nd 3rd 4th 5th 6th 7th 8th 9th 10th 11th 12th CalFresh Program CF BDA CF SAR7 CF SAR7 CalWORKs Program CW BDA CW SAR7 1st CW RRR Month 13th 14th 15th 16th 17th 18th 19th 20th 21st 22nd 23rd 24th CalFresh Program CF SAR7 CF RRR CalWORKs Program CW SAR7 2nd CW RRR Example 2: CF household with a 12 month certification period. The BDA is March 2016 (Cycle 3). Applies for CW May 2016. Align CW program to existing CF case as follows: Match CW cycle to CF Cycle 3 and match the CW RRR to CF existing RRR. Month 1st 2nd 3rd 4th 5th 6th 7th 8th 9th 10th 11th 12th CalFresh Program CF BDA CF SAR7 CF RRR CalWORKs Program CW BDA CW SAR7 CW RRR Example 3: CF household with no earned income and a 24 month certification period. The BDA is March 2016 (Cycle 3). Applies for CW on May 2016. Align CW to existing CF as follows: Match CW cycle to CF Cycle 3. (If CalWIN does not correctly align the cycle, a supervisor can change it.) Match the CW RRR to CF existing RRR. Since CF has a RRR at 24 months, match the CW RRR to the CF SAR 7 due at 12 months. CF/CW will have an RRR at 24 months. See chart below: Month 1st 2nd 3rd 4th 5th 6th 7th 8th 9th 10th 11th 12th CalFresh Program CF BDA CF SAR7 CalWORKs Program CW BDA CW SAR7 1st CW RRR Month 13th 14th 15th 16th 17th 18th 19th 20th 21st 22nd 23rd 24th CalFresh Program CF RRR CalWORKs Program CW SAR7 2nd CW RRR How to align CF case to existing CW case: Example 1: CW BDA is February 2016, Cycle 2 and RRR January 2017. CF household living on an Indian Reservation with no earned income applies June 2016. (24 month certification period) Match CF cycle to CW Cycle 2. (If CalWIN does not correctly align the cycle, a supervisor can change it.) Match CF SAR 7 at the 12 month to the CW RRR. See chart below: Month 1st 2nd 3rd 4th 5th 6th 7th 8th 9th 10th 11th 12th CalFresh Program CF BDA CF SAR7 CalWORKs Program CW BDA CW SAR7 1st CW RRR Month 13th 14th 15th 16th 17th 18th 19th 20th 21st 22nd 23rd 24th CalFresh Program CF RRR CalWORKs Program CW SAR7 2nd CW RRR Example 2: CW BDA is February 2016 (Cycle 2) and RRR is January 2017. CF E/D household with earned income applies June 2016. Match CF cycle to CW cycle 2. (If CalWIN does not correctly align the cycle, a supervisor can change it.) Match CF SAR 7 at the 12 month to CW RRR. See chart below. Month 1st 2nd 3rd 4th 5th 6th 7th 8th 9th 10th 11th 12th CalFresh Program CF BDA CF SAR7 CF SAR7 CalWORKs Program CW BDA CW SAR7 1st CW RRR Month 13th 14th 15th 16th 17th 18th 19th 20th 21st 22nd 23rd 24th CalFresh Program CF SAR7 CF RRR CalWORKs Program CW SAR7 2nd CW RRR Example 3: CW BDA is February 2016 (Cycle 2) and RRR January 2017. Regular CF household applies May 2016. Match CF cycle to CW cycle 2. (If CalWIN does not correctly align the cycle, a supervisor can change it.) Match CF RRR to existing CW RRR. See chart below. Month 1st 2nd 3rd 4th 5th 6th 7th 8th 9th 10th 11th 12th CalFresh Program CF BDA CF SAR7 CF RRR CalWORKs Program CW BDA CW SAR7 CW RRR Expedited Services - Late Determination s Example: A customer consisting of a single mother with two children applies for CalFresh benefits on June 3rd. The application did not contain sufficient information to determine eligibility to Expedited Services. The customer is scheduled for a regular appointment on June 8. On the date of the interview, the HSS discovers that the customer is eligible to Expedited Services. The three-day time frame begins June 9th. Case comments must be entered to show that eligibility for Expedited Services was discovered on June 8 and that Expedited Services CalFresh was approved within three calendar days. Expedited Services – PACF Cases Example: An application was submitted on October 11 for CalWORKs and CalFresh with a request for ES. An appointment is scheduled for CalWORKs face-to-face interview on October 20. In order to meet the three days Expedited Services time frame requirement, a phone interview for Expedited Services is scheduled for October 12 before the face-to-face interview appointment. However, if the customer prefers a face to face interview, an appointment will be scheduled within three calendar days to process both programs. Expedited Services - Processing Procedures Customers who are unable to come into the office can request that the EBT and PIN number be mailed to them. Mailing time does not affect the Expedited Services 3-day timeframe. Example: A customer comes into the FRC office on Monday and submits a CalFresh application (day zero). They are determined eligible to Expedited Services given a phone interview appointment for Tuesday (day one). The customer is unable to come into the office Tuesday due to car trouble and requests that the EBT card and PIN be mailed. The HSS mails the EBT/PIN to the customer on Tuesday (day one). The Expedited Services Clock stops when the HSS mails the EBT/PIN to the customer. The customer received the EBT card on Thursday (day two) and the PIN on Friday (day three). The County has met the ES timeframe when both the EBT card and PIN number were put in the mail at the customer’s request. Household Cooperation Failure to Cooperate with QC (State / Federal Reviews) Example 1: (State Review) A household is discontinued on 5/31/19 for refusal to cooperate with a State QC review and never completes the review. The QC annual review period ends 9/30/19. Therefore, the household can reapply on or after 2/3/20, which is 125 days after 9/30/19. Example 2: (State Review) A household is discontinued on 10/31/18 for refusal to cooperate with a State QC review and never completes the review. The QC annual review period ends 9/30/19. The household can reapply on or after 2/3/20, which is 125 days after 9/30/12. Example 3: (Federal Review) A household is discontinued 4/30/19 for failure to cooperate with a Federal QC review and never completes the review. The QC annual review period ends 9/30/19. The household can reapply on or after 7/1/20, which is 9 months after 9/30/19. Non-Cooperating Household Member leaves the Household and joins another CalFresh Household Example: Household #1: A CalFresh household consists of a mother and father and their two children. The mother refuses to participate in the CalFresh QC review. The entire household is discontinued due to the mother’s noncooperation with the QC review. During the sanction period, the mother leaves the existing CalFresh Household (Household #1) and moves in with another CalFresh Household (Household #2). The mother is no longer part of Household #1. The remaining members of that household (father and two children) are eligible to reapply for CalFresh benefits without the need to wait until the end of the sanction period. Household #2 will be discontinued from the CalFresh program and will remain ineligible until the mother cooperates, leaves this household, or after the end of the sanction period. The Notice of Action must state the specific reason for the termination of benefits. Income Exclusions In-Kind Income Example: A CalFresh recipient receives reduced rent in exchange for managing and apartment building. His apartment would mormally rent for $900, but the recipient pays only $200. Exclude $700 as earned in-kind; allow $200 as rent deduction. Vendor Payments Example A friend or relative uses his or her own money to pay the household’s entire rent directly to the landlord. This is considered a vender Payment and is excluded. The household is not entitled to the shelter deduction. Monies Withheld to Pay an Overpayment Example 1 A CalFresh household recipient is eligible to receive $1,472 in Social Security Disability benefits. The recipient receives a net amount of $1, 251 because $220 is being deducted to repay an overpayment owed to Social Security Administration (SSA). Count the net amount of $1,251 because the overpayment is being collected to pay an overpayment from the same source, SSA. Example 2 Same situation as above except that the reduction of $220 is to repay an overpayment owed to the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). (The overpayment was due to noncompliance with VA requirements). Since a VA overpayment is being collected from a different source, Social Security, count the gross amount of Social Security benefits, $1,472. Contributions from People or Organizations EXAMPLE 1 An uncle gives $200 to the household to purchase new tires. The $200 is not considered income when the receipt for the expense verifies the contributor’s intended purpose for the contribution. If the uncle provides a written statement saying the $200 was given to buy tires this would be considered sufficient verification. EXAMPLE 2 A household member signed an affidavit and provided a statement from a friend indicating that she received $300 to pay a portion of the rent. The household also provided a rent receipt as verification that the rent of $700 has been paid in full. The household shall be allowed a deduction for the amount they paid toward the expense. In the scenario above the household spent only $400 of her own money to pay the rent. She would be able to claim $400 as a shelter deduction, not the entire $700. The contribution will not be counted as income if the household provides verification the money was used for the intended purpose. The verification can be a written statement from the contributor. Legally Obligated Child Support Payments Budgeting Example A household has $800 in total gross earned income and $200 in total unearned income. A member of the household pays $400 in courtordered child support per month. Treat the child support payment as follows: Step Description Computation 1 Deduct the child support $200 - $400 payment first from the unearned income =$0 ($200 remaining child support payment) 2 Determine the 20% earned income deduction $800-20% earned deduction =$640 in adjusted gross income 3 Deduct the remaining child support payment from the adjusted gross income from Step 2 $640 - $200 =$440 in gross earnings 4 Determine total income $440 earnings +$0 unearned income =$440 in total income IEVS Processing Timeframe Examples PVS are to be processed no later than 45 days from the run date. Example 1: A CalFresh case has an IEVS PVS with a 02/29 run date which is considered VUR. Per the PVS report, the customer receives SDI which will affect the budget but is not over IRT. The PVS was reviewed and processed on 03/28 and is considered timely for an IEVS report. If PVS would have been reviewed prior to ten day, VUR action would have been effective 04/01. Since the PVS was reviewed 03/28, the VUR action is effective 05/01. Because the IEVS report was processed timely, but not in time to provide the client with adequate 10 day notice for April; there will be no overissuance established for April. As everything in the process was done timely, there would be no QC error (ACL 12-25, page 77). Example 2: A CalFresh case has an IEVS PVS with a 02/29 run date. Per the PVS report, the customer receives SDI which will affect the budget and is over IRT. The case was over IRT effective January and the HH failed to report. The PVS was reviewed and processed on 03/28 and is considered timely for an IEVS report. The worker was able to determine that if the HH had reported timely, benefits would have been reduced effective March. Although the IEVS report was processed timely, it was a mandatory mid-period report for the HH and they failed to act. In this example, there will be an overissuance established for March and April. Example 3: An IEVS was ordered at application. IEVS report date 3/12/2018 in CalWIN. There was no discrepancy but the HSS did not update the Create IEVS Applicant Review Document. Should HSSs complete that screen whether or not there was a discrepancy? Answer: Yes. Search IEVS Applicant Reports should be completed as Processed, No Discrepancy. Overissuance s -Calculating Overissuance s Based on Customers Circumstance s When establishing a CalFresh overissuance, the overissuance amount is computed by determining the customer’s actual circumstances, including changes the customer failed to report. This includes decreases or increases in income. Example 1: A non-assistance CalFresh household applies for benefits in January and inaccurately reports that they have gross income of $500 per month (income is actually $900 per month). In March, the household stops working but does not report the loss of income to the CWD. In May an IEVS match reveals that the household actually had income of $900 for January, February, and March and the employment terminated in March. Answer: Since January, the household was issued benefits based on the reported income of $500 per month. The OI is calculated based on the income of $900 per month for the months in which the household received that income. Since the income stopped in March, the income should not be used in the calculation of benefits for April and May as no income was received in those months. No OI should be assessed for any months in which the household did not have earnings. Example 2: An IEVS match reveals that a customer failed to report income on the semi-annual report. How is the income counted if the income stops in the Data Month? Answer: In this scenario, because the Data Month income did not continue into the upcoming SAR Payment Period, there would be no OP. While all income received in the Data Month is required to be reported, in this scenario, even if the income had been reported correctly on the SAR 7 it would not have been used to calculate the benefits for the upcoming SAR Payment Period because the income was not anticipated to continue. Example 3: An IEVS match reveals that a customer failed to report income on the semi-annual report. The income continued for the first four months of the SAR Payment Period. How is the OP calculated? Answer: When the OP begins will depend on whether or not the income that should have been reported on the SAR 7 for the Data Month was over IRT. If the income from the Data Month was over the IRT, the OP should begin in the Submit Month and continue until the income ends. If the income was under the IRT, the OP should begin in the first month of the SAR Payment Period and continue until the income ends. ACL No. 15-95 Overissuance s - Establishing a Claim Examples of Establishing a Claim: Situation Outcome Claim for $250 is discovered on 2/13/20. HH was active on date of discovery. HH was set to be discontinued on 2/29/20. The claim must be established since the HH was active during the date of discovery and the claim exceeds the threshold for an active case. Residency - Homeless Households Example: County A reviews EBT usage indicating that a Homeless customer has been accessing their benefits in another state (or county) for 3 months. Try to call the customer to clarify if they are still a resident of San Diego County. If unable to reach the customer by phone, send a CF 387 Request for Information (RFI) to the last known address to determine if the customer has moved to another state or intends to return to County A. The last known address may be a county PO Box or other general delivery address. If the customer does not respond to the CF 387 Request for Information (RFI) within 10 days, the case must be discontinued. If the customer responds to the CF 387 Request for Information (RFI) within the 10-day time period, the county must evaluate the customers residency and determine if the case should be transferred, terminated, or if eligibility is to be maintained in the original county. Residency - ICT When a customer reports that they have moved to another county, the ICT process must be followed. Example: A customer reports that the entire household has moved from County A to County B. This is not a temporary absence. County A will need to initiate the ICT process. (ACL 11-22) Residency - Out of State Out- of- State refers to customers who are in a state other than their established state of residence for various reasons but may intend to return to their state of residence at some point. Example 1: County A reviews EBT usage indicating that a customer has been accessing their benefits in another state for 3 months. Call the customer to try to clarify their residency over the phone. If unable to reach the customer by phone, send a CF 387 Request for Information (RFI) to the last known address to determine if the customer has moved to the other state or intends to return to County A. The household responds stating that they are temporarily in another state caring for a sick relative, or fleeing domestic abuse, or any other reason, but intends to return to County A. As long as the household continues to meet its reporting requirements, County A shall keep the case active. However, if the household has not returned to County A within one year, the household will be considered to have changed its state of residency and must be discontinued. No notice of action is required. If the customer does not respond to the CF 387 Request for Information (RFI), the county should discontinue the case with 10 day notice for failure to respond to the CF 387 Request for Information (RFI). Example 2: County A reviews EBT usage indicating that a customer has been accessing their benefits in another state for 3 months. Call the customer to try to clarify their residency over the phone. If unable to reach the customer by phone, send a CF 387 Request for Information (RFI) to the last known address to determine if the customer has moved to the other state or intends to return to County A. If the customer does not respond to the CF 387 Request for Information (RFI), the county should discontinue the case with 10 day notice for failure to respond to the CF 387 Request for Information (RFI). Example 3: County A reviews EBT usage indicating that a customer has been accessing their benefits in another state for 3 months. The county must attempt to call the customer to clarify residency. If unable to reach the customer by phone, send a CF 387 Request for Information (RFI) to the last known address to request the needed information to clarify residency. The household responds that they are now living in another state. No notice of action is required. The household’s benefits shall be terminated for loss of residency or for having moved out of state. Residency - Persons applying in California who live in another state Example: A customer applies for CalFresh benefits in a California county. The customer discloses that they are visiting friends and will be staying for several months with an unknown return date. The customer is eligible for CalFresh, but states their residency is in Washington. The customer’s application must be denied. The customer should be told to apply in Washington. Residency - Temporary Absences Temporary absences refer to customers who are temporarily residing in another county for various reasons but intend to return to their initial county of residence. Example 1 A household lives in County A but the husband has been temporarily relocated in County B for three months for his job. He intends to return to County A once his job ends. In this example, the household maintains its residency in County A and the husband may use CalFresh benefits in County B. Example 2 County A reviews EBT usage and discovers that a household may be residing in County B. County A will call the customer to see if they are still a resident of San Diego County. If unable to reach the customer and clarify residency, send a CF 387 Request for Information (RFI) to the household’s last known address to request the needed information to clarify residency. If the household provides the requested information within the 10-day time frame confirming it is now residing in County B, County A should initiate an ICT. If the household responds that they are still a resident, County A should keep the case active. If the household does not respond, the household’s benefits shall be terminated at the end of the month in which a 10-day notice can be provided for failing to respond to the CF 387 Request for Information (RFI). Example 3 County A reviews EBT usage indicating that a customer has been accessing their benefits in another county for 3 months. The county must attempt to contact the customer by phone. If unable to reach the customer and clarify residency, send a CF 387 Request for Information (RFI) to the last known address to request the needed information to clarify residency. The household responds stating that it is temporarily in another county caring for a sick relative, or fleeing domestic abuse, or any other reason, but intends to return to County A. As long as the household continues to meet its reporting requirements, no ICT shall be sent and County A shall keep the case active. However, if the household has not returned to County A within one year, the household will be considered to have changed its county of residence and an ICT shall be initiated. If the customer does not respond to the CF 387 Request for Information (RFI), the County A should discontinue the case with 10 day notice for failure to respond to the CF 387 Request for Information (RFI). SAR 7 - Required Information If other reported information received while processing the SAR 7 indicates that the information was unknown by the customer until after the Data month, the change will be treated as a voluntary mid-period report. The following scenarios are examples of voluntary mid-period reports that may occur while processing a SAR 7. Example 1: Scenario: A customer submits a timely SAR 7 on June 8 (the Submit Month) that includes information about May (the Data Month) and all reasonably anticipated changes for the remaining six months of the certification period. On June 15, the customer calls the county and reports that her June income has increased and is higher than she anticipated on her SAR 7 and she anticipates that this income will continue at this amount for the rest of the semi-annual period. The income is not over IRT. Outcome: Because this information was unknown to the customer in the Data Month, the report of increased income will be considered a voluntary mid-period report and will not be acted on unless it results in an increase to her benefits. Example 2: Scenario: Same scenario as above, except when the customer makes the second report on June 15, she reports that her income actually increased in May (the Data Month). Outcome: Because this information should have been reported on her SAR 7, this is considered a correction to her previously incomplete SAR 7 report, and shall be considered in determining eligibility and benefit amounts for the remaining six months of the certification period. Example 3: Scenario: A customer submits a timely SAR 7 on June 5 (the Submit Month) and reports that their income decreased in May (the Data Month). Outcome: This information should be treated as a voluntary mid-period report of decreased income and a supplement should be provided for the month of June (the month the decrease was reported). This decreased income will also be used to calculate the customer’s benefit amount for the remaining six months of the certification period. Scholarship and Grants Determine Net Monthly Educational Income Example: A student receives a $1,500 private scholarship on October 10, 2015. The school year begins on September 7, 2015 and will end on June 3, 2016. The expenses are: • $200 for tuition • $300 for books and • $500 for dependent care Step Action 1 Obtain verification of student income and expenses 2 Determine the number of months the educational assistance and educational expenses are intended to cover: There are 10 months in the school year, September through June 3 Subtract the educational expenses from the educational assistance: $1,500 scholarship -$1,000 exempt expenses $500 net student income 4 Divide the net student income (step 3) by the number of months the educational assistance and educational expenses are intended to cover: $500 divided by 10 months=$50 month will be counted in the CalFresh budget for 10 months, September through June. Student Eligibility Example 1- Applicant who is a studentApplicant graduates from high school in June, enrolls in Community College on 08/17 and applies for CalFresh on 08/19. College classes begin on 08/30/12. The applicant would be considered a non-student from 08/19 through 08/29. On 08/30, the applicant would be considered a student and would have to meet “Student Eligibility requirements/ Criteria” to remain eligible. The case would be set up treating the applicant as a non-student for August and as a student in September. Example 2- Applicant who is a Non-continuing student: A 19 years old student applies for CalFresh on 06/05. He attends college half time in June. His school spring semester ends June 24. Student specifically stated that he wants to take a break from school and he does not intend to enroll for the following school term. In June the applicant would be considered a CalFresh student and would have to meet” Student Eligibility requirements/Criteria” to be determined eligible. The case would be set up treating the applicant as a student in June and non-student for upcoming months. Do not classify individuals as ineligible for CalFresh who do not intend to be enrolled in school for a future term. Time Limits and Delays Approval Actions Example: All CalFresh applications must be processed and approved, if otherwise eligible as soon as possible, but no later than the 30th day after the date of application. If the 30 th day falls on a weekend or holiday, the application must be approved prior to the 30th day. The 30th day falls on a weekend and Monday is a holiday; approve the case on Friday before the weekend and holiday. Application Pending for Other Programs Example: Do not delay granting a CalFresh application because information or verification pertaining only to other programs is still pending. CalWORKs may have pending items like a Project 100% investigation, child support questionnaire, birth certificates, or vehicle registration that does not affect CalFresh eligibility. Approve CalFresh if all required verification has been provided while the CalWORKs is pending verifications. Denial Actions Example 1: If the last day for a denial action falls on a Sunday or other holiday; take action on the next normal working day. The 30th day falls on a weekend and Monday is a holiday; deny the case on Tuesday after the weekend and holiday; do not deny the case prior to the 30th day. Example 2: If 30-day denial action falls on a weekend, the denial should be effective and dated the Monday following the weekend. Unearned Income Legally Obligated Payments Diverted to a Third Party: Examples: 1. A household receives court-ordered monthly support payments in the amount of $400. Later, $200 is diverted by the provider and paid directly to a creditor for a household expense. The entire payment is counted as income. 2. A court awards support payments in the amount of $400 a month and in addition orders $200 to be paid directly to a bank for repayment of a loan. The $400 payment is counted as income and the $200 payment is excluded income. sections.text: 63-1103 CalFresh Definitions and Examples Calculating Net Monthly Income of Households that Include and Elderly or Disabled Member The household consists of a mother, child and an elderly grandmother. The grandmother purchases and prepares meals with her daughter and grandchild. The total combined monthly unearned income is $2,121 (MCE household). The household pays $1,200 for rent and is entitled to the Standard Utility Allowance. The medical expenses are $235 per month, of which $200 is the medical deduction (the amount in excess of $35). The computation to determine benefits for the household is as follows: Step Action The household is exempt from the gross income test (130% of FPL) due to the elderly/disabled member 1 a.Add the total monthly unearned income of all household members that can be anticipated and b.Deduct the legal obligated child support paid ($2,121-$0): $2,121 2 a.Add the total gross earned income of all household members that can be anticipated: b.Subtract the earned income deduction (20%) and c.Deduct any remaining legal obligated child support paid $0 3 Adjusted Gross Income Add total unearned income plus the adjusted gross earned income (Step 1 + Step 2) [$2,121+$0] $2,121 4 Adjusted Net Income From the total adjusted gross income (Step 3) subtract: $2,121 a.The standard deduction: - $167 b.The excess medical expense [$235- $35=$200]: - $200 c.The monthly dependent care cost: - $0 d.The homeless shelter deduction: - $0 Adjusted Net Income: $1,754 Shelter Deduction Computation Rent: $1,200 SUA: + $397 a. Total Shelter Cost: $1,597 b. 50% of Adjusted Net Income ($1,754/2) = $877 c. Subtract from the total shelter cost 50% of Adjusted Net Income (5a – 5b) $1,597 - $877 5 d. Allowable shelter deduction: $720 Net Income Computation $1,754 - $720 Subtract the shelter cost from the adjusted net income: $1,034 The shelter deduction is not limited to the Maximum Shelter Deduction for households with elderly or disabled members, 6 Net Income: $1,034 7 Do not compute the Net Income Test because the household is MCE Refer to 63-254.6 to determine the household’s allotment CalFresh Allotment Computation Step Action 1 The total net income of a household of four (4) is $725 2 The maximum allotment for a household size of 4 (as of October 2019) is $646 3 Multiply the net monthly by 30%: $725 x 30%=$217.5 rounded up to $218 4 Subtract the amount in #3 above ($218) from the maximum allotment for a household size of 4 ($646): $646 - $218 = $428 Determining Allotment Level EXAMPLE: A CalFresh household of 4 has a net monthly income of $725. Under the “Monthly Net Income” column in the CalFresh Allotment Table ( 63- 1101.5) in page 7, find row “724 - 726.” The CalFresh allotment for 4 persons is $422. See “How to Use the CalFresh Allotment Tables” desk aid. Disabled Household Member A disabled CalFresh household member is a member of a household who is at least one of the following: •Receives disability retirement benefits from a governmental agency because of a disability considered permanent under Section 221(i) of the Social Security Act; or •Receives interim assistance benefits pending receipt of SSI, provided that the eligibility to receive those benefits is based upon disability or blindness criteria, which are at least as stringent as those used under Title XVI of the Social Security Act; or •Receives disability-related medical assistance under Title XIX (Medi-Cal) of the Social Security act; or •Receives disability-based general assistance benefits, provided that the eligibility to receive those benefits is based upon disability or blindness criteria which are at least as stringent as those used under Title XVI of the Social Security Act; or •Is a veteran: oWith a service-connected, or non-service-connected disability rated by the Veteran's Administration (VA) as total or paid as total by the VA under Title 38 of the United States Code; or oConsidered by the VA to be in need of regular aid and attendance or permanen

title: 63-113 Authorized Representatives
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageAuthorized Representatives 63-113 1 of 2 Revision Date: 03/01/2023 Background: Customers may choose an adult non-household member as an Authorized Representative (AR) to act on their behalf. Purpose: This section provides guidance on AR requirements. This section is being revised to incorporate AR information for Drug/Alcohol Treatment Centers (D/ATC) and Group Living Arrangements (GLA). Policy: The AR is designated by the customer to act on their behalf in any of the following situations: •Complete the application and recertification process •Obtain and use the Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card •Complete required reporting (such as mid-period reporting, SAR7, voluntary reporting) •Complete any required forms 1. Designation of an AR: Designation of the AR may be made in one of three ways: •On the application or recertification form itself •Using a CalFresh AR designation form •A written statement signed by the customer Household’s (HH’s) may select an AR anytime during the certification period. Multiple ARs may be chosen to fulfill distinct roles and responsibilities. For example, the AR designated to apply for the HH may be different from the AR chosen to use the EBT card. The designation of the AR will remain in effect for the duration of the certification period, unless the HH chooses to change the AR. An AR must be an individual and cannot be an organization or agency. Customers seeking assistance from Community-Based Organizations (CBO), agencies, residential facilities or other similar institutions must designate an individual employee of that facility as the AR. The AR must have sufficient knowledge of the customers circumstances to complete the application and/or recertification process. Customers must be informed that the HH will be responsible for any overissuance (OI) that results from incorrect information given by the AR. An AR may represent more than one HH. The following table provides guidance on AR designations for special HH situations: HH Situation AR Designation Customer has a Social Security Representative Payee The representative payee can act as AR, but the HH must designate the representative payee as the AR. AR provides documents such as Power of Attorney, conservatorship, or guardianship The documents may be used to authorize a third party to act as AR. Once it has been determined that the third party has the authority to act on behalf of the customer, the third party is not required to be designated as an AR. Customer resides at a Drug/Alcohol Treatment and Rehabilitation Centers The resident must use an AR who is employed and designated by the D/ATC to apply, obtain, and use County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageAuthorized Representatives 63-113 2 of 2 (D/ATC) benefits. The AR must be an employee of the D/ATC and cannot be an organization or institution. Customer resides at a Group Living Arrangement (GLA) The resident has the option to apply on their own behalf, through an AR of their choice or an AR employed and designated by the GLA. If the resident uses an AR designated by the GLA, the AR must be an employee of the GLA and cannot be an organization or institution. Note: Refer to 63-123 Residents of Drug/Alcohol Treatment and Rehabilitation Centers (D/ATC) and Group Living Arrangements (GLA) for guidance on D/ATC and GLA requirements. 2. Verification of AR: The identity of both the AR and the customer must be verified and imaged at intake, recertification and whenever a new AR is appointed. D/ATC and GLA must provide a written statement on the center’s letterhead designating the AR and provide the identity of the AR. 3. Restrictions on AR Designations: The following individuals cannot be designated as AR’s: •Employees involved in the eligibility determination process or retailers who are authorized to accept CalFresh benefits. If no one else can act as AR, a request must be sent to the CalFresh Program Manager for approval of the individual to be designated as AR. •Individuals disqualified for an Intentional Program Violation (IPV) cannot act as an AR during the disqualification periods. If no one else can act as AR, a request must be sent to the CalFresh Program Manager for approval of the individual to be designated as AR. •Employees of homeless meal service providers, such as soup kitchens or shelters, that are authorized to accept CalFresh benefits. •An AR that has been disqualified for knowingly providing false information about HH circumstances or improper use of EBT benefits cannot act as an AR during the disqualification period. 4. Emergency AR Designation: HH’s can designate an emergency AR to obtain benefits and purchase food for a specific month. The designation must be made using the CalFresh AR designation form or a written statement signed by the customer and AR. References: ACL 19-55, MPP 63-402, MPP 63-503, ACIN I-08-18 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 03/31/2026. Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-115 Interview Requirements
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageInterview Requirements 63-115 1 of 2 Revision: 08/01/2020 Background: Customers applying or reapplying for CalFresh must be interviewed prior to initial certification and recertification. There are no changes due to State legislation, this section is being re-formatted after sunset review. Purpose: This section describes the policies for the interview process. Policy: An interview must be completed at initial certification and at least once every 12 months thereafter. An interview must be completed by phone unless the customer is unable to do so or request otherwise. The interview must be completed with the head of household, their spouse, a designated Authorized Representative (AR) or another responsible household member. Customers can ask any person they choose to attend the interview. Confidentiality guidelines must be preserved when interviewing the customer. Note: Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) cases will require an interview at initial certification. The recertification interview requirements for ESAP cases are outlined in CFPG 63-360. 1. Interview Requirements: A review of the application to determine if the information is consistent with what has been reported or is known to the county must be completed to assist staff with the interview. During the interview staff must explore, clarify, and resolve any unclear or inconsistent information with the customer. Customers must also be informed of the Rights & Responsibilities, and reporting requirements, including how to complete the SAR 7. When there are pending verifications, staff must explain why the verifications are needed and offer assistance in obtaining them. Provide the customer with a printed copy of the Statement of Facts for their records. Case Comments must be entered detailing all the information obtained and shared during the interview. 2. Face-to-Face or Home Visit Interviews: Customers that do not have a phone, are unable to come into the office due to a hardship or prefer to not to complete the interview by phone may be scheduled for a face-to-face or home visit interview. The reason for face-to-face or home visit interview must be documented in case comments. 3. Language Needs: Non-English-speaking customers must be informed of their right to have an interpreter, and when available, must receive the forms in the customers preferred language. The “Language Needs” form is required for all cases, regardless of the customer’s language. Refer to the Civil Rights Eligibility Policy and Procedures Guide for information on providing services to non-English speaking customers and customers with disabilities. 4. Missed Interview: When a customer misses their scheduled interview, a Notice of Missed Interview (NOMI) must be sent. The NOMI informs the customer that they need to reschedule the interview. When the customer does not reschedule the interview, or reschedules and fails to attend subsequent interviews, the County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageInterview Requirements 63-115 2 of 2 application will be denied on the 30 th day. The customer will be mailed the Notice of Action (NOA) “Notice of Denial of Pending Status” on or after the 30 th day following the date of application. Customers who reschedule and fail to attend subsequent interviews will not be mailed additional NOMI’s. When a customer contacts the county and the county fails to reschedule the initial interview within 30 days of the date the application was filed, it will be considered county caused delay. Refer to 63-109 for policies regarding time limits and delays in application processing. Other Program Impacts: None References: ACL 09-62 MPP 63-300.4 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 08/31/2023 Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Eligibility Operations

title: 63-117 Verification and Documentation
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Verification and Documentation 63-117 1 of 5 Revision Date: 09/01/2021 Background: Verification is the use of third-party information or documentation to establish the accuracy of statements on the application. Purpose: This section details mandatory and optional verifications for CalFresh and the different ways to verify. Policy: The household has primary responsibility for providing required verification and to resolve any questionable information. Before requesting additional verifications from the household, the Human Services Specialist (HSS) is to attempt verification via electronic means such as Income Eligibility Verification System (IEVS), Payment Verification System (PVS), Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS) and the Work Number (WN). If unable to verify or information is questionable, send a request for information to the household. Do not limit verification to any single type of document. Assist customers in obtaining required verifications as needed. Use a collateral contact or home visit if necessary. Households or the Authorized Representative may provide verification in person, through the mail, online, fax, or email. Any reasonable verification provided by the household will be accepted and used to verify the statements given on the application. Issue receipts to CalFresh applicants and recipients when they submit verifications in-person at the office. When documents are submitted other than in person, a receipt is not required. 1. Questionable Information: For information to be considered questionable, the information on the application must be inconsistent with statements made by the applicant, with other information on the application or previous applications, or with information received by the County. When determining if information is questionable, base the decision on the household's individual circumstances. For example, a report of expenses exceeding the household’s income prior to deductions may be grounds to request verification or additional verification. A household reporting no income while still managing their financial affairs could justify the need for an additional verification request. These circumstances, however, will not be grounds for an immediate denial or discontinuance. Instead, explore with the household how they are managing their finances, whether the household receives excluded income or has resources, and how long the household has managed under these circumstances. When verification is required to resolve questionable information, the HSS must document in case comments: •Why the information is considered questionable, or at a minimum indicate where in the case the inconsistency exists •What documentation was used to resolve the questionable information (if it is resolved) and if applicable, the reason why an alternate source of verification such as a collateral contact or home visit was needed County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Verification and Documentation 63-117 2 of 5 2. Mandatory Verifications: Verification must be obtained in these categories if it is applicable to the household. •Gross Non-Exempt Income: Determine the amount to be used for certification purposes based on the best available information. Households must provide information about income received during the 30 days prior to submission of their application or recertification. For recertifications, staff must verify a change in income if one of the following circumstances occur: the source has changed, the amount has changed by more than $50, or if the information is incomplete, inaccurate, inconsistent, or outdated (See 63-220 and 63-304). •Non-Citizen Eligibility: Verify the immigration status of those non-citizens who are applying for CalFresh benefits. See Processing Guide 117-02 for additional information regarding non-citizen eligibility. •Identity: See 63-152 for information regarding identity. See the Verification Requirements Chart for additional information. •Social Security Numbers (SSN): Households must provide the SSN of each member or provide verification of application for an SSN prior to certification. If individuals have more than one SSN, all numbers are required. See 63-161 for additional SSN information. •Residency: Verification of residency in the County of San Diego will be accomplished to the extent possible using the verification of other information such as, identity or as a last resort the customer’s statement on the Statement of Facts (SOF). See 63-152 for additional residency information. 3. Mandatory Verifications That Do Not Impact Eligibility: Verifications obtained in these categories do not impact eligibility, however, they do impact benefit allotment amount. Failure to provide the verification is not a basis for denying or discontinuing a case if the person is otherwise eligible. If verification is not provided, the expense, exemption, or exclusion is not allowed. •Medical Expenses: Prior to allowing the Excess Medical Deduction or Standard Medical Deduction (SMD), verify the amount of medical expenses that are deductible as listed in 63-232. •Disability: Receipt of any of the benefits listed below qualifies as verification of disability:. oSocial Security Disability Benefits oDisability Retirement Benefits oDisability Related Medi-Cal Assistance - Verify through county records that the individual receives disability based Medi-Cal as determined by the State Program Disability Determination Service Division (DDSD). oVeteran Related Disabilities oRailroad Retirement •Student Exemption: A customer’s statement is sufficient evidence that a student meets one of the exemptions unless the information provided is questionable or when a student’s claim of physical or mental unfitness is not evident. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Verification and Documentation 63-117 3 of 5 •Legally Obligated Child Support and Actual Payments: Verify child support or obtain payment information from the Local Child Support Agency (LCSA) automated data files if the data is available. Once the verification is received, the circumstances need not be verified again unless there is a change in the legal obligation or an increase in the amount of the payment. See 63-224 for additional child support payments exclusion information. 4. Optional Verifications: Below is a list of items that fall under optional verifications. Optional verifications are non-mandated and must only be requested if relevant information is questionable. Request optional verifications for the purposes of maximizing benefits, however they must be marked as “optional” on the request. Failure to provide verification of optional verifications must not result in a denial or discontinuance or cause a delay in the determination of eligibility. •Dependent Care Costs: Dependent care costs can be verified through an affidavit on the application, the Dependent Care Cost Affidavit or other affidavit. The household must specify under penalty of perjury on the affidavit: oThe name of the provider oThe total amount billed oThe amount of out-of-pocket expenses oThe amount of any subsidies Once verified, the expense will not be verified again unless the provider has changed, the amount has changed (which could affect the amount of the deduction) or the expense is questionable. See 63-233 for additional information regarding dependent care costs. •Liquid Resources and Loans: A legally binding agreement is not required. A simple statement signed by both parties indicating the payment is a loan that must be repaid, is sufficient for verification. If the household receives payments on a recurring or regular basis from the same source, but claims the payments are loans, request a statement or affidavit from the provider of the loan stating repayments are being made, or that the payments will be made in accordance with an established repayment schedule. See 63-200 for additional information regarding resources. Note: The resources of Categorically Eligible (CE) and Modified Categorical Eligible (MCE) households will not be evaluated. See 63-201 and 63-120 for additional information regarding CE and MCE. •Household Size/ Composition: If separate household status is questionable, individuals who claim to be a separate household from those with whom they reside will be responsible for proving that they are a separate household. See 63-101 for additional information. •Standard Utility Allowance (SUA): Accept the customer’s written or verbal statement as verification. See 63-236 for additional information regarding the SUA and the Standard Utility Assistance Subsidy (SUAS). •Rent/Mortgage Expense: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Verification and Documentation 63-117 4 of 5 A narrative entry of the amount claimed is required. Accept and document any verification of shelter costs voluntarily provided by the household. See 63-235 for additional information regarding shelter deductions. Reminder: Shelter expense changes reported mid-period are considered verified upon receipt (VUR). See 63-284 for additional information on VUR. •Citizenship – Acceptable forms of verification include: oBirth certificates, religious records oCertificates of citizenship N-560 or its replacement N-561 (for Acquired/Derivative Citizenship) oAn “Application for Certification of Naturalization” form N-600 for a child or form N-643 for an adopted child provided by United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) oA United States (U.S.) passport If the above forms of verification cannot be obtained, accept a signed statement from someone who is a U.S. citizen declaring, under penalty of perjury, that the person in question is a U.S. citizen. The signed statement will contain a warning of the penalties for helping someone commit an intentional program violation. See 63-153 for information regarding citizenship. The member whose citizenship is in question will be ineligible to participate until proof of U.S. citizenship is obtained and will have his/her income and resources treated as an ineligible noncitizen. (See 63.244) •Voluntary Quit and Reduction of Work Effort – Acceptable sources of verification include, but are not limited to: oThe previous employer oEmployee associations oUnion representatives oGrievance committees or organizations The household will not be denied CalFresh, if they are unable to obtain the requested verification from these or other sources because the reason for the quit was from circumstances that for good reason cannot be verified, such as: oA resignation from employment due to discrimination practices oUnreasonable demands by an employer oThe employer cannot be located References: 7 CFR 273.2 MPP 300.5 All County Letters (ACL) 13-102, 14-54, 14-66, 14-100, 17-98, 19-86, 20-48, 20-135 and 21-24 All County Information Notices (ACIN) I-10-04, I-45-11 and I-45-11E Processing Guides 117-01 & 117-02 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 09/30/2024. Approval for Release: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Verification and Documentation 63-117 5 of 5 RICK WANNE, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-118 Income and Eligibility Verification System
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Income and Eligibility Verification System Number Page 63-118 1 of 2 Revision Date: 07/01/2026 Background: The Income and Eligibility Verification System ( IEVS) is a computerized information system that performs data matches against several state and federal agency databases to verify certain types of income and/or property. The IEVS system consists of the following data matches: • Applicant IEVS (A-IEVS) • Recipient IEVS (R-IEVS) o Beneficiary Earnings Exchange Record (BEER) o Franchise Tax Board (FTB) o Integrated Fraud Detection (IFD)/Earning Clearance System (ECS) Match o Internal Revenue Service (IRS) Asset Match System o Payment Verification System (PVS) o California Youth Authority (CYA) o Deceased Persons Match (DPM) o Fleeing Felon Match (FFM) o New Hire Registry (NHR) o Nationwide Prisoner Match (NPM) o California (CA) Lottery Match P urpose: This section describes the IEVS system , and how it is used in the CalFresh eligibility determination. This section is being updated to include information about the California Lottery Match. P olicy: All IEVS data matches listed above except for PVS, IRS, IFD, and BEER must be processed at application and recertification. IRS, IFD, BEER, and CA Lottery matches are processed by Quality & Eligibility Support Department (QESD) staff. PVS matches contain information that is considered Verified Upon Receipt (VUR) and must be processed upon receipt. W hen processing matches staff must compare the information to the case record to assist with the determination of eligibility and benefit levels . A-IEVS data must be requested no later than five days after the initial interview and at least 15 days prior to the recertification interview. If the IEVS data is received during the application process, the information must be used in determining eligibility. The granting of benefits must not be delayed waiting for the IEVS data when other information establishes eligibility. T he following resources are available to assist with the processing of IEVS matches: • IEVS Processing Guide 118-01 • Eligibility Policy and Procedures Guide (EPPG) The Work Number (TWN) 1. T imely Processing of IEVS Potential discrepancies are considered “Discovered/Identified” on the “run date” or “date of receipt” of the IEVS match, whichever is later. Follow up on IEVS data must be completed within 45 days from the date the data is received, except for CYA, DPM, FFM, and NPM matches . If a potential County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Income and Eligibility Verification System Number Page 63-118 2 of 2 discrepancy exists, a request for information must be mailed to the customer within 45 days of receipt of the IEVS match, to meet timely processing requirements. R-I EVS matches received on closed cases must be processed within 12 months from the run date or the date of receipt, whichever is later. Any R -IEVS match received on a closed case beyond 12 months must be dispositioned as no impact. All actions taken must be documented in the case record. 2. V erification All IEVS information must be independently verified before any case action can be taken except for the PVS data match and CA Lottery Winnings, which are considered VUR. Customers must be given the first opportunity to verify the discrepancy. If necessary, assist the customer to obtain the required information. If the household fails or refuses to respond with sufficient information to clear the discrepancy, an appropriate third- party payroll source such as TWN must be used to resolve IEVS discrepancies. Third-party payroll sources such as TWN, will be considered appropriate income sources for the purpose of verifying IEVS discrepancies. If the employer is not associated with a third-party payroll source, then the employer must be contacted. I f an appropriate third -party payroll source such as T WN provides information beyond what was reported in an IEVS match showing a missed mandatory report over Income Reporting Threshold (IRT), an attempt must be made to verify the discrepancy by sending a verification letter to the household. If the household fails or refuses to respond with sufficient information to clear the discrepancy, the income reported by TWN/Third-party payroll source will be considered as verified and will be used to determine eligibility. Any o verissuance ( OI) must be assessed based on mandatory reporting rules for the months the customer failed to report income over their IRT. If TWN/Third-party payroll source shows current income, determine if the income affects current benefit levels. R eferences: Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 20-006 All County Letter (ACL) 17-41, 18-22, 19-52, 19-78, 21-16, 24-29, 24-29E, 26-05 All County Welfare Directors Letter (ACWDL) dated 12/28/18 S unset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 06/30/2029. A pproval for Release: A lberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services
