title: 63-120 Categorical Eligibility
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Categorical Eligibility 63-120 1 of 5 Revision Date 06/01/2019 Background: Household in which all eligible members receive Public Assistance (PA) benefits shall be considered categorically eligible (CE) for CalFresh benefits because of their status as PA recipients. This section is being revised to reflect the change in regulation as a result of the reversal of the SSI/SSP cash-out policy. Effective June 1, 2019, individuals receiving SSI/SSP are eligible for CalFresh, provided they meet all other eligibility requirements. Households in which all members receive or are authorized to receive SSI/SSP benefits are categorically eligible for CalFresh. Federal Nutrition Services (FNS) identifies three types of Categorical Eligibility (CE): Traditional Categorical Eligibility (CE) Traditional CE refers to the mandatory policy that makes households eligible for CalFresh benefits because the household receives cash benefits such as Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), CalWORKs in California, or General Relief (GR). Modified Categorical Eligibility (MCE) or Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility (BBCE) MCE/BBCE refers to the policy that makes most households categorically eligible for CalFresh because they receive a non-cash TANF/MOE-funded benefit or service, such as PUB 275 in California. MCE is only intended to exempt resources for households who meet all other conditions of eligibility. Narrow Categorical Eligibility This refers to the policy that makes a smaller number of households eligible through the receipt of a TANF/MOE-funded service such as childcare or counseling. Note: Non-Assistance CalFresh (NACF) does not include cases within this category. Purpose: This section describes the regulations and eligibility requirements for CE. Policy: 63-120.1 Categorical Eligibility (CE): A household will be considered (traditional) Categorical Eligible (CE) when ALL CalFresh eligible members receive or are authorized to receive cash aid through a Public Assistance (PA) program funded in full or in part with federal money under Title IV-A or with state money counted for maintenance of effort (MOE) purposes under Title IV-A. The following cash aid customers are considered CE: •CalWORKs recipients (Immediate Need payments are also considered a PA benefit) •State funded CalWORKs in which household members have reached their federal TANF time limit. These households will continue to receive benefits that are means-tested and primarily TANF MOE-funded •CalWORKs Diversion payments •Tribal TANF •General Relief (GR) •SSI/SSP ACIN I-34-05; I-16-05 and I-18-07 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Categorical Eligibility 63-120 2 of 5 The inclusion of the following household members does not affect CE status: •Ineligible noncitizens •Ineligible students •SSN disqualified persons •People institutionalized in an unauthorized facility •A household member who is disqualified for failure to comply with CalWORKs Welfare to Work requirements and CalFresh Employment and Training requirements ACIN I-34-99 CE is not affected when the household is authorized to receive CalWORKs or GR benefits. This includes households whose: •Cash overpayment adjustment results in the issuance of zero PA benefits •GR benefits have been suspended or recouped, or those who are entitled to GR benefits but are not paid such benefits because the grant is below the minimum payable under the GR program •PA benefits have been suspended, or those who are entitled to PA benefits but are not paid such benefits because the grant is less than $10.00 MPP 63-102(p)(12)(a) •If a household member loses both CalWORKs and CalFresh eligibility, the remaining household members’ CE status is not affected. The disqualification of a CalFresh household member does not affect the eligibility of an otherwise eligible CE household ACIN 1-34-99 63-120.2 Non-Categorically Eligible Households: The following households are not considered CE and are subject to all CalFresh eligibility regulations: •Households in which an adult(s) has/have timed out of both the federal Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program and the state CalWORKs program •Mixed households (63-302.3) •A household with disqualified members (Intentional Program Violation (IPV), fleeing felons, probation parole violators) ACIN I-58-08; ACL 98-19 •A household with any member(s) receiving or authorized to receive state-funded California Food Assistance Program (CFAP) •CalWORKs’ family reunification parents. These individuals are not CE for CalFresh benefits because they are not receiving or authorized to receive cash benefits •A household with ineligible members under the striker provisions (63-101.12) 63-120.3 Categorical Eligibility (CE) Verification Requirements: CE means being considered eligible for CalFresh because of the household’s eligibility for CalWORKs or GR benefits. CE only relates to federal SNAP eligibility. The following items will be verified for the Public Assistance (PA) programs and will not need to be reverified for CalFresh program, unless questionable. •Resources •Gross and net income limits (income tests) •Social Security Number information County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Categorical Eligibility 63-120 3 of 5 •Sponsored noncitizen information •Residence ACIN I-79-03 Use the following criteria when determining if a household is categorically eligible. If the household: •Contains only CalFresh eligible members that are PA recipients •Meets the definition of a household as specified in 63-101 •Includes all persons who purchase and prepare food together in one CalFresh household regardless of whether they are separate units for PA purposes •Has not been disqualified or does not include persons who have been disqualified IPV or fleeing felons ACIN I-58-08. 63-120.4 Categorically Eligible General Relief (GR) Households: Any household in which all CalFresh eligible members receive or are authorized to receive GR benefits are considered eligible for CalFresh because of their status as GR recipients. The eligibility factors that are acceptable for CalFresh eligibility without verification are: •Gross and net income limits •Resources •Sponsored noncitizen information •Residency A household is not considered CE when: •The household refuses to cooperate in providing information that is necessary for making an eligibility determination or for completing any subsequent eligibility review •The household is disqualified because the head of household fails to comply with a work requirement •A household who is ineligible under the striker provisions •A household knowingly transferred resources for the purpose of qualifying or attempting to qualify for assistance The following individuals are not included as a member of an otherwise CE household: •Disqualified for an Intentional Program Violation •Not the head of household and disqualified for failure to comply with the work requirements as specified in 63-900 •Disqualified for failing to provide the Social Security Number •Ineligible noncitizen •Ineligible student •Institutionalized in a nonexempt facility as specified in 63-123 Note: Advise all GR applicant households of the potential eligibility for CalFresh benefits and provide them with the CalFresh application form CF 285 or SAWS 2 Plus. The MCE evaluation must be documented for Quality Control purposes. Expedited Services •Refer to 63-105 MCE Households •Households with gross income at or below 200% of FPL •Households that do not include any of the following individuals: oA member who has been disqualified for an IPV oA head of household who has failed to comply with work requirements Procedure: Refer to CalFresh Processing Guide #120-01 Determining the Allotment for an MCE Household: MCE households consisting of: One or two members are entitled to at least the minimum allotment even if their net income exceeds the Maximum Net Income limit. Three or more members will receive an allotment according to the household size as determined by the CalFresh Allotment Table. •If the minimum allotment determined by the CalFresh Allotment Table is zero, deny the application or discontinue the case for exceeding the net income limit. See the “How to Use the CalFresh Allotment Table Desk Aid.” •If the allotment amount is less than $10 or is $0 in the month of application due to proration, but the household is eligible to receive ongoing benefits, approve the application without issuing benefits for the application month. sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Categorical Eligibility 63-120 1 of 5 Revision Date 06/01/2019 Background: Household in which all eligible members receive Public Assistance (PA) benefits shall be considered categorically eligible (CE) for CalFresh benefits because of their status as PA recipients. This section is being revised to reflect the change in regulation as a result of the reversal of the SSI/SSP cash-out policy. Effective June 1, 2019, individuals receiving SSI/SSP are eligible for CalFresh, provided they meet all other eligibility requirements. Households in which all members receive or are authorized to receive SSI/SSP benefits are categorically eligible for CalFresh. Federal Nutrition Services (FNS) identifies three types of Categorical Eligibility (CE): Traditional Categorical Eligibility (CE) Traditional CE refers to the mandatory policy that makes households eligible for CalFresh benefits because the household receives cash benefits such as Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), CalWORKs in California, or General Relief (GR). Modified Categorical Eligibility (MCE) or Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility (BBCE) MCE/BBCE refers to the policy that makes most households categorically eligible for CalFresh because they receive a non-cash TANF/MOE-funded benefit or service, such as PUB 275 in California. MCE is only intended to exempt resources for households who meet all other conditions of eligibility. Narrow Categorical Eligibility This refers to the policy that makes a smaller number of households eligible through the receipt of a TANF/MOE-funded service such as childcare or counseling. Note: Non-Assistance CalFresh (NACF) does not include cases within this category. Purpose: This section describes the regulations and eligibility requirements for CE. Policy: 63-120.1 Categorical Eligibility (CE): A household will be considered (traditional) Categorical Eligible (CE) when ALL CalFresh eligible members receive or are authorized to receive cash aid through a Public Assistance (PA) program funded in full or in part with federal money under Title IV-A or with state money counted for maintenance of effort (MOE) purposes under Title IV-A. The following cash aid customers are considered CE: •CalWORKs recipients (Immediate Need payments are also considered a PA benefit) •State funded CalWORKs in which household members have reached their federal TANF time limit. These households will continue to receive benefits that are means-tested and primarily TANF MOE-funded •CalWORKs Diversion payments •Tribal TANF •General Relief (GR) •SSI/SSP ACIN I-34-05; I-16-05 and I-18-07 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Categorical Eligibility 63-120 2 of 5 The inclusion of the following household members does not affect CE status: •Ineligible noncitizens •Ineligible students •SSN disqualified persons •People institutionalized in an unauthorized facility •A household member who is disqualified for failure to comply with CalWORKs Welfare to Work requirements and CalFresh Employment and Training requirements ACIN I-34-99 CE is not affected when the household is authorized to receive CalWORKs or GR benefits. This includes households whose: •Cash overpayment adjustment results in the issuance of zero PA benefits •GR benefits have been suspended or recouped, or those who are entitled to GR benefits but are not paid such benefits because the grant is below the minimum payable under the GR program •PA benefits have been suspended, or those who are entitled to PA benefits but are not paid such benefits because the grant is less than $10.00 MPP 63-102(p)(12)(a) •If a household member loses both CalWORKs and CalFresh eligibility, the remaining household members’ CE status is not affected. The disqualification of a CalFresh household member does not affect the eligibility of an otherwise eligible CE household ACIN 1-34-99

title: 63-121 Denial Withdrawal Granting
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Denial, Withdrawal, and Granting Number Page 63-121 1 of 2 Revision Date: 03/01/2025 Background: All CalFresh applications must be dispositioned within certain timeframes to meet timely processing guidelines. Purpose: This s ection provides guidance on denials, withdrawals and granting cases . The section is being revised to include clarification of benefits issuance for households (HHs) who apply and are granted after the 15th of the month. Policy: 1. Denial Deny CalFresh applications as follows: If the denial is due to… then deny the case… failure to complete the intake interview, on the 30th day failure to provide verifications, on the 30th day. If the Verification Check List (VCL) due date is after the 30th day, allow customer the date on the VCL. the HH is not meeting eligibility requirements or refusal to cooperate with the application process, as soon as possible but no later then the 30th day. Note: Refer to CalFresh Program Guide ( CFPG) 63-109 Time Limits and Delays for situations regarding delayed actions. Send a denial Notice of Action (NOA) to the HH as soon as it is determined that a denial action is appropriate. Refer to CFPG 63- 303 Notice of Action for more information. The NOA must be in the HH’s primary language when the notice is made available by the California Department of Social Services (CDSS) and must state, in easy-to-understand language the: • Denial reason. • HH’s right to request a state hearing. • Title of the state regulation on which the denial is based. • Availability to free legal representation. • Phone number to call for additional information. 2. Withdrawal Applications cannot be withdrawn after eligibility has been determined. HHs may voluntarily withdraw an application any time prior to the determination of eligibility. A withdrawal can only be initiated by the HH. Do not advise or suggest that the customer withdraw an application. When a HH withdraws an application: • Attempt to contact the HH and d ocument that contact was made (or attempted) to confirm the withdrawal. • Document the reason for the withdrawal, if any was stated by the HH. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Denial, Withdrawal, and Granting Number Page 63-121 2 of 2 • Advise the HH of their right to reapply at any time. • Send Notice of Withdrawn Application (CW 10). 3. Granting Grant and issue CalFresh benefits as soon as possible after eligibility is determined. Granting and issuance must follow the regulations and timelines specified in CFPG 63- 105 Expedited Services and CFPG 63-109 Time Limits and Delays. HHs that apply for benefits after the 15 th of the month and are found eligible will receive benefits for the initial and the subsequent month of aid on the same day. Once eligibility is determined and approved, send a NOA informing the HH the: • Application is approved. • Certification period. • Benefit allotment. • Right to a fair hearing. If application processing is delayed beyond 30 days due the fault of the HH, prorate the CalFresh benefit amount from the date the HH submits all required verifications. Note: HHs are to be provided a copy of the Statement of Facts (SOF) and Statement of Facts Notification (09-105 HHSA) when the interview is complete. References: Manual Policies and Procedures (MPP) 63-300.3, 63-301.2, 63-301.3, 63-301.546 All County Information Notices (ACIN) I-08-03, I-48-03 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 02/29/2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-123 Residents of Drug Alcohol Treatment Center and Group Living Arrangement
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Residents of Drug/Alcohol Treatment Centers (D/ATC) and Group Living Arrangements (GLA) Number Page 63-123 1 of 3 Revision Date: 03/01/2023 Background: Drug/Alcohol Treatment Centers (D/ATC) and Group Living Arrangements (GLA) must follow specific regulations to be eligible to apply and receive CalFresh benefits for their residents. Purpose: This section describes the regulations and requirements that D/ATC and GLA must follow to apply and receive CalFresh benefits for residents who live in their center s. This section is being updated to incorporate the California Department of Social Services (CDSS) GLA website into the program material. Policy: 1. D/ATC Facilities: D/ATC must be authorized by Food and Nutrition Service ( FNS) as a retailer or meet the definition of a drug addiction or alcoholic treatment program and provide meals to residents to be an authorized D/ATC facility. Residents who participate and reside in authorized D/ATC must apply for CalFresh through an Authorized Representative (AR) that is employed and designated by the D/ATC. Customers cannot apply on their own behalf when residing in a D/ATC. For more information regarding AR refer to 63- 113 Authorized Representatives. The AR is required to complete the application process and receive an Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) to purchase food for the resident. Residents of a D/ ATC must be certified as a one- person HH unless their children are living with them, in which case their children must be included in the HH. Facilities requesting to be added to the authorized D/ATC list will need to be elevated to CalFresh program. Refer to “Desk Aid List of Authorized Drug and Alcohol Treatment Centers” in Eligibility Essentials for a list of authorized D/ATC facilities and designated AR’s. 2. GLA Facilities: GLA are public or private nonprofit residential homes for disabled or blind individuals that serve no more than 16 residents and are certified by California Department of Social Services (CDSS). To be eligible for CalFresh, residents of the GLA must be blind or disabled as defined by CalFresh. Residents have the option to apply on their own behalf , through an AR of their choice or through an AR employed and designated by the GLA. If the resident is physically or mentally unable to apply on their own behalf, the GLA may determine that the resident must apply through the AR designated by the GLA. For more information regarding AR refer to 63 -113 Authorized Representatives. For a list of current GLA facilities, refer to “California Department of Social Services (CDSS) Certified Group Living Arrangement List” found on the CDSS website: https://cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/calfreshresource-center/policy. 3. Sober Living Environments (SLE) Sober living environments are residential living arrangements for individuals transitioning from drug or alcohol rehabilitation or treatment centers. SLEs are not licensed or certified by any state agency and cannot be considered a DATC for CalFresh. Customers residing in SLE’s are eligible to apply for CalFresh, provided they meet all eligibility requirements. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Residents of Drug/Alcohol Treatment Centers (D/ATC) and Group Living Arrangements (GLA) Number Page 63-123 2 of 3 Customers who receive a majority of meals (over 50% of three meals per day) as part of the service provided by the SLE, will be ineligible for CalFresh. 4. Reporting Changes: The treatment center, group home, and/or group resident is responsible for reporting any changes in the resident’s income or household circumstances. The center AR must complete, sign, and return the SAR 7. When a resident leaves the treatment center, group home, or ceases to participate in the treatment program, the center/group home will: • Instruct the person to contact the county as soon as they leave the center. • Provide the resident with a change form to report the new address and other changes in circumstances after leaving the center. • Return the AR EBT card after cutting the card in half, to the Family Resource Center ( FRC). For confidentiality purpose, the FRC is to shred the card upon receipt. • Inform the resident that they are entitled to one- half of the monthly benefit if they leave the center or group home before the 16 th of the month. The resident is to contact the county to request an EBT card or to reactivate their existing card if they are still interested in receiving CalFresh benefits. • Tell the resident that they will not receive any benefits for the current month if they leave on or after the 16th of the month as the benefits have already been issued and used. • Inform the resident that they are entitled to the full allotment if no benefits have been used. • GLA residents who apply on their own behalf will keep their EBT cards when they leave. If a group of residents have applied as one household, a pro- rata share of the remaining benefits will be provided to any departing household member. 5. Reporting Requirements: The treatment center/group home is required to submit a list of active CalFresh residents residing in their center. This list will be sent each month to the CalFresh Program Authorized Representative/ Alcohol and Drug Section Coordinator ( AR/ADSC). The list must be signed by a responsible center official, attesting to the validity of the list, and must be emailed to the AR/ADSC by the first week of each month. If the center refuses to provide the list of residents or refuses to allow the AR/ADSC access to the center to verify the list, the county will terminate the participation of all certified households in the center for refusal to cooperate. Timely informing notices of termination will be sent to the residents. Once denied or terminated the residents can reapply but will be certified only when the center cooperates. 6. Losses or Misuse: The treatment center or group home will be responsible for any misrepresentation or fraud which it knowingly commits in the certification of its residents. The center or group home must be knowledgeable about household circumstances and should carefully review those circumstances with residents prior to applying on their behalf. The resident is not responsible for any overissuance (OI) that occurs while they are residing at the center. The center or group home will be liable for any OI that occurs while the resident is residing at the center. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Residents of Drug/Alcohol Treatment Centers (D/ATC) and Group Living Arrangements (GLA) Number Page 63-123 3 of 3 7. Worker Responsibilities: Refer to Processing Guide 123-01 for guidance on processing D/ATC and GLA cases. Other Program Impact/s: No impact References: ACL 19-51, ACL 18-90, MPP 63-503.47, MPP 63-402.64 MPP 63-402.621, MPP 63-402.61, MPP 63- 503.48, Processing Guide 123-01 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 03/31/2026. Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-124 Domestic Violence Shelters
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Domestic Violence (DV) Shelters Number Page 63-124 1 of 2 Revision Date: 06/01/2024 Background: Individuals residing in Domestic Violence ( DV) shelters are not considered to be resident s of an institution and are considered separate households (HHs) and are eligible to apply for CalFresh. Purpose: This section provides policies regarding CalFresh applications for customers residing in DV shelters. This section is being revised after sunset review, there are no changes being made due to state legislation. The section title is updating the term “Battered Person Shelters” to “Domestic Violence (DV) Shelters”. Policy: DV shelters are defined as public or private nonprofit residential facilities that serve battered individuals. If the facility also serves other individuals, a portion of the facility must be set aside on a long-term basis to serve only victims of DV and/or individuals with children. P rior to certifying shelter residents, it must be determined that the shelter meets the definition of a DV shelter. Customers temporarily residing in DV shelters may apply for CalFresh on their own behalf or through an Authorized Representative (AR). Customers residing in DV shelters that have already received benefits for the current month as a member of their abuser’s CalFresh HH may apply as a separate HH and may be eligible for an additional allotment of benefits in their own case. The customer must complete a new application. Benefits must be issued under a different case name, number, and new Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card. 1. Income/Resources/Expenses Customers residing in DV shelters will be certified using the income, resources, and expenses that they are responsible for at the time of application. Income, resources, or expenses of their former HH will not be considered available to the customer . Resources held jointly with members of their former HH will not be considered available to the customer. 2. Actions on Former Case If the victim of DV is the head of HH, they may request to close the former CalFresh case that included the abuser. Requests to close a case by the h ead of HH are considered Verified Upon Receipt (VUR) and require no further verification. If the request is made… then discontinue the case with… verbally, timely and adequate notice. in writing or in the presence of staff, adequate notice, timely notice is not required. If the abuser is head of H H, action must be taken to ensure the former HH’s eligibility and allotment reflects the change in the HH’s composition. The former CalFresh HH will be notified of the adverse action and change in HH composition with timely and adequate notice. Note: Document all actions in the case record. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Domestic Violence (DV) Shelters Number Page 63-124 2 of 2 References: All County Information Notice (ACIN) I-09-18. All County Letters (ACLs) 17-30; 19-51; 21-101. Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 63-102; 63-503. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 06/30/2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-125 Income Reporting Threshold (IRT)
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) 63-125 1 of 4 Revision Date: 04/01/2022 Background: Households (HH) are required to report when their income exceeds the Income Reporting Threshold (IRT). The IRT is the amount likely to make a HH ineligible for CalFresh. This is considered a mandatory mid-period report. Purpose: This section details IRT reporting requirements. IRT information is being removed from 63-283 and moved to 63-125. No changes have been made due to state legislation. Policy: The IRT is an income threshold that informs the HH when they are required to make a mid-period report of an increase in income. HHs that have an IRT are required to report when their income exceeds the IRT limit. Income that exceeds the IRT must be reported within 10 calendar days from the date the change becomes known to the HH. This applies to all HH members, including ineligible members. Action must be taken mid-period, regardless of the impact on benefits. HHs with no IRT are not required to report income changes. When HHs with no IRT report an income change, it is considered a voluntary report. Note: One time increases in income over IRT that are not expected to continue are not required to be reported. Examples are unexpected overtime, or an extra paycheck received in the month. A HH will have an IRT when their income is at or below the 130% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) for the HH size. The table below provides additional guidance for when a HH will have an IRT: If the Non-Assistance CalFresh HH is… Then … Certified Modified Categorical Eligibility (MCE) or Non-MCE with income at or below 130% FPL, the IRT is 130% of the FPL for the HH size. Certified MCE with income between 131% and 200% FPL, the HH will have no IRT. The HH IRT is determined at the time of initial application, SAR 7, recertification, or whenever there is a change in HH composition. The IRT for the HH will be the 130% FPL for the HH size. When a HH reports income that may be over IRT, determine if the income is expected to continue. •If the HH reports and provides verification that the income is over IRT and the income is expected to continue, reevaluate the budget and reduce or discontinue benefits with timely and adequate notice. •If the HH reports that the income is over IRT and expected to continue, but the verification is not provided, send the HH the CW 2200 requesting verification of the income and allow 10 days to provide. If the income verification is provided reevaluate the budget and decrease or discontinue benefits with timely and adequate notice. If income verification is not provided, discontinue the case for failure to provide verification with timely and adequate notice. Below are examples of reported changes for HHs that have an IRT and must report if their income exceeds 130% FPL. It is confirmed with the customer that the income is not over IRT. Outcome Take no action, send the “No Change Notice of Action (NOA) CF 377.4 SAR”. Document information in case record for follow up at next SAR 7 or recertification, whichever comes first. Scenario A HH reports an increase in income and is not sure if the income is over IRT. It is confirmed with the customer that the income is over IRT but is not expected to continue. Outcome Take no action, send the “No Change Notice of Action (NOA) CF 377.4 SAR”. Document information in case record for follow up at next SAR 7 or recertification, whichever comes first. Scenario A HH reports an increase in income and is not sure if the income is over IRT. It is confirmed with the customer that the income is over IRT and is expected to continue. Outcome Send the HH a CW 2200 requesting verification of the income. If income verification is provided, decrease benefits at the end of the month in which timely and adequate notice can be provided. If income verification is not provided, discontinue the case for failure to provide verification at the end of the month in which timely and adequate notice can be provided. Scenario A HH reports increased income that is not over IRT. Outcome If the change will result in a decrease in benefits, do not request verification. Send the “No Change NOA”. Document information in case record for follow up at next SAR 7 or recertification, whichever comes first. If the change will result in an increase in benefits, send the HH a CW 2200 requesting verification of the income. If income verification is provided, act on the change to increase the benefits. If income verification is not provided, send the “No Change Notice of Action (NOA) CF 377.4 SAR”. Document information in case record for follow up at next SAR 7 or recertification, whichever comes first. Below is an example of a reported change for HH’s that do not have an IRT and are not required to report income changes. Example: Scenario A HH reports their income has increased over the 200% FPL. This is a voluntary report, these HH do not have an IRT and are not required to report. Outcome If the change will result in a decrease in income, do not request verification. Send the “No Change NOA”. Document information in case record for follow up at next SAR 7 or recertification, whichever comes first. If the change will result in an increase in benefits, send the HH a CW 2200 requesting County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) 63-125 3 of 4 verification of the income. If income verification is provided, act on the change to increase the benefits. If income verification is not provided, send the “No Change Notice of Action (NOA) CF 377.4 SAR”. Document information in case record for follow up at next SAR 7 or recertification, whichever comes first. Below are examples of a reported change for a HH with an excluded member: Example: Income increase with excluded HH member Scenario A HH of three including one ineligible noncitizen. The HH’s IRT for three is $2,379 (effective 10/01/2021). The HH reports that the noncitizen member found work, which is expected to continue. The new monthly income is $3,000. Outcome Prorate the noncitizen’s income to determine if the income is over the IRT: $3,000 / 3 = $1,000 $1,000 x 2 = $2,000 The HH income of $2,000 is not over the IRT. If the change will result in a decrease in income, do not request verification. Send the “No Change NOA”. Document information in case record for follow up at next SAR 7 or recertification, whichever comes first. If the change will result in an increase in benefits, send the HH a CW 2200 requesting verification of the income. If income verification is provided, act on the change to increase the benefits. If income verification is not provided, send the “No Change Notice of Action (NOA) CF 377.4 SAR”. Document information in case record for follow up at next SAR 7 or recertification, whichever comes first. Example: Income increase with excluded HH member Scenario A HH of three including one ineligible noncitizen. The HH’s IRT for three is $2,379 (effective 10/01/2021). The HH reports that their income is now $4,000. The ineligible noncitizen is earning $3,000/month. The other HH member earns $1,000 a month. Outcome Prorate the noncitizen’s income and add it to the eligible HH member’s income: $3,000 / 3 = $1,000 $1,000 x 2 = $2,000 $2,000 + $1,000 = $3,000 total income The HH is over the IRT. Reevaluate the HH’s budget and decrease/discontinue the case with timely notice. title: 63-151 Non Financial Criteria
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Non-Financial Eligibility Criteria Number Page 63-151 1 of 1 Revision Date 06/01/2025 Background: There are multiple eligibility standards that need to be evaluated for CalFresh and California Food Assistance Program (CFAP), including various non-financial criteria. Purpose: This section lists the non-financial criteria that must be evaluated when determining eligibility for CalFresh and CFAP. Policy: An evaluation of the following non-financial criteria must be completed when establishing eligibility for CalFresh and CFAP: • Identity • Residency • Household composition • Institutionalization status • Citizenship • Noncitizen status and sponsorship • Social Security Number • Student status • Fleeing felon status and parole or probation violations • Voluntary quit and reduction of hours • Participation in the Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations • Categorical Eligibility (CE) or Modified Categorical Eligibility (MCE) • Resources [for CalFresh Expedited Services (CFES) and non-CE/MCE cases only] • Intentional Program Violator (IPV) status • Work registration • Able-bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWD) time limit References: Manual of Policy and Procedures (MPP) 63-400 – 63-411, 63-501, Processing Guide 117-01 Verifications and Documentation, Desk Aid Verification Requirements Chart, Desk Aid Verification Processing Guidelines for CF-CW-MC Apps, Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 06/30/2028. title: 63-152 Identity and Residency
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Identity and Residency 63-152 1 of 2 Revision Date: 11/01/2020 Background Identity and residency must be verified as part of the application process for CalFresh. Purpose: This section describes the policies for identity and residency verification. There are no changes due to State legislation, this section is being updated after sunset review. Policy: The identity and residency of the person applying for CalFresh must be verified. When an Authorized Representative (A/R) applies on behalf of a household, the identity of both the A/R and head of household must be verified. Customers who do not have any form of identification (ID) may verify their identity through a collateral contact. A collateral contact is a verbal confirmation of a customer’s identity by a person outside of the household. To meet residency requirements, customers must live in the county in which they are applying for benefits. Customers may not receive benefits in more than one county or state, in the same month. The exception to this is victims of domestic violence residing in shelters for battered persons who’s current CalFresh household includes the abuser. Refer to CFPG 63-124 for information on individuals living in battered persons shelters. Residency requirements do not require customers to live in a permanent dwelling, have a fixed mailing address or “intent to reside permanently” in the county. Persons on vacation in the county are not considered residents. 1. Verification Requirements: Any documents which reasonably establish the applicant's identity or residency must be accepted, and no requirement for a specific type of document may be imposed. Identity verification needs to be provided only once by the customer, not for each application. Refer to Eligibility Policy and Procedure Guide (EPPG) “Reduced and No Fee DMV ID Cards” for information on how customers can get a Department of Motor Vehicle (DMV) ID for a reduced rate. Refer to “Desk Aid Verification Requirement Chart” in Eligibility Essentials for a detailed listing of acceptable forms of identity verifications. 2. Out of County / State Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) Usage: Customers may use their EBT benefits in other states or counties, so long as they remain residents of the county in which they applied for benefits or county benefits are being received in. Out of county or state EBT usage is not a reason to discontinue benefits for loss of residency. Refer to Processing Guide # 152-01 for guidance on determining residency when customers are using EBT benefits in another county or state. 3. Homeless Households: Homeless households meet residency requirements by stating that they live in the county in which they are applying for benefits. Households may be considered homeless when they experience any of the following: •Have no fixed, regular place to sleep at night •Live somewhere that people do not normally live •Live in a shelter designed to provide temporary accommodations County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Identity and Residency 63-152 2 of 2 •Live for less than 90 days in another person’s home. The 90-day period starts when the applicant or recipient moves into a temporary residence, and a new 90-day period will start if the customer moves into a different temporary residence 4. Whereabouts Unknown: When mail is returned as “undeliverable” or “address unknown” it is necessary to determine if the customer is still a resident of the county in which they applied and are receiving benefits in. A discontinuance based on “whereabouts unknown” is not permitted for CalFresh cases. Refer to Processing Guide # 152-01 for guidance on determining residency for whereabouts unknown issues. Other Program Impacts: None References: ACL 15-94; ACL 15-94E; ACL 10-01 MPP 63-300.5; MPP 63-401 CalFresh Processing Guide # 152-01 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 11/30/2023. Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Eligibility Operations

title: 63-153 Citizenship Status and Eligibility for CalFresh
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Citizenship Status and Eligibility for CalFresh Number Page 63-153 1 of 2 Revision Date: 04/01/2026 Background: Participation in CalFresh is limited to United States (U.S.) Citizens and qualified Non Citizens. Purpose: This section describes the citizenship requirements for the CalFresh program. The section is being updated to include new Non Citizen requirements due to House of Representatives 1, An Act to Provide Reconciliation Pursuant to Title II of H. Con. Res. 14 (H.R. 1), signed into Federal law on July 4, 2025. Policy: The following individuals are eligible for CalFresh: • U.S. Citizens. • Qualified Non Citizens: o Non Citizen U.S. Nationals. o Lawful Permanent Residents (LPRs). o Individuals who reside in the U .S. in accordance with a Compact of Free Association (COFA) agreement. o Cuban and Haitian Entrants (CHEs). 1. U.S. Citizenship To be considered a U.S. Citizen, an individual must meet one of the following: • Have been born in: o One of the 50 states. o The District of Columbia. o Puerto Rico. o Guam. o The U.S. Virgin Islands. o The Northern Mariana Islands on November 4, 1986, or later. • Be a Naturalized U.S. Citizen. • Have acquired U.S. citizenship (children born abroad to a U.S. Citizen parent). • Have derived citizenship through the naturalization of their parents prior to their 18th birthday. 2. Verification of Citizenship Unless questionable, an individual’s statement is sufficient verification of U.S. citizenship. U.S. citizenship is considered questionable when the claim of citizenship is: • Inconsistent with statements made by the individual or with other information on current or previous applications. • Inconsistent with information received by another source. Refer to Section 63-117 for acceptable verification of citizenship. 3. Five Year Waiting Period Certain LPRs are subject to a five- year waiting period before becoming eligible for CalFresh, unless they are exempt or meet a N on Citizen condition. Refer to Section 63-154 Non Citizen Status for County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Citizenship Status and Eligibility for CalFresh Number Page 63-153 2 of 2 information on the N on Citizen conditions. Qualified Non Citizens who are not eligible for CalFresh benefits, solely based on their immigration status, may be eligible for the California Food Assistance Program (CFAP) if they meet all other eligibility requirements. R eferences: Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 63-405 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 273.4(a) All County Letter (ACL) 25-92 S unset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 03/31/2029. A pproval for Release: A lberto Banuelos. Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-154 Non Citizen Status
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Non Citizen Status Number Page 63-154 1 of 7 Revision Date: 04/01/2026 Background: Lawfully present Non Citizens may be eligible to CalFresh as long as they meet all other eligibility requirements. When a qualified Non Citizen is ineligible to CalFresh solely due to not meeting a Non Citizen condition, they may be eligible to California Food Assistance Program (CFAP) benefits. Receipt of CalFresh or CFAP is not considered a “public charge” as defined by the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS). Purpose: This section describes the requirements N on Citizens must meet to be eligible to CalFresh or CFAP. The section is being updated to include new N on C itizen requirements due to House of Representatives 1, An Act to Provide Reconciliation Pursuant to Title II of H. Con. Res. 14 (H .R. 1), signed into Federal law on July 4, 2025. Policy: Certain lawfully present Non Citizens are eligible to receive federally funded food benefits known as CalFresh while others are eligible to state funded food benefits known as CFAP. The individual’s Non Citizen category determines whether they may be eligible to CalFresh, CFAP, or neither. 1. Qualified Non Citizens The following lawfully present N on Citizens are known as qualified N on Citizens and are eligible to CalFresh so long as they meet all other eligibility requirements including Non Citizen conditions. Non Citizen Category Description United States (U.S.) Nationals Born in American Samoa, Swains Island, or Northern Mariana Islands Individuals born in American Samoa or Swains Island after 12/21/1952 are considered U.S. Nationals, but not U.S. Citizens. These individuals may have a U.S. passport that notates that the bearer of the passport is a U.S. National and not a U.S. Citizen. Citizens of the Northern Mariana Islands born before November 4, 1986 who opted out of becoming U.S. Citizens are considered U.S. Nationals. Lawful Permanent Residents (LPRs) An individual who is lawfully admitted to the U.S. for permanent residence. These individuals hold a Permanent Resident card (I-551) also known as a green card. Compacts of Free Association (COFA) Citizens COFA countries include the Federated States of Micronesia, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the Republic of Palau. As of March 9, 2024, COFA Citizens who lawfully reside in the U.S. are eligible to CalFresh, provided they meet all other eligibility criteria. Cuban and Haitian Entrants A Cuban/Haitian Entrant as defined in §501(e) of the Refugee Education Assistance Act of 1980. The law defines a Cuban/Haitian Entrant as any of the following: • Any individual granted parole as a Cuban/Haitian Entrant or granted any other special status established under the immigration laws for Nationals of Cuba or Haiti, regardless of the status of the individual at the time they apply for benefits. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Non Citizen Status Number Page 63-154 2 of 7 • A National of Cuba or Haiti for whom a final, non-appealable, and legally enforceable order of removal has not been entered and is either: o Paroled into the U.S. and has not acquired any other Non Citizen status under the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA). Unlike other parolees, Cuban/Haitian Entrants may still be eligible if their parole period has expired, if they have not acquired any other immigration status. o Subject of removal proceedings under the INA. o Has an application for asylum pending under the INA. • Haitian orphans permitted to enter the U.S. as Humanitarian Parolees, meet the definition of a Cuban/Haitian Entrant. A Haitian orphan will have an I-94 indicating “paroled” into the U.S. on or after January 12, 2010. • Cuban medical professionals, their Cuban spouses, and Cuban children, paroled under INA §212(d)(5). • Non-Cuban spouse and/or children of a Cuban National admitted as a parolee under §212(d)(5) may not be considered a Cuban/Haitian Entrant. • A child born to at least one Haitian National parent regardless of the country the child is born in is deemed a Haitian National and may be considered a Cuban/Haitian Entrant. This same rule does not apply to children born outside of Cuba to Cuban Nationals. Note: Cuban/Haitians granted Temporary Protected Status (TPS) are not eligible for CalFresh or CFAP, unless they acquired TPS after arriving as a Cuban/Haitian Entrant. 2. Non Citizen Conditions Certain LPRs are subject to a five year waiting period and are not eligible for CalFresh until they meet one of the Non Citizen conditions listed below or are exempt from the waiting period. If the LPR does not meet a Non Citizen condition, they are eligible to CFAP as long as they meet all other eligibility criteria. • Have been lawfully residing in the U .S. as a qualified Non Citizen for five years beginning on their date of entry. If the individual was granted a qualified N on Citizen status while already living in the U.S., the five-year period begins on the date the N on Citizen obtained status as a qualified N on Citizen through USCIS. If USCIS grant ed qualified status retroactively, use the date that USCIS granted qualified status. • Children under 18 years of age regardless of the date of entry into the U.S. • Individuals lawfully admitted into the U .S. for permanent residence that can be credited with 40 qualifying quarters of work under the Social Security system. See Section 63-154.7 below. • Elderly individuals who were lawfully residing in the U .S. on August 22, 1996, and were 65 years or older on August 22, 1996. • Blind or disabled individuals receiving benefits or assistance for their condition regardless of when they entered the U.S. Non Citizens are considered disabled if they are receiving any of the following disability-based income: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Non Citizen Status Number Page 63-154 3 of 7 o Supplemental Security Income/State Supplementary Payment (SSI/SSP) that is disability based. o Interim assistance pending SSI/SSP that is disability based. o Social Security Disability benefits. o Federal or State disability retirement benefits for a permanent disability. o Veteran’s disability benefits. o Railroad Retirement disability benefits. • Are an American Indian born abroad and have become an LPR: o A Native American born in Canada that is living in the U .S. under §289 of the INA or Non Citizen members of a Federally recognized Native American tribe, as defined in §4(e) of the Indian Self -Determination and Education Assistance Act. This includes, but is not limited to, the Saint Regis Band of the Mohawk in New York State, the Micmac in Maine, the Abanaki in Vermont, and the Kickapoo in Texas. Applicants must provide a membership card or other tribal document demonstrating membership in a Native American tribe or an I -551 with C lass of Admission (COA) code S13. • Certain Hmong or Highland Laotian tribal members and have become an LPR: o Non Citizens lawfully residing in the U .S. who are from Laos, Vietnam, Cambodia, or another country with Hmong or Highland Laotian populations, who were members of a Hmong or Highland Laotian tribe at the time the tribe rendered assistance to the US Armed Forces during the Vietnam era (August 5, 1964, to May 7, 1975). This category includes the spouse (but not a divorced spouse), unmarried dependent child (under the age of 18, or a full -time student under the age of 22) or un- remarried surviving widow(er) of a deceased Hmong or Highland Laotian. • An active member of the U .S. Armed Forces (excluding National Guard) or veteran of the U .S. Armed Forces who is lawfully residing in the U .S. This includes the spouse, unmarried dependent children, or un- remarried surviving spouse of a deceased veteran. See table below for descriptions of a veteran, surviving spouse, and unmarried dependent child as they relate to this specific condition. Term Description Veteran An individual who has been honorably discharged for a reason other than on account of alienage as documented by a DD Form 214 or other acceptable verification and has met the minimum active-duty service requirements (24 months or the period for which the person was called to active duty). A discharge “Under Honorable Conditions” is not the same as an honorable discharge and does not meet the requirement. A veteran also includes an individual who served before July 1, 1946, in the organized military forces of the Government of the Commonwealth of the Philippines. Surviving spouse The spouse of a deceased veteran or an individual who died while on active duty that has not remarried, and the marriage fulfilled one of these requirements: • Married for at least one year. • Married before the end of a 15-year time span following the end of the period of military service in which the injury or disease causing the death of the veteran was incurred or aggravated. • Married for any period if a child was born of the marriage or was born before the marriage. Unmarried A legally adopted or biological child who is under the age of 18, or under the age County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Non Citizen Status Number Page 63-154 4 of 7 dependent child of 22 and a student, or 18 or older if the child was/is disabled and a dependent prior to turning 18. The following exemptions from the five- year waiting period allow LPRs to receive CalFresh immediately: • Previously held one of the following categories of Non Citizens and has since become a LPR: o Refugees. o Asylees. o Deportation or Removal Withheld. o Cuban and Haitian Entrants (eligible to CalFresh prior to becoming LPR). o COFA Citizens (eligible to CalFresh prior to becoming LPR). o Iraqis and Afghans with Special Immigrant Visas (SIV). o Certain Afghan Nationals Granted Parole Between July 31, 2021 and September 30, 2023. o Certain Ukrainian Nationals Granted Parole Between February 24, 2022 and September 30, 2024. o Non Citizens admitted to the U.S. as Amerasian immigrants. o Victims of Trafficking. 3. Ineligible Non Citizens The following N on C itizens are not eligible to CalFresh unless their status changes to a qualifying status: • Asylees. • Refugees. • Parolees (unless they are Cuban and Haitian Entrants). • Deportation/Removal Withheld. • Conditional Entrants. • Battered Non Citizens. • Victims of Trafficking. • Certain Afghan Nationals granted parole between July 31,2021, and September 30, 2023. • Certain Ukrainian Nationals granted paroled between February 24, 2022 and September 30, 2024. • Foreign nationals holding non-immigrant visas such as student, visitor, business, or tourist visas. • Those admitted under color of law. • T emporary Protected Status (TPS) holders. • Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) recipients. • Non Citizens who have applied for qualified status but have not yet been approved. • Undocumented Non Citizens. • Non-immigrant visa holders who stayed in the U.S. beyond the period authorized on their visa. 4. S ponsored Non Citizens LPRs who are sponsored as a condition of entry into the U .S. must be evaluated for CalFresh/CFAP based on sponsorship and deeming regulations. Any LPR who immigrates to the U .S. based on a family member is sponsored. A sponsor is someone who signs an affidavit of support (I -864 or I - 864A) promising to provide financial support for the N on Citizen. Refer to Section 63-157 Sponsored Noncitizens for more information on sponsorship and deeming regulations. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Non Citizen Status Number Page 63-154 5 of 7 5. Opt Out at Initial Application or Recertification Prior to determining eligibility at initial application or recertification, a Non Citizen HH member has the option to opt out of applying for CalFresh or CFAP. If they choose to opt out, do not request verification of their Non Citizen status. Any individual that opts out will be evaluated as an ineligible Non Citizen and their income and resources will be considered available to the CalFresh HH and evaluated. A Non Citizen that has chosen to opt out may change their mind and request to be added to the case at any time. 6. Verification of Non Citizen Status Verification of Non Citizen status is a requirement in order for a Non Citizen to be aided in the CalFresh HH. The verification must be reviewed to ensure the individual is reporting the correct status. The category on the I -551, the COA on the I -94, or the category listed on the Employment Authorization Document (I -766) may assist in determining the Non Citizen status of the individual. The validity of the document must be verified through the USCIS Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) system at initial application and recertification. If a Non Citizen does not want to provide verification of their immigration status, they will be considered an ineligible Non Citizen. They will not be aided in the CalFresh HH, however their income and resources will be considered available to the HH. See Section 63- 255 Treatment of Income and Expenses of Ineligible and Non-Household Members. 7. Changes in Non Citizen Status HHs are not required to report a change in Non Citizen status mid-period. If a HH voluntarily reports a change in N on Citizen status that results in a decrease or discontinuance in benefits, document the change in the case record, send a no- change notice, and follow-up at the HH’s next recertification. If a SAVE report is received mid- period that verifies a change in N on Citizen status and results in a decrease or discontinuance in benefits, timely action must be taken as a SAVE report is considered Verified Upon Receipt (VUR). If a HH voluntarily reports a change in N on Citizen status that results in an increase in benefits, take timely action. At each recertification, ask whether any Non Citizen HH members have experienced a change in Non Citizen status. Document the HH’s response in the case record and request verification when applicable. A SAVE report must be requested at each recertification. 8. 40 Quarters A qualified Non Citizen may meet a CalFresh qualified Non Citizen condition by being credited with 40 quarters (10 years) of work. A quarter is a Social Security Administration (SSA) credit earned by working a job or as self -employed. One credit equals one calendar quarter of qualifying employment. A Non Citizen may be credited with 40 quarters of qualifying employment through quarters earned by: • The Non Citizen themself. • Parents, up through the quarter the applicant turned 18, including quarters earned before the child was born. • Stepparents, if at the time the quarters were worked the child was under 18, unmarried, and there was a marital relationship between the stepparent and the child’s parent. If the marital relationship ends for reasons other than death, the stepparent’s quarters cannot be used. • A current spouse for work performed during their marriage. If the marriage ends for a reason other than death the quarters of the former spouse may not be used. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Non Citizen Status Number Page 63-154 6 of 7 • A deceased spouse for quarters earned during the marriage if the Non Citizen has not remarried. Note: A parent may not use a child’s quarters. A Non Citizen may have more than four quarters in a year through quarters credited from other people, for example: Scenario HH consists of married LPR mom, U.S. Citizen dad, and U.S. Citizen minor child. Mom and dad both worked the third quarter of 2023. Outcome Mom can be credited with 2 quarters for the third quarter of 2023. From 1978 ongoing, quarters are based solely on an individual’s total yearly amount of earnings. The amount of earnings needed to earn a quarter increases and is different for each year . Refer to the SSA’s Quarter of Coverage website for the dollar amount of earnings needed to earn one quarter based on the year the individual was working. Quarters earned prior to 1978 are established based on the following: • A quarter was earned for each calendar quarter in which an individual was paid $50 or more in wages, including agricultural wages, for years 1951 through 1954. • Four quarters were earned for each calendar year in which an individual’s net earnings from selfemployment were $400 or more. • A quarter (max 4 per year) was earned for each $100 of agricultural wages paid during the year for years 1955 through 1977. Qualifying quarters of employment must be verified. Quarters may be verified in one of two ways: • T hrough the SSA’s automated system, which can be viewed in an Applicant Income and Eligibility Verification System (IEVS) report. o Non C itizens who believe that the records provided by the SSA’s automated system are incorrect may request a review of work history provided by SSA. A document from SSA indicating that a determination of work quarters is under review must be provided to the county. The N on C itizen will be allowed to participate in CalFresh until SSA completes its investigation, or for a maximum of six months from the date of the original determination of insufficient quarters, whichever comes first. If upon further review SSA cannot establish additional earnings and the N on C itizen does not have at least 40 qualifying quarters, an Inadvertent Household Error (IHE) claim will be established for the months CalFresh w as issued in error. • Through employment records provided by the individual. o Qualifying quarters of employment may be verified by employment information provided by the HH. E mployer-prepared wage statements, W -2 or W -2c forms, a copy of the federal or state income tax return as proof of earnings, or other similar employment records are acceptable. The normal application p rocessing timeframes apply if obtaining verification of work quarters from the HH. After all the earnings are obtained for or on behalf of the Non Citizen, calculate the number of quarters to which they are eligible. Beginning with the first quarter of 1997, credits will not be allowed if the individual who earned it received any federal means-tested public benefits during that quarter. Federal means-tested benefits include CalWORKs/Aid to Families with Dependent Children ( AFDC), Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA), CalFresh, SSI, or Medi -Cal/Medicaid. A quarter is allowed if the benefit received was 100 percent state or county funded, for example, CFAP, state funded CalWORKs, Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants (CAPI), or General Relief. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Non Citizen Status Number Page 63-154 7 of 7 R efer to Processing Guide 154- 01 for guidelines on determining qualifying work quarters during the interview process. 9. Non Citizens with Orders of Deportation When a Non Citizen HH member voluntarily reports and provides documentation of a Final Order of Deportation, notify CalFresh Program through the appropriate channels. sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Non Citizen Status Number Page 63-154 1 of 7 Revision Date: 04/01/2026 Background: Lawfully present Non Citizens may be eligible to CalFresh as long as they meet all other eligibility requirements. When a qualified Non Citizen is ineligible to CalFresh solely due to not meeting a Non Citizen condition, they may be eligible to California Food Assistance Program (CFAP) benefits. Receipt of CalFresh or CFAP is not considered a “public charge” as defined by the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS). Purpose: This section describes the requirements N on Citizens must meet to be eligible to CalFresh or CFAP. The section is being updated to include new N on C itizen requirements due to House of Representatives 1, An Act to Provide Reconciliation Pursuant to Title II of H. Con. Res. 14 (H .R. 1), signed into Federal law on July 4, 2025. Policy: Certain lawfully present Non Citizens are eligible to receive federally funded food benefits known as CalFresh while others are eligible to state funded food benefits known as CFAP. The individual’s Non Citizen category determines whether they may be eligible to CalFresh, CFAP, or neither. 1. Qualified Non Citizens The following lawfully present N on Citizens are known as qualified N on Citizens and are eligible to CalFresh so long as they meet all other eligibility requirements including Non Citizen conditions. Non Citizen Category Description United States (U.S.) Nationals Born in American Samoa, Swains Island, or Northern Mariana Islands Individuals born in American Samoa or Swains Island after 12/21/1952 are considered U.S. Nationals, but not U.S. Citizens. These individuals may have a U.S. passport that notates that the bearer of the passport is a U.S. National and not a U.S. Citizen. Citizens of the Northern Mariana Islands born before November 4, 1986 who opted out of becoming U.S. Citizens are considered U.S. Nationals. Lawful Permanent Residents (LPRs) An individual who is lawfully admitted to the U.S. for permanent residence. These individuals hold a Permanent Resident card (I-551) also known as a green card. Compacts of Free Association (COFA) Citizens COFA countries include the Federated States of Micronesia, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the Republic of Palau. As of March 9, 2024, COFA Citizens who lawfully reside in the U.S. are eligible to CalFresh, provided they meet all other eligibility criteria. Cuban and Haitian Entrants A Cuban/Haitian Entrant as defined in §501(e) of the Refugee Education Assistance Act of 1980. The law defines a Cuban/Haitian Entrant as any of the following: • Any individual granted parole as a Cuban/Haitian Entrant or granted any other special status established under the immigration laws for Nationals of Cuba or Haiti, regardless of the status of the individual at the time they apply for benefits. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Non Citizen Status Number Page 63-154 2 of 7 • A National of Cuba or Haiti for whom a final, non-appealable, and legally enforceable order of removal has not been entered and is either: o Paroled into the U.S. and has not acquired any other Non Citizen status under the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA). Unlike other parolees, Cuban/Haitian Entrants may still be eligible if their parole period has expired, if they have not acquired any other immigration status. o Subject of removal proceedings under the INA. o Has an application for asylum pending under the INA. • Haitian orphans permitted to enter the U.S. as Humanitarian Parolees, meet the definition of a Cuban/Haitian Entrant. A Haitian orphan will have an I-94 indicating “paroled” into the U.S. on or after January 12, 2010. • Cuban medical professionals, their Cuban spouses, and Cuban children, paroled under INA §212(d)(5). • Non-Cuban spouse and/or children of a Cuban National admitted as a parolee under

title: 63-156 California Food Assistance Program
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide California Food Assistance Program Number Page 63-156 1 of 4 Revision Date: 06/01/2026 B ackground: The State of California provides state funded food benefits through the California Food Assistance Program (CFAP). CFAP provides food benefits for qualified Non Citizens who are not eligible for federal CalFresh benefits because of their immigration status . CFAP is issued in the same method as CalFresh. P urpose: This section details the regulations for CFAP benefits. This section is being revised to include updated CFAP eligibility for Parolees and information regarding the Able- Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWD) time limit. P olicy: In order to be eligible to CFAP, Non Citizens must be ineligible for CalFresh benefits solely due to their immigration status under the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act (PRWORA) of 1996 or battered Non Citizens. Refer to Section 63-157 for regulations about sponsored Non Citizen CFAP eligibility and deeming rules. 1. No n Citizen Conditions CFAP qualified Non Citizens that do not meet a Non Citizen condition as detailed in Section 63-154, are eligible to CFAP as long as they meet all other eligibility criteria. However, once a Non Citizen condition is met, the Non Citizens are ineligible for CFAP. Battered Non Citizens are potentially eligible for CFAP regardless of meeting a Non Citizen condition. Refer to Non Citizen eligibility scenarios below for examples. 2. CF AP Qualified Non Citizens CFAP qualified Non Citizens that do not meet a Non Citizen condition as detailed in Section 63-154, are eligible to CFAP as long as they meet all other eligibility criteria. However, once a Non Citizen condition is met, the Non Citizens, with the exception of battered Non Citizens, are ineligible for CFAP. See below examples of Non Citizen categories potentially eligible for CFAP: Non Citizen Category Description Lawful Permanent Resident (LPR) An individual who is lawfully admitted to the United States (U.S.) for permanent residence. These individuals hold a Permanent Resident card (I- 551) also known as a green card. Conditional Entrant A conditional entrant under §203(a)(7) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA). Prior to April 1, 1980, conditional entrant was the primary method of entry for refugees. The provision was abolished by the Refugee Act of 1980; however, there may still be individuals with this Non Citizen category. Parolee An individual paroled into the U.S. under §212(d)(5) of the INA. Parole allows an individual who may be inadmissible or otherwise ineligible for admission into the U.S. to enter for a temporary period due to urgent humanitarian reasons or significant public benefit. A Class of Admission code of DT signifies parole granted at a port of entry under §212(d)(5) of the INA. Once County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide California Food Assistance Program Number Page 63-156 2 of 4 parole has expired, if the individual has not been approved for re-parole or acquired another qualified Non Citizen status, they are considered to have undocumented status and are no longer eligible to CFAP. Battered Non Citizen The battered Non Citizen must meet all of the following requirements: • Have an approved or pending petition presenting a prima facie case for immigration status in one of the following categories: o Form I-130 filed by the battered Non Citizen’s spouse or the battered Non Citizen child’s parent. • The Non Citizen, the Non Citizen’s child, or the Non Citizen child’s parent has been battered or subjected to extreme cruelty within the U.S. by their U.S. Citizen or LPR spouse, parent, or member of the family residing in the same household (HH). • There is substantial connection between the abuse and the need for benefits. • The Non Citizen no longer resides with the batterer. Note: Battered Non Citizens are eligible for CFAP regardless of meeting a Non Citizen condition. Victim of Human Trafficking Non Citizen victims of human trafficking may apply for a T Visa. Prior to being approved a T Visa a victim of human trafficking may be eligible to CFAP. To be eligible the trafficking victim must do all the following: • Provide a sworn statement that they are a victim of human trafficking. • Provide one of the following items as evidence they are a victim of trafficking: o Police, government agency, or court records or files. o News articles. o Documentation from a social services, trafficking, or domestic violence program or a legal, clinical, medical, or other professional from whom the victim has sought assistance from in dealing with the crime. o A statement from an individual with knowledge of the trafficking. o Other documentary evidence. o A copy of a completed T Visa application. o Written notice from United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) of the receipt of the T Visa application. o If additional evidence cannot be provided a sworn statement may be accepted on its own if the information provided in the statement appears credible. • Have a pending application for a T Visa, is preparing to file an application for a T Visa, or have been granted a T Visa without an Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) or Office of Trafficking in Persons (OTIP) certificate. Any of the following documents may be accepted as verification the Non Citizen has filed or is preparing to file for a T Visa: • A confirmation receipt or letter from USCIS verifying an application for a T Visa has been filed. • A copy of the Application for T Nonimmigrant Status (I-914). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide California Food Assistance Program Number Page 63-156 3 of 4 • A statement from a law enforcement official or victim advocate who is assisting the victim with the T Visa application. • If no documentation is available, the applicant’s statement that they have filed or intend to apply for a T Visa. CFAP benefits terminate when one of the following occur: • The T Visa is administratively denied. • The individual has not applied for a T Visa within one year of applying for CFAP. • A request by law enforcement officers on behalf of the recipient for federal continued presence status has not been made within one year. • The Non Citizen is approved a T Visa with an ORR or OTIP certificate. Review Section 63-154 for treatment of changes in Non Citizen Status. Victim of Other Serious Crimes Non Citizen victims of a serious crime may apply for a U Visa. To be eligible to CFAP , the Non Citizen must have already applied for a U Visa and is awaiting a decision or has been granted a U Visa. Any of the following documents may be accepted as verification the Non Citizen applied for or was approved a U Visa: • A confirmation receipt or letter from USCIS that a Petition for U Nonimmigrant Status (I-918) has been filed. • An I-797 approving a U Visa. • An I-797 serving as a receipt confirming an application for an Employment Authorization Document (EAD) has been received based on a U Visa application. • An EAD issued with category A19 or A20 for a Non Citizen approved a U Visa. When an application for a U Visa is administratively denied, the Non Citizen loses their eligibility to CFAP. Review Section 63-154 for treatment of changes in Non Citizen status. S ee below for Non Citizen eligibility scenarios: Scenario Outcome 30 year old parolee has a date of entry in 2010. They are not potentially eligible for CalFresh because they do not have a qualifying Non Citizen status for CalFresh (parolee). They are not potentially eligible to CFAP because they meet a Non Citizen condition (have been residing in the U.S. longer than 5 years). 16 year old conditional entrant with a date of entry 2 years ago. They are not potentially eligible for CalFresh because they do not have a qualifying Non Citizen status for CalFresh (conditional entrant). They are not potentially eligible for CFAP because they meet a Non Citizen condition (under 18 years of age). 20 year old conditional entrant with a date of entry 2 years ago. They are not potentially eligible for CalFresh because they do not have a qualifying Non Citizen status for CalFresh (conditional entrant). They are potentially County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide California Food Assistance Program Number Page 63-156 4 of 4 eligible for CFAP because they do not meet a Non Citizen condition. 25 year old entered as a refugee 1 year ago. They are not potentially eligible for CalFresh because they do not have a qualifying Non Citizen status for CalFresh (refugee). They are not potentially eligible for CFAP because they do not have a CFAP qualifying Non Citizen status (refugee). 25 year old entered as a refugee 1 year ago, is now a LPR. They are potentially eligible to CalFresh because they are currently in a qualifying Non Citizen status for CalFresh (LPR). They are not potentially eligible to CFAP since they have potential eligibility to CalFresh. 45 year old parolee with a date of entry 2 years ago and lives with their 15 year old child who is also a parolee with same date of entry. The HH is not potentially eligible for CalFresh because they do not have qualifying Non Citizen status for CalFresh (parolees). The 45 year old is potentially eligible for CFAP because they do not meet a Non Citizen condition. The 15 year old is not potentially eligible for CFAP because they do meet a Non Citizen condition (under 18 years of age). 3. Wo rk Requirements All CFAP recipients must be assessed for potential exemptions from work registration and ABAWD work requirements. Refer to Sections 63-901 and 63-904 for more information. 4. ABAWD T ime Limit When a CFAP recipient begins receiving federally funded CalFresh benefits, ABAWD status must be re-assessed and the ABAWD must receive a new set of three countable months of federally funded CalFresh. If the ABAWD lost eligibility for CFAP due to reaching the ABAWD time limit, they must reapply for assistance. Refer to Section 63-904 for more information. Ref erences: Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 63-403, 63-410, 63-411 All County Letter (ACL) 19-93, 25-92, 26-03, 26-29 Su nset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 05/31/2029. Appr oval for Release: Al berto Banuelos. Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services
