title: 63-157 Sponsored Noncitizens
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Sponsored Noncitizens Number Page 63-157 1 of 6 Revision Date: 01/01/2025 Background: Sponsored noncitizens must be evaluated for CalFresh or California Food Assistance Program (CFAP) based on sponsorship and deeming regulations. Purpose: This section outlines sponsorship and deeming regulations for CalFresh and CFAP eligibility. Policy: The following are definitions of common terms that will be used throughout this section: Term Definition Sponsored Noncitizen A noncitizen Legal Permanent Resident (LPR) for whom a sponsor signed the Affidavit of Support (I-864) form. Sponsor An individual who has signed an I-864 or the Contract Between Sponsor and Household Member (I-864A) promising to financially support a LPR as a condition of their entry into the United States (US). Deeming Attribution of a sponsor’s income and resources to the sponsored noncitizen. I-864 The form a sponsor must sign to show they have adequate income and/or assets to support the sponsored noncitizen. I-864A An attachment to an I-864 that must be signed by the sponsor who is completing an I-864 and a household (HH) member of the sponsor who promises to make their income and/or assets available to help support the sponsored noncitizen. The I-864A is only used when a sponsor’s income and assets do not meet the income requirements of the I-864 and a HH member chooses to combine their income and assets with those of the sponsor to meet the requirements. The income and resources of a sponsor and the sponsor’s spouse , if one signed an I-864A, must be counted during the eligibility determination of a sponsored noncitizen, unless the sponsored noncitizen meets an exemption or opts out . Resources will only be counted if the HH is not Categorically Eligible (CE) or Modified Categorically Eligible (MCE). Sponsorship deeming ends when one of the following circumstances applies to the sponsored noncitizen: • Achieves US citizenship through naturalization. • Has 40 qualifying quarters of work. • Loses LPR status and leaves the US permanently. • Death occurs (or upon death of the sponsor). Sponsored noncitizens will be identified by the Class of Admission (COA) listed as category on the I- 551 Permanent Resident Card. Refer to the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) COA table found in the Eligibility Essentials Desk Aids for a full list of COAs and which ones correspond to sponsored noncitizens. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Sponsored Noncitizens Number Page 63-157 2 of 6 1. Exemptions to Sponsorship Deeming A sponsored noncitizen will be exempt from sponsorship deeming when any of the following circumstances apply to them: • Sponsorship occurred prior to December 19, 1997. • The sponsor signed Form I-134 Declaration of Financial Support and not an I-864. • Is a victim of human trafficking, domestic violence, or other serious crimes. • Is participating in the same CalFresh HH as the sponsor. • Is indigent. • Is sponsored by an organization or group and not an individual. • Is under 18 years of age. 2. Options Available to Sponsored Noncitizens Prior to determining eligibility, the following three options must be explained to non-exempt sponsored noncitizens and allow them to choose the option they would like for themselves: • Be evaluated for indigence; • Opt out of receiving CalFresh/CFAP benefits; or • Provide the sponsor’s information. Document in the case record that the options were explained, and which option was chosen. The table below provides a description of each option: Option Description Indigence evaluation A sponsored noncitizen may self-declare that that they are indigent (not being supported by their sponsor). Once a determination of indigence is made, the noncitizen remains indigent for 12 months. A noncitizen is determined to be indigent when their HH’s current income plus any cash contributions and/or in-kind assistance the sponsor provides them is below 130% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) for the HH size. Verification of the sponsor’s income and in-kind assistance is not needed to make an indigence determination. However, if the noncitizen receives cash contributions from the sponsor, it must be counted when determining eligibility to CalFresh. When determined to be indigent, the name of the sponsored noncitizen and their sponsor(s) must be reported to USCIS via USCIS Letter for Indigent Sponsored Noncitizens (09-99) form. Opt out Sponsored noncitizens can opt out of applying for CalFresh/CFAP prior to a determination of eligibility being made. If the noncitizen opts out, they will be considered an ineligible HH member. Once the sponsored noncitizen opts out, they are not required to provide any information regarding their immigration status and sponsor. Provide sponsor’s information Sponsored noncitizens that are not indigent and do not opt out must provide the sponsor’s information. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Sponsored Noncitizens Number Page 63-157 3 of 6 Refer to CalFresh Processing Guide 157 -01 Sponsored Noncitizens for guidance on determining whether sponsorship provisions apply, conducting the indigence evaluation, requesting sponsorship information, and the Notices of Action (NOA) required. 3. Victims of Human Trafficking, Domestic Violence, or Other Serious Crimes Sponsored n oncitizens who are victims of human trafficking, domestic violence, or other serious crimes are exempt from sponsorship deeming. The exemption will run for a 12 -month period when the sponsored noncitizen does not live with the person causing the abuse and there is a connection between the abuse and the need for benefits. The list below includes, but is not limited to, circumstances that may demonstrate a substantial connection between the abuse and the need for benefits: • Become self-sufficient following separation from the abuser. • Escape the abuser and/or the community in which the abuser lives. • Fulfill a financial need due to loss of financial support from the abuser as a result of the separation. • Fulfill a financial need caused by the loss of a job due to the abuse. The exemption must be reassessed every 12 months. After the initial 12 months have passed the noncitizen must demonstrate that the abuse has been recognized in an order by a judge or a determination made by USCIS to continue receiving the exemption. 4. Providing Sponsorship Information and Documentation Sponsored noncitizens, besides those that are exempt or opting out , are responsible for providing the I-864 and I-864A, if one was signed, to verify their sponsor(s). Prior to requesting the I-864 and I- 864A, if one was signed, attempt to verify the sponsor using a Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE). Refer to the table below for more information on how to verify the sponsor. If the… then… SAVE report in the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) does not list the sponsor nor the date the I-864 and I-864A, if applicable, was signed, order an electronic SAVE (eSAVE). eSAVE does not list the sponsor nor the date the I-864 and I-864A, if applicable, was signed, send a Request for Verification (CW 2200) to the sponsored noncitizen asking them to provide the I-864 and I-864A, if applicable. Allow 10 days to provide. sponsored noncitizen cannot provide the I-864 and I-864A, if applicable, send a G-845 Verification Request and G-845 Supplement Verification Request to USCIS to verify sponsorship. Note: Sponsorship verification and documentation is not required when determining CalFresh Expedited Services (CFES). Sponsored noncitizens , besides those that are exempt or opting ou t, must provide t he Sponsor’s Statement of Facts Income and Resources (SAR 22) along with mandatory verifications at intake, County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Sponsored Noncitizens Number Page 63-157 4 of 6 recertification, and anytime a sponsored noncitizen , who is no t exempt, requests CalFresh /CFAP mid-period. A Sponsor’s Semi -Annual Income and Resources Report (SAR 72) along with mandatory verifications must be provided with the Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7). 5. Failure or Refusal to Provide Sponsor’s Information The sponsored noncitizen will be considered an ineligible noncitizen if they fail or refuse to provide the sponsor ’s information or are unable to obtain it . Each adult sponsored noncitizen will be responsible for providing their sponsorship information. In situations where the sponsor’s information is not provided, the following must be applied: If the same sponsor is responsible for the entire HH and it includes… then… no children under the age of 18, the entire HH is ineligible until the required information is provided and/or verified. children under the age of 18, sponsorship regulations do not apply to children under 18. Evaluate eligibility to CalFresh for the children. Sponsored HH members 18 or older will be determined as ineligible noncitizens. 6. Deeming Rules Sponsored noncitizens that have been in the US for less than five years and do not meet a noncitizen condition of eligibility, are ineligible to federal CalFresh but may receive benefits through CFAP. Refer to Section 63-154 Noncitizen Status for more information. Sponsorship deeming rules apply to CFAP eligible sponsored noncitizens as follows: If it is… sponsorship deeming rules… less than 3 years from the date the I-864 was signed, apply. within 3-5 years of the date the I-864 was signed, do not apply. more than 5 years from the date the I-864 was signed, apply and they are now eligible for federal benefits. Once the sponsored noncitizen becomes eligible to federal CalFresh, deeming rules apply indefinitely or until the sponsored noncitizen: • Achieves US citizenship through naturalization. • Has 40 qualifying quarters of work. • Loses LPR status and leaves the US permanently. • Is deceased (or upon death of the sponsor). • Meets a sponsorship deeming exemption. 7. Determining Deemed Income Use the information provided on the SAR 22 and SAR 72 to calculate the deemed income for the sponsored noncitizen. Deemed income must be calculated at initial application, semi-annual report, recertification, and at any time CalFresh/CFAP is requested for a sponsored noncitizen. The following steps must be applied to determine the sponsored noncitizens deemed income: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Sponsored Noncitizens Number Page 63-157 5 of 6 Step Action 1 Add the total monthly earned and unearned income of the sponsor and sponsor’s spouse, if they signed an I-864A. 2 Deduct 20 percent from the earned income. 3 Deduct the CalFresh monthly gross income eligibility limit for a HH size equal to the sponsor’s HH. Note: The sponsor’s HH includes all individuals who are or could be claimed as dependents for federal income tax purposes. 4 The remaining amount is the income deemed available to the sponsored non-citizen. Note: A s ponsor’s income reported for CalWORKs can be used for CalFresh /CFAP deeming purposes, but the steps listed above must be applied. Direct cash payments provided by the sponsor and the sponsor’s spouse , if they signed an I-864A, will not be considered income to the sponsored noncitizen unless the amount exceeds the deemed amount. Example: Scenario Based on the information reported at intake on the SAR 22 and the verification provided, it is determined that the income deemed to the sponsored noncitizen from their sponsor is $400. The sponsored noncitizen reports at intake that they receive a total of $600 per month in cash from their sponsor. Outcome $200 ($600 cash payment - $400 deemed income) would be counted in the budget as a cash gift, while $400 would be counted as deemed income from the sponsor to the sponsored noncitizen. 8. Deemed Income for HH’s with Sponsored Children Under 18 or Multiple Sponsored Noncitizens A noncitizen child under the age of 18 is exempt from sponsor ship deeming. The child’s share of the deemed income is not counted when determining eligibility. When a sponsor declares on the SAR 22 that they have signed an I -864 for multiple noncitizens, the share for the other sponsored noncitizens that are not part of the CalFresh HH will not be counted in the budget. The following steps must be applied to determine the share for the child under the age of 18 or the other sponsored noncitizens that are not part of the CalFresh HH: Step Action 1 Divide the total deemed income by the number of sponsored noncitizens to get each person’s share. 2 Deduct the share for the child under the age of 18 and/or the other sponsored noncitizens that are not part of the CalFresh HH. 3 The remainder will be counted as unearned income when determining eligibility. Review sponsorship deeming at the next recertification w hen a sponsored child, who was previously exempt due to age, turns 18. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Sponsored Noncitizens Number Page 63-157 6 of 6 Example: Scenario Child is receiving CalFresh benefits in a HH with a certification period of January through December. The child turns 18 in August. Outcome Evaluate sponsorship deeming at the next recertification in December. References: All County Letter (ACL) 11-06, 11-06E, 21-24. Manual of Policy and Procedures (MPP) 63-300.5(e)(8), 63-405.3,63-405.7, 63-503.49. Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 273.2(f)(10)(vi), 273.4(c). Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 12/31/2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-159 Voluntary Quit and Reduction of Work Hours
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Voluntary Quit and Reduction of Work Hours Number Page 63-159 1 of 3 Effective Date: 05/01/2024 Background: Mandatory work registrants are ineligible to participate in CalFresh if they voluntarily quit a job or reduce work hours, without good cause. Household (HH) members who qualify for one of the work registration exemptions listed in section 63-901 are exempt from these disqualification provisions. Purpose: This section details the CalFresh policy regarding voluntary quit and reduction of work hours . This section is being updated to add additional good cause reasons. Policy: 1. Voluntary Quit and Reduction of Work Hours: Mandatory work registrants are ineligible to receive CalFresh if they voluntarily quit a job of 30 hours or more per week or reduce the number of hours worked in paid employment to less than 30 hours per week without good cause. Voluntary quit and reduction of work hours are defined as follows: Term Definition Voluntary Quit Voluntarily resigning or quitting a job of 30 hours or more per week or which provides weekly earnings equivalent to at least the federal minimum wage multiplied by 30 hours. Reduction of Work Hours Voluntarily decreasing the number of hours worked in paid employment to less than 30 hours per week. Job quit or reduction of work hours applies to both applicants and recipients. • A pplicants that voluntarily quit or reduce work hours without good cause within 60 days prior to the date of application will be denied for one, three or six months. • R ecipients that voluntarily quit or reduce work hours without good cause anytime during the certification period will be discontinued for one, three or six months. When no good cause exists for the voluntary quit or reduction of work hours, the HH member will be disqualified from CalFresh. The length of the disqualification period will apply as follows: Instances of Non-Compliance Disqualification Period First instance One month Second instance Three months Third instance Six months 2. Good Cause Determination: Good cause must be determined when a HH member voluntarily quits a job of 30 hours per week or reduces the number of hours worked to less than 30 hours per week. Verification of good cause is not required, unless questionable. Good cause includes but is not limited to: • Circumstances beyond the HH member’s control such as: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Voluntary Quit and Reduction of Work Hours Number Page 63-159 2 of 3 • Illness. • Illness of another HH member requiring the presence of the work registrant. • HH emergency. • Unavailability of transportation. • Language barriers. • Resigning/quitting a job that is considered unsuitable employment as specified in section 63-901.2. • Discrimination by an employer based on a protected class. • Work demands or conditions that make continued employment unreasonable. • Acceptance by the registrant of employment, or enrollment of at least half -time in any recognized school, training program, or institution of higher education that requires them to leave employment. • Resignations by registrants under the age of 60 which are recognized by the employer as retirement. • Acceptance of an offer of employment, and due to circumstances beyond the registrant’s control, the job falls through or results in employment of less than 30 hours a week. • Leaving a job in connection with patterns of employment in which workers frequently move from one employer to another such as migrant farm labor or construction work. • Having no adequate childcare arrangements available for a registrant’s children who have reached age six but are under twelve years of age. • A registrant’s workplace rights were violated. • A registrant provides documentation that the work schedule or work hours are so unpredictable that it does not allow the customer to anticipate the amount of monthly income from the job. Note: Federal, state, or local government employees who have been dismissed from the job because of participation in a strike have no good cause for leaving employment. 3. Required Actions: Upon determining that a HH member has voluntary quit or reduced work hours without good cause, the following actions shall be taken: • Issue a Notice of Action (NOA) informing the HH of the disqualification period being imposed. • The NOA must explain the following: • reason for the denial/discontinuance. • the HH members right to reapply at the end of the disqualification period. • how to regain eligibility before the disqualification period begins. • the right to reapply if the HH member becomes exempt during the disqualification period. • the right to request a state hearing. • The HH member will be discontinued/denied for one, three or six months, depending on the instance. • For applicants, the first month of the disqualification period is the month in which the HH member is determined ineligible. • For recipients, the disqualification period will begin the first of the month following the issuance of a timely NOA. • The disqualified HH member is considered an excluded HH member and ineligible to CalFresh. • If the HH member leaves the CalFresh HH before the disqualification can be imposed, the period of ineligibility will run continuously beginning with the first of the month after issuing a timely NOA unless the disqualification is ended. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Voluntary Quit and Reduction of Work Hours Number Page 63-159 3 of 3 • If the voluntary quit or reduction of work hours occurs in the last month of a certification period or it is determined in the last 30 days of the certification period, the period of disqualification begins the day after the last certification period ends and continues for the length of the disqualification regardless of whether the HH member reapplies for CalFresh. 4. Re-establishing Eligibility: CalFresh eligibility may be re-established when one of the following occurs: • The work registrant meets a work registration exemption. • The disqualification period has ended. To re-establish eligibility the work registrant must reapply for benefits. If… then… the work registrant is part of an active case, they must request to be added back to the case and agree to comply with work registration requirements. the case is closed, the work registrant must re-apply and agree to comply with work registration requirements. References: ACL 23-30; MPP 63-408 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 05/31/2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-161 Social Security Number Requirement
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Social Security Number Requirement Number Page 63-161 1 of 4 Revision Date 08/01/2024 Background: All CalFresh household (HH) members are required to provide a Social Security Number (SSN) or apply for one prior to certification. Purpose: This section details the SSN requirements for individuals applying for CalFresh . It includes updated guidance on referring individuals to the Social Security Administration (SSA) when they do not have a SSN and are required to apply for one. Policy: Prior to certification, applicants are required to provide the SSN or verification of application for a SSN for each HH member. If an individual has more than one SSN all numbers are required to be provided. Explain to the HH that failure/refusal to provide a SSN without good cause will result in ineligibility of the individual for whom the SSN was not provided. Note: The SSN requirement does not apply to individuals in the HH who are not requesting CalFresh, are undocumented, or noncitizens opting out. 1. Validating/Verifying the SSN A Social Security Card is not required to be provided; a verbal or written statement of the SSN is sufficient. All SSNs must be verified/validated through the Income Eligibility Verification System (IEVS). An applicant IEVS is automatically requested by CalSAWS when a case is pended in the system if the applicant’s name, date of birth, and SSN are entered. If an applicant IEVS is not automatically generated, request one to verify/validate the SSN. The issuance of benefits shall not be delayed, if otherwise eligible, while pending a response from IEVS. However, the IEVS report must be processed within 45 days of receipt. If the SSN has already been verified/validated by a previous IEVS then no additional verification is needed. The table below details the SSN verification codes that may be accepted to verify/validate a SSN and the actions to take if an acceptable SSN verification is not received. If the SSN verification code is… then… “A” or “W” in MEDS or “J” on the IEVS report, the SSN is validated/verified. No further verification/clarification is needed. anything other than “A” or “W” in MEDS or “J” in IEVS, Note: Refer to CalSAWS Tip there is either a data mismatch (the name and/or date of birth does not match that associated with the SSN) or the SSN validation/verification failed. Contact the HH to clarify the individual’s name, date of birth, and SSN are correct. If unable to resolve the data mismatch with the HH, issue a Request for Verification (CW 2200) and allow them 10 days to provide verification from the SSA that the data mismatch has been County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Social Security Number Requirement Number Page 63-161 2 of 4 MEDS SSN for more information on each SSN verification code. resolved. A Social Security Administration Referral Notice (MC 194) may be provided to the customer to bring to SSA to complete. Once the verification/clarification has been received, update CalSAWS and manually request another applicant IEVS to verify/validate the SSN; CalSAWS will not automatically request another applicant IEVS when demographic information is updated. Note: Individuals should be entered into the eligibility determination system under the exact name associated with their SSN to avoid data mismatches. 2. Exemption for Expedited Services (ES) HHs eligible for ES are not required to provide or apply for a SSN until after they have received their first allotment. HHs eligible for ES with postponed verifications must provide the missing SSN (s) or verification of an application for a SSN before the next issuance . The next issuance could be the second month for HHs applying before the 15 th of the month or the third month for HHs applying after the 15th of the month. 3. Exemption for Victims of Trafficking, Domestic Violence, or Other Serious Crimes Noncitizens who are victims of trafficking, domestic violence , or other serious crimes do not have to provide or apply for a SSN as a condition of eligibility for state funded benefits ( California Food Assistance Program [CFAP]). Once the trafficking victim has been certified by the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR), they will be eligible for federal benefits (CalFresh) and are required to provide/apply for a SSN. 4. Newborns HHs reporting a newborn in the home may not have a SSN for the newborn at the time the report is made. If the customer cannot self -attest or provide proof of an application for a SSN at the time the newborn is reported in the home, the newborn will be eligible to CalFresh until the HHs next recertification or the sixth month following the child’s birth, whichever is later. The table below details when the SSN or verification of application for a SSN must be provided for a newborn. If the sixth month is… then the SSN, application for a SSN, or good cause must be provided … after the HH’s recertification and the SSN or application for SSN was not provided at recertification, by the end of the sixth month otherwise the child is ineligible starting the seventh month. before the HH’s recertification, at recertification otherwise the child is ineligible starting the first month of the new certification period. 5. Obtaining a SSN HH members who qualify for, but do not have a SSN are required to apply for one. Assist in obtaining a SSN by: • Providing them with one of the following to bring to the SSA to apply for a SSN: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Social Security Number Requirement Number Page 63-161 3 of 4 If the individual is a…. then provide them with… United States (US) citizen, legal permanent resident (LPR), refugee, asylee, or any other qualified noncitizen status with authorization to work in the US, a Social Security Administration Referral Notice (MC 194) to bring to SSA when applying for a SSN. Note: An MC 194 is not required to be brought to SSA to apply for a SSN. Inform customers that they do not need to wait for the form to go apply. qualified noncitizen without authorization to work in the US; does not have an I-766 Employment Authorization Document (EAD) or a pending application for an EAD, a Non-Work Social Security Number Request form (GEN 2101). The GEN 2101 must be completed by the Human Services Specialist (HSS) and signed by a Family Resource Center (FRC) Manager to be considered valid. • Providing the address of the local SSA office. • Informing the customer of the documentation the SSA will need , such as identity and verification of US citizenship or noncitizen status. • Assisting in obtaining documents required by the SSA to apply for an SSN. Verification an application for a SSN was submitted includes, but is not limited to: • MC 194 with Part II completed by the SSA office. • Form SSA 5028 (receipt of application for an SSN from the SSA). • Form SSA-2853-OP4 (receipt showing that the parent has requested a SSN for the newborn at the hospital). • Form I-765 Application for Employment Authorization if the applicant has consented on the form to disclose their information to the SSA for purposes of obtaining a SSN. Questions 14 and 15 marked as “Yes” indicate the applicant is requesting a SSN. 6. Failure/Refusal to Comply with SSN Requirement HH members who fail /refuse to provide a SSN, apply for one, or resolve a data mismatch without good cause , will be ineligible until compliance occurs. Ineligibility applies only to the HH member whose SSN was not provided and not the entire HH. Compliance occurs when one of the following is provided: • Their SSN. • Verification of application for a SSN. • Verification the SSN mismatch was resolved. • Good cause. Note: For guidance on treatment of income and expenses of SSN disqualified individuals refer to Section 63-255 Treatment of Income and Expenses of Ineligible and Non-Household Members. 7. Good Cause Determination for Not Providing a SSN Determine if good cause exists for failure to comply with the SSN requirements. When determining good cause, consider the information provided by the customer and the SSA. Documentary evidence or collateral information that the customer has applied for a SSN or made every effort to supply the County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Social Security Number Requirement Number Page 63-161 4 of 4 SSA with the necessary information to apply, will be considered good cause. Good cause does not include delays due to illness, lack of transportation, or temporary absences. If the individual can show good cause why an application for a SSN has not been completed in a timely manner, that individual will be allowed to participate for one month in addition to the month of application. Good cause must be shown on a monthly basis for the individual to continue to receive CalFresh benefits. If they fail to provide their SSN , application for a SSN , or do not continue to show good cause on a monthly basis, the individual will become ineligible. References: Manual of Policy and Procedures ( MPP) 63-404, 63 -403.211; Code of Federal Regulations ( CFR) 273.6; All County Informational Notice (ACIN) I-54-22, I-54-01; All County Letter (ACL) 07-45, 07-45E, 24-44; MEDS Network User Manual. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 07/31/2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

Purpose: This section details the SSN requirements for individuals applying for CalFresh . It includes updated guidance on referring individuals to the Social Security Administration (SSA) when they do not have a SSN and are required to apply for one. Policy: Prior to certification, applicants are required to provide the SSN or verification of application for a SSN for each HH member. If an individual has more than one SSN all numbers are required to be provided. Explain to the HH that failure/refusal to provide a SSN without good cause will result in ineligibility of the individual for whom the SSN was not provided. title: 63-162 Students
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Students Number Page 63-162 1 of 6 Revision Date: 06/01/2026 Bac kground: Students enrolled in an institution of higher education must meet student eligibility criteria for CalFresh. Purpos e: This section defines student eligibility for CalFresh and provides guidance on exemptions. This section is being revised to include the following: • Updated assessment process for Local Programs that Increase Employability (LPIE). • Clarification on Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) Funded Cal Grant A and B, summer enrollment, and Adult Education Programs. Polic y: 1. Institution of Higher Education A student is considered enrolled in an institution of higher education if they are in a: • Business, technical, trade, or vocational school that normally requires a high school diploma or equivalent certificate. • Regular curriculum at a college or university that offers degree programs regardless of a high school diploma. Enrol lment status is determined by the school and may be verified using student statement or information gathered while completing the Student Eligibility Worksheet (09- 55 HHSA). Enrollment begins on the first day of the school term and will continue through normal class attendance and vacation, unless the student graduates, is suspended, drops out, or does not intend to register for the next school term. 2. Evaluating Student Status Evaluate student status at intake and recertification (RE). Student status is not a mandatory mid-period reporting requirement and is not considered Verified Upon Receipt (VUR). If student status is reported mid-period, document the voluntarily reported change in the case record, the reason for not acting on the change, and send a No-Change Notice of Action (NOA). The NOA must remind the household (HH) to report the information at the next Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7) or RE, whichever comes first. Act only on changes that will increase the CalFresh allotment except for mandatory mid-period reports and information that is considered VUR. 3. Summ er Enrollment Students who submit an initial application for benefits in the summer before their first official day of the regular school term are not considered students for CalFresh at the time of application. Reassess their student status at RE. Continuing students are subject to student eligibility rules during regular school breaks. 4. Adul t Education Programs The following adult education programs are considered non-regular curriculums and are not considered institutions of higher education for CalFresh: • Adult education programs. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Students Number Page 63-162 2 of 6 • Remedial education. • Continuing or community education. • Professional development. • English for speakers of other languages. • Workforce development and training programs. • Enrollment in kindergarten through grade 12 (K-12) adult schools. • Community college non- credit classes that do not require a high school diploma or equivalency certificate. 5. Eligibility Requirements Only one exemption is needed to qualify a student for CalFresh, however it is mandatory to document all exemptions being claimed in the case record. If a student loses an exemption, assess whether the student meets the criteria for another exemption before taking negative action. Complete the 09- 55 HHSA when determining student eligibility and image the form into the case record. S tudents must meet one of the following exemptions to be eligible for CalFresh: • Age 17 or younger. • Age 50 or older. • Physically or mentally unfit for employment. o This may be a temporary or permanent illness, disability, or life circumstance that reduces the student’s ability to work an average of 20 hours a week on an ongoing basis. o If a student’s unfitness is not apparent, the exemption may be verified by receipt of temporary or permanent disability benefits or with a statement from a doctor or licensed psychologist. A student’s statement or affidavit is not sufficient verification. o Indicators of apparent unfitness include but are not limited to chronic homelessness, struggling with substance use, and having experienced domestic violence. • Enrolled less than half time. o The definition of enrolled half time is being registered each term to half the number of credits required to graduate within four years as a first time freshman or two years as a transfer student. • Disabled and receiving disability-based income: o For example, Social Security Disability, Supplemental Security Income, Veterans Disability, Worker’s Compensation, or other disability-based income qualify for an exemption. o The disability must be expected to last more than 30 days. • Receiving TANF Funded Cal Grant, A or B. To qualify for TANF funded cash or non- cash benefits the student must be: o Unmarried; o 25 years of age or younger; and o Have parental and/or student income of $50,000 a year or less. Note: Cal Grant A is typically awarded to students at four -year institutions of higher education due to the California Promise grant that is awarded to undergraduate students at California Community Colleges (CCCs) that covers tuition and fees. • Does not expect to be enrolled next term. o Due to the student graduating, suspension/expulsion, dropping out, or not intending to register for the next normal school term (excluding summer school). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Students Number Page 63-162 3 of 6 Example 1 Scenario The student applies in February but states they plan to graduate in June Outcome The student is not subject to the student eligibility criteria. Example 2 Scenario The student applies in March but states they do not plan to return to school in the fall. Outcome The student is not subject to the student eligibility criteria. • R eceive California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids (CalWORKs) , Tribal TANF , or another program funded with the TANF block grant under Title IV of the Social Security Act such as the Job Opportunities and Basic Skills (JOBS) program. • Enrolled in Workforce Innovation Opportunity Act (WIOA). o San Diego Workforce Partnership (SDWP) administers the WIOA programs and determines who qualifies for WIOA funded training at local educational institutions. o Additional information on WIOA can be found here: https://workforce.org/training-wioa/. • Approved for Work Study. o Must be approved, awarded, or accepted for state or federally financed Work Study for the current school term and anticipated working during the term. o Exemption would begin the month the school term begins, or the month Work Study is approved, whichever is later. The exemption will end the month the school term ends or if the student refuses a Work Study position. o For treatment of Work Study income refer to Section 63-222 Earned Income. • Participating in CalFresh Employment and Training (CFET). • Participating in a LPIE. o Effective June 1, 2026, all associate and bachelor’s degree programs offered by the following campuses are approved statewide as General Programs under LPIE.  CCC.  University of California (UC).  California State University (CSU). o A student that has not declared a major but is enrolled in general education courses required to obtain an associate or bachelor’s degree is eligible for this exemption. Note: Students in graduate/advanced degree programs, certificate programs, career and technical education programs, apprenticeship programs must continue to be reviewed for specific campus based programs on the CalFresh Student Eligibility: List of Approved LPIEs list found at www.cdss.ca.gov/ inforesources/calfresh-resource-center/policy. This list is updated monthly on the California Department of Social Services (CDSS) website. Programs at private institutions continue to be excluded and cannot be LPIEs. • Participating in an on-the-job training program. • Work at least 20 hours per week or a total of 80 hours per month in paid employment. o When calculating hours worked, average the hours using the multiplier 4.33 or the number of weeks in the year. o For self-employed students, determine the average hours by dividing the net income by federal minimum wage. Note: Net income is the gross income minus the standard or actual deduction (whichever the student chose). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Students Number Page 63-162 4 of 6 Example 1: Using 4.33 Multiplier Scenario A student provides their pay stubs showing they work 19 hours per week. Even though the student does not work 20 hours per week, they do work more than an average of 80 hours or more each month. Outcome Average hours: 19 hours per week x 4.33 = 82.77 hours per month. The student is eligible for the paid work exemption. Example 2: Using Number of Weeks in the Year Scenario A student provides their previous month’s pay stubs showing they work 16 hours per week. This student does not work an average of 20 hours per week and does not maintain an average of at least 80 hours per month. Outcome Average hours: 16 hours per week x 52 weeks per year = 832 hours per year/12 months = 69.33 hours per month. The student is not eligible for the paid work exemption. o I f the student reports a change in work hours on the SAR 7, determine whether the work hours average to 20 hours per week or an average of 80 hours per month to continue with this exemption. o If the change in work hours does not average 20 hours per week or an average of 80 hours per month, determine if the student meets another exemption. • A single parent enrolled full time in college and exerting parental care and control of a child under age 12. • Exerting parental care and control for a child: o Under the age of 6. o Aged 6-11 and the student does not have adequate childcare to attend school and work 20 hours per week or participate in Work Study. Note: If two students exert parental care and control in the HH, allow the exemption status for only one. If there is more than one child under age 12 and it is reported that each student exerts care and control for a separate child, explore the exemption. Evaluate why one student is unable to care for all or the reason why each student is “responsible” for separate children. 6. I neligible Students Students who do not meet any of the exemptions listed above are ineligible and will be considered excluded HH members. Ineligible students’ income and resources are exempt from benefit determination. Refer to Section 63- 255 Treatment of Income and Expenses of Ineligible and Non- Household Members for guidance on treatment of ineligible students’ income and resources. 7. S tudent Meal Plans Students who live on campus and receive more than half their meals from a meal plan are considered residents of an institution and are ineligible for CalFresh benefits. There are 21 meals in a week (3 meals a day over 7 days per week). Students who live on campus and whose meal plan provides half of their meals (ten meals per week) may qualify for CalFresh benefits if all other eligibility criteria are met. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Students Number Page 63-162 5 of 6 Review mandatory and optional meal plans and the college website to obtain the latest meal plan information to determine eligibility for CalFresh. Students who live off campus are not considered residents of an institution and are potentially eligible for CalFresh, even if they have a meal plan that provides more than half their daily meals. CalFresh benefits cannot be used to pay for college meal plans. 8. V erification of Student Exemptions A student’s statement is sufficient to verify a student exemption. Verification of student exemption should only be requested when the information provided by the student is questionable or a student’s claim of physical or mental unfitness is not apparent. Refer to Section 63- 117 Verification and Documentation for more information on questionable information. The case record must document all student exemptions. No n-receipt of financial aid may be verified by student statement and must be documented in the case record. Federal or state government -funded grants, awards, scholarships, loans, or fellowships conferred for the purposes of attending higher educational institutions are exempt income. Evaluate the source of education- related income to determine whether to exempt it or count it when determining eligibility and benefit amounts. Educational related income and calculations must be documented in the case record. F or students receiving TANF-funded Cal Grant A or B, if the student’s attestation is questionable, the California Student Aid Commission ( CSAC) provides students with an electronic or paper letter regarding their potential eligibility for CalFresh. This letter serves as verification that a student receives this exemption as only TANF-funded Cal Grant A or B recipients receive this letter. E ligibility staff must continue to verify the HH ’ s gross nonexempt income, including any educational assistance and/or stipends including but not limited to Department of Veteran Affairs (VA) housing and subsistence payment portions of VA educational benefits . These educational benefits are counted as income. Refer to Section 63- 222 Earned Income and 63- 224 Income Exclusions, for guidance on treatment of Students income. Procedure: 09-55 HHSA. P rogram Impacts: None. R eferences: All County Letters (ACLs) 26-25, 24-31, 22-46, 21-101, 21-58, 20-34, 19-93, 19-32, 18-27, 17-97, 17- 05, 17-05E. All County Information Notices (ACINs) I-89-15. Manual Policies and Procedures (MPP) 63-406.1; 63-300.5; 7. Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 273.5, 273.2(f)(1)(i), 273.2(f)(2). S unset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 05/31/2029. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Students Number Page 63-162 6 of 6 Approval for Release: A lberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-166 Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservation 63-166 1 of 1 Revision Date 01/24/2020 Background: Customers living on Indian Reservations or tribal members living off the reservation may choose to receive food from the Food Distribution Program instead of receiving CalFresh. Food received from the Food Distribution Program is called commodities. Customers cannot receive CalFresh and commodities in the same month. Customers can transfer from one program to the other, with timely notice. This revision updates the section to the new format. There are no changes due to state legislation. Purpose: This section describes the regulations about CalFresh and commodities. Policy: 63-166.1 Dual Participation: Dual participation means customers are getting both CalFresh and commodities in the same month. During the intake process, it is important to ask customers if they are receiving commodities. Asking this question will help to avoid dual participation and any overissuance (OI) for the customer. Procedure: 63-166.2 CalFresh Program Specialist Responsibilities: In San Diego County, the Food Distribution Program is run by Southern California Tribal Chairman’s Association (SDCTA). Each month SCTCA notifies the CalFresh Program Specialist of customers who are receiving food commodities. The CalFresh Program Specialist is responsible for determining if these customers are receiving CalFresh benefits. Customers who received CalFresh and commodities in the same month will have an OI. The CalFresh Program Specialist and SDCTA will determine if the county or SDCTA is responsible for the OI. 63-166.3 Overissuances: Receiving CalFresh and commodities in the same month will result in an OI. Instructions will be sent to the Family Resource Center (FRC) to set up the OI as an Inadvertent Household Error (IHE). Other Program Impacts None References: MPP 63-402.7 CFR 253.1 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 01/31/2023 Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Eligibility Operations

title: 63-167 Fraud Prevention
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageFraud Prevention 63-167 1 of 2 Revision Date: 08/01/2022 Background: Fraud exists when a household (HH) member or Authorized Representative (AR) knowingly makes false statements or fails to disclose information for the purpose of obtaining or maintaining CalFresh benefits. Purpose: This section details the fraud policy for the CalFresh program. This section is being revised due to sunset review. Policy: A fraud referral will be made to the Bureau of Public Assistance Investigation (BPAI) unit when there are allegations/suspicions of fraud, or there is questionable information that cannot be resolved. Applicants will be referred for investigation prior to granting benefits. Recipients will be referred for investigation within 5 working days from the determination a referral was needed. Below is a list of possible fraud indicators: •Questionable residency •Suspected duplicate aid •Questionable HH composition •Unreported income •Expenses exceeding income •Submitted documentation appears to have been altered •An overissuance (OI) that may have occurred due to failure to report •Customer’s failure to cooperate with providing questionable information •Situations involving embezzlement, perjury, trafficking, other general program violations •Fraud allegations received from other government agencies A referral must not cause a discontinuance or denial unless the findings from an investigation result in a change in eligibility. A referral must not delay the issuance of CalFresh or Expedited Service (ES) benefits. Note: A fraud referral must not be submitted for allegations of child abuse/neglect, drug/alcohol abuse, nonpayment of housing obligations, or unreported income from illegal sources. 1. Resolving Discrepancies: Staff must use all available sources, such as the Income Eligibility and Verification System (IEVS), Medi-Cal Eligibility Data Systems (MEDS) and The Work Number (TWN) to explore and resolve any unclear and incomplete information. When unable to clarify a discrepancy, staff must: •Contact the customer to clarify any questionable information •Assist the customer with obtaining the requested information •Assess for circumstances that may prevent the HH from providing necessary information, such as: ˗Physical, emotional, educational barriers ˗Language barriers ˗Experiencing domestic violence issues ˗Not understanding reporting responsibilities and Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) ˗Not being aware of what constitutes fraud Note: Refer to 63-118 for additional methods of resolving discrepancies. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageFraud Prevention 63-167 2 of 2 2. Findings Received: When it is determined that fraud exists, timely action must be taken to deny, reduce or terminate benefits. Staff will determine the action to take based on the information received from BPAI findings, the customer statements and CalFresh regulations. Negative actions that result in an OI, must be processed in accordance with the CalFresh OI section. For guidance on communication with BPAI and dispositioning a referral go to Eligibility Operations Processing Guide (EOPG) Fraud Referral Family Resource Center Liaison Protocol for Ongoing Eligibility Cases. 3. Fraudulent/Altered Documents: Documents that appear to be fraudulent or altered, can be referred to BPAI. Prior to making a referral to BPAI, staff must: •Make attempts to verify the document through: ˗Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) for documents related to immigration status ˗Immediate needs request for birth certificate ˗Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) to verify a California driver’s license or identification card •Image an enlarged copy of the document •Document in the case record the information that was found fraudulent/altered Note: Fraudulent/altered documents cannot be confiscated and must be returned to HH. 4. Fraud Hotline: Complaints of public assistance fraud are received via the San Diego County Public Assistance Fraud Hotline and B-Link Complaint Portal, which are both managed by BPAI. Each complaint is evaluated to determine if there is a potential public assistance fraud issue. 5. California Department of Social Services (CDSS) Alerts: CDSS alerts are received when a HH’s Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card was identified as having unusual transactions that were made at a retailer that has since been disqualified due to illegal trafficking. BPAI evaluates the alert and will initiate an investigation if needed. BPAI reports the outcome of the investigation to CDSS. References: MPP: 20-001, ACL: 13-89, ACWDL: 05-01-2019 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 08/31/2025. Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

For guidance on communication with BPAI and dispositioning a referral go to Eligibility Operations Processing Guide (EOPG) Fraud Referral Family Resource Center Liaison Protocol for Ongoing Eligibility Cases. 3. Fraudulent/Altered Documents: Documents that appear to be fraudulent or altered, can be referred to BPAI. Prior to making a referral to BPAI, staff must: •Make attempts to verify the document through: ˗Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) for documents related to immigration status ˗Immediate needs request for birth certificate ˗Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) to verify a California driver’s license or identification card •Image an enlarged copy of the document •Document in the case record the information that was found fraudulent/altered Note: Fraudulent/altered documents cannot be confiscated and must be returned to HH.

title: 63-168 Electronic Theft
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Electronic Theft Number Page 63-168 1 of 3 Revision Date: 03/01/2025 Background: CalFresh households (HHs) that report their benefits have been electronically stolen may be eligible to receive replacement benefits. Purpose: This section is being updated due to electronic theft policy changes that were implemented in December 2023. Policy: Electronic theft occurs when a CalFresh HH has their benefits electronically stolen from their account while they have their Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card in their possession. There are two types of electronic theft, skimming and scamming. In both cases , the HH’s benefits are stolen by creating a counterfeit EBT card or by manually entering the card number on a keypad connected to the point-ofsale device to conduct a transaction without the use of the physical card. The following are descriptions of the two types of electronic theft: Theft Type Definition Skimming The use of electronic equipment to capture an EBT card’s number and Personal Identification Number (PIN) without the cardholder’s knowledge. Scamming Deceiving or misleading an EBT cardholder to unwittingly give out their card number and PIN. Common forms of scamming include text messaging and phone calls. When electronic theft is reported by a HH the EBT card must be deactivated immediately and a replacement card issued. To request replacement benefit s, a Report of Electronic Theft of Benefits (EBT 2259) must be submitted. Deny any request for replacement benefits that does not meet either definition of electronic theft. Document in the case record detailed information relating to the request for replacement benefits and the outcome of the request. Note: Supplemental Nutrition Benefits (SNB) and Transitional Nutrition Benefits (TNB) are not eligible for replacement due to electronic theft. 1. Reporting Timeframe and Methods HHs have 90 days from the date the theft occurred to submit a completed EBT 2259. If the EBT 2259 is received more than 90 days from the date the theft occurred, the request for replacement benefits must be denied. A completed EBT 2259 may be submitted in any of the following ways: • In person at a Family Resource Center (FRC). • Online through BenefitsCal. • By mail. • Fax to the Document Processing Center (DPC) at (619) 236-9167. • E-mail to the DPC at DPC.HHSA@sdcounty.ca.gov. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Electronic Theft Number Page 63-168 2 of 3 • By calling Access at 1 -866-262-9881 to complete an EBT 2259 over the phone using telephonic signature. Process t he EBT 2259 and issue replacement benefits upon receipt, but no later than 10 days of receiving the completed form. 2. Countable Replacements A countable replacement refers to each overall electronic theft sequence reported by a HH, regardless of the number of specific transactions that were involved. A series of transactions listed on one EBT 2259 will be considered one countable replacement. The report may include transactions within and outside the 90 -day reporting timeframe. In such circumstances, only the transactions reported within 90 days of the theft may be replaced. Example: Scenario HH submits an EBT 2259 on March 10, 2024, and reports the following skimming transactions: • January 22, 2024, for $50. • January 23, 2024, for $100. • January 24, 2024, for $60. • January 26, 2024, for $80. • February 2, 2024, for $150. • February 3, 2024, for $40. Outcome This reported sequence of transactions is considered one countable replacement. A HH may only receive two countable replacements each Federal Fiscal Year (FFY). A FFY starts October 1 and ends September 30. Review the case prior to processing the EBT 2259 to determine how many countable replacements have already been issued in the current FFY. If two countable replacements have already been issued, deny the request for replacement benefits. HHs may receive up to two months’ worth of food benefits for each countable replacement. The maximum amount that can be replaced for each countable replacement is two times the amount of benefits that were issued directly prior to the first theft transaction repo rted on the EBT 2259 or the amount of benefits electronically stolen, whichever is less. Example: Scenario HH receives their monthly CalFresh benefits of $400 on January 8, 2024. On February 10, 2024, they submit an EBT 2259 reporting the following skimming transactions: • January 10, 2024, for $250. • January 11, 2024, for $100. • January 11, 2024, for $260. • January 12, 2024, for $80. In total the HH reported $690 in benefits were skimmed. Outcome The HH would be issued $690 in replacement benefits. The maximum amount of replacement benefits the HH could get is $800 ($400 x 2). Since the amount of County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Electronic Theft Number Page 63-168 3 of 3 benefits electronically stolen was less than $800 we would issue replacement benefits for the lesser amount. Note: Replacement of benefits due to a HH misfortune is not considered a countable replacement. For more information on replacement benefits due to HH misfortune refer to CalFresh Program Guide 63 - 509 Replacement Benefits. 3. Referrals to the Bureau of Public Assistance Investigations (BPAI) A referral to BPAI must be made when any of the following occur: • A public allegation or report of fraud is made. • There is reason to suspect that fraud exists or has been attempted based on the information reported on the EBT 2259, presented in the case record, or knowledge of electronic theft patterns. A request for replacement benefits may be delayed up to 25 calendar days from the date the EBT 2259 was received while awaiting a response from BPAI. If BPAI determines… then… within the 25 days that the claim is fraudulent, deny the replacement request. within the 25 days that the claim is not fraudulent, issue replacement benefits as soon as possible but no later than the 25th day. a referral will not be completed within 25 days, issue replacement benefits as soon as possible but no later than the 25th day. the claim is fraudulent after the 25th day and replacement benefits have been issued, establish an overissuance for the amount replaced. 4. Notices of Action (NOA) Once the EBT 2259 has been processed a NOA must be issued to the HH informing them of the approval or denial of replacement benefits. The following NOAs should be issued depending on the outcome of the request: • EBT Replacement Approval NOA (WI 10072A). • EBT Replacement Denial NOA (M44-350K). References: All County Letter (ACL) 21-133, 23-92, 24-62. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 02/29/2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-169 Restaurant Meals Program (RMP)
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Restaurant Meals Program (RMP) Number Page 63-169 1 of 2 Revision Date: 08/01/2025 Background: The Restaurant Meals Program (RMP) offers certain households (HH), who may have difficulty preparing meals for themselves or who do not have a place to store and/or cook food , additional options for purchasing low-cost meals. Purpose: This section details the RMP eligibility criteria and required notices that must be issued when a HH is approved or terminated for RMP. The section is being updated due to the implementation of the revised RMP eligibility determination policy and the updated RMP Notice of Action (NOA) that went into effect May 2025. Policy: RMP allows eligible HHs to use their Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card to purchase meals from participating restaurants. RMP eligibility is evaluated at initial application, recertification, periodic report, and mid-period when a change is reported. HHs determined eligible to RMP must be referred to https://www.cdss.ca.gov/rmp for a list of approved restaurants. 1. Eligibility for RMP To be eligible for RMP, all members of the CalFresh HH must be: • Aged (60 years or older); or • Disabled (refer to 63-101 for disabled definition); or • The spouse of an individual who is aged or disabled; or • Experiencing homelessness. See examples below: Household Composition Eligible for RMP HH of 2 • Wife - 62 years old (y/o) • Husband - 58 y/o Yes HH of 2 • Wife - 38 y/o • Husband - 40 y/o and disabled Yes HH of 2 • Mom - 35 y/o and disabled • Child - 10 y/o No HH of 3 • Mom - 35 y/o and disabled • Dad - 35 y/o and disabled • Child - 5 y/o No County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Restaurant Meals Program (RMP) Number Page 63-169 2 of 2 HH of 2 • Mom - 45 y/o and disabled • Child - 16 y/o and disabled Yes HH of 2 • Mother - 70 y/o • Child - 40 y/o and disabled Yes HH of 2 • Father - 30 y/o • Child - 10 y/o and disabled No HH of 2 • Mom - 35 y/o experiencing homelessness • Child - 6 y/o and experiencing homelessness Yes 2. RMP Notice Requirements The Notice of Approval/Termination for the CalFresh Restaurant Meals Program (CF 889) serves as both the RMP approval and termination NOA. The NOA must be provided to the HH upon approval or termination from RMP. References: Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 272.9, 278.1 All County Information Notice (ACIN) I-31-04, I-13-07, I-71-11 All County Letter (ACL) 14-49, 16-112, 21-100, 23-72, 24-01, 25-53 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 08/31/2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-201 Resource Eligibility Determination
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Resource Eligibility Determination Number Page 63-201 1 of 5 Revision Date: 09/01/2026 Background: Resources are considered in the CalFresh eligibility de termination . A household’s (HH’s) non-exempt resources must not exceed the property limit for the HH type and size. Purpose: This section details the CalFresh resource evaluation policy. This section is being updated to include the treatment of HH composition changes reported during the certification period. Policy: HHs that have been determi ned to be Categorical ly Eligible (CE) or M odified Categorical ly Eligible (MCE) ar e not r equired t o have resources eva luated. R efer t o Section 63 -120 for i nformation on determining CE and MCE eligibility. For HHs who ar e not C E or MCE, verify and determine the value of the HH’s resources. Evaluate resources at ini tial ap plication, periodic report, recertification, or when adding a new H H member. A H H w hose resources exc eed t he maximum allowable n on-exempt property l imit w ill be determined ineligible for C alFresh. R efer t o Sectio n 63- 1101 for the current maximum allowable resource limit. 1. Countable Resources Include the following types of r esources in the evaluation for C alFresh at application, periodic report, and recertification: • Liqui d resources such as cash on hand, money in checking and savings accounts, savings certificates, stocks or bonds, non-recurring lump sum payments, funds held in Individual Retirement Accounts (IRAs), and in accessible Keogh plans, provided they are not excluded as described below. Note: The value of an IRA or Keogh is the total cash value minus the amount of the penalty for early withdrawal of the entire amount in the plan. • Non-liquid resources such as personal property, land, buildings, and recreational properties provided they are not excluded as described below. Note: The value of non-liquid resources is the equity value, which is the fair market value less any loans owed on the resource. 2. Tr eatment of Resources The following table describes how to treat resources in different eligibility circumstances: Circumstance Treatment of Resources Joint Ownership of Resources Resources owned jointly by separate HHs (including non-CalFresh HHs) will be considered entirely available to the HH, unless the HH can demonstrate that the resources are inaccessible. If t he HH can demonstrate having access to only a portion of a resource, the value of only the accessible portion will be counted toward the HH’s resource level. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Resource Eligibility Determination Number Page 63-201 2 of 5 The resource will be considered inaccessible to the HH if the resource cannot practically be subdivided and the HH’s access to the value of the resource is dependent on the agreement of a joint owner who refuses to comply. A resource cannot be practically subdivided if the financial value of the proportionate share would be significantly reduced by the sale of only the subdivision. I f a resource is jointly held by members of the same CalFresh HH and some receive Public Assistance (PA) and others do not, the amount counted in determining the PA eligibility will be excluded. B ank accounts held jointly with military personnel deployed overseas will be excluded when the HH cannot use the funds for its own purposes, and only has access to the account to pay bills for the service member. It is the responsibility of the applicant to provide verification of this arrangement. • Verification may be a written statement from the military service person, a statement from the bank or other means attesting to this arrangement. • The funds will be counted as a resource for the HH if the customer has access to the service member’s bank account for their own purposes. Resources of Excluded HH Members The resources of excluded and ineligible HH members such as ineligible non-citizens, Social Security Number (SSN) Disqualified, Intentional Program Violators (IPV), Fleeing Felons and Probation/Parole Violators, CalFresh Employment and Training (CFET) Sanctioned, and Able-Bodied Adult Without Dependents (ABAWD) individuals not meeting work requirements will count in their entirety to the remaining HH members. The resources of ineligible students will be considered unavailable to the remaining HH members. Resources for HHs with Sponsored Non- Citizens The resources of a sponsor and the sponsor’s spouse (if the spouse signed the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services [USCIS] Form I-864 or I-864A) will be deemed to the sponsored noncitizen and will be considered in determining the HH’s eligibility. • The amount deemed to the non-citizen’s HH will be the total amount of the sponsor’s resources reduced by $1,500. If a sponsored non-citizen verifies that their sponsor is responsible for other sponsored non-citizens, the sponsor’s resources will be deemed and divided equally among all sponsored individuals applying for or receiving CalFresh. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Resource Eligibility Determination Number Page 63-201 3 of 5 • If the non-citizen does not provide verification, the full resource amount will be deemed to the applicant until the information is received. If the non-citizen changes sponsors during the certification period, deemed resources will be recalculated using the new sponsor’s information. Resources of Residents in Battered Person Shelters Eligible residents of shelters for battered persons must be certified based on the resources the HH members have on the date of application, and their resource level as of the date of their interview. If resources are held jointly with members of their former HH from which they fled and access to the resources requires consent of the former HH member, those resources will be considered inaccessible. 3. R esource Evaluations Evaluate resource eligibility for HHs that are non- CE and non-MCE at application, Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7) and at recertification. Use the information reported on the application, SAR 7, and recertification forms to determine continuing eligibility for the certification period or remaining months of the certification period. • CalFresh HHs are not required to report any changes related to property mid- period; do not take action mid-period on any voluntary reported change in property that will result in a decrease or discontinuance of benefits. • Discontinue the case at the end of the SAR 7 or recertification submit month with timely notice if the HH exceeds the resource limit based on property reported. If the HH provides verification that their resources are within the resource limit prior to the effective date of discontinuance, rescind the negative action as long as the HH continues to meet all other CalFresh eligibility criteria. 4. HH Composition Changes Reported During the Certification Period When a non-CE and non-MCE HH reports a new HH member, it is considered Verified Upon Receipt (VUR) and must be acted on promptly. The new HH member’s income, resources, and other eligibility factors must be evaluated to determine the HH’s continued eligibility and benefit level. The following scenarios demonstrate appropriate actions to take: S cenario 1: A non-CE and non-MCE HH voluntarily reports a new HH member and provides adequate information and verification. If the reported change would result in… then… a decrease or discontinuance of benefits, do not add the new HH member, send the HH a no-change NOA, document the information in the case record, and followup on the HH composition change at the next mandatory report (SAR 7 or recertification). an increase in benefits, add the new HH member and re-evaluate CalFresh eligibility. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Resource Eligibility Determination Number Page 63-201 4 of 5 Scenario 2: A non-CE and non-MCE HH voluntarily reports a new HH member and does not provide adequate information or verification. As a result, it is unknown how adding the new HH member will impact the HH’s benefits and a CW 2200 must be sent to request necessary information or verification. If the HH… then… provides the required information and/or verification and the reported change would result in a decrease or discontinuance of CalFresh benefits, do not add the new HH member, send the HH a nochange NOA, document the information in the case record, and follow-up on the HH composition change at the next mandatory report (SAR 7 or recertification). provides the required information and/or verification and the reported change would result in an increase in benefits, add the new HH member and re-evaluate CalFresh eligibility. does not provide adequate information and/or verification to add the new HH member, do not add the new HH member, send the HH a nochange NOA, document the information in the case record, and follow-up on the HH composition change at the next mandatory report (SAR 7 or recertification). 5. T ransfer of Resources During initial application, the HH must provide information regarding resources that have been transferred within the three-month period immediately preceding the date of application. This includes excluded HH members’ resources that are considered available to the HH. The following resource transfers will not affect eligibility to the CalFresh program: • Excluded resources. • Have been sold or traded at, or near, fair market value. • Transferred between members of the same HH, including ineligible non-citizens or disqualified HH members, whose resources are considered available to the HH. • Transferred for reasons other than qualifying or attempting to qualify for CalFresh benefits, for example, a parent placing funds into an educational trust fund. A pplicants who knowingly transfer resources for the purpose of qualifying for CalFresh benefits will be denied and sent a Notice of Action (NOA) explaining the denial reason and disqualification period. The disqualification period will begin with the month of application. HHs that are already participating when the transfer is discovered will be discontinued and sent a NOA explaining the discontinuance reason and length of the disqualification period. The disqualification period will begin with the first day of the month following timely notice. D etermine the length of the disqualification period by: • Adding the value of the transferred resource to the total countable resource value. • Subtract the resource limit from the total amount of resource value. • The amount over the resource limit is used to determine the length of the disqualification period.
