title: 63-235 Shelter Costs and Utility Allowances
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Shelter Expenses and Utility Allowances Number Page 63-235 1 of 7 Revision Date: 01/01/2026 Background: CalFresh households (HH s) are eligible to deduct allowable shelter and utility expenses from their income to determine CalFresh eligibility. Purpose: This section is being updated to provide new guidance on the policy change regarding State Utility Assistance Subsidy (SUAS) eligibility. Policy: The excess shelter deduction is the portion of a HH’s monthly shelter and utility expenses that exceed 50 percent of the HH’s income after all other allowable deductions have been applied. This deduction is limited to the maximum amount established by the California Department of Social Services (CDSS), unless the HH includes an elderly or disabled (E/D) member, in which case no maximum limit applies. The following sections outline the types of shelter expenses and utility allowances that may be included when calculating the excess shelter deduction. 1. Shelter Expense Shelter expense is the amount the HH is responsible to pay for the home they reside in, the following is a list of allowable expenses related to shelter: • Rent. • Mortgage. • Homeowner’s association (HOA) fees. • Loan payments for the purchase of a mobile home, including interest on such payments. • Property taxes, state, and local assessments. • Insurance on the structure itself, but not separate costs for insuring furniture or personal belongings. • Space rent in a mobile home park. • Costs for the repair of the home, which was substantially damaged or destroyed due to a natural disaster such as a fire or flood. • Costs of a home temporarily not occupied by the HH because of employment or training away from home, illness, or abandonment caused by natural disaster or casualty as long as one of the following exists: o HH intends to return to the home. o The current occupants, if any, must not be claiming the same shelter expense for CalFresh purposes on another case. o The home must not be leased or rented during the absence of the HH. The following payments are excluded from the shelter expense: • One-time deposits, such as security deposits. • Penalty fees for making late payments. • Costs for home repairs that have been or will be reimbursed by private or public agencies, insurance companies, or from any other source. • Garage rental. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Shelter Expenses and Utility Allowances Number Page 63-235 2 of 7 • Shelter expenses claimed as a business expense. Apply the corresponding income conversion factors, 4.33, 2.167, or 2 when the HH is billed rent on a weekly, bi -weekly or semi -monthly basis , respectively . Use the conversion factor only when a full month’s expense is anticipated to continue throughout the certification period. When a HH chooses to or is obligated to pay rent in advance , allow the monthly amount of the rent obligation each month, regardless of when it is paid. Example: Scenario HH’s monthly rent is $1,000. The HH chooses to pay the landlord a year’s rent in advance totaling $12,000. Outcome The HH will be allowed a monthly shelter expense of $1,000 in the CalFresh budget. 2. Shared Shelter Expense The HH may reside with and share the shelter expense with excluded or ineligible HH member s, or with another separate HH. The table below provides guidance on calculating the portion of the shelter expense that is allowed as a deduction. If the shelter expense is shared with… then… a separate HH, allow the amount paid by the CalFresh HH. If the amount paid cannot be differentiated per HH, the shelter expense will be divided by the number of HHs contributing to the expense. an Intentional Program Violation (IPV) disqualified and/or work sanctioned individual(s) who otherwise would be an eligible HH member, allow the entire shelter expense including the IPV and/or work sanctioned individual’s portion. an ineligible noncitizen, Social Security Number (SSN) disqualified individual or timed out Able- Bodied Without Dependent (ABAWD) individual who contributes to the shelter expense from their own income or resources, prorate the shelter expense among all eligible and ineligible HH members. Count only the eligible members’ portion. an ineligible noncitizen, SSN disqualified individual or timed out ABAWD individual who does not have their own income or resources to contribute to the shelter expense, do not consider the ineligible noncitizen’s, SSN disqualified individual’s or timed out ABAWD’s income in the proration of the shelter expense if proration is needed. an ineligible student that contributes a set dollar amount to the shelter expense or does not contribute at all, allow the entire shelter expense excluding the student’s contribution. an ineligible student that contributes to the shelter expense but the amount they contribute cannot be differentiated from the rest of the HH, prorate the shelter expense among eligible and ineligible HH members. Count only the eligible members’ portion. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Shelter Expenses and Utility Allowances Number Page 63-235 3 of 7 Note: If a HH contains multiple ineligible noncitizens and/or SSN disqualified individuals, if at least one of them contributes or has income , then include all the ineligible noncitizens and/or SSN disqualified individuals in the proration calculation. Example: Scenario HH consists of ineligible noncitizen mom and 2 United States (US) citizen children. Mom works and contributes to the rent and the children receive CalWORKs. Total rent is $1200 per month. Outcome Mom is an ineligible noncitizen that contributes her earnings from work to the rent, therefore mom is included in the proration. $1200 / 3 (mom and 2 children) = $400 per person. Since there are only 2 eligible HH members $400 X 2 (2 eligible children) = $800 is allowed as the deduction. Example: Scenario HH consists of ineligible noncitizen dad, eligible noncitizen mom, and 2 US citizen children. Dad has no income. Mom and the children receive CalWORKs. Total rent is $1200 per month. Outcome Dad has no income therefore lacking the means to contribute, so he is not included in the proration. The entire rent of $1200 is allowed as the deduction. Example: Scenario HH consists of ineligible noncitizen mom, 3 US citizen children and 1 unrelated adult that does not Purchase and Prepare (P&P) with the CalFresh HH. Mom works and contributes to the rent, 2 of the children receive CalWORKs, 1 of the children is 20 years old and an ineligible student, who does not contribute to the rent, and the unrelated adult contributes $200 to the rent. Total rent is $1000. Outcome Since the unrelated adult is considered a separate HH, first deduct their portion of the rent from the total, $1000 - $200 (unrelated adult’s contribution) = $800. Since the ineligible student does not contribute, subtract zero from the remaining rent, $800 - $0 (ineligible student’s contribution) = $800. Since mom contributes, she is included in the proration with the 2 children receiving CalWORKs, $800 / 3 (mom and 2 children) = $266.67 per person. $266.67 X 2 (2 eligible children) = $533.33 allowed as the deduction. Example: Scenario HH consists of an ineligible IPV mom who has earned income, 2 US citizen children, and ineligible noncitizen grandmother who P&Ps with the HH and contributes $150 to the rent each month. Total rent is $1200. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Shelter Expenses and Utility Allowances Number Page 63-235 4 of 7 Outcome The known contribution of grandmother is not deducted as she P&Ps with the HH. She is included in the proration, but her portion is not allowed as part of the deduction. $1200 / 4 (total HH members) = $300 per person. $300 X 3 (IPV mom and 2 eligible children) = $900 allowed as the deduction. 3. Utility Allowances There are three different utility allowances to which a HH may be eligible. Utility allowances are adjusted to the cost-of-living. The table below explains the different types of allowances and gives guidance on when to include them in the benefit calculation. The HH is eligible to the… if the HH incurs an expense for… Standard Utility Allowance (SUA), heating or cooling (for example, gas, electricity, butane, propane, coal, or firewood) whether paid to the utility company directly, the landlord, or to someone with whom the HH shares the expense, and the expense is separate from their rent. Limited Utility Allowance (LUA), at least two of the following utilities: telephone, water, sewer, and garbage or trash collection, but does not incur an expense for heating and cooling. Telephone Utility Allowance (TUA), only a phone or in its absence, an equivalent form of communication (for example, internet for email, prepaid phone card, line for a fax machine), whether billed to them or someone else. Example: Scenario The HH is charged a flat amount of $250 for rent and a separate flat amount of $50 (paid separate from rent) for gas and electric. The HH writes a check to the landlord for $300. Outcome Allow the SUA deduction. Example: Scenario The HH is charged $300 for rent, which includes utilities used for heating and cooling. Outcome Do not allow the SUA deduction because the expense is not separate from the rent. Refer to the current CalFresh Assistance Standards Chart for utility allowance amounts. 4. State Utility Assistance Subsidy (SUAS) SUAS is a payment that provides HHs with a cash amount of $20.01, and entitles the HH to the SUA deduction. Issue the SUAS payment only if the HH contains an E/D HH member and the HH will receive more benefits or become eligible for CalFresh as a result of the SUA deduction. Do not issue SUAS to HHs that: • Do not include an E/D HH member. • Are already eligible to the SUA deduction because they incur heating or cooling expense. • Are already receiving the maximum benefit allotment for their HH size. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Shelter Expenses and Utility Allowances Number Page 63-235 5 of 7 • Are unhoused and would receive a higher benefit from the homeless shelter deduction. Refer to Desk Aid SUAS for SUA Flowchart for more information. Note: A CalFresh HH that includes an E/D HH member who is excluded or ineligible for CalFresh qualifies the household for a SUAS payment as long as all other eligibility criteria are met. Example: Scenario The E/D HH filed an initial application on November 17. The HH does not incur a heating or cooling expense, therefore not entitled to the SUA deduction. It is determined the HH is eligible to the maximum CalFresh allotment for its HH size. Outcome The E/D HH is not eligible to receive the SUAS because they are already receiving the maximum allotment. Example: Scenario The E/D HH filed an initial application on November 17. The HH does not incur a heating or cooling expense, therefore not entitled to the SUA deduction. It is determined that the HH is eligible to CalFresh but not the maximum allotment for their HH size. If the HH had the SUA deduction, the benefit amount would increase. Outcome The E/D HH is eligible to SUAS since it will increase their benefits, and the $20.01 payment should be issued. The SUA deduction will now be included in the benefit calculation. Note: When determining eligibility to Expedited Services (ES) use the actual utility allowance for the expenses the HH incurs. Do not account for SUAS when evaluating ES. If eligible, and upon approval of the case, the HH can then be issued the SUAS payment of $20.01. Evaluate for SUAS at application, recertification, Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7), or mid-period if a change is reported that could potentially make the HH eligible to it . HHs are eligible to the SUA deduction effective the month the $20.01 SUAS payment is issued. The SUA deduction cannot be applied for any month prior to the issuance of the SUAS payment. Example: Scenario The E/D HH filed an initial application on November 17. The HH did not incur a heating or cooling expense and was not eligible to the SUA deduction. It is determined the HH is not receiving the maximum shelter deduction, but if the HH had the SUA deduction they would be eligible to increased benefits. The case was approved for November and ongoing on December 5 and the SUAS payment was issued December 6. Outcome Since the case was approved and the SUAS payment was not issued until December, then the HH is eligible to the SUA deduction for the month of December through the remainder of the certification period. The HH is not eligible County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Shelter Expenses and Utility Allowances Number Page 63-235 6 of 7 to the SUA deduction in the November budget because they did not receive the SUAS payment until the month after November. When a HH receives the $20.01 SUAS payment, they are eligible to the SUA deduction for a maximum of 12 consecutive months, however there are instances when the HH could receive multiple SUAS payments in a 12-month period. The table below provides guidance on when to issue a SUAS payment and for how long the HH is eligible to the SUA deduction based on receiving the payment. If the HH… then the HH… is certified for 12 months, and is eligible to and receives the SUAS payment at intake or recertification, is eligible to the SUA deduction for the entire certification period. is certified for 12 months, and is eligible to and receives the SUAS payment based on information reported on the SAR 7 or information reported mid-period, is eligible to the SUA deduction for the rest of the certification period. HHs that receive the SUAS payment mid-period will receive another SUAS payment at recertification, if still eligible to it. is certified for 12 months, received a SUAS payment, and is restoring their benefits, is not eligible to another SUAS payment if they already received one during the certification period but will continue to be allowed the SUA deduction for the remainder of it. received the SUAS payment but the case discontinued before the end of the 12-month certification period. The HH reapplies after the restoration period and is still eligible to SUAS, is issued another SUAS payment making them eligible to the SUA deduction for the entire new 12-month certification period. is certified for 24 months, and is eligible to and receives the SUAS payment at intake or recertification, is eligible to the SUA deduction for the first 12 months and must be re-evaluated for SUAS at the SAR 7. If eligible they will receive another SUAS payment and be allowed the SUA deduction for the remaining 12 months of the certification period. is certified Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP), eligible to and receives the SUAS payment at intake or recertification, is eligible to the SUA deduction for the first 12 months and will have SUAS reissued automatically at the 13th and 25th month as long as no changes have been reported that make them ineligible for SUAS. The SUAS payment is issued via Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) card as a cash benefit . Ensure that the cash account is activated when issuing SUAS payments. When a HH is eligible to SUAS they must be issued a Notice To All CalFresh Recipients (CF 1) informing them of the SUAS payment provided on their EBT card. SUAS payments issued in error are not considered an overissuance. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Shelter Expenses and Utility Allowances Number Page 63-235 7 of 7 5. Shared Utilities Do not prorate SUA, LUA, or TUA when the HH lives with and shares utility expenses with an excluded or ineligible HH member, or when the CalFresh HH lives with and shares utility expenses with another HH. 6. SUAS and Transitional CalFresh (TCF) HHs transitioning from Public Assistance CalFresh (PACF) to TCF that were receiving the SUA deduction will continue to receive it. Do not issue the SUAS payment to a TCF case if the PACF HH was not receiving the SUA deduction. Evaluate TCF HHs that transition to regular CalFresh for the SUAS payment and the SUA deduction at the time of transitioning. 7. SUAS and Inter-County Transfers (ICTs) HHs transferring from another county that already received the SUAS payment from the sending county will not receive another SUAS payment during the same certification period. Communicate with the sending county to ensure that duplicate SUAS payments are not issued in the same certification period. References: Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 63-502.36, 63-502.37. Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 273.9(d)(6). All County Letter (ACL) 12-61, 13-35, 14-66, 25-68. All County Welfare Directors Letter (ACWDL) 6-30-14. All County Information Notice (ACIN) I-34-04. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 12/31/2028. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-247 Substantial Lottery or Gambling Winnings
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageSubstantial Lottery or Gambling Winnings 63-247 1 of 2 Revision Date: 04/01/2022 Background: Substantial lottery or gambling winnings is considered a mandatory mid-period report. Purpose: This section details the reporting requirements and eligibility rules for substantial lottery or gambling winnings. Information about substantial lottery or gambling winnings is being removed from 63-283 and moved to 63-247. No changes are being made due to state legislation. Clarification is being added regarding the determination of substantial lottery or gambling winnings when customers report multiple winnings. Policy: Substantial lottery or gambling winnings are defined as a cash prize won in a single game, purchase of a ticket, or similar bet. Substantial lottery or gambling winnings that are equal to or greater than the elderly or disabled (E/D) resource limit will make a household (HH) ineligible to CalFresh. Substantial lottery or gambling winnings must be reported within 10 calendar days of receipt of the winnings. Substantial lottery or gambling winnings that are received prior to initial application do not need to be reported. Refer to the CalFresh Assistance Standards Chart in Eligibility Essentials for the current E/D resource limit. 1. Determination of Substantial Lottery or Gambling Winnings: The dollar amount of the substantial lottery or gambling winnings is determined before taxes or any other withholding. Substantial lottery or gambling winnings should be evaluated individually and not combined or added together. If the HH member shared the winnings with a non-HH member, the portion allocated to the HH is the amount that will be used to determine if the amount exceeds the E/D resource limit. This requirement applies even if the HH immediately spends or loses the winnings, and the remaining winnings are below the E/D resource limit. Below is an example of substantial lottery or gambling winnings determination: Scenario: Customer reports the following winnings to the county. Customer reports that all winnings have been spent. Month Dollar Amount of Winnings August 15 $1500 September 4 $1000 September 10 $ 900 September 24 $1400 October 5 $ 600 Outcome: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageSubstantial Lottery or Gambling Winnings 63-247 2 of 2 Each winning will be evaluated individually and not combined. The customer did not exceed the E/D resource limit of $3750 in any one winning. No action is required, case remains active. 2. Required Action: When substantial lottery or gambling winnings are reported verify the winnings. If the winnings are equal to or greater than the E/D resource limit, discontinue the entire HH with timely notice. A verbal declaration of winnings is acceptable, and no verification will be necessary. Staff must document the declaration in the case record. A HH discontinued for the receipt of substantial lottery or gambling winnings will remain ineligible until the HH’s income and resources do not exceed the resource and income limits. 3. Reapplication After Discontinuance: HH’s discontinued due to receipt of substantial lottery or gambling winnings may reapply for CalFresh at any time. HH reapplying will not be considered Categorically Eligible (CE) or Modified-Categorically Eligible (MCE). The CalFresh gross income, net income and resource test must be applied. This requirement only applies the first time a HH is certified following the discontinuance for substantial lottery or gambling winnings, regardless of the length of time between the discontinuance and reapplication. At the time of reapplication, if the HH composition has changed, this will be considered a distinctly different HH than the one that was previously discontinued due to substantial lottery or gambling winnings. Staff will process this as a regular CalFresh application and not apply the substantial lottery or gambling winning policies. This includes when the primary and sole applicant is the recipient of the substantial lottery or gambling winnings. Note: Staff must use BENDS 59282 when a case must be discontinued or when a HH reapplies after being discontinued due to substantial lottery or gambling winnings until the system is updated. 4. Informing HH of Reporting Requirement: Staff must verbally inform new and existing HH’s of the substantial lottery and gambling winnings reporting requirement during the initial certification and recertification interview. The information on this new reporting requirement is part of the recorded rights and responsibilities. Confirmation that the HH was verbally informed of the substantial lottery or gambling winnings reporting requirement must be documented in case record. References: ACL 20-132; Policy Interpretation 21-60 (12/27/2021) Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 04/30/2025. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-251 Prospective Budgeting and Reasonably Anticipated Income
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Prospective Budgeting and Reasonably Anticipated Income Number Page 63-251 1 of 4 Revision Date: 05/01/2024 Background: CalFresh benefits for the certification period must be determined using prospective budgeting and reasonably anticipated income. Purpose: This section describes the use of prospective budgeting and reasonably anticipated income to calculate CalFresh allotments. This section is being re -formatted after sunset review, there are no changes due to legislative updates. Policy: Reasonably anticipated income and prospective budgeting are defined below: Term Definition Prospective Budgeting The computation of a household (HH)’s CalFresh allotment, based on an estimate of income and circumstances which will exist. Reasonably Anticipated Income Any anticipated income the HH and staff are reasonably certain will be received during the certification period. Prospective budgeting must be applied to calculate a (HH’s) reasonably anticipated income and expenses for the purpose of determining benefits for a certification period, at: • Application • Semi-Annual Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7) • Recertification • When a HH is over Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) • When information reported is Verified Upon Receipt (VUR) Income that will or won’t be reasonably anticipated, changes in income and/or expenses, calculation(s) applied, effective dates, and any case actions taken must be documented in the case record. 1. Reasonably Anticipated Income: Reasonably anticipated income will be counted only in the month(s) it is expected to be received. The portion of income that is uncertain, because of when it will be received or amount expected, will not be counted. A HH that is reasonably certain of the income that will be received but the monthly amount may fluctuate, may elect to have their income averaged. For income to be reasonably anticipated the following must be known to staff and the HH: • Income that has or will be received. • Amount of the income is known and verified. • Start date of the income is known and verified. 2. Stable Income: Whenever a HH has stable income and does not expect any changes for the certification period, the worker will use either exact monthly figure that can be anticipated for each month of the certification period. Stable income received weekly or bi-weekly will be converted into a monthly average. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Prospective Budgeting and Reasonably Anticipated Income Number Page 63-251 2 of 4 3. Fluctuating Income: Income that varies each month during the certification period is considered fluctuating income. To budget fluctuating income eligibility staff must count the amount of income that a HH can reasonably anticipate during the certification period. If the averaged amount does not accurately reflect the HH’s actual circumstances, calculate the income based on the amount that can be anticipated. Fluctuating income that cannot be anticipated will not be in the budget. Staff may use the most recently reported information when fluctuating income meets the following criteria: • Income is seasonal. • Income varies to the extent that a projection of future income cannot be anticipated. • Income is unknown by how much or when it will be received. Note: When a HH is unable to estimate income, staff may assist by contacting the employer or other source of income with written authorization from the HH member. 4. Contract/Self-Employment Income: Contract and self -employment income must be averaged over the period the income is intended to cover. HHs who receive their annual income by contract or self -employment in a period shorter than a year, will have their income averaged over the period the business has been in operation. HHs that receive contracted income may include school employees, sharecroppers, farmers, and self - employed individuals. These provisions do not apply to migrant or seasonal farm workers. Please refer to the example below: Example 1 Scenario A HH applies for CalFresh in June, a member of the HH receives income that is considered contract/self-employment from August to April. The HH reports the job stops in April and expects to return in August. The HH member received the following income: Aug. Sep. Oct. Nov Dec. Jan Feb. Mar Apr. $1,600 $1,600 $1,600 $1,200 $1,200 $1,200 $1600 $1600 $1600 Outcome To calculate average monthly income for the certification period, the income received from August to April must be averaged for the year as follows: HH total income for the year $13,200 Months in a year 12 Average monthly income $ 1,100 5. Income Verification: Eligibility and benefit amount for the certification period will be determined based on income verifications requested during the past 30 days, unless the income: • Is not expected to continue. • Is not representative of what the HH expects to receive during the certification period. • Fluctuates to the extent that a 30-day period cannot be accurately anticipated. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Prospective Budgeting and Reasonably Anticipated Income Number Page 63-251 3 of 4 A longer period of income history can be requested if it will provide a more accurate indication of future income. HHs with fluctuating seasonal income may use, the most recent season comparable to the certification period, rather than the last 30 days. 6. Counting Income that is Ending: Income that is ending will be used to determine eligibility and benefit amount in the month in which it was reasonably anticipated to be received. Below are some examples on ending income: Example: Application Scenario A HH applies on the 25th of the month and reports income ended on the 21st of the same month. Income was received bi-weekly, paychecks viewed for the 7th $400 and 21st $380. Outcome The income total of $780 will be used to determine benefits for the application month only and not will not be counted for ongoing months. Factoring will not be applied. Example: Recertification Scenario A HH reports on the 26th day of the recertification month, income ended on the 3rd of the previous month, last amount received was $500. Outcome No income will count effective the month of the new certification period. The income received in the recertification month can no longer be reasonably anticipated. Example: SAR 7 Scenario A HH reports on the 6th of the submit month, income ended on the 7th of the data month, amount received was $800. Outcome No income will count effective the month of the new certification period. The income received in the submit month can no longer be reasonably anticipated. 7. Reasonably Anticipated Expenses: As part of prospective budgeting s taff must reasonably anticipate a HHs expenses over the certification period. A HH’s most recent bills will be used to anticipate the expenses, unless the HH is reasonably certain a change will occur. HHs reporting a one -time expense during the certification period may elect: • A one-time deduction in the month the expense was billed or • The expense averaged over the remaining months of the certification period A deduction is allowed for the month the expense was billed or comes due, regardless of when the HH intends to pay the expense. Amounts carried forward from past billing periods are not deductible, even if included with the most recent billing and actually paid by the HH. For additional information on deductions, refer to chapter 63-230. 8. Fluctuating Expenses: Fluctuating e xpenses may be average d over the certification period , only if they are regularly recurring, reasonably anticipated, and verified to recur over the certification period. The HH may elect to average expenses billed less often than monthly over the certification period or claim the expenses in the month billed. Fluctuating expenses include but are not limited to: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Prospective Budgeting and Reasonably Anticipated Income Number Page 63-251 4 of 4 • Medical services • Medical treatments received • Prescribed medication Note: Past expenses will be used only as an indicator of the expenses that are estimated or reasonably anticipated during the certification period. References: ACL: 17-35, 15-42, 12-25 MPP 63-503 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 05/31/2027. Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Prospective Budgeting and Reasonably Anticipated Income Number Page 63-251 1 of 4 Revision Date: 05/01/2024 Background: CalFresh benefits for the certification period must be determined using prospective budgeting and reasonably anticipated income. Purpose: This section describes the use of prospective budgeting and reasonably anticipated income to calculate CalFresh allotments. This section is being re -formatted after sunset review, there are no changes due to legislative updates. Policy: Reasonably anticipated income and prospective budgeting are defined below: Term Definition Prospective Budgeting The computation of a household (HH)’s CalFresh allotment, based on an estimate of income and circumstances which will exist. Reasonably Anticipated Income Any anticipated income the HH and staff are reasonably certain will be received during the certification period. Prospective budgeting must be applied to calculate a (HH’s) reasonably anticipated income and expenses for the purpose of determining benefits for a certification period, at: • Application • Semi-Annual Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7) • Recertification • When a HH is over Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) • When information reported is Verified Upon Receipt (VUR) Income that will or won’t be reasonably anticipated, changes in income and/or expenses, calculation(s) applied, effective dates, and any case actions taken must be documented in the case record. 1. Reasonably Anticipated Income: Reasonably anticipated income will be counted only in the month(s) it is expected to be received. The portion of income that is uncertain, because of when it will be received or amount expected, will not be counted. A HH that is reasonably certain of the income that will be received but the monthly amount may fluctuate, may elect to have their income averaged. For income to be reasonably anticipated the following must be known to staff and the HH: • Income that has or will be received. • Amount of the income is known and verified. • Start date of the income is known and verified. 2. Stable Income: Whenever a HH has stable income and does not expect any changes for the certification period, the worker will use either exact monthly figure that can be anticipated for each month of the certification period. Stable income received weekly or bi-weekly will be converted into a monthly average. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Prospective Budgeting and Reasonably Anticipated Income Number Page 63-251 2 of 4 3. Fluctuating Income: Income that varies each month during the certification period is considered fluctuating income. To budget fluctuating income eligibility staff must count the amount of income that a HH can reasonably anticipate during the certification period. If the averaged amount does not accurately reflect the HH’s actual circumstances, calculate the income based on the amount that can be anticipated. Fluctuating income that cannot be anticipated will not be in the budget. Staff may use the most recently reported information when fluctuating income meets the following criteria: • Income is seasonal. • Income varies to the extent that a projection of future income cannot be anticipated. • Income is unknown by how much or when it will be received. Note: When a HH is unable to estimate income, staff may assist by contacting the employer or other source of income with written authorization from the HH member. 4. Contract/Self-Employment Income: Contract and self -employment income must be averaged over the period the income is intended to cover. HHs who receive their annual income by contract or self -employment in a period shorter than a year, will have their income averaged over the period the business has been in operation. title: 63-252 Households with Migrant or Seasonal Farmworkers
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Households with Migrant or Seasonal Farmworkers 63-252 1 of 5 Revision Date: 07/01/2022 Background: Migrant and seasonal farmworker households (HH) are eligible to special income calculations if they meet specific destitute criteria for CalFresh purposes. Purpose: The following section shall be used to determine when migrant or seasonal farmworker HHs meet the destitute criteria therefore entitling them to special income calculations for the application month or first month of the certification period. No policy changes have been made. This section is being relocated to 63-252 and reformatted to remove information pertaining to boarders, which is now found in Section 63-225. Policy: At application and recertification all migrant or seasonal farmworker HH’s are to be screened to see if they meet the destitute criteria. Destitute evaluations are limited solely to migrant or seasonal farmworker HHs, other types of HHs are not eligible to this evaluation. A migrant or seasonal farmworker HH meets the destitute criteria if its only income during the month of application is either: •From a terminated source •From a new source •A combination of terminated and a new source The sections below provide further details into the 3 criteria and if the HH meets any of the criteria, how to determine if they are eligible to Expedited Services (ES) and calculate the first month’s benefits. 1. Income from a Terminated Source: The table below provides guidance on how to determine if income is from a terminated source based on its payment frequency. If income is received… then the income will be considered as coming from a terminated source… monthly, semi-monthly, biweekly, weekly, or daily, if the HH will not receive any more payments from the source in the remaining days of the application month or during the month following the application. annually, semi-annually, quarterly, or bi-monthly, if the HH will not receive any more payments from the source in the remaining days of the application month or month in which the next payment would normally be received. Example: Income not considered coming from a terminated source Scenario A migrant farmworker applies for benefits on August 20. She reports that her job will be ending, and she will receive her last paycheck on August 27. She will not receive any more paychecks after the August 27. Outcome The income is not considered to be from a terminated source since she will receive one more check in the remaining days of the application month. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Households with Migrant or Seasonal Farmworkers 63-252 2 of 5 Example: Terminated source of income received weekly Scenario A migrant farmworker applies for benefits on July 16 and reports that work with a local grower ended in early July and that he got his last weekly pay on July 15. He will not receive any more payments from this grower. Outcome The income is considered coming from a terminated source because he will not get any further income from the grower in July or August. Example: Terminated source of income received quarterly Scenario A migrant farmworker applies for benefits on January 15. He reported his job terminated and he was paid on a quarterly basis (e.g., January 1, April 1, July 1, and October 1). He reports receiving his last paycheck on January 1. He will not receive any more payments from this grower. Outcome The income is considered coming from a terminated source since the HH does not anticipate receiving a payment in April. 2. Income from a New Source: The table below provides guidance on how to determine if income is from a new source based on its payment frequency. If income is received… then the income will be considered as coming from a new source… monthly, semi-monthly, biweekly, weekly, or daily, if income of more than $25 from that source was not received in the 30 days before the application. annually, semi-annually, quarterly, or bi-monthly, if income of more than $25 was not received within the last normal interval between payments. Example: Income not considered coming from a new source Scenario A migrant farmworker HH applies on September 5. The only income expected for the application month is pay from a job with a new grower. Work began on August 20, and she received her first check on September 1 in the amount of $65. Outcome The income is not considered to be from a new source because she received income of more than $25 from the new source within 30 days of the application. Example: New source of income received monthly Scenario A migrant farmworker applies on April 5. At application he reports he started working for a new grower on March 25. He will be paid weekly and received his first paycheck from the new grower on April 1 for $20, he will not get his next check until April 8. Outcome The income is considered to be from a new source because he did not receive income of more than $25 from the new grower in the 30 days prior to application. Example: New source of income received quarterly Scenario A migrant farmworker applies on January 5. He states he started a job with a new grower on December 1 and will be paid quarterly. He will receive his first paycheck County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Households with Migrant or Seasonal Farmworkers 63-252 3 of 5 on March 1. Outcome The income is considered to be from a new source because the HH has not received income of more than $25 from the new source from October to the date of application. 3. Income from a Terminated Source and a New Source: Refer to the information in Sections 1 and 2 above for guidance on how to determine if income is from a terminated source and a new source. Example: HH with income from a terminated and new source meeting destitute criteria Scenario A migrant farmworker HH applying on July 10 is part of a crew that moved from one grower to another to harvest different crops. The HH received its last pay from the previous grower on July 8 and will not receive any more income from the grower. He will receive its first pay from the new grower on July 21. Outcome The HH meets destitute criteria, because its only income for the application month is from both new and terminated sources. Note: A migrant farmworker’s source of income/employer is the grower for whom the migrant is working for and not the crew chief. A migrant farmworker who travels with the same crew chief but moves from one grower to another shall be considered to have moved from a terminated income source to a new source. A migrant or seasonal farmworker who changes jobs but continues to work for the same employer shall be considered still receiving income from the same source. 4. Eligibility to ES for HHs Meeting the Destitute Criteria: A migrant or seasonal farmworker HH is eligible to ES if it meets one of the criteria below and their liquid resources do not exceed $100. •The HHs only source of income during the application month is received prior to the application date and is from a terminated source. Example: Scenario A migrant farmworker HH applies on June 10. The migrant farmworker reports he was working but his job terminated June 1. He received his last bi-weekly paycheck on June 5 for $600. He states he has no bank accounts and the only liquid resources he has is $80 cash on hand which is left over from the paycheck he received on June 5. Outcome The HH is eligible to ES because the only source of income in the application month was from a terminated source and received on June 5, which is prior to the application date. In addition, the HHs liquid resources are only $80 which is less than $100. For migrant or seasonal farmworkers, there is no limit as to how much they can earn prior to application to be eligible to ES, unlike all other types of HHs that must have monthly income of less than $150. •The HHs only income for the month of application is from a new source and income of more than $25 from the new source will not be received by the 10th calendar day after the date of application. Example: Scenario A migrant farmworker HH applies on June 10. The migrant farmworker reports County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Households with Migrant or Seasonal Farmworkers 63-252 4 of 5 he started working June 1 and will receive his first monthly paycheck on June 25 in the amount of $500. He states he has no bank accounts and the only liquid resources he has is $80 cash on hand. Outcome The HH is eligible to ES. The income meets the criteria for income from a new source, the HH will not receive more than $25 from the new source within 10 days of the date of application. •The HHs only income is from a terminated source prior to the date of application and no other income from the terminated source will be received in the application month. In addition, income from a new source will be received after the date of application, as long as income of more than $25 from the new source will not be received by the 10th calendar day after the date of application. Note: The $25 maximum from the new source applies to the entire HH. If two people in the HH each received $20 from a new source within ten calendar days after the date of application, the HH does not meet destitute criteria since $40 exceeds $25. 5. Income Calculation at Intake and Recertification for HHs Meeting the Destitute Criteria: HHs that have met the destitute criteria are eligible for special income calculations. The table below explains how the income is calculated at application and recertification. If… then… at application, the HH has met the criteria of income from a terminated source, the application month’s benefits will be calculated by considering only income which is received between the first of the month and the date of application. at application, the HH has met the criteria of income from a new source, any income from the new source that is anticipated after the date of application shall be disregarded in the application months benefit calculation. at recertification, the HH has met the criteria of income from a new source, the income from a new source will be disregarded in the first month of the new certification period if income of more than $25 will not be received from the new source by the 10th calendar day after the date of the HH’s normal issuance date. Note: Subsequent month’s benefits for the certification period will be calculated according to prospective budgeting and reasonably anticipated income procedures, refer to Section 63-282. 6. Treatment of Travel Advances Received by HHs Meeting the Destitute Criteria: Some employers provide travel advances to cover the travel costs of new employees who must journey to the location of their new employment. Travel advances have no effect on the determination of destitute criteria. The payments are considered either a reimbursement or an advance on wages and should be treated accordingly. If the travel advance is … then … considered a reimbursement, the income is excluded per Section 63-224. by written contract, an advance on wages that will be subtracted from wages later earned by the employee, the wage advance will count as income per Section 63-222. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Households with Migrant or Seasonal Farmworkers 63-252 5 of 5 Example: Travel advance given as a reimbursement Scenario HH applies on May 10. On May 1 he received a $50 travel check for travel expenses from his new employer. He will not receive his first regular paycheck until May 31, therefore the HH meets destitute criteria. Outcome Disregard both the May 31 paycheck and the travel expenses as income in the application month. Example: Travel advance given as an advance on wages Scenario HH applies on May 10 and received a $50 travel advance on May 1 but will not receive any other wages from the employer until May 30, therefore the HH meets destitute criteria. Outcome The May 30 payment shall be disregarded from the budget calculation for the month of application, but the wage advance received prior to the date of application will be counted as income. References: MPP 63-503.43, CFR 273.10(e)(3) Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 07/31/2025 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-254 Gross and Net Income Calculations and Benefit Allotment
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Gross and Net Income Calculations and Benefit Allotment Determination Number Page 63-254 1 of 5 Revision Date: 05/01/2024 Background: Federal regulation requires households (HH) to meet specific income limits to be income eligible for CalFresh. Purpose: This section demonstrates how to calculate the CalFresh budget and determine the HH’s benefit allotment. It explains the gross and net income tests that HHs must pass to be potentially eligible to benefits. Policy: A HH’s income shall be determined a t intake, Semi-Annual Report period, recertification, or when a mid-period change is acted upon. The monthly income shall then be compared to the gross and net income limits, for the appropriate HH size, to determine eligibility and benefit level. 1. Use of Conversion Factors: When a HH receives gross income or is billed for an expense on a weekly, bi-weekly, or semi-monthly basis, the income or expense shall be converted into a monthly amount based on the following: If income is received or an expense is billed… then multiply the average by…. weekly, 4.33 bi-weekly, 2.167 semi-monthly, 2 2. Gross Income Test: Gross income is the combined earned and unearned income of all HH members from any source that is not excluded. HH composition directly affects whether the gross income test applies to the HH. The table below demonstrates which HHs are subject to the gross income test and what the gross income limit is for the HH. Refer to Section 63-1101 for the maximum gross income amounts. HH Type Maximum Gross Income Limit HH contains an elderly or disabled member Not subject to the gross income test HH is Categorically Eligible (CE), which means all HH members receive cash assistance - e.g., CalWORKs, General Relief, or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) Not subject to the gross income test HH is Modified Categorically Eligible (MCE) 200% of Federal Poverty Level (FPL) HH contains an Intentional Program Violator (IPV) 130% of FPL The head of HH does not comply with work requirements 130% of FPL Note: When the HH type changes and it becomes entitled to a different maximum gross income limit, staff shall apply the new limit at the next recertification, reported change, or Semi-Annual Report period whichever occurs first. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Gross and Net Income Calculations and Benefit Allotment Determination Number Page 63-254 2 of 5 Follow the steps in the table below to determine if a HH passes the gross income test. Refer to Section 63-101 on how to determine the HH size. Step Action 1. Does the HH contain an elderly or disabled individual or are all HH members in receipt of cash assistance? • If YES – Stop, the gross income test does not apply. • If NO – Go to step 2. 2. Add all gross non-excluded earned and unearned income together. 3. Is anyone in the HH (besides an individual who is an ineligible noncitizen/Social Security Number (SSN) disqualified/fails to meet Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWD) work requirements) responsible for paying legally obligated child support to a non-HH member? • If YES – Proceed to Step 4. • If NO – This is the HH’s total gross income, proceed to Step 5. Note: If an individual who is an ineligible noncitizen/SSN disqualified/fails to meet ABAWD work requirements pays child support, the child support is deducted from their gross income prior to it being prorated. 4. Subtract any child support that is legally obligated to be paid to a non-HH member from the amount calculated in Step 2 to get the HH’s total gross income. 5. Round the HH’s total gross income: • Up if the cents equal 50 – 99. • Down if the cents equal 0 – 49. 6. Compare the HH’s total gross income to the maximum gross income limit for the HH (refer to Section 63-1101 for the current amounts). Is the gross income at or below the FPL for the HH size? • If YES – The HH passes the gross income test and will now have its net income calculated to determine the benefit allotment. • If NO – Deny CalFresh the HH is ineligible based on excess income. 3. Net Income Test: The net income of a HH is the income after all allowable deductions have been subtracted. The net income limit for all HHs is 100% of the FPL. Follow the steps in the table below to calculate the net monthly income for a HH without an elderly or disabled individual. Refer to Section 63-101 on how to determine the HH size. Step Action 1. Gross Unearned Income: a. Add all gross non-excluded unearned income together. b. Subtract legally obligated child support paid, if applicable, from the unearned income calculated in Step 1a (if there is any remaining child support subtract in Step 2d). 2. Gross Earned Income: a. Add all non-excluded gross earned income together. b. Multiply Step 2a by 20%. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Gross and Net Income Calculations and Benefit Allotment Determination Number Page 63-254 3 of 5 c. Subtract Step 2b from Step 2a. d. Subtract the remainder of the legally obligated child support paid (balance from Step 1b), if applicable from Step 2c. 3. Nonexempt Gross Income: Add gross unearned income (Step 1) and the gross earned income (Step 2) together. 4. Adjusted Net Income: From the total nonexempt gross income (Step 3) subtract: a. The standard deduction (refer to 63-1101 for the current amount). b. Dependent care expense, if applicable. c. The homeless shelter deduction, if applicable. 5. Excess Shelter Deduction: (Do not calculate if the HH receives the homeless shelter deduction) a. Add together all shelter expenses e.g., rent, mortgage, property tax, homeowners’ association fees, utility allowances, to get the total shelter cost. b. Calculate 50% of the adjusted net income (Step 4). c. Subtract Step 5b from Step 5a. 6. Allowable Shelter Deduction: a. Subtract the maximum excess shelter deduction (refer to 63-1101 for the current amount) from Step 5. b. The lesser of the Step 6a or the maximum excess shelter deduction (refer to 63-1101 for the current amount) is the allowable shelter deduction. 7. Net Monthly Income: Subtract the allowable shelter deduction (Step 6) from the adjusted net income (Step 4). If the HH contains at least one member who is elderly or disabled, follow the steps in the table below to calculate the HH’s net monthly income. Refer to Section 63-101 on how to determine the HH size. Step Action 1. Gross Unearned Income: a. Add all non-excluded gross unearned income together. b. Subtract legally obligated child support paid, if applicable from Step 2a (if there is any remaining child support subtract in Step 2d). 2. Gross Earned Income: a. Add all non-excluded gross earned income together. b. Multiply Step 2a by 20%. c. Subtract Step 2b from Step 2a. d. Subtract the remainder of the legally obligated child support paid (balance from Step 1b), if applicable from Step 2c. 3. Nonexempt Gross Income: Add gross unearned income (Step 1) and gross earned income (Step 2) together. 4. Adjusted Net Income: From the nonexempt gross income (Step 3) subtract: a. The standard deduction. b. Medical expenses, if applicable. c. Dependent care expense, if applicable. d. The homeless shelter deduction, if applicable. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Gross and Net Income Calculations and Benefit Allotment Determination Number Page 63-254 4 of 5 5. Allowable Shelter Deduction: (Do not calculate if the HH received the homeless shelter deduction) a. Add together all shelter expenses e.g., rent, mortgage, property tax, homeowners’ association fees, utility allowances, to get the total shelter cost. b. Calculate 50% of the adjusted net income (Step 4). c. Subtract Step 5b from Step 5a to get the allowable shelter deduction. Note: There is no maximum shelter deduction for a HH with an elderly or disabled member. 6. Net Income: Subtract the allowable shelter deduction (Step 5) from the adjusted net income (Step 4). Once the net income is calculated for a HH refer to the table below to determine the HH’s eligibility and allotment. Type of HH If the HH is Over the Net Income Limit If the HH is Below the Net Income Limit Non-CE or Non- MCE of any size Deny the application. HH is eligible to CalFresh (refer below for how to determine the HH’s allotment). CE or MCE with 1 or 2 HH members Entitled to the minimum allotment (refer to 63- 1101 for the current minimum allotment). CE or MCE with 3 or more HH members May be entitled to benefits (refer below for how to determine the HH’s allotment). If the allotment is zero, the HH will be denied. Note: Refer to Section 63-120 for more info on CE and MCE. 4. Determining the Allotment: A HH’s allotment may be determined either by using the CalFresh Monthly Allotment Table or by calculating the allotment manually. To determine the HH’s allotment using the CalFresh Monthly Allotment Table , located in Eligibility Essentials under Desk Aids, follow the steps below. Step Action 1. Refer to Desk Aid CalFresh Monthly Allotment Tables and Calculator. 2. Under the Monthly Net Income column find the row that that contains the HH’s net monthly income. 3. Move along the row until you have reached the column that displays the correct HH size. That is the HH’s monthly allotment. Note: The table may show HHs of one or two that are over the net income limit as being eligible to more than the minimum allotment; however, they are only eligible to the minimum allotment and shall not receive more. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Gross and Net Income Calculations and Benefit Allotment Determination Number Page 63-254 5 of 5 To calculate the HH’s allotment manually follow the steps below. Step Action 1. Determine the HH’s total net monthly income. 2. Determine the maximum allotment for the HH size according to CalFresh Maximum Allotment Table (refer to Section 63-1101 for the amount). 3. Multiply the net monthly income as determined in Step 1 by 30%. Round it up to the next whole dollar if ending in 1 – 99 cents. 4. Calculate the CalFresh allotment by subtracting the amount determined in Step 3 from the maximum allotment determined in Step 2. To prorate benefits for the initial month, calculate the HHs allotment, then refer to the Reciprocal Table for Prorating in 63-1101 to calculate the prorated benefit amount. If the HH is eligible to less than $10 in the initial month, benefits will not be issued to the HH for that month. References: MPP 63-503.31-.32 ACL 14-56, 14-63 CFR 273.9(a), 273.10(a), 273.10(e) Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 05/31/2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-255 Treatment of Income and Expenses of Ineligible and Non-Household Members
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Treatment of Income and Expenses of Ineligible and Non- Household Members Number Page 63-255 1 of 5 Revision Date: 05/01/2024 Background: Federal regulation requires special treatment of the income and expenses of households (HH) with ineligible and non-HH members when determining eligibility to CalFresh benefits. Purpose: This section details the treatment of income and expenses of ineligible and non-HH members based on their reason for ineligibility. Policy: Income and expenses shall be evaluated at intake, Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7), recertification, or when a mid-period change is reported. HHs are required to report the income and expenses of ineligible HH members. There are various reasons a HH member may be ineligible to benefits, the reason for the individual’s ineligibility determines the treatment of their income and expenses in the budget. 1. Treatment of the Income of Ineligible or Non-HH Members: Refer to the table below on how to treat the gross income of ineligible and non-HH members: Reason for Ineligibility Treatment of Their Income • Social Security Number (SSN) disqualified • Ineligible noncitizen • Failing to meet Abled Bodied Adult Without Dependents (ABAWD) work requirements Prorate the income, count only the eligible HH member(s) portion. • Intentional Program Violator (IPV) • Fleeing felon • Probation/parole violator • Work sanctioned Count all the income in the budget. • Ineligible student • Non-HH member Income is not considered available to the CalFresh HH. Note: Cash payments from the student or a non-HH member to the eligible HH will be considered unearned income. 2. Proration of Income Calculation: If the HH contains more than one individual who is an ineligible noncitizen/SSN disqualified/failing to meet ABAWD work requirements and at least one of them has income, then all of them shall be included in the proration calculation. Prior to prorating the income, any child support the ineligible HH member pays to an individual outside the home shall be deducted. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Treatment of Income and Expenses of Ineligible and Non- Household Members Number Page 63-255 2 of 5 The following are the steps to prorate income: Step Action 1. Determine the ineligible individual’s income as follows: Ineligible individual’s gross income – ineligible individual’s legally obligated child support paid = ineligible individual’s income. 2. Determine the portion of income per person as follows: Ineligible individual’s income  (eligible HH members + all ineligible HH members) = portion of income per person. 3. Determine the income that should be counted in the budget as follows: Portion of income per person  (eligible HH members + all IPV/work sanctioned/probation or parole violators/fleeing felons in the HH) = income counted in the budget. The following are examples of how to calculate the income when a HH has ineligible or non-HH members: Example: Scenario HH consists of: Mother (ineligible noncitizen) earns $2200 per month, pays $200 per month in child support to a child not in the home. Three children (all US citizens) have no income. Outcome Income $2200 − $200 (child support) = $2000. $2000  4 (mother and three children) = $500. $500  3 (three children who are eligible HH members) = $1500. $1500 will count in the CalFresh budget. Example: Scenario HH consists of: Mother (ineligible noncitizen) earns $2500 per month. Father (ineligible noncitizen) has no income. Three children (all US citizens) have no income. Outcome Income $2500  5 (mother, father, and three children) = $500. $500  3 (three children who are eligible HH members) = $1500. $1500 will count in the CalFresh budget. The father is included in the proration even though he has no income because the mother is also an ineligible noncitizen and she has income. Example: Scenario HH consists of: Mother (ineligible noncitizen) has no income. Three children (all US citizens) receiving CalWORKs of $1130 per month. Outcome $1130 will count in the CalFresh budget. The income will not be prorated because the ineligible noncitizen does not have any income of their own to contribute. Example: Scenario HH consists of: Wife (US citizen) has no income. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Treatment of Income and Expenses of Ineligible and Non- Household Members Number Page 63-255 3 of 5 Husband (US citizen and is an IPV) earns $2000 per month. Outcome $2000 will count in the CalFresh budget. All income of an IPV is counted in the budget and is not subject to proration. 3. Treatment of Income Shared With a Non-HH member: When gross income of one or more CalFresh HH members is combined with the income of a non -HH member, the income of the CalFresh HH members will be determined as follows: If the CalFresh HH member’s portion… then… can be identified, count their portion as income. cannot be distinguished from the non-HH member’s, prorate the income by all those who it is shared by and count the CalFresh HH’s prorated portion as income. The following are the steps for prorating the income when the CalFresh HH member’s portion cannot be distinguished from the non-HH member’s: Step Action 1. Determine the portion of income per person as follows: Total gross income  all people who share the income = portion of income per person. 2. Determine the income that should be counted in the budget as follows: Portion of income per person  number of eligible CalFresh HH members who share the income = income counted in the budget. 4. Treatment of Expenses When the HH Contains an Ineligible or Non-HH Member: Refer to the table below on how to treat the expenses of HHs with an ineligible or non-HH member. Reason for Ineligibility Treatment of Expenses when the Ineligible or Non-HH Member… Pays All of the Expense Contributes but Amount Cannot be Differentiated Contributes a Flat Amount Does Not Contribute • SSN disqualified • Ineligible noncitizen • Failing to meet ABAWD work requirements Prorate, count only the eligible HH member(s) portion. Prorate, count only the eligible HH member(s) portion. Prorate, count only the eligible HH member(s) portion. The entire expense shall be applied to the eligible HH members. • IPV • Fleeing felon • Probation/parole violator • Work sanctioned The entire expense shall be applied to the eligible HH members. The entire expense shall be applied to the eligible HH members. The entire expense shall be applied to the eligible HH members. The entire expense shall be applied to the eligible HH members. • Ineligible student • Non-HH member Count $0 as the expense Prorate, count only the eligible Deduct the contribution from total expense, the The entire expense shall County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Treatment of Income and Expenses of Ineligible and Non- Household Members Number Page 63-255 4 of 5 for the eligible HH. HH member(s) portion. remainder counts for the eligible HH. count for the eligible HH. Note: Utility deductions are never prorated. If the HH contains more than one individual who is an ineligible noncitizen/SSN disqualified/failing to meet ABAWD work requirements and at least one of them contributes to an expense, th en all of them shall be included in the proration calculation. The following are the steps to prorate expenses: Step Action 1. Total expense  (eligible HH members + all ineligible HH members) = portion of expense per person. 2. Portion of expense per person  (eligible HH members + all IPV/work sanctioned/probation or parole violators/fleeing felons in the HH) = expense counted in the budget. The following are examples of how to calculate expenses when a HH has ineligible or non -HH members: Example: Scenario HH consists of: Mother (ineligible noncitizen) has no income. Three children (all US citizens) receive CalWORKs. Rent is $1000 per month. Outcome The HH will be entitled to the entire $1000 shelter expense. Rent is not prorated because the ineligible noncitizen does not contribute. Example: Scenario HH consists of: Mother (ineligible noncitizen) has income and pays the entire rent. Father (ineligible noncitizen) has no income does not contribute to the rent. Three children (all US citizens) no income. Rent is $2000 per month. Outcome Rent $2000  5 (mother, father, and three children) = $400. $400  3 (three children who are eligible HH members) = $1200. The HH will be entitled to a $1200 shelter expense. Dad is included in the proration because a ll ineligible noncitizens are included when at least one ineligible noncitizen contributes. Example: Scenario HH consists of: Mother (US citizen) with earned income. Three children (all US citizens) but one is an ineligible student who contributes $200 per month to the rent. Rent is $2000 per month. Outcome Rent $2000 − $200 (ineligible student’s contribution) = $1800. The HH will be entitled to a $1800 shelter expense. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Treatment of Income and Expenses of Ineligible and Non- Household Members Number Page 63-255 5 of 5 When an ineligible student contributes a flat amount to an expense, the flat amount is deducted from the total expense. 5. Ineligible HH Member that has More than One Reason for Ineligibility: If an ineligible HH member meets two or more reasons for ineligibility, the more stringent category shall be used when determining the treatment of their gross income and deductible expenses. Reason for Ineligibility Additional Reason for Ineligibility Treatment of Their Income and/or Expenses Noncitizen Student Prorate SSN disqualified Failing to meet ABAWD work requirements Noncitizen IPV Count all Fleeing felon/parole violator Work sanctioned SSN disqualified IPV Fleeing felon/parole violator Work sanctioned Failing to meet ABAWD work requirements IPV Fleeing felon/parole violator Work sanctioned Student IPV Fleeing felon/parole violator Work sanctioned The following is an example of an ineligible HH member that meets two ineligibility reasons: Example: Scenario An individual is an ineligible noncitizen and a fleeing felon. Outcome The rules regarding the fleeing felon shall be used. Count all the of the individual’s income (if applicable) in the budget. The entire expense (if applicable) shall be applied to the eligible HH members. References: MPP 63-502.37, 63-503.44; ACL 99-64, 18-90; CFR 273.11(c), 273.11(d) Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 05/31/2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-271 Semi Annual Report (SAR)
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageSemi-Annual Reporting (SAR) 63-271 1 of 4 Revision Date: 06/01/2021 Background: Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) is the simplified reporting option under federal Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) reporting requirements that California elects to use. Recipients are required to submit one Eligibility Status Report Form (SAR 7) in the 6, 12 ,18 or 24 month interval. Purpose: This section includes policies on Household (HH) reporting requirements, responsibilities, mid-period reporting and treatment of the information provided. This section is being reformatted after sunset review. Policy: HHs must be informed at the application interview of SAR requirements. HHs must receive the SAR 7 prior to the end of the data month. The information provided for the SAR data month will be used to determine ongoing eligibility and calculate benefit amounts for the next SAR payment period. Staff must assist the HH in completing the SAR 7 and obtaining all required verifications. Documentation must be entered detailing the type of assistance offered for example, in person, by phone or in writing. For additional information on reasonably anticipated income refer to 63-282. 1. Households’ Reporting Responsibilities: HHs are required to report the following information and or changes on the SAR 7: •HH composition •Address and shelter costs •Medical costs, child support paid and dependent or childcare costs •Resources •Changes exceeding $100 to ongoing unearned income received in the data month •Changes or anticipated changes since the last report (application or recertification) •Earned income •Expenses for the data month 2. Voluntary Mid-Period Information at SAR: Changes reported at SAR 7 that did not occur or were not known to the HH in the data month, will be treated as a voluntary mid-period report. The HH may be entitled to a supplement for the SAR submit month due to the decrease in income. Refer to 64-274 for additional information on increases in benefits. Below are some examples for reported changes that may be considered voluntary midperiod reports: Example: Reported income increase after submitting SAR 7 Scenario A HH provides a SAR 7 on the 8 th of the submit month. The report includes information from the data month. On the 15 th of the submit month, the HH calls to report that her income has increased. She anticipates that this income will continue at this amount for the rest of the semi-annual period. Outcome The SAR 7 was received timely, and the income is not over the Income Reporting Threshold (IRT). The report of increased income will be considered a voluntary midperiod report because the information was unknown to the HH in the data month. The information will not be acted on unless it results in an increase to her benefits. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageSemi-Annual Reporting (SAR) 63-271 2 of 4 Example: Income increase occurred on data month Scenario A HH provides a SAR 7 on the 8th of the submit month. The report includes information from the data month. On the 15th of the submit month, the HH calls to report that her income in the data month was higher than she originally reported. She anticipates that this income will continue at this amount for the rest of the semiannual period. Outcome The SAR 7 was received timely. Information reported should have been provided on her SAR 7, this is considered a correction to her previous report. The income will be considered in determining eligibility and benefit amounts for the certification period. Example: Income decrease reported on SAR 7 submit month Scenario A HH provides a SAR 7 on the 5 th of submit month and reports that their income decreased in the data month. Outcome The SAR 7 was received timely. This information should be treated as a voluntary mid-period report and will be used to calculate the HH’s benefit amount for the next certification period. A supplement may be provided for the submit month if the income decreases and all other factors on the SAR 7 cause a benefit increase. 3. Verification Responsibilities: HHs must provide verification of the information reported on the SAR 7 if applicable, when changes have occurred or if questionable. Contact must be made to confirm the income changes and to identify if the income can be reasonably anticipated. Refer to 63-282 for additional information on prospective budgeting and reasonably anticipated income. Staff must assist the HH in obtaining all required verifications and use available data matches such as The Work Number (WN), Income Eligibility and Verification System (IEVS) or Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS) to verify the information detailed below: •Gross non-excluded earned income (includes self-employment) •Newly reported non-excluded unearned income or when a change exceeding $100 has occurred to previously reported unearned income •Non-excluded income of any sponsor (SAR 72) if applicable, refer to 63-246 for treatment of sponsor’s income •Dependent care costs •Medical expenses, refer to 63-253.8 on processing reported medical expenses •Self-Employment expenses only if the HH is claiming actual expenses and not the 40% standard deduction •Child support payments, or legal obligation to pay child support to a person not in the CalFresh (CF) HH (63-224.15) •Social Security Number (SSN), only when a member is being added to a CF HH (63-161) •The source of excluded income when it is first reported and when there is a change 4. Complete SAR 7 Criteria: HHs are required to submit a complete SAR 7 with verifications needed to determine ongoing eligibility and benefit allotment. HHs are not required to report on the SAR 7 voluntary mid-period information that has been reported and verified. The HH is only required to provide verification with the SAR 7 if voluntarily reported information was not verified during the mid-period (such as income County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageSemi-Annual Reporting (SAR) 63-271 3 of 4 under Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) and information not considered Verified Upon Receipt (VUR). The SAR 7 will be considered complete if: •All questions and items are answered and complete or otherwise clarified with the HH •Necessary verifications have been provided •The documentation provided is sufficient to make an eligibility and benefit level determination •The form is signed and dated NOTE: There is no requirement that a SAR 7 must be signed and dated on or after the first day of the submit month. Please refer to examples provided below: Example: SAR 7 submitted with data month verifications Scenario A HH completes, signs and date a manual SAR 7 on January 12 th and submits on April 23 rd. The verifications provided are for March data month and the remaining criteria for a complete SAR 7 was met. Outcome This will be considered complete. The HH submitted all required documents and verifications for the SAR 7. Example: SAR 7 submitted with non-data month verifications Scenario A HH completes, signs, and dates a manual SAR 7 on January 12th and submits on April 23rd. The verifications provided are for February. Outcome This will be considered incomplete. The HH does not meet the criteria for a complete SAR 7, because data month verifications were not provided. 5. Action on Reported Changes: Staff must act on the following information which may result in a change of benefits during the SAR payment period: •Information that is required to be reported on the SAR 7 and was not included •Information considered VUR even if the change results in a mid-period decrease (refer to 63-284 for additional guidance) •A change in either HH composition or a decrease in income that is verified and results in a midperiod increase •Mandatory mid-period reports that result in a decrease/discontinuance of benefits •County initiated actions that result in a decrease/discontinuance of benefits •HH request to discontinue benefits An overissuance can be calculated, if a Public Assistance CalFresh (PACF) HH fails to report income over the CalWORKs IRT. No overissuance will be calculated if the unreported income is under IRT for CF, because it is not mandatory for CF. References: All County Letters (ACL) 21-24, 18-18 and 18-18E, 15-90, 15-42, 13-57, 13-26, 13-17, 13-08, 12-59, 12-25, 12-25E ACIN I-58-12 MPP 63-509, MPP 63-504 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 06/30/2024 Approval for Release: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageSemi-Annual Reporting (SAR) 63-271 4 of 4 Rick Wanne, Director Self Sufficiency Services
