title: 63-272 Semi Annual Report (SAR) Cycle
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageSemi-Annual Reporting (SAR) Cycle 63-272 1 of 4 Revision Date: 04/01/2022 Background: Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) is the simplified reporting option under federal Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) reporting requirements that California elects to use. Recipients are required to submit one Semi-Annual Eligibility Report form (SAR 7) in the 6, 12 ,18 or 24-month interval after the Beginning Date of Aid (BDA). Purpose: This section includes policies on SAR household (HH) types, cycles, and alignment responsibilities. This section is being revised to update SAR requirements for Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) HHs. Policy: HHs are required to complete a SAR 7. The SAR cycle will be determined by the BDA. The frequency of SAR 7s the HH will be required to submit depends on the HH composition and types of income. The following is terminology used to describe the months and the period of the SAR cycle: Term Definition Data Month The month for which the HH is required to report all information necessary to determine eligibility. Submit Month The month in which the SAR 7 must be submitted. SAR Payment Period The period in which benefits are issued. The period that starts with the BDA or the month after the submit month. 1. Determining the SAR Submission Month: To determine when a SAR 7 must be submitted, eligibility staff must consider the BDA, HH composition and types of income. The following table shows when a SAR 7 form must be completed by each HH type: HH Type Certification Period SAR 7 Frequency Regular, homeless, and migrant/seasonal farmworker. 12-month 6-months All adult members are Elderly or Disabled and HH includes nondisabled minor children with no earned income. 24-month 12-months Residing on an Indian Reservation with no earned income. 24-month 12-months All adult members are Elderly or Disabled and HH includes nondisabled minor children with earned income. 24-month 6, 12, and 18-months Residing on an Indian Reservation with earned income. 24-month 6, 12, and 18-months HHs losing ESAP eligibility. 36-month 12 and 24-months 2. SAR Cycles: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageSemi-Annual Reporting (SAR) Cycle 63-272 2 of 4 The first SAR payment month when actual benefits are issued is the BDA. This includes a subsequent month in which a supplemental payment is made. SAR cycles will be assigned based on the BDA. HH’s not eligible in the month of application will have the SAR cycle align with the BDA. Cycles will be assigned as follows: HH’s with a BDA month in … Will be assigned to cycle … January or July One February or August Two March or September Three April or October Four May or November Five June or December Six 3. Alignment of Cycles: For Public Assistance CalFresh (PACF) cases, recertification/redetermination dates must be aligned as follows: If a HH applies for … Then the cycle/redetermination for … CalWORKs and is already receiving CalFresh. CalWORKs must be aligned with the existing CalFresh cycle. CalFresh and is already receiving CalWORKs. CalFresh must be aligned with the CalWORKs cycle. The certification may be for less than 12-months to align with the existing CalWORKs/CalFresh program and must be set at application or recertification. If an existing CalFresh HH has a 24-month certification period, the 1 st CalWORKs redetermination will align to CalFresh. The 2 nd CalWORKs redetermination will then be aligned with CalFresh recertification at 24-months. Examples on alignment are provided below: Example: Aligning CalWORKs to existing CalFresh with 12-month certification period Scenario An active CalFresh HH with BDA of 01/10/2020, their next recertification will be 12/2020. title: 63-274 SAR 7 Processing
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageSemi-Annual Reporting Form (SAR 7) Process 63-274 1 of 3 Revision Date: 06/01/2021 Background: CalFresh (CF) Households (HH) are required to complete Eligibility Status Report Form (SAR 7) in 6, 12, 18, or 24 month intervals after the Beginning Date of Aid (BDA). Purpose: This section includes policies on the SAR 7 process including: Notices of Action (NOA’s), late and incomplete reports, timeliness, completeness criteria, good cause and restoration. This section is being reformatted after sunset review. Policy: CalFresh HHs must be provided a SAR 7 prior to the end of the data month. HHs are asked to provide their SAR 7 by 5 th day of the submit month to ensure timely processing. The report will be considered late if it is received after the 11th day of the submit month. 1. Missing or Incomplete SAR 7: Proper notifications must be provided if the SAR 7 has not been received or is incomplete. An attempt to contact the HH to complete the report or obtain the missing information must be completed after the notification is sent. The attempt must be documented in the case record. Below is a description of the NOA’s used when processing the SAR 7: Notice Description X NOA (NA 960X SAR) Notifies the HH a SAR 7 has not been received. This NOA is generated when a SAR 7 is not received by the 11th day of the submit month. Y NOA (NA 960Y SAR) Notifies the HH a SAR 7 was received and determined to be incomplete. The NOA will include: a list of the missing verifications, what must be done to complete the SAR 7, and a deadline to avoid a discontinuance. SAR 90 (SAR 90) Notifies the HH of missing items for a complete SAR 7. This notice is sent after a Y or X NOA has been provided and the SAR 7 submitted continues to be incomplete. Examples of when to mail a SAR 90 or Y NOA: Example: Sending a Y NOA Scenario A HH provides a SAR 7 on the 7th of the submit month, it is assigned and processed on the same day. The SAR 7 is determined to be incomplete due to missing verifications. Outcome Staff must mail a Y NOA, because the SAR 7 was submitted by the HH and processed prior to an X NOA being mailed. Example: Sending a SAR 90 Scenario A HH provides a SAR 7 on the 20 th of the submit month, it is assigned and processed on the same day. The SAR 7 is determined to be incomplete due to missing verifications. Outcome Staff must mail a SAR 90, because the X NOA was sent to the HH on the 12 th of the submit month. Example: Sending a SAR 90 after a Y NOA County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageSemi-Annual Reporting Form (SAR 7) Process 63-274 2 of 3 Scenario A HH provides a SAR 7 on the 3 rd of the submit month it is assigned and processed on the same day. The SAR 7 is determined to be incomplete due to missing verifications. A Y NOA was mailed to the HH with a list of pending verifications. The HH provides some missing items on the 8 th of the submit month, however the SAR7 remains incomplete. Outcome The HH will be mailed a SAR 90, because the HH has been previously provided a Y NOA . NOTE: A SAR 90 and Y NOA will only be considered adequate when they contain the following information: a list of missing verifications, what must be done to complete the SAR 7 and deadline to avoid discontinuance. 2. Prior to Termination An attempt to contact the HH will be made via automated contact, after mailing X NOA, Y NOA or SAR 90. A discontinuance is only valid if the attempt to contact is documented in case records. Please refer to EPPG on Text Messaging Service as an option. 3. Extended Filing Date Cases that have discontinued when a SAR 7 is not received or is incomplete, will have an opportunity to provide a completed form on the extended filing date. The extended filing date is identified as the first working day after the submit month. 4. Benefit Decreases: HH’s are to be provided timely 10-day notice to decrease or discontinue benefits. When a late SAR 7 is received and there is insufficient time to provide 10-day notice, CF benefits will remain at the prior month level. Refer to 63-303 for more information on adequate and timely notice. Below are some examples regarding decreasing and increasing benefits: Example: Benefits decreased with timely notice Scenario A HH reports income increase on their SAR 7 on the 10 th of the submit month this will cause a decrease in the HH benefit, the form was processed as complete. Outcome Considering there is sufficient time to provide the HH a 10-day notice, the reduction in benefits will take place at the start of the new SAR cycle and no overissuance will be applied. Example: Benefits decreased and no timely notice available Scenario A HH reports income increase on their SAR 7 on the 27 th of the submit month this will cause a decrease in the HH benefit, the form was processed as complete. Outcome There is insufficient time to provide the HH a 10-day notice, benefits will not be reduced for the start of the cycle and will remain at the same level as the submit month. An overissuance will be established. 5. Benefit Increase 10-day notice requirements do not apply to HH’s reporting information on the SAR 7 that cause an increase in benefits. Adequate notice is still required. The date eligibility receives verifications causing an increase in benefits, will be the date considered as the month for applying a supplement. Example: Benefit increase Scenario A HH reports expenses for housing increase on their SAR 7 on the 28 th of the submit month this will cause an increase in the HH benefit, the form was processed County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageSemi-Annual Reporting Form (SAR 7) Process 63-274 3 of 3 as complete. Outcome There are no 10-day requirement rules for increases in a HHs benefits. Supplements will be issued for the submit month and if needed for the month following. 6. Good Cause Evaluation: An evaluation of good cause must be made after the extended filing date, prior to processing restoration, and no later than the last day of the month following termination. A verbal or written request for good cause can also be made by the HH, presenting their explanation for not meeting reporting requirements. Good cause may exist in the following situations: •The HH has a mental or physical condition that impedes them from submitting a timely and complete report •Extenuating circumstances exist that might have contributed to the HH’s inability to submit a timely report (i.e., domestic violence) •Failure to submit a timely and complete report is directly attributable to county error •The appeals issue is SAR 7 related Once good cause has been granted the discontinuance will need to be rescinded and benefits restored at prior level and determine if information provided will cause a decrease or increase in benefits. Refer to 63-303 for additional information on adequate and timely notice. 7. Restoration of Benefits: After discontinuance and determining good cause does not apply, CF HHs are eligible to have their benefits restored at any time in the month following the discontinuance if the reason for the discontinuance is resolved and they were otherwise eligible. Restoration will be applied effective the date the SAR 7 is considered complete. Refer to 63-306 for additional information on restoration. References: All County Letters (ACL) 21-24, 18-18 and 18-18E, 15-90, 15-42, 13-57, 13-26, 13-17, 13-08, 12-59, 12-25, 12-25E ACIN I-58-12 MPP 63-509, MPP 63-504 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 06/30/2024 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self Sufficiency Services

title: 63-283 Mid-Period Reports
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Mid-Period Reports Number Page 63-283 1 of 12 Revision: 09/01/2026 B ackground: Changes reported during the certification period that occur outside of the Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7) or recertification (RE) process are considered mid-period reports. This policy outlines the categories of mid-period reports and the corresponding actions required. P urpose: This section has been revised to implement policy changes and procedures for processing voluntary mid-period reports. CalFresh Program Guide (CFPG) Sections 63-284, 63-285, 63-286 and Processing Guide 283-01 are now obsolete. The following updates for mid-period reports have been incorporated into this section: • Guidance on actions to take when a change will result in an increase, decrease, or no change of benefits. • Verification requirements for voluntary income changes. • New guidance on when to issue supplemental payments and re-evaluation of benefit allotments. P olicy: Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) HHs are informed of their mandatory reporting responsibilities via the Reporting Changes for Cash Aid and CalFresh (SAR 2) informing notice. The SAR 2 is issued when a case is initially approved, and when the Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) changes during the certification period. For Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) HHs, the SAR 2 is sent on the 12th and 24th month of the certification period as a reminder of the ESAP HH’s reporting requirements. T he SAR 2 informs the HH of the following: • The HH’s size, current gross monthly income, and IRT amount. • How to report when gross monthly income exceeds the IRT and the 10-day reporting requirement. • What will happen when mandatory changes are reported. • The potential consequences for not reporting income exceeding IRT. • Voluntarily reporting information. • For HHs with an Able -Bodied Adult Without Dependent (ABAWD), to report when work or training hours drop to less than 20 hours a week or 80 hours a month. Mi d-period reports are categorized as mandatory, voluntary , and county-initiated. The required action for mid-period reports is dependent on the category, reporting requirements, and impact to the HH’s benefits. Mid-period reports may be made in writing, online, verbally, or in person. The following forms must be made available for HHs to report mid- period changes in writing at initial application, RE , or upon request: • Mid-Period Status Report for Cash Aid and CalFresh (SAR 3). • CalFresh Mid-Certification Period Status Report (CF 377.5 SAR). 1. C alFresh Mandatory Mid-Period Reports SAR HHs must report the following mandatory changes within 10 days of the date the HH becomes aware of the change: • The HH’s gross income exceeds their CalFresh IRT. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Mid-Period Reports Number Page 63-283 2 of 12 • An ABAWD’s work or training hours drop below an average of 20 hours per week or 80 hours a month. • The HH receives substantial lottery or gambling winnings that is equal to or greater than the resource limit for Elderly or Disabled (E/D) HHs. T ake the appropriate action on mandatory reports, regardless of the impact to the HH’s benefits. Refer to the following CFPG sections for further information: • 63-125 Income Reporting Threshold (IRT). • 63-247 Substantial Lottery or Gambling Winnings. • 63-904 Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents Time Limit. 2. D ecrease in Benefits: When a SAR HH reports a change during the certification period, it is a mid- period report. Action on mid-period reports must not be taken if the information received decreases or terminates the HH’s benefits unless one of the following applies: • The HH voluntarily requests benefit termination. • The information received is Verified Upon Receipt (VUR). • A HH member has been identified as a fleeing felon or parole violator. • There is a change in the Public Assistance (PA) grant. • County-initiated mid period changes. • The information received is a mandatory mid-period report. W ith the exception of the items above, do not request verification of reported changes that result in a decrease or no change in benefits. Document the change being reported by the HH in the case record, the reason for not acting on the change, and send a No- Change Notice of Action ( NOA). The NOA must remind the HH to report the information at the next SAR 7 or RE , whichever comes first. Action must be taken at the next SAR 7 or RE, regardless of the impact on benefits. S ee examples below of reported changes that result in a decrease in benefits. Example 1 Scenario HH reports an income increase but is under IRT, and the change will result in a decrease in benefits. Outcome Do not request verification. Send a No-Change NOA. Document the change in case record and follow up at next SAR 7 or RE, whichever comes first. Example 2 Scenario HH voluntarily reports a change in HH composition, to add a person that will result in a decrease in benefits. Outcome Do not request verification of the new members’ income or other mandatory verifications. Send a No-Change NOA. Document the change in case record and follow up at the next SAR 7 or RE, whichever comes first. Note: Proper documentation used in the eligibility determination and benefit level must be clearly included in the case record to support changes reported mid- period, even when no action is taken on County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Mid-Period Reports Number Page 63-283 3 of 12 the case. Documentation must be in sufficient detail to determine the reasonableness and accuracy of the determination. 3. C ounty-Initiated Mid-Period Changes County-initiated changes include mass changes and information known to the county. Action must be taken on all county-initiated changes regardless of the impact on the HH’s benefits. The following are considered county-initiated changes and require mid-period action: • HH is approved for PA benefits including California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids (CalWORKs), Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants (CAPI), Supplemental Security Income/State Supplementary Payment (SSI/SSP), Tribal Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), and General Relief. • Failure of a HH member to comply with a Quality Control (QC) review. • Verified Nationwide Prisoner Match (NPM) or Deceased Person Match (DPM). • Verified information that the HH is receiving benefits in another state. • Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA). • Individuals subject to the ABAWD time limit, whose three-month time limit ended or an ABAWD who regained eligibility and stopped meeting the work requirement. 4. V UR VUR is information that is clear, consistent, complete and does not require additional verification from the HH. For information to be considered VUR, it must meet all the following criteria: VUR Criteria Definition Complete The information has all the components necessary to take action. Not questionable There are no discrepant elements to the information that would cast doubt on its accuracy, completeness or timeliness. Requires no further verification Action can be taken without needing any further verification. Obtained from the primary source The primary source is a first-hand direct source that has complete knowledge and accurate information about the circumstance. I nformation considered VUR may become known to the county through a voluntary report, mandatory report, electronic source, or another means. When information is received that is considered VUR, it must be acted on, regardless of the impact on the HH’s benefits. Exceptions to this are HH composition and voluntary income changes not over IRT that would result in a decrease in benefits. V UR is limited to the following: • A voluntary report made by the HH of a: o HH composition change. o Change of address. • A Payment Verification System (PVS) report. The PVS report may contain: o Retirement, Survivors and Disability Insurance (RSDI) data from the Social Security Administration (SSA). o State Unemployment Insurance Benefits (UIB) from the Employment Development Department (EDD). o State Disability Insurance (SDI) from the EDD. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Mid-Period Reports Number Page 63-283 4 of 12 • Social Security and SSI and/or SSP benefit information obtained from the SSA. o Benefit information obtained from SSA is considered reported and verified on the day the information is first known to the county through any of the following automated data exchanges: Income and Eligibility Verification System (IEVS), or the Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS) “Title XVI – SSI/SSP Information” INQX screen. • UIB and SDI benefit information reported through IEVS and obtained from the California EDD. o UIB/SDI information is considered reported and verified on the date of the IEVS notification. • Worker’s Compensation benefits obtained from the California Worker’s Compensation agency. • A California Intentional Program Violation (IPV) report. o The IPV must be established to disqualify a HH member. • PA benefit amount information. o PA benefit amount is considered reported and verified on the date the PA benefit amount is authorized. • Non-citizen status obtained from the Systemic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) system. • In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS) provider wages obtained from the Case Management Information and Payrolling System (CMIPS). • Information regarding the removal of a child from a CalFresh HH obtained from the Child and Family Well-Being or Foster Care system. • Information that a HH member received substantial lottery or gambling winnings obtained from a gaming entity data match. I nformation that is considered VUR may or may not result in a mid- period action after the information is reviewed. If it is determined that no action will be taken mid- period, send a No-Change NOA to the HH and follow up at the next SAR 7 or RE, whichever comes first. I nformation cannot become VUR when additional information is provided at a later date. For example, a HH reports an income increase (under IRT) over the phone but does not provide additional details during the call. The HH later sends their paystubs, this information does not become VUR. In this situation, send a No-Change NOA to the HH and follow up at the next SAR 7 or RE, whichever comes first. 5. V oluntary Mid-Period Reports When a voluntary report is made by the HH, determine if the report will result in an increase or a decrease to the HH’s benefits. Do not act on voluntary mid-period reports that will result in a decrease or termination of the HH’s benefits unless the information is VUR. Take action on voluntary reports that will result in an increase in the HH’s benefits, with a few exceptions. C hanges must be effective the month following when the HH reports a change. Review and process changes within 10 days after the date the change was reported. If the case requires additional verification, process the change within 10 days after the verification is received. If the HH fails to provide the required verifications within 10 days but submitted them later, the timeframe for taking action on the change begins when the verifications are received, process the change and issue the updated benefit amount the month following when the verifications were received. When a mid-period report is received but not acted on because it will result in a decrease in the HH’s benefits: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Mid-Period Reports Number Page 63-283 5 of 12 • Document clearly in the case record the reason for not taking action. • Send the HH a No-Change NOA. • Ensure the NOA reminds the HH that they must report the information at the next SAR 7 or RE, whichever comes first. W hen processing the next SAR 7 or RE, ensure the information is reported, if still applicable, and resolve any inconsistencies or discrepancies. Take action after the information is verified and document all actions in the case file. As a reminder, HH’s certified with income between 131 and 200 percent of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) do not have a mandatory income reporting requirement because they have already reported income over 130 percent at application and met their mandatory IRT reporting requirement. 6. Verification Requirements for Voluntary Income Changes A voluntary mid-period income change that results in an increase to the HH’s benefits requires verification when the income change is: • More than $50 and the income change will result in an increase in benefits. • $50 or less and the income source has changed. The H H must be informed in writing of any additional verification requirements and that failure to provide verification within the specified date will result in no change to their benefits. If th e income amount has changed by $50 or less and the income source has not changed, do not verify income changes unless the information is incomplete, inaccurate, inconsistent, or outdated (older than 60 days). S ee table below for detailed guidance on verification requirements. If verification is… then… provided, benefits will be evaluated to take effect the following month after the report is made. not provided within the requested timeframe, send a No-Change NOA. provided after the requested timeframe, benefits will be re-evaluated to take effect the following month after the verification is received. See section 7 – Supplements above for further guidance. N ote: If the HH reports an income change of $50 or less and this change is over the HH’s IRT, then it becomes a mandatory mid- period report and verification must be requested to determine ongoing eligibility. See bel ow for examples of reported changes that result in an increase in benefits. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Mid-Period Reports Number Page 63-283 6 of 12 Example 1 Scenario HH reports on April 10th that work hours were reduced to 35 hours a week. As a result, income has decreased by $100. The change will result in an increase in benefits. Outcome Send a Request for Verification (CW 2200) requesting income verification and allow 10 days to provide. If the HH provides the required verification… then… within 10 days, act on the change. Do not issue supplements for current or prior months. after 10 days, evaluate benefits effective the first of the following month that the verification was provided. Do not issue supplements for current or prior months. If the HH does not provide verification, send the HH a No-Change NOA. Example 2 Scenario HH reports on April 10th that work hours were reduced to 35 hours a week. The employer has not changed, and income is decreased by $40. The change will result in an increase in benefits. Outcome Verification of the income is not required; the amount is less than $50 and the income source has not changed. Process the change within 10 days to reflect an increase in the benefit allotment in May. Do not issue a supplement for April. Example 3 Scenario HH reports on April 27th that work hours were reduced to 35 hours a week. Income has decreased by $40. The change will result in an increase in benefits. Outcome Verification of the income is not required; the amount is less than $50 and the income source has not changed. The increase must be effective for May, as it is the following month when the change was reported. Issue a supplement for May no later than May 10th. Do not issue a supplement for April. Example 4 Scenario HH voluntarily reports a change in HH composition that will result in an increase in benefits. Outcome Send the HH a CW 2200 requesting verification of the new HH members’ income and other mandatory verifications and allow 10 days to provide. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Mid-Period Reports Number Page 63-283 7 of 12 If the HH provides the required verification… then… within 10 days, act on the change to add the HH member effective the following month the report was received. Do not issue supplements for current or prior months. after 10 days, evaluate benefits effective the first of the following month that the verification was provided. Do not issue supplements for current or prior months. If the HH does not provide verification, send the HH a No-Change NOA. 7. S upplements A supplement is an additional issuance of benefits that ensures the HH’s total allotment for the month is accurate. Supplements must not be issued for the report month or months prior to the change report. W hen a change that increases benefits requires verification, the HH must submit the verification within 10 days. If the verifications are submitted timely, process the change from the date it was reported, issue the increased benefits with the HH’s next regular monthly benefit allotment date. If th e HH fails to provide the required verifications within 10 days but submitted them later, the timeframe for taking action on the change begins when the verifications are received, process the change and issue the updated benefit amount the month following when the verifications were received. I f the change is processed too late in the month to increase the HH’s next monthly benefit allotment, issue the increased benefits no later than the 10 th day of the month that the increased benefit amount is to be issued. R eminder: Do not issue supplements for the report month or for any months prior to the change report. See examples below of change reports that result in a supplemental issuance. Example 1 Scenario HH reports and verifies a $51 decrease of income on October 28th. The change will result in an increase in benefits. Outcome Increase the benefit allotment beginning with the November benefit month. Do not issue a supplement for October. Issue the HH a supplement to their November benefits by November 10th. Example 2 Scenario HH received their monthly benefit on the 1st of the month. The weekly hours decreased to 30 hours a week resulting in income decreasing on September 1st by $200 a month. The HH does not submit the verifications of this change until November 28th. This change will result in an increase in CalFresh benefits. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Mid-Period Reports Number Page 63-283 8 of 12 S ee example below of a change report that does not result in a supplemental issuance. 8. P A CalFresh (PACF) Cases When PA benefits such as CalWORKs, CAPI, or General Relief are recalculated mid-period, take action on the CalFresh case to be effective the next regular monthly benefit allotment. If the result is a decrease in benefits the effective date must allow for a timely notice. Refer to the table below for actions to take on PACF cases. If the reported changes result in… then CalFresh must… a change to the PA benefits, act on the change regardless of the impact on benefits. no change to the PA benefits, only act on the change if it results in a benefit increase, unless the information is VUR. 9. R eport of Reduction in ABAWD Work Hours ABAWDs must report when their work hours drop below 20 hours per week, or 80 hours averaged month within 10 days of the date the ABAWD becomes aware of the change. When an ABAWD reports a reduction in work hours, determine if the ABAWD meets any of the time limit exemptions. I f the ABAWD has exhausted their three full countable months of benefits in their fixed 36-month period, terminate benefits at the end of the month in which timely and adequate notice can be provided. Further guidance regarding ABAWDs can be referenced in Section 63-904. 10. U nclear Information Unclear information received mid-period is information reported about a HH ’s circumstances in which a determination on the continued eligibility or benefit amount cannot be made. Unclear information may potentially be considered VUR but needs additional information to act on the change appropriately. W hen information is reported that is typically considered VUR but is not sufficient to take action. The information would then be considered unclear, because additional information is needed to act on the change. Ou tcome Process the change within 10 days of the verifications being received. Do not issue a supplement for September, October, or November. The increase in benefits is effective in December; issue a supplement by December 10th. Example 3 Scenario HH received their monthly benefit on the 1st of the month. The HH reported their weekly hours decreased to 30 hours a week resulting in income decreasing effective September 1st by $200 a month. The HH submitted the requested income verifications of this change on September 8th. This change will result in an increase in CalFresh benefits. Outcome Process the change within 10 days of the verifications being received. Do not issue a supplement for September. The increase in benefits is effective in October. Do not issue a supplement. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Mid-Period Reports Number Page 63-283 9 of 12 Follow up if the unclear information received meets the following criteria: • Is less than 60 days old from the current month’s benefit; and • Indicates the HH may have failed to report information at initial application, SAR 7, RE, or a mandatory mid-period change. If i nformation reported meets the criteria for unclear information, then send the HH a CW 2200 and allow the HH 10 days to respond. See detailed guidance below on required actions after the CW 2200 is sent. If the HH… then… responds and clarifies the information, determine if: 1. The information and/or verification is a mandatory mid-period requirement. For example, income over IRT, a drop in work hours for ABAWDs, substantial lottery/gambling winnings, or VUR. • T ake action regardless of the impact to the HH’s benefits. 2. The change would result in an increase or decrease to the HH’s benefits. • E v aluate the impact on the HH’s benefits and act only if the result is an increase in benefits. Document all actions in the case record and send the HH the appropriate NOA. does not respond within 10 days or refuses to provide verification, discontinue the case. Send the HH a timely and adequate NOA with information that explains the reason for the action. does not meet the criteria for unclear information, do not act on the information and do not request verification until the HH’s next SAR 7 or RE, whichever comes first. Send a No-Change NOA. 11. Address Changes Review a voluntary mid- period report made by the HH with a change of address or an institution, for example, a Drug or Alcohol Treatment Center (DATC) reports that a HH moved out of the location. Determine the impact on shelter costs. Shelter costs must not be verified, unless they are questionable. Do not disregard a change in shelter cost related to the address change. When a change of address is reported mid-period that does not include the updated shelter cost, send a CW 2200 to the HH and allow 10 days for them to respond. R efer to the table below for required actions. If the HH… then… provides updates shelter costs, re-evaluate benefits with timely notice. does not respond to the request, end date the existing shelter expense and re - evaluate benefits without the deduction, with timely notice. Provides the updated shelter cost at any time , after the 10 days, re-evaluate benefits with timely notice. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Mid-Period Reports Number Page 63-283 10 of 12 12. Significantly Conflicting Unclear Information Significantly conflicting unclear information applies when information received mid- period about a HH is greatly conflicting with the information used to determine eligibility for initial applications under normal processing and expedited services , and RE. Follow up if there is unclear information that appears to be significantly conflicting with the HH’s circumstances that were used to determine eligibility at initial application or RE. S ee detailed guidance below on required actions for significantly conflicting unclear information. Example Scenario A HH was certified in January 2026 with no earned income and later obtains information from a third-party source four months into the certification period indicating the HH had earned income of $1200 during the initial certification month. Outcome Send the HH a CW 2200 requesting employment and pay information from January 1, 2026 to clarify the discrepancy and verify the income. If the HH does… then… not provide verification, discontinue the case due to failure to provide. provide verification and a discrepancy is verified from the information used to determine eligibility previously, process the information and review for an overissuance as appropriate. Send the appropriate NOA. provide verification and no discrepancy is verified, send a No-Change NOA. 13. D isqualified Recipient Database Matches Action must be taken on Recipient IEVS (R-IEVS) database matches received mid- period regardless of the impact on the HH’s benefits. Do not hold unclear information regardless of when the information was reported. Take immediate action to pursue verification of positive matches when one is received mid-period from the database. T he disqualified recipient database match includes but is not limited to Fleeing Felon Match (FFM), California Youth Authority (CYA) Match, and NPM. F or further guidance on R -IEVS data matches reference CFPG 63 -118 and Self-Sufficiency Services Processing Guide – Income and Eligibility Verification System (IEVS). 14. Multiple Mid-Period Changes When a HH reports multiple changes at once, each change must be evaluated individually and apply the applicable policy to each change. Take action on mid-period reports that are mandatory mid period reports and reports considered VUR. If a report is not a mandatory mid-period report or VUR and causes the HH’s benefits to decrease while another report would cause an increase, only act on the report that would result in a benefit increas e. Document the report that would cause a decrease in the case record and follow up at the next SAR 7 or RE, whichever comes first. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Mid-Period Reports Number Page 63-283 11 of 12 See an example with detailed guidance below on required actions for multiple mid-period changes. Example Scenario A HH reports adding two new HH member’s mid-period: a newborn and the parent of the newborn. Outcome Evaluate whether adding the newborn would result in an increase or decrease in the HH’s benefits. If adding the newborn would result in… then… an increase in benefits, send the HH a CW 2200 requesting verification, if applicable, and take action to add the newborn. a decrease in benefits, send the HH a No- Change NOA. Document the change in the case record and follow up at the next SAR 7 or RE, whichever comes first. A fter the impact of the first report is known, evaluate the impact of the second report. I f adding the newborn would cause an increase in benefits and adding the parent would cause a decrease in benefits, only add the newborn to the case mid-period. Add the parent of the newborn at the next SAR 7 or RE, whichever comes first. Note: If the HH does not respond to the CW 2200 when a new HH member is reported mid-period, send a No-Change NOA because adding a HH member mid-period is not a mandatory mid-period report. O ther Program Impacts: No Impact. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Mid-Period Reports Number Page 63-283 12 of 12 References: Code of Federal Regulations ( CFR) 272.1, 272.2, 272.17, 273.8, 273.9, 273.10, 273.11, 2 73.12, 273.13, and 273.18. All County Letter (ACL) 12-25, 12-25E, 12-59, 13-08, 13-17, 13-26, 13-80, 15-42, 17-41, 18-20, 19-33, 19-86, 19-93, 20-132, 21-25, 21-101, 21-101E, 24-47, and 25-93. All County Information Notice (ACIN) I-58-13, I-58-13E, and I-58-25. S unset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 08/31/2029. A pproval for Release: A lberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services

sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Mid-Period Reports Number Page 63-283 1 of 12 Revision: 09/01/2026 B ackground: Changes reported during the certification period that occur outside of the Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7) or recertification (RE) process are considered mid-period reports. This policy outlines the categories of mid-period reports and the corresponding actions required. P urpose: This section has been revised to implement policy changes and procedures for processing voluntary mid-period reports. CalFresh Program Guide (CFPG) Sections 63-284, 63-285, 63-286 and Processing Guide 283-01 are now obsolete. The following updates for mid-period reports have been incorporated into this section: • Guidance on actions to take when a change will result in an increase, decrease, or no change of benefits. • Verification requirements for voluntary income changes. • New guidance on when to issue supplemental payments and re-evaluation of benefit allotments. P olicy: Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) HHs are informed of their mandatory reporting responsibilities via the Reporting Changes for Cash Aid and CalFresh (SAR 2) informing notice. The SAR 2 is issued when a case is initially approved, and when the Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) changes during the certification period. For Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) HHs, the SAR 2 is sent on the 12th and 24th month of the certification period as a reminder of the ESAP HH’s reporting requirements. T he SAR 2 informs the HH of the following: • The HH’s size, current gross monthly income, and IRT amount. • How to report when gross monthly income exceeds the IRT and the 10-day reporting requirement. • What will happen when mandatory changes are reported. • The potential consequences for not reporting income exceeding IRT. • Voluntarily reporting information. • For HHs with an Able -Bodied Adult Without Dependent (ABAWD), to report when work or training hours drop to less than 20 hours a week or 80 hours a month. Mi d-period reports are categorized as mandatory, voluntary , and county-initiated. The required action for mid-period reports is dependent on the category, reporting requirements, and impact to the HH’s benefits. Mid-period reports may be made in writing, online, verbally, or in person. The following forms must be made available for HHs to report mid- period changes in writing at initial application, RE , or upon request: • Mid-Period Status Report for Cash Aid and CalFresh (SAR 3). • CalFresh Mid-Certification Period Status Report (CF 377.5 SAR). 1. C alFresh Mandatory Mid-Period Reports SAR HHs must report the following mandatory changes within 10 days of the date the HH becomes aware of the change: • The HH’s gross income exceeds their CalFresh IRT. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Mid-Period Reports Number Page 63-283 2 of 12 • An ABAWD’s work or training hours drop below an average of 20 hours per week or 80 hours a month. • The HH receives substantial lottery or gambling winnings that is equal to or greater than the resource limit for Elderly or Disabled (E/D) HHs. T ake the appropriate action on mandatory reports, regardless of the impact to the HH’s benefits. Refer to the following CFPG sections for further information: • 63-125 Income Reporting Threshold (IRT). • 63-247 Substantial Lottery or Gambling Winnings. • 63-904 Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents Time Limit. 2. D ecrease in Benefits: When a SAR HH reports a change during the certification period, it is a mid- period report. Action on mid-period reports must not be taken if the information received decreases or terminates the HH’s benefits unless one of the following applies: • The HH voluntarily requests benefit termination. • The information received is Verified Upon Receipt (VUR). • A HH member has been identified as a fleeing felon or parole violator. • There is a change in the Public Assistance

title: 63-287 Overissuances and Underissuances
content: 63-287 Overissuances and Underissuances Table of Contents Section Establishment of CalFresh Overissuances under SAR 287.1 Failure to Report Income 287.2 Examples: Failure to Report Income 287.3 Late or Incomplete SAR 7 287.4 Aid paid Pending 287.5 County Error 287.6 Voluntary Reports 287.7 Discrepancy After Income Has Been Reasonably Anticipated Based on Available Information 287.8 Budget Re-computation to Determine an Overissuance 287.9 Claim Recoupment by Allotment Reduction 287.10 Underissuances 287.11 x 63-287.1 Establishment of CalFresh Overissuance s under SAR Regulations governing the establishment of a CalFresh overissuance under Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) regulations will vary depending on the eligibility factor in question, when the household is required to report, and required worker action. An overissuance will be established as applicable based on: •The household’s failure to report accurately, completely or timely; and/or •County error. When assessing whether an overissuance should be established based on the mandatory reporting of mid-period changes, the worker must determine if the household reported the change in a timely manner (i.e., within 10 days). If a household makes a mandatory report of a mid-period change timely (within 10 days), the worker will not establish an overissuance if the correct allotment cannot be issued due to timely notice requirements. •An overissuance will not be assessed based on a timely, accurate and complete report where timely (10-day) notice alone delayed issuance of the correct allotment. •An overissuance will be assessed when late reporting alone or together with timely notice requirement delayed issuance of the correct allotment. Refer to 63-287.2 Examples 2 and 3 and 63-451. NOTE: Due to CalWORKs and CalFresh having different mid-period reporting requirements, there will be times when failure to report something (such as income over the CalWORKs IRT) will result in an overpayment in CalWORKs but will not result in an overissuance in CalFresh. This is the case even though CalFresh would have taken mid-period action to decrease the allotment amount based on a mandated CalWORKs report had it been made timely. Refer to 63- 283.8. 63-287.2 Failure to Report Income The determination of an overissuance based on household failure to report accurately and/or timely will be determined based on mandatory household reporting requirements under SAR regulations. Households will make mandatory reports of income: •On the SAR 7, •During recertification, and •When income is over the IRT. If a household fails to report income that it is required to report, or if the worker fails to take action on a mandatory household report, the worker will re-determine the benefits the household would have received based on an accurate report and correct County action. •If the recalculation results in an overissuance, the date that the overissuance begins is the first date that the change would have been made had timely and correct action been taken based on a timely and accurate household report. •If a recipient receives income which is under the IRT that they did not reasonably anticipate at the time of their last mandatory report, this is NOT considered a failure to report and no overissuance will be assessed. Example 1: Scenario A client works through a temporary employment agency and reports on his SAR 7 that his job ended in the Data Month and provides verification. Additionally, the client reports that he is on-call, but that he can’t anticipate whether or not he will get another job or make any money in the next six months. Outcome Based on the information provided by the client, the worker agrees that he can’t reasonably anticipate any income. Therefore, issues a supplement for the Submit Month and budgets no income for the remaining months of the certification period. The worker later learns that the temporary agency found him a new job that started in the Submit Month. Unless he failed to report income over IRT or the worker has evidence that the temporary agency had confirmed the job offer with him in the Data Month, including start date and amount of income, there would be no overissuance. •If a household reports an income increase that exceeds the IRT, which results in ineligibility, but it is too late to provide timely notice to discontinue the case, the worker will issue benefits for the next month at the previous (higher) level, discontinue the case with timely notice and determine whether a household incurs an overissuance as follows: oAn overissuance will not be assessed if the household reported income over the IRT timely (within 10 days of the occurrence). oAn overissuance will be assessed if the household did not report the income over the IRT timely. oFor Public Assistance CalFresh (PACF) households, there is no overissuance if the household fails to report income over the first or second CalWORKs IRT. Example 2: Scenario A CalWORKs/PACF household assigned to the January through June semi-annual period reports timely (within 10 days) on March 28th that they are receiving income over the IRT. Outcome After ensuring that the income will continue at the same level, the worker determines that the recipient is financially ineligible for both CalWORKs and CalFresh and should be discontinued. Although the household reported the income increase timely, it was received too late in the month to be able to discontinue the case effective March 31st. The worker will issue timely notice to discontinue the case effective April 30th. •The cash grant for April is an overpayment. •The CalFresh allotment for April is not an overissuance because the household reported the change timely. •Transitional CalFresh (TCF) benefits would begin on May 1st. NOTE: If the Assistance Unit (AU) waives the 10- day timely notice for CalWORKs, the CalWORKs case will be discontinued March 31 st and TCF would begin April 1st. Example 3: Scenario Same as above, but the income increase, which is over the CalWORKs IRT, only results in a decrease to the CalWORKs grant and does not render the household ineligible for either CalWORKs or CalFresh. Outcome The worker issues timely notice to decrease CalWORKs and CalFresh benefits effective April 30th. •An overpayment will be assessed in April for CalWORKs for the amount of the grant that was released at the higher amount. •The CalFresh allotment for April is not an overissuance because the household reported the change timely. . 63-287.3 Examples: Failure to Report Income Example 1: Scenario In the semi-annual period designated as July through December, the worker determines through an IEVS match (on October 15 th) that a household member had earnings that exceeded their CalWORKs IRT beginning January 5 th (the previous semi-annual period). However, the income is not over the CalFresh IRT. The person is still working and earning the same amount, but never reported the income mid-period or on their May SAR 7. Outcome The worker determines that the household should have reported this change for CalWORKs on January 15 th, and their cash grant should have been decreased effective February 1st. The worker will: Step Action 1 Re-compute the CalWORKs and CalFresh budgets counting the unreported earnings beginning: •February for CalWORKs •July for CalFresh 2 Send timely and adequate notice to decrease CalWORKs and CalFresh benefits effective November 1st. 3 Establish a: •CalWORKs overpayment from February through October, and •CalFresh overissuance from July through October For the amount of benefits they were not entitled to receive. NOTE: The only mandatory mid-period report of income for CalFresh is income the CalFresh IRT ( 63- 283.3). Therefore, as long as the income did not exceed the CalFresh IRT, an overissuance would only be established for July through October, because the household was not required to report the income change until their next reporting period on the May SAR 7. Example 2: Scenario The CalFresh certification period is January through December. Reviewing an IEVS report on October 15 th, the worker determines that a household member had income that exceeded their CalFresh IRT beginning on January 5th. The household member is still working and earning the same amount, but did not report the income mid-period or on their June SAR 7. Outcome The worker determines that the household should have reported this change on January 15 th and the CalFresh case should have been discontinued effective February 1st. An overissuance will be established from February through October because the household was required to report income over IRT no later than January 15 th. The worker will discontinue the case effective November 1st with timely notice. . 63-287.4 Late or Incomplete SAR 7 A. LATE OR INCOMPLETE SAR 7 An overissuance will be assessed when a household submits a late or incomplete SAR 7 and the worker is unable to decrease benefits or discontinue the case due to timely notice requirements. Refer to 63- 274.5. Example 1: Scenario The CalFresh certification period is January through December. The household submits the SAR 7 on June 25th. A household member reports starting a new job in May and received the first pay check the last day of May. She will be paid $800 per month. Outcome The worker is unable to reduce benefits effective July 1st due timely notice requirements. Therefore, •July benefits will be issued at June’s level. •The new earnings will be budgeted for August and benefits will be decreased effective August 1 st with timely notice. •An Inadvertent Household Error (IHE) overissuance will be established for the amount the household was not entitled to receive in July. B. UNVERIFIED CHANGE REPORTED MID-PERIOD If the household voluntarily reported an unverified change mid-period and that change is not included on the SAR 7, the worker will call the client to attempt to resolve the discrepancy. •If the worker cannot resolve the discrepancy, the SAR 7 will be considered incomplete. •If the discrepancy is resolved late in the Submit Month and the worker does not have timely notice to decrease benefits, the worker will release the benefits at the prior (higher) level and an IHE overissuance will be established for the amount the household was not entitled to receive. Example 2: Scenario The certification period is January through December. The household submits a timely SAR 7 on June 7. However, the client did not report a new job that was voluntarily reported mid-period for which verification was not provided. Outcome The worker calls the household to clarify the discrepancy. The client states that they still have the job. The worker sends suspense notice NA 960Y SAR requesting income verification. The household submits the complete SAR 7 late on June 28th. After re-determining benefits based on information reported on the SAR 7, the worker determines that the July through December benefits should be reduced due to the new income. The SAR 7 was submitted too late in the month for the worker to provide (10-day) timely notice to decrease benefits for July. The worker will: •Provide timely notice to decrease benefits effective August 1st, •Issue July’s benefits at the June level, and adjusts benefits to the correct amount for August through December, and •Calculates an IHE overissuance for the amount the household was not eligible to receive in the month of July. C. GOOD CAUSE SAR households that have been discontinued for failing to submit a timely or a complete SAR 7 must be evaluated for good cause when the household submits a complete SAR 7 or reapplies in the calendar month following the discontinuance. Once good cause has been determined and the discontinuance rescinded, benefits must be released to the household at the previous level until timely notice can be sent to decrease benefits. An overissuance will be established when benefits are released at a previous higher level as a result of the worker's inability to decrease benefits without timely notice. Refer to 63-274.6 and 7. 63-287.5 Each individual or household has the right to request a fair hearing to Aid Paid Pending appeal a denial, reduction, or termination of benefits. An IHE overissuance will be established if the household received more benefits than it was entitled to receive pending a state hearing decision because the household requested a continuation of benefits (Aid Paid Pending (APP)) based on the mistaken belief that it was entitled to such benefit. Refer to 63-451.9. When APP is granted for a CalWORKs case, the PACF allotment will be determined by using the actual CalWORKs grant paid to the household, which will be the higher APP level. Since this would result in a decrease of CalFresh benefits, the worker must give the household timely notice prior to decreasing their benefits. If there is no timely notice, CalFresh benefits will not be reduced until the month for which timely notice can be provided. The APP amount can be included in the computation of the CalFresh allotment because the APP is “ Known-to-County” information and can be reasonably anticipated. However, once the APP stops, the CalFresh benefits will be recalculated mid-period. Example 2: Scenario An AU/household is in the January through June SAR Payment Period. On February 15 th, the worker reduces the CalWORKs grant effective March 1 st, resulting in an increase in CalFresh. The recipient files a timely request for a fair hearing and begins receiving APP on April 25th. Outcome The CalFresh allotment cannot be reduced for May because there is timely notice. The CalWORKs grant that includes the APP will be used in the computation of the CalFresh allotment beginning in June, after giving the AU/household timely notice to decrease CalFresh. . 63-287.6 County Error Overissuances related to county error will be determined based on the worker failing to act correctly on a mandatory household report. •If the worker fails to act correctly on a mandatory recipient report, the worker will re-determine the benefits the household would have received based on an accurate report and correct County action. •If the worker’s recalculation results in an overissuance, the date that the overissuance begins is the first month that the change would have been made had timely and correct action been taken based on a timely household report. Example: Scenario A household reports on the SAR 7 submitted on June 5th (for the January through December certification period) that the father started a job on February 10th. The income did not exceed the IRT and it is expected to continue at the same level for the remaining months of the certification period. Outcome The worker processing the SAR 7 fails to budget the new income effective July 1st. A supervisor discovers the error October 5 th during a case review. An Administrative Error (AE) overissuance will be established from July to October and benefits will be decreased effective November 1st with timely notice. . 63-287.7 Voluntary Reports Changes that are not required to be reported, but that may be voluntarily reported, should not be considered when determining an overissuance. Unverified voluntary mid-period changes must be reported on the SAR 7 or recertification that follows the change. Refer to 63-287.5(B). Verified mid-period reports are considered part of the case record and will be entered into CalWIN at the time they were verified. The household is not required to report a verified change again on the SAR 7 or recertification. Failure to act on a reported change that was verified mid-period would be considered a County error. A CalFresh household is not required to report a new household member mid-period unless the new household member’s income together with the ongoing household’s income is over the IRT. 63-287.8 Changes After Income Has Been Reasonably Anticipated Based on Available Information The worker will not assess an overissuance when the actual income received during the certification period differs from the amount of income that was reasonably anticipated at initial application or when processing the SAR 7 or recertification, as long as the household has reported accurately and timely to the best of its ability and the worker has acted correctly on all available information to reasonably anticipate income and household circumstances. In other words, no reconciling based on actual income is ever done so long as the requirement to report completely and accurately is met and the worker determined and issued the benefits correctly based on reasonably anticipated income. For example, if a worker receives an IEVS match that shows a discrepancy between the actual and reported earnings, the worker will determine if the household was mandated to report that income midperiod. An overissuance would only be assessed if the income was over the IRT and the household failed to make the mandatory report of income over the IRT within 10 days of receipt. A mid-period income discrepancy would not result in an overissuance unless the household has failed to meet their mandatory reporting requirements under SAR rules. Refer to 63-282.6 for additional information. NOTE: Due to CalWORKs and CalFresh having different IRT reporting requirements, there will be times when failure to report income over the IRT will result in an overpayment for CalWORKs, but will not result in an overissuance for CalFresh. This is the case even though CalFresh would have taken mid-period action to decrease the allotment amount based on the report of income over the CalWORKs IRT when reported mid-period. 63-287.9 Budget Recomputation to Determine an Overissuance When re-computing benefits to determine an overissuance, the worker will recreate case circumstances to determine what income should have been reasonably anticipated at the time the change shall have been reported using the correct processing timeframes. The worker will not use actual verified income (actual income determined after the fact) to reconcile against prospectively budgeted income that was used in the original allotment calculation. 63-287.10 Claim Recoupment by Allotment Reduction Recoupment by allotment reduction will be initiated only at the beginning of a semi-annual period, the beginning of a certification period or the month after the SAR 7 Submit Month, unless the recoupment does not result in a decrease in benefits. An allotment reduction to recover an overissuance is not a “ County-Initiated” change. However: •A recoupment can be discontinued mid-period as appropriate when the overissuance has been recouped. •When a recoupment of one overissuance is completed midperiod, CalWIN may begin recoupment of the next overissuance mid-period as long as the amount that is going to be recouped does not result in a decrease of benefits. Example 1: Scenario A household has two AE claims. In the January through June semi-annual period, the worker is recouping from one of the AE overissuances via allotment reduction at the rate of five percent. Outcome When the overissuance is fully recouped in February, the worker will begin recoupment of the second AE overissuance in March at the same five percent rate. The allotment reduction mid-period is allowed in this situation because benefits did not decrease mid-period. Example 2: Scenario Same scenario as above, except that one of the overissuances is IHE. Outcome When the AE overissuance is fully recouped, in February the worker cannot start collecting in March from the second overissuance that was due to client error. Since collection for the second overissuance would be at the ten percent collection rate, the worker may not initiate mid-period collection of the second overissuance, because this would result in a midperiod decrease in benefits. Example 3: Scenario Same scenario as Example 2, except the worker is recouping from the IHE overissuance at the rate of ten percent. The IHE overissuance is fully recouped in February. Outcome The worker can start collecting from the AE overissuance in March at the five percent rate. The recoupment of the second overissuance is allowed mid-period in this situation, because it would result in an increase of benefits. . 63-287.11 Underissuanc es When a household receives fewer benefits than it was entitled to receive, they are considered to have lost benefits, which the worker is required to provide (restore) to the household (an underissuance). If the worker determines that an underissuance has occurred due to an administrative error, and the recipient is entitled to restoration of those benefits, the worker must immediately take action to restore the benefits that were lost. •Restoration of benefits under these circumstances would be based on SAR rules. •The worker will not use actual verified income to reconcile against prospectively budgeted income that was used in the original allotment calculation. The worker can only use income that could have been “reasonably anticipated” at the time benefits were initially calculated. Refer to 63-456.

sections.text: 63-287 Overissuances and Underissuances Table of Contents Section Establishment of CalFresh Overissuances under SAR 287.1 Failure to Report Income 287.2 Examples: Failure to Report Income 287.3 Late or Incomplete SAR 7 287.4 Aid paid Pending 287.5 County Error 287.6 Voluntary Reports 287.7 Discrepancy After Income Has Been Reasonably Anticipated Based on Available Information 287.8 Budget Re-computation to Determine an Overissuance 287.9 Claim Recoupment by Allotment Reduction 287.10 Underissuances 287.11 x 63-287.1 Establishment of CalFresh Overissuance s under SAR Regulations governing the establishment of a CalFresh overissuance under Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) regulations will vary depending on the eligibility factor in question, when the household is required to report, and required worker action. An overissuance will be established as applicable based on: •The household’s failure to report accurately, completely or timely; and/or •County error. When assessing whether an overissuance should be established based on the mandatory reporting of mid-period changes, the worker must determine if the household reported the change in a timely manner (i.e., within 10 days). If a household makes a mandatory report of a mid-period change timely (within 10 days), the worker will not establish an overissuance if the correct allotment cannot be issued due to timely notice requirements. •An overissuance will not be assessed based on a timely, accurate and complete report where timely (10-day) notice alone delayed issuance of the correct allotment. •An overissuance will be assessed when late reporting alone or together with timely notice requirement delayed issuance of the correct allotment. Refer to 63-287.2 Examples 2 and 3 and 63-451. NOTE: Due to CalWORKs and CalFresh having different mid-period reporting requirements, there will be times when failure to report something (such as income over the CalWORKs IRT) will result in an overpayment in CalWORKs but will not result in an overissuance in CalFresh. This is the case even though CalFresh would have taken mid-period action to decrease the allotment amount based on a mandated CalWORKs report had it been made timely. Refer to 63- 283.8. 63-287.2 Failure to Report Income The determination of an overissuance based on household failure to report accurately and/or timely will be determined based on mandatory household reporting requirements under SAR regulations. Households will make mandatory reports of income: •On the SAR 7, •During recertification, and •When income is over the IRT. If a household fails to report income that it is required to report, or if the worker fails to take action on a mandatory household report, the worker will re-determine the benefits the household would have received based on an accurate report and correct County action. •If the recalculation results in an overissuance, the date that the overissuance begins is the first date that the change would have been made had timely and correct action been taken based on a timely and accurate household report. •If a recipient receives income which is under the IRT that they did not reasonably anticipate at the time of their last mandatory report, this is NOT considered a failure to report and no overissuance will be assessed. Additionally, the client reports that he is on-call, but that he can’t anticipate whether or not he will get another job or make any money in the next six months. Outcome Based on the information provided by the client, the worker agrees that he can’t reasonably anticipate any income. Therefore, issues a supplement for the Submit Month and budgets no income for the remaining months of the certification period. title: 63-301 Certification Periods
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageCertification Periods 63-301 1 of 2 Revision: 03/01/2021 Background: A certification period is the number of months for which a CalFresh household is certified to receive benefits without completing a new application. Purpose: This section describes certification period policies for CalFresh. The purpose of this material revision is to reformat the section and due to sunset review. Policy: All eligible CalFresh households must be assigned a definite period of time for which they will be certified to receive benefits. The length of the certification period will be based on the household’s circumstances at the time eligibility is certified. Eligibility to benefits will end at the expiration of the certification period. Benefits must not be continued after the end of the certification period without a new determination of eligibility. Certification periods will be matched with Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) cycles. (Refer to 63-272 regarding aligning certification periods and SAR cycles with CalWORKs.) NOTE: The CalFresh certification period should not be adjusted to align with a Medi-Cal application or renewal. 1. Initial Month of Certification At initial application, the first month of the certification period is generally the month of application. When the household is ineligible in the month of application, the first month of the certification period will be the first month in which the household is eligible to benefits. This is also known as the beginning date of aid (BDA). The new certification period for timely recertifications will begin with the month following the last month of the previous certification period. NOTE: If processing of the application was delayed beyond 30 days due to the fault of the household, the household will lose the first month’s benefits and the second month’s benefits will be prorated from the date the required verification/information was received by the Human Services Specialist (HSS). In this instance the certification period begins in the second month. (63-109.6) 2. Establishing Certification Periods Establish certification periods as follows: Generally, a certification period will be no fewer than 4 months. If it appears likely that the household will become ineligible for CalFresh in the near future, then a one- or two-month certification period may be assigned. All households will be assigned a 12-month certification period unless they fit into one of the following categories: When the household consists of: Then the certification period will be: ALL adult members who are elderly or disabled, 24 months ALL members who are elderly or disabled with no earned income, 36 months (63-360) Members living on an Indian Reservation, 24 months County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageCertification Periods 63-301 2 of 2 Procedure: Shortening Certification Periods: The certification period can be ended only if the Agency determines that the household is ineligible, and a timely Notice of Action is sent to the household. Lengthening Certification Periods: An established certification period may be lengthened, as long as the total months of the certification period do not exceed the maximum for the household type (12/24/36). If the certification period is extended: •Align the SAR Cycle to the new recertification period, if applicable •Send the household a Notice of Action advising them of the extended certification period Approval of CalFresh Pending CalWORKs: When CalFresh and CalWORKs eligibility are determined separately to meet required eligibility requirements and timeframes, the intake HSS will make a Non-Assistance CalFresh eligibility determination at the time the household meets the eligibility criteria or meets Expedited Services criteria, but no later than the 30th day after the application date. When CalFresh eligibility has been established, granting CalFresh will not be delayed pending a determination of CalWORKs eligibility. When the CalWORKs and CalFresh approval action is taken in a month other than the application month, the initial month of the public assistance grant is considered a retroactive payment and is not counted in the CalFresh budget. (63-285). References: MPP 63-504.1 CFR 273.10(f) CFPG 63-333 and 63-360 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 02/29/2024. RICK WANNE, Director Eligibility Operations

title: 63-302 Household Classification
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageHousehold Classification 63-302 1 of 2 Revision: 03/01/2021 Background: A household classification identifies the type of application being processed. Purpose: This section describes household classification policies. The purpose of this material revision it to reformat the section and due to sunset review. Policy: The classification of the CalFresh household determines numerous factors in the evaluation of eligibility, such as verification requirements and certification periods. The different categories of household classifications are detailed below. The presence of a non-household member, such as a Foster Care / Approved Relative Caretaker (ARC) child or an ineligible noncitizen, has no effect on the household’s classification. 1. Household Classifications The table below defines the different CalFresh households: A household that during any month . . . Will be classified as . . . at least one member: •does not receive federal CalWORKs benefits, •receives State CalWORKs benefits, or •does not receive Supplementary Security Income (SSI) Non-Assistance CalFresh (NACF) all members are receiving: •federal CalWORKs benefits, including two-parent family benefits, •SSI, or •Tribal TANF (Temporary Assistance to Needy Families) [ACIN I-34-05] Public Assistance CalFresh (PACF) there are members receiving federal CalWORKs and members who receive non-federal CalWORKs cash aid or members receiving no aid. Mixed CalFresh household (A mixed household is considered a NACF household) NOTE: For purposes of family reunification, parents, although ineligible for cash aid, will be considered a PACF household based on the children’s temporary absence from the home and the parent’s receipt of CalWORKs family reunification services. 2. Other CalFresh Household Classifications Other CalFresh classifications include Categorical Eligibility (CE) and Modified Categorical Eligibility (MCE). Refer to 63-120 for more information on these classifications References: MPP 63-102, 63-301.7, 80-301. title: 63-303 Notice of Action
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Notices of Action 63-303 1 of 2 Revision Date: 10/01/2021 Background: A Notice of Action (NOA) must be provided to households (HH) when action is being taken to approve, deny, discontinue, or change CalFresh benefits. Purpose: This section describes NOA requirements and is being revised after sunset review. Policy: An adequate NOA must inform the HH of the action being taken, the reason for the action, and the state regulation that supports the action. Adverse NOA’s must list what mandatory verification(s) are missing. The NOA must include information about the right to request a state hearing, the availability to receive Aid Paid Pending (APP) while waiting for a state hearing and the potential overissuance (OI) if the action is upheld at the hearing. The NOA must include a phone number to call for additional information and the availability of free legal representation. An adequate and timely NOA is required to inform a HH of any change in eligibility status or benefit level during the certification period. For a NOA to be considered timely, it must be mailed at least 10 calendar days prior to the effective date of the upcoming change(s) in benefits. A NOA must be provided in the HH’s preferred language when available. If a translated NOA is not available, the “Notice of Language Services” form must be provided to the HH with the NOA. HH’s have the option to receive certain NOAs electronically, instead of paper correspondence. For more information on electronic notices, refer to E- Notifications Processing Guide in Eligibility Operations Processing Guide (EOPG). 1. Timely NOA: The following actions do not require a timely NOA: •Mass changes where notices or posters are used to inform HH’s of a change in benefit amount. •HH receives an increase in benefits. •Terminating the eligibility of a resident of a drug and alcoholic treatment center when the facility loses its state certification. •A HH member is disqualified for an Internal Program Violation (IPV). This includes when the HH’s allotment is reduced or terminated due to the disqualification. •Benefits are reduced or discontinued because of the HH not responding to a request for verification which was postponed for Expedited Services (ES). •Voluntarily requests in writing or in person to discontinue their case. •The HH moves and is approved for benefits in another State or County. •A HH’s eligibility and benefits are being approved or denied under restoration. 2. NOA Exemptions: The following situations do not require a NOA: •All HH members are deceased. •HH has moved out of the County. •The HH has been receiving an increased allotment because of a restoration of lost benefits. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Notices of Action 63-303 2 of 2 •A Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) HH’s allotment is adjusted to consider changes which were anticipated at the time of certification. •A HH applied for Public Assistance (PA) and CalFresh benefits and has been receiving CalFresh pending the approval of the PA grant. The HH must have been notified at the time of the certification that CalFresh benefits may be reduced or terminated if the PA benefits were approved. •A HH is converted from a voluntary repayment to allotment benefit reduction because of failure to make agreed repayments. •A HH’s did not respond to a Notice of Expiration of Certification (NEC). •A HH did not respond to the X NOA (NA 960X SAR Stop Aid Report Not Received) or Y NOA (NA 960Y Stop Aid Report Incomplete). •Mass changes where notices or posters are used to inform HH’s of a change in benefit amount. Impacts: None References: ACIN I-33-21 MPP 63-504.2 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 10/31/2024. Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Self-Sufficiency Services
