title: 63-304 Recertification
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Recertification Number Page 63-304 1 of 7 Revision: 07/01/2024 Background: Households (HH) are required to complete a recertification prior to the end of their certification period to determine continuing eligibility. Purpose: This section describes the CalFresh recertification policy. It has been updated to include additional information about delayed processing and updated guidance on the recertification Notice of Action (NOA) requirements. Policy: CalFresh benefits may not continue beyond the end of the certification period without a new determination of eligibility . The information reported on the application for recertification, during the interview and through the verifications provided is to be used to determine continuing eligibility. Benefits for the new certification period shall be calculated using prospective budgeting and reasonably anticipated income and expenses. 1. Recertification Notice Requirements: HHs shall be provided a CalFresh Notice of Expiration of Certification (NEC) informing them of the impending expiration of their certification period. The NEC is to be provided to the HH before the first day of the last month of the certification period, but no more than 60 days prior to the end of the certification period. In addition to the NEC, a recertification appointment letter along with a packet containing the Recertification for CalFresh Benefits form (CF 37) shall be provided to the HH . The appointment notice specifies the date of the interview and the 15 -minute time block in which the HH will be contacted. Recertification interviews shall be scheduled by the 15 th day of the final month of the certification period. Documentation in the case record of when and how the HH was informed of the time-block interview appointment is required. For information on the recertification requirements for Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) HHs refer to Section 63-360. 2. Application for Recertification: HHs are required to complete an application for recertification as part of the recertification process. The application for recertification along with supporting documents may be submitted in person, by mail, fax , electronically, or over the phone with a telephonic signature and must be imaged in the case record. Any of the following forms may be accepted as the application for recertification if signed by an adult HH member: • CF 37. • Application for CalFresh Benefits (CF 285). • Application for CalFresh, Cash Aid, and/or Medi-Cal/Healthcare Programs (SAWS 2 Plus). • Initial Application for CalFresh, Cash Aid, and/or Medi-Cal/Healthcare Programs (SAWS 1). • CalFresh Elderly Simplified Application (CF 485). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Recertification Number Page 63-304 2 of 7 Note: The CF 485 was designed specifically for ESAP HHs; however, ESAP HHs can recertify using any acceptable application. If a non -ESAP HH provides a CF 485 it is to be accepted as an application for recertification. 3. Income Eligibility Verification System (IEVS) Processing at Recertification: An Applicant IEVS must be ordered and processed at recertification for all HH members whose income and resources are to be considered when determining eligibility. Use the IEVS report to assist in resolving any potential discrepancies that were reported on the application for recertification or during the interview. Note: A determination of eligibility must not be delayed while pending receipt of an Applicant IEVS. 4. Timely Applications for Recertification: Applications filed by the 15th day of the last month of the certification period will be considered timely . In the circumstance that a HH is certified for one or two months, the application for recertification will be considered timely if the HH returns the application within 15 days of the date the NEC is provided to them. HHs that file a timely application and meet all recertification requirements by the end of the certification period are entitled to receive uninterrupted benefits by their normal issuance cycle, if determined eligible. HHs lose their right to uninterrupted benefits when delaying the process by missing a scheduled interview and/or failing to provide requested information by the due date. A HH can still get uninterrupted benefits if all recertification requirements are completed by the end of the certification period. 5. Recertification Interview: HHs are required to complete an interview as part of the recertification process. Contact the HH on the scheduled date and time of their interview appointment. Several attempts must be made during the 15-minute time block to contact the HH. All attempts to contact the HH must be documented in the case record. Refer to Flexible Interview Scheduling Eligibility Policy and Procedure Guide (EPPG) for further guidance. Send a Notice of Missed Interview (NOMI) when all attempts to contact the HH during their scheduled appointment are unsuccessful. The NOMI shall be dated to reflect the end of the certification period, even when the certification period end date falls on a weekend or holiday. For more information on the interview requirements refer to Section 63 -115. During the recertification interview staff are required to: • Provide the Rights and Responsibilities (R&Rs). • Provide the SAR 7 Eligibility Status Report requirements and instructions. • Review information and verification s provided and clarify/resolve any missing, unclear or inconsistent information. • Explain the verifications that are needed to complete the recertification and provide the HH with a verification checklist (VCL). • Inform individuals subject to work registration of their requirements. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Recertification Number Page 63-304 3 of 7 6. Delayed Processing: An application for recertification is considered delayed when the process is not completed by the end of the last month of the certification period. The cause of the delay will be defined as follows: Cause of Delay Definition County County caused delays include, but are not limited to: • Telephonic signature was not obtained during the interview. • A valid VCL was not issued to the HH. • Assistance was not offered in obtaining required verifications. • 10 days were not allowed for the HH to submit required verifications. • The interview was not scheduled. • The interview could not be rescheduled until late in the certification period and the 10 days to provide missing verifications extended passed current certification period. HH HH caused delays include, but are not limited to failure to: • Complete the recertification process. • Appear for the interview. • Reschedule the interview until the month following the end of the certification period. 7. Benefit Determination for County Caused Delays: When the recertification is delayed due to the fault of the county, once the recertification process is completed and the HH is found to be eligible for ongoing benefits , it is entitled to a full month of benefits for the first month of the new certification period . If the HH is found to be ineligible for ongoing benefits, deny the application for recertification and do not issue any benefits. Below are examples of county caused delays: Example: County Caused Delay Scenario • Certification period ends March 31. • HH submits the CF 37 on March 10. • Interview is scheduled March 11. • Interview is completed on March 11 and there are pending verifications, but the county did not send a VCL. • No verifications are provided by March 31. • The recertification is denied and a failure to provide denial NOA sent to the HH no later than March 31. • HH contacts the county on April 2 because they did not get their benefits. • VCL mailed April 2; verifications due by April 12. • HH provides verifications April 10. Outcome Rescind the denial, complete the recertification, and provide the full allotment to the HH within five working days of April 10. Example: County Caused Delay Scenario • Certification period ends March 31. • HH submits the CF 37 on March 10. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Recertification Number Page 63-304 4 of 7 • Interview is scheduled for March 15. • HH fails to complete the interview and NOMI is issued. • HH calls March 17, and the county reschedules the interview for April 2. • The recertification is denied and a failure to complete the recertification denial NOA sent to the HH no later than March 31. • Interview is completed April 2 and a VCL sent; verifications due by April 12. • HH submits verifications on April 8. Outcome Rescind the denial, complete the recertification and provide the full allotment to the HH within five working days of April 8. Example: County Caused Delay Scenario • Certification period ends March 31. • HH submits the CF 37 on March 10. • Interview not scheduled in March. • The recertification is denied and a failure to complete the recertification denial NOA sent to the HH no later than March 31. • HH contacts county because no benefits were issued for April. • County schedules interview for April 5. • Interview completed April 5 and a VCL is sent; verifications due by April 15. • Verification provided on April 15. Outcome Rescind the denial, complete the recertification and provide the full allotment to the HH within five working days of April 15. 8. Benefit Determination for HH Caused Delays: The HH loses the right to uninterrupted benefits when it has been given at least 10 days to provide required verification and has failed to do so or has not completed the recertification interview. The HH has 30 days from the end of the certification period to complete the recertification process . If the recertification is completed within this timeframe, prorate benefits from the date the last required action was completed if the HH is found to be eligible to ongoing benefits . A HH making an untimely application for recertification will not be denied the right to complete the recertification unless they refuse to cooperate, or the delayed processing period has ended. Below are examples of HH caused delays: Example: HH Caused Delay Scenario • Certification period ends March 31. • HH submits the CF 37 on March 10. • Interview is scheduled for March 15. • Interview is completed March 15, and the VCL sent; verifications due by March 25. • Verifications are not provided by March 25. • The recertification is denied and a failure to provide denial NOA sent to the HH no later than March 31. • The HH provides the verifications late on April 3. Outcome Complete the recertification, issue prorated benefits as of April 3. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Recertification Number Page 63-304 5 of 7 Example: HH Caused Delay Scenario • Certification period ends March 31. • CF 37 submitted March 10. • Interview scheduled March 12. • HH fails to complete the interview; NOMI is issued. • The recertification is denied and a failure to complete the recertification denial NOA sent to the HH no later than March 31. • HH contacts the county on April 5. • Interview rescheduled for April 6. • Interview completed April 6 and a VCL is sent; verifications due by April 16. • Verifications not provided by April 16. • Denial NOA sent to the HH for failure to provide. • Verifications provided April 29. Outcome Complete the recertification and issue prorated benefits as of April 29. Example: HH Caused Delay Scenario • Certification period ends March 31. • CF 37 submitted March 10. • Interview scheduled March 13. • HH fails to complete the interview; NOMI is issued. • The recertification is denied and a failure to complete the recertification denial NOA sent to the HH no later than March 31. • HH contacts the county on April 4. • Interview completed April 4 and a VCL is sent; verifications due by April 14. • Verifications provided April 7. Outcome Complete the recertification and issue prorated benefits as of April 7. 9. 30-Day Income Verification Requirement at Recertification: HHs are required to provide 30 days of income verification. The 30-day timeframe will be determined as follows: If the HH… then… provides verification of the most recent 30 days of income with their recertification, this is sufficient, and no additional verification is required. does not provide income verification with their recertification, verification of income must be requested for the 30 days prior to the date the VCL is provided. provides partial or verification older than 30 days prior to recertification or date specified on the VCL, but the income can be reasonably anticipated for the upcoming payment period, it is sufficient to use. Example: Scenario HH provides the CF 37 prior to the interview but does not provide income verification along with it. During the interview on May 3 the customer states they County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Recertification Number Page 63-304 6 of 7 have income and verification is required to be provided. Outcome A VCL is provided to the HH on May 3 requesting proof of income received between April 3 and May 2 (30 days from the date the VCL is issued). Note: For assistance calculating the 30 days refer to Desk Aid 30-Day Period Calculator. 10. Personal Contact: Prior to terminating benefits, an attempt to contact the HH to remind them that their recertification is incomplete must be made. If successful in reaching the HH, attempt to collect the information needed to complete the recertification process. Document all call attempts in the case record. 11. NOA Requirements for Recertifications: A recertification is an application for a new certification period and an approval or denial NOA shall be issued. Recertifications do not require 10-day notice to decrease benefits. When an application for recertification is received but the HH misses the scheduled interview or fails to provide required documents, the recertification shall be denied and an accurate denial NOA shall be sent. The NEC does not satisfy the requirement for denying an application for recertification. The NEC, alone, is only sufficient when the HH never submitted an application for recertification. Below are examples of which NOA shall be sent in various scenarios. Example Scenario • Certification period ends March 31. • CF 37 submitted March 12. • Interview completed March 15; VCL sent with verifications due March 25. • Verifications provided March 20. Outcome Approval NOA is provided. Example Scenario • Certification period ends March 31. • CF 37 submitted March 10. • Interview completed March 15; VCL sent with verifications due March 25. • Verifications are not provided by March 25. Outcome Failure to provide denial NOA is provided listing the items the HH did not provide. Example Scenario • Certification period ends March 31. • CF 37 submitted March 10. • Interview scheduled for March 12. • HH fails to show for the interview; NOMI is issued. • HH does not reschedule the interview by March 31. Outcome Denial NOA is provided to the HH no later than March 31 with the denial reason of failure to complete the recertification. Example Scenario • Certification period ends March 31. • Interview scheduled for March 12. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Recertification Number Page 63-304 7 of 7 • HH fails to show for the interview; NOMI is issued. • HH does not submit a CF 37 by March 31. Outcome No further NOA is necessary, the NEC NOA is sufficient. sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Recertification Number Page 63-304 1 of 7 Revision: 07/01/2024 Background: Households (HH) are required to complete a recertification prior to the end of their certification period to determine continuing eligibility. Purpose: This section describes the CalFresh recertification policy. It has been updated to include additional information about delayed processing and updated guidance on the recertification Notice of Action (NOA) requirements. Policy: CalFresh benefits may not continue beyond the end of the certification period without a new determination of eligibility . The information reported on the application for recertification, during the interview and through the verifications provided is to be used to determine continuing eligibility. Benefits for the new certification period shall be calculated using prospective budgeting and reasonably anticipated income and expenses. 1. Recertification Notice Requirements: HHs shall be provided a CalFresh Notice of Expiration of Certification (NEC) informing them of the impending expiration of their certification period. The NEC is to be provided to the HH before the first day of the last month of the certification period, but no more than 60 days prior to the end of the certification period. In addition to the NEC, a recertification appointment letter along with a packet containing the Recertification for CalFresh Benefits form (CF 37) shall be provided to the HH . The appointment notice specifies the date of the interview and the 15 -minute time block in which the HH will be contacted. Recertification interviews shall be scheduled by the 15 th day of the final month of the certification period. Documentation in the case record of when and how the HH was informed of the time-block interview appointment is required. For information on the recertification requirements for Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) HHs refer to Section 63-360. 2. Application for Recertification: HHs are required to complete an application for recertification as part of the recertification process. The application for recertification along with supporting documents may be submitted in person, by mail, fax , electronically, or over the phone with a telephonic signature and must be imaged in the case record. Any of the following forms may be accepted as the application for recertification if signed by an adult HH member: • CF 37. • Application for CalFresh Benefits (CF 285). • Application for CalFresh, Cash Aid, and/or Medi-Cal/Healthcare Programs (SAWS 2 Plus). • Initial Application for CalFresh, Cash Aid, and/or Medi-Cal/Healthcare Programs (SAWS 1). • CalFresh Elderly Simplified Application (CF 485). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Recertification Number Page 63-304 2 of 7 Note: The CF 485 was designed specifically for ESAP HHs; however, ESAP HHs can recertify using any acceptable application. If a non -ESAP HH provides a CF 485 it is to be accepted as an application for recertification. 3. Income Eligibility Verification System (IEVS) Processing at Recertification: An Applicant IEVS must be ordered and processed at recertification for all HH members whose income and resources are to be considered when determining eligibility. Use the IEVS report to assist in resolving any potential discrepancies that were reported on the application for recertification or during the interview. Note: A determination of eligibility must not be delayed while pending receipt of an Applicant IEVS. 4. Timely Applications for Recertification: Applications filed by the 15th day of the last month of the certification period will be considered timely . In the circumstance that a HH is certified for one or two months, the application for recertification will be considered timely if the HH returns the application within 15 days of the date the NEC is provided to them. title: 63-306 Restoration of Eligibility
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Restoration of Eligibility Waiver Number Page 63-306 1 of 2 Revision Date: 06/01/2024 Background: The restoration of eligibility waiver allows households (HH s) that have been discontinued from CalFresh for failure to provide required verification at the periodic report to have their eligibility restored in the month following termination. Purpose: This section details the policies for restoration of eligibility. This section is being revised due to sunset review, there are no changes in legislation. Policy: HHs that discontinue for failure to provide a timely or complete SAR 7 Eligibility Status Report Form , required verification, or other information at periodic report may have their benefits restored in the month following the discontinuance. The missing verifications must be submitted within the 30 days following the date of discontinuance. If the HH provide s the missing verifications needed to reestablish eligibility , a new application or interview is not required, and restoration of benefits may be processed. Benefits for the initial month of restoration will be prorated as of the date the HH provides all the required information needed to establish eligibility. 1. Good Cause Determination Good cause must be evaluated before processing restoration. Refer to CalFresh Program Guide section 63-274 for guidance on good cause. If the HH does not meet good cause criteria, evaluate for restoration. 2. HHs Not Eligible for Restoration The following HHs are not eligible for restoration and must reapply for CalFresh: • HHs that did not complete their recertification. • HHs returning to the County after moving away and being discontinued. • Disqualified HHs, for example Intentional Program Violators ( IPVs) or individuals who voluntary quit a job without good cause. 3. Certification and Semi-Annual Report (SAR) Cycle HHs that have had their eligibility restored will keep their original certification and SAR cycle. Restored HH s are considered recipients, and therefore, should not be evaluated for expedited services. 4. Restoration Processing When the HH submits a complete SAR 7 the month immediately after discontinuance, eligibility and allotment amount will be determined based on the information that is reported for the SAR 7 data month. When processing the SAR 7, recipient budgeting rules will apply. If the HH is determined to be ineligible, the original discontinuance will remain in effect. Changes reported at SAR 7 that did not occur or were not known to the HH in the data month, will be treated as a voluntary mid- period report. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Restoration of Eligibility Waiver Number Page 63-306 2 of 2 Act only on those voluntary mid- period reports that are considered verified upon receipt (VUR) or result in an increase in benefits. 5. Decrease in Benefits at Restoration If information provided on the SAR 7 results in a decrease in benefits from the amount previously issued, timely notice is not required to restore aid at a lower amount. Timely notice is not required to decrease benefits when restoring eligibility. 6. Erroneous Discontinuances If during the restoration process if it is determined that a HH has been erroneously discontinued, then the discontinuance must be rescinded, and eligibility and benefits reestablished at the prior level without proration. Refer to Job Aid (JA) How to Rescind a Case for additional guidance. 7. Notices of Action (NOAs) When restoring eligibility, the following NOAs must be sent to the HH: • CF 388 CalFresh Notice of Restoration Approval. • CF 389 Notice of Denial of Restoration. References: All County Letters (ACLs) 10-32; 12-35; 13-88; 18-96; 22-51. All County Information Notices (ACINs) I-50-12. JA How to Rescind a Case. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 06/30/2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-321 Transitional CalFresh
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Transitional CalFresh Number Page 63-321 1 of 5 Revision Date: 12/01/2023 Background: California has opted into the f ederal regulation which allows states the option to offer Transitional CalFresh (TCF) benefits to households (HH) leaving the CalWORKs program. TCF benefits ensure HHs can continue to meet their nutritional needs once they are no longer receiving the cash benefits. Purpose: This section defines the TCF program , identifies when the program should be implemented , and explains the TCF recertification process. The section is being revised to merge together all information regarding TCF. Policy: A HH receiving Public Assistance CalFresh (PACF) in the month their CalWORKs discontinues must automatically be provided TCF benefits if CalWORKs discontinues for a qualifying reason. At least one HH member must have received CalWORKs and PACF in the month CalWORKs discontinues for the HH to be eligible for TCF. When a HH is approved for TCF, the benefits will begin the first of the month following the CalWORKs discontinuance. A CalFresh Notice of Approval/Termination Transitional Benefits ( CF 1239) shall be sent to the HH upon TCF approval. The TCF certification period will be five-months and TCF benefits will remain unchanged for the duration of the certification period. At the end of the certification period the HH will be required to recertify to regular CalFresh, or the benefits will discontinue. In no circumstance shall TCF benefits be issued for more than five months. 1. Conditions of Eligibility to TCF A HH is eligible to TCF, if CalWORKs discontinues for one of the following reasons and the HH is receiving PACF in the month of discontinuance. • HH exceeded the income or property limit. • HH requested to close CalWORKs. • The only eligible HH member was a parent and the parent timed out. • The only eligible HH member was a child and the child aged out. • The only eligible HH member(s) were children, and they left the home. • HH is disqualified due to a CalWORKs rule change. • Whereabouts unknown. • Only adult in the case is incarcerated. A HH would not be eligible to TCF if CalWORKs discontinues for one of the following reasons, even if they were receiving PACF in the month of discontinuance. • HH was approved Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) or Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF) in another state. • All HH members are sanctioned. • Incomplete or failure to submit an Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7). • Incomplete or failure to submit the CalWORKs redetermination. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Transitional CalFresh Number Page 63-321 2 of 5 • HH moved out of state. • A HH containing two or more CalWORKs cases in which all of the CalWORKs cases are not being discontinued. • All HH members are deceased. • Failure to provide information/verification necessary to determine CalWORKs eligibility. • The CalWORKs grant decreases to a zero basic grant. • HH issued diversion payments instead of CalWORKs. • HH issued CalWORKs immediate need and is later denied CalWORKs. Note: A HH discontinuing from Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA), General Relief (GR), or Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants (CAPI) is not eligible to TCF. 2. TCF HH Members All HH members receiving PACF , that are not sanctioned from CalWORKs in the month CalWORKs discontinues, will be eligible to TCF. TCF benefits will be calculated excluding the CalWORKs sanctioned individual from the TCF HH size. In addition, any HH member who was ineligible to PACF in the month CalWORKs discontinued will also be ineligible to TCF. Example: Scenario HH of 3 (mom and 2 minor children) is receiving CalWORKs and PACF. Mom is sanctioned from CalWORKs for failure to comply with Welfare to Work (WTW). She is receiving PACF due to a work registration exemption. On May 5th the HH reports mom started working and the HH is over income for the CalWORKs program. Outcome CalWORKs discontinues as of May 31st. TCF is approved as of June 1st for a HH of 2. Mom is ineligible to receive TCF since she was sanctioned from CalWORKs in the month of discontinuance. 3. Calculation of TCF Benefits TCF benefits are calculated using the existing income that was in the PACF budget in the final month the HH received CalWORKs minus the CalWORKs grant. The new or increased income that may have resulted in the loss of CalWORKs will not be counted when calculating the TCF benefits. Example: Scenario HH of 2 (mo m and 1 child, age 5 ) receiving CalWORKs and PACF . Mom was earning $600 bi -weekly, and they pa y $1000 per month in rent + S tandard Utility Allowance (SUA). On July 10, 2023, HH reports mom’s income increased to $1200 bi-weekly, which exceeds the CalWORKs income limit. CalWORKs discontinues for over income. The HH is eligible to TCF as of August 1, 2023. Outcome The TCF HH would consist of mom and 1 child. Budget July 2023 August 2023 Earned income $1300.20 $1300.20 CalWORKs grant $545 $0 Shelter $1000 $1000 SUA $560 $560 CalFresh Allotment $285 - TCF Allotment - $449 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Transitional CalFresh Number Page 63-321 3 of 5 4. Incorrect TCF Benefits and Overissuance Calculation If TCF benefits are correctly computed based on the PACF benefits the HH received in the final month of CalWORKs, both the county and the HH shall be held harmless for inaccuracies in the TCF benefit due to prior errors in the PACF benefit. When the PACF amount issued during the last month of CalWORKs could not be decreased because timely notice could not be given to reduce the benefits . The TCF benefit amount will be based on what the HH was receiving at the time of the CalWORKs discontinuance and no overissuance will be created. TCF benefit overissuances shall only be created for the following reasons: • The initial TCF benefit amount was determined incorrectly due to county error. • The TCF benefit amount erroneously increased during the five-month certification period. Note: Overissuances being recouped in the month of CalWORKs discontinuance will continue to be recouped during the TCF period. HHs are not required to report any changes during the TCF period , nor will action be taken on any changes reported. Once TCF benefits are calculated, they will be frozen for the duration of the TCF certification period. TCF benefits will not be recalculated or terminated even if the following changes occur: • HH moves out of the state. • HH moves in with another HH who has active CalFresh, and they report to Purchase and Prepare (P&P) together or are restricted HH members. • Case is Inter-County Transferred (ICT). • A HH member becomes ineligible to CalFresh e.g.: ineligible student. • HH has out-of-state Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) usage. The following are exceptions and action must be taken to recalculate or discontinue TCF during the five-month certification period: If… then… HH requests discontinuance of TCF, discontinue TCF. CalWORKs is rescinded, discontinue TCF. the entire HH is approved CalWORKs (TANF) and/or CalFresh (SNAP) benefits in any other case, county, or state, discontinue TCF. if an individual member of the HH is approved CalWORKs (TANF) and/or CalFresh (SNAP) benefits in any other case, county, or state, the TCF benefit amount shall be recalculated for the remaining HH members by removing the individual from the HH along with his/her income and expenses. the HH fails or refuses to cooperate with a Quality Control (QC) review, discontinue TCF. an individual is determined to be an Intentional Program Violator (IPV) while the HH is receiving TCF, the TCF benefit amount shall be recalculated by removing the IPV as an eligible HH member while continuing to count their income in the TCF budget. Note: An individual may not receive CalWORKs and TCF simultaneously. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Transitional CalFresh Number Page 63-321 4 of 5 5. Recission of CalWORKs After TCF is Approved When the CalWORKs discontinuance is rescinded within 30 days of the discontinuance date due to good cause, TCF will be transferred back to PACF the following month and CalFresh benefits will be re-calculated. An overissuance will not be created , because TCF was correctly granted based on available information at the time CalWORKs discontinued . When the HH is transferred to PACF from TCF, the recertification month must be transferred back to the original recertification month prior to TCF being granted. 6. Reapplication of CalWORKs After TCF is Approved A HH may reapply and be approved for CalWORKs after TCF is approved. When that happens the HH will be transferred back to PACF, and benefits shall be re-calculated based on the information provided on the application. The recertification date for CalFresh must be aligned with the recertification date of the newly approved CalWORKs case. The HH may receive one or two months of TCF before PACF is issued, depending on when CalWORKs is approved. Example: Scenario CalWORKs discontinues March 31, 2023, due to over income. TCF is approved April 1, 2023, thru August 31, 2023. The HH reapplies for CalWORKs on May 10, 2023, and is approved CalWORKs on June 5, 2023, for a twelve-month certification period with a redetermination due in April 2024. Outcome Since the HH cannot receive CalWORKs and TCF simultaneously, once CalWORKs is approved TCF must be transferred back to PACF with benefits recalculated based on the information reported on the CalWORKs application. TCF must be terminated and transferred back to PACF as of July 1, 2023, and the recertification date for CalFresh will be aligned with CalWORKs to April 2024. 7. Recertification During the TCF Period HHs receiving TCF may elect to recertify eligibility to CalFresh at any time during the five -month TCF certification period. In order to recertify, the HH shall submit an application for recertification. When the HH elects to recertify during the first four months of the TCF certification period, benefits may increase or decrease once recertified to regular CalFresh. HHs have the option to withdraw the recertification application and continue TCF if this is more advantageous to them. The table below identifies the process staff must follow when the HH elects to recertify TCF benefits in the first four months of the TCF period. If… then… staff determine that the HH is entitled to more CalFresh benefits than it is currently receiving for TCF and TCF benefits have already been issued for the first month of the certification period, issue a supplement for the first month of the CalFresh certification period. The new certification period will begin the first of the month following the month the HH submitted the application for recertification. A CF 1239 shall be sent to the HH informing them of the TCF discontinuance. The HH is determined to be ineligible for regular CalFresh, deny the application. TCF will continue until the end of five-month certification period and the regular County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Transitional CalFresh Number Page 63-321 5 of 5 recertification process will be initiated the fourth month of the TCF certification period. The HH is determined eligible for CalFresh, but is entitled to a benefit lower than their current TCF benefit, ask if the HH would like to withdraw their application for recertification allowing them to continue receiving TCF until the end of the five-month certification period. If the HH chooses to continue with the recertification, process the recertification and begin a new certification period. A CF 1239 shall be sent to the HH informing them of the TCF discontinuance. The application for recertification is denied for a reason besides the HH being ineligible to regular CalFresh, deny the application. TCF will continue until the end of five-month certification period and the regular recertification process will be initiated the fourth month of the TCF certification period. Example: Scenario HH applies on May 25 th for recertification, May is the third month of the TCF certification period. The HH is determined eligible to more CalFresh benefits than they are currently receiving for TCF. Outcome The new certification period for regular CalFresh will begin June 1 st. If the HH already got TCF benefits for June, a supplement will be issued. 8. Recertification at the End of the TCF Period At the end of the five-month TCF certification period, the HH must recertify eligibility to regular CalFresh. The HH will receive a Notice of Expiration (NEC) in the fourth month, informing them their benefits will terminate at the end of the following month if a recertification is not completed. A CalFresh recertification application and packet will be sent to the HH. TCF recertification follows the same rules as regular CalFresh recertification. sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Transitional CalFresh Number Page 63-321 1 of 5 Revision Date: 12/01/2023 Background: California has opted into the f ederal regulation which allows states the option to offer Transitional CalFresh (TCF) benefits to households (HH) leaving the CalWORKs program. TCF benefits ensure HHs can continue to meet their nutritional needs once they are no longer receiving the cash benefits. Purpose: This section defines the TCF program , identifies when the program should be implemented , and explains the TCF recertification process. The section is being revised to merge together all information regarding TCF. Policy: A HH receiving Public Assistance CalFresh (PACF) in the month their CalWORKs discontinues must automatically be provided TCF benefits if CalWORKs discontinues for a qualifying reason. At least one HH member must have received CalWORKs and PACF in the month CalWORKs discontinues for the HH to be eligible for TCF. When a HH is approved for TCF, the benefits will begin the first of the month following the CalWORKs discontinuance. A CalFresh Notice of Approval/Termination Transitional Benefits ( CF 1239) shall be sent to the HH upon TCF approval. The TCF certification period will be five-months and TCF benefits will remain unchanged for the duration of the certification period. At the end of the certification period the HH will be required to recertify to regular CalFresh, or the benefits will discontinue. In no circumstance shall TCF benefits be issued for more than five months. 1. Conditions of Eligibility to TCF A HH is eligible to TCF, if CalWORKs discontinues for one of the following reasons and the HH is receiving PACF in the month of discontinuance. • HH exceeded the income or property limit. • HH requested to close CalWORKs. • The only eligible HH member was a parent and the parent timed out. • The only eligible HH member was a child and the child aged out. • The only eligible HH member(s) were children, and they left the home. • HH is disqualified due to a CalWORKs rule change. • Whereabouts unknown. • Only adult in the case is incarcerated. A HH would not be eligible to TCF if CalWORKs discontinues for one of the following reasons, even if they were receiving PACF in the month of discontinuance. • HH was approved Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) or Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF) in another state. • All HH members are sanctioned. • Incomplete or failure to submit an Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7). • Incomplete or failure to submit the CalWORKs redetermination. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Transitional CalFresh Number Page 63-321 2 of 5 • HH moved out of state. • A HH containing two or more CalWORKs cases in which all of the CalWORKs cases are not being discontinued. • All HH members are deceased. • Failure to provide information/verification necessary to determine CalWORKs eligibility. • The CalWORKs grant decreases to a zero basic grant. • HH issued diversion payments instead of CalWORKs. • HH issued CalWORKs immediate need and is later denied CalWORKs. Note: A HH discontinuing from Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA), General Relief (GR), or Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants (CAPI) is not eligible to TCF. 2. TCF HH Members All HH members receiving PACF , that are not sanctioned from CalWORKs in the month CalWORKs discontinues, will be eligible to TCF. TCF benefits will be calculated excluding the CalWORKs sanctioned individual from the TCF HH size. In addition, any HH member who was ineligible to PACF in the month CalWORKs discontinued will also be ineligible to TCF. Example: Scenario HH of 3 (mom and 2 minor children) is receiving CalWORKs and PACF. Mom is sanctioned from CalWORKs for failure to comply with Welfare to Work (WTW). title: 63-330 CalFresh Expansion for SSI-SSP Recipients
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageCalFresh Expansion for Recipients of Supplementary Security Income (SSI) and/or California State Supplementary Payment (SSP) 63-330 1 of 2 Effective Date: 06/01/19 Background: The federal government allows a state the option to increase the SSP grant instead of administering the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) to SSI/SSP recipients. This option is known as SSI/SSP cash-out. California chose to implement the cash-out policy in 1974 when the federal government began the combined federal-state SSI/SSP program. Effective June 1, 2019, California is reversing this policy and expanding CalFresh eligibility to individuals receiving SSI/SSP, provided they meet all other eligibility criteria. Purpose: This section details the policy change and impacts to determining eligibility for SSI/SSP recipient households. Policy: 63-330.1 Household Effective Dates Newly Eligible Households Households in which all members are SSI/SSP recipients are potentially eligible as of the implementation date (June 1, 2019). Benefits may NOT be issued before the implementation date. Ongoing Households Households currently receiving CalFresh with an excluded member who is an SSI/SSP recipient, will have the policy change implemented on a rolling basis at the next periodic report, recertification or when voluntarily requested by the household, no earlier than the implementation date. If an ongoing household makes a voluntary mid-period report of a household composition change, it will be considered a request to implement the reversal of the cash-out policy and the previously excluded SSI/SSP recipient will be added to the household. This rule applies whether or not the reported household composition change is specific to the SSI/SSP recipient. The voluntary midperiod report may be made verbally or in writing and is considered verified upon receipt (VUR). Adjust the household’s benefits prospectively, as soon as timely and adequate notice can be provided. 63-330.2 Income, Resources and Deductions As of the household effective date, members who were previously excluded due to receipt of SSI/SSP will become included household members. Their income, resources and deductions will be considered when determining eligibility for the household. Reevaluate deductions when the deduction was previously prorated, due to the contribution of the SSI/SSP recipient who is now included in the household. 63-330.3 Verification Before requesting documentation, verify SSI/SSP recipient income, payment status, etc. using existing data matches and databases such as: •Payment Verification System (PVS) •Income and Eligibility Verification System (IEVS) •Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS) Network County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageCalFresh Expansion for Recipients of Supplementary Security Income (SSI) and/or California State Supplementary Payment (SSP) 63-330 2 of 2 63-330.4 Staggered Certification Periods To stagger the increase of recertification cases after initial implementation, newly eligible SSI/SSP only households approved between June 1, 2019 and November 30, 2019, will be assigned a shorter certification period. See Processing Guide 330-01 for more information. Procedure: Processing Guide 330-1 Program Impact/s: Automation CalWIN will be updated with Release 57 Other Programs Affected No Impact Quality Control Quality Control will cite the appropriate error when regulations cited in this program material have not been followed. title: 63-331 Supplemental Nutrition Benefit Program
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Supplemental Nutrition Benefit (SNB) Program 63-331 1 of 3 Effective Date: 06/01/19 Background: Effective June 1, 2019, California is reversing cash-out policy and expanding CalFresh eligibility to individuals who receive SSI/SSP, provided they meet all other eligibility criteria. SNB is a state-funded nutrition benefit program intended for existing CalFresh households negatively impacted by the reversal of cash-out policies. (63-330) SNB will provide households with additional nutrition benefits to offset the reduction of CalFresh benefits. Purpose: This section details the impacts of the SNB Program when determining eligibility, as of the implementation date, for existing households that include at least one SSI/SSP recipient. Policy: 63-331.1 Eligibility to SNB Households are eligible for SNB if they are both: •Receiving CalFresh benefits, include at least one excluded SSI/SSP recipient on the implementation date (June 1, 2019); and •Experience a CalFresh benefit reduction when the previously excluded SSI/SSP recipient(s) is added to the household on the effective date. Note: The benefit reduction is not required to be caused solely as a result of adding the previously excluded SSI/SSP recipient to the household. 63-331.2 SNB Household Effective Date The effective date for existing households will be the household’s next periodic report, recertification* or when voluntarily requested by the household, on or after the implementation date. *Including recertification of Transitional CalFresh (TCF) cases. 63-331.3 Households Not Eligible to SNB •Households that include an SSI/SSP recipient and experience a benefit reduction after the household’s effective date. •The household’s only SSI/SSP recipient at the household’s effective date is not the same SSI/SSP recipient(s) excluded from the household on the implementation date. •Households that include only an SSI/SSP recipient in suspense status (not receiving SSI/SSP benefits) receiving CalFresh benefits on the implementation date. •Households that lose CalFresh eligibility, also lose SNB eligibility. •Households that are eligible for and receive TNB Program benefits will not, at any time, be eligible for SNB Program benefits. 63-331.4 Household Reporting/Recertification •SNB eligible households are not required to make any SNB specific mid-period or midcertification reports. •If you discover the household no longer includes at least one of the same SSI/SSP recipients excluded from the household on the implementation date, discontinue SNB eligibility, mid period, at the periodic report, or at recertification. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Supplemental Nutrition Benefit (SNB) Program 63-331 2 of 3 •SNB eligibility will be re-determined at CalFresh recertification. 63-331.5 Restoration •Restore without proration, an SNB eligible household’s benefits when CalFresh benefits are restored following discontinuance for failure to provide necessary documentation or information. 63-331.6 SNB Benefit Issuance •The amount of benefits issued monthly to each eligible household will be based on the benefit table. (See Table in 63-1105) •The benefit level is assigned to the eligible household permanently, based on circumstances on the effective date, as long as they remain eligible to the SNB Program. •The benefits cannot be prorated. A full month’s SNB Program benefit will be issued for the month that the prorated CalFresh benefits are issued. (e.g.: At CalFresh Restoration) •The monthly benefit will be made available in the EBT account based on the last digit of the household’s case number at the time of the effective date. Exception: A victim of domestic violence who was included as a member of a household that also includes the abuser, but who was assigned a new case number in order to receive benefits as a separate household. SNB eligibility may be transferred to the new household if it includes at least one of the same SSI/SSP recipients excluded from the household on the implementation date. 63-331.7 SNB Program InterCounty Transfers (ICT) •Transfer SNB Program benefits along with the household’s CalFresh to the new county of residence. •Do not terminate SNB Program benefits as a result of an ICT. 63-331.8 SNB Benefit Use, Account Aging and Expungement •SNB benefits can be used the same way that CalFresh benefits can be used. •SNB benefits are subject to existing EBT account aging and expungement rules. •Expunged SNB benefits will not be reinstated. Procedure: Processing Guides 330-01 and 331-01 Program Impact/s: Appeals SNB households have the right to appeal actions taken on their case and benefits may be issued as a result of an appeal or a hearing decision. However, SNB benefits cannot be issued as Aid Paid Pending (APP) an appeal. Automation CalWIN will be updated with Release 57 Other Programs Affected SNB Program benefits are nutrition benefits and will not be considered income for any means-tested program, including but not limited to, CalWORKs, Medi-Cal, General Relief and SSI/SSP. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Supplemental Nutrition Benefit (SNB) Program 63-331 3 of 3 Quality Control Quality Control will cite the appropriate error when regulations cited in this program material have not been followed. title: 63-332 Transitional Nutrition Benefit (TNB) Program
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Transitional Nutrition Benefit (TNB) Program Number 63-332 Page 1 of 2 Revision: 01/01/2022 Background: Transitional Nutrition Benefit (TNB) is a state-funded program offered to CalFresh (CF) recipients who are negatively impacted by the CF program expansion to Supplemental Security Income/State Supplementary Payment (SSI/SSP) recipients. Purpose: This section includes policy information related to the eligibility for TNB. This section is being revised to include changes to the recertification and restoration timeframe. Effective November 2021, all TNB recertifications will be paused for two years to implement the necessary automation. Policy: As of June 1, 2019, previously excluded SSI/SSP recipients were added to active CF cases. If at that time the newly added SSI/SSP recipient caused ineligibility, then the household (HH) is eligible to TNB. The date that the HH becomes TNB eligible will be known as the effective date. TNB is not considered as income. TNB can be used the same way as CF benefits and is subject to existing Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) account aging and expungement rules. The following circumstances make a HH ineligible to TNB: • Discontinuance for not complying with the CF recertification process Supplemental Nutrition Benefits (SNB) eligible HHs SSI/SSP recipients in suspense status receiving CF benefits on the implementation date Non-California residents • HH that no longer includes the SSI/SSP recipient(s) Note: TNB HHs are not required to make any TNB mid-period reports. HHs that regain eligibility for regular CF, will be discontinued from TNB, and eligibility cannot be re-established. 1. Benefit Levels: TNB is a fixed benefit level determined by HH size. Refer to the Eligibility Standards Table in 63- 1101.9. TNB benefits cannot be prorated. The monthly benefit will be made available in the EBT account based on the last digit of the HH's case number at the time of the effective date. 2. Certification/Recertification: The TNB initial and recertification period will be 12-months. The Notice of Recertification for the TNB Program (TNB 4) is also the Notice of Expiration of Certification (NEC). The TNB Program recertification process does not require an interview. title: 63-333 Social Security Administration (SSA) Joint Processing of CalFresh Application
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Social Security Administration (SSA) Joint Processing of CalFresh Application Number Pa ge 63-333 1 of 3 Revision Date: 2/1/2025 Background: As of June 1, 2019, CalFresh pr ogram eligibility expa nded to include households (HHs) that consist solely of Supplemental Security Income (SSI)/St ate Supplementary Payment (SSP) recipients. To support this change, a national Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) has been established outlining CalFresh related services that the SSA will pr ovide, including the SSA operations for taking applications. Purpose: This section outlines the SSA jo int application process and the tr ansition from the GetCalFresh application assistance tool to the BenefitsCal online portal for the submission of CalFresh applications by the SSA. Policy: Under federal regulations, HHs including only SSI/SSP applicant s or recipients may apply and be certified for CalFresh under SSA joint processing procedures, if all eligibility criteria are met. HHs that include both SSI/SSP applicants or recipients and non-SSI applicant or recipient members must be referred by the SSA to the BenefitsCal online applic ation or their nearest Family Resource Center (FRC) to apply for CalFresh benefits. 1. HHs Eligible for Joint Processing To be eligible under joint processing procedures, all HH members must be SSI/SSP applicants or recipients and must:  Not currently receive CalFresh benefits; or  Be receiving CalFresh and have received a rece rtification notice in the last 30 days; or  Have applied for CalFresh in t he last 60 days but were denied; and  Have agreed to apply through the SSA. 2. Application Submission from SSA When the SSA determines the SSI/SSP HH is eligible under joint processing and the HH agrees to the SSA application assistance, the SSA must assist the HH in completing and submitting a CalFresh initial application or application fo r recertification. The SSA must s ubmit the application electronically through BenefitsCal. When an application is rece ived from the SSA through BenefitsCal, do not request an additional signature from the HH, the signature of the SSA technician assisting the HH is sufficient. The default method for the SSA to a ssist HHs with submitting a CalF resh initial application or application for recertification is BenefitsCal; however, the HH may request to submit a paper application. The SSA must assist the HH in completing and submi tting a paper application to the county’s Document Processing Center (DPC) wit hin one business day of receipt of the signed application along with the SSA Transmittal for Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program Applications (SSA 4233) cover sheet. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Social Security Administration (SSA) Joint Processing of CalFresh Application Number Pa ge 63-333 2 of 3 3. Date of Application For applications received electronically, the applicatio n file date will be the date it is received via the interface at the DPC. For applications submitted on paper at the SSA office, the application file date will be the date the office receives the signed paper application. SSA will indicate the date of receipt on the application. 4. Expedited Services (ES) The ES processing time standard will begin on the da te the signed application is received by the county. The SSA technician will scr een the application for ES elig ibility on the day the signed application is received by SSA. For paper applications , if the customer appears potentially eligible to ES, the SSA technician will note “Expedited Proces sing” on the first page of the application. The county will screen all applications for ES, whether or not the SSA technici an has identified the application as potentially eligible to ES. 5. title: 63-351 General Responsibilities
content: 63-351 General Responsibilities Table of Contents Section General 351.1 Explaining the Program 351.2 Non-Discrimination 351.3 Rights and Responsibilities of Applicant/Recipients 351.4 Replacement 351.5 Benefit Issuance 351.6 Claim Determinations 351.7 x 63-351.1 General The worker assigned to a case action is responsible for the eligibility determination in the CalFresh Program. 63-351.2 Explaining the Program The worker will explain the program requirements in simple, understandable terms to encourage eligible low-income households to utilize the program. 63-351.3 Non- Discriminatio n Non-discrimination information can now be found in the Civil Rights Bases of Discrimination section of the Eligibility Desk Guide (EDG). Click here to access the EDG. 63-351.4 Rights and Responsibiliti es of Applicant/ Recipient The worker must advise households of their rights and responsibilities during the application and recertification interview, including the appropriate application processing standard and the households' responsibility to report changes. CalFresh applicants will not be required to attend the Family Resource Center (FRC) group orientation as explained in Section 63-115.2. 63-351.5 Replacement The worker will ensure that lost, stolen or underpaid Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) authorizations and benefits are replaced in the current month to avoid forced non-participation. 63-351.6 Benefits Issuance Under the EBT system, CalFresh benefit availability is staggered over the first ten (10) days of the month for ongoing cases. Benefits are always discontinued the last day of the month. 63-351.7 Claim Determination s The worker will process all claim determinations per procedures in Section 63-450.

title: 63-352 Case Assignment
content: 63-352 Case Assignment Table of Contents Section General 352.1 Case Handling 352.2 Referrals and Transfers between Cash Assistance and CalFresh 352.3 Referrals for Cash Assistance 352.4 CalWORKs/CalFresh to Transitional CalFresh Conversions 352.5 x 63-352.1 General The worker assigned to the case action/task is responsible for determining eligibility and certification, answering applicant/recipient questions and resolving problems. 63-352.2 Case Handling CalFresh case handling procedures will be followed according to the Family Resource Center’s (FRC) internal procedures or Task Based procedures as indicated in the Caseload Management section of the Eligibility and Employment Operations Guide and the No Wrong Door Guidelines as explained in the Eligibility Desk Guide (EDG). 63-352.3 Referrals and Transfers between Cash Assistance and CalFresh The purpose of this section is to ensure that applicants and recipients are served as efficiently as possible and that delays in determinations of eligibility and granting CalFresh are kept to a minimum. Specific procedures will be observed in all cases: •Worker will ensure that CalFresh is not issued twice in the same month to any household. All applicants will be cleared prior to granting. •The worker who can meet the CalFresh needs of the applicant/recipient most promptly and efficiently will take all actions necessary to do so. •Disagreements within a FRC as to which worker will handle a given situation will be resolved through the FRC’s discretion and policy. •Routine referrals will be handles as outlined in 63-352.4 below and the No Wrong Door Guidelines as indicated in the Eligibility Desk Guide (EDG). •The appropriate FRC management will resolve problem cases and/or boundary disputes. •Staff will not refer applicant/recipients to another FRC’s except as explained in the “Referral to Other Offices” section of the No Wrong Door Guidelines in the EDG. 63-352.4 Referrals for Cash Assistance REFERRALS TO CALWORKS When a Non-Assistance CalFresh household requests CalWORKs, staff will process the request as follows: •If the applicant calls ACCESS, the ACCESS worker will refer the applicant to the proper FRC. The ACCESS worker will mail the CalWORKs application packet upon request. •If the applicant requests CalWORKs at an FRC, staff will process the application even if the applicant resides in another FRC’s zip code. Refer to the No Wrong Door Guidelines in the EDG for more information. REFERRALS TO GENERAL RELIEF When a Non-Assistance CalFresh household requests General Relief (GR), staff will process the request as follows: •If the applicant calls ACCESS, the ACCESS worker will refer the applicant to the proper FRC. •If the applicant requests GR at an FRC which does not process GR, staff will refer them to the proper FRC according to zip code. Refer to the No Wrong Door Guideline Exceptions in the EDG for more information. 63-352.5 CalWORKs/ CalFresh to Transitional CalFresh Conversions When eligibility to CalWORKs ends and the household was receiving CalFresh through that case, the CalWORKs worker must process a Transitional CalFresh case within 10 calendar days following the CalWORKs discontinuance. Refer to 63-321 for more information.

title: 63-353 Confidentiality
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageConfidentiality 63-353 1 of 2 Revision: 03/01/2021 Background: Confidentiality regulations outline under what circumstances and to whom information may be released. These regulations pertain to all case records, electronic files, papers, and communications administered, or supervised by HHSA, including CalFresh, CalFresh Employment and Training (CFET) and the Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWD) Work Programs. These regulations were created to protect customers from identification or exploitation. Additional information regarding HHSA policies for Confidentiality in Self-Sufficiency Programs may be found in the Eligibility Policy and Procedure Guide. Purpose: The purpose of this policy is to protect the agency’s records while providing authorized persons access to information. This revision updates the section to the new format. There are no changes due to State legislation. Policy: Names, addresses and all other eligibility information concerning the circumstances of any customer, including whether that person is or is not an applicant/recipient will not be disclosed for any purposes not directly related to the administration of public social services programs. 1. Collateral Contacts Before a collateral contact is initiated, the customer must be informed of their option to get the required information themselves without using County forms. Except for Bureau of Public Assistance Investigations (BPAI) staff, the customer’s signed consent must be obtained and made part of the case record prior to initiating collateral contacts. 2. Unauthorized Disclosure of Confidential Information Unauthorized disclosure of confidential information by a County employee is a misdemeanor and may lead to criminal or civil liability for both the employee and the County. 3. Case Records Case records are the original and permanent records of HHSA and are maintained for reference and audit purposes to document eligibility. All information in case records is considered confidential and will be safeguarded. References: MPP 19-000 and 63-201.3 Welfare and Institutions (WI) Code 10850 EPPG Confidentiality Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 02/29/2024. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageConfidentiality 63-353 2 of 2 Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-354 Release of Information
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageRelease of Information 63-354 1 of 3 Revision: 03/01/2021 Background: Use or disclosure of information obtained from CalFresh applicant or recipient households is restricted to persons directly connected with the administration or enforcement of the provisions of the Food and Nutrition Act or similar means-tested public programs. Purpose: This section includes policies for sharing information and obtaining release of information from customers. Policy: Confidential information may only be released, without the consent of the customer, for purposes directly connected with the administration of public social services programs. The Human Services Specialist (HSS) will record in the case comments all requests for information and the disposition of the request. 1. Authorized Disclosure List In addition to HHSA staff of this County and other counties or states, the following agencies and/or persons are authorized to receive or exchange confidential information. This list is not intended to be complete or result in the automatic disclosure of information to persons or agencies on the list. The list will provide a quick reference of persons and agencies most frequently making authorized inquiries. •Auditor and Controller (County, State and Federal) •County Counsel (except for investigations of workers’ compensation claims or other questionable situations) •Department of Social Services (County, State, Federal) •Department of Health Services (County, State, Federal) •United Behavioral Health (UBH) •District Attorney (Bureau of Public Assistance Investigations (BPAI), Bureau of Child Support Enforcement, Welfare Employee Fraud Prosecutions, Child Support Prosecutions only) •Employment Development Department (EDD) •Mental Health Services (County or County Contractor) •Social Security Administration (SSA) •Voluntary Refugee Agencies (VOLAGS and Central Intake Unit) •Juvenile Probation Department (for billings on AFDC Foster Care cases) •Grand Jury •Revenue and Recovery •Housing Authorities (County, State, or Federal Government) •Contracted Employment Services Note: If in doubt as to the appropriateness of releasing any program specific information, contact HHSA Self-Sufficiency Services, CalFresh Program. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageRelease of Information 63-354 2 of 3 2. Public Administrator In San Diego County, the Public Administrator is the Indigent Burial Officer and operates the Indigent Burial Program as an agent of HHSA. CalFresh records are not to be released to the Public Administrator without the consent of the customer. Note: If all members of the household are deceased, CalFresh records cannot be released. 3. Research Organizations/Graduate Students Before access to case records can be granted, research organizations or graduate students conducting research for a thesis or term paper must submit information regarding the project to HHSA Self-Sufficiency Services, CalFresh Program to resolve confidentiality issues and provide policy and procedures regarding the release of information. 4. Customer Consent Required Information contained in applications or other documents made and/or kept by HHSA may be released to the customer or their authorized representative subject to the following conditions: •The customer has authorized the release of the information, and •The information was provided solely by the customer, or the customer authorized HHSA to obtain the information (bank verifications, income verifications, etc.) 5. Written Authorization Written authorization to release confidential information must be signed and dated by the customer and must be received by the HSS prior to release of the information. The authorization does not have to specify the exact information to be released. A general release is sufficient. However, the HSS will comply with limits on information to be shared if the authorization identifies only specific items. •The authorization may be faxed, emailed or uploaded electronically to the HSS. If submitted electronically, a follow-up hard copy is not required. •The authorization expires one year from the date signed unless the document expressly limits it to a shorter period. •The customer may revoke the authorization at any time. •To use the authorization, the representative must first be positively identified and documented in case comments. 6. Telephone Authorization Telephone authorization may be accepted when the customer has positively identified themselves to the County. A telephone authorization is temporary and acceptable for one-time contacts. If the customer wishes to authorize release for a longer period, a written authorization is required. References: MPP 19-000, 63-201 and 63-300 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or before 02/29/24. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageRelease of Information 63-354 3 of 3 Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-355 Request for Information
content: 63-355 Request for Information 63-355.1 Questionable Requests/Clo sed Cases When a request for information does not appear to be reasonably related to the responsibilities of the requesting office, a written statement concerning the request and circumstances must be forwarded to the Family Resource Center (FRC) Manager for review and approval/disapproval of the request. Inquiries from agencies and persons listed on the Authorized Disclosure List (see Section 63-354.2) on cases that have been closed and forwarded to the Record Library are to be referred to the Public Assistance Information Unit (PAI). 63-355.2 Requests from Board of Supervisors/ Other Political Entities Most inquiries from the Board of Supervisors or other political entities are referred to Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Eligibility Operations, however some inquiries may be referred to the Family Resource Center (FRC) Manager or Assistant Manager for resolution. These inquiries may include: •General requests for information on program or office procedures; or •Requests based on complaints by an applicant/recipient pertaining to the handling of his/her case; or •Requests based on any anonymous complaints pertaining to case handling or to a particular applicant/recipient. The manager will respond to the inquiry or attempt to resolve the issue without releasing information concerning a specific applicant/recipient. Usually these inquiries can be handled by the manager by providing general program information or procedures. If the request for information is about a specific applicant/recipient or the results of following up action with a specific applicant/recipient, a verbal or written consent must be provided by the applicant/recipient prior to the release of information. The only case information that may be released is information provided by or authorized by the applicant/recipient. If the issue or result cannot be resolved, the FRC Manager or Assistant Manager will contact the Eligibility Operations CalFresh Manager for additional clarification and direction needed to respond to the inquiry. 63-355.3 Absent Parents/ Client Family or Friends Release of information to absent parents, the applicant/recipient’s family or friends requires the written consent of the applicant/recipient. In handling such requests, the following procedures must be followed: •The worker will not acknowledge to the requesting person that the applicant/recipient or the applicant/recipient’s child(ren) have applied for or are receiving assistance or services. •The worker will advise the requesting person that he/she must submit a written request for any information including his/her address and phone number. •When the worker receives the written request, he/she will notify the client of the request for information. The applicant/recipient may then provide the information to the requesting party. •If the applicant/recipient does not wish to provide the information directly but will provide written authorization to release the requested information, the worker will provide the information to the requesting person. The written authorization must be received before any information is released and the requesting party must provide proof of identity before the worker provides the information. •Should the applicant/recipient refuse consent, the information will not be released. The requesting parties may then, as appropriate, contact the District Attorney or a private attorney and use legal recourse. •If an absent parent alleges that the aided parent has kidnapped, abused or neglected the child(ren), the case must be referred to Child Protective Services (CPS). The worker must report the allegation to the Child Abuse Hotline at 1-858-560- 2191. The worker should also provide the absent parent with the hotline number. 63-355.4 Defense Attorneys and Businesses The worker will refer requests from defense attorneys, including Legal Aid and the Public Defender, that do not include an applicant/recipient release, to the HHSA Subpoena Liaison, who is the PAI Supervisor, for an explanation or how to subpoena records. Release of information to businesses is only authorized when HHSA has a written and dated authorization from the applicant/recipient. Valid business inquiries, may include grant and address information to establish an applicant/recipient’s credit, but do not include inquiries to pursue collection on a delinquent account. 63-355.5 Law Enforcement Officials Representatives of official law enforcement agencies can receive confidential case information in specific instances. In releasing information to law enforcement the following procedures must be observed: •All requests must be made in writing by the head of the agency or his/her designee and must specify that an arrest warrant has been issued for an applicant/recipient for the commission of a felony or misdemeanor. The request must be for an individual, unless warrants have been issued for several persons in the same case. A faxed request is acceptable. •The disposition of each request must be documented on the written request. Documentation will include the case name, case number, name of manager, type of response and the name of the person to whom the information was released. The original request is to be maintained in a central control file by the FRC Manager. If information is released, a copy of the request is to be filed under the MISC tab in the case folder. •Requests for information from local law enforcement agencies (i.e. Sheriff’s Department, a city Police Department, Probation Department, etc.) are to the referred to the FRC Manager where the case is currently or last active. Only the FRC Manager or their designee may release information. •Requests for information from Federal or State law enforcement agencies (i.e. Federal Bureau of Investigations (FBI), Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), State and Federal Parole Officers, Military Police, etc.) and any requests from other law enforcement related sources (including bounty hunters and court orders) are to be referred to the Eligibility Operations Chief of HHSA for disposition. 63-355.6 Specific Circumstance s The specific circumstances in which information may be released are detailed below: A. CRIMINAL ACTS IMPACTING DEPARTMENT/EMPLOYEE Confidential information about an applicant/recipient may be released to a law enforcement agency investigating or gathering information regarding a violation of federal, state or local law committed: •In a FRC office or other agency office; •Against any agency or agency contracted employee when the employee was involved in the administration of public social services; or •Against any off-duty agency or agency contracted employee in retaliation for an act performed by the employee as a job duty. Information to be released is limited to the applicant/recipients name, physical description and address. Only site management or Eligibility Operations may release this information. (W & I Code, Section 10850) B. OTHER CRIMINAL ACTIVITY If an HHSA employee or contracted employee observes a client engaged in a crime in progress that is unrelated to the performance of the employee’s duties, the employee may report the crime, but not release confidential information (client name, address, etc.). If further information is requested by law enforcement, contact the Eligibility Operations CalFresh Manager who will handle the request on a caseby-case basis in consultation with County Counsel. C. DECEASED APPLICANTS/RECIPIENTS Disclosure of information on a deceased applicant/recipient from a CalFresh only case record is strictly prohibited. D. FELONY AND/OR MISDEMEANOR ARREST WARRANTS Confidential information from case records will not be protected from disclosure to a law enforcement agency should a felony and/or misdemeanor arrest warrant be issued in the client’s name. 63-355.7 Private Organizations / Persons Private organizations and individuals not on the authorized disclosure list who request case information, including whether or not a person is receiving or has received aid, must be informed about the regulations regarding confidentiality of case records. No case information is to be released without the written authorization of the client. If the inquiry is not case specific, often general statistics or specific program information can resolve the inquiry. Inquiries about general statistical information are to be referred directly to the FRC Manager. All media inquiries are to be referred directly to the site manager who, when necessary, will refer the media to the HHSA Media Coordinator. 63-355.8 Other Requests Confidentiality questions or requests for release of information not specifically addressed in this chapter should be referred to FRC management for review. Unauthorized disclosure of confidential information may render the County and/or staff liable for criminal and civil suits.
