title: 63-356 Applicant Recipient Request for Information
content: 63-356 Applicant/Recipient Request for Information 63-356.1 Applicant/ Recipient Request for Information/ Photocopies Information relating to eligibility that has been provided solely by the applicant/recipient or authorized by the applicant/recipient and is contained in applications or other documents completed by the applicant/recipient and kept by HHSA may be released to the applicant/recipient or his/her authorized representative. Examples include: •Bank verification requests. •Employment verification requests. •Medical verification requests, etc. Staff may photocopy specific items in the case record for the applicant/recipient and/or his/her authorized representative. Note: Photocopies, in response to general requests (the whole case file, all SAR 7’s, etc.) will not be provided. Also, photocopies of case narratives will not be provided. 63-356.2 Information Provided by a Third Party Information provided confidentially to the Agency by a third party and not provided solely by the applicant/recipient will not be disclosed to the applicant/recipient or his/her authorized representative. Examples include: •PAFD reports; •Informant identity; and •Other privileged communication. 63-356.3 IEVS Information Case information obtained through the Income Eligibility Verification System (IEVS) requires special handling to protect the confidentiality of IEVS information that may have been mismatched to the applicant/recipient or other household members. Workers are to use the following guidelines concerning the sharing of IEVS information with the applicant/recipient or his/her authorized representative: •If the IEVS report verifies information previously reported by the applicant/recipient, the report will be treated as verification authorized by the applicant/recipient and may be released to the applicant/recipient. •If the IEVS report does not appear to pertain to the applicant/recipient, or if it contains previously unreported information, it will be treated as information provided confidentially by a third party and the report may not be released until the discrepancy has been clarified and the accuracy confirmed. •Sufficient information from the IEVS report may be provided to the applicant/recipient to allow them to obtain additional verification and/or clarification. Example: EDD reports a match of the SSN to a UIB recipient. The name does not match and the recipient claims no UIB income. The EDD Field Office number from the report may be provided to the recipient to aid EDD in clarifying the discrepancy. The name of the UIB recipient may not be released.

title: 63-357 Inspection of Case Records
content: 63-357 Inspection of Case Records Table of Contents Section Family Resource Center (FRC) Procedures 357.1 Privileged Communication/ Information which Cannot be Released to the Client 357.2 x 63-357.1 Family Resource Center (FRC) Procedures Authorized persons requesting review, as well as those authorized to actually complete the inspection will be subject to the Family Resource Center (FRC) review procedures listed below. This includes those persons requesting review in preparation for a State Hearing. If a more extensive review is requested, the applicant/recipient should be referred to the Appeals section to schedule an appointment. FRC review procedures are as follows: Review Procedure Requirement 1. The complete case record, except for privileged communications as noted in 63-357.2 below and information not provided solely by or authorized by the client or his/her authorized representative, will be made available for inspection. The privileged communication and information not provided solely by or authorized by the applicant/recipient or his/her authorized representative, will be removed from the case record before any review by the applicant/recipient or his/her authorized representative. Note: The case narratives must be provided for review; however, privileged communication/information must first be removed from the case record prior to the inspection. (See 63-357.2 below for a summary of privileged communication/information.) 2. Case inspection is permitted only during normal work hours. 3. FRC’s will make a private room available for case record review where reviewers may discuss the case contents. No case will be made available unless the worker or a suitable substitute is present in the room during the entire period of examination. 4. The reviewers will not be permitted to remove, alter, photocopy or photograph anything in the case record. The reviewers are permitted to make notes. On request, eligibility staff may photocopy specific items in the case record for the reviewer. Photocopies in response to general requests (the whole case file, all SAR 7’s etc.) should not be provided. Program Guides or other regulations may be made available, on request, during the case review. Entire chapters are not to be copied but photocopies of applicable regulations may be made. 5. The worker will record in the case comments all requests for inspection of case records. Note: Requests to review a closed case in Record Library should be directed to the Public Assistance Information (PAI) Unit. 63-357.2 Privileged Communicati on/ Information which cannot be Released to the Client There are communications/information contained in case records which are not subject to review by the applicant/recipient or his/her representative. Additionally, there are communications that are not subject to review by the applicant/recipient’s authorized representative without specific consent of the applicant/recipient as referenced in Sections 63-353 and 63-354. Some of the privileged communications are briefly summarized below: PHYSICIAN – MEDICAL PERSONNEL/PATIENT Confidential information from a physician cannot be disclosed to the authorized representative without specific written consent of the client/patient. Some physicians may request a report not be released to the patient. In such cases, the physician’s consent to release the report must be obtained. PAFD REPORTS All reports, summaries and other confidential communications and information obtained by PAFD in the process of investigating an alleged fraud will be removed from the case record prior to its inspection by an applicant/recipient or an authorized representative. IDENTITY OF INFORMER Staff may not disclose the identity of an informer to the applicant/recipient or his/her authorized representative. CHILD ABUSE HOTLINE REPORTS All reports and other confidential communications/information obtained as a result of a Child Abuse Hotline complaint will be removed from the case record prior to its inspection by an applicant/recipient or an authorized representative. LAWYER/APPLICANT/RECIPIENT Matters of confidential communication between a lawyer and client cannot be disclosed to an authorized representative without specific written consent of the applicant/recipient. SPOUSES Confidential communication between spouses during their marital relationship cannot be disclosed unless both agree to its disclosure, even after the marriage has terminated.

title: 63-358 Court Appearances and Subpoenas
content: 63-358 Court Appearances and Subpoenas 63-358.1 General A subpoena is a court order to compel a person to appear at a deposition or court proceeding to testify as a witness. A subpoena duces tecum is a court order normally used to compel a person to produce all documents or records named in the subpoena. The testimony of Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) employees involving case records for matters not directly related to the administration of public social service programs is an inappropriate use of case records and a violation of confidentiality. To avoid violating confidentiality and/or court orders the procedures in 63-357.2 and .3 below will apply. These procedures apply only to subpoenas involving HHSA records and applicants/recipients. 63-358.2 District Attorney/ County Counsel Subpoena Staff is routinely served with subpoenas issued by the District Attorney’s (DA) office. It is HHSA policy to fully cooperate with the DA in the investigation or prosecution of all matters directly related to the administration of public social services. Procedures for staff served with a subpoena issued by the DA are outlined below: •A demand for witness fees and mileage should not be made. •The employee will notify his/her supervisor or the appropriate Family Resource Center (FRC) manager immediately when served with a subpoena. •The employee named on the subpoena is expected to appear as directed. oWhen the employee is no longer assigned to HHSA, the supervisor or FRC manager will immediately contact the Deputy DA identified on the subpoena to provide the identity of the employee who will respond as a substitute. oIf there has been a change in the worker assigned to the case, the Deputy DA must be informed so that he/she may make the decision on who will be required to appear. •The employee must contact the Deputy DA to discuss the case and restrictions to availability for court (planned vacation or medical leave). •If unsure whether the subpoena relates to a matter directly connected to HHSA programs, the employee’s supervisor or FRC Management must contact the Subpoena Liaison who is the Public Assistance Information (PAI) Supervisor. •If the subpoena relates to a matter not directly related to the administration of public social service programs, the employee will follow the procedures outlined in 63-356.4 below. 63-358.3 Private Attorney Subpoena/ Subpoenas Duces Tecum General Staff is occasionally served with subpoenas or subpoenas duces tecum that are initiated by: •Private attorneys; •Legal Aid Society; or •The Public Defender. These subpoenas normally request the presence of staff and/or case records and may deal with civil or criminal matters not directly related to the official administration of public social service programs, such as: •Divorce; •Child support; •Child custody; or •Property settlement matters. By State Law (W & I Code 10850), the testimony of staff and/or use of case records for matters not related to the administration of public social service programs is considered inappropriate use of public social service records and is a violation of confidentiality. Subpoena Addressed to the “Custodian of Record” Frequently these subpoenas will be for the case record, rather than a specific person and will be addressed to the “Custodian of Record”. HHSA staff must not accept service of subpoenas addressed to the “Custodian of Record”. The server of the subpoena duces tecum must be informed that the Custodian of Record for HHSA is the Eligibility Operations Chief and that service of the subpoena may be arranged by the server by contacting the PAI Supervisor. 63-358.4 Private Attorney Subpoena Procedures All HHSA staff served with a subpoena or subpoena duces tecum from a private attorney that is addressed to the staff person (not the “Custodian of Record”) must accept the subpoena and adhere to the following procedures: Procedures 1 The employee must demand witness fees and mileage at the time the subpoena is served. HHSA employees must also demand that HHSA receive the fees and mileage prior to the court appearance. Witness fees and mileage reimbursement amounts are established by State Law. The person delivering the subpoena may write a check and present it at the time the subpoena is served (payee on the check should be the “Health and Human Services Agency”). The employee must send the check with the subpoena to the Subpoena Liaison Eligibility Operations, Mail Stop W414. For subpoena duces tecum, send to the PAI Supervisor at Mail Stop W409. 2 Immediately following the serving of the subpoena, the employee’s immediate supervisor will call the Subpoena Liaison, who will determine if the pending legal proceedings are related to the administration of a public social service program. 3 Upon notification, the Subpoena Liaison will request that the subpoena and check for witness fees, if applicable, be delivered to him/her as soon as administratively possible. 4 Upon receipt of the subpoena, the Subpoena Liaison will contact the serving attorney and explain the legal provisions of confidentiality (W& I Code 10850) and request the subpoena be withdrawn. 63-358.5 Attorney Agrees/ Refuses to Withdraw Subpoena Attorney Agrees to Withdraw Subpoena The Subpoena Liaison will notify the employee’s supervisor that the employee is excused from compliance with the subpoena. Attorney Refuses to Withdraw Subpoena The Subpoena Liaison will return the subpoena to the employee and provide him/her with a copy of the “Points and Authorities in Opposition to Subpoena Duces Tecum”. The “Points and Authorities” is a statement prepared by the County Counsel’s Office, and serves as a formal request to the court to excuse the witness and/or records on the grounds that the records are confidential. The employee must appear in court at the designated time. The employee must not testify or allow anyone to see the record until the “Points of Authorities” has been presented to the judge and the judge has made a determination. The “Points and Authorities” should be given to the judge at the time the employee is called to the stand to testify. If the judge rules against the “Points of Authorities”, the employee must: •Comply with the decision; •Submit the case record; and •Give testimony. If parts of the case record are introduced as evidence, the employee will seek court approval, on the record, of substitution of photocopies so that the case record and its documents can remain intact when the employee is excused.

title: 63-359 Inter-County Transfer
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page CalFresh Inter-County Transfers 63-359 1 of 3 Revision Date: 11/01/2023 Background: The Inter-County Transfer (ICT) is designed to help customers receive uninterrupted benefits when they move within the state of California. Purpose: This section has been revised due to sunset review. There are no changes in legislation. Policy: The ICT transfers the responsibility of the case management of self-sufficiency services to a different county. Staff must initiate an ICT when a household (HH) reports a move from one county to another, this includes HHs experiencing homelessness. A HH may voluntarily report their move to either the receiving (county to which the HH has moved to) or sending (county from which the HH has moved from) county. The county the customer notifies of their move will initiate the ICT within seven business days. Counties must communicate with each other throughout the ICT process to ensure that the HH’s benefits are not interrupted. An ICT will not require the HH to complete a new application, recertification, submit verifications previously provided, or complete an interview. The transfer period of benefits must be completed within 30 days after a county is notified of a HH’s move. Note: When the 30th day lands on a weekend or holiday, the next business day is considered the last day of the 30 th day transfer period. A transfer of responsibility may occur at an earlier date if there is mutual agreement between the counties involved. The example below shows when a transfer may occur at an earlier date. Example: ICT is initiated April 20th, the receiving county would be required to assume responsibility May 21st. However, the receiving county notifies the sending county of proposed benefit approval on May 18th. The sending county will discontinue benefits in a timely manner and receiving county will approve benefits effective June 1st. 1. Sending County Responsibilities The following are the sending county’s responsibilities: •Notify the customer of the transfer using the CalFresh Informing Notice of Sending Inter-County Transfer (NA 1268). •Provide the receiving county, the following items: Copies of all verifications that were in the HH’s file. Any information which might affect eligibility. CalFresh Notification of Intercounty Transfer (CF 215). Public Assistance CalFresh (PACF) cases must include CalWORKs Notification of Intercounty Transfer (CW215). Note: The name and phone number of the ICT specialist must be included in the comment section. Application for Cash Aid, CalFresh and/or Medical Assistance (SAWS 2 Plus), Application for CalFresh Benefits (CF 285), and Initial Application for CalFresh, and/or Medi-Cal/Healthcare Programs (SAWS 1). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page CalFresh Inter-County Transfers 63-359 2 of 3 Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7). CalFresh Household Change Report (CF 377.5) if applicable. •Any outstanding over-issuance (OI) repayment records (with supporting documentation such as OI Notice of Action [NOA’s], budgets, etc.) that will not be repaid before the end of the transfer period. Once all documents have been sent and notification is obtained that the receiving county is responsible, the sending county will no longer be responsible for the collection of the claim and will remove the claim from their case record. Refer to CalFresh ICT Receiving and Sending County Job Aid and CalFresh ICT Processing Guide 359-01 for additional information and procedures. •Transferring the benefit responsibility to the receiving county no later than the first day of the next available benefit month. 2. Receiving County Responsibilities The following are the receiving county’s responsibilities: •Process the SAR 7 or recertification when the customer moves during the last two months of the Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) period. The SAR cycle and recertification that were assigned in the sending county must continue in the receiving county. The customer may be sent the NOA of the approval of benefits in the receiving county along with the Notice of the Expiration of Certification period or separate notices may be sent. The table below illustrates when a customer’s case will be picked up by the receiving county when their recertification is due in September. If the… then the receiving county… ICT is initiated in the month of August, completes the recertification in September with an ICT pickup date of October 1st. recertification is completed by the sending county prior to initiating the ICT in September, picks up the ICT on November 1st. ICT is initiated in the month of September, completes the recertification in September with an ICT pickup date of October 1st, rather than November 1st due to the recertification ending September in the sending county. Note: The sending county may process the SAR 7 or recertification if the sending and receiving counties agree that it is in the customer’s best interest for them to do so. •Notify the customer of the transfer using the CalFresh Informing Notice of Receiving Inter-County Transfer (NA 1267). •Process eligible Transitional CalFresh (TCF) cases. The receiving county will be responsible for processing the recertification and determining eligibility for regular CalFresh. The customer will continue to receive TCF benefits from the original county until recertification is completed in the receiving county. •When the HH consists of an Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWD) individual, the county of residence is responsible to check if the participant is meeting the ABAWD work rule (Refer to 63-904). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page CalFresh Inter-County Transfers 63-359 3 of 3 3. HH’s Excluded from the ICT Process Do not initiate an ICT when only some members of the HH move to another county. Those individuals will be added or removed from the current HH according to existing SAR rules. Individuals leaving the current HH must be removed from the case and may apply in their new county of residence or be added to an existing CalFresh HH. 4. Restoration of Aid HH’s may be eligible for restoration if the HH applies in a new county in the month following their discontinuance. The discontinuance can be for any reason other than failure to complete a recertification or disqualification from receiving benefits. Staff shall communicate with the previous county to determine which is more beneficial to the HH, having the benefits restored or completing a new application (in the event the HH is eligible for expedited services). The sending county is responsible for restoring the case and the receiving county must provide any information needed to complete the restoration. If it is determined that the HH is better served by completing a new application, the receiving county will notify the HH and assist in the completion of the application. 5. Domestic Abuse Strict confidentiality must be maintained for domestic abuse victims during ICT process. All communication of domestic abuse issues, including documentation must be kept confidential so that the customer’s information is not available to any staff who will not be directly involved in the case. The use of fax for domestic abuse cases is discouraged. The sending county is strongly encouraged to provide the customer with references to local domestic abuse services that are in the receiving county. Domestic abuse ICT cases must be assigned to staff who have received the required domestic abuse training to address the customer’s specific need to ensure a smooth case transfer. Victims of domestic abuse and their families can use the “Safe at Home” service for confidential mail services. Program Impacts: Refer to the CalWORKs ICT process for Public Assistance CalFresh cases when at least one member of the CalFresh HH receives CalWORKs (CalWORKs Program Guide 40-100). The HH will be discontinued from the prior county at the same time the transfer of the CalWORKs case is completed. Refer to the Medi-Cal ICT process for CalFresh cases when at least one member of the CalFresh HH receives Medi-Cal (Medi-Cal Program Guide Article 3, Section 2 Inter-County Transfer). sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page CalFresh Inter-County Transfers 63-359 1 of 3 Revision Date: 11/01/2023 Background: The Inter-County Transfer (ICT) is designed to help customers receive uninterrupted benefits when they move within the state of California. Purpose: This section has been revised due to sunset review. There are no changes in legislation. Policy: The ICT transfers the responsibility of the case management of self-sufficiency services to a different county. Staff must initiate an ICT when a household (HH) reports a move from one county to another, this includes HHs experiencing homelessness. A HH may voluntarily report their move to either the receiving (county to which the HH has moved to) or sending (county from which the HH has moved from) county. The county the customer notifies of their move will initiate the ICT within seven business days. Counties must communicate with each other throughout the ICT process to ensure that the HH’s benefits are not interrupted. An ICT will not require the HH to complete a new application, recertification, submit verifications previously provided, or complete an interview. The transfer period of benefits must be completed within 30 days after a county is notified of a HH’s move. Note: When the 30th day lands on a weekend or holiday, the next business day is considered the last day of the 30 th day transfer period. A transfer of responsibility may occur at an earlier date if there is mutual agreement between the counties involved. The example below shows when a transfer may occur at an earlier date. Example: ICT is initiated April 20th, the receiving county would be required to assume responsibility May 21st. However, the receiving county notifies the sending county of proposed benefit approval on May 18th. The sending county will discontinue benefits in a timely manner and receiving county will approve benefits effective June 1st. 1. Sending County Responsibilities The following are the sending county’s responsibilities: •Notify the customer of the transfer using the CalFresh Informing Notice of Sending Inter-County Transfer (NA 1268). •Provide the receiving county, the following items: Copies of all verifications that were in the HH’s file. Any information which might affect eligibility. CalFresh Notification of Intercounty Transfer (CF 215). Public Assistance CalFresh (PACF) cases must include CalWORKs Notification of Intercounty Transfer (CW215). Note: The name and phone number of the ICT specialist must be included in the comment section. Application for Cash Aid, CalFresh and/or Medical Assistance (SAWS 2 Plus), Application for CalFresh Benefits (CF 285), and Initial Application for CalFresh, and/or Medi-Cal/Healthcare Programs (SAWS 1). title: 63-360 Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP)
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) Number Page 63-360 1 of 3 Revision Date: 10/01/2025 Background: ESAP is a set of waivers that simplify the CalFresh application and recertification process for Non- Assistance CalFresh (NACF) households in which all members are age 60 or older or disabled. The goal is to increase CalFresh participation among eligible households by simplifying the application and recertification process. Purpose: This section details eligibility criteria and interview requirements for ESAP households. This section is being updated due to sunset review and to include the CalFresh Elderly Simplified Application (CF 485). Policy: A CalFresh household is considered ESAP when all members are aged or disabled (including ineligible or excluded household members) and have no earned income. Upon approval of CalFresh, ESAP households are assigned a 36-month certification period and are not required to complete the Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7). The following waivers apply only to ESAP households:  Recertification interview waiver.  Data matching waiver to reduce customer provided verifications.  Certification extension waiver.  SAR 7 waiver. 1. Application The CF 485 is a single signature CalFresh application designed specifically for use by ESAP households and is available in the Eligibility Forms Library. The CF 485 includes only required questions that are relevant to ESAP households. Note: An ESAP eligible household may apply for CalFresh using any of the acceptable applications, refer to CalFresh Program Guide (CFPG) 63-103. 2. Interview Requirements An interview is required at initial application. If the household is determined to meet ESAP criteria, document in the case record, and inform the household that a recertification interview is not required. Recertification interviews are waived for ESAP households, unless one of the following applies:  ESAP household requests an interview.  Information provided on the application for recertification will result in a denial.  Information supplied by the household is questionable, incomplete, or contradictory. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) Number Page 63-360 2 of 3 Note: A copy of the Statement of Facts containing all information used to determine eligibility along with the Statement of Facts Notification (09-105 HHSA) form must be sent to the household when processing an ESAP recertification, even if an interview was not required. 3. Verifications Electronic resources, such as Income Eligibility Verification System (IEVS), Payment Verification System (PVS), and Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS) must be used to the greatest extent possible, refer to CFPG 63-117. 4. Reporting Requirements For ESAP households, a Changes for Cash Aid and CalFresh (SAR 2) form will be sent to the household in the 12th and 24th months of their 36-month certification period. These households are not required to submit a SAR 7. If an ESAP household submits a SAR 7, it will be treated as a voluntary mid-period report. 5. Losing ESAP Eligibility Households that are no longer eligible for ESAP will remain in their current 36-month certification period until it ends. At recertification, an interview will be required. If the household is still eligible for CalFresh, they will be placed in a 12-month or 24-month certification period, depending on their circumstances. Note: When the household loses ESAP eligibility, Semi-Annual Reporting requirements will resume, refer to CFPG 63-272. 6. ESAP Notices Each household will be mailed a Notice of Expiration of Certification (NEC) in the month prior to the last month of the certification period. The following notices will be sent based on the ESAP case circumstances: Notice Description CF 377.2B – CalFresh Notice of Expiration of Certification for Households with Only Elderly and/or Disabled Members. ESAP households that are not required to complete a recertification interview. CF 377.2C – CalFresh Notice of Expiration of Certification for Households with Only Elderly and/or Disabled Members. Former ESAP households that are required to complete an interview. CF 377.2D – CalFresh Notice of Status Change for Households with Only Elderly and/or Disabled Members. The customer reports a change that would result in the household no longer meeting ESAP eligibility. Other Program Impacts: No impacts. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) Number Page 63-360 3 of 3 References: All County Letter (ACL) 13-58, 17-34, 17-53, 20-126, 20-145, 22-15, 23-85. Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 273.2(e)-(f), 273.10(f)(1)-(f)(4), 273.14(b)(3). Food and Nutrition Service (FNS) 2008 Sections 3(f), 11(e)(3), 17(b). Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 63-300.4, 63-300.5, 63-404.6, 63-504.14.142. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 09/30/2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-370 Minimum Nutrition Benefit (MNB) Pilot Program Guide
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Minimum Nutrition Benefit (MNB) Pilot Program Number Page 63-370 1 of 4 Effective Date: 01/01/2026 Background: The MNB program is a state-funded supplemental food benefit program for eligible households (HHs) that will operate from December 1, 2025, through November 3 0, 2026, pending availability of state funding. Purpose: This section introduces MNB policy information and Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) benefit issuance type code “MNB.” Policy: The MNB program provides up to 12 months of additional food benefits to certain HHs receiving less than $60 monthly in CalFresh or California Food Assistance Program (CFAP) benefits. Eligible HHs will receive a monthly supplement that will bring the total amount of CalFresh benefits up to $60 during the pilot period. 1. Eligibility Criteria and Benefit Determination Eligible HHs must meet all the following requirements: • Be eligible for a monthly CalFresh benefit of less than $60 with a beginning date of aid on or before December 1, 2025. • Have conferred Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) status on or before December 1, 2025. • Have at least two CalFresh-eligible HH members. HHs that apply for CalFresh or are conferred ESAP status after December 1, 2025, are not eligible to participate in the MNB program. For approved MNB HHs whose monthly CalFresh benefit s are reduced due to recoupment of an overissuance, the MNB benefits will be calculated based on the full CalFresh eligibility amount before the benefit reduction. Example: If… then… the HH is eligible for $46 in CalFresh, but receives only $36 due to benefit recoupment, the HH will receive $14 in MNB benefits. $60 Total food benefit - $46 CalFresh amount prior to recoupment = $14 MNB benefits Notes: HHs receiving Supplemental Nutrition Benefit (SNB) are ineligible to the MNB program. Additionally, HHs that receive a prorated CalFresh benefit for any reason are not eligible to MNB benefits for that month. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Minimum Nutrition Benefit (MNB) Pilot Program Number Page 63-370 2 of 4 2. Discontinuance and Reinstatement HHs that no longer meet MNB eligibility requirements will be discontinued from the program effective the first of the month following timely notice. HHs that regain MNB eligibility through a rescind, restoration, or reapplication, without a break in aid of more than 30 calendar days, will resume receiving MNB program benefits for the remainder of the pilot period. HHs with a break in aid exceeding 30 calendar days will not be eligible for any remaining months of the MNB program. 3. Overissuances and Underissuances Process all corrections to MNB program benefits separately from CalFresh error corrections. If a HH’s CalFresh benefit increases to $60 or more, discontinue the MNB program with timely notice. Do not establish overissuances for any MNB benefits issued in error. MNB benefits cannot be used to repay any CalFresh overissuances. If a HH received more CalFresh benefits than they were eligible for, the correct CalFresh benefit amount must first be determined, and any necessary CalFresh overissuance established. The MNB benefit s must then be recalculated based on the correct ed CalFresh benefit amount. The HH must be issued the difference between the MNB benefits previously received and the amount for which they are now eligible. Example: A HH of two with conferred ESAP status is determined eligible for $40 in CalFresh and $20 in MNB program benefits for December 2025. CalFresh eligibility is later corrected to $65 for December 2025, and the HH is therefore eligible for a $25 CalFresh supplement. MNB benefits are discontinued with timely notice, and no overissuance is established for the MNB benefits received in error. December 2025 Original Benefit Recalculated Benefit Overissuance Supplement CalFresh $40 $65 -- $25 MNB $20 $0 N/A -- Total Monthly Food Benefit $60 $65 Example: A HH of two with conferred ESAP status is determined eligible for $70 in CalFresh for December 2025. The CalFresh benefit amount exceeds $60 and is therefore ineligible for the MNB program. CalFresh eligibility is later corrected to $24 for December 2025 , and a CalFresh overissuance of $46 is established. Since all MNB program eligibility factors are now met, issue a $36 MNB supplement. December 2025 Original Benefit Recalculated Benefit Overissuance Supplement CalFresh $70 $24 $46 -- MNB $0 $36 -- $36 Total Monthly Food Benefit $70 $60 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Minimum Nutrition Benefit (MNB) Pilot Program Number Page 63-370 3 of 4 Note: No MNB benefits may be issued after June 30, 2027, under any circumstances. 4. Additional Considerations • MNB program benefits will not be replaced due to disaster, HH misfortune, or electronic theft. • HHs requesting a state hearing may still be eligible for Aid Paid Pending (APP) for regular CalFresh benefits, however there is no eligibility for APP relating to MNB benefits. • Errors specific to MNB will not count toward Quality Control (QC) error rates. 5. MNB Benefit Issuance Type Code and Use of Benefits MNB program benefits are issued onto the HHs existing EBT card under the MNB benefit issuance type code. Once issued, MNB program benefits are used in the same manner as regular CalFresh benefits, including at Restaurant Meals Program (RMP) providers, if the HH is otherwise eligible. MNB program benefits are subject to the same EBT expungement rules as regular CalFresh benefits. 6. Forms and Notices The following NOAs were developed for the MNB program and must be used: Form Definition CF 378A Notice of Approval for the CalFresh Minimum Nutrition Benefit Pilot Program CF 378B Notice of Discontinuance for the CalFresh Minimum Nutrition Benefit Pilot Program The CF 378A must be issued when a HH is approved for the MNB program. A new CF 378A is not required if the MNB program benefits increase or decrease during the pilot period due to changes in the CalFresh benefit amount. The CF 378B must be issued w hen a HH is discontinued from the MNB program, either due to ineligibility or at the end of the pilot period. Timely and adequate notice requirements apply. If… then… CalFresh benefits are discontinued, or increase to $60, or more, issue the 378B informing of the MNB program discontinuance along with a CalFresh benefit change notice. The CF 378A and 378B are available in English and Spanish only. For HHs that require translation services in other languages, issue notices with a Notice of Language Services (GEN 1365). Note: The EBT Replacement Denial (M44-350K) Notice of Action (NOA) has been updated to include a denial reason specific to the MNB program. References: All County Letter (ACL) 20-145, 17-34, 22-15, 22-62, 23-92, 24-62, 25-01, and 25-59. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 11/30/2026. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Minimum Nutrition Benefit (MNB) Pilot Program Number Page 63-370 4 of 4 Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-380 Prepared Meal Programs
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Prepared Meal Programs Number Page 63-380 1 of 2 Revision Date: 10/01/2025 Background: CalFresh households (HHs) that meet specific eligibility criteria may use their CalFresh benefits to purchase prepared meals from providers approved by Food and Nutrition Services (FNS). Purpose: The section has been updated due to sunset review. This section has been renamed to incorporate CalFresh benefit usage at communal dining facilities and authorized homeless meal providers for eligible CalFresh HHs. There are no changes to the policy. Policy: Eligible HHs may use their CalFresh benefits for home-delivered meals, at communal dining facilities, or with other authorized homeless meal providers. Home-Delivered Meals To qualify for home-delivered meals, the CalFresh recipient must not reside in a boarding house or institution and meet the following:  Be 60 years or older; and unable to leave their home due to a disability, medical condition, or have limited mobility that prevents them preparing their own meals.  Be the spouse living with an individual who meets one of the above criteria. Home-delivered meals must be provided through non-profit meal delivery service programs that are approved by FNS to accept CalFresh benefits. Communal Dining Facilities CalFresh recipients who are 60 or older, or who receive Supplemental Security Income (SSI), and their spouses, may use their CalFresh benefits to purchase meals from approved communal dining facilities. Authorized Homeless Meal Providers CalFresh recipients who are experiencing homelessness may use their CalFresh benefits to purchase prepared meals from FNS authorized homeless meal providers. For a list of approved home-delivered meal providers, communal dining meal facilities, or homeless meal providers, HHs may contact:  Aging & Independence Services (AIS) Call Center: (800) 339-4661.  2-1-1 San Diego. References: Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 63-604.2. Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 274.7(g)(1). All County Letter (ACL) 19-51. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Prepared Meal Programs Number Page 63-380 2 of 2 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 09/30/2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-420 Work Incentive Nutrition Supplement (WINS)
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Work Incentive Nutrition Supplement (WINS) Program Number Page 63-420 1 of 4 Revision Date: 10/01/2025 Background: WINS is a state funded food benefit for CalFresh households (HH) that meet Work Participation Rate (WPR) requirements. WINS supports working families and helps improve the state’s WPR. Purpose: This section details WINS eligibility requirements for the WINS program. This section is being updated due to sunset review and includes clarification regarding the CalFresh Notice of Approval/Denial/Termination Work Incentive Nutritional Supplement (WINS) Benefit (WINS 1239) notice requirements. There are no changes to policy. Policy: WINS is a $10 monthly food benefit added to the Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) account for qualifying CalFresh HHs. WINS is evaluated at:  Initial application.  Semi-Annual Report (SAR 7).  Recertification.  When the HH reports a change. When determined eligible, the WINS benefit is issued prospectively between the 20 th and 24 th of the month until a change is reported that results in WINS ineligibility. WINS is issued at the case level, and not per individual. If two or more families are aided under one CalFresh case and are eligible for WINS, only one $10 WINS benefit is issued for the case. 1. WINS Terminology Refer to the table below for WINS-related terminology: Term Definition Parent A natural, adoptive, or stepparent acting on behalf of a child. Caretaker Relative A relative (up to the fifth degree of kinship) acting on the behalf of the parent of a child. Work-Eligible Individual (WEI) An adult (or minor child head-of-HH) living with a child unless the parent is:  A minor parent and not the head-of-HH.  Ineligible due to immigration status.  Caring for a disabled family member living in the home.  Receiving Social Security Administration (SSA) Disability benefits.  In a HH receiving Tribal Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF). Non-Two-Parent/Caretaker Relative A single parent with a child age 6 or older or a twoparent/caretaker relative HH with one WEI. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Work Incentive Nutrition Supplement (WINS) Program Number Page 63-420 2 of 4 Unsubsidized Employment A job where the employer does not receive public funds to help pay wages. Subsidized Employment A job where the employer does get public funds, such as TANF, to help pay wages. Core Work Activities Any combination of cumulative hours from the following:  Subsidized employment.  Unsubsidized employment.  Work experience (WEX).  Job search and readiness.  Community service programs.  Mental health/substance abuse domestic violence services.  Vocational education training.  Job skills training (directly related to employment).  Education (directly related to employment).  Satisfactory school attendance.  Work activities other than those specified. 2. WINS Eligibility Requirements To qualify for WINS, a CalFresh HH must not have gross income that exceeds 200% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) and meet the following criteria:  Not receiving CalWORKs or Tribal TANF.  Have a child in the home who is: o Under the age of 18; or o Under the age of 19 if the child is still in high school and will graduate before their 19 th birthday.  Have at least one parent/caretaker relative who: o Is receiving CalFresh. o Meets the WEI definition. o Meets the required number of hours of core work activity hours.  Provide verification of hours work in subsidized or unsubsidized employment. 3. WINS Work Hour Requirements To be eligible to WINS, the WEI(s) must meet the following in subsidized or unsubsidized employment based on their HH type: Hours Required Per Week WEI HH Type 20 hours per week Single custodial parent/caretaker relative with a child under the age of 6 (one WEI). 30 hours per week Non-two parent/caretaker relative or single custodial parent/caretaker relative with all children aged 6-18 (one WEI). 35 hours per week combined, with at least 30 core work activity hours completed by one parent (one WEI) Two-parent/caretaker relative (both working) with all children under the age of 18 (two WEIs). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Work Incentive Nutrition Supplement (WINS) Program Number Page 63-420 3 of 4 If the verification provided does not include the hours worked, estimated work hours may be calculated as follows:  Divide gross wages by the state minimum wage plus $0.50.  For self-employed individuals, divide net income (gross minus 40% or actual expenses) by the federal minimum wage. 4. WINS Aid Codes and HH Scenarios For information on WINS aid codes and WINS HH scenarios, refer to the WINS Desk Aid. 5. Mid-Period Changes and WINS Discontinuance If the HH reports a change mid-period report, determine if the reported change meets mandatory midperiod reporting requirements and take action accordingly. If the WEI’s hours fall below the required threshold, discontinue WINS benefits and issue adequate notice. For additional information regarding mandatory mid-period reporting, refer to CalFresh Program Guide (CFPG) 63-283. 6. Notice Requirements The WINS 1239 notice may be required depending on the WINS benefit status and specific case circumstances. The WINS 1239 approval and discontinuance notice will auto-generate in the automated system. WINS Status Notice Requirement Approved Issue the WINS 1239 approval notice. Discontinued Issue the WINS 1239 discontinuance notice in the month the ineligibility occurs (10-day timely notice is not required). Denied The WINS 1239 denial notice should never be issued when a HH fails to qualify for WINS during an initial evaluation. If a HH specifically requests to be evaluated for WINS (such as during a voluntary or mid-period report) but does not qualify for it, verbal notification is acceptable and must be documented in the case record. If contact is unsuccessful, issue the WINS 1239 denial notice. 7. Cases Approved for Transitional CalFresh (TCF) HHs discontinued from CalWORKs are screened for WINS eligibility at the start of the TCF period. To be eligible for WINS during the TCF period, the HH’s income must not exceed 200% of the FPL and must meet all other WINS eligibility criteria. If eligible, WINS benefits are issued for the entire TCF certification period. During the TCF period, HHs are not required to report any changes, and no action should be taken if a voluntary change is reported. If a TCF HH reports a change or requests to be evaluated for WINS before the end of the TCF period, the HH should be informed of the option to wait until the TCF period ends and then recertify for CalFresh; or recertify CalFresh at the time of the request. For additional information on TCF, refer to CFPG 63-320. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Work Incentive Nutrition Supplement (WINS) Program Number Page 63-420 4 of 4 8. Benefit Use WINS can only be used to purchase food and cannot be applied toward repayment of CalFresh overissuance or CalWORKs overpayment claims. WINS benefits will be expunged if there is no activity (purchases or withdrawals) on the EBT account for 274 days. Once expunged, WINS benefits cannot be restored, even if the HH remains eligible for CalFresh. References: All County Information Notice (ACIN) I-14-14, I-14-14E, I-27-15. All County Letter (ACL) 13-71, 13-71E, 14-83, 22-62. All County Welfare Directors Letter (ACWDL) December 5, 2014, February 2, 2015. Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 16-120, 42-716. title: 63-451 Establishment of CalFresh Claim
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageEstablishment of Non-Fraud CalFresh Claims 63-451 1 of 3 Revision Date: 09/01/2022 Background: A claim is an amount owed because of benefits that were overissued to the household (HH) or benefits that were trafficked. Claims are categorized as Inadvertent Household Error (IHE), Administrative Error (AE), or Intentional Program Violation (IPV) claims. IHEs and AEs are considered non-fraud and IPVs are considered fraud related claims. Purpose: This section details the types of overissuance (OI) claims and provides guidance on how to establish and calculate them. Effective July 1 st, 2022, there is a 24-month timeframe to establish and calculate a non-fraud claim. This change will be applied prospectively. This section is being revised to incorporate this change. Policy: To complete the collection process, claims must be established when an OI is calculated. A claim shall not be established in the following circumstances: •The customer did not sign the application form. •The HH resides in another county and the case was certified in San Diego County by mistake. •The 24-month time frame to act on a non-fraud OI has passed. •The customer reported a mandatory change timely, and the correct benefits could not be issued due to the 10-day notice requirement. •When the OI is based on excess property for a Categorically Eligible (CE) HH. The table below describes the types of claims: Claim Description IHE Established when an OI results from a misunderstanding or unintended error caused by the customer. AE Established when an OI results from an action or failure to act by the agency. Note: IHE’s could potentially result in an IPV, refer to section 63-453 for further guidance. Effective July 1, 2022, a non-fraud claim must only be established when it occurs within 24-months from the date of discovery. Any OI that occurred outside of the 24-month period will not be acted on. The date of discovery is the date the OI is calculated, and the claim is established when a demand letter, budget and repayment agreement are issued to the HH. This information must be entered in the case record. Below is an example of the 24-month claim establishment time frame: Example Scenario On July 1, 2022, a potential IHE OI is identified from January 1, 2019, through March 31, 2021. Outcome Staff may only calculate an OI and establish a claim for the period of July 2020 through March 2021. An OI calculation and claim establishment must not be completed for the months of January 2019 through June 2020 because they are County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageEstablishment of Non-Fraud CalFresh Claims 63-451 2 of 3 outside the 24-month timeframe. Note: For a non-fraud claim that was already established, but is later determined to be fraudulent, the timeframe may include OI months beyond the 24-month timeframe. 1. Threshold Amounts for Establishing Claims: The table below illustrates the threshold amount for when a claim must be established: Status of case and claim type Threshold amount Action Active AE $35 or less Do not establish a claim Closed AE $400 or less Do not establish a claim Active IHE $1 or more Establish a claim Closed IHE $400 or less Do not establish a claim The threshold amount will be applied based on the case status. Staff must reassess the claim if the status of the case has changed since the date of discovery. The following table will assist in making this determination: If the case status is … then the case is considered … closed on the date of discovery, and is later rescinded with no break in aid, active, apply the threshold limits specified above. closed on the date of discovery and the HH submits a new application (with a break of aid) at a later date, closed, apply the threshold limits specified above. 2. Claim Responsibility: When establishing a claim, a responsible individual must be assigned for the collection to begin. Responsible individuals include: •All adult members of the HH when the OI occurred. This includes excluded HH members. •A person connected to the HH such as an Authorized Representative (AR). •Sponsor of a noncitizen and sponsored noncitizen will both be liable, if the claim is a result from incorrect information provided by the sponsor. A sponsor will not be held at fault for an AE claim. 3. Lomeli v. Saenz Court Settlement: The Lomeli v. Saenz court settlement established that all AE OI are to be recouped at a rate of five percent (5%) or $10 whichever is greater. The allotment reduction will be set up for a period of 36- month consecutive calendar months starting with the month the actual collection begins. After the 36- month period, the collection will be suspended, and the remaining balance will be compromised (“Compromised” means that the claim is reduced or forgiven). Claims can still be collected after the case is discontinued; the months would continue to count towards the 36-month limit. When the 36- month period of recoupment expires, the system will automatically compromise the claim, reducing the remaining balance to zero ($0.00). Program Impacts: Automation: How to #532 Process Overissuance/Overpayments. ACIN I-33-14, I-33-14E. MPP 63-801.1 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 09/30/2025. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-452 Non-Fraud Claim Determination
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Non-Fraud Claim Determination 63-452 1 of 3 Revision Date: 04/01/2019 Background: Inadvertent Household Errors (IHE) and Administrative Error (AE) claims are considered non-fraud OI claims. This section is being reformatted and revised to reflect the change in regulation as a result of the settlement of the lawsuit Brown and Espinosa -Tapia v. Lightbourne. This regulation changes the look back period for collection of Inadvertent Household Error (IHE) and Administrative Error (AE) overissuances from 6 years to 3 years. Effective immediately, all newly established IHE and AE claims must comply with the new 3 year look back timeframe. OI claims established prior to this revision will not be affected. Purpose: This section details the establishment and determination of non-fraud CalFresh claims. Policy: 63-452.1 Establishment of IHE Claims: Initial IHE Overissuance Month For Inadvertent Household Error (IHE) claims, the initial month of overissuance will be the first month that the customer received more benefits than it was entitled to, unless the overissuance was caused by failure to report a required change. In cases involving failure to report a required change, the first month affected by the customer’s failure to report will be the first month in which the change would have been effective had it been reported timely. Determination of IHE Claims When determining the amount of benefits the household should have received, do not apply the twenty (20) percent earned income deduction to the portion of earned income the customer failed to report. •Calculate the amount of the IHE claim. •Offset the amount of the claim against any underissuance that was calculated for the same month of the new claim. •Adjust the claim balance to zero if the underissuance is more than the amount of the claim. Issue the balance of the underissuace to the customer as a restoration of lost benefits. Refer to 63-456. Establish an IHE claim for households when the customer: •Failed to report required information accurately and/or timely •Failed to report a change on the SAR 7 for the Data Month and the SAR Payment period was incorrectly computed based on this failure •Submits the SAR 7 late and benefits cannot be decreased due to ten-day notice requirements If a CalFresh customer has an existing overissuance that is being recouped by benefit reduction and a recoupment for another type of overissuance needs to be calculated, base the amount of the second overissuance recoupment on the initial CalFresh benefit, not on the adjusted benefit after the OI has been deducted. Refer to Definition and Examples 63-1103 for an example. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Non-Fraud Claim Determination 63-452 2 of 3 63-452.2 Establishment of AE Claims: Initial AE Overissuance Month For Administrative Error (AE) claims, the initial month of overissuance will be the first month the household receives more benefits than it was entitled to due to an error caused by the county. When the AE overissuance involves failure to act timely on a reported change, the initial month of overissuance will be the first month of the SAR payment period for which a change should have been made, subject to timely notice. Determination of AE Claims Determine the claim amount by computing the difference between the allotment the customer received and the allotment the customer should have received for each month of the overissuance. If a CalFresh customer has an existing overissuance that is being recouped by benefit reduction and a recoupment for another type of overissuance needs to be calculated, base the amount of the second overissuance recoupment on the initial CalFresh benefit, not on the adjusted benefit after the OI has been deducted. Refer to Definition and Examples 63-1103 for an example. Refer to 63-451.5 for the three-year time frame requirement to establish an AE claim. Do not offset the amount of an AE claim against any amount of underissuances, which have not yet been restored to the household. Refer to 63-454.7. 63-452.3 Determining Non-Fraud Claim Months: Calculate the amount of the non-fraud overissuance that occurred during the 3 years before the date the overissuance was discovered as long as the overissuance was established timely (within the 3- year time frame). If the overissuance is not established timely, the overissuance cannot be recouped. Refer to 63-454 for recoupment regulations and procedures. Date of Discovery The date that the budget is computed showing that the overissuance actually occurred. Date Claim Established The date the claim is established is the date adequate notice (demand letter, budget and repayment agreement) is issued to the household. A claim is established when the following happens: •The amount and reason for the overissuance is entered in case comments, and •A demand (overissuance) letter is issued to the customer The date the overissuance letter is mailed to the customer is the date the claim is considered to be established for tracking purposes. 63-452.4 Lomeli v. Saenz Court Settlement: The Lomeli v. Saenz court settlement established that all new AE overissuances established on March 1, 2000 and ongoing are to be recouped at a rate of five percent (5%) or $10 whichever is greater. The allotment reduction will be set up for a period of 36 consecutive calendar months starting with the month the actual collection begins. After the 36-month period, the collection will be suspended and the remaining balance will be forgiven (compromised). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Non-Fraud Claim Determination 63-452 3 of 3 Lomeli v. Saenz claims can still be collected after the case is discontinued; the months would continue to count towards the 36-month limit. When the 36-month limit expires, the claim will be compromised. When the 36-month period of recoupment (collection) expires, the system will automatically compromise the claim, reducing the remaining balance to zero ($0.00). 63-452.5 Determination of an Overissuance in CalWIN: Refer to Processing Guide 450-01 63-452.6 Non-System Determined Claims (NSDC): Refer to How To # 536 How To Enter a Non-System Determined Claim. Other Program Impact/s: N/A References: ACL 18-99 MPP 63-801.111; 63-801.112; 63-801.311(b) How To # 536 in Eligibility Essentials Processing Guide 450-01 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 04/30/2022. Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Eligibility Operations

title: 63-453 Intentional Program Violation
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Intentional Program Violation Number Page 63-453 1 of 2 Revision Date: 07/01/2024 Background: A fraudulent overissuance (OI) is a claim determined to have been caused by an Intentional Program Violation (IPV) . An IPV can only be established during the following processes : an Administrative Disqualification Hearing (ADH) decision, when a customer signs an ADH waiver, during a criminal court conviction, or when a customer signs a Disqualification Consent Agreement. Purpose: This section provides guidance on IPV criteria and fraud referrals. Policy: An IPV disqualifies a customer from receiving CalFresh , either for a limited time or permanently. Disqualification periods are based on the offense type and frequency. An IPV is determined when one of the following actions is taken by a household (HH) member or their sponsor: • Providing a false or misleading statement, misrepresentation, concealment, or withholding of facts. • Not complying with the CalFresh program regulations or statute relating to the use of benefits ( for example, presentation, transfer, acquisition, receipt, or possession of CalFresh benefits). • Trafficking of benefits, Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards, or devices that deliver benefits. 1. IPV Disqualification Periods: If an IPV is established by a criminal court conviction or ADH decision, the convicted IPV disqualification periods are as follows: Disqualifying Acts Disqualification Period Trading CalFresh for a controlled substance. • Two-year disqualification for the first conviction. • Permanent disqualification for the second conviction. Trading CalFresh benefits for firearms, ammunition, or explosives. • Permanent disqualification for the first conviction. Falsifying the identity or place of residence of an individual to receive multiple CalFresh benefits. • Ten-year disqualification. Trafficking in CalFresh benefits with a value of $500 or more. • Permanent disqualification for the first conviction. For any other IPV. • One-year disqualification for the first conviction. • Two-year disqualification for the second conviction. • Permanent disqualification for the third conviction. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Intentional Program Violation Number Page 63-453 2 of 2 Note: Customers may request to be reinstated verbally, in person, writing or by submitting the Request for Restoration of CalFresh Benefits After Administrative Disqualification form (CF 377.7A1). 2. Referrals to BPAI: When reviewing eligibility, identify cases where fraud is suspected and generate referrals to the Bureau of Public Assistance Investigations (BPAI) for criminal prosecution. If fraud is suspected and one or more of the following criteria are found, then refer alleged IPV cases and Inadvertent Household Error (IHE) OIs to BPAI: • The CalFresh OI is customer caused and is $5,000 or more. • A combined customer caused CalWORKs/CalFresh overpayment (OP)/OI of $5,000 or more. • There is a prior IPV and there is a current customer caused OI of $400 or more. References: All County Letters (ACLs) 17-41, 17-118, 18-22, 23-19. Manual Policies and Procedures (MPP) 63-804, 20-300.1, 300.3, 20-007, 20-300.2, 20-352. Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 273.16. sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Intentional Program Violation Number Page 63-453 1 of 2 Revision Date: 07/01/2024 Background: A fraudulent overissuance (OI) is a claim determined to have been caused by an Intentional Program Violation (IPV) . An IPV can only be established during the following processes : an Administrative Disqualification Hearing (ADH) decision, when a customer signs an ADH waiver, during a criminal court conviction, or when a customer signs a Disqualification Consent Agreement. Purpose: This section provides guidance on IPV criteria and fraud referrals. Policy: An IPV disqualifies a customer from receiving CalFresh , either for a limited time or permanently. Disqualification periods are based on the offense type and frequency. An IPV is determined when one of the following actions is taken by a household (HH) member or their sponsor: • Providing a false or misleading statement, misrepresentation, concealment, or withholding of facts. • Not complying with the CalFresh program regulations or statute relating to the use of benefits ( for example, presentation, transfer, acquisition, receipt, or possession of CalFresh benefits). • Trafficking of benefits, Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards, or devices that deliver benefits. 1. IPV Disqualification Periods: If an IPV is established by a criminal court conviction or ADH decision, the convicted IPV disqualification periods are as follows: Disqualifying Acts Disqualification Period Trading CalFresh for a controlled substance. • Two-year disqualification for the first conviction. • Permanent disqualification for the second conviction. Trading CalFresh benefits for firearms, ammunition, or explosives. • Permanent disqualification for the first conviction. Falsifying the identity or place of residence of an individual to receive multiple CalFresh benefits. • Ten-year disqualification. Trafficking in CalFresh benefits with a value of $500 or more. • Permanent disqualification for the first conviction. For any other IPV. • One-year disqualification for the first conviction. • Two-year disqualification for the second conviction. • Permanent disqualification for the third conviction. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Intentional Program Violation Number Page 63-453 2 of 2 Note: Customers may request to be reinstated verbally, in person, writing or by submitting the Request for Restoration of CalFresh Benefits After Administrative Disqualification form (CF 377.7A1). 2. Referrals to BPAI: When reviewing eligibility, identify cases where fraud is suspected and generate referrals to the Bureau of Public Assistance Investigations (BPAI) for criminal prosecution. If fraud is suspected and one or more of the following criteria are found, then refer alleged IPV cases and Inadvertent Household Error (IHE) OIs to BPAI: • The CalFresh OI is customer caused and is $5,000 or more. • A combined customer caused CalWORKs/CalFresh overpayment (OP)/OI of $5,000 or more. • There is a prior IPV and there is a current customer caused OI of $400 or more. References: All County Letters (ACLs) 17-41, 17-118, 18-22, 23-19. Manual Policies and Procedures (MPP) 63-804, 20-300.1, 300.3, 20-007, 20-300.2, 20-352. Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 273.16. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 06/30/2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-454 Recoupment of Claims
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Recoupment of Claims Number Page 63-454 1 of 5 Revision Date: 01/01/2024 Background: The county shall initiate collection action f or all I nadvertent Household Error (IH E), Administrative Error (AE) and Intentional Program Violation (IPV) established claims. Purpose: This section details recoupment procedures for Overissuance ( OI). Revisions have been made to incorporate implementation of the new CalFresh OI compromise policy for households (HH) with elderly and/or disabled members. Effective December 31st, 2023, Administrative Error (AE) and Inadvertent Household Error (IHE) claims are compromised for active and closed cases that include at least one elderly and/or disabled member responsible for the repayment of the claim at the time of claim discovery. Policy: 1. Non-Fraud Error Claim Recoupment Procedures for Active Cases: To start the recoup ment of a n esta blished claim , an OI notice , repayment agreement and budget computation shall be sen t to the HH. The following table shows the required information in the OI notice, repayment agreement and budget computation: Notices Required Information OI Notice • The amount of benefits the HH erroneously received. • T he period of the claim. • The amount required to be repaid. • T he amount of benefits the HH should have received. • T he specific cause of the OI. • How the HH (or its sponsor) may pay the claim. • The HHs or the sponsor’s right to a state hearing. Note: If the HH or the sponsor disagrees with the amount of the claim, the HH has 90 days to request a hearing. Repayment Agreement Provides information and the option to pay AE and IHE claims by: • L ump sum payment: Paid in full by cash , check, money order or by a reduction of their CalFresh benefits. HHs will n ot be requir ed to liquidate resources to make a lump sum payment. • B enefit reduction: Benefits will be reduced monthly by 5% or $10 whichever is greater for AE claims and 10% or $10 whichever is greater for IHE claims. • Insta llments: Paid monthly by cash, check, money order payments or by a reduction of their CalFresh benefits. Installments paid by the customer must be equal to the amount which could be recovered through benefit reduction. This amount will remain unchanged regardless of subsequent changes in the HH’s monthly benefit. Budget Computation Provides the information of the amount of earned and/or unearned income, HH size and the allowed deductions used in the CalFresh budget. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Recoupment of Claims Number Page 63-454 2 of 5 Once the not ices have been sent to the HHs, they w ill need to choose repayment option. HH’s who fail to s end back t he repayment agreement notices within 30 days will have their claims reduced by benefit reduction. 2. Recoupment Regulations: • Initiate AE or IHE OI recoupment at the beginning of a new certification or mid-period with timely notice. • C ollection will be made on one active claim at a time. • R ecoupment can stop mid-period when the OI has been completely recouped. • AE claims established under Lomeli will not be collected with any other type of claims at the same time through benefit reduction. • When a recoupment of one OI is completed, recoupment of the next OI can begin mid-period if the recoupment does not result in a decrease in benefits. • Claims may be recouped from separate HHs at the sam e time for the same claim from multiple adult members who received an OI as one HH but moved to separate CalFresh HH. However, the amount recouped from all HHs may not exceed the total OI. 3. Postponement of IHE Recoupment: Postpone recoupment action of IHE claims in ca ses where an OI is referred for possible legal prosecution or for administrative disqualificati on, and t he county determines that recoupment action will prejudice the case. 4. IHE and AE Recoupment Procedures for Noncitizen HHs with Sponsors: Any noncitizen’s sponsor and the sponsored noncitizen will be held jointly liable for repayment of any OI of CalFresh benefits that results from incorrect inf ormation provided by the sp onsor. Determine whether the incorrect information was provided due to error on the part of the noncitizen or the noncitizen's sponsor prior to initiating recoupment action against the sponsored noncitizen HH. The noncitizen HH will be solely liable for repayment of an OI when it has be en determined that the sponsor has good cause or was not at fault for providing incorrect information. Recoupment for all IHE claims against the HH and sponsor will initiate when the sponsor did not have good cause or was at faut and the HH or sponsor cannot be located. A sponsor will not be held at fault for an AE claim. Note: A claim can also be established against the party most likely to repay first. 5. IPV Recoupment for Active Cases: Recoupment by benefit reduction will be made at a rate of 20% or $20, w hichever is greater. Timely notice is not required to reduce the HHs benefit due to an IPV disqualification. 6. Collection Procedures for Closed Cases: The claim establishment threshold will be $400.00 for closed CalFresh cases with an OI caused by an AE or IHE. This threshold does not apply t o OIs arising from IPV or Quality Control (QC) reviews. When a CalFresh case is discont inued with an outstanding claim balance, a transaction is sent to the Office o f Rev enue and Recovery (O RR). A n acco unt will be established, and collection will be initiated on all OIs over $400. Refer to Processing Guide 454-01 for steps to ta ke on OI for clo sed cases. Customers can repay a claim by d educting CalFresh benefits from the E lectronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) a ccount at any tim e, even if the claim is currently being recouped or the c ase has been closed. To begin recoupm ent, the responsible HH member shall complete and sign the Authorization for Benefit Collection from EBT Account (16-102 HHSA) form. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Recoupment of Claims Number Page 63-454 3 of 5 7. Compromising a Claim for an Elderly and/or Disabled HH: Effective December 31st, 2023, AE and IHE claims for active and closed HH that include at least one elderly and/or disabled member will be compromised. For the definition of elderly and/or disabled, refer to CalFresh Program Guide 63- 101. Compromising a claim means that a previously established claim is reduced or forgiven. AE and IHE OI claims f or active and closed cases will only be automatically compromised if the claim was established on or after the implementation date of December 31st, 2023. AE and IHE claims must be compromised according to the HH composition, claim responsibility and participation status at the time of discovery as follows: Type of Claim HH members responsible for repayment of the claim at the time of claim discovery Case Status Compromised Percentage AE and IHE all elderly and/or disabled members Active or closed 100% mixed HH in which only the elderly and/or disabled members are responsible for the claim Active or closed 100% mixed HH where at least one member who is not elderly and/or disabled are responsible for the claim Active 50% The examples below illustrate the perce ntage a claim will be comp romised based on the HH composition, claim responsibility and status at the time of discovery. Example Scenario Married couple receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI) income receive an AE OI due to county not using the correct SSI income. Case is active and the discovery date is January 1st, 2024. Both adults are responsible for the claim. Outcome The AE OI claim will be compromised 100%. Example Scenario Disabled mother and their m inor child receive an IHE OI due to unreported income back in January 2023 . Case is clos ed and the discovery date is February 1st 2024. Only the mother is responsible for the claim. Outcome The IHE claim will be compromised 100 % because the claim was established after the policy implementation date of December 31st, 2023. Example Scenario Husband, disabled wife, and disabled adult child received an AE OI due erroneous deduction being counted in the budget . Case is active and the discovery date is January 21st, 2023. All adults in the HH are responsible for the claim. Outcome The AE claim will be compromised 50 % because at least one member who is not elderly and/or disabled is responsible for the claim and the claim w as established County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Recoupment of Claims Number Page 63-454 4 of 5 after the implementation date. At the time the OI i s discovered, staff will de termine if an individual is elderly and/or disabled based on the following: • Elderly status for active and closed cases shall be verified based on the HHs member’s age at the time of discovery using the date of birth provided. • Disability status for active cases shall be verified base d on the most recently verified information known to staff at the time of discovery. • Disability status for closed cases shall be verified based o n a HHs member’s disability status the last month they w ere receiving CalFresh benefits if more current disabi lity information is not available. The total cumulative amount of the OI will be r educed. HH members who become either disabled or elderly during collection of an OI must be e ligible for reduction. HHs may also qualify for t he OI compromise ev en if they are already in collection. The HH must inform staff and must have their elderly/disabled status verified to have the remaining b alance of their OI claim reduced. T his compromise policy will not be applied retroactively. The amount to be compromised for a claim already in collection is determined based on the date the HH made the request. Any reductions to the claim amount will be applied from that point forward. There is one instance where an OI cannot be compromised due to their elderly and/or disabled status. The following is an example: Example Scenario An elderly HH appeals their CalFresh case due to a change in their benefits. The HH requests and is approved aid paid pending while waiting for the hearing. After review, th e hearing is unsuccessful, and aid paid pendin g becomes an OI for the HH. Outcome The HH must not have the portion of the claim caused by aid paid pending compromised. However, t he portion of the cla im that was not caused by aid paid pending can be compromised. 8. Compromise Notices of Action (NOA): Staff are only required to inform HHs of a reduction if the HH’s claim is reduced by 100% on an already established claim. If a HH’s OI is reduced by 100% p rior to the initial establishment of the OI, then the HH is not required to be informed. For HHs receiving a 50% compromise, staff must issue a NOA to inform the HH of the compromise and the remaining balance. The r eason is that the amount overissued and the amount the HH is required to pay will be different if they are eligible to have thei r OI claim c ompromised. Staff shall use the following notices to inform customers of compromised amounts: • CalFresh Overissuance Notice Inadvertent Household Errors Only (CF 377.7B). • CalFresh Overissuance Notice County Administrative Error (CF 377.7D3). • CalFresh Repayment Notice-Inadvertent Household Errors Only Final Notice (CF 377.7B1). • CalFresh Repayment Notice-County Administrative Error Only Final Notice (CF 377.7D2). Staff shall manually enter an ex planation of the reason for the OI in the NO A and provide sufficient detail to allow the HH to determine if any incorrect information was used in the OI determination and County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Recoupment of Claims Number Page 63-454 5 of 5 the reason for the OI compr omise. This inf ormation shall outline how the HH qualified for the compromise, and the amount the OI was reduced. References: All County Information Notice (ACIN) I-33-14. All County Letter (ACL) 19-50, 18-99, 15-95, 13-79, 13-79E, 21-118, 22-61, 22-61E, and 22-61E2. MPP 63-801. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 01/31/2027. Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Self-Sufficiency Services
