title: 63-608 Transitional CalFresh Q&A
content: 63-608 Transitional CalFresh (Q&A) Table of Contents Subject Question/Answer Transitional CalFresh Eligibility after CalWORKs Consecutive Discontinuances CalWORKs Discontinued Untimely - Beginning of Transitional CalFresh CalWORKs Discontinuing Due to Ineligibility of the Only Child Household Member Leaving the Month After Transitional CalFresh is Granted CalWORKs Discontinuing at the Same Time the Child is Approved for SSI/SSP CalWORKs Discontinuing Before Adding a New Person to the Assistance Unit Kin-GAP Children – Transitional CalFresh Eligibility Child Residing with Unknown Relative (Payee) after Mother Dies Transitional CalFresh Initial Eligibility Parents Sanctioned the Same Month the CalWORKs Case is Discontinued Transitional CalFresh Household Member Granted CalWORKs Only CalWORKs Household Reapplies and Discontinues Again before the Transitional CalFresh Case is Discontinued Changes in Household Circumstances CalFresh Budget After Transitional CalFresh is Discontinued Transitional CalFresh Eligibility after CalWORKs Consecutive Discontinuan ces QUESTION A household’s CalWORKs case discontinues. Transitional CalFresh is granted, the client reapplies for CalWORKs and CalWORKs is approved. The CalWORKs discontinues the second time. Is the household eligible for Transitional CalFresh a second time? Can we keep going back and forth between cash assistance and Transitional CalFresh? Is there a limit to how many times a client can get Transitional CalFresh? ANSWER Transitional CalFresh will be issued and a new five-month period will begin each time the CalWORKs cash assistance ends, if the household is receiving CalFresh in the last month of cash assistance. There is no limit to the number of times a household can go on and off Transitional CalFresh. ACIN I-21-04 CalWORKs Discontinued Untimely - Beginning of Transitional CalFresh BACKGROUND: An absent father with earnings returned to the home July 2004. The CalWORKs case would have been discontinued at the end of the payment quarter on August 31, 2004, if the information had been reported timely. When the county learned of the situation, the CalWORKs case was discontinued on November 30, 2004. QUESTION: In a situation in which the CalWORKs case should have been discontinued, but the client continued to receive a CalWORKs grant, will Transitional CalFresh benefits begin the month after the CalWORKs grant is actually discontinued or the month the CalWORKs grant should have been discontinued? ANSWER: Transitional CalFresh benefits would begin December 1 st because the last month the client received a CalWORKs grant was November. Transitional CalFresh cases begin the month following the discontinuance from CalWORKs. All Transitional CalFresh cases are to be given a five-month certification period. Workers shall not subtract time from the Transitional CalFresh case if ineligibility existed in prior months on the CalWORKs case. ACIN I-34-05 CalWORKs Discontinuing Due to Ineligibility of the Only Child QUESTION The whole CalWORKs cash assistance case is discontinued due to ineligibility of the child. Is this a Transitional CalFresh case? ANSWER If a household loses cash benefits because it no longer includes an eligible child, they can still receive Transitional CalFresh. However, if the child receives benefits in another CalWORKs or CalFresh household, then the worker would need to remove the child from the Transitional CalFresh household. If the child’s leaving results in the household member being designated as an Able Bodied Adult Without Dependent Children (ABAWD), the household is still eligible for Transitional CalFresh. The law does not require an analysis of their ABAWD status. ACIN I-21-04 Household Member Leaving the Month after Transitional CalFresh is Granted QUESTION During the month cash aid is discontinued, will a household member be included in the Transitional CalFresh household if it is known to the County that the individual will not be in the home the following month? ANSWER Yes. Transitional CalFresh benefits are issued based on circumstances in the last month of CalWORKs eligibility. If the individual was included in the last month of CalWORKs, that individual should be included in the Transitional CalFresh household. However, if the individual applies for and is granted benefits in another CalWORKs or CalFresh household, then the worker would need to remove them from the Transitional CalFresh household. ACIN I-21-04 CalWORKs Discontinuing at the Same Time the Child is Approved for SSI/SSP QUESTION A mother and child are receiving CalWORKs. The child is approved for SSI/SSP and the mother gets a job, which makes the family ineligible for CalWORKs. Is the household eligible for Transitional CalFresh? If so, for how many people? ANSWER The mother and the child would be eligible for Transitional CalFresh if the child was not receiving SSI/SSP in the last month the household was receiving CalWORKs. However, if the child is already receiving SSI/SSP, in the month prior to the household being discontinued from CalWORKs, the child would not be eligible for Transitional CalFresh — only the mother would be eligible. ACIN I-21-04 CalWORKs Discontinuing Before Adding a New Person to the Assistance Unit QUESTION If the County is in the middle of adding a person to the CalWORKs/CalFresh household and CalWORKs is discontinued, should the new person be included in the Transitional CalFresh benefit amount? ANSWER No. The new person had to be part of the CalWORKs/CalFresh case at the time of discontinuance. ACIN I-72-04 Kin-GAP Children – Transitional CalFresh Eligibility QUESTION A needy caretaker relative was discontinued from CalWORKs for herself and her grandchild. There are also Kin-GAP children in the home and they also receive CalFresh. Is there eligibility for Transitional CalFresh since Kin-GAP continues to be received for the children? ANSWER Yes, the household would receive Transitional CalFresh. Kin-GAP is funded through Title IV-E funds, unlike CalWORKs which is funded from Title IV-A funds. The Transitional CalFresh case is set up based upon the CalWORKs household discontinuance for the existing CalFresh members in the scenario. Benefits are issued in the amount of the allotment received in the last month of CalWORKs eligibility, adjusted for the change in household income as a result of termination in the CalWORKs program. ACIN I-84-09 Child Residing with Unknown Relative (Payee) after Mother Dies QUESTION The CalWORKs assistance unit consisted of a mother and a minor child. The mother died and the child went to live with relatives. The relative’s information is unknown. Does the County set up the Transitional CalFresh for the child only? What if the payee is unknown? ANSWER The Transitional CalFresh case could only be set up if there is a designated authorized representative prior to benefits being issued. The child would not be in his/her own household, therefore there would not be a Transitional CalFresh case. If the child’s relatives were eligible for CalFresh, they could apply for regular CalFresh benefits. ACIN I-72-04 Parents Sanctioned the Same Month the CalWORKs Case is Discontinued BACKGROUND On October 20, 2006, a worker imposed a CalWORKs/CalFresh Welfare-to-Work sanction to both parents and issued a timely 10-day notice to decrease benefits. That same night, CalWIN issued an “X” Notice of Action (NOA) for non-receipt of the QR 7. The household failed to provide the QR 7 by the extended filing date and the case was discontinued. Transitional CalFresh was issued in November 2006. QUESTION Are the sanctioned parents eligible to Transitional CalFresh? ANSWER Yes, the parents should receive Transitional CalFresh because they received CalWORKs and CalFresh in the last month of CalWORKs eligibility and the sanction had not yet been imposed (the sanction was going to take effect in November). ACIN I-42-07 Transitional CalFresh Household Member Granted CalWORKs Only Scenario: The client was receiving Transitional CalFresh for herself and one child. The child was removed from the home and placed in another home. The other household applied for CalWORKs only for the child and not CalFresh. Since the child was approved for CalWORKs effective 08/08, he was removed from the Transitional CalFresh household effective 10/08. Question: Should the child have been removed from the Transitional CalFresh household? Answer: Yes. The child must be removed because the individual cannot receive CalWORKs and Transitional CalFresh at the same time. Transitional CalFresh eligibility is based upon receiving CalWORKs and regular CalFresh benefits in the last month of CalWORKs eligibility. Transitional CalFresh issuance is based upon household’s terminating its participation in the CalWORKs program. Transitional CalFresh eligibility occurs when CalWORKs is terminated; receipt of CalWORKs by the Transitional CalFresh household will end Transitional CalFresh eligibility. In this case, since a Transitional CalFresh recipient remains who is not on CalWORKs (the mother) Transitional CalFresh continues for her. ACIN I-84-09 CalWORKs Household Reapplies and Discontinues Again before the Transitional CalFresh Case is Discontinued CASE SCENARIO: 04/30 A household receiving Transitional CalFresh reapplies for CalWORKs 05/15 The applicant attends the CalWORKs intake interview 05/22 CalWORKs is approved with a beginning date of 04/30/07 (04/30 was the application date). Transitional CalFresh is set to discontinue 06/30 05/31 The household requests CalWORKs discontinuance 06/30 Transitional CalFresh is set to discontinue, the CalWORKs case is discontinued 06/30 due to 10-day notice requirement QUESTION Is the household eligible for Transitional CalFresh benefits beginning 07/01/07 after the CalWORKs discontinuance? ANSWER No. To be eligible to Transitional CalFresh, CalWORKs and regular CalFresh must have been issued in the month the CalFresh household loses CalWORKs. There is no Transitional CalFresh eligibility 07/01/07 because the household did not receive regular CalFresh benefits in June. ACIN I-58-08 CalFresh Budget After Transitional CalFresh is Discontinued CASE SCENARIO Client applied for CalWORKs in 01/05. The first quarter is 01/05- 03/05. Client had an active Transitional CalFresh case, which was discontinued on 01/31/05 because 01/05 was the fifth month. The worker approved the case in 02/05, CalWORKs effective 01/05 and Public Assistance CalFresh effective 02/05. The client received wages in 01/05, 02/05 and was expected to receive them in 03/05 too. She also received cash contributions in 01/05 only. She did not receive anything in 02/05 and did not expect anything for 03/05 either. QUESTION What is the proper method to count the income in the Public Assistance CalFresh budget? 1) Do we count the income for the three months, divide by three and then enter the average in the CalFresh budget for 02/05 & 03/05? or 2) Do we count the income for 02/05 & 03/05 only, divide by two and then enter the average in the CalFresh budget for 02/05 & 03/05? ANSWER The income that is anticipated to be received in the Public Assistance CalFresh payment quarter is the income that is used for the determination of CalFresh benefits. Therefore, the worker shall count the income anticipated for 02/05 & 03/05 only, divide by two, and use the average for 02/05 & 03/05. PI 2005-17

title: 63-609 Claims and Adjustments Q&A
content: 63-609 Claims and Adjustments (Q&A) Table of Contents Subject Question/Answer CalWORKs Grant CalWORKs Grant Recalculation to Determine an Overissuance or Underissuance Collection of Overissuances • Collection of Overissuances from Adult Household Members • Collecting a Claim from Two Separate Households • Collection of Overissuances from Excluded Household Members Including SSI/SSP Recipients Determination of Overissuance Calculating Overissuance of Household with Self- Employment and Regular Earnings CalWORKs Grant Recalculation to Determine an Overissuance or Underissuanc e QUESTION To determine an overissuance, do we count the CalWORKs grant that was actually issued, or do we recalculate the CalWORKs grant? ANSWER When computing an overissuance or underissuance, the worker will use the actual CalWORKs grant amount that was anticipated with reasonable certainty or that was reasonably anticipated. QR regulations support using the amount of the grant that was reasonably anticipated with no look-back for recalculation of the CalWORKs grant. An overissuance or underissuance will not be assessed when actual income received during the quarter differs from the amount of income reasonably anticipated, as long as the recipient met his or her mandatory reporting obligations. Since CalWORKs grants are knownto-county information and not subject to recipient reporting, a recalculated grant is not required. ACIN I-16-05 Collection of Overissuance s from Adult Household Members QUESTION Can the county collect from any adult member present in the household at the time of an overissuance, including adult children, but not collect from children who leave the case and establish their own household? ANSWER Yes. All adult household members, including children who are adults in the household, are liable for any overissuances that occurred while they were in the household. Per Section 63-451.1, a claim shall be established against any household that has received more CalFresh benefits than it is entitled to receive or to any household which contains an adult member who was an adult member of another household that received more CalFresh benefits than it was entitled to receive. While minor children are not liable for overissuances, if the household consists of all minors, a collection action can be initiated against a household whose only eligible members are minors. However, if a minor leaves an “all minor” household, that minor is not liable for the overissuance. ACIN I-16-05 Collecting a Claim from Two Separate Households CASE SCENARIO: A household consists of three adult sisters and five children all receiving CalFresh. An overissuance occurs and collection activity begins. Two of the adult sisters and their children move out of the home leaving only one sister and two children active (Case A). One sister moves in with her boyfriend who is receiving CalFresh with his mother and brother (Case B). Collecting activity now begins in Case B as the sister that was active in Case A is now active in Case B. QUESTION: Can we collect from both cases at the same time for one claim? Per Section 63-451.2, we can collect from all adults who were in the household when the overissuance occurred, and at the same time for the same claim? According to this section, claim collection will be from all adults who were in the household when the overissuance occurred. ANSWER: Yes. The worker can collect from two separate cases at the same time for the same claim as long as each case consists of an adult member who was an adult member of another household that received more CalFresh benefits than it was entitled to receive. A collection can be initiated in a new CalFresh household (Case B) if the “liable” member moves to a new household. The worker shall establish a claim against any household that has received more CalFresh benefits than it is entitled to receive or any household which contains an adult member who was an adult member of another household that received more CalFresh benefits than it was entitled to receive. ACIN I-58-08 Collection of Overissuance s from Excluded QUESTION Can the county demand repayment from an excluded household Household Members Including SSI/SSP Recipients member such as an SSI/SSP recipient or an undocumented person? ANSWER Yes, but for excluded household members other than SSI/SSP members. Federal regulations state adult members of the household are responsible for overissuances. Excluded household members, are part of the household, but not currently receiving benefits due to ineligibility status, such as being sanctioned, having SSI status or having drug/fleeing felon status (please refer to Section 63-101.6). Given the fact that they are adults and considered part of the household and could have caused the overissuance, excluded household members not currently in a status to be receiving benefits, are responsible for repayment of a claim. Although SSI/SSP recipients may be responsible for the overissuance, repayment cannot be demanded from the SSI/SSP benefit. Repayment can be demanded from the other excluded adult household members. Calculating Overissuance of Household with Self- Employment and Regular Earnings A CalFresh household member receiving benefits since 2002 has been reporting earned income from her full-time job. Three years later an Income Eligibility Verification System (IEVS) report showed the household member has also been working as self-employed, paid in cash. The worker received a copy of the household member’s tax forms from IRS showing the annual income the household did not report to the county. QUESTION Since this household member has two different incomes, what is the correct methodology to determine the overissuance? ANSWER Based on Section 63-241.5, which states “Self-employment must be averaged over the period of time the income is intended to cover....,” it is appropriate to average self-employment income over the year it was received. That monthly figure is considered gross self-employment income. The self-employed income needs to be computed separately from income earned on the job to arrive at a “net gross” self-employment income amount. The preferred methodology to determine the overissuance in this case is as follows: Step Action 1 Verify and average the gross self-employment income as explained in Sections 63-241.5, 63-241.6 and 63-241.9. 2 Subtract 40 percent for self-employment expenses from the gross income in Step 1, or deduct the actual costs of doing business to arrive at the “net gross” self-employment income amount (Section 63-241.7). 3 Compute all earned income: Add the gross earned income from the job, and the “net gross” from self-employment to obtain the total gross earned income. 4 Allow all applicable deductions. When determining the amount of benefits the household should have received, the worker will not apply the 20 percent earned income deduction to the portion of earned income the household failed to report. 5 Deduct what should have been received from what the client actually received to determine the amount of the overissuance. ACIN I-96-06

title: 63-610 Other Q&A
content: 63-610 Other (Q&A) Table of Contents Subject Question/Answer Replacement of Food Replacement of Food due to a Household Misfortune Replacement of Food due to a Household Misfortune QUESTION 1 Household (owns their own home) states their refrigerator stopped working and the part needed had to be ordered from Canada. The household lost the food contents of the refrigerator due to this incident. Is this considered a “household misfortune”? ANSWER 1 Although there is no specific definition to the term “household misfortune,” MPP section 63-603.113 states that food purchased with CalFresh benefits can be received by the household through a replacement issuance. This regulation in general, indicates that replacement benefits are a one-time occurrence. This scenario constitutes a household misfortune; therefore, the household is eligible to replace the food that was lost due to the refrigerators not working. QUESTION 2 All of the household’s “dry goods” were destroyed by insects. Does this scenario fall under the definition of “household misfortune”? ANSWER 2 This scenario would generally not fall under the definition of “household misfortune” because it is considered a preventable circumstance and one that happens periodically to other households. However, the determination is the county’s based on the given circumstances of the case. Whatever the determination made by the county, the case record should be documented. ACIN I-54-09E

sections.text: 63-610 Other (Q&A) Table of Contents Subject Question/Answer Replacement of Food Replacement of Food due to a Household Misfortune Replacement of Food due to a Household Misfortune QUESTION 1 Household (owns their own home) states their refrigerator stopped working and the part needed had to be ordered from Canada. The household lost the food contents of the refrigerator due to this incident. Is this considered a “household misfortune”? ANSWER 1 Although there is no specific definition to the term “household misfortune,” MPP section 63-603.113 states that food purchased with CalFresh benefits can be received by the household through a replacement issuance. This regulation in general, indicates that replacement benefits are a one-time occurrence. This scenario constitutes a household misfortune; therefore, the household is eligible to replace the food that was lost due to the refrigerators not working. QUESTION 2 All of the household’s “dry goods” were destroyed by insects. Does this scenario fall under the definition of “household misfortune”? ANSWER 2 This scenario would generally not fall under the definition of “household misfortune” because it is considered a preventable circumstance and one that happens periodically to other households. However, the determination is the county’s based on the given circumstances of the case. Whatever the determination made by the county, the case record should be documented. ACIN I-54-09E

title: 63-901 Work Registration
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Work Registration Number Page 63-901 1 of 4 Revision Date: 12/01/2025 Background: All CalFresh household (HH) members must be screened for work registration. The general CalFresh work requirements are referred to as work registration and non-exempt HH members are referred to as work registrants. Work registration differs from CalFresh Employment & Training (E&T) and the Able- Bodied Adult Without Dependents (ABAWD) time limit. For guidance on E&T or the ABAWD time limit reference CalFresh Program Guide (CFPG) Sections 63-903 and 63-904, respectively. Purpose: This section provides guidance on the rules for work registration screening, exemptions, requirements, and changes in exemption status. The policy was updated to add the requirement to provide an oral and written explanation of the general CalFresh work rules to all CalFresh HHs. Policy: Screen all CalFresh HH members for work registration at initial application, recertification, and when there is a change in work registration exemption status. It is not mandatory for w ork registrants to participate in E&T as a condition of CalFresh eligibility. 1. Screening Process Provide the CalFresh Notice of Work Rules (CF 886) and an oral explanation to all CalFresh HHs, this includes work registrants and those who are exempt. All CalFresh HH members are subject to work registration unless they meet an exemption. Register all non-exempt CalFresh HH members for work registration. Screening includes: • Registering non-exempt HH members between the ages of 16 through 59. • Providing the CF 886 and an oral explanation of the CalFresh work rules. • Informing HHs of available employment services. • Referring appropriate HH members who would like to voluntarily participate in CalFresh E&T. Document the screening information in the case record, including HH members who are work registrants and who are exempt. 2. Work Registration Exemptions HH members exempt from work registration at initial application or recertification remain exempt until their next recertification unless they experience a change that impacts their status. HH members are exempt from work registration if they meet at least one of the criteria below: • Under 16 or over 59 years of age. • A 16 or 17 -year-old who is not head of household can meet work registration requirements by attending school or an employment training program at least half-time. • Physically or mentally unfit for employment. • Subject to and complying with any work requirements under Title IV of the Social Security Act including the CalWORKs program. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Work Registration Number Page 63-901 2 of 4 • A parent of or responsible for the care of a dependent child under age 6. o The child does not have to be a member of the CalFresh HH or living in the home. • Responsible for the care of an incapacitated person. o The incapacitated person does not have to be a member of the CalFresh HH or living in the home. • Applying for, or receiving, unemployment insurance benefits. • A regular participant in a drug or alcohol treatment program. • Employed or self-employed at least 30 hours per week or receiving weekly earnings at least equal to the federal minimum wage multiplied by 30 hours. o The calculation of federal minimum wage x 30 hours = $217.50 weekly – This amount is based on 2025 federal minimum wage and subject to change based on federal updates. • Enrolled in a school, training program, or institution of higher education on at least a half-time basis. o Students enrolled at least half -time in an institution of higher education must meet student eligibility requirements. 3. Work Registration Requirements HH members are considered registered when their status is confirmed in the automated system. Complete the following steps to confirm registration: • Complete applicable data collection screens in the automated system. o Confirm work registration status in the CalFresh Eligibility Benefit Determination Calculation (EDBC) Summary screen. • Document the information in the case record. All work registrants must comply with the following general CalFresh work requirements: • Accept an offer for suitable employment. Employment is considered suitable unless: o The wage offered is less than federal minimum wage, the state minimum wage, or 80% of the federal minimum wage if neither the federal nor state minimum wage is applicable. o The employment offered is on a piece- rate basis and the average hourly wage the employee can reasonably be expected to earn is less than the applicable hourly wages specified above. o The HH member, as a condition of employment or continuing employment, is required to join, resign from, or refrain from joining any legitimate labor organization. o The work offered is at a site subject to a strike or lockout at the time of the offer. o The degree of risk to health and safety is unreasonable. o The employment offered within the first 30 days of registration is not in the member's major field of experience. o The distance from the member's home to the place of employment is unreasonable considering the expected wage and the time and cost of commuting. o The daily commute time exceeds 2 hours per day, not including the transport of a child to and from a childcare facility. o The distance to the place of employment prohibits walking and neither public nor private transportation is available to transport the HH member to the job site. o The working hours or nature of the employment interferes with the HH member's religious observances, convictions, or beliefs. • Register for work or be registered at the time of application and every 12 months thereafter. • Provide sufficient information to determine employment status or availability for work. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Work Registration Number Page 63-901 3 of 4 • Not voluntarily quit a job of 30 or more hours a week or reduce work hours to fewer than 30 hours a week without good cause. o The calculation of federal minimum wage x 30 hours = $217.50 weekly – This amount is based on 2025 federal minimum wage and subject to future federal updates. Refer to Section 63-159 for guidance on voluntary job quit or reduction of work hours. 5. Changes in Work Registration Exemption Status When a change in circumstance impacts a HH member’s work registration status during the certification period, screen them for another work registration exemption. If the HH member is not exempt, then register them as a work registrant at: • The Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7). • A change that is a mandatory mid-period report, refer to Section 63-283. • A voluntary mid-period report that is Verified Upon Receipt (VUR), refer to Section 63-283. If any of these c hanges occur and the HH member is subject to work registration, then they must be screened for another exemption and registered within 10 days of the date the change was reported. The following are examples of registering a HH member at the time a change is reported: References: All County Letter (ACL) 19-93, 20-10, 22-74, 22-99, 23-30, 24-42, and 25-64. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 11/30/2028. Example: Mandatory Mid-Period Report Scenario HH consists of 40 -year-old dad and his 10-year-old daughter. At intake , it was verified that dad was earning a gross amount of $250.00 per week , therefore he was exempt from work registration. At SAR 7, dad’s gross earnings dropped below $217.50 per week (amount based on 2025 federal minimum wage and subject to future federal updates). Outcome Dad no longer meets a work registration exemption because he is earning less than 30 hours per week at federal minimum wage ($217.50 per week). Dad is now subject to work registration and must be registered within 10 days. Example: Mid-Period Change Report That is VUR Scenario At recertification HH consisted of 30 -year-old mom and her 4 -year-old son. Mom reported to be earning a gross amount of $195.00 per week. Mom was exempt from work registration due to caring for a child under 6 years of age. Mid-period she voluntarily report ed her son is no longer in the home; he is living with his father. Outcome Mom no longer meets a work registration exemption because she is no longer caring for a child under 6 and does not meet any other exemptions. Mom is now subject to work registration and must be registered within 10 days. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Work Registration Number Page 63-901 4 of 4 Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-902 Deferrals and Substitute Programs
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Deferrals and Substitute Programs 63-902 1 of 2 Revision Date: 06/12/2017 Background: Each work registrant will be screened to determine whether they will participate or be deferred from the Employment & Training (E&T) program. The following individuals will be deferred from participation in E&T: •Participants in a substitute program as described in the policy below •Veterans who have been honorably discharged from United States Armed Forces •Victims of Domestic Violence Policy: 63-902.1: Refugee Resettlement Agencies The Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) provides new populations with opportunities to maximize their potential in the United States. The objective is to ensure that refugees become self-sufficient in the shortest time possible. Refugees enrolled with Resettlement Agencies (RAs), formerly known as Voluntary Agencies (VolAgs), are deferred from E&T. The RAs contract with the Department of State to provide services to refugees. The California Department of Social Services (CDSS) Resettlement Agencies website has a current listing of RAs in California. As of 10/28/14 California Resettlement Agencies in San Diego County include: •Alliance for African Assistance (AAA) •Catholic Charities, Diocese of San Diego •International Rescue Committee (IRC) •Jewish Family Service of San Diego •Kurdish Human Rights Watch •La Maestra Legal Advocacy Services •Wilson/Fish Project for Refugees 63-902.2: Substitute Program Participants Refugees enrolled with RAs are deferred from E&T. 63-902.3: Veteran Deferrals Veterans who have been honorably discharged from the United States Armed Forces are deferred from E&T. Deferred veterans may choose to volunteer to participate in E&T. Deferred veterans will be provided with a referral to the local County Veterans Service Offices (VSOs). An updated list of VSOs by county can be found at www.cacvso.org. 63-902.4: Domestic Violence Deferrals Victims of Domestic Violence (DV) are deferred from E&T. They may choose to volunteer to participate in E&T. Procedure: Handling Substitute Programs: If a participant fails without good cause to comply with the Resettlement Agencies (RA) requirements, he or she loses the deferral and must be registered for the E&T program. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Deferrals and Substitute Programs 63-902 2 of 2 Handling Veteran Deferrals: Verification of Honorable Discharge Status •A completed DD 214 or other appropriate verification (The DD214 is the current form used by the military to prove separation from active duty); or •A Statement of Service (SoS). If the veteran is unable to provide verification of honorable discharge, they will be referred to the local VSO for assistance in securing the document. The veteran will be temporarily deferred from E&T participation until documentation is received that the verification of honorable discharge has been requested. Once the DD 214 or SoS confirming the Veteran was honorably discharged is received, the Veteran will be permanently deferred from E&T. If the DD214 or SoS states that the Veteran was not honorably discharged, the temporary deferral will end. The Veteran will then be subject to E&T requirements unless otherwise exempt. If the Veteran fails to provide the necessary verification within the 30 day time frame, the temporary deferral will end. The Veteran will then be subject to E&T participation requirements unless otherwise exempt. Handling Domestic Violence Deferrals: Verification of Domestic Violence can be the customer’s statement. No further verification is required unless strong evidence suggests that the customer’s statement is questionable. Other Program Impacts: No Impact References: MPP 63.407 ACL 13-107 ACL 17-30 Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) - https://www.acf.hhs.gov/orr Resettlement Agencies - https://www.acf.hhs.gov/orr/resource/voluntary-agencies Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 06/30/2020. Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Eligibility Operations

title: 63-903 CalFresh Employment and Training (CFET) Components and Transportation Payments
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageCalFresh Employment & Training (CFET) Components and Transportation Payments 63-903 1 of 3 Revision Date: 03/01/2023 Background: CalFresh Employment & Training (CFET) components are designed to provide recipients training and work experience. San Diego’s CFET program consist of the following components: Education, Supervised Job Search (SJS), Job Retention, and Work Experience (WE) delivered by Work Activity and Work Based Learning. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide component definitions and the methods in which they are administered. This section is being revised to update the Workfare component to WE (Work Activity and Work Based Learning) and provide new guidance on transportation allowances. Policy: Components are administered directly by CFET Social Worker (SW) staff, additional services are contracted with San Diego Workforce Partnership (SDWP) and Fresh Success. The table below details the components offered by each provider: Provider Components Offered CFET SW •SJS •WE by means of Work Activity and Work Based Learning SDWP •SJS •WE by means of Work Based Learning •Job Retention •Education Fresh Success •Education 1. CFET Delivery: The method in which CFET services are provided are as follows: Provider Method of Delivery CFET SW Participants assigned to complete: •SJS are referred to SDWP Job Centers to fulfill the assignment •WE by means of Work Activity are referred to one of our community partners to fulfill the assignment SDWP SDWP delivers the following services: •SJS, Job Retention, and Education are provided in a classroom at one of San Diego County’s 6 Job Centers •WE by means of Work Based Learning is delivered through following subpartners: oInternational Rescue Committee Market Project/Mission Edge oKitchens for Good oDreams for Change County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageCalFresh Employment & Training (CFET) Components and Transportation Payments 63-903 2 of 3 oSolutions for Change oSan Diego Continuing Education Foundation oNiles Sisters oCenter for Economic Opportunity Fresh Success Education services are delivered at community colleges by means of supportive services such as career counseling, interview training, job search, placement, and retention services. Note: CalFresh recipients who chose to volunteer, can participate in one or more components concurrently. 2. CFET Summary: The diagram below provides a visual aid of the components offered by CFET SW, SDWP, and Fresh Success. 3. Transportation Allowance: CFET participants who do not have a means of transportation to commute to their assignments are eligible for transportation payments. Refer to CFET Transportation Payment Processing Guide 903- 04 for system entry instructions. Procedure: CalFresh Processing Guide 901-01 CalFresh Employment and Training Other Program Impacts: Ongoing General Relief Work Project assignments will run concurrent with the E&T WE assignment. title: 63-904 Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents Time Limit
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents Time Limit Number Page 63-904 1 of 8 Effective Date: 06/01/2026 Background: California was under a waiver from the Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs) time limit. On July 4, 2025, House of Representatives 1 (H.R. 1) was signed into Federal law. H.R. 1 limited ABAWD time limit waivers to only areas with unemployment rates above 10 percent and removed the ability for waivers to be based on lack of sufficient jobs. These changes eliminated California’s statewide ABAWD time limit waiver and California will reimplement the ABAWD time limit for non-waived counties effective June 2026. San Diego is not a waived county and will be required to implement ABAWD time limit provisions. Purpose: This section provides updated guidance on the reimplementation of the ABAWD time limit. Applications received and recertifications due on or after June 1, 2026, are required to be evaluated under the updated policy below. Policy: There are two work-related policy areas within the CalFresh program, work registration and the ABAWD time limit. An individual is considered an ABAWD if they are between the ages of 18 through 64 and able-bodied without dependent children under 14. The ABAWD time limit is separate from work registration. Screen for work registration requirements and if not exempt, then screen for an ABAWD exemption. ABAWDs may receive up to three full months of benefits in a 36-month period, unless they meet an exemption or satisfy the work requirement. 1. 36-Month Period All California counties are on a fixed 36- month period, refer to the table below for the date ranges of these periods. 36-Month Periods January 1, 2026 – December 31, 2028 January 1, 2029 – December 31, 2031 January 1, 2032 – December 31, 2034 2. Screening for ABAWD Status Before applying the ABAWD three- month time limit, evaluate individual s for exemptions. Inform households (HHs) with non -exempt ABAWDs of the ti me limit and work requirement . Screen for ABAWD exemptions at application, recertification, and whenever the HH reports that ABAWD work hours have decreased below 20 per week or 80 hours averaged monthly. ABAWD work hours may include a combination of working, volunteering, and enrollment in a school or a job training program . The screening must be clearly explained to the HH and documented in the case record. If an ABAWD meets an exemption, then they will remain exempt from the time limit until their next recertification. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents Time Limit Number Page 63-904 2 of 8 3. ABAWD Time Limit Exemptions ABAWDs meeting one or more of the exemptions below are not subject to the time limit: • Meeting a work registration exemption, refer to Section 63-901. o Please note, ABAWDs between ages 60 and 64 who are work registration exempt solely due to age must meet an additional work registration exemption. • U nder 18 or over 64 years of age. • Included in a CalFresh HH with an child under the age of 14. o The exemption may be applied to multiple HH members. o The child may be an ineligible CalFresh HH member. • Pregnant. • Participating in an Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) training program. • Indian, Urban Indian, or California Indian under the Indian Health Care Improvement Act (IHCIA). Definitions are below: o Indian: Part of an Indian Tribe, band, nation, or other organized group recognized by federal programs. o Urban Indians reside in an urban center and are one of the following:  A member of a tribe, band, or organized group.  Inuit, Aleut, or another Alaska Native.  D etermined to be an Indian under regulations issued by the: • Secretary of the Interior. • Secretary of Health and Human Services.  Note: An urban center is a community with a sufficient Urban Indian population with unmet health needs, needing assistance from the IHCIA. o California Indians are one of the following:  A member of a federally recognized Indian Tribe.  A descendent of an Indian who resided in California on June 1, 1852; a member of the Indian community served by a local Indian Health Service program; and regarded as an Indian by their community.  An Indian who holds trust interests in public domain, national forest, or reservation allotments in California.  A California Indian listed in the plans for distribution of assets of rancherias and reservations under the Act of August 18, 1958, or a descendant. • Physically or mentally unfit for employment, this includes those who: o Applied for or are receiving temporary or permanent public or private disability benefits. o Are obviously unfit for work based on staff observation. Apply this exemption if meeting the work requirement would place unnecessary burden on an individual who is clearly unfit for employment.  P otential indicators of obvious unfit ness for work include chronic homelessness, substance abuse, domestic violence, being impacted by the Child Welfare and Juvenile Justice systems. o Are determined physically or mentally unfit to work by medical or other appropriate personnel. Note: Do not document personal medical information in the case record. For verification of ABAWD exemptions, refer to Desk Aid Able- Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWD) Verifications. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents Time Limit Number Page 63-904 3 of 8 4. Work Requirement ABAWDs who do not meet an ABAWD time limit exemption must satisfy the work requirement to maintain CalFresh eligibility for more than three months in the fixed 36-month period. Each full month in which an ABAWD receives CalFresh and does not meet an ABAWD time limit exemption, the work requirement, or good cause is considered a countable month against their three-month time limit. The work requirement may be met through 20 hours per week or 80 hours monthly of qualifying activities which can include a combination of working, volunteering, and enrolling in a school or a job training program . Additionally, hours participating in qualifying CalFresh Employment and Training (CFET) activities also meet the work requirement. The table below shows the qualifying activities and number of hours that meet the work requirement. Qualifying Activities Description Working (paid, unpaid, or in-kind) At least 20 hours per week or 80 hours averaged monthly. Volunteering or community service At least 20 hours per week or 80 hours averaged monthly. Job training program At least 20 hours per week or 80 hours averaged monthly. Qualifying CFET Activity Hours are determined by CFET. ABAWDs satisfying the work requirement through self -employment must provide verification of total hours worked. Verification may include business records, written statements from individuals or organizations to which they provide service, or a collateral contact. If a collateral contact is used, document the contact’s name and phone number or email address in the case record. If self - employment hours cannot be verified through documents or collateral contact, use the ABAWD’s self - employment income to calculate the total hours using the method below: • Subtract self-employment expenses from the gross self-employment income. • Divide the adjusted income amount by the federal minimum wage. ABAWDs may voluntarily participate in CFET to satisfy their work requirement. Qualifying CFET components are tracked by the CFET Social Workers. The qualifying CFET components include: • Workfare. o Hours will be determined by the CFET Social Worker.  Assigned workfare hours apply to the entire CalFresh HH and not by individual ABAWDs. o Completion of assigned w orkfare hours will satisfy the ABAWD work requirement even if under 20 hours per week. • Work Experience. • On-the-Job Training. • Education. • Vocational Training. • Supervised Job Search (SJS). o If SJSs are completed in combination with another qualifying CFET component, up to 9 hours per week may count towards meeting the work requirement. o SJSs completed without another qualifying CFET component do not satisfy the work requirement. Please note, SJSs are considered a qualifying activity and up to 20 hours per week may count towards meeting the work requirement if they are administered through: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents Time Limit Number Page 63-904 4 of 8 • The Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA). • A program of employment and training for veterans operated by the Department of Labor or the Department of Veterans Affairs. Job training program, volunteer and community service hours may be combined with work or qualifying CFET components to meet the ABAWD work requirement. Qualifying volunteer and community service hours may be completed at a nonprofit or public institution, including religious or community organizations. Qualifying job training programs include those through the San Diego Workforce Partnership or any other program under WIOA . Additionally, activities through an approved Trade Adjustment Assistance program may be applied to the work requirement. 5. Determining Countable Months A countable month is any month in which an ABAWD subject to the time limit receives CalFresh benefits for a full month while they are not exempt, satisfying the work requirement, or meeting good cause. For additional information on good cause determinations, please review the following section. The c ounty must retroactively correct a time limit record any time during the current 36-month period when the HH provides information or verification regarding an exemption, work hours, or if staff determine there is good cause. A month is not countable if any of the following are true, the ABAWD: • Received partial or prorated CalFresh benefits. • Met an ABAWD time limit exemption for any part of the month. • S atisfied the work requirement during the month. • Is determined to have good cause. • Lived in a waived county or area. For a current list of waived counties, review the California Department of Social Services (CDSS) CalFresh Work and Community Engagement Requirements website: https://www.cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/calfresh/abawd. Review for countable months used in a 36-month period for ABAWDs who moved from other counties or states. Countable months from other California counties may be reviewed through the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) . Out of state verification of countable months and 36-month time periods may be obtained through written/printed documentation or verbal statement from a Supplemental Assistance Nutrition Program (SNAP) agency . When screening the customer, staff must discuss whether custome rs have received SNAP benefits in any other state during California’s fixed 36-month period. If an ABAWD moved from a waived county to San Diego County, then apply the time limit rules starting with the first full month of residence in San Diego following the Intercounty Transfer (ICT). Please note that when ICTs include an ABAWD as part of the CalFresh HH, the receiving county is responsible for tracking whether the participant is meeting the ABAWD work requirement starting the month of the ICT. Refer to the Intercounty Transfer (ICT) Handbook for more information on ICTs for ABAWD HHs. 6. Good Cause Determination Before applying a countable month against the ABAWD’s time limit, determine on a case-by-case basis if good cause exists for not meeting the work requirement. Good cause includes but is not limited to: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents Time Limit Number Page 63-904 5 of 8 • Illness of: o the ABAWD. o a HH member that requires the presence of the ABAWD. • A HH emergency. • A declaration of disaster. • Lack of transportation. If good cause is determined, document it in the case record. Verification is not required for good cause, the individual’s statement is acceptable unless questionable. Note: Good cause must be determined for a single month and must be redetermined if additional. 7. Mandatory Mid-Period Report ABAWD HHs have a mandatory mid-period report and must report within 10-days when ABAWD work hours decrease below 20 per week or 80 hours averaged monthly. ABAWDs in qualifying CFET components, such as workfare, will not be subject to mandatory mid-period reporting as this information is known to the county. Staff may verify an ABAWDs participation in qualifying CFET components via CFET Social Worker documentation in the CalSAWS Journal along with verification of participation hours submitted by the HH. For more information on verifying CFET components, refer to Desk Aid Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWD) Verifications . A ll other hours such as work, volunteer activities, or any other activities performed by the ABAWD must be reported when they drop below 20 hours per week or an average of 80 hours per month. When there is a re port in a reduction in ABAWD work hours, take the following steps to review if the ABAWD met: • A work registration exemption, other than the exemption of over age 59. • An ABAWD time limit exemption. • The work requirement. • Good cause criteria. If the ABAWD does not meet any of the criteria above, then review the case to determine the number of countable months that have been used within the 36- month period. If the ABAWD has not used all three countable months, then they are eligible to receive CalFresh benefits until they meet the ABAWD time limit. If the ABAWD has already received their three countable months, then discontinue the ABAWD for not satisfying the work requirement for three full countable months during the 36- month period. If timely notice cannot be applied and benefits have already been issued, an overissuance must be created. 8. Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) HHs ESAP HHs are certified for 36 months and do not require recertification interviews. However, if an ESAP HH contains members between the ages 60 through 64, then a time limit exemption screening is required. At ESAP recertification, attempt to complete the time limit exemption screening by first reviewing information available in the case record or on a completed CalFresh Time Limit Exemption Screening Form for ABAWDs (CF 377.11E). If the information provided is adequate to exempt the customer and determine ongoing eligibility, no further contact with the ESAP HH is required. If information provided is questionable or not enough information was received to exempt the ESAP HH from the ABAWD time limit or determine ongoing eligibility , then complete 3 separate attempts to County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents Time Limit Number Page 63-904 6 of 8 contact the ESAP HH and document the contact attempts in the case record. If unable to reach the ESAP HH, schedule an interview as detailed in CalFresh Program Guide 63-360. If the ESAP HH fails to complete the required interview, deny the recertification for missed interview. 9. Losing Eligibility If an ABAWD fails to satisfy the work requirement and receives all three countable months of CalFresh benefits within the 36- month period, then discontinue the ABAWD with timely notice. Establish an overissuance if the following month’s benefits have been issued. The case will remain active if the HH has other eligible members. The discontinued ABAWD will be determined an ineligible HH member, refer to CalFresh Program Guide 63-255, 63-101, and 63-201 for information regarding treatment of income and expenses, resources, and benefits. 10. Regaining Eligibility An ABAWD who was discontinued for not satisfying the work requirement will remain ineligible until the 36-month period is over unless they meet an exemption, satisfy the work requirement , or move to a waived county or area. ABAWDs who were discontinued due to receiving three full countable months in the fixed 36-month period may regain CalFresh eligibility by satisfying the work requirement for 30 consecutive days. Verification of satisfying the work requirement is required prior to granting eligibility. For more information on verifying the work requirement, review Desk Aid Able -Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWD) Verifications. The 30 consecutive day period does not need to be immediately preceding the application date but must be within the fixed 36-month period. If an ineligible ABAWD is being reinstated to an existing case, follow the policy to add a person to the HH. A new application is required when a case has discontinued. 11. Additional Three Consecutive Months of Benefits ABAWDs who were discontinued for receiving three full countable months in a 36- month period may receive an additional three consecutive months of benefits if they have: • Exhausted their three countable months and have been discontinued, then • Regained eligibility by meeting the work requirement for 30 consecutive days anytime in the fixed 36-month period, and • Subsequently stopped meeting the work requirement. The additional three consecutive months of benefits may only be used once in a 36- month period. ABAWDs must comply with all reporting and eligibility requirements while receiving the three consecutive months of benefits , including any mandatory mid- period reports, the Eligibility Status Report ( SAR 7 ), and recertification. Failure to comply with CalFresh reporting and eligibility requirements during the three consecutive months may result in discontinuance and loss of any remaining consecutive months of CalFresh benefits. Refer to the examples below regarding the eligibility determination of these months and the corresponding calendar tracking. Example 1 Scenario An ABAWD does not satisfy the work requirement for April, May, and June and receives their three full countable months in a 36-month period. CalFresh is discontinued July 1. The ABAWD gains employment, satisfies the work County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents Time Limit Number Page 63-904 7 of 8 requirement for 30 consecutive days, and regains CalFresh eligibility. The ABAWD then reports losing their job on September 1. Outcome The ABAWD is eligible for the additional three consecutive months of benefits. September, October, and November are the three additional consecutive months, and the ABAWD will discontinue December 1, unless they meet an exemption or satisfy the work requirement. 9= Inactive, N= Countable month, W= Satisfied work requirement, C= One of three additional consecutive months Example 2 Scenario The ABAWD does not satisfy the work requirement for January, February, and March and receives their three full countable months in a 36-month period. CalFresh is discontinued April 1. The ABAWD gains employment, satisfies the work requirement for 30 consecutive days, and regains CalFresh eligibility. The individual then reports they lost their job on June 20. Outcome The ABAWD is eligible for an additional three consecutive months of benefits. July, August, and September will be the three consecutive months, and the ABAWD will discontinue September 1, unless they meet an exemption or satisfy the work requirement. 9= Inactive, N= Countable month, W= Satisfied work requirement, C= One of three additional consecutive months 12. California Food Assistance Program (CFAP) Until October 1, 2027, ABAWDs receiving CFAP benefits are subject to the ABAWD time limit policy and must be tracked monthly . If an ABAWD becomes eligible to federally funded CalFresh benefits during the 36-month period, reassess their ABAWD status, and create a new 36-month calendar in the automated system separate from CFAP tracking. ABAWDs newly eligible to receive federally funded CalFresh benefits must receive a new set of three countable months, regardless of whether they previously lost eligibility due to reaching the ABAWD time limit as a CFAP recipient . Do not count previous months received under CFAP against the ABAWD’s CalFresh time limit. 13. Notices of Action (NOAs) For guidance regarding NOAs, refer to Desk Aid Able- Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWD) Client Correspondence. Administrative Hearings If an ABAWD requests an administrative hearing and they have received three countable months in the 36-month period, then with the issuance of Aid Paid Pending (APP), the third countable month must be removed, and benefits will continue until there is a hearing decision. If the result of the hearing supports the… then the… County, original third countable month is counted and any benefits received beyond that month will be considered an overissuance. sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents Time Limit Number Page 63-904 1 of 8 Effective Date: 06/01/2026 Background: California was under a waiver from the Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs) time limit. On July 4, 2025, House of Representatives 1 (H.R. 1) was signed into Federal law. H.R. 1 limited ABAWD time limit waivers to only areas with unemployment rates above 10 percent and removed the ability for waivers to be based on lack of sufficient jobs. These changes eliminated California’s statewide ABAWD time limit waiver and California will reimplement the ABAWD time limit for non-waived counties effective June 2026. San Diego is not a waived county and will be required to implement ABAWD time limit provisions. Purpose: This section provides updated guidance on the reimplementation of the ABAWD time limit. Applications received and recertifications due on or after June 1, 2026, are required to be evaluated under the updated policy below. Policy: There are two work-related policy areas within the CalFresh program, work registration and the ABAWD time limit. An individual is considered an ABAWD if they are between the ages of 18 through 64 and able-bodied without dependent children under 14. The ABAWD time limit is separate from work registration. Screen for work registration requirements and if not exempt, then screen for an ABAWD exemption. ABAWDs may receive up to three full months of benefits in a 36-month period, unless they meet an exemption or satisfy the work requirement. 1. 36-Month Period All California counties are on a fixed 36- month period, refer to the table below for the date ranges of these periods. 36-Month Periods January 1, 2026 – December 31, 2028 January 1, 2029 – December 31, 2031 January 1, 2032 – December 31, 2034 2. Screening for ABAWD Status Before applying the ABAWD three- month time limit, evaluate individual s for exemptions. Inform households (HHs) with non -exempt ABAWDs of the ti me limit and work requirement . Screen for ABAWD exemptions at application, recertification, and whenever the HH reports that ABAWD work hours have decreased below 20 per week or 80 hours averaged monthly. ABAWD work hours may include a combination of working, volunteering, and enrollment in a school or a job training program . The screening must be clearly explained to the HH and documented in the case record. If an ABAWD meets an exemption, then they will remain exempt from the time limit until their next recertification. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents Time Limit Number Page 63-904 2 of 8 3. ABAWD Time Limit Exemptions ABAWDs meeting one or more of the exemptions below are not subject to the time limit: • Meeting a work registration exemption, refer to Section 63-901. o Please note, ABAWDs between ages 60 and 64 who are work registration exempt solely due to age must meet an additional work registration exemption. • U nder 18 or over 64 years of age. • Included in a CalFresh HH with an child under the age of 14. o The exemption may be applied to multiple HH members. o The child may be an ineligible CalFresh HH member. • Pregnant. • Participating in an Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) training program. • Indian, Urban Indian, or California Indian under the Indian Health Care Improvement Act (IHCIA). Definitions are below: o Indian: Part of an Indian Tribe, band, nation, or other organized group recognized by federal programs. o Urban Indians reside in an urban center and are one of the following:  A member of a tribe, band, or organized group.  Inuit, Aleut, or another Alaska Native.  D etermined to be an Indian under regulations issued by the: • Secretary of the Interior. • Secretary of Health and Human Services.  Note: An urban center is a community with a sufficient Urban Indian population with unmet health needs, needing assis

title: 63-905 Non-Compliance
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageNon-Compliance 63-905 1 of 3 Revision Date: 01/01/2020 Background: San Diego County’s CalFresh Employment and Training (E&T) Program consists of four components, Workfare (WF), Supervised Job Search (SJS), Education and Work Experience/Apprenticeship (WE). Social Workers (SW) will make appropriate assignments to any or all components for non-exempt members of the target population. This section has been revised to remove references to UJS, and add SJS, Education and WE components. Policy: 63-905.1 Cause Determination: When a participant does not fulfill the E&T program requirements by either failing to attend the scheduled assessment interview or complete the component assignment, the SW will make a cause determination for the failure. Participants are required to notify the SW if they are unable to keep a scheduled interview or complete a component assignment. The cause determination is based on this notification or other known circumstances, including information received from the worker. If no notification or information is received, a “No Good Cause” determination will be made. 63-905.2 Good Cause: A determination of Good Cause will be made if the reason for failure to comply meets any of the following criteria: •Circumstances beyond the control of the E&T participant. Such circumstances include, but are not limited to: oIllness or incapacitation of the participant, oIllness or incapacitation of another household member which requires the presence of the participant, oA household emergency*. •Participant became exempt from the E&T work requirements. •Household moved out of the area of the E&T Program. •Cost of transportation and other expenses exceed $50 per month and are not being reimbursed by E&T. Verification of the above or similar circumstance is not required unless the household's statements are questionable. In such cases, document in the case file the reason the statement(s) was questionable, and the means used to resolve the question. It is not necessary to contact the worker unless the information is questionable or the worker needs to know the good cause reason, i.e., change of address, became exempt, temporary job that may affect CalFresh allotment. *A reasonable judgment is expected to be made as to whether the nature of a given emergency is such that it would be unreasonable to expect the participant to complete the component. A determination of No Good Cause will be made when the customer does not contact the SW or does not provide a reason for failure that meets “Good Cause”. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageNon-Compliance 63-905 2 of 3 Aid Paid Pending: When a participant appeals an E&T disqualification and aid is paid pending the hearing, the participant's E&T case will remain closed. When the hearing decision is received, the Work Experience Appeals Liaison will forward a copy to the SW for action. Procedure: Notification: After determining that the participant had “No Good Cause” for failing to complete the component assignment, notify the E&T Liaison of the CalFresh office of record via email that the customer has been dropped from the program. Also enter an “S” code in the Good Cause column of the E&T/Work Project Spreadsheet. The cause determination by the SW is the final determination. The worker has no responsibility in determining whether or not the finding is correct. If there is pertinent information not previously communicated to the SW, the worker is to notify the SW immediately so the removal of the participant from the program can be re-evaluated. If no additional information is available, the worker will enter a case comment that the customer has been dropped from the program and will no longer participate in E&T. Ending a Disqualification Period: Participation in E&T is voluntary; therefore, individuals are not sanctioned for non-compliance. Participants who are non-compliant will remain registered for E&T but will be dropped from the program. Sanctioning of CalWORKs/CalFresh Households: When a public assistance CalFresh household member is sanctioned for not cooperating with CalWORKs Welfare to Work requirements, the participant will also be disqualified from CalFresh unless they meet another exemption (see 63-901.3). Send an appropriate NOA to the Household when they are disqualified from participating. (See processing Guide 905-01 Length of Disqualification Period: As the program is voluntary, participants are not sanctioned for non-compliance with the E&T Program. However, if an individual failed to comply with the work requirements of a substitute program (CalWORKs), and does not meet another CalFresh work requirement exemption, the person must be disqualified from CalFresh for one, three, or six months, depending on the instance of non-compliance. Instance of Non-Compliance Length of Disqualification First Instance 1 month Second Instance 3 months Third Instance 6 months Disqualifications applied to a Closed Case: Disqualify individuals who are determined to be subject to the disqualification even if the person or case is discontinued for another reason. In these situations, the worker will send the appropriate work disqualification NOA. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Number PageNon-Compliance 63-905 3 of 3 Ending the Disqualification Period: After the worker has imposed a work registration disqualification, the disqualified individual may regain eligibility by: •Reapplying; and •Being otherwise eligible to CalFresh; and •Agreeing to comply/complying with the work registration requirements; or •Becoming exempt to the requirements of the work registration program. Other Program Impacts: No Impacts References: MPP 63-407 Work Registration Requirements CFR 273.7 Work Provisions ACL 10-11 Elimination of FS Sanctions for Non-Compliance with GR Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 12/31/2022 Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Eligibility Operations

title: SN 18-02 Treatment Of Child Support Payments Issued In Error
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh Program Guide Special Notice Treatment Of Child Support Payments Issued In Error Number Page CalWORKs 18-02 CalFresh 18-02 1 of 2 Issue Date: 02/05/18 Background: During the Maximum Family Grant (MFG) repeal clean-up process, a consortium sent old eligibility dates and case data to the Child Support Enforcement (CSE) System, overwriting current eligibility dates and case data. This has caused some current Assistance Units (AUs) to receive child support payments rather than only the $50 disregard payment. In other situations , the incorrect data has caused child support payments to be retained by the Department of Child Support Services (DCSS) when it should have been issued to the family. Policy: Child Support Received in Error Child support payments issued in error cannot be counted against the AU’s grant unless the county has reliable information from the CSE/LCSA staff that the payments can be reasonably anticipated or the county is certain they will continue to occur. $50 Child Support Disregard Retained by the State in Error The State will issue child support disregards, retained by DCSS in error, to the affected AUs as soon as the cases have been identified or the clean-up process is completed. The retroactive disregard paid as lump sum will not be treated as income or property. Note: This only applies to any $50 chil d support disregard that was collected by the State beginning January 1, 2017. Any disregard retained before January 1, 2017 do not fall under this change. Procedure: • If an AU receives one or two child support payments, the payments will not be considered as reasonably anticipated income and will not be used to determine grant calculations. • However, when more than one payment is received , reach out to the LCSA to determine if the payments will continue and can be reasonably anticipated. • If it is determined the payments can be reasonably anticipated, recalculate the AU’s grant applying the $50 child support disregard, and treat the remaining child support payment as unearned income. Note: The AU has the option of returning the child support payment to prevent the payment from being counted against the grant. Program Impacts: CalFresh • The child support payments (received in error) cannot be reasonably anticipated; therefore these payments cannot be counted in the budget. (CFPG 63-282.3). • The $50.00 child support disregard payments received by C alWORKs recipients will count in the budget, if they will continue, and can be reasonably anticipated (CFPG 63-223.5). • Retroactive Lump Sum payments would be counted as resources in the month received (CFPG 63-224.10). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh Program Guide Special Notice Treatment Of Child Support Payments Issued In Error Number Page CalWORKs 18-02 CalFresh 18-02 2 of 2 Note: The resources of Categorically Eligible (CE) or Modified Catego rical Eligible (MCE) households are not evaluated to determine eligibility to CalFresh (CFPG 63- 201.1, 63-203.13, 63- 120). References: All County Welfare Directors Letter, dated December 28, 2017. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by February 28, 2019. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations

Purpose: This notice provides staff with an overview of the COLA changes and instructions for implementation. Policy: The following changes are part of the FFY 2020 COLA: ITEM CHANGE Allotments Maximum Allotments increased and can be found on the CalFresh Assistance Standards Chart Income Eligibility Standards Income Eligibility Standards increased and can be found on the CalFresh Assistance Standards Chart Shelter Deduction The Excess Shelter Deduction increased from $569 to $586 Standard Deduction The Standard Deduction Amoun ts increased according to the Eligible CalFresh Household size as follows: • 1 – 3 Eligible household members = $167 • 4 Eligible household members = $181 • 5 Eligible household members = $212 • 6 or more Eligible household members = $243 Homeless Household S helter Allowance The Homeless Household S helter Allowance increased from $152 to $156 Standard Utility Allowance (SUA) The SUA amount increased from $432 to $438 Limited Utility Allowance (LUA) The LUA amount increased from $135 to $139 The following were NOT changed as part of the FFY 2021 COLA: • The Minimum Allotment remained unchanged at $16; • Resource limits remain unchanged: o $3,500 for households that include an elderly or disabled (E/D) member, and o $2,250 for all other households. • Telephone Utility Allowance (TUA) – The TUA amount remained the same at $18. RICK WANNE, Director Eligibility Operations NOTICE TO ALL CALFRESH RECIPIENTS IMPORTANT PLEASE READ The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) has approved a Cost of Living Allowance to the CalFresh program. Effective October 1, 20 20, your CalFresh benefits may change due to this federal law change. • The Maximum Allotments increased. • The Maximum Excess Shelter cost deduction increased from $569 to $586. • The Gross/Net Income Eligibility Standards increased. • The Standard Utility Allowance (SUA) deduction increased from $432 to $438. • The Standard Deduction increased according to your household size (an increase to $167 for 1 to 3 people; $181 for 4 people; $212 for 5 people; and $2 43 for 6 or more people). With the changes , the amount of CalFresh benefits you will get depends on your household status. You will get a notice if your CalFresh benefits change. If you think we made a mistake in figuring your October 2020 allotment because of the federal law change, you may ask for a state hearing within 90 days of the date you received this information by: Writing to: San Diego County Health and Human Services Agency Appeals Section –W402 1255 Imperial Avenue Suite 300 San Diego, CA 92101 OR Calling toll free: 1-800-952-5253. If you are hearing impaired and use TDD, please call 1-800-952-8349. When you ask for a hearing you must tell us why you believe we made a mistake. You may speak for yourself at the state hearing. You can have a friend, attorney or other person speak for you . You may ask for free legal aid at the Legal Aid Society of San Diego office in your area. You can speak for yourself at the hearing or you can have a friend, attorney, or other person speak for you. If you need someone to speak for you, you must get someone to help you. You may ask for free legal aid at a legal aid office in your area.
