title: SN 24-04 Implementation of the New Statewide Minimum Wage
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide Special Notice Implementation of the New Statewide Minimum Wage Number Page CW 24-04 CF 24-04 GR 24-03 1 of 2 Effective Date: January 1, 2025 Background: Employees in California are required to be paid the minimum wage as required by state law, with certain exemptions. The current California minimum wage is $16.00 per hour. Purpose: To inform staff of the increase in the statewide minimum wage and its impact on CalWORKs, CalFresh, Employment Services, CalFresh Employment & Training, and General Relief Work Project assignment and credit. Policy: Effective January 1, 202 5, the California minimum wage will increase to $1 6.50 per hour. Refer to CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 44-270.F and CalFresh Program Guide (CFPG) 63-251 for guidance on Prospective Budgeting and Reasonably Anticipated Income . See General Relief Program Guide (GRPG) 90-700.8 for General Relief Work Project assignment and credit. Procedure: CalWORKs and CalFresh Programs Individuals are expected to report income reflecting the minimum wage increase beginning in the SAR 7 data month of January 2025 or Redetermination/Recertification/Renewal (RRR) month of February 2025. Customers are required to report mid -period when their income exceeds their Income Reporting Threshold (IRT). If the customer reports a pay increase prior to January 1, 2025, use current reporting regulations to determine when the change of income should be used in the budget. Refer to CPG 44- 270.G and CFPG 63-283 for further guidance on Mandatory Mid-Period Reports and refer to CPG 44- 270.H and CFPG 63-284 on Voluntary Mid-Period Reports. Employment Services Employment Case Managers (ECMs) must perform the Simplified CalFresh Program (SCFP) calculation to determine the maximum number of hours that a participant can be required to participate in a Work Experience (WEX) or Community Service (CS) assignment. ECMs must continue using the minimum wage of $1 6.00 when completing such a calculation through December 31, 202 4. Refer to CPG 10-050.A and CalWORKs Processing Guide No. 10-050.A1 for further guidance. General Relief Work Project Work Project assignments are determined by dividing the net CalFresh allotment by the federal or state minimum wage, whichever is higher. As the current California minimum wage is higher than the federal minimum wage, use the new California minimum wage for the number of Work Project days assigned effective January 2025 and ongoing. For example: A single employable customer living alone with no income will receive the maximum CalFresh allotment of $ 292 ÷ $16.50 = 17.69. The customer will be assigned 16 hours and the remaining time will still show as an amount owed to the county when the case closes. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide Special Notice Implementation of the New Statewide Minimum Wage Number Page CW 24-04 CF 24-04 GR 24-03 2 of 2 The credit for Work Project hours completed is determined by multiplying the number of hours worked by the current federal or state minimum wage, whichever is higher. For example: Using the example above, the customer worked 16 hours each month. 16 hours x $16.50 = $264 repaid per month. Please refer to Attachment A for a reference table of the number of Work Project days to be assigned based on the corresponding CalFresh allotment amounts. Impacts: None. References: All County Information Notice (ACIN) No. I-41-24. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by January 31, 2026. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services ATTACHMENT A GENERAL RELIEF WORK PROJECT DAYS Work Project Days Assigned CalFresh Allotment 0 Days $0 - $131 1 Day $132 - $263 2 Days $264 - $292

title: SN 24-05 Social Security Administration - COLA FFY 2025
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide/CalFresh Program Guide Special Notice Social Security Administration - Cost of Living Adjustment Number Page CalWORKs 24-05 CalFresh 24-05 1 of 2 Effective Date: January 1, 2025 Background: Social Security Administration ( SSA) recipients will receive a 2.5 percent Cost-of-Living-Adjustment (COLA) effective December 31, 2024, and payable January 1, 2025. In addition, starting January 2025 the Medicare Part B premium will increase to $185 per month. Policy: New Applicants The actual amount of the SS A benefit, including the COLA increase, must be used for eligibility and budgeting purposes beginning in January 2025. The SS A amount budgeted for January will be considered reasonably anticipated income for applications received in November and December 2024. Treatment of SSA COLA for Ongoing Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) Customers The SSA COLA is considered a mid -period county-initiated action. As a result, a decrease in CalWORKs/CalFresh benefits may occur effective January 1, 2025, with timely and adequate notice. Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) Requirements CalWORKs customers are required to report if the increase in SSA benefits combined with earned income, results in exceeding their IRT. If income exceeding the IRT is reported an evaluation is required to determine if the customer is still eligible to benefits. If CalWORKs discontinues due to exceeding the IRT, the CalFresh households (HH) is eligible to Transitional CalFresh (TCF). CalFresh HH must report if the increase in SSA benefits combined with all other income the HH receives results in exceeding their IRT. If income exceeding the IRT is report ed an evaluation is required to determine if the HH is still eligible to benefits. Treatment of SSA COLA for CalWORKs Annual Reporting/Child Only (AR/CO) Cases The only cases where this action will not be considered mid -period are those AR/CO cases with a December 202 4 redetermination. For those cases, include the updated SSA benefit amount in budgeting for the upcoming AR/CO period. Timely and Adequate Notice As with any adverse action, timely and adequate notice is required to decrease benefits . If unable to change the January 2025 CalWORKs grant/CalFresh allotment, take the appropriate action to decrease benefits the first of the following month after timely adequate notice can be provided. Recalculate January 2025 benefits using the increased SSA benefits and Medicare Part B premium amounts; and if the calculation results in a decrease, an overpayment/overissuance will need to be established as appropriate. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide/CalFresh Program Guide Special Notice Social Security Administration - Cost of Living Adjustment Number Page CalWORKs 24-05 CalFresh 24-05 2 of 2 Procedure: The automatic adjustment will not occur on cases where there was a discrepancy. Case list reports requiring action will be shared when available. Policy: New Applicants The actual amount of SSI/SSP benefits , including the COLA adjustment, must be used for eligibility and budgeting purposes beginning in January 2025. The SSI/SSP amount budgeted for January will be considered reasonably anticipated income for applications received in January 2025. Ongoing Households (HHs) SSI/SSP COLA updates are considered verified upon receipt (VUR). The Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) perform s a data match against CalSAWS to produce a file with the updated SSI/SSP payment amounts due to the COLA adjustment. Based on the information received SSI/SSP payment amounts were updated accordingly: If an SSI/SSP recipient’s… then the SSI/SSP payment amounts were… ELIGIBLE amount is less than or equal to their PAID amount, adjusted to the ELIGIBLE amount automatically in CalSAWS on January 11, 2025. Changes to the HH’s benefit allotment will take effect February 2025. PAID amount is less than their ELIGIBLE amount or their SSI/SSP benefits could not be matched, not automatically updated in CalSAWS. SSI/SSP payment amounts must be adjusted at the next Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7) or recertification, whichever comes first. A PAID amount that is less than the ELIGIBLE amount indicates a possible recoupment . The reason for the recoupment must be explored at SAR 7 or recertification, whichever comes first, and the SSI/SSP income must be included in the budget as follows: If the recoupment is due to… then use the following SSI/SSP amount in the budget… an SSI/SSP overpayment, the PAID amount. any other reason, the ELIGIBLE amount. title: SN 25-03 -Social Security Administration (SSA) Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA) -2026
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide/CalFresh/Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice Social Security Administration – Cost-of-Living Adjustment Number Page CalWORKs 25-04 CalFresh 25-03 Medi-Cal 25-07 1 of 3 Effective Date: January 1, 2026 Background: Social Security Administration ( SSA) recipients will receive a 2.8 percent Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) effective December 31, 2025, and payable January 1, 2026. In addition, starting January 2026 the Medicare Part B premium will increase to $202.90 per month. Policy: New Applicants The actual amount of the SS A benefit, including the COLA increase, must be used for eligibility and budgeting purposes beginning in January 202 6. The SS A budgeted amount for January will be considered reasonably anticipated income for applications received in November and December 2025. Treatment of SSA COLA for Ongoing Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) Customers The SSA COLA is considered a mid- period county-initiated action. As a result, a decrease in CalWORKs/CalFresh benefits may occur effective January 1, 2026, with timely and adequate notice. Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) Requirements CalWORKs customers are required to report if the increase in SSA benefits combined with earned income results in exceeding their IRT. If income exceeding the IRT is reported an evaluation is required to determine if the customer is still eligible to benefits. If CalWORKs discontinues due to exceeding the IRT, the CalFresh households (HH) are eligible to Transitional CalFresh (TCF). CalFresh HHs must report if the increase in SSA benefits combined with all other income receive d results in exceeding the HH’s IRT. If income exceeding the IRT is report ed, then an evaluation is required to determine if the HH is still eligible to benefits. Treatment of SSA COLA for CalWORKs Annual Reporting/Child Only (AR/CO) Cases The only cases where this action will not be considered mid- period are those AR/CO cases with a December 2025 redetermination. For those cases, include the updated SSA benefit amount in budgeting for the upcoming AR/CO period. Timely and Adequate Notice As with any adverse action, timely and adequate notice is required to decrease benefits . If unable to change the January 2026 CalWORKs grant/CalFresh allotment, take the appropriate action to decrease benefits the first of the following month after timely adequate notice can be provided. Recalculate January 2026 benefits using the increased SSA benefits and Medicare Part B premium amounts; and if the calculation results in a decrease, an overpayment/overissuance will need to be established as appropriate. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide/CalFresh/Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice Social Security Administration – Cost-of-Living Adjustment Number Page CalWORKs 25-04 CalFresh 25-03 Medi-Cal 25-07 2 of 3 Treatment of SSA COLA for Non-MAGI Medi-Cal Eligibility Groups The increase will not be applied to the Aged, Blind, and Disabled Federal Poverty Level (ABD FPL) and Medicare Savings Programs (MSPs) until April 1, 2026. Effective January 1, 2026, all medically needy cases with Title II income must have the share of cost (SOC) adjusted to reflect the COLA. Medicare Part B Disregard the income equal to the amount of the customer’s Medicare Part B premium when determining eligibility for the ABD FPL program, regardless of the state’s payment of the premium. This income disregard is applied to the budget as long as the countable income remains within the ABD FPL program limits. Note: Customers who are evaluated as Medically Needy (MN) must pay the premium before receiving the deduction. Procedure: When updating the SSA benefit amount the calculation is to be completed as follows: When Medicare Part B is not paid by the customer: Step Action 1 Use the previous SSA Title II benefit amount. 2 Multiply the amount by 1.028. 3 Round down to the next lower dollar (remove the cents). 4 Final amount will be the new anticipated SSA benefit amount. When Medicare Part B is paid for by the customer: Step Action 1 Add the 2005 Part B premium ($185) to the 2024 net Title II benefit amount. 2 Multiply the amount by 1.028. 3 Round down to the next lower dollar (remove the cents). 4 Subtract the 2026 Part B premium and round down to the next lower whole dollar. 5 Final amount will be the new anticipated SSA benefit amount. Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 11.1A Assistance Standards for updated premium values. Impacts: Automation A COLA mass update will run on December 6, 2025, automatically adjusting SSA benefit amounts and Medicare Part B premiums for open SSA and Medicare expense records in CalSAWS. On December 13, 202 5, a batch Eligibility Determination Benefit Calculation (EDBC) run will occur and effective January 2026 CalWORKs/CalFresh benefits will reflect the SSA benefit and Medicare premium increases. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide/CalFresh/Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice Social Security Administration – Cost-of-Living Adjustment Number Page CalWORKs 25-04 CalFresh 25-03 Medi-Cal 25-07 3 of 3 The automatic adjustment will not occur on cases where there was a discrepancy including manual overrides. Case list reports requiring action will be shared when available. Cases not included in the COLA run will require staff to manually update the information in the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) to reflect in the January 2026 benefits. Other Programs Affected The SSA COLA also applies to Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) and Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program (TCVAP). References: All County Information Notice (ACIN) No. I-56-25. All County Welfare Directors Letter (ACWDL) 25-22, 25-26. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by December 31, 2026. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: SN 25-04 Joint SN Implementation of the New Statewide Minimum Wage
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide Special Notice Implementation of the New Statewide Minimum Wage Number Page CW 25-05 CF 25-04 GR 25-01 1 of 2 Effective Date: January 1, 2026 Background: Employees in California are required to be paid the minimum wage as required by state law, with certain exemptions. The current California minimum wage is $16.50 per hour. Purpose: To inform staff of the increase in the statewide minimum wage and its impact on CalWORKs, CalFresh, Employment Services, CalFresh Employment & Training (CFET), and General Relief Work Project assignment and credit. Policy: Effective January 1, 2026 , the California minimum wage will increase to $1 6.90 per hour. Refer to CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 44-270.F and CalFresh Program Guide (CFPG) 63-251 for guidance on Prospective Budgeting and Reasonably Anticipated Income. See General Relief Program Guide (GRPG) 90-700.8 for General Relief Work Project assignment and credit. Procedure: CalWORKs and CalFresh Programs Individuals are expected to report income reflecting the minimum wage increase beginning in the Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7) data month of January 2026 or the Redetermination/Recertification (RE) month of February 2026. Customers are required to report mid- period when their income exceeds their Income Reporting Threshold (IRT). If the customer reports a pay increase prior to January 1, 2026, use current reporting regulations to determine when the change of income should be used in the budget. For further guidance on: • Mandatory Mid-Period Reports refer to CPG 44-270.C and CFPG 63-283. • Voluntary Mid-Period Reports refer to CPG 44-270.H and CFPG 63-284. Employment Services Employment Case Managers (ECMs) must perform the Simplified CalFresh Program (SCFP) calculation to determine the maximum number of hours that a participant can be required to participate in a Work Experience (WEX) or Community Service (CS) assignment. ECMs must continue us ing the minimum wage of $1 6.50 when completing such a calculation through December 31, 202 5. Refer to CPG 10-050.A and CalWORKs Processing Guide No. 10-050.A1 for further guidance. CalFresh Employment & Training and General Relief Work Project Work Project assignments are determined by dividing the net CalFresh allotment by the federal or state minimum wage, whichever is higher. title: SN 26-01 Supplemental Security Income (SSI) and State Supplementary Payment (SSP) Cost of Living Adjustment
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Special Notice Supplemental Security Income (SSI) and State Supplementary Payment (SSP) Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) Number Page CalFresh 26-01 1 of 2 Effective Date: 02/01/2026 Background: SSI/SSP recipients received a COLA effective January 1, 2026. Purpose: SSI and SSP recipients receive a COLA Adjustment annually. This notice provides update and guidance on applying the 2026 COLA adjustment for initial applications and ongoing cases that failed the batch process. Policy: New Applicants The actual amount of SSI/SSP benefits , including the COLA adjustment, must be used for eligibility and budgeting purposes. The SSI/SSP amount budgeted for January will be considered reasonabl y anticipated income for applications received in January 2026. Ongoing Households (HHs) SSI/SSP COLA updates are considered Verified Upon Receipt (VUR). The Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) conducts a data match against the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) to produce a file with the updated SSI/SSP payment amounts due to the COLA adjustment. Based on the information received, SSI/SSP payment amounts were updated during the batch process on January 8, 2026. Ongoing Transitional CalFresh (TCF) Cases TCF cases containing an SSI/SSP recipient had their payment amounts automatically adjusted in CalSAWS on January 8, 2026. The new payment amounts must be counted in the budget at the end of the TCF certification period after the HH recertifies to regular CalFresh benefits. Other Public Assistance Record Not Updated The SSI-SSP Excluded Other Public Assistance Records Report will be generated monthly to assist in identifying cases with an Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7) or recertification due. This report will continue to be generated until all excluded cases have been reviewed and updated. Based on the information received SSI/SSP payment amounts were updated accordingly: If an SSI/SSP recipient’s… then the payments were… eligible amount is less than or equal to the paid amount, updated to the eligible amount automatically. Changes to the HH’s benefit allotment will take effect February 2026. paid amount is less than their eligible amount (or their SSI/SSP benefits could not be matched), not updated in CalSAWS. Review and update the payment amounts at the next Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7) or recertification, whichever comes first. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Special Notice Supplemental Security Income (SSI) and State Supplementary Payment (SSP) Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) Number Page CalFresh 26-01 2 of 2 A paid amount that is less than the e ligible amount indicates a possible recoupment. The reason for the recoupment must be reviewed at the next SAR 7 or recertification, whichever comes first, and the SSI/SSP income must be included in the budget as follows: If the recoupment is due to… then use the following amount in the budget… an SSI/SSP overpayment, the paid amount. any other reason, the eligible amount. Procedure: The following case list reports along with instructions on action to take will be shared: • Cases Excluded from SSI COLA. • Programs Discontinued by the Batch EDBC Process. • Cases Where Batch EDBC Process Closed a Person. • Unprocessed Cases Where Batch EDBC Process Skipped a Program. • SSI-SSP OPA Record Not Updated – this is sent as a monthly report. References: All County Information Notice (ACIN) I-74-22, I-74-22E, I-56-25. Sunset Date: 12/31/2026 Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph. D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: SN 26-02 Joint Special Notice - Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) Outreach 2026
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach Number Page CW 26-01 CF 26-02 MC 26-02 GR 26-01 CAPI 26-01 CMS 26-01 1 of 4 Effective Date: March 1, 2026 Background: San Diego County’s Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) campaign provide s outreach which is intended to provide customers with information to access potentially eligible tax credits, free tax preparation, and other filing services and resources. EITC payments and credits may have impact to Self -Sufficiency Services (SSS) programs such as California Work Opportunity and Responsibility for Kids (CalWORKs), CalFresh, Medi -Cal, General Relief (GR), Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants (CAPI) and County Medical Services (CMS). Purpose: To provide guidance on treatment of EITC payments and credits for SSS programs and outreach resources available for eligibility staff to provide to customers who are potentially eligible to tax credits, free tax preparation, and other filing services and resources. Policy: Treatment of Income from EITC EITC payments are exempt for CalWORKs, CalFresh, CAPI, Medi-Cal and CMS. For General Relief , EITC payments are counted as unearned income in the month received. If a customer received GR during 2025, and the customer receives the EITC, review the case for potential unreported earnings since EITC is for earned income. EITC related payments and credits that customers may receive are EITC, CalEITC, Foster Youth Tax Credit (FYTC), Expanded Young Child Tax Credit (EYCTC). Treatment of Property from EITC payments The table below outlines the treatment of Property for payments received from EITC. Program Treatment of Property CalWORKs and CalFresh Exempt resources for 12 months, starting with the month that the payment is received. Medi-Cal EITC payments are exempt as property in the month following the month of receipt. General Relief Refund retained by the customer in the month following receipt is considered personal property. CAPI EITC payments are exempt as property in the month following the month of receipt. CMS Any portion of the refund retained by the beneficiary in the month following receipt is considered exempt personal property. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach Number Page CW 26-01 CF 26-02 MC 26-02 GR 26-01 CAPI 26-01 CMS 26-01 2 of 4 Procedure: FRCs and ES Staff If customers report EITC payments or credits, treat the income and property as listed in this notice. Distribute the EITC postcards to c ustomers at all contacts and encourage them to contact 2 -1-1 to receive free assistance with filing their taxes and claim available tax credits. If additional postcards are needed, they can be ordered through XEROX printing services. References: All County Information Notice (ACIN) No. I-01-26 Resources: CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 44-100.C and 44-100.H2 CalFresh Program Guide (CFPG) 63-203 and 63-204. Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 09.06.01,10.02.01 and Desk Aid 56 MAGI Eligibility Groups and Aid Codes General Relief Program Guide (GRPG) 90-400.5F CAPI Program Guide (CAPI) PG 99-103.2B and 99-104.4B CMS Program Guide (CMSPG) 06.01.02A and 06.04.03H Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by March 31, 2027. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services Appendix A Appendix B Appendix B

title: SN 21-03 Suspected Unemployment Insurance Fraud and Identity Theft Information
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Suspected Unemployment Insurance Fraud and Identity Theft Information Number Page CW 21-03, CF 21-03, MC 21-03, GR 21-02, CAPI 21-02, CMS 21-02 1 of 3 Effective Date: February 12, 2021 Background: The State has received reports from customers who are stating that Unemployment Insurance Benefits (UIB) claims were filed using their personal identifying information without their knowledge or consent. Purpose: To provide guidance on information to be provided to customers when it is suspected someone else has used their personal identifying information to collect UIB. Policy: Employment Development Department (EDD) Benefit Fraud EDD benefit fraud is when individuals knowingly give false or misleading information to collect Disability Insurance Benefits (DIB), Paid Family Leave (PFL), or UIB they are not entitled to. Examples of EDD benefit fraud include: • Using another person’s identity (for example: name, social security number) to file a fraudulent claim • Stealing someone’s mail, which is a federal crime, and cashing their benefit payments • Working while collecting UIB, and not reporting it to the EDD • Aiding someone in filing a fraudulent claim • Falsifying information or failing to disclose information • Failing to accurately report hours of work and earnings • Not reporting cash wages • Certifying for UIB while intentionally reporting job search activities that were not actual performed • Failing to be able and available for work (for example: out of the area, on vacation) while certifying for UIB • Faking an illness or injury while collecting DIB or PFL benefits • Falsifying medical information to collect DIB or PFL benefits Procedure: County Information Notice • This notice has been created to provide customers with resources and information on how to contact the proper agencies when they suspect someone has used their personal identifying information to gain benefits unlawfully • The notice may also be sent to the customer in conjunction with any case verifications being requested to verify unclear information related to UIB issued in the customer’s name reported on a potentially discrepant Payment Verification System (PVS) Income Eligibility Verification System (IEVS) match • The notice, or the information provided in this special notice, also can be used to inform customers of their options when there is suspected UIB fraud or identity theft by another individual using personal information to apply for and receive benefits unlawfully from the EDD, Social Security Administration (SSA) or the County County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Suspected Unemployment Insurance Fraud and Identity Theft Information Number Page CW 21-03, CF 21-03, MC 21-03, GR 21-02, CAPI 21-02, CMS 21-02 2 of 3 Suspected Unemployment Insurance Fraud and Identity Theft In cases of identity theft, the Human Services Specialist (HSS) will not require the customer to provide any other proof, such as a police report or specific documents from the EDD to resolve any reporting discrepancies. A signed affidavit/electronic signature is an acceptable verification for resolving these reporting discrepancies. You can also fax 1-866-340-5484 or call the Employment Development Department (EDD) Fraud Hotline at 1-800-229-6297. • If someone applied for Social Security Income benefits under your name, you can file a report online at oig.ssa.gov. • If someone applied for Medi-Cal, CalWORKs or CalFresh under your name, you should report this to your county welfare office. When contacting EDD to report fraud, please provide as much information as you can, such as: • Who is committing fraud? • What is their address and telephone number? • What is their Social Security number or employer number? • What are they doing? • When did they start doing this? • What is your name, address, and phone number? (Optional) You may remain anonymous if you prefer. If you think you are a victim of identity theft, you can take steps to protect yourself. • Get a free copy of your credit report at freecreditreport.com and report errors to the major credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian and TransUnion). • Contact your creditors and let them know someone may have stolen your information. • File a complaint with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC). You can file a complaint with the FTC and get an individual recovery plan at www.identitytheft.gov. • File a report with local police or law enforcement. • Get legal help. Your local legal aid may be able to help you with problems related to identity theft. The County may be able to give you information on local legal aid organizations. • Get more information about your rights at oag.ca.gov/idtheft. _________________________________________________________________________________________________

title: SN 21-06 CalWORKs Time-On-Aid Good Cause Time Limit Exemption
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Special Notice Number PageCalWORKs Time-On-Aid Good Cause Time Limit Exemption 21-06 1 of 2 Effective Date: July 1, 2021 Background: Executive Orders (EOs) N-29-20, N-69-20 and N-75-20 provided relief to families during the COVID- 19 pandemic by exempting months of aid from counting towards the CalWORKs 48-month time limit. The exemption was effective from March 4, 2020 through June 30, 2021. Under the EO guidance, exemptions were given to all current CalWORKs customers who had not reached their CalWORKs 48- month time limit and had not exceeded their TANF 60-month time limit. The exemption criteria also applied to customers who reached their TANF 60-month time limit (but not exceeded) if they had not exhausted their CalWORKs 48-month time limit. Purpose: The purpose of this material is to provide guidance to implement the provision in Assembly Bill (AB) 128 that extends the COVID-19 Good Cause time limit exemption to aided CalWORKs adults. The time limit exemption is effective July 1, 2021 through the implementation of the 60-month CalWORKs time limit. Policy: Under AB 128, effective July 1, 2021, all current CalWORKs customers (aided adults) who have not reached their CalWORKs 48-month time limit are eligible to receive the COVID-19 AB 128 exemption regardless of their TANF time limit. Refer to the illustration below: CalWORKs Time Clock TANF Time Clock Is the customer eligible to receive the COVID-19 AB 128 exemption? 40 42 Yes, the customer is under the CalWORKs 48-month time limit 45 60 Yes, the customer is under the CalWORKs 48-month time limit 48 60 No, the customer already reached the CalWORKs 48-month time limit. Customer is considered CalWORKs timed-out and is no longer eligible to received CalWORKs unless the customer meets a time limit extender. Customers with a time limit extender are not eligible for the COVID-19 AB 128 exemption. 40 61 Yes, the customer is under the CalWORKs 48-month time limit Procedure: Automation CalWIN will continue to run the monthly Structured Query Language (SQL) to update cases with Exemption 407- Lack of Supportive Services to the 48-Month Time Clocks. As of July 1, 2021, CalWIN updates are functioning as designed and manual corrections to these exemptions do not need to be made. Any cases identified that require manual correction will be issued by Automation or CalWORKs Program for appropriate action. Time-On-Aid (TOA) Reviews Human Services Specialist (HSS) must continue to conduct TOA reviews and inform customers of their TOA: •At intake County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Special Notice Number PageCalWORKs Time-On-Aid Good Cause Time Limit Exemption 21-06 2 of 2 •At each annual redetermination •Upon customer’s request •On the 42 nd, between 42nd and 46th and on the 48th month of aid and •After reaching the 48 th month, if their children remain on aid and child support or overpayment recoupment reimburses month(s) of aid. If the customer’s time clock is inaccurate, HSS are required to correct the clock(s) and apply the exemption if applicable. Program Impact/s: Forms and Document Capture The Time on Aid Verification for CalWORKs/TANF 48-Month Time Limits (CW 2191) form is available in the Eligibility Forms Library (EFL). The CW 2191 may be used as a job aid to complete the TOA reviews. References: ACWDL dated: March 27, 2020, June 16, 2020 and August 31, 2020 ACL 21-82 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by July 30, 2023. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self Sufficiency Services

title: SN 21-08 Overpayments Incurred during the COVID-19 Pandemic Emergency
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Special Notice Overpayments Incurred During the COVID-19 Pandemic Emergency Number Page 21-08 1 of 2 Effective Date: September 1, 2021 Background: Assembly Bill (AB) 135 was passed in order to implement a new CalWORKs overpayment policy to help lessen the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic emergency on CalWORKs families due to overpayments. Purpose: The purpose of this material is to provide guidance to staff on new overpayment policies and procedures as a result of AB 135 and to provide an overview of current overpayment policies. Policy: AB 135 Effective August 1, 2021, all nonfraudulent CalWORKs overpayments established on or after August 1, 2021, for the benefit months of April 2020 through the end of the COVID-19 pandemic emergency or June 30, 2022 (whichever is sooner) must be classified as administrative-error (AE). Overpayment claims established after August 1, 2021 that include any months during the COVID-19 pandemic emergency period beginning in April 2020, must be classified as AE regardless of case circumstances. For example, an overpayment claim established for the semi-annual payment period starting in November 2019 - April 2020 must be established as AE because the overpayment claim includes the overpaid month of April 2020. An overpayment classified as an AE under this policy cannot be reclassified to client error if it is nonfraudulent. Definition and Calculation of Overpayments An overpayment is any amount of any aid payment received by and Assistance Unit (AU) that they were not entitled to receive. An overpayment may be all, or a portion, of the payment. This includes payments issued for regular aid payment, Immediate Need, Homeless Assistance, Aid Paid Pending (APP) for a state hearing, or Employment Services (ES). Human Services Specialists (HSS) need to take all reasonable steps necessary to promptly correct and collect any overpayments that are known to the county including recovery of overpayments due to either client error or AE. The amount of any CalWORKs grant overpayment is the difference between the grant amount the AU received, and the grant amount the AU would have received under Semi-Annual reporting (SAR), annual reporting/child on (AR/CO), and the prospective budgeting system if no county error had occurred and if the customer had timely, completely, and accurately reported as required by SAR and AR/CO rules. AE Overpayments and Grant Adjustment An AE overpayment is an overpayment caused by error on the part of the county staff when all information necessary to make a correct grant determination was in possession of the county. AE overpayments are recouped by reducing the Maximum Aid Payment (MAP) amount for the AU by five percent rounded to the next lower dollar. Grant adjustment recoupments: • For SAR AUs must only be collected at the beginning of the SAR payment period • M ust be discontinued mid-period when the overpayment debt is paid in full • Collection of a new overpayments claim may begin mid-period by grant adjustment if the amount of the new collection is less than or equal to the amount previously collected • AR/CO only: recoupment of new overpayment claims can begin mid-period even when the collected amount results in decreases to the CalWORKs grant mid-period County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Special Notice Overpayments Incurred During the COVID-19 Pandemic Emergency Number Page 21-08 2 of 2 Overpayments and Mandatory Mid-Period Reports CalWORKs customers are required to report verbally, in person, or in writing specific changes during the SAR or AR/CO payment period withing 10 days of when the change become known to the AU. These mandatory mid-period reports are: • Fleeing felon status • Violations of conditions of probation or parole • Address changes • Income exceeding the AUs Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) • AR/CO only: changes in household composition Note: A discrepancy between the AUs circumstances and the grant amount issued for a given month will not result in and overpayment if the change in circumstance was not required to be reported. An overpayment cannot be assessed for the month following a change in income over IRT for the first through fifth months of a current SAR payment period if the customer has timely reported the change and the HSS was unable, before the first of the month following the change to provide a 10-day notice of the termination or reduction of benefits. For AR/CO cases, an overpayment cannot be assessed for the month following a change in come over the IRT or household composition for an AU that does not include an eligible adult if the customer has reported the change and the county was unable, before the first of the month following the change, to provide 10-day notice of the termination of reduction of benefits. Unear ned income would need to be paired with earned income to be considered over the IRT mid-period. The customer’s failure to report an address change will not result in a reduction in aid or termination of benefits. As a result, an overpayment cannot be established when the customer fails to report an address change. Procedure: After August 1, 2021, when an HSS is re-evaluating a case in CalWIN which will result in an overpayment, the error type will be entered as “Admin Error” regardless of case circumstances for nonfraudulent cases. Program Impacts: Other Programs Affected The changes to the CalWORKs overpayment process also apply to the Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA), Entrant Cash Assistance (ECA), and Traffickin g and Crime Victims Assistance Program (TCVAP) cash assistance programs. References: AB 135 ACL 21-85 CalWORKs Program Guide section 44-350 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by August 31, 2022. Approval for Release: R ick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: SN 21-15 RMR Ceilings Effective 1-1-2022
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Special Notice Child Care Regional Market Rate Ceilings Number Page 21-15 1 of 3 Revision Date: 12/01/2021 Background: The Regional Market Rate (RMR) ceilings are the maximum amount child care providers can be reimbursed by the State for subsidized child care under CalWORKs Child Care programs . RMR ceilings were last updated 1/1/2018 as per CalWORKs Child Care Special Notice 17-05. Policy: Assembly Bill 131 (Chapter 116 of the Statues of 2021), which was signed into law on July 23, 2021, maintained the previous Regional Market Rate ceilings through December 31, 2021. Effective January 1, 2022 the new Regional Market Rate ceilings for licensed providers are established at the 75th percentile of the 2018 Regional Market Rate survey or the Regional Market Rate ceilings as they existed on December 31, 2021, whichever is greater. Also commencing January 1, 2022, reimbursement to licensed exempt care shall be 70% of the commensurate Family Child Care Home Rate. RMR ceilings will increase effective 1/1/2022 in accordance with Assembly Bill (AB) 131. The increased rates for San Diego County are as follows: CHILD CARE CENTERS FAMILY CHILD CARE HOMES TRUSTLINED/RELATIVE PROVIDERS County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Special Notice Child Care Regional Market Rate Ceilings Number Page 21-15 2 of 3 Procedure: Child Care Case M anagers (CCMs) are to use the increased RMR ceilings to determine the appropriate reimbursement rate for child care services provided on or after 01/ 01/2022 for each family. CCMs are to provide affected families with a timely Child Care Change Notice of Action (NOA) , NA 833 (04/20), regarding the change in child care subsidy amount due to the State-approved reason: “The State of California changed reimbursement limits.” Each NOA must include the required hearing rights information (NA Back 9). CCMs are to ensure the NA 833 is specific to each child care provider in accordance with County policy regarding provider notification as outlined in CPG 10 -010.F. The NA 833 may list multiple children and/or multiple rates for the child(ren), if appropriate, for each provider. Note: Rate Sheets Per AB 131, licensed child care providers may alter rate levels for subsidized children as needed and shall provide the alternative payment program and resource and referral agency with a copy of their updated rate sheet to reflect any changes. Updated rates shall be effective within 60 days of submission of the updated rate sheet. The only applies to licensed child care providers. CCMs do not have to collect rate sheets from license-exempt providers. See CPG 10-010.E for Child Care Payments and CPG 10-010.F for Child Care NOA requirements. Impacts: Automation: The provider r eference table i n CalWIN was updated on 12/ 15/2021 to reflect t he increased RMR ceilings effective 01/01/2022. Forms and Document Capture: Child Care desk aids for the RMR Ceilings effective 01 /01/2022 and for the prior RMR Ceiling effective 01/01/2018 – 12/31/2021, RMR Ceilings effective 1/1/2017- 12/31/17, RMR Ceiling effective 10/1/2015 – 12/31/2016 and RMR Ceilings effective 1/1/2015 - 9/30/2015 are available in the CalWIN Intranet for internal staff use. The manual Child Care Change NOA, NA 833 ( 04/20), is available for immediate print in English and Spanish via the Electronic Forms Library. Staff must follow instructions as per the Printing Barcoded Documents-Instruction Desk Aid to ensure the CERMS barcode prints correctly on the issued NOA. Reminder: A copy of any manual NOA that is generated outside of the CalWIN system must be retained in the Child Care case file. Programs Affected: None Quality Control (QC): County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Special Notice Child Care Regional Market Rate Ceilings Number Page 21-15 3 of 3 QC will cite the appropriate error on any case that does not comply with the requirements outlined in this material. References: Child Care Bulletin 21-21 Assembly Bill 131 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 11/30/2022. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations

title: SN 22-02 - CalWORKs Time-On-Aid 60-Months Implementation
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Special Notice CalWORKs Time-On-Aid 60-Months Implementation Number Page 22-02 1 of 4 Effective Date: May 1, 2022 Background: California implemented the California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids Program (CalWORKs) on January 1, 1998. The CalWORKs Program established a life time limit on the receipt of cash assistance for all adults. From January 1, 1998 to June 30, 2011, the CalWORKs Time on Aid (TOA) limit was 60 -months. Beginning July 1, 2011, the TOA limit was changed to 48- months. Any months of aid received prior to January 1, 1998 from California or any other state, do not count toward the CalWORKs time limit. Purpose: The purpose of this Special Notice is to provide guidance to implement the provision in Assembly Bill (AB) 79 that extends the CalWORKs time limit from 48-months to 60-months and AB 135 that provides temporary CalWORKs policies and policy waivers to implement a temporary mid-period county-initiated change as a result of the 60-month time limit. Policy: Effective May 1, 2022, adults will be eligible to receive CalWORKs for a maximum of 60 countable months. This 60-month CalWORKs time limit replaces the 48-month CalWORKs time limit. Customers who meet the following conditions will be added automatically to their respective Assistance Unit (AU): • Living in the home with an existing CalWORKs AU, but currently are not being aided solely due to reaching the 48-month CalWORKs time limit. • Mandatorily included filing unit member and are included on the most recent Statement of Facts. • Joining an existing AU mid-period because of the 60-month time limit waiver. • They have not exhausted their CalWORKs 60-month time limit. C ustomers who meet these conditions are referred to as “formerly timed- out household members.” Timed-out customers who are optional household members or new household members are not considered “formerly timed-out household members” and they must request to be added to the AU. N ote: Refer to the Procedure section of this material for more information regarding the automated process. Optional Household Members or New Household Members There is no change in the policy of adding optional household members or new household members. They will not be added automatically and must request to be added to the AU. The request must be documented in the case record. Optional household members, including stepparents, registered domestic partners and needy caretaker relatives may choose to stay unaided. New household members who are mandatory household members are required to be reported and added to the AU at the beginning of the next Semi -Annual Reporting (SAR) payment period. The new household member may request to be added prior to the County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Special Notice CalWORKs Time-On-Aid 60-Months Implementation Number Page 22-02 2 of 4 next SAR payment period and if eligible, they will be added to the AU if their addition does not result in a decrease to the existing AU’s grant amount. O ptional household members and new household members are required to complete the form CW 8 – Statement of Facts for A n Additional Person and provide all the necessary verification to complete a determination of eligibility. If eligible, the customer is to be added the month following receipt of all required verifications. If the request was made more than 30-days prior to 05/01/2022, the request must be denied and staff must inform the customer of the earliest date they may request to be added to the AU. Temporary CalWORKs Policies and Policy Waivers AB 135 issued temporary policies and policy waivers to allow adding the formerly timed-out household members to an existing AU as a county -initiated mid -period change effective May 1, 2022. The temporary policies and policy waivers include the following: 1. County-Initiated Mid-Period Changes – A dding the formerly timed- out household members to an existing AU will be considered a county -initiated change. Staff are to treat these mid- period AU additions as they would other county initiated mid- period changes per CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 44-270.I County-Initiated Actions and Third Party Information. 2. Statement of Facts – Waives the CW 8/CW 8A Statement of Facts form requirement to add a member to an existing AU. 3. Child Support – Waives the child support cooperation requirement for 60- days. Refer to the Child Support Cooperation section of this material for additional guidance concerning child support. T hese temporary policies and policy waivers are for the sole purpose of implementing the CalWORKs 60-month time limit. They are effective May 1, 2022 through August 29, 2022 (120- days from implementation date) until eligible “ formerly timed-out household members” have been added to their respective AUs. These temporary policies and policy waivers do not apply to all adults. They strictly apply to “formerly timed-out household members” as defined earlier in this material. Child Support Cooperation The following child support requirements will be waived for 6 0-days after a “ formerly timed -out household member” has been added to their existing AU or by next SAR or redetermination, whichever is earlier: • Assignment of support rights as a condition of eligibility for CalWORKs customers requesting to be aided or any other family member required to be in the AU unless the customer is exempt from complying or the forms are already on file. • Customer to complete, sign and date the CW 2.1 NA Notice and Agreement for Child, Spousal and Medical Support and CW 2.1 Q Support Questionnaire for each absent parent or alleged parent. If t he formerly timed-out household member fails to submit the required child support forms ( CW 2.1 NA and CW 2.1 Q ) within 60-days or by the next SAR or redetermination, they will be excluded from the AU. A timely and adequate Notice of Action (NOA) must be provided to inform the customer of the sanction and discontinuance of the adult customer’s aid. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Special Notice CalWORKs Time-On-Aid 60-Months Implementation Number Page 22-02 3 of 4 Reminders: 1. Unless the AU is exempt, the CW 2.1 NA and CW 2.1 Q for the current application period must be on file. A new set of forms must be completed each time there is a break in the AU’s aid that requires a new application. In addition, for any child born after the application date , completed and signed child support forms (CW 2.1 NA and CW 2.1Q) may also be required to be on file. 2. Particularly for cases with aid code K1/3F (Child Only cases), after a “formerly timed-out household member” is added to an existing AU, budgets for CalWORKs and CalFresh may be revised. Budget revisions are needed when the Local Child Support Agency ( LCSA) stops dispersing the full child support amount and begins to disperse only the child support disregard to the AU. Staff must update the direct child support income entry in CalWIN with an end date once the signed child support forms are received. Failure to revise the budgets when “formerly timed-out household members” are added back to the AU may result in underpayments . Refer to Processing Guide 43- 200.D1 for more information regarding Child Support Payments. Exemption and Exception (Extenders) The exception (extender) months must count towards the CalWORKs 60- month time limit unless the time limit exception (extender) is also a time limit exemption. Procedure: Refer to Attachment A for examples that reflect the CalWORKs 60 -month time limit implementation including the state of emergency CalWORKs time limit exemption that occurred from March 2020 through April 2022. Automation Effective May 15, 2022, upon CalWIN Release 69, all “ formerly timed-out household members” who have been discontinued due to exhausting their CalWORKs 48 -month timeclock will be automatically returned to the AU if: • The customer is still living in the home. • The customer is marked as requesting aid in CalWIN. • The existing CalWORKs case is active case. N ote: CalWORKs grant supplements will be issued to customers on May 15, 2022, when applicable. Al l applicable form and NOAs text will be updated from 48-month to 60-month time limit. CalWORKs timeclocks will be updated to 60- months for all adults on active CalWORKs cases. The 46 th-month notice informing CalWORKs individuals that they would discontinue May 2022 or after will be suppressed by CalWIN. Program Impacts: CalFresh The addition of the “formerly timed-out adult” to an existing AU may increase the family’s grant amount. Therefore, the AU’s CalFresh allotment may be recalculated as a county -initiated action and may change due to the increase in the CalWORKs grant. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Special Notice CalWORKs Time-On-Aid 60-Months Implementation Number Page 22-02 4 of 4 On May 15, 2022, a mass CalWIN update will automatically apply the revised CalWORKs grant for the June 2022 CalFresh budget. In addition, the CalFresh Change NOA will be generated for the applicable cases as part of the mass update when the case is authorized. Medi-Cal The “formerly timed-out household member” who is added to an existing AU and who was previously aided under a Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) or Non-MAGI Medi-Cal aid code will transition to a cash-linked Medi-Cal aid code. Employment Services (ES) Separate material will be issued to provide guidance on the ES participation for the “formerly timed-out household members” being added to an existing AU. Child Care Customers who had previously exhausted their 48-month of CalWORKs time limit who are eligible for additional months of aid under this policy will potentially need child care services to work or participate in other approved ES activities. Staff should ensure that customers requesting child care services are assisted or referred to the appropriate stage of child care based on their CalWORKs status and eligibility. References: ACL 20-113, 21-89, Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by August 29, 2022. Approval for Release: R ick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services Attachment A CalWORKs 60-Month Time Limit Examples Bel ow are examples of how the CalWORKs 60-month time limit will apply. Unless otherwise stated, these examples reflect the state of emergency CalWORKs time limit exemption (related to COVID -19) that occurred from March 2020 through April 2022. Example A - Customer with Less Than 48 Countable Months: An Assistance Unit (AU) of three (a parent and two children) has been receiving aid in California since Jan uary 2020. The parent received the time limit exemptions in the months of March 2020 through April 2022. In this scenario, the parent’s time limit would change from 48-months to 60-months in May 2022. 03/2020 04/2022 05/2022 CalWORKs Time On Aid (TOA) months 2 2 3 Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) TOA months 3 28 29 Example B - Formerly Timed-out Mandatorily Included Adult in an Annual Reporting/Child Only (AR/CO) Household: An AU of two (timed-out parent and two children) has been receiving aid. The parent did not receive the time limit exemption because the customer already exhausted their CalWORKs 48-month limit prior to March 2020 . In this scenario, the parent would be added automatically to the AU in May 2022. The AU would change from AR/CO to a Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) household at the same time. The case will continue to have the same reporting cycle and redetermination date. Unless exempt, the parent will be required to complete the CW 2.1 - NA Notice and Agreement for Child, Spousal and Medical Support and CW 2.1 Q - Support Questionnaire for each absent parent or alleged parent and must provide it within 60-days after they are added to their existing AU. 03/2020 04/2022 05/2022 CalWORKs TOA months Timed out Timed out 49 TANF TOA months 48 48 49 Attachment A CalWORKs 60-Month Time Limit Examples Example C - Formerly Timed-out Mandatorily Included Adult in an AR/CO Household: An AU of two (parent and one child) has been receiving aid in California since May 2017 under state-funded CalWORKs. The parent has exceeded their TANF 60 -month time limit prior to March 2020 and for that reason, the parent did not receive time limit exemptions in the months of March 2020 through June 2021. The parent reached their CalWORKs 48-month limit on April 2021. Therefore, the parent is removed from the AU as of May 2021. In this scenario, the parent would be added automatically to the AU in May 2022 and the AU would change back to a SAR household. Unless exempt, the customer will be required to complete the CW 2.1 and CW 2.1 Q for each absent parent or alleged parent and must provide it within 60 -days after they are added to their existing AU. 03/2020 04/2021 05/2021 04/2022 05/2022 CalWORKs TOA months 35 48 Parent removed from the AU Timed out 49 TANF TOA months Timed out N/A N/A N/A N/A Example D - Formerly Timed-out Optional Household Member in an AR/CO Household: An AU of two (two children only with non-needy caretaker relative) has been receiving aid since January 2020. The caretaker relative was previously aided in another AU and was timed-out prior to January 2020. The caretaker relative made a request on April 2022 to be added to the AU. The caretaker relative reported that they own a vehicle and have earned income. The CW 8 Statement of Facts for An Additional Person, CW 80 Self-Certification Form for Motor Vehicle, and CW 2200 Request for Verification were mailed out to request the necessary documentation to complete the caretaker’s eligibility determination. The caretake r relative provided all the requested forms and documentation in the same month. In this scenario, the caretaker relative would be added to the AU in the following month, May 2022. 04/2022 05/2022 CalWORKs TOA months Timed out 49 TANF TOA months 48 49 Attachment A CalWORKs 60-Month Time Limit Examples Example E - Formerly Timed-out Mandatorily Included Adult with Time Limit Extender: An AU of two (timed-out parent and two children). As of December 2019, the parent’s total countable months for CalWORKs and TANF is 48-months. The parent timed -out from CalWORKs in January 2020. In February 2022, the parent was determined eligible for an exception (extender) due to disability. In this scenario, the customer would be added to the AU in May 2022 and their extended months would not count towar ds their CalWORKs 60 -month time limit as the time limit exception (extender) criterion is also a time limit exemption criterion. 12/2019 01/2020 02/2022 05/2022 CalWORKs TOA months (before 60- month time implementation) 48 Removed from the AU Time Limit Exception (extender) N/A CalWORKs TOA months (after 60- month time implementation) N/A N/A Time limit Exception (extender) Time limit exemption TANF TOA months 48 N/A 49 52 Example F - Counting Out of State Months Towards the CalWORKs 60-Month Time Limit: In April 2022, an AU of three (parent and two children) , moves to California from Michigan, applies for CalWORKs and is determined to be eligible as of April 1. The TOA review identified that the parent received 36-months of TANF in Michigan during 2018 and 2021. In this scenario, the parent is eligible to receive 24 countable months of CalWORKs aid in California. Unless the parent meets a CalWORKs time limit exemption or exception (extender) criteria, they will be removed from the AU once the CalWORKs 60-month time limit is exhausted. The children would be moved into the Safety Net program on the first of the following month, April 2024, if otherwise eligible. 03/2022 04/2022 03/2024 04/2024 CalWORKs TOA months 36 (previous aid received out of state) 37 (start of aid in California) 60 Parent removed from AU TANF TOA months 36 37 60 Timed-out Attachment A CalWORKs 60-Month Time Limit Examples Example G - Counting Out of State Months of TANF Received Prior to January 1, 1998: In May 2022, an AU of three ( grandparent/needy caretaker relative and two grandchildren) moves to California from South Carolina. The grandparent previously received TANF aid for 19- months from November 1996 through May 1998. South Carolina implemented its TANF Program on October 12, 1996. From June 1998 until the AU moved to California, the grandparent was not receiving aid any state. In this scenario, the grandparent has a total of 19 countable months of federal aid but only 5 months will be counted toward the CalWORKs clock (January 1998 to May 1998). Therefore, when the grandparent applied and was determined eligible as a needy caretaker relative in August 2022, the grandparent still had 55-months remaining on their CalWORKs time limit but only 41 months remaining on their TANF time limit. Unless the grandparent meets a CalWORKs time limit exemption or exception (extender), the grandparent will be removed from the AU effective December 2026. 04/2022 05/2022 9/2025 10/2025 11/2026 CalWORKs TOA months 5 (aid received out of state) 6 46 47 60 TANF TOA months 19 20 60 Timedout N/A

title: SN 25-03 Increase to the IRT Levels - October 2025
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Special Notice Increase to the Income Reporting Threshold Levels – October 2025 Number Page 25-03 1 of 2 Effective Date: October 1, 2025 Background: Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) Under Semi -Annual Reporting (SAR) and Annual Reporting/Child -Only (AR/CO) regulations, customers are required to report only certain changes in their income or family circumstances midperiod. One such mandatory mid-period report is when the Assistance Unit’s (AU) total earned income, or combined unearned and earned income, exceeds the IRT level. An AU with only unearned income is not required to report when unearned income exceeds the IRT level mid-period. The IRT level for an AU is the lower of the two following tiers: 1. Tier 1: 55% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) for a family of three, plus the amount of income last used to calculate the AU’s monthly grant amount. 2. Tier 2: 130% of the FPL which is also the level of income at which a household may become financially ineligible for CalFresh. Purpose: The purpose of this Special Notice is to inform staff of IRT levels increase. The increase takes effect October 1, 2025. Policy: IRT Customers must be informed of their IRT level at least once per SAR or AR/CO payment period or whenever the AU’s IRT level changes. The IRT level in which the customer was last notified will be used for reporting purposes until the county informs the customer of a change in their IRT level. Procedure: IRT The informing notice that provides the IRT limits must be individualized for each AU. Staff will inform customers of their IRT level at least once per payment period or whenever the AU’s IRT changes. Upon approval of an application and any time the AU’s IRT level changes during the recertification/payment period, the IRT level must be provided to the customer using SAR 2 – Reporting Changes for Cash Aid and CalFresh , AR 2 - Reporting Changes for CalWORKs and CalFresh , or AR 2 SAR - Reporting Changes for CalWORKs and CalFresh form as appropriate. The SAR 2, AR 2, or AR 2 SAR forms are generated in CalSAWS. Staff are to review the information in the form and provide the appropriate form to the customer. The IRT level in which the customer was last notified will be used for reporting purposes. The new IRT level will be applied as soon as the customer receives the notification of a change in their IRT level. Staff will not use the new IRT for any AU until the AU has received notification that their IRT has changed, and the new IRT level will not be retroactively applied to the case. A report of income over the IRT may result in either a mid -period decrease or discontinuance of CalWORKs. Once the family receives income in excess of the IRT and reports it, staff must take action to determine continued financial eligibility. If the new Net Nonexempt Income (NNI) will continue but is County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Special Notice Increase to the Income Reporting Threshold Levels – October 2025 Number Page 25-03 2 of 2 at a level not exceeding the AU’s Tier 2, staff must use the new NNI to recalculate the grant amount based on the reported income. If staff determine the grant should be decreased, the grant will be decreased at the end of the month in which timely and adequate notice can be provided. If the NNI is reasonably anticipated to continue to exceed the AU’s Tier 2 IRT for the remainder of the payment period, staff will determine the AU financially ineligible and discontinue the AU at the end of the month in which timely and adequate notice can be provided. As long as the AU’s NNI does not exceed the Tier 2 IRT (130% of the FPL) , the case will stay open, and the AU may remain eligible for supportive services and CalWORKs special needs. This may also allow some CalWORKs cases to remain open with a Zero Basic Grant (ZGB) if the AU’s NNI remains below 130% of the FPL. Impacts: Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) and Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Programs (TCVAP) The above instructions also apply to RCA and TCVAP, unless specifically superseded by RCA/TCVAP regulations. CalFresh CalFresh income eligibility standards by household size will be updated and issued separately. Automation The CalSAWS reference tables , to reflect the new IRT levels , have been updated . Additional information and case exceptions and online correspondence reports will be issued to staff for appropriate action. Forms and Document Capture The SAR 2, AR 2, and AR 2 SAR forms are available for immediate use in CalSAWS. Scratch Budget/Assistance Charts The CalWORKs-CalFresh Scratch Budget has been updated with the new IRT levels for October 2025. The CalWORKs Assistance Standards Chart has been updated with the new IRT levels. References: All County Letter No. 25-61. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by October 31, 2026. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: SN 25-04 Social Security Administration (SSA) Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA) 2026
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide/CalFresh/Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice Social Security Administration – Cost-of-Living Adjustment Number Page CalWORKs 25-04 CalFresh 25-03 Medi-Cal 25-07 1 of 3 Effective Date: January 1, 2026 Background: Social Security Administration ( SSA) recipients will receive a 2.8 percent Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) effective December 31, 2025, and payable January 1, 2026. In addition, starting January 2026 the Medicare Part B premium will increase to $202.90 per month. Policy: New Applicants The actual amount of the SS A benefit, including the COLA increase, must be used for eligibility and budgeting purposes beginning in January 202 6. The SS A budgeted amount for January will be considered reasonably anticipated income for applications received in November and December 2025. Treatment of SSA COLA for Ongoing Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) Customers The SSA COLA is considered a mid- period county-initiated action. As a result, a decrease in CalWORKs/CalFresh benefits may occur effective January 1, 2026, with timely and adequate notice. Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) Requirements CalWORKs customers are required to report if the increase in SSA benefits combined with earned income results in exceeding their IRT. If income exceeding the IRT is reported an evaluation is required to determine if the customer is still eligible to benefits. If CalWORKs discontinues due to exceeding the IRT, the CalFresh households (HH) are eligible to Transitional CalFresh (TCF). CalFresh HHs must report if the increase in SSA benefits combined with all other income receive d results in exceeding the HH’s IRT. If income exceeding the IRT is report ed, then an evaluation is required to determine if the HH is still eligible to benefits. Treatment of SSA COLA for CalWORKs Annual Reporting/Child Only (AR/CO) Cases The only cases where this action will not be considered mid- period are those AR/CO cases with a December 2025 redetermination. For those cases, include the updated SSA benefit amount in budgeting for the upcoming AR/CO period. Timely and Adequate Notice As with any adverse action, timely and adequate notice is required to decrease benefits . If unable to change the January 2026 CalWORKs grant/CalFresh allotment, take the appropriate action to decrease benefits the first of the following month after timely adequate notice can be provided. Recalculate January 2026 benefits using the increased SSA benefits and Medicare Part B premium amounts; and if the calculation results in a decrease, an overpayment/overissuance will need to be established as appropriate. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide/CalFresh/Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice Social Security Administration – Cost-of-Living Adjustment Number Page CalWORKs 25-04 CalFresh 25-03 Medi-Cal 25-07 2 of 3 Treatment of SSA COLA for Non-MAGI Medi-Cal Eligibility Groups The increase will not be applied to the Aged, Blind, and Disabled Federal Poverty Level (ABD FPL) and Medicare Savings Programs (MSPs) until April 1, 2026. Effective January 1, 2026, all medically needy cases with Title II income must have the share of cost (SOC) adjusted to reflect the COLA. Medicare Part B Disregard the income equal to the amount of the customer’s Medicare Part B premium when determining eligibility for the ABD FPL program, regardless of the state’s payment of the premium. This income disregard is applied to the budget as long as the countable income remains within the ABD FPL program limits. Note: Customers who are evaluated as Medically Needy (MN) must pay the premium before receiving the deduction. Procedure: When updating the SSA benefit amount the calculation is to be completed as follows: When Medicare Part B is not paid by the customer: Step Action 1 Use the previous SSA Title II benefit amount. 2 Multiply the amount by 1.028. 3 Round down to the next lower dollar (remove the cents). 4 Final amount will be the new anticipated SSA benefit amount. When Medicare Part B is paid for by the customer: Step Action 1 Add the 2005 Part B premium ($185) to the 2024 net Title II benefit amount. 2 Multiply the amount by 1.028. 3 Round down to the next lower dollar (remove the cents). 4 Subtract the 2026 Part B premium and round down to the next lower whole dollar. 5 Final amount will be the new anticipated SSA benefit amount. Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 11.1A Assistance Standards for updated premium values. Impacts: Automation A COLA mass update will run on December 6, 2025, automatically adjusting SSA benefit amounts and Medicare Part B premiums for open SSA and Medicare expense records in CalSAWS. On December 13, 202 5, a batch Eligibility Determination Benefit Calculation (EDBC) run will occur and effective January 2026 CalWORKs/CalFresh benefits will reflect the SSA benefit and Medicare premium increases. Case list reports requiring action will be shared when available. Cases not included in the COLA run will require staff to manually update the information in the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) to reflect in the January 2026 benefits. Other Programs Affected The SSA COLA also applies to Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) and Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program (TCVAP). References: All County Information Notice (ACIN) No. I-56-25. All County Welfare Directors Letter (ACWDL) 25-22, 25-26. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by December 31, 2026. In addition, starting January 2026 the Medicare Part B premium will increase to $202.90 per month. Policy: New Applicants The actual amount of the SS A benefit, including the COLA increase, must be used for eligibility and budgeting purposes beginning in January 202 6. The SS A budgeted amount for January will be considered reasonably anticipated income for applications received in November and December 2025. Treatment of SSA COLA for Ongoing Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) Customers The SSA COLA is considered a mid- period county-initiated action. As a result, a decrease in CalWORKs/CalFresh benefits may occur effective January 1, 2026, with timely and adequate notice. Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) Requirements CalWORKs customers are required to report if the increase in SSA benefits combined with earned income results in exceeding their IRT. If income exceeding the IRT is reported an evaluation is required to determine if the customer is still eligible to benefits. If CalWORKs discontinues due to exceeding the IRT, the CalFresh households (HH) are eligible to Transitional CalFresh (TCF). CalFresh HHs must report if the increase in SSA benefits combined with all other income receive d results in exceeding the HH’s IRT. If income exceeding the IRT is report ed, then an evaluation is required to determine if the HH is still eligible to benefits. Treatment of SSA COLA for CalWORKs Annual Reporting/Child Only (AR/CO) Cases The only cases where this action will not be considered mid- period are those AR/CO cases with a December 2025 redetermination. For those cases, include the updated SSA benefit amount in budgeting for the upcoming AR/CO period. If unable to change the January 2026 CalWORKs grant/CalFresh allotment, take the appropriate action to decrease benefits the first of the following month after timely adequate notice can be provided. Recalculate January 2026 benefits using the increased SSA benefits and Medicare Part B premium amounts; and if the calculation results in a decrease, an overpayment/overissuance will need to be established as appropriate. title: SN 25-05 Implementation of the New Statewide Minimum Wage
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide Special Notice Implementation of the New Statewide Minimum Wage Number Page CW 25-05 CF 25-04 GR 25-01 1 of 2 Effective Date: January 1, 2026 Background: Employees in California are required to be paid the minimum wage as required by state law, with certain exemptions. The current California minimum wage is $16.50 per hour. Purpose: To inform staff of the increase in the statewide minimum wage and its impact on CalWORKs, CalFresh, Employment Services, CalFresh Employment & Training (CFET), and General Relief Work Project assignment and credit. Policy: Effective January 1, 2026 , the California minimum wage will increase to $1 6.90 per hour. Refer to CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 44-270.F and CalFresh Program Guide (CFPG) 63-251 for guidance on Prospective Budgeting and Reasonably Anticipated Income. See General Relief Program Guide (GRPG) 90-700.8 for General Relief Work Project assignment and credit. Procedure: CalWORKs and CalFresh Programs Individuals are expected to report income reflecting the minimum wage increase beginning in the Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7) data month of January 2026 or the Redetermination/Recertification (RE) month of February 2026. Customers are required to report mid- period when their income exceeds their Income Reporting Threshold (IRT). If the customer reports a pay increase prior to January 1, 2026, use current reporting regulations to determine when the change of income should be used in the budget. For further guidance on: • Mandatory Mid-Period Reports refer to CPG 44-270.C and CFPG 63-283. • Voluntary Mid-Period Reports refer to CPG 44-270.H and CFPG 63-284. Employment Services Employment Case Managers (ECMs) must perform the Simplified CalFresh Program (SCFP) calculation to determine the maximum number of hours that a participant can be required to participate in a Work Experience (WEX) or Community Service (CS) assignment. ECMs must continue us ing the minimum wage of $1 6.50 when completing such a calculation through December 31, 202 5. Refer to CPG 10-050.A and CalWORKs Processing Guide No. 10-050.A1 for further guidance. CalFresh Employment & Training and General Relief Work Project Work Project assignments are determined by dividing the net CalFresh allotment by the federal or state minimum wage, whichever is higher. As the current California minimum wage is higher than the federal minimum wage, use the new California minimum wage for the number of Work Project days assigned, effective January 2026 and ongoing. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide Special Notice Implementation of the New Statewide Minimum Wage Number Page CW 25-05 CF 25-04 GR 25-01 2 of 2 For example: A single employable customer living alone with no income will receive the maximum CalFresh allotment of $ 292 ÷ $16.90 = 17.28. Hours are rounded down to the nearest eight-hour increment. The customer will be assigned 16 hours. The General Relief Employable Program aligns with the CFET policy . Any remainder of the General Relief benefit will still show as an amount owed to the county when the case closes. The credit for Work Project hours completed is determined by multiplying the number of hours worked by the current federal or state minimum wage, whichever is higher. For example: Using the example above, the customer worked 16 hours each month. 16 hours x $16.90 = $270 repaid per month. Please refer to Attachment A for a reference table of the number of Work Project days to be assigned based on the corresponding CalFresh allotment amounts. Impacts: None. References: All County Information Notice (ACIN) No. I-45-25. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by January 31, 2027. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services ATTACHMENT A GENERAL RELIEF WORK PROJECT DAYS Work Project Days Assigned CalFresh Allotment 0 Days $0 - $135 1 Day $136 - $270 2 Days $271 - $292
