title: SN 26-01 - Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) Outreach
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach Number Page CW 26-01 CF 26-02 MC 26-02 GR 26-01 CAPI 26-01 CMS 26-01 1 of 4 Effective Date: March 1, 2026 Background: San Diego County’s Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) campaign provide s outreach which is intended to provide customers with information to access potentially eligible tax credits, free tax preparation, and other filing services and resources. EITC payments and credits may have impact to Self -Sufficiency Services (SSS) programs such as California Work Opportunity and Responsibility for Kids (CalWORKs), CalFresh, Medi -Cal, General Relief (GR), Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants (CAPI) and County Medical Services (CMS). Purpose: To provide guidance on treatment of EITC payments and credits for SSS programs and outreach resources available for eligibility staff to provide to customers who are potentially eligible to tax credits, free tax preparation, and other filing services and resources. Policy: Treatment of Income from EITC EITC payments are exempt for CalWORKs, CalFresh, CAPI, Medi-Cal and CMS. For General Relief , EITC payments are counted as unearned income in the month received. If a customer received GR during 2025, and the customer receives the EITC, review the case for potential unreported earnings since EITC is for earned income. EITC related payments and credits that customers may receive are EITC, CalEITC, Foster Youth Tax Credit (FYTC), Expanded Young Child Tax Credit (EYCTC). Treatment of Property from EITC payments The table below outlines the treatment of Property for payments received from EITC. Program Treatment of Property CalWORKs and CalFresh Exempt resources for 12 months, starting with the month that the payment is received. Medi-Cal EITC payments are exempt as property in the month following the month of receipt. General Relief Refund retained by the customer in the month following receipt is considered personal property. CAPI EITC payments are exempt as property in the month following the month of receipt. CMS Any portion of the refund retained by the beneficiary in the month following receipt is considered exempt personal property. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach Number Page CW 26-01 CF 26-02 MC 26-02 GR 26-01 CAPI 26-01 CMS 26-01 2 of 4 Procedure: FRCs and ES Staff If customers report EITC payments or credits, treat the income and property as listed in this notice. Distribute the EITC postcards to c ustomers at all contacts and encourage them to contact 2 -1-1 to receive free assistance with filing their taxes and claim available tax credits. If additional postcards are needed, they can be ordered through XEROX printing services. References: All County Information Notice (ACIN) No. I-01-26 Resources: CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 44-100.C and 44-100.H2 CalFresh Program Guide (CFPG) 63-203 and 63-204. title: SN 26-02 COLA Increase to MBSAC and IIK Levels - July 2026
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency CalWORKs Program Guide Special Notice CalWORKs Cost of Living Adjustment Increase to Minimum Basic Standards of Adequate Care and Income In-Kind Levels – July 2026 Number Page 26-02 1 of 2 Effective Date: July 1, 2026 Background: CalWORKs Minimum Basic Standards of Adequate Care (MBSAC) and Income In-Kind (IIK) levels are updated annually due to Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA). Purpose: This Special Notice provides information and instructions for eligibility staff regarding the MBSAC and IIK increase. The Scratch Budget and the CalWORKs Assistance Standards Chart have been updated with the increased MBSAC and IIK levels. Policy: Fiscal Year 2026-27 COLA increases the MBSAC and IIK levels by 3.59%, effective July 1, 2026. Procedure: Applicants Use the updated MBSAC levels to determine financial eligibility for families who apply for CalWORKs on or after July 1, 20 26. Take immediate action to review and correct any applications denied on or after July 1, 2026, if the sole reason for denial was failure to pass the CalWORKs applicant test due to the previous MBSAC or IIK amounts used. If the Assistance Unit (AU) is not financially eligible for the application month of June 2026, evaluate eligibility beginning July 2026, using reasonably anticipated income and the updated MBSAC and IIK levels. Refer to CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 44-100.A. Recipients The COLA change is a county -initiated mid-period action for CalWORKs recipients. The updated IIK amounts are to be used prospectively with timely and adequate notice. Impacts: Automation The reference tables in California Statewide Automated Welfare System ( CalSAWS) have been updated with the increased MBSAC and IIK levels beginning July 2026. Management Reports (MR) have been previously provided to Family Resource Centers (FRC) to review potential impacted cases. These MRs have been posted in the 2026 – MBSAC – In-kind Income Reports folder in the MR SharePoint site. Other Programs Affected The updated MBSAC and IIK levels also apply to Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) and Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program (TCVAP). References: Welfare and Institutions Code (W&IC) 11450, 11452, 11453. All County Letter (ACL) 26-39. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services

P urpose: The purpose of this special notice is to inform staff of a 1.8% MAP increase, and Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) levels increase. The increases take effect October 1, 2026. title: A. CalWORKs and Employment Services Overview
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageCalWORKs and Employment Services Overview 10-001 1 of 2 Revision Date: July 01, 2022 Purpose: This revision incorporates policy changes to the California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids (CalWORKs) program due to the passage of Assembly Bill (AB) 79 that repeals the CalWORKs 48- month Time-on-Aid limit, repeals the Welfare to Work 24-Month Time Clock (WTW 24-MTC) and changes the WTW program hourly participation requirements. The policy updates became effective May 1, 2022. Background: The Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act (PRWORA) became federal law on August 22, 1996, and established a cash assistance program, Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF), which limited federal funding to a maximum of 60 months in a lifetime and required states to develop and implement programs that would move individuals from dependency to selfsufficiency through employment. The Welfare-to-Work act of 1997 established the CalWORKs program which is California’s version of TANF. The CalWORKs program was originally implemented with a 60-month lifetime limit for nonexempt adults, and with a provision to allow children to continue receiving aid until they reach 18 years of age. Effective January 1,1998, the CalWORKs program began helping families achieve selfsufficiency through the Welfare-to-Work (WTW) program, also known as the Employment Services (ES) program that has participation requirements and a ‘Work-First’ emphasis, while at the same time supporting families by offering services that help remove barriers to employment and encourage independence. Effective July 1, 2011, the CalWORKs time limit for aid to adult recipients changed from 60 months to 48 months, per Senate Bill (SB) 72. However effective May 1, 2022, the CalWORKs time limit has been extended back from 48 months to 60 months, per AB 79. In summary, from January 1, 1998, through June 30, 2011, the CalWORKs time limit was 60 months. From July 1, 2011 to April 30, 2022, the CalWORKs time limit was 48 months. Effective May 1, 2022 the CalWORKs time limit is again 60 months. Effective January 1, 2013, per SB 1041, a 24-month time clock was implemented limiting the number of months participants can choose freely from the full range of activities offered by the Employment Services program without meeting core work participation hours. After the 24-months were used, a participant had to meet minimum hourly participation requirements in core work activities. Other ES activities were allowed if core work participation requirements were met. Effective May 1, 2022, per AB 79, the 24-month month time clock, and the core participation hours associated with it, have been repealed. Policy: Effective May 1, 2022, adults will be eligible to receive CalWORKs for a maximum of 60 months. The 60-month CalWORKs time limit replaces the 48-month CalWORKs time limit. When counting the months of the 60-month CalWORKs time limit, a month does not count against the time limit when the County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageCalWORKs and Employment Services Overview 10-001 2 of 2 adult meets one of the exemption criteria and there are certain situations that will qualify an individual to an extension of time on aid. As of May 1, 2022, the CalWORKs minimum participation standards are the sole set of required hours of participation throughout the customer’s time on aid and are referred to as the CalWORKs Hourly Participation Requirement. Employment Services Employment Services help participants find employment, stay employed, move to higher paying jobs, and eventually to become self-sufficient. The services provided include job search, job preparation, education and training, paid and unpaid work experience, and other services to remove employment barriers such as: Substance Abuse Treatment, Mental Health Services, Domestic Violence Counseling, Housing Support, Family Stabilization Services, and Home Visiting Services. Financial assistance is provided for child care, transportation, and work or training related costs. Participation Requirements If the hourly participation and work activity requirements are not met, participants may be sanctioned which means their cash aid is reduced by removing the adult’s portion of the cash aid. There are some good cause reasons for failure to meet ES requirements and some individuals are exempt from participation. References: •CPG 10-002 Work Participation Requirements •CPG 10-005 Employment Services •CPG 10-020 Exemptions and Good Cause •CPG 10-025 Compliance and Sanctions •CPG 15-100 Time on Aid •CDSS ACL: 97-65, 98-38, 99-27, 99-90, 99-90E, 12-67,12-69, 14-16, 16-21, 17-01, 18-70, 18-123, 20-113, 20-120 •CDSS MPP: 40-107(a)(4)(A), 42-301, MPP 42-302, 42.711, 42.714 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or before July 31, 2025. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: A. Federal Work Participation Rate (WPR) Data Reporting
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Federal Work Participation Rate (WPR) Data Reporting Number Page 10-002.A 1 of 3 Revision Date: October 01, 2026 Background: Counties must report work participation data to the California Department of Social Services (CDSS), and the Federal Data Reporting and Analysis Bureau (FDRAB) monthly, in accordance with County Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF) data reporting instructions. CDSS utilized two systems to collect work participation data: the Research and Development Enterprise Project (RADEP) and Enterprise II Lite (E2Lite) . RADEP was used to collect data for the federal sample for submission to the F ederal Administration for Children and Families (ACF) , including the statewide Work Participation Rate ( WPR). E2Lite was used to collect data for the county sample, which supplements the RADEP sample, monitor s local and regional WPR performance, and calculates each county’s share of any federal fiscal penalty that California may incur due to not meeting WPR requirements. . Purpose: The purpose of this section is to outline federal WPR policies regarding weekly participation, countable core activities, CalSAWS data requirements, and related documentation. This section was revised as the RADEP and E2Lite system s were eliminated and replaced with a streamlined data collection process that pulls directly from the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) administrative data. CDSS further clarified that counties are no longer subject to a WPR penalty passthrough so there is no need to calculate a county-specific WPR via E2Lite. Updates were also made to add clarifying language and guidance regarding core WPR activities, to update the section to the current format, and for sunset review. Policy: There are two WPR measures with distinct requirements : the All Families Rate and the T wo-Parent Families Rate. The All Families WPR is the average of the participation rates for all families, including the Two-Parent Families, for each month in the Federal Fiscal Year (FFY). The Two-Parent WPR only includes the average of the participation rates for families that meet the federal definition of T wo- Parent Families for WPR – having two work-eligible individuals (WEIs) – for each month in the FFY. Federal Requirements for All Families WPR Fifty percent of all families receiving TANF assistance (one-parent and two-parent families combined) must meet the following conditions: • One WEI must participate in federally allowable activities, for an average of thirty hours per week, with the following exceptions: o A single custodial parent with a child under six years old needs to particip ate in core activities for an average of twenty hours per week to meet federal All Families Rate requirements. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Federal Work Participation Rate (WPR) Data Reporting Number Page 10-002.A 2 of 3 o A single head of household under twenty years old, without a high school diploma or equivalent, meets the federal All Families Rate requirements in a month if the individual maintains satisfactory attendance at a secondary school (or equivalent), or participates in education directly related to employment, for an average of twenty hours per week. • At least twenty of the thirty hours must be in core activities. Federal Requirements for Two-Parent Families WPR Ninety percent of two-parent families with two WEIs must meet both of the following requirements: • The WEIs must participate in federally allowable work activities for a combined average of thirty five hours per week. • At least thirty of the thirty five weekly hours must be in core activities. Co re Activities There are nine federal WPR activities that count for the first twenty core hours required for the All Families WPR or the thirty hour core requirement for the Two-Parent Family WPR: • Unsubsidized employment. • Subsidized private-sector employment. • Subsidized public-sector employment. • Work experience. • On-the-job training. • Job search/job readiness assistance. • Community service programs. • Vocational educational training (not to exceed the twelve-month lifetime limit for any individual). • Providing childcare services to an individual who is participating in a community service program. Note: The WPR I nstructions and Definitions guide is available in the Resources section of the CalWORKs and Welfare-To-Work SharePoint sites. sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Federal Work Participation Rate (WPR) Data Reporting Number Page 10-002.A 1 of 3 Revision Date: October 01, 2026 Background: Counties must report work participation data to the California Department of Social Services (CDSS), and the Federal Data Reporting and Analysis Bureau (FDRAB) monthly, in accordance with County Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF) data reporting instructions. CDSS utilized two systems to collect work participation data: the Research and Development Enterprise Project (RADEP) and Enterprise II Lite (E2Lite) . RADEP was used to collect data for the federal sample for submission to the F ederal Administration for Children and Families (ACF) , including the statewide Work Participation Rate ( WPR). E2Lite was used to collect data for the county sample, which supplements the RADEP sample, monitor s local and regional WPR performance, and calculates each county’s share of any federal fiscal penalty that California may incur due to not meeting WPR requirements. . Purpose: The purpose of this section is to outline federal WPR policies regarding weekly participation, countable core activities, CalSAWS data requirements, and related documentation. This section was revised as the RADEP and E2Lite system s were eliminated and replaced with a streamlined data collection process that pulls directly from the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) administrative data. CDSS further clarified that counties are no longer subject to a WPR penalty passthrough so there is no need to calculate a county-specific WPR via E2Lite. Updates were also made to add clarifying language and guidance regarding core WPR activities, to update the section to the current format, and for sunset review. title: A. Welfare-to-Work Sequence Overview
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageSubject: Welfare-to-Work Sequence Overview 10-005.A 1 of 2 Issue Date: 10/8/2014 Effective Date: Upon Receipt Background: The Welfare-to-Work (WTW) Program is the employment and training aspect of CalWORKs (CPG 10- 001.A). WTW is a statewide program designed to enable participants to achieve self-sufficiency through employment. MPP 42-701.1 Policy: Recipients must participate in the WTW program as a condition of eligibility for CalWORKs, unless exempt per CPG 10-020.A. Exempt recipients may voluntarily participate. MPP 42-712.1 Failure or refusal to meet WTW requirements without good cause may result in financial sanction and ineligibility to receive supportive services (CPG 10-025.A). MPP 42-721.2 Procedure: 1. The eligibility worker refers non-exempt recipients and exempt volunteers to participate in WTW after establishing eligibility to CalWORKs (Processing Guide 10-005.A1 in Eligibility Essentials SharePoint site). MPP 42-702.2 2. The Employment Case Manager (ECM) provides employment and training activities and supportive services to participants while ensuring state and federal participation requirements are met (CPG 10-005.C; 10-003.B; and 10-011.A). MPP 42-711.5 and 42-750 3. The ECM initiates the noncompliance process when a participant fails or refuses to meet WTW requirements without good cause. The ECM requests financial sanction for non-exempt participants (CPG 10-020.B and 10-025.A). MPP 42-721 and 42-713.2 4. The ECM schedules a cause determination appointment to allow an opportunity for the noncompliant participant to demonstrate good cause (CPG 10-025.B) MPP 42-721.24 and 42-721.3 5. The Overpayment Specialist Unit (OSU) reviews the sanction request and imposes a financial sanction if the request is valid and good cause does not exist. OSU rescinds the sanction if good cause exists or the participant agrees to a Compliance Plan (Processing Guide 40-200.D1). MPP 42-721.4 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageSubject: Welfare-to-Work Sequence Overview 10-005.A 2 of 2 6. The ECM works with sanctioned individuals to cure their WTW sanction. The ECM notifies the eligibility worker when a sanctioned individual completes their sanction cure (CPG 10-025.D). 7. The eligibility worker lifts the sanction and restores aid to the individual the first day of the month following the date the individual contacted the county to cure the WTW sanction (Processing Guide 40-200.D1). MPP 42-721.48 Impacts: CalFresh: CFPG 63-903.3 and 63-912.4 Child Care: CPG 10-010.A; 10-010.H; 10-010.K; and 10-010.Q References: MPP 42-701.1 Introduction to WTW: http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/ord/entres/getinfo/pdf/6EAS.pdf#page=7 MPP 42-702.2 CalWORKs WTW Enrollment Requirements: http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/ord/entres/getinfo/pdf/6EAS.pdf#page=15 MPP 42-711.5 Assignment of Recipients to WTW Activities: http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/ord/entres/getinfo/pdf/6EAS.pdf#page=19 MPP 42-712.1 Exemptions from WTW Participation: http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/ord/entres/getinfo/pdf/6EAS.pdf#page=42 MPP 42-713.2 Good Cause for Not Participating: http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/ord/entres/getinfo/pdf/6EAS.pdf#page=50 MPP 42-721 Noncompliance with Program Requirements: http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/ord/entres/getinfo/pdf/7EAS.pdf#page=45 MPP 42-721.24 Cause Determination: http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/ord/entres/getinfo/pdf/7EAS.pdf#page=47 MPP 42-721.3 Good Cause for Failure or Refusal to Comply with Program Requirements: http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/ord/entres/getinfo/pdf/7EAS.pdf#page=48 MPP 42-721.4 Sanctions: http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/ord/entres/getinfo/pdf/7EAS.pdf#page=50 MPP 42-721.48 Restoration of Aid: http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/ord/entres/getinfo/pdf/7EAS.pdf#page=52 MPP 42-750 Supportive Services: http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/ord/entres/getinfo/pdf/7EAS.pdf#page=71 Approval for Release: 10/8/2014 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 10/8/2017.

title: C. Summary of Employment Staff Responsibility
content: 10-005 C. Summary of Employment Staff Responsibility Table of Contents The Summary of Employment Staff Responsibility section includes the following information: Section Topic 10-005.C.1 Overview 10-005.C.2 Processing Referrals to WTW 10-005.C.3 Employment Staff Activities 10-005.C.1 Overview The primary responsibility of Employment Staff is to assist Welfare-to- Work (WTW) participants in achieving self-sufficiency through participation in employment and employment related activities. 10-005.C.2 Processing Referrals to WTW Employment Case Managers (ECMs), or other staff designated by the Employment Site Manager, is responsible for ensuring that WTW referrals are processed daily which benefits the recipient family. The following activities are completed by employment staff to process WTW referrals: •Check Alerts daily for WTW referrals on the Display Alert Summary window in CalWIN (include 30 days at a time for search criteria) through the Scheduling Bank Caseload. •Alert “Orientation Needed for WTW” will be displayed on the Display Alert Summary window. Reference: How To #221 - WTW Referral Process for Employment Staff on the CalWIN Intranet. •Check the zip code to ensure the case is in the appropriate region. Refer to the FRC Zip Code list and Employment Services Caseload Banks desk aid in Eligibility Essentials SharePoint site. •If a WTW referral is made to an incorrect region, complete case assignment to the correct region and contact receiving region of referral. •Transfer a WTW case when a participant moves to another region by completing case assignment to appropriate region based on zip code. Upon receipt, the receiving site assigns the case to an ECM and completes case assignment to the ECM. Refer and schedule the participant to a WTW Intake/Appraisal appointment. Reference: How To #214 - Schedule WTW Orientation on the CalWIN Intranet. •At the time of the initial WTW referral, clear the WTW case for an active Child Welfare Services Case. Follow the steps below: Step Action 1 Call the Child Welfare Services, Public Information Line at (858) 694-5191, the name and phone number of the Child Welfare Services Social Worker (CWS SW) will be provided. 2 Narrate CWS information in Case Comments. 3 ECM to contact the CWS SW for client’s information on active CWS case. 10-005.C.3 Employment Staff Activities It is the responsibility of the Employment Case Manager (ECM) to do the following: Step Action 1 Conduct the WTW Intake/Appraisal with the participant, including completion of the Welfare to Work Participant Profile (27-01). Refer to CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) Section 10-005-D. Welfare to Work Appraisal for Intake/Appraisal completion requirements. 2 Evaluate the participant’s plan for supervision of child(ren): If the… Then… WTW Case File does not have a CalWORKs Stage One Child Care Request Form and Payment Rules (CCP7), have the client complete a new CCP7 to document whether or not childcare assistance is needed. client needs childcare services to participate in WTW, but does not have a plan, refer and schedule the client to the Arranging Child Care (ACC) activity in CalWIN and provide the client with Child Care resources. Reference: How To #231 - Refer and Schedule WTW Activities on the CalWIN Intranet. client needs childcare and does have a plan in place, follow the procedure for referring a client to Child Care Case Manager. client’s plan puts the children in an unsafe situation, and they are unwilling to develop a more appropriate plan, refer the situation to Child Welfare Services. Refer to CPG Section 10-010-K. Employment Case Managers Actions for details on completing a child care referral. 3 Refer and schedule to Initial Job Search (JCL or JSN) activity in CalWIN. Reference: How To #213 - Schedule Job Club/Job Search on the CalWIN Intranet. 4 Complete Assessment on clients who are not employed after completion of the Initial Job Search 5 Develop a WTW Plan, assigning activities to meet participation requirement and assist clients with overcoming barriers to employment.

title: D. Employment Services Orientation and Appraisal
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageWelfare-to-Work Orientation and Appraisal 10-005.D 1 of 2 Revision Date: February 1, 2022 Background: CalWORKs recipients who are referred to Employment Services (ES) are required to attend an Orientation (ORE) and complete an Appraisal (APR) to identify abilities, skills, education, and work history, as well as potential barriers to self-sufficiency. The Online CalWORKs Appraisal Tool (OCAT) will be used to document the Appraisal interview and outcome. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to streamline policies and remove Orientation and Appraisal procedures from the program guide. A corresponding Processing Guide (10-005.D1) has been created for this purpose. Policy: ES ORE is to be conducted prior to APR. The ORE and APR must be completed within 15 business days of the ES referral date for individuals who are: •New ES participants •Referred to ES as Exempt Volunteers •Re-referred to ES after a break in aid of 30 calendar days or more, after an exemption lasting 30 days or more, or as mandatory participants after an Exempt Voluntary status has ended •Sanctioned participants referred to ORE/APR to cure the sanction OCAT The OCAT is an online appraisal tool that is used to assist the Employment Case Manager (ECM) to identify abilities, skills, education and work history, as well as identify potential barriers to selfsufficiency. The OCAT will be used to document APR interview discussions, unless the participant declines to complete the OCAT, or the OCAT cannot be administered entirely due to language translation not being appropriate for sensitive sections addressing mental health/substance use or domestic abuse. In those instances, participants must be referred directly to the appropriate evaluations rather than using the OCAT for screening. A participant will not be sanctioned for declining to complete the OCAT. However, a sanction may apply if the participant refuses or fails to complete APR via Form 27-01 without good cause. A participant will be considered compliant with the appraisal process even if they do not wish to disclose answers to specific questions in OCAT, as long as they complete the required APR forms and provide enough information to the ECM to evaluate for the appropriate ES activity. Behavioral Health Screenings Behavioral Health for Substance Use and Mental Health screenings are required at the time of APR for all recipients referred to ES. After ORE is completed, the regional Behavioral Health Services contractor will screen the participant in a private setting. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageWelfare-to-Work Orientation and Appraisal 10-005.D 2 of 2 Learning Disabilities Screening ECMs must offer participants a screening for Learning Disabilities (LD) at ORE/APR. Information must be provided both verbally and in writing about the screening. Domestic Violence If a customer discloses being a victim of domestic violence during APR, the ECM is not required to ask questions related to the alleged perpetrator in the domestic abuse section to avoid placing the victim at further risk of abuse if the participant’s partner is present. OCAT Action Plan and Referral/Evaluation Status An action plan contains specific actions that the ECM assigns to a participant in order to comply with the recommendations in OCAT. An action plan and referral/evaluation status must be completed by the ECM for each recommendation generated by OCAT for each participant. The recommendations may include evaluation for Family Stabilization (FS), Self-Initiated Programs (SIPs), ES exemptions, Job Search (JS), and/or an assessment for education/training. These recommendations are to be used to determine the next best steps for the participant in the ES process and assign the most appropriate activities. Appraisal Summary and Recommendations (ASR) The ASR is a printout from OCAT with the participant’s demographic, household and financial information, strengths, barriers, recommendations, and action items. The ASR does not require a signature. Procedure: Processing Guide 10-005.D1 Impacts: None References: EAS 42-711.52, ACL 15-43, ACL 15-69, ACL 16-67, ACL 21-04 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by February 28, 2025. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: E. Initial Engagement Activities
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page Initial Engagement Activities 10-005.E 1 of 2 Revision Date: 09/1/2018 Background: Effective 1/1/2014, Assembly Bill (AB) 74 modified the WTW sequence to allow individuals who are identified during Appraisal as being in need of Mental Health/Substance Abuse and/or Family Stabilization Services to be engaged in WTW through these barrier removal activities. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to include AB 74 changes and streamline policies and procedures related to initial engagement activities. Policy: Newly referred WTW participants, whose CalWORKs has been approved for the first time or after a break in aid longer than 30 days, are required to participate in Initial Job Search (JS) after Appraisal, unless they meet specific exclusion criteria or are identified as being better served by other initial engagement activities such as Family Stabilization (CPG 10-007.A), Mental Health/Substance Abuse Services (MHS/SAS) and/or Domestic Violence Services (CPG 40-100.O). Initial engagement activities may be assigned in sequence or concurrently prior to the signing of the first WTW plan. Initial Job Search Initial JS activities include looking for suitable job openings through independent and/or supervised Job Search, contacting potential employers, completing applications, submitting resumes, interviewing for jobs and networking. Job Clubs may be used to develop job seeking strategies and inform participants of employer’s expectations and employee’s responsibilities. Initial JS is a core activity that cannot exceed federal limits (up to a total of 6 weeks or up to a total of 12 weeks in a 12-month period when the State of California is considered a “Needy State”). Initial JS is assigned for up to 4 consecutive weeks. Extension(s) beyond the initial 4 weeks may only be approved, one week a time, if needed to complete scheduled job interviews and/or accept employment offer(s) resulting from participation in the previous weeks. If after the 4 consecutive weeks there are no pending interviews or job offers requiring a follow-up, JS extension will not be granted and an Assessment will be completed to assign appropriate activities in a WTW plan. The length of Initial Job Search may be shortened when: •Identified barrier(s) are precluding participation and satisfactory progress in assigned activity •The participant would benefit from education or training in place of Initial Job Search activities Initial Job Search Exclusions The following are allowable exclusions from Initial Job Search: •Participant has barriers that must be addressed with different initial engagement activities •Participant is meeting participation requirements with employment or self-employment •JS activity conflicts with employment or participation in SIP or other approved educational/training activity County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page Initial Engagement Activities 10-005.E 2 of 2 •Participant is a 19-year old parenting teen with no high school diploma or equivalent certificate, who is ineligible to participate in Cal-Learn •Participant is a noncitizen victim of human trafficking, domestic violence or other serious crimes who is not yet authorized to work in the United States (CPG 10-200.A) Mental Health and Substance Abuse Assessment A participant may be referred to MHS and/or SAS as an initial engagement core activities for up to 4 weeks if there is a concern that a mental health and/or substance abuse problem exists that will impair his/her ability to obtain/retain employment, or participate in other WTW activities. An assessment and development of a WTW plan are required to extend these activities beyond the fourweek period. WTW Plan and Treatment Services WTW Plans will be developed based on the results of the mental health and/or substance abuse assessment, and will include appropriate accommodations or restrictions, supportive services, and treatment requirements to meet the participants’ needs. Substance Abuse Services may include: •Assessment/Evaluation •Case management •Treatment and/or Counseling •Monitoring of attendance and satisfactory progress •Referral to or provision of other appropriate services 10-005.E.5 Substance Abuse Treatment and Concurrent Activities Concurrent participation in another WTW activity is required if the participant is in a substance abuse treatment program for longer than six months. WTW participation requirements are considered to be met and concurrent activities are not required if the participant is either: •In a state-licensed residential facility or a certified nonresidential substance abuse program that requires him/her to stay at the program site for at least three hours a day, three days per week, or •Unable to participate in other WTW activities as determined by the treatment provider Procedure: Processing Guide 10-005.E.1 References: All County Letter (ACL) 15-09, Eligibility Assistance Standards (EAS) 42.711.53, CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 10-005.H. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 09/30/2021.

title: F. Assessment or Reassessment
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageAssessment and Reassessment 10-005.F 1 of 3 Revision Date: May 1, 2021 Background: The primary focus of Employment Services (ES) is to help participants set and achieve career goals and build skills necessary to obtain and retain employment. ES participants must be assigned to activities leading to self-sufficiency through employment, education or training. Employment Case Managers (ECMs) utilize the Assessment (ASMT) as the primary tool for developing the first ES plan to assign the most appropriate activities and supportive services. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to provide information per Senate Bill (SB) 1232 on new regulations regarding participants who are enrolled in publicly funded postsecondary education. Policy: ASMT is the evaluation of various factors related to a participant’s employability, such as personal and family needs, work and education history, career goals, areas of strength, skills, and needs for supportive services to remove barriers to employment and participation. The ECM is required to complete an ASMT when the participant is ready to sign the first ES plan after: •Successfully completing Initial Job Search •Being excluded from Initial Job Search or other Initial Engagement activities for a valid reason •Being assigned to Mental Health/Substance Abuse/Family Violence Services in excess of four consecutive weeks, which requires the development of a plan Note: An ASMT is not required to assign activities and supportive services specified in a Family Reunification Plan (CPG 40.183.D). ES Participants Enrolled in Publicly Funded Postsecondary Education ES participants enrolled in publicly funded postsecondary education will complete an ASMT or Reassessment (ASMT2) only for the purpose of assigning appropriate activities to address identified barriers. If ASMT/ASMT2 is completed, the outcome cannot be used to limit or restrict a participant’s choice in educational or training goals. ES participants cannot be prevented from attending school due to a barrier or placed in Noncompliance for refusal to complete ASMT/ASMT2. The ECM will document the reason for refusal to complete ASMT/ASMT2 in case comments. Note: Students not enrolled in publicly funded postsecondary education are still required to complete an ASMT/ASMT2, as applicable, to develop a plan to assign appropriate activities and necessary supportive services. Assessment The ASMT evaluation process includes the following: •Evaluating the participant’s performance in Initial Job Search and outcome County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageAssessment and Reassessment 10-005.F 2 of 3 •Reviewing information gathered during Appraisal and participation in Family Stabilization (FS) or other Initial Engagement activities such as Behavioral Health Services (BHS) and or Initial Job Search •Identifying the participant’s job skills, career, and self-sufficiency goals in relation to local market conditions, educational and training needs, and remaining CalWORKs (CW) and Welfare to Work (WTW) 24-Month Time Clock months •Evaluating potential referral to Work Experience (WEX) or similar training/work programs based on the participant’s work history and job readiness •Completing a comprehensive discussion regarding educational/training opportunities to meet CW federal or minimum standards during the WTW 24-Month Time Clock (WTW 24-MTC) or CW federal standards after the WTW 24-MTC is exhausted •Developing the first ES plan to assign appropriate activities and necessary supportive services to help the participant to achieve career and self-sufficiency goals and address barriers to participation and employment •Working with the participant to create a road map with necessary steps to achieve long and shortterm goals set as the result of the ASMT •Evaluating potential referral to barrier removal activities and programs (e.g. BHS, FS, Housing Support Program (HSP)) Reassessment ASMT2is the evaluation method used by the ECM to develop subsequent ES plans and includes all pertinent elements discussed during ASMT. The ECM will conduct a ASMT2 in the following circumstances: When the Participant… Then the ECM Will … •Completes assigned activities/plan •Requests to participate in additional activities •Does not complete assigned activities for any reason •Does not maintain satisfactory progress in assigned activities •Identify the reason why the participant is not able to complete assigned activities or is not making satisfactory progress •Develop a new plan based upon the ASMT2 outcome May benefit from additional education or training to acquire marketable job skills and address barriers to employment and participation Develop a new plan by assigning additional activities to assist the individual in becoming employed and overcoming barriers Is transferred to another ES site and the newly assigned ECM determines that a ASMT2 is needed due to a change in Registration Status, ES activities, and/or participation hours • Develop a new plan based upon the ASMT2 outcome If the ES participant disagrees with the outcome of the ASMT or ASMT2, the matter must be referred to a Third-Party Assessor who will complete an independent evaluation of the participant’s circumstances, needs and ES plan in question. ES staff and the participant are required to comply with the Third-Party Assessor’s findings and recommendations. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageAssessment and Reassessment 10-005.F 3 of 3 Modified Assessment/Reassessments A Modified ASMT/ASMT2 may be conducted through a telephone call any time an office visit creates an unnecessary burden on the participant due to work/class scheduling conflicts, excessive travelling time or any other valid reasons. Elements evaluated during a Modified ASMT/ASMT2 or an ASMT/ASMT2 completed in person at an ES site are the same. Procedures: CalWORKs Processing Guides 10-005.F.1, 10-300.A.1 and 10-300.D.1 References: Eligibility Assistance Standards (EAS) 42.711.55; ACL 21-04 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by May 31, 2024. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: G. Employment Services Plan
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide Employment Services Plan Number Page 10-005.G 1 of 3 Revision Date: October 01, 2025 Background: Employment Services (ES) participants must be assigned to activities leading to self-sufficiency through employment, education and/or training. These activities are assigned through an ES plan using the Welfare-To-Work Plan Activity Assignment (WTW 2) form after the participant’s initial engagement. Per state regulations, an ES plan must include activities and services designed to remove barriers to participation and employment leading to self-sufficiency. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to provide guidance on ES plan requirements for Student Training and Education Program (STEP) participants attending publicly funded or nonprofit postsecondary educational institutions per Senate Bill (SB) 768. Policy: Assessment ES participants will be assessed for the following items when developing an ES plan:  Work history and job readiness  Education level and vocational interest and goals  Learning Disabilities (LD)  Mental Health, Substance Use Disorder, Domestic Violence  Basic reading/math competencies  English language skills  Local labor market conditions  Other needs, such as Family Stabilization and Housing Procedure: Timeframe All non-exempt customers are required to sign an ES plan within 90 calendar days of whichever occurs first: the completion of initial Job Search or other initial engagement activities, the date the customer’s eligibility for cash aid is determined, or the date the customer is required to participate in ES. The 90-day period to develop an ES plan does not include the time that a participant spends in good cause determination, compliance or sanction curing processes, or time between the date an LD evaluation appointment is scheduled and the date the final report is received (up to a maximum of 90 days). The 90-day period will resume after the final report from the LD evaluator is received, or on the 91st day if the final report has not been received. All participants are required to sign an ES plan except participants who are assigned to initial engagement activities as referenced in Processing Guide 10-005.E1. Elements of the ES Plan All ES plans will include the following:  Participation status County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide Employment Services Plan Number Page 10-005.G 2 of 3  Total hourly requirements  Activities, location, schedule and hours  Date when participation verification is due  Standards for maintaining satisfactory progress  ES supportive services, including accommodations  Participant's certification, including rights and responsibilities  Date to change terms of the ES Plan  Participant and Employment Case Manager (ECM) signature/date Change to an ES Plan Any time there is a change in a participant's current activity, a new ES plan is required. Participants have:  30 days from the beginning of their initial ES activity to request a change or reassignment to another activity Note: This is only available once in a lifetime to each participant  3 business days after signing an ES plan to evaluate and request changes to the terms of the plan If the participant and the ECM are unable to reach an agreement on the ES plan, the matter must be referred to a Third-Party Assessor for a review of the participant's assessment and ES plan. Prior to making the third-party referral, the ECM must contact their assigned Self-Sufficiency Services (SSS) Program Specialist to review the request and the ES plan to ensure the plan is suitable for the participant's self-sufficiency goals. The ECM is required to contact the participant and schedule an appointment to complete a reassessment prior to the expiration of the current ES plan. The ECM will document all efforts to contact the participant and attempt to conduct the reassessment to avoid gaps in services. Backdating of an ES Plan Backdating of an ES activity start date on the WTW 2 is only allowed when a participant contacts the ECM timely to report new employment or a new educational activity and:  The participant is unable to attend an appointment to complete a WTW 2 due to work or school schedule conflicts  The ECM does not follow-up with the participant timely and the WTW 2 is not signed within the appropriate time frames due to ECM error Limited and Non-English-Speaking Participants The ES plan must be provided in a language that is understood by the participant. When the ES plan is not available in the participant's preferred language, bilingual staff or interpreter services must be provided. Use of bilingual staff or interpreter services during the development of the ES plan must be clearly documented in a journal entry. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide Employment Services Plan Number Page 10-005.G 3 of 3 Enrollment in Publicly Funded or Nonprofit Postsecondary Education ES participants enrolled in publicly funded or nonprofit postsecondary educational institutions are required to sign a WTW 2 plan each semester/quarter to receive supportive services. If enrollment verification is obtained, the ECM will develop/sign the WTW 2 plan with the participant and issue an Advance Standard Payment (ASP) at least 10 calendar days prior to the beginning of the academic period. If enrollment verification is not obtained at least 10 calendar days prior to the beginning of the academic period, the ECM will develop/sign the WTW 2 plan with the participant and issue an ASP no later than 10 calendar days from the date of receipt of all required items. If the participant provided school enrollment verification and the WTW 2 plan is not developed/signed timely with the participant for the next academic period, an ASP will be issued to the participant. The ECM will follow-up with the participant regarding the development and signing of any ES plans as required. See Processing Guide 10-011.A2 Ancillary Supportive Services for information regarding ASP and reimbursements. Important: The ECM will discuss the importance of reporting school enrollment as soon as possible with the participant to ensure timely issuance of an ASP and successful participation. Procedure: Processing Guide 10-005.G1 References: Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 42-711.4-.8, 42-714.2, 42.750.2-.4 All County Information Notices (ACIN) 1-03-19 All County Letter (ACL) 15-80, 20-120, 21-04, 21-75E, 22-80, 24-32 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by October 31, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: H. Employment Services Activities
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Activities Number Page 10-005.H 1 of 5 Revision Date: May 1, 2022 Background: Employment Services (ES) participants must be assigned to employment, education and/or training activities, including barrier removal activities, which will lead to self-sufficiency. Participants may receive supportive services to ensure participation and satisfactory progress. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to remove policy referencing the Welfare-to-Work 24-Month Time Clock (24-MTC). Per Assembly Bill AB 79, 24 -MTC and the CalWORKs federal standards have been repealed. AB 79 establishes the CalWORKs minimum standards as the sole set of CalWORKs hourly participation requirements throughout their time on aid. Policy: When determining appropriate ES activities, consideration must be given to the participant’s: • Employment history, education level, career goals and employability • English language and basic reading/math skills • Destabilizing factors (i.e. homelessness, mental health, substance use, domestic violence) • Learning disabilities • Remaining months on the CalWORKs 60-month time limit ES Activities • Adult Basic Education (ABE): ABE is assigned when a participant lacks basic literacy, mathematics skills or English language skills • Behavioral Health Services (BHS): BHS includes the following activities: Family Violence Services (FVS): FVS assists participants who are past or present victims of domestic violence to obtain employment and become self-sufficient Mental Health Services (MHS): MHS helps participants with mental health issues that impair their ability to obtain/retain employment and/or participate in ES activities. Substance Use Disorder (SUD): SUD provides counseling and treatment that enable participants to address issues that impair their ability to obtain/retain employment and/or participate in ES activities See CPG 10-005.E for FVS/MHS/SUD as initial engagement activities • Community Service (CS): CS is a supervised training activity performed in the public or private non-profit sector that provides participants with basic job skills while meeting a community need. CS has a 12 consecutive month lifetime limit County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Activities Number Page 10-005.H 2 of 5 • Education Directly Related to Employment (ERE): ERE is education/training related to a specific job or job offer. Participants may also be assigned to ERE to obtain a high school diploma/certificate of high school equivalency • English as a Second Language (ESL): ESL addresses language barriers for participants with limited English skills to improve their employability • Expanded Subsidized Employment (ESE): ESE offers work -ready participants the opportunity to obtain part -time or full -time subsidized employment which may lead to future unsubsidized employment and self-sufficiency • Expanded Work Experience (EWE): EWE offers participants the opportunity to acquire or enhance job skills in the work environment through paid on-the-job training to become work-ready • Family Stabilization (FS): FS is designed to ensure a basic level of stability within a family prior to, or concurrently with, participation in ES activities See CPG 10-005.E. for FS as initial engagement activity • Home Visiting Program (HVP): HVP is a voluntary evidence-based program model that pairs new parents with a nurse, or other trained professional, who makes regular visits to the participant’s home or other agreed upon meeting place to provide guidance, coaching, access to prenatal and postnatal care, and other health and social services • Job Search/Job Readiness (JS): JS may be assigned as an initial engagement activity to prepare the participant to obtain or retain employment or in an ES plan to address sudden unemployment or improve current employment. JS activities may be completed at approved locations and/or online • Job Skills Training Directly Related to Employment (ERT): ERT is training or education that enables a participant to acquire or improve job skills and obtain vocational certification necessary to attain and retain employment. ERT may include: o Customized or general training to prepare an individual for employment, including literacy and language instruction and other remedial education leading to employment o Four-year bachelor’s degree programs directly related to a specific job or occupation • Other Activities Necessary to Assist in Obtaining Employment (OAN/MIS): OAN/MIS is assigned to assist a participant in removing barriers to employment. OAN/MIS activities may include, but are not limited to, parenting/life skill classes, acculturation classes, consumer education or job fairs. These activities are captured on the WTW2 as ‘Other Activity to Remove Barriers to Employment’ . H owever, assignment and p articipation hours will be documented in CalWIN under ‘Misc. One-Day Group’ (MIS) if the activity is scheduled to last only one day, or under ‘Other Activities Necessary’ (OAN) if scheduled to last longer • Secondary School or Preparation for a Certificate of General Educational Development (GED): County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Activities Number Page 10-005.H 3 of 5 GED is an activity for participants who do not have a high school diploma or equivalent. GED may include regular/online classes and ESL classes as needed. If the participant chooses not to pursue a high school diploma or equivalent, the choice must be documented in the “Additional Comments” section of the ES Plan or in other written documentation signed by the participant and attached to the plan • Self-Employment (SLE): SLE may be assigned for a minimum of six months to give the participant the opportunity to establish a profitable business leading to self-sufficiency. This six-month period is only offered once and does NOT restart with each new SLE assignment. After the initial six-month period, monthly net earnings must average at, or above, federal minimum wage for the participant to continue in an assigned SLE activity • Unsubsidized Full Time Employment (FTE) or Part Time Employment (PTE) FTE or PTE is unsubsidized employment in the public or private sector • Vocational Education and Training (VTR): VTR consists of organized educational programs which prepare participants for employment in current or emerging occupations . VTR may include approved Self -Initiated Plans (SIPs), undergraduate programs offered at local universities/ colleges or online, teaching credential programs, adult education, occupational programs, and Vocational English-as Second Language (VESL) for ESL classes with a work-related component • Work Experience (WEX): WEX is an unpaid ES training activity in the public or private sector to provide basic job skills and work experience or enhance existing skills in a position that may lead to unsubsidized employment • Work Study (WS): WS is employment in the public or private sector, related to the student’s course of study, for which the employer receives a subsidy from T emporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF)/CalWORKs or other public funds to offset wages and other costs of employing CalWORKs recipients Additional Provisions for Educational Activities • Self-Initiated Plan (SIP): o Participants enrolled in self-initiated education/training at the time of Appraisal will be evaluated for exclusion from Job Search as an initial engagement activity if the program leads to an Undergraduate Degree/Certificate, an Associate Degree for trans fer to a university or a California Teaching Credential program o Participants may only be evaluated for a SIP once in their CalWORKs lifetime, either at the time of Appraisal or if the Employment Case Manager (ECM) failed to evaluate the participant for a SIP during the Appraisal (Administrative Error) o Participants enrolled in an education/training activity not meeting SIP requirements will be allowed to continue the program as VTR, ERT or ERE only until the next educational quarter or semester break. After that, a new plan will be developed to assign other appropriate activities County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Activities Number Page 10-005.H 4 of 5 o Exempt individuals who volunteer to participate in ES may qualify for SIPs if they did not complete an Appraisal or were not enrolled in a SIP prior to becoming exempt o Participants may resume participation in a previously approved SIP if it was interrupted with Good Cause and the education/training program still meets SIP approval criteria o SIP participants are required to complete an average of 30 hours per week to reach thei r Assistance Unit (AU) hourly requirement, unless they are single parents with a child in the home who is under the age of six (CPG 10-005.G) • Online Courses: Required online courses may be approved as ABE, VTR, ERT or ERE when provided through colleges, adult education, regional occupational centers, or other qualifying educational institutions. Online classes are subject to the same verification requirements as on campus classes • Study Time: Hours spent in supervised study time and up to one hour of unsupervised study time for each hour of class and/or supervised lab time may be included in ES plans as part of ABE, GED, ESL, ERE, activities. Total study time must not exceed the hours required or recommended by the educational program, up to allowable limits. See below for exceptions to this provision • Enrollment in Publicly Funded Postsecondary Education: ES participants enrolled in publicly funded postsecondary education are allowed three hours of study time per week for each academic unit towards hourly participation requirements, with no distinction between supervised and unsupervised study time. Academic units, as defined by the educational provider, and the counting of study time include both credit and non-credit classes Note: Post-secondary education, also called higher education, is an optional level of schooling beyond what is required by law in most places. University learning is one of the most common examples, but community colleges, vocational schools, and trade programs also qualify. Satisfactory Participation/Progress ES participants are required to maintain satisfactory progress in each assigned activity and complete the required number of hours listed in the ES Plan. Satisfactory participation and progress are defined by the educational institution, employer, or service provider. ECMs are required to evaluate satisfactory participation and progress monthly and document the evaluation outcome. Supervision of ES Activities ES activities are supervised and monitored by the employer, the work site, or service provider at the same level as other employees, students, or trainees of the organization. Procedure: Processing Guide 10-005.H1 References: All County Letters (ACLs) No. 15-80, 17-78, 18-115,19-42, 21-04, 20-120 Eligibility Assistance Standards (EAS) 42-716, 42-716.61 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Activities Number Page 10-005.H 5 of 5 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by May 31, 2025. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Activities Number Page 10-005.H 1 of 5 Revision Date: May 1, 2022 Background: Employment Services (ES) participants must be assigned to employment, education and/or training activities, including barrier removal activities, which will lead to self-sufficiency. Participants may receive supportive services to ensure participation and satisfactory progress. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to remove policy referencing the Welfare-to-Work 24-Month Time Clock (24-MTC). Per Assembly Bill AB 79, 24 -MTC and the CalWORKs federal standards have been repealed. AB 79 establishes the CalWORKs minimum standards as the sole set of CalWORKs hourly participation requirements throughout their time on aid. Policy: When determining appropriate ES activities, consideration must be given to the participant’s: • Employment history, education level, career goals and employability • English language and basic reading/math skills • Destabilizing factors (i.e. homelessness, mental health, substance use, domestic violence) • Learning disabilities • Remaining months on the CalWORKs 60-month time limit ES Activities • Adult Basic Education (ABE): ABE is assigned when a participant lacks basic literacy, mathematics skills or English language skills • Behavioral Health Services (BHS): BHS includes the following activities: Family Violence Services (FVS): FVS assists participants who are past or present victims of domestic violence to obtain employment and become self-sufficient Mental Health Services (MHS): MHS helps participants with mental health issues that impair their ability to obtain/retain employment and/or participate in ES activities. Substance Use Disorder (SUD): SUD provides counseling and treatment that enable participants to address issues that impair their ability to obtain/retain employment and/or participate in ES activities See CPG 10-005.E for FVS/MHS/SUD as initial engagement activities • Community Service (CS): CS is a supervised training activity performed in the public or private non-profit sector that provides participants with basic job skills while meeting a community need. CS has a 12 consecutive month lifetime limit County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Activities Number Page 10-005.H 2 of 5 • Education Directly Related to Employment (ERE): ERE is education/training related to a specific job or job offer. Participants may also be assigned to ERE to obtain a high school diploma/certificate of high school equivalency • English as a Second Language (ESL): ESL addresses language barriers for participants with limited English skills to improve their employability • Expanded Subsidized Employment (ESE): ESE offers work -ready participants the opportunity to obtain part -time or full -time subsidized employment which may lead to future unsubsidized employment and self-sufficiency • Expanded Work Experience (EWE): EWE offers participants the opportunity to acquire or enhance job skills in the work environment through paid on-the-job training to become work-ready • Family Stabilization (FS): FS is designed to ensure a basic level of stability within a family prior to, or concurrently with, participation in ES activities See CPG 10-005.E. for FS as initial engagement activity • Home Visiting Program (HVP): HVP is a voluntary evidence-based program model that pairs new parents with a nurse, or other trained professional, who makes regular visits to the participant’s home or other agreed upon meeting place to provide guidance, coaching, access to prenatal and postnatal care, and other health and social services • Job Search/Job Readiness (JS): JS may be assigned as an initial engagement activity to prepare the participant to obtain or retain employment or in an ES plan to address sudden unemployment or improve current employment. title: I. Case Transfers and Returns Between Regions
content: Page 1 of 2 I. Case Transfers and Returns Between Regions Case Transfer Overview When a Welfare-to-Work (WTW) participant moves from one county region to another, the current Employment Case Manager must transfer the case to the new region where the participant now resides for continued services. Status Codes for Transfer Cases Cases in active status can be transferred. Cases with sanctioned and non-compliant individuals in non-active statuses can be transferred when mutual agreement is reached between the sending and receiving regions. Transfer of Companion Cases Companion cases (spouse, child, teen of the participant) must be transferred together. Transfer Procedures for WTW Cases Refer to CalWORKs Processing Guide 10-260.A.1 WTW Document Capture Activities Transferring Sanctioned and/or Compliance Plan Cases Cases may not be transferred when there is a pending sanction or pending completion of a compliance plan, except on a case-by-case basis when mutual agreement is reached between the sending and receiving region. Regions should assign the authority to accept cases in non-active status to a specific staff level or person. When a WTW sanctioned individual moves and it is in their best interest to have his or her WTW case transferred to the new region of residence to facilitate a conciliation or sanction “cure”, the sending region should follow the procedure below: Step Action 1 Contact the new region and request acceptance of sanction case transfer. •If the region agrees to accept the case, then continue to Step 2. 2 Complete the WTW Case Transfer/Closing Checklist (27-313) ensuring all appropriate areas are checked. •Write in “Comments” section that the participant is in sanctioned or noncompliance status. •Note the name of the person in the receiving region who agreed to accept the case. 3 Ensure that case is sent to receiving region within 24 hours of the time the mutual agreement was reached for transfer. Timing of Transfer of Cases may not be transferred after the 20 th of the month unless supportive service payments for the next month have been approved and issued. This is to ensure that Page 2 of 2 Case all necessary supportive payments are issued timely. Transfers to Incorrect Regions Cases transferred to an inappropriate region will be returned to the sending region. Former Refugee Cases Unless a Federal Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) waiver is in effect, refugee cases, for people who have been in the United States for five or more years, are to be transferred from the Refugee WTW Employment Services provider regions to the mainstream WTW Regions. Case Return Regions must keep the number of returned cases to the lowest level possible to avoid unnecessary disruption of services, inconvenience and confusion to participants. A case shall only be returned if at least one of the following occurs: 1. One of the following required forms is missing, as appropriate: •Signed WTW 1 •Completed assessment with case comments •Current and appropriate WTW Plan Activities open in CalWIN must match assigned activities on the WTW Plan Note: In a situation where the applicant has not reached the stage for obtaining a particular form, the case cannot be returned for missing such a form. 2. There are no appropriate CalWIN participation entries for the last month. 3. A required service is not provided. Example: The case record indicates the participant requested ancillary payments for tools to attend an approved vocational training and there is no record of issuance of such payment, nor is there explanation for non-issuance. Since supportive services were not approved, it is possible that the participant may not be able to participate in required activities. 4. A required referral is not made. Example: The Simple Screening Instrument for Substance Abuse indicates a high degree of abuse but a referral was not made to the County Alcohol and Drug Services.

title: K. Employment Services Participation for Teens
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Participation for Teens Number Page 10-005.K 1 of 4 Revision Date: October 1, 2025 Backgr ound: State regulations require teen customers ages 16 and 17 years old receiving CalWORKs benefits to be referred to Employment Services (ES) as mandatory participants when the school attendance exemption criteria, as defined in CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 10-020.A, are not met. Not e: Chronic truancy and post -secondary education are defined in CPG sections 42-100.B and 10- 020.A. Pur pose: The purpose of this section is to provide guidance regarding ES participation requirements for teen customers who receive CalWORKs assistance. The purpo se of this revision is to incorporate regulation changes that removed the once- in-a-lifetime ES participation exemption limit for 16 and 17 year old teens who are required to attend school, remove references regarding the obsolete Welfare To Work (WTW) 24-Month Time Clock, update references, add clarifying language, and to complete the sunset review. Pol icy: Teen ES Program Requirements Teen customers ages 16 to 18 years old receiving CalWORKs assistance are exempt from ES participation if attending an educational program in grade 12 or below , or attending a vocational or technical school on a full-time basis as defined by the school/school program. Teens wi ll be referred to ES if deemed a chronic truant, not meeting the school attendance requirement, or if they have graduated from high school or the equivalent and are not meeting the post-secondary education exemption, including former Cal-Learn teens. These teens are required to participate in ES and are subject to ES program requirements. This includes teens who have completed participation in the Cal-Learn program. Teens wi ll be evaluated for ES exemptions (see CPG 10-020.A for a list of qualifying exemptions) and, if determined exempt, may participate in ES voluntarily. Teens w ho are referred to ES will attend Orientation and Appraisal. The Employment Case Manager (ECM) will also conduct an Assessment to evaluate the teen’s individual service needs and develop an ES plan that considers their educational and occupational goals. Requa lifying for ES Student Exemption for Teens 16 and 17 Years Old Teens aged 16 and 17 years old who lose their ES exemption for not meeting the student criteria, may requalify for the student exemption from ES participation by resuming full -time school attendance in high school, or a vocational or technical school and providing supporting documentation from their school/school program. This exemption does not apply to pregnant or parenting teens in the Cal-Learn program. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Participation for Teens Number Page 10-005.K 2 of 4 Note: Teens referred to ES after being deemed as chronic truants cannot requalify under the student exemption and will participate in ES until completion of secondary school to avoid a school attendance penalty. Only 16 and 17 year old teens who resume and verify full-time school attendance can requalify for the exemption from ES participation. E S Forms, Notices, and Appointments All ES forms and notices sent to the teen will also be addressed and sent to their parent/caretaker . Teens are required to sign all applicable ES forms, including the ES plan. Teens will attend all ES appointments. The parent/caretaker is not required to attend the teen’s ES appointments but may do so. The parent/caretaker may not attend ES appointments or sign any required ES documents on behalf of the teen. S chool Attendance Verifications Documentation to verify regular school attendance may include monthly attendance records, classroom time sheets, report cards, etc. S upportive Services Supportive services may be issued to the extent needed for the teen to attend school and be successful in their activities. The payments will be issued to the teen’s parent/caretaker’s EBT account. ES Participation Requirements and Time Clocks Teens are not subject to the following requirements: • Minimum hourly ES participation. • CalWORKs Time on Aid (TOA). The r equired number of participation hours for the teen’s ES plan may not exceed 20 average hours per week. Any hours assigned beyond 20 average hours per week will be considered voluntary. The t een’s required participation or noncompliance: • Has no effect on the parent’s TOA clock. • Cannot contribute toward the parent’s participation requirements, nor can the parent contribute hours toward the teen’s participation requirements. A s a reminder, a parent’s ES plan will reflect their child’s school attendance requirements and any participation required by the parent to ensure their child’s school attendance. C alFresh Sanctions Non head of household 16 and 17 year old teens are exempt from CalFresh work registration requirements and are not subject to CalFresh sanctions if they fail to meet ES program requirements. (However, if the head of household teen fail s to comply with ES program requirements, they may be subject to a CalFresh sanction which will result in a reduction to the household’s CalFresh allotment amount.) ES Pla n Requirements for Teens Not Regularly Attending High School (HS) The sole purpose of an ES plan for a teen who is not regularly attending high school is to ensure that the teen completes high school or its equivalent. The teen may voluntarily participate in other ES County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Participation for Teens Number Page 10-005.K 3 of 4 activities if the activities do not interfere with their school attendance. The teen will sign the ES plan in agreement with their assigned ES activities . Non-participation in voluntary activities is not considered non-compliance. Teens referred to ES for the sole purpose of completing high school or its equivalent will be identified on the ES plan as participating in, “satisfactory progress in a secondary school or in a course leading to a certificate of general educational development ”, along with other approved activities that do not interfere with the primary school activity. If a teen is unable to comply with the ES requirement because they have not been enrolled in a secondary school, the ECM will assist them in becoming enrolled and allow good cause until they are enrolled. N oncompliance with ES for Teens Not Regularly Attending HS A teen who fails to comply, without good cause, with their required ES plan activity is subject to a school attendance penalty, not an ES sanction. A school attendance penalty will not be applied if the teen meets an ES exception reason. R estoration of Aid for Teens Not Regularly Attending HS Once imposed, the school attendance penalty will continue unless: • Documentation is received that verifies the teen is no longer deemed a chronic truant. • The teen complies with their ES plan. • Good cause exists. • An ES exemption/exception reason is met. • The teen receives a high school diploma or equivalent. C onclusion of ES Participation for Teens Not Regularly Attending HS Verification issued by the school will be provided to demonstrate that the teen has earned a high school diploma or the equivalent . If the teen continues to be eligible for CalWORKs, and mandatory ES participation is required, a new ES plan would be developed. ES P lan Requirements for Teens Who Completed HS or Equivalent ES plans for teens who complete HS or equivalent: • May include any ES activity leading to further education, job preparation, and employment. • Will indicate all ES activities and hours . • Will indicate a required number of weekly participation hours agreed upon by the ECM and teen – not to exceed 20 hours per week. • Will be signed by the teen. N oncompliance with ES for Teens Who Completed HS or Equivalent Teens who have completed high school or the equivalent are subject to ES noncompliance and sanction regulations. These teens may cure a sanction by participating in a sanction curing plan and performing the activities t hey previously failed or refused to perform, or other appropriate activit ies determined by the ECM. P rocedure: Processing Guide 10-005.K1 - ES Activities for High School Students. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Participation for Teens Number Page 10-005.K 4 of 4 References: EAS 42-712, 42-713, 42-719. ACL No. 15-22, 16-99, 23-30. S unset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by October 31, 2028. A pproval for Release: R ick Wanne, Director Self Sufficiency Services
