title: A. Learning Disabilities
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Learning Disabilities Number Page 10-006.A 1 of 4 Revision Date: July 1, 2026 Background: Learning Disabilities (LD) may interfere with an Employment Services (ES) participant’s ability to obtain or retain employment or participate in certain ES activities. In accordance with state policy, the ES program offers screening and evaluation for LD to participants in order to identify potential learning needs that may impact their learning skills, such as reading, writing, or math that can, in turn, interfere with other life skills such as organization, time planning, abstract reasoning, long- or short -term memory and attention. The ES program can provide reasonable accommodations needed to help the participant be successful in completing their ES activities. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to provide staff clarification regarding LD services. In addition, this section has been rereviewed for sunset review. Policy: Information and Screening Requirements Information about the screening process for LD and an offer for a screening must be provided to all participants both, verbally and in writing, at the first ES contact (such as orientation or appraisal). The LD information must include a description of the purpose and benefits of having a screening and evaluation. The LD screening must be provided in the participant’s primary language if there is a validated screening tool available in that language. If no validated screening tool exists in the participant's primary language, the participant may request a direct referral for a LD evaluation. Participants have the right to decline a LD screening and evaluation. They cannot be sanctioned for refusing to be screened or evaluated. If a participant initially waives the screening and later request it, the screening must be performed as soon as possible prior to the participant being assigned to another ES activity. The participant will be granted good cause for not participating in their assigned activity when their screening appointment conflicts with their activity schedule. LD Evaluation A referral for a LD evaluation will be completed if a n ES participant is suspected of having a learning disability and agrees to an evaluation. This includes individuals who meet at least one of the following criteria: • Have been identified as having a potential LD based on the LD screening score. • Are suspected of having a LD even if the screening did not indicate a potential LD. • Were previously identified as having a LD (such as attending special education classes). • Have requested a referral to a LD evaluation because no validated screening too l exists in their primary language. Only trained professionals who use recognized and validated assessment tools are authorized County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Learning Disabilities Number Page 10-006.A 2 of 4 to conduct LD evaluations. If a participant declines to participate in an LD evaluation, their ES activities will not include any accommodations for LD. LD evaluations include: • Discussion about learning/education experiences. • Observations of work habits and classroom ability. • Testing for learning aptitudes and vocational interests. • Evaluation for other impairments to participate in ES activities. LD Evaluation Report The ES participant will receive a copy of the LD Evaluation Report and an explanation of the evaluation results from the LD Specialist during an exit interview or from their Employment Case Manager (ECM). The LD evaluation report must include, at a minimum, the following core information: • Relevant vocational/educational background and interests. • General aptitude/cognitive level. • Areas of strength and areas of deficiency. • Summary of the participants’ conditions and services needed. The LD evaluation report may also include: • Local resources to assist participants. • Documentation of recommended accommodation and/or assistive technology needs. • Discussion of the participant's short/long-term employment goals and general/specific vocational recommendations. If a participant provides previous LD evaluation results that were conducted outside of the ES program and the evaluation does not contain information to determine the participant’s current ability to become employable, an evaluation will be done by ES to determine whether to accept the results or to obtain a second opinion by referring the participant for another evaluation. Response to the Evaluation Report If it is determined that the participant did not have a LD, the participant must begin or resume their ES assignment without special accommodation. If it is determined that the participant does have a LD that interferes with obtaining or retaining employment or participating in an ES activity, the ECM will develop or modify with the participant form WTW 2, Welfare to Work (WTW) Plan Activity Assignment, to reflect the appropriate activities and accommodations based on the results of the LD evaluation. The participant has the right to file for a state hearing if they disagree with the county’s actions based on the evaluation. Confidentiality The participant's medical records and written LD evaluations are confidential documents and are County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Learning Disabilities Number Page 10-006.A 3 of 4 only to be shared with other counties, other LD evaluators, and ES partner agencies, on a "needto-know" basis. The participant's written consent , on form WTW 20 - Permission to Release Learning Disabilities Information, must be obtained for this information to be shared with individuals or organizations outside of ES. LD Participation Requirements Unless exempt from participation, an individual with a LD generally must participate for the required number of hours. If the LD Evaluation Report recommends fewer hours of participation, the ECM may modify the WTW 2 form as necessary to reflect a reasonable accommodation to help the participant be successful in completing their ES activities. For participants with a LD, the required hours of participation may include supplemental activities that support the participant's employment goals and are consistent with the recommendations of the LD Evaluation Report and WTW 2, such as, but not limited to: • Adult Basic Education. • Literacy tutoring. • Additional study time. Good Cause, Compliance, and Sanctions If a LD is confirmed through an evaluation during a part icipant's good cause determination or compliance process , the ECM must determine if the disability contributed to the participant's failure to comply. If it is determined that the LD impacts the participant's ability to participate: • The participant will be considered to have good cause for their failure to participate in the required hours, or if appropriate, to be exempt from ES activities. • The participant will not be considered to have an instance of noncompliance. • The ECM must also review the ES activity and/or WTW 2 and modify it as needed to accommodate the participant's disability. If a LD is confirmed through an evaluation for a participant who is attempting to stop an ES sanction, the ECM must determine if the disability contributed to the participant's noncompliance. If it is determined that the LD was a contributing factor to becoming non-compliant, the ECM will: • Rescind the sanction, and the participant will not be considered to have an instance of noncompliance. • Review the ES activity, and ES plan and modify it appropriately for the participant's disability. If the LD was not a contributing factor to noncompliance, the noncompliance process will continue as required. Inter-County Transfers of Individuals with LD When a CalWORKs recipient with a verified LD moves from one county to another, the sending county must, with the participant's written permission, forward a copy of the written LD evaluation to the receiving county. The receiving county must develop a new, or modify the existing, WTW2 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Learning Disabilities Number Page 10-006.A 4 of 4 as necessary, to reflect appropriate activities and necessary reasonable accommodations. When the participant refuses to give permission for the sending county to forward the LD evaluation to the receiving county, the participant will not have good cause for failure to participate in the receiving county if the receiving county fails to provide services and accommodation based on the LD. sections.heading: 10-006Learning Disabilities
sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Learning Disabilities Number Page 10-006.A 1 of 4 Revision Date: July 1, 2026 Background: Learning Disabilities (LD) may interfere with an Employment Services (ES) participant’s ability to obtain or retain employment or participate in certain ES activities. In accordance with state policy, the ES program offers screening and evaluation for LD to participants in order to identify potential learning needs that may impact their learning skills, such as reading, writing, or math that can, in turn, interfere with other life skills such as organization, time planning, abstract reasoning, long- or short -term memory and attention. The ES program can provide reasonable accommodations needed to help the participant be successful in completing their ES activities. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to provide staff clarification regarding LD services. In addition, this section has been rereviewed for sunset review. Policy: Information and Screening Requirements Information about the screening process for LD and an offer for a screening must be provided to all participants both, verbally and in writing, at the first ES contact (such as orientation or appraisal). The LD information must include a description of the purpose and benefits of having a screening and evaluation. The LD screening must be provided in the participant’s primary language if there is a validated screening tool available in that language. If no validated screening tool exists in the participant's primary language, the participant may request a direct referral for a LD evaluation. Participants have the right to decline a LD screening and evaluation. They cannot be sanctioned for refusing to be screened or evaluated. If a participant initially waives the screening and later request it, the screening must be performed as soon as possible prior to the participant being assigned to another ES activity. The participant will be granted good cause for not participating in their assigned activity when their screening appointment conflicts with their activity schedule. LD Evaluation A referral for a LD evaluation will be completed if a n ES participant is suspected of having a learning disability and agrees to an evaluation. This includes individuals who meet at least one of the following criteria: • Have been identified as having a potential LD based on the LD screening score. • Are suspected of having a LD even if the screening did not indicate a potential LD. • Were previously identified as having a LD (such as attending special education classes). • Have requested a referral to a LD evaluation because no validated screening too l exists in their primary language. Only trained professionals who use recognized and validated assessment tools are authorized County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Learning Disabilities Number Page 10-006.A 2 of 4 to conduct LD evaluations. If a participant declines to participate in an LD evaluation, their ES activities will not include any accommodations for LD. LD evaluations include: • Discussion about learning/education experiences. • Observations of work habits and classroom ability. • Testing for learning aptitudes and vocational interests. • Evaluation for other impairments to participate in ES activities. LD Evaluation Report The ES participant will receive a copy of the LD Evaluation Report and an explanation of the evaluation results from the LD Specialist during an exit interview or from their Employment Case Manager (ECM). The LD evaluation report must include, at a minimum, the following core information: • Relevant vocational/educational background and interests. • General aptitude/cognitive level. • Areas of strength and areas of deficiency. • Summary of the participants’ conditions and services needed. title: A. Family Stabilization
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Family Stabilization Number 10-007.A Page 1 of 3 Revision Date: May 1, 2022 Background: Individuals may participate in the Family Stabilization (FS) program to overcome an emergency that is destabilizing their family and impairing their participation to Employment Services (ES) activities. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to remove policy referencing the Welfare to Work 24-Month Time Clock (24-MTC). Per Assembly Bill AB 79, 24-MTC and the CalWORKs federal standards have been repealed effective May 1, 2022. AB 79 establishes the CalWORKs minimum standards as the sole set of CalWORKs hourly participation requirements throughout their time on aid. Policy: Qualifying Emergencies CalWORKs families may participate in the FS program if the family is experiencing an emergency that interferes with employment and ES participation. Qualifying emergencies may include, but are not limited to, domestic violence, behavioral health needs, housing and utility needs, and essential vehicle repairs. Family Eligibility The CalWORKs Assistance Unit (AU) must include an aided individual whose ability to participate in the ES program is affected by the reported emergency. The FS request will not be approved if CalWORKs eligibility is not yet determined or expected to continue in the future month. FS participants are required to sign form FS2 Family Stabilization Plan listing assigned activities and necessary supportive services. Eligible family members may include: • • Noncompliant or sanctioned individuals who sign a Compliance Plan or Sanction Cure Plan Non-aided parents who are eligible to ES services while in a Family Reunification Plan Participation Requirement FS participants are not subject to the average 20/30/35 weekly hour requirements when unable to participate concurrently in ES activities. Participants must comply or demonstrate good cause for not complying with their plan to continue receiving FS services. Eviction Prevention Services ES participants may be eligible to housing assistance through the FS program if they are at risk of becoming homeless due to past due rent. The FS program may cover overdue rent amount(s) to avoid an eviction and rent subsidies for a minimum of three months. ES participants qualifying for subsidies will be responsible for contributing at least 30% of their income towards the rent while participating in employment-related and/or barrier removal activities leading to self-sufficiency. Bridge Housing Assistance The FS program may cover the costs of temporary accommodations while the homeless family is seeking permanent housing. Bridge Housing Assistance may supplement CalWORKs Temporary Homeless Assistance (THA) when insufficient to cover daily rates. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Family Stabilization Number Page 10-007.A 2 of 3 Rental Assistance As an alternative or in addition to CalWORKs/Permanent Homeless Assistance (PHA), the FS program also provides housing assistance for ES participants who are homeless or at risk of becoming homeless due to an eviction. In alignment with PHA guidance, participants are required to show that they will be able to maintain stable housing without additional assistance. Rental assistance may cover past due rent, late fees to resolve an eviction notice, credit check fees, storage fees, and a security deposit and/or first month’s rent to secure permanent housing. FS payments will only cover the AU’s portion of the housing/utility expense when the AU is in a shared housing situation. Utility Assistance The FS program may cover past due utility bills and late fees to prevent electric, gas, water, cable, or phone service shut-off, and charges to establish new utility services (deposit, activation fee), including credit check fees. FS participants are required to provide the supporting documentation necessary to evaluate eligibility to housing/utility assistance including, but not limited to: • • • Written notice of termination/eviction or overdue rent Shut-off or late payment notice from the utility company Written statement from a shelter or shared housing provider requesting to vacate the property Transportation Emergency Assistance (TEA) The FS program provides assistance to cover the cost of essential vehicle repairs necessary to ensure reliable transportation to/from assigned ES activities when the participant has no access to another privately owned vehicle. The vehicle that requires repairs must be lawfully registered to the participant and/or the participant’s spouse or domestic partner, and not be registered as “non -operational”. App roved repairs must be completed by a licensed (California Bureau of Automotive Repair) and bonded auto repair shop, car dealership, or professional mechanic who is Automotive Service Excellence (ASE) certified. TEA may cover, but it is not limited to: • • • • • • Essential vehicle repairs not exceeding the verified vehicle value Regular maintenance when necessary to complete the approved vehicle repair Costs of making the vehicle legally drivable on the road (may include, but are not limited to tires , breaks, windshield damage repairs, vehicle registration fee) Car rental while the vehicle is being repaired and there is no other transportation option Vehicle repair estimate (if not provided free of cost or deducted from final invoice) Towing charges to the service provider completing the authorized vehicle repair The FS participant is required to provide supporting documentation necessary to evaluate TEA eligibility. Verification may include: • • Current vehicle registration under the participant and/or the participant’s spouse or domestic partner’s name Two written estimates completed by different qualifying service providers Payments FS has a consecutive 12-month cumulative payment limit that is based on the AU size and the type of service requested. The 12-month eligibility period begins from the date the first FS payment is issued. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Family Stabilization Number 10-007.A Page 3 of 3 FS payments are issued to the service provider on behalf of the participant and may not exceed the established payment limit without County approval. The participant is responsible for the payment of any services not previously authorized by the County. Referral Services FS participants may be referred to Behaviora l Health Services (BHS) if a need is identified and/or services are requested. Referral services for family members must be related to the barrier that is affecting the individual’s successful participation and satisfactory progress in assigned ES activities. References: MPP 42-749, ACL 14-12, 14-61, 20-120 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by May 31, 2025. Financial Payment Type Limitations Eviction Prevention • Past due rent • Late fees Maximum of 2 months Bridge Housing • Hotel/Motel Voucher Up to 90 days Permanent Housing • Rental Deposits • First/last month rent As reasonable and within customer’s ability to sustain Rental Assistance Monthly rental subsidy, based upon 30% - 100% of the family’s current income: • If the family has no income, the rent is paid 100% with HSP funds • If the family has stable income, the family’s rent share is anywhere from 30% to 100% of their current income, remainder is paid with HSP funds Up to 6 months, based on need Customer’s share to increase monthly Other • Housing application fees • Credit check fees • Relocation services As needed The HSP program follows the Rapid Rehousing/Housing First model in this priority: permanent housing, rental subsidy, temporary housing. Attachment A CalWORKs and Employment Services (ES) Homeless Assistance Programs Summary 08/2025 ES Family Stabilization Financial Assistance Guidelines (Registered in ES. Managed by ES Contractors) Family Stabilization has a consecutive up to 12 months payment limit that is based on the size of the CalWORKs Assistance Unit (AU) and the type of services requested. Financial Payment Type 12-Month Cumulative Limit Eviction Prevention • Past due rent • Late fee Maximum of two months Bridge Housing • Hotel/motel voucher • Storage Fees Up to $150 per day, up to 90 days (as needed) , including taxes and fees Permanent Housing • Rental Deposit • First and/or Last Month’s Rent as required in the lease AU size 1-4 Up to $3,500 AU size 5+ Up to $4,500 CalWORKs Homeless Assistance (Enrolled in CalWORKs. Managed by County Family Resource Centers) Homeless Assistance is limited to once every 12 months Temporary Homeless Assistance (Bridge Housing - hotel/motel): • $85 per day up to 16 days for an Assistance Unit size of 4 • Additional Assistance Unit members can get an additional $15 per day, maximum is **$145 per day Permanent Homeless Assistance: Rental assistance benefit threshold is 80% of the family’s Total Monthly Household Income

title: A. CalWORKs Housing Support Program (HSP)
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide CalWORKs Housing Support Program (HSP) Number Page 10-008.A 1 of 4 Revision Date: October 1, 2025 Background: The CalWORKs Housing Support Program (HSP) provides assistance to CalWORKs families experiencing barriers to self -sufficiency due to homel essness or housing instability. HSP is not an entitlement program and will remain as funding and slots are available. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide eligibility requirements of HSP. This material revision is to add language regarding the required individualized housing plan, to update HSP services information and update the Homeless Programs Payment Grid (Attachment A). Policy: Eligibility Criteria Eligible CalWORKs families must meet the following HSP requirements: • Have an active CalWORKs case. • Be considered homeless, as defined in 24 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Section 91.5 under Homeless: (1) An individual or family who lacks a fixed, regular, and adequate nighttime residence, meaning: i. An individual or family with a primary night-time residence that is a public or private place not designed for or ordinarily used as a regular sleeping accommodation for human beings, including a car, park, abandoned building, bus or train station, airport, or camping ground. ii. An individual or family living in a supervised publicly or privately-operated shelter designated to provide temporary living arrangements (including congregate shelters, transitional housing, and hotels and motels paid for by charitable organizations or by federal, state, or local government programs for low-income individuals). iii. An individual who is exiting an institution where they resided for 90 days or less and who resided in an emergency shelter or place not meant for human habitation immediately before entering that institution. (2) An individual or family who will imminently lose their primary nighttime residence, provided that: i. The primary night -time residence will be lost within 14 days of the date of application for homeless assistance, ii. No subsequent residence has been identified, and iii. The individual or family lacks the resources or support networks such as family, friends, faithbased or other social networks needed to obtain other permanent housing. (3) Unaccompanied youth under 25 years of age, or families with children and youth, who do not otherwise qualify as homeless under this definition, but who: i. Are defined as homeless under section 387 of the Runaway and Homeless Youth Act (42 U.S.C. 5732a), section 637 of the Head Start Act (42 U.S.C. 9832), section 41403 of the Violence Against Women Act of 1994 (42 U.S.C. 14043e -2), section 330(h) of the Publi c Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 254b(h)), section 3 of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 (7 U.S.C. 2012), section 17(b) of the Child Nutrition Act of 1966 (42 U.S.C. 1786(b)), or section 725 of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 11434a), County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide CalWORKs Housing Support Program (HSP) Number Page 10-008.A 2 of 4 ii. Have not had a lease, ownership interest, or occupancy agreement in permanent housing at any time during the 60 days immediately preceding the date of application for homeless assistance, iii. Have experienced persistent instability as measured by two moves or more during the 60 - day period immediately preceding the date of applying for homeless assistance, and iv. Can be expected to continue in such status for an extended period of time because of chronic disabilities, chronic physical health or mental health conditions, substance addiction, histories of domestic violence or childhood abuse (including neglect), the presence of a child or youth with a disability, or two or more barriers to employment, which include the lack of a high school degree or General Education Development (GED), illiteracy, low English proficiency, a history of incarceration or detention for c riminal activity, and a history of unstable employment, or (4) Any individual or family who: i. Is fleeing, or is attempting to flee, domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, stalking, or other dangerous or life-threatening conditions that relate to violence against the individual or a family member, including a child, that has either take n place within the individual's or family's primary nighttime residence or has made the individual or family afraid to return to their primary nighttime residence, ii. Has no other residence, and iii. Lacks the resources or support networks, such as family, friends, faith-based or other social networks, to obtain other permanent housing. Prioritization HSP services will be prioritized for families who lack a fixed, regular, and adequate nighttime residence followed by those who will imminently lose their primary nighttime residence. HSP Service Examples The following services will be provided under HSP: • Intensive Case Management: o Assessment of housing barriers. o Development of a housing plan. o Financial literacy/coaching. o Help resolving legal issues. o Referrals to resources as needed. • Housing Navigation: o Landlord recruitment and retention. o Help finding and securing permanent housing for customers. • Financial Assistance: o Bridge housing. o Relocation costs. o Move-in costs (such as deposits, moving expenses, utilities). o Rental subsidy. o Eviction prevention services to avoid a pending eviction. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide CalWORKs Housing Support Program (HSP) Number Page 10-008.A 3 of 4 HSP is offered in addition to the following programs or services available to CalWORKs customers, if they are otherwise eligible: • Temporary Homeless Assistance (THA)/Permanent Homeless Assistance (PHA). o When a housing need is identified, in addition to THA/PHA, customers must also be automatically referred to HSP staff for evaluation for HSP. o When appropriate, HSP staff will also refer the customer to apply for THA/PHA. • Family Stabilization , Non-Housing Services, such as utility assistance and car repairs, if participating in Employment Services (ES). Housing First Concept Contractors will establish a Housing First concept for HSP. Housing First-oriented programs are low or no barrier and customer-centered, emphasizing customer-choice. Housing is viewed as necessary to help a family or individual stabilize and meaningfully access services, which are offered as needed on a voluntary basis. In practice, this means that programs connect participants to permanent housing as quickly as possible with few to no preconditions, behavioral contingencies, or other barriers at enrollment or throughout the program. Instead of requiring people to stabilize before receiving housing, programs using a Housing First approach focus on helping people achieve housing stability before addressing other barriers that may exist. To ensure effective implementation of Housing First, HSP staff will work collaboratively with the customers to develop individualized housing and services plans for all customers after their HSP enrollment, by utilizing form 27-392 HHSA – Housing Support Program Agreement and Assessment Plan. Procedure: Procedures for administering HSP services and the referral process can be found in the following: • CalWORKs Processing Guide 10-008.A1, Housing Support Program Referral Process. o Family Resource Center staff will refer CalWORKs families meet ing all eligibility requirements described above to the County’s HSP providers. • Attachment A, CalWORKs Desk Aid, Homeless Programs Payment Grid. Impacts: Forms Form 27-392 HHSA, has been created to develop housing plans with HSP customers: • This form provides an overview of the housing search process and outlines the expectations of both the customer and the housing specialist. This form must be used to develop individualized housing and services plans, by collecting information from customers regarding their past and current living situations to identify and address barriers to housing stability. • The form is not available in CalSAWS. A manual PDF fill-in enabled form is available for immediate print from the Eligibility Form s Library (EFL) . Shelf stock may be ordered from the Xerox Print Center. title: A. CalWORKs Home Visiting Program
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide CalWORKs Home Visiting Program (HVP) Number Page 10-009.A 1 of 5 Revision Date: June 1, 2025 Background: The CalWORKs Home Visiting Program (HVP) is a voluntary evidence-based program model that pairs new parents with a nurse, or other trained professional who makes regular visits in the participant’s home to provide guidance, coaching, access to prenatal and postnatal care, and other health and social services. HVP is not an entitlement program and will remain as funding and slots are available. Purpose: The purpose of the HVP is to support positive health, development and well -being outcomes for pregnant and parenting persons, families, and infants born into poverty. The long-term goals for program participants include expanding their future educational, economic, and financial opportunities, stabilizing families and improving the likelihood of exiting poverty. This section is being revised to incorporate the requirement for referrals to the HVP perinatal services for pregnant people receiving Pregnancy Special Need (PSN) payments. Policy: Eligibility Criteria To be eligible for HVP, the customer must be pregnant or a parent or caretaker relative of a child less than 24 months of age at the time of enrollment in HVP and must be one of the following: • A member of the CalWORKs Assistance Unit (AU). • The parent/caretaker relative for a child-only case. • An individual who is apparently eligible for CalWORKs aid. • A CalWORKs applicant who has begun receiving HVP services and subsequently is denied or chooses to withdraw their application. These customers can continue receiving HVP services if no other home visiting program services are available. • An individual who is in the Cal-Learn program. This program can serve participants for up to 24 months or until the child’s second birthday, whichever is later. Re-enrollment and Program Time Limits HVP participants may be eligible to re -enroll if they were unable to complete 24 months of services during their initial enrollment in CalWORKs HVP and all of the following apply: • The initial enrollment was discontinued because the previously eligible child was permanently removed from the AU due to death of the child, termination of parental rights, or relinquishment of parental rights. • At the time the CalWORKs HVP services were discontinued, there were no other eligible children in the AU. • The family is now eligible for CalWORKs HVP with a new pregnancy or new eligible child. • The evidence -based model being implemented by the county allows for the participant’s re - enrollment. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide CalWORKs Home Visiting Program (HVP) Number Page 10-009.A 2 of 5 The re-enrolled participant will be eligible for 24 months of services or until the new child turns two years old, whichever is later. There is no limit to the number of times a participant may re-enroll if they meet all of the above criteria. Participants re-enrolled in the program will be considered new enrollments for the purpose of HVP-19 reporting. Continued Enrollment Where the Status of the Child Has Changed In circumstances when the initial eligible child is no longer part of the household, HVP services may continue if the participant has another child(ren) in the home and the evidence -based model allows. Their participation in HVP will be completed once they have received 24 months of service. Voluntary Evidence-Based Home Visitation Participation in HVP is voluntary. However, a pregnant person receiving PSN payments is required to be referred to HVP for perinatal home visiting services. If customers choose to participate in this program, their participation will not affect their CalWORKs eligibility, benefits, supports, or services. Customers may enter and exit the program based on their needs and if they meet HVP eligibility criteria. Home visitors will provide resources directly and refer customers to services so that they can receive the support they need. Customers participating in HVP will receive: • Coaching and guidance through regular, planned home visits. • Information about strategies to improve their family's health and provide better developmental opportunities for their children. • Information that will connect them to an array of employment and other services. Note: Home visits will not be random or unannounced. Case Management Services The county and home visiting agency will establish a collaborative case management plan. These activities include assessing the family's needs, developing a case plan, monitoring progress in achieving case plan objectives, and ensuring the provision of all services specified in the case plan. The case plan should build on the strengths established during the home visiting period, and the family’s associated connections to childcare. Coordination with County Staff Home visitors will coordinate closely with county (Eligibility/Employment Services [ES]) staff. Close coordination and communication are essential to ensure that customers have access to services without adding any additional burdens to the customers or duplication of processes and services by the county or home visiting agency. Enrollment in Early Learning Programs High-quality early learning programs have a demonstrated ability to improve both short-term and long- term outcomes for children with unmet needs. The home visitors will encourage customers to enroll their children in high-quality early learning settings, participate in playgroups, or engage in other child enrichment activities. Customers will have a n opportunity to select from high -quality early learning settings that may provide developmental screenings and assessments, and offer a core curriculum that is developmentally, culturally, and linguistically appropriate. If a customer volun teers in the early County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide CalWORKs Home Visiting Program (HVP) Number Page 10-009.A 3 of 5 learning setting, these hours will count towards their allowable activities under their ES plan. Children enrolled in an early learning setting through the HVP may remain enrolled for 24-months regardless of the customer’s participation in activities. Cultural Competency Minimum Requirements Establishing minimum training standards as a basis for ensuring cultural sensitivity, understanding, and decision making should be embedded in the overall principles of home visiting practices. ES Participation Hours Participation in ES is not a requirement to receive HVP services. However, if the customer is participating in ES, the hours spent directly with a home visitor (home visiting sessions) and, if applicable, the hours spent volunteering in an early learning s etting under HVP must be assigned in the customer’s ES or Cal-Learn Plan. Supportive services for HVP activities must be included in their plan. ES staff must communicate and coordinate with the HVP service provider to monitor and verify participation and address any issues or concerns regarding the customer. Work Participation Rate (WPR) HVP participation in home visiting sessions and volunteering in an early learning setting may be counted for WPR. Home visiting sessions may be counted as Job Search and Job Readiness for four consecutive weeks (120 hours) and six weeks (180 hours) total in a 12 -month period, in accordance with federal reporting instructions. Beyond this time limit, home visiting session hours are to be reported as “other activities that directly lead to unsubsidized employment”. Volunteer hours in an early learning setting may be counted as community service, WEX, or job readiness. Supportive Services For HVP customers in ES, supportive services for HVP must be included in the ES plan (mandatory or voluntary), where a plan has been developed. If supportive services are not available for HVP activities needed to meet ES requirements, good cause must be given. Customers in ES sanction and in a plan to have aid restored may receive supportive services. For HVP customers who are not eligible for supportive services, home visitors will provide information, resources, and referrals to other community resources for services. Material Goods HVP participants are eligible to receive material goods for items of need for the health and safety of the child and family. The material goods will be purchased by the HVP contractors and provided to the customer when a need is identified. The material goods are: • For items for care, health, and safety of the child and family. • Not to exceed the amount limit for each family served by HVP (as instructed below) throughout the length of the customer’s engagement in HVP. • To be offered as needed. • Cumulative per case and do not reset annually or otherwise (including instances of Inter -County Transfers). • A household that is granted re -enrollment or continued enrollment is eligible for the remaining balance of what is left of the material goods fund from their initial enrollment. These funds are County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide CalWORKs Home Visiting Program (HVP) Number Page 10-009.A 4 of 5 once-in-a-lifetime. Material goods fund limit: • $500 through June 30, 2022 (ACWDL dated April 25, 2019). • $1,000 effective July 1, 2022 (ACL No. 22-86). Some examples of appropriate uses of material goods funds include, but are not limited to child safety kits, car seats, cribs, diapers, formula, appliance repairs, adaptive equipment for children with disabilities, resources related to child and family language, or literacy needs. The funds may be spent on food if it is an immediate need for the family. The customer will be informed of other food assistance programs for which they may be eligible, including but not limited to CalFresh. The funds are not intended to be an incentive for the customer to participate, but rather a response to the family’s specific needs. Not all families’ needs will fall into the scope of these funds, but if an appropriate family need is identified, an effort will be made to offer material goods to the family. In circumstances where the parent or assisted caretaker relative has been removed from the AU or exits the CalWORKs program, voluntary HVP services may continue until the completion of the program or until the parent or assisted caretaker relative terminates their own participation. In this case, if the parent or caregiver continues participating in HVP, they would still be eligible for HVP services including the material goods. The county and home visiting agency may incorporate participation of the noncustodial parent of a child who is a member of an AU into HVP services. This offer is subject to the permission of the custodial parent and further mutual agreement of the custodial and noncustodial parents. The material good must not exceed $1,000 total per case between the custodial and non - custodial parents. The material goods funds must never be issued directly to customers (via Electronic Benefit Transfer [EBT] card, gift cards, vouchers, or cash). Rather, a home visitor will observe a situation and engage in discussions with customers regarding items which are necessary for the positive health and safety of the child and family. The home visiting agency will purchase the items and then submit a copy of the purchase order to the county, and requests reimbursement of the funds used to purchase items for the customer. The material goods must be tracked in case documentation. Impacts: Informing Notice and Request to Opt-In to HVP Form • CW 2224 - CalWORKs Home Visiting Program (HVP) The CW 2224 serves both as notification and for customers to submit requests in writing. • Home Visiting Initiative (HVI) Flyer This flyer serves as HVP outreach to customers and to encourage them to participate. Both the form and flyer must be provided to customers at application, annual redetermination, or any time home visiting services are requested. Procedure: CalWORKs Processing Guide 10-009.A1 - Home Visiting Program Referral Procedures. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide CalWORKs Home Visiting Program (HVP) Number Page 10-009.A 5 of 5 References: • Welfare & Institutions Code (W&IC) Article 3.4. (11330.6 – 11330.9). • Assembly Bill (AB) 1811 (Chapter 35, Statutes of 2018). • Senate Bill (SB) 840 (Chapter 29, Statutes of 2018), SB 80 (Chapter 27, Statutes of 2019), SB 1083 (Chapter 715, Statutes of 2022). • All County Letters (ACLs) No. 19-42, 19-42E, 20-13, 22-86, 23-11, 23-83. • All County Information Notice (ACIN) No. I-4-20. • All County Welfare Directors Letters (ACWDLs) dated July 31, 2018; April 25, 2019. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by June 30, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide CalWORKs Home Visiting Program (HVP) Number Page 10-009.A 1 of 5 Revision Date: June 1, 2025 Background: The CalWORKs Home Visiting Program (HVP) is a voluntary evidence-based program model that pairs new parents with a nurse, or other trained professional who makes regular visits in the participant’s home to provide guidance, coaching, access to prenatal and postnatal care, and other health and social services. HVP is not an entitlement program and will remain as funding and slots are available. Purpose: The purpose of the HVP is to support positive health, development and well -being outcomes for pregnant and parenting persons, families, and infants born into poverty. The long-term goals for program participants include expanding their future educational, economic, and financial opportunities, stabilizing families and improving the likelihood of exiting poverty. This section is being revised to incorporate the requirement for referrals to the HVP perinatal services for pregnant people receiving Pregnancy Special Need (PSN) payments. Policy: Eligibility Criteria To be eligible for HVP, the customer must be pregnant or a parent or caretaker relative of a child less than 24 months of age at the time of enrollment in HVP and must be one of the following: • A member of the CalWORKs Assistance Unit (AU). • The parent/caretaker relative for a child-only case. • An individual who is apparently eligible for CalWORKs aid. • A CalWORKs applicant who has begun receiving HVP services and subsequently is denied or chooses to withdraw their application. These customers can continue receiving HVP services if no other home visiting program services are available. • An individual who is in the Cal-Learn program. This program can serve participants for up to 24 months or until the child’s second birthday, whichever is later. Re-enrollment and Program Time Limits HVP participants may be eligible to re -enroll if they were unable to complete 24 months of services during their initial enrollment in CalWORKs HVP and all of the following apply: • The initial enrollment was discontinued because the previously eligible child was permanently removed from the AU due to death of the child, termination of parental rights, or relinquishment of parental rights. • At the time the CalWORKs HVP services were discontinued, there were no other eligible children in the AU. • The family is now eligible for CalWORKs HVP with a new pregnancy or new eligible child. • The evidence -based model being implemented by the county allows for the participant’s re - enrollment. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide CalWORKs Home Visiting Program (HVP) Number Page 10-009.A 2 of 5 The re-enrolled participant will be eligible for 24 months of services or until the new child turns two years old, whichever is later. There is no limit to the number of times a participant may re-enroll if they meet all of the above criteria. Participants re-enrolled in the program will be considered new enrollments for the purpose of HVP-19 reporting. Continued Enrollment Where the Status of the Child Has Changed In circumstances when the initial eligible child is no longer part of the household, HVP services may continue if the participant has another child(ren) in the home and the evidence -based model allows. Their participation in HVP will be completed once they have received 24 months of service. Voluntary Evidence-Based Home Visitation Participation in HVP is voluntary. However, a pregnant person receiving PSN payments is required to be referred to HVP for perinatal home visiting services. title: A. Child Care Overview
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page CalWORKs Child Care 10-010.A 1 of 3 Revision Date: April 1, 2023 Background: The California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids (CalWORKs) Child Care Program is for current and former CalWORKs cash aid recipients to assist with paying for childcare with a provider of their choice, if they are employed or participating in approved activities. The CalWORKs Child Care Program is provided in a single three-stage system. Effective July 1, 2021, all three stages of the CalWORKs Child Care program are supervised by the California Department of Social Services (CDSS) Child Care and Development Division. •Stage One is provided through the County of San Diego’s CalWORKs Employment Services (ES) program and is designed to help customers quickly access child care when they begin working or participating in ES or Cal-Learn activities •Stage Two and Stage Three are provided through CDSS contracts with Alternative Payment Programs (APP) and are designed to provide families long-term, stable child care to continue working once their cash aid ends Purpose: This revision removes reference to the previous version of Processing Guide (PG) 10-010.A4 Form 27-128 which is now obsolete and renames PG 10-010.A5 Transitioning Child Care Cases to Stage Two, to PG 10-010.A4 Transitioning Child Care Cases to Stage Two. Policy: CalWORKs Child Care may begin when a family starts receiving CalWORKs cash aid. Stage One Child Care is available to: •CalWORKs recipients who are in an ES activity, or working •Cal-Learn Pregnant or Parenting Teens who are in a high school program as well as when working in addition to the high school program •CalWORKs sanctioned individuals who need child care to cure an ES sanction •CalWORKs families or Former CalWORKs families who cannot receive services in Stage Two because of program barriers, Stage Two funding/staffing issues, or other administrative issues •Former CalWORKs families with unresolved program barriers, up to 24-months post-aid Stage Two Child Care is available to: •CalWORKs recipients in an ES activity or working, who meet the County definition of “stable” •Sanctioned or exempt individuals who are not in ES but who are in approved activities, or working •Former CalWORKs families during the first 24 months off cash aid •Families that receive lump-sum diversion services if there is no funding available in Stage Three Stage Three Child Care is available to: •Former CalWORKs families who are working, whose income when they transition off cash aid, does not exceed 85% of the State Median Income (SMI) and their children are not over the eligibility age; the 24-month limit does not apply to Stage Three •Families that receive lump-sum diversion services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page CalWORKs Child Care 10-010.A 2 of 3 Form CCP7 Informing Notice Requirement The CalWORKs Stage One Child Care Request and Payment Rules form (CCP7) must be provided to all CalWORKs customers to inform them about the availability of Stage One child care. The customer may request CalWORKs child care either verbally or in writing upon entry into the CalWORKs assistance program or at any later time. The earliest date of eligibility of child care is determined based upon the earliest date of the customer’s verbal or written request. Stage One Time Limit A customer will be served a maximum of six months in Stage One unless the family’s situation is determined to be unstable, or childcare is not available in Stage Two or Three. Under these circumstances, the Stage One services may be extended for more than six months. The County of San Diego Self-Sufficiency Services (SSS) Department contracts the administration of Stage One Child Care services with Public Consulting Group (PCG) and Equus Workforce Services. Equus subcontracts childcare services with YMCA Stage One. In the County of San Diego there are two Stage Two agencies: Child Development Associates (CDA) and YMCA Stage Two. SSS staff monitor the transfer of cases to Stage Two to ensure an equitable distribution of cases between the two Stage Two agencies. For information about transfers, including the County’s definition of stability see Processing Guide 10-010.A4 Transitioning Child Care Cases to Stage Two. Stage One Child Care transfers cases to Stage Two primarily according to regional assignment: Region Stage One Agency Stage Two Agency Central PCG 4389 Imperial Avenue San Diego, CA 92113 (619) 270-4250 CDA 5473 Kearny Villa Road, Suite 350 San Diego, CA 92123 (619) 427-4411, Ext 1700 East PCG 151 Van Houten Avenue El Cajon, CA 92020 (619) 270-4000 YMCA Stage Two 3601 Arey Drive San Diego, CA 92154 Phone Number: (619) 474-4707 South PCG 690 Oxford Street Chula Vista, CA 91911 (619) 270-4100 YMCA Stage Two 3601 Arey Drive San Diego, CA 92154 Phone Number: (619) 474-4707 N. Coastal Equus-YMCA Stage One 3708 Ocean Ranch Boulevard Oceanside, CA 92056 (619) 521-3055, Ext 2480 CDA 5473 Kearny Villa Road, Suite 350 San Diego, CA 92123 (619) 427-4411, Ext 1700 N. Inland Equus-YMCA Stage One 613 W. Valley Parkway, Suite 200 Escondido, CA 92025 (619) 521-3055, Ext 2466 CDA 5473 Kearny Villa Road, Suite 350 San Diego, CA 92123 (858) 836-8065 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page CalWORKs Child Care 10-010.A 3 of 3 Non-CalWORKs Parents/Caretaker Relatives CalWORKs Assistance Units who do not include at least one CalWORKs or Former CalWORKs parent/caretaker relative who has received aid within the last 24 months, are not eligible for CalWORKs Stage One Child Care. The Non-CalWORKs parent/caretaker relatives who have a child care need, may be referred to the Centralized Eligibility List (CEL) at 1(800)-521-0560 or https://carewait2-family.carecloud.io/SDCEL . Procedure: 10-010.A1 Child Care Request Process 10-010.A2 Form CCP7 10-010.A3 Form CCP8 10-010.A4Transitioning Child Care Cases to Stage Two References: MPP 47-101, 47-301; CCR, Title 5, Chapter 19 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by April 30, 2026. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self Sufficiency Services

title: B. Child Care Eligibility
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageChild Care Eligibility 10.010.B 1 of 8 Revision Date: October 1, 2025 Background: The CalWORKs Stage One Child Care (Stage One Child Care) program is for current and former CalWORKs customers. The program assists in paying for child care services to a provider of the customer’s choice. CalWORKs customers will be authorized for 24 months of child care upon CalWORKs approval or anytime thereafter when a CalWORKs customer indicates a need for child care. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to explain the criteria for Stage One Child Care eligibility. The material revisions are to incorporate policies to extend 12-month eligibility to 24 months and to clarify policies for abandonment of care, discontinuing child care, and verification of a child’s exceptional needs. Policy: CalWORKs customers, who meet child care eligibility criteria, will have access to 24 months of Stage One Child Care once they are determined eligible for CalWORKs, and they: •Are requesting child care services. •Have secured a child care provider. •Are expected to be referred to Employment Services (ES). Eligible Adult CalWORKs customers who are eligible to receive Stage One Child Care include: •Mandatory ES participants. •Cal-Learn (CL) participants. •ES exempt volunteers. •ES sanctioned participants who express an intent to cure the sanction. •Sanctioned or penalized participants who are working or participating in county-approved activities. CalWORKs families with no aided adults are not eligible for Stage One Child Care, for example: •Adults receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits. •Ineligible noncitizen adults. •Non-needy caretaker relatives. •Timed-out adults eligible to Stage Two Child Care. Timed-out and Former CalWORKs Customers Timed-out adults and former CalWORKs customers who received aid within the past 24 months may receive Post Aid child care services through Stage One under the following circumstances: •The CalWORKs customer cannot receive child care services in Stage Two because of program barriers or other administrative issues. •The child care services are not available in Stage Two or Stage Three due to funding. •The customer will benefit from remaining with Stage One Child Care services; for example, when a customer has a request for retroactive child care that isn’t allowed in Stage Two. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageChild Care Eligibility 10.010.B 2 of 8 Timed-out adults and former CalWORKs customers who received aid within the past 24 months, and ES participants who are in a long-term sanction, will be referred to Stage Two Child Care, unless they meet one of the circumstances listed above. Eligible Children Children up to and through age 12 are eligible to receive child care services. Children who are under court supervision may receive services up to age 18. Children with exceptional needs and/or who are severely disabled may continue to receive child care services up to age 21. Children may receive Stage One Child Care when all the following apply: And at least one of the following applies: •The parent has a need for child care services. •The family is receiving CalWORKs, or received CalWORKs within the last 24 months and child care isn’t available in Stage Two or Stage Three Child Care. •There is no parent or legal guardian or member of the Assistance Unit (AU) living in the home who is able and available to provide child care. •Lack of child care would result in the customer not being able to participate in ES or CL activities, employment, or any other county approved activity. •The child is a member of the AU, including the child of a CL participant. •The child is not a member of the AU because the child is receiving SSI/State Supplementary Payment (SSP) benefits or is in a Foster Care program. •The child is a member of a family with a former CalWORKs parent (who received aid within the past 24 months) who has a verified child care need. •The child is a non-AU member, but a CalWORKs parent is responsible for the care and control of that child (for example exempt stepsibling or half-sibling). The preferred placement for 11 and 12-year-old children is in a before or after school program. Subsidized child care should only be utilized for the portion of care needed that is not available in a before or after school program. However, to ensure child care needs are met: •Children may continue to receive child care subsidized services when a before or after school program is not available. •Families may combine care provided in a before or after school program with subsidized child care for those hours when the before or after school program does not operate. Note: Children who are 12 years old when certified must be certified for no less than 12 months of child care. If a child turns 13 years old during the first 12 months of the eligibility period, their certification of child care services should clearly indicate that they are only eligible for 12 months, including time after they turn 13 years. Their eligibility does not extend to 24 months. When child care is being determined for a child 13 through 21 years of age because the child is physically or mentally incapable of caring for self, verification must be provided that the child requires child care or supervision. The parent must provide: •Form 24-707 Documentation of a Child’s Exceptional Needs, and •A written statement from a physician or licensed or certified psychologist, or County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageChild Care Eligibility 10.010.B 3 of 8 •Verification of SSI/SSP benefit, or •Individualized Education Program (IEP) and Form 24-793 Statement of Exceptional Needs. Note: If a provider requests an adjusted reimbursement rate to cover extra costs for caring for a child with exceptional needs, the provider must submit verification of the accommodation and extra costs needed to meet the child’s exceptional needs. For more information about exceptional needs rate adjustments see CPG 10-010.E Child Care Payments and 10-010.E1 Payment Procedures. Two-Parent Families Stage One Child Care will not be granted for two-parent households in which one parent is able and available to provide care for the children. A parent is considered available to provide care unless they are working (or sleeping after working a night shift), going to school, participating in an approved ES activity or has a condition that prevents them from caring for the children. When both parents are participating in ES, working, or are otherwise unavailable to care for their children, Stage One Child Care will be made available to them. ES Exempt Volunteers Customers who have been determined to be exempt from ES participation who express an intent to participate in ES on a voluntary basis are eligible to receive Stage One Child Care. The customer may communicate the intent to volunteer in ES in any manner (written, or orally). The request must be documented with a journal entry. After securing child care, the exempt volunteer shall sign an ES plan. Exempt volunteers who do not subsequently sign an ES plan will have their child care discontinued until they become mandatory participants or sign an ES plan. ES Sanctioned Customers ES sanctioned customers who express an intent to cure the sanction are eligible to Stage One Child Care. The customer may communicate the intent to cure the sanction in any manner (written, or orally). The request must be documented with a journal entry. After securing child care, the sanctioned customer shall sign form WTW 29 Plan to Stop a Welfare to Work Sanction. Sanctioned customers who later fail to sign a curing plan will have their child care discontinued. When customers who request to cure their sanction are already receiving Stage Two or Three Child Care, they may continue in Stage Two or Three Child Care if their needs are being met. ES sanctioned customers who do not request to cure their sanction, including those in long-term sanctions are considered former CalWORKs customers and are eligible for Stage Two Child Care services if they have received CalWORKs within the last 24 months. Mandatory ES or CL customers who become sanctioned after being authorized for 24 months of child care services may continue in Stage One Child Care for the remainder of the 24-month period or until they are transferred to Stage Two Child Care. Domestic Violence Waivers Customers with a domestic violence waiver remain eligible to continuous child care regardless of their participation in ES activities. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageChild Care Eligibility 10.010.B 4 of 8 CL Program Transition to ES Program CL customers who were certified for 24 months of child care services while participating in CL will continue for the remainder of the 24-month certification period when they transition to ES. Program Activities Program activities for which full-time immediate and continuous Stage One Child Care should be authorized include, but are not limited to: •Any ES or CL activity (orientation, appraisal, assessment, job search, job club, work experience, employment, family stabilization services, mental health services, substance abuse services, education, vocational training, etc.). •Any other county approved activity (housing search and classes, homeless support programs, shelter participation activities, eviction proceedings, parenting classes, court appearances, medical or education-related appointments for participants or their dependents, etc.). Note: This list of program activities applies to CalWORKs customers expected to be referred to ES such as mandatory ES participants, exempt volunteers, and sanctioned customers who express an intent to cure their sanction. Stage One Child Care Authorization and Certification CalWORKs customers, who meet the Stage One Child Care aided-adult criteria listed above, will receive a 24-month Stage One Child Care authorization at the time CalWORKs is approved or redetermined. Refer to 10-010.A3 Child Care Authorization for more information. Customers who are authorized to receive 24 months of Stage One Child Care services must also have their child care certified and approved in order to be reimbursed for child care services. To be certified and approved for child care, the parent and provider will need to complete an enrollment process with Stage One Child Care by submitting any required information and documentation. Child care will be either certified or denied based on an eligibility determination for the parents, children, and provider. When it is certified that an eligible parent has secured child care with a provider who is enrolled with Stage One Child Care and who meets the parent’s child care needs, a Child Care Certificate and an approval Notice of Action will be issued to the parent to certify and approve the child care for a 24- month certification period. The provider will be mailed a copy of the certificate. The approved begin date of the 24-month period is based on the earliest date that child care can be reimbursed. Refer to CalWORKs Processing Guide 10-010.A2 Child Care Request for more information about the begin date of child care reimbursement. Stage One Child Care Recertification Customers who are receiving Stage One Child Care services must recertify eligibility than every 24 months unless one of the following changes occur: •The child care needs have increased. •They have a new child who needs care. •They have changed child care providers. •The eligible child becomes ineligible. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageChild Care Eligibility 10.010.B 5 of 8 Note: Upon certification or recertification of eligibility, a customer receiving Stage One Child Care shall be considered eligible and receive those services for no less than 24 months. The customer shall not be required to report changes to income or other changes during the 24-month certification. The 24- month certification period restarts whenever the child care eligibility is recertified. Child Care Discontinuance Stage One Child Care will be discontinued when any of the following circumstances occur: •The customer is transferred to Stage Two and the Stage Two Child Care agency confirms the enrollment. •When at initial post aid certification or recertification, the family income exceeds income eligibility of 85% of the State Median Income (SMI) for their corresponding family size. •An ES exempt participant or ES sanctioned participant who initially expresses an intent to participate or cure their sanction fails to sign an ES plan. •When a customer moves to another county in California. Refer to CPG 40-100.H Inter-County Transfer for more information. •The child/family is no longer eligible, e.g., no eligible child, no longer residing in California. •When there is substantiated evidence of fraud that invalidated the initial certification, and the family is not otherwise eligible. •The customer has abandoned care. Discontinuance due to Abandonment of Care If there has been no communication from the family for a total of 30 consecutive days, the family will be discontinued from Stage One Child Care based on abandonment of care. The staff must issue a notice of action terminating child care services based on abandonment of care. For discontinuation due to abandonment of care the following steps must be taken: •When the customer has not been in communication with the child care provider for seven consecutive calendar days and has not notified the provider of the reason the customer is not using services, the provider must promptly notify their child care worker. •The child care staff must attempt to contact the customer by phone, and in writing, which may be through electronic methods. All communication attempts must be documented, which includes a journal entry in CalSAWs and keeping copies of all written communication in the customer’s file. The staff must inform the customer in these communications that failure to communicate with the staff or provider may result in termination of child care services. Transitioning from Stage One to Stage Two Child Care Customers who have been receiving child care services Stage One Child Care services for at least 60 days will be evaluated to determine if the customer meets the criteria of stability. Cases that meet the criteria of stability will be transferred to Stage Two Child Care. Refer to CalWORKs Processing Guide 10-010.A4 Transitioning to Stage Two. Post Aid Child Care Eligibility Customers who have timed-out or discontinued from CalWORKs within the past 24 months are to be evaluated for Post Aid Child Care with Stage One Child Care when they do not qualify for Stage Two Child Care because of program barriers. When the customer timed-out or discontinued mid-period in a County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageChild Care Eligibility 10.010.B 6 of 8 24-month certification period, the Post Aid Child Care eligibility will be evaluated at the customer’s next recertification. The following are considered in evaluating Post Aid Child Care eligibility: •The need for child care services. •The adjusted monthly income. •The family size. Customers may receive Stage One Post Aid Child Care services for no more than 24 months after CalWORKs discontinues. The 24-month limit applies to each instance of CalWORKs discontinuance. When a customer who is receiving Stage One Post Aid Child Care then applies for and receives Diversion Services, their 24-month limit of Post Aid Child Care will reset. Family Size and Parent Definitions The family size is composed of the parents and the children related by blood, marriage, or adoption living in the same home with the child receiving child care services. Parent means a biological parent, adoptive parent, stepparent, foster parent, caretaker relative, legal guardian, domestic partner of the parent as defined in Family Code Section 297, or any other adult living with a child who has responsibility for the care and wellbeing of the child. When another adult living in the household is neither the parent of the child nor the spouse of the parent, that adult, and their children if any, shall be excluded from the calculation of the family size. When a child and their siblings are living in a family that does not include their biological or adoptive parents, the following must be considered when identifying the family size and income eligibility: •Only the child and related siblings will be counted in the family size. •The adjusted monthly income of the child and any related siblings, which includes payments specifically for the care and wellbeing of the child will be counted to determine eligibility. The payments must be made payable to and received by the adult who lives with and is responsible for the care and wellbeing of the child. •The adult who lives with and has responsibility for the care and wellbeing of the child must have a child care need. •Partners who have filed for domestic partnership with the state are considered the equivalent of a married couple for determination of the family size. Refer to CalWORKs Processing Guide 10-010.B1 Post Aid Child Care Procedures and to the Family Size Desk Aid for examples of household composition and determining the family size. Post Aid Child Care Income Eligibility When determining eligibility at initial Post Aid Child Care certification and recertification, to be income eligible, the family’s adjusted monthly income must be at or below 85% of SMI for their corresponding family size. Adjusted monthly income is the total countable earned and unearned income received by included family members. Verified child support payments paid by the parent whose child or guardian is receiving child care services is subtracted from the countable income. Other adjusted deductions, voluntary or involuntary, are to be counted in the adjusted monthly income. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageChild Care Eligibility 10.010.B 7 of 8 Refer to CalWORKs Processing Guide 10-010.B1 Post Aid Child Care Eligibility Procedures for how to calculate the countable income, including how to average fluctuating income. Countable income includes, but is not limited to, the following: •Wages or salary, advances, commission, overtime, tips, bonuses, gambling, or lottery winnings •Self-employment earnings (business expenses are not counted) •CalWORKs grant •Unemployment •State or Private Disability Payments •Workers Compensation payments •Spousal (Alimony) or Child Support received •Social Security benefits (Retirement, Survivor, Disability) •Dividends, interest on bonds, income from estates or trust, or royalties •Net rental income including rental income for renting a room within the family’s residence •Foster care payments for children receiving child care services •Financial assistance received for the care of a child living with an adult who is not the child’s biological or adoptive parent •Veterans pension •Pension or annuities •Inheritance •Allowances for housing or automobiles provided as part of compensation •Any portion of a non-government student grant/ scholarship that exceeds the amount intended for educational purposes and is available for living costs •Insurance or court settlements for lost wages or punitive damages •Net proceeds from the sale of real property, stocks, or inherited property •Other enterprise for gain Non-countable income, includes but is not limited to, the following: •Earnings of a child under age 18 years •Loans •Student grants and loans intended for educational purposes made by a state or federal agency •Student loans, grants and scholarships obtained under conditions that prevent their use for living costs •CalFresh allotment or other food assistance •Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) or tax refund •Adoption Assistance Payments •Non-cash assistance or gifts •Government Issue (GI) Bill entitlements, hardship duty pay, hazardous duty pay, hostile fire pay, or imminent danger pay •All income of SSI and/or State Supplemental Program (SSP) recipient •Reimbursement for work-required expenses such as uniforms, mileage, or per diem expenses for food and lodging •Business expense for self-employed •When there is no cash value to the employee, the portion of medical and/or dental insurance documented as paid by the employer and included in the gross pay •Disaster relief grants or payments, except any portion for rental assistance or unemployment •AmeriCorps Volunteers In Service to America (VISTA) and Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) stipends, room and board, and grants •Guaranteed Income Payments, from but not limited to, the California Guaranteed Income Pilot Program County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageChild Care Eligibility 10.010.B 8 of 8 •Insurance or court settlements for pain and suffering When customers are found eligible for Post Aid Child Care services, some customers may be assessed with a fee based on their adjusted monthly income and family size. The assessed fee is referred to as a family fee. Customers are required to pay the family fee directly to the child care provider. Refer to CalWORKs Processing Guide 10-010.E2 Family Fees for more information. Procedure: Processing Guide 10-010.A1 – Child Care Request and Authorization Processing Guide 10-010.A3 – Child Care Authorization Form – CCP 8 Processing Guide 10-010.A5 – Transitioning Child Care Cases to Stage 2 Processing Guide 10-010.B1 – Post Aid Child Care Eligibility Procedures References: EAS: 47-201, 47-220, 47-230 ACL: 11-52,19-99 ACIN: I-15-20, I-26-20, I-09-21 5 CCR §: 18078, 18083.1, 18066.5 WIC 10271 (h) (5), 10271.6 (c), 10227.5(b)(2)(A) CCB: 22-04, 23-28, 24-34 (E), 25-15 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by October 31, 2028. sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageChild Care Eligibility 10.010.B 1 of 8 Revision Date: October 1, 2025 Background: The CalWORKs Stage One Child Care (Stage One Child Care) program is for current and former CalWORKs customers. The program assists in paying for child care services to a provider of the customer’s choice. CalWORKs customers will be authorized for 24 months of child care upon CalWORKs approval or anytime thereafter when a CalWORKs customer indicates a need for child care. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to explain the criteria for Stage One Child Care eligibility. The material revisions are to incorporate policies to extend 12-month eligibility to 24 months and to clarify policies for abandonment of care, discontinuing child care, and verification of a child’s exceptional needs. Policy: CalWORKs customers, who meet child care eligibility criteria, will have access to 24 months of Stage One Child Care once they are determined eligible for CalWORKs, and they: •Are requesting child care services. •Have secured a child care provider. •Are expected to be referred to Employment Services (ES). Eligible Adult CalWORKs customers who are eligible to receive Stage One Child Care include: •Mandatory ES participants. •Cal-Learn (CL) participants. •ES exempt volunteers. •ES sanctioned participants who express an intent to cure the sanction. •Sanctioned or penalized participants who are working or participating in county-approved activities. CalWORKs families with no aided adults are not eligible for Stage One Child Care, for example: •Adults receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits. •Ineligible noncitizen adults. •Non-needy caretaker relatives. •Timed-out adults eligible to Stage Two Child Care. Timed-out and Former CalWORKs Customers Timed-out adults and former CalWORKs customers who received aid within the past 24 months may receive Post Aid child care services through Stage One under the following circumstances: •The CalWORKs customer cannot receive child care services in Stage Two because of program barriers or other administrative issues. •The child care services are not available in Stage Two or Stage Three due to funding. •The customer will benefit from remaining with Stage One Child Care services; for example, when a customer has a request for retroactive child care that isn’t allowed in Stage Two. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageChild Care Eligibility 10.010.B 2 of 8 Timed-out adults and former CalWORKs customers who received aid within the past 24 months, and ES participants who are in a long-term sanction, will be referred to Stage Two Child Care, unless they meet one of the circumstances listed above. Eligible Children Children up to and through age 12 are eligible to receive child care services. Children who are under court supervision may receive services up to age 18. Children with exceptional needs and/or who are severely disabled may continue to receive child care services up to age 21. Children may receive Stage One Child Care when all the following apply: And at least one of the following applies: •The parent has a need for child care services. •The family is receiving CalWORKs, or received CalWORKs within the last 24 months and child care isn’t available in Stage Two or Stage Three Child Care. •There is no parent or legal guardian or member of the Assistance Unit (AU) living in the home who is able and available to provide child care. •Lack of child care would result in the customer not being able to participate in ES or CL activities, employment, or any other county approved activity. •The child is a member of the AU, including the child of a CL participant. •The child is not a member of the AU because the child is receiving SSI/State Supplementary Payment (SSP) benefits or is in a Foster Care program. •The child is a member of a family with a former CalWORKs paren
