title: A. Employment Services Supportive Services
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Supportive Services Number Page 10-011.A 1 of 4 Revision Date: July 1, 2024 Background: Necessary supportive services must be available to every CalWORKs (CW) recipient participating in approved Employment Services (ES) activities. Participants will have good cause for not participating if supportive services are not available. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to add eligibility factors for ancillary payments for qualifying ES participants enrolled in Self-Employment. Policy: Payment for supportive services must be made as soon as possible to allow for the individual’s participation in assigned ES activities. Payments, except for child care, will be advanced so that personal funds are not used to pay for ES related expenses. Supportive Service Types Supportive Services include ancillary, transportation and child care expenses. Specific policies related to child care are provided in CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) section 10-010. Supportive services are also issued under the following circumstances: Transportation Costs Reasonable transportation costs are paid to a participant as needed for the following: • Travel to/from approved ES and Family Stabilization activities • Travel for both the parent and children to/from child care providers Circumstance Description Child Care for ES Sanctioned Individuals (who do not request to cure their sanction) ES sanctioned individuals are potentially eligible for child care assistance if they have received CW in the last 24 months. Participation to Cure a Sanction Supportive services may be authorized as needed for a sanctioned CW recipient who wants to participate in ES activities to cure a sanction. Voluntary Participant (Exempt/Excused 2nd Parent) Supportive services may be authorized as needed for a voluntary ES participant. Failure to Provide Verification of Attendance or Satisfactory Progress Supportive services cannot be withheld pending verification of attendance or satisfactory progress in an assigned ES activity. Supportive Services Pending an Appeal Participants are not entitled to a continuation of supportive services in the same amount or f rom pending a hearing decision. Participants are entitled to supportive services only at the level and in the form authorized by the Appeals decision. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Supportive Services Number Page 10-011.A 2 of 4 • Parking fees Ancillary Expenses Ancillary payments cover approved expenses other than child care and transportation. All ancillary expenses must be required, necessary and reasonable for the individual to participate in assigned ES activities and/or to accept/retain employment. Ancillary Expenses for Postsecondary Educational Programs ES participants who are enrolled full time or part time in a publicly funded postsecondary educational program will receive a n advanced standard payment (ASP) for books and college supplies prior to the start of the academic period. ES participants may also request an advanced payment or reimbursement for the actual costs of educational expenses exceeding the ASP. Ancillary Expenses for Self-Employment Participants assigned to Self-Employment may be eligible to receive one-time basic ancillary start-up expenses required to do their job. However, ES is not obligated to pay all cost s incurred by a participant when starting a business. Ancillary expenses may include, but are not limited to, tools, clothing, licensing, permitting and other fees and expenses necessary for self-employed participants to comply with local operating requirements. Student Financial Aid Statement Participants who receive financial aid for attendance in education and/or training programs may choose to receive ancillary supportive services payments for school -related costs such as supplies and books, even though the financial aid may include funds for those items. Employment Case Managers (ECMs) are required to obtain a signed Student Financial Aid Statement (WTW8) from all ES participants in approved educational or training activities to ensure that they are adequately informed of their rights and responsibilities regarding financial aid and supportive services. Disability Accommodations Ancillary supportive services must be issued to provide reasonable accommodations when necessary for individuals to participate on an equal basis with non -disabled participants in approved ES activities. Disabled individuals who request accommodations are not required to disclose their diagnosis, but only to verify the nature and extent of their disability. Diaper Supportive Services Assistance with diaper costs is considered a necessary supportive service to ensure ES participation of eligible families. Qualifying ES participants will receive diaper supportive services each month as an advanced ancillary payment for each child who is under 36 months of age meeting eligibility criteria. Participants will have good cause for not participating if diaper supportive services are not provided in advance of an assigned ES activity, and the lack of advanced supportive services impacted participation. To be eligible for diaper supportive services, ES participants must: 1. Have a child who is under 36 months of age at the beginning of the month and is receiving CW assistance or ineligible to receive cash aid but under the primary responsibility, care and control of the ES participant. The ineligible child must be linked to the Assistance Unit (AU) and living in the home. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Supportive Services Number Page 10-011.A 3 of 4 Examples: Sibling or half-sibling ineligible to receive cash aid due to undocumented status, receipt of Social Security Income (SSI/SSP), no deprivation due to either parent in the home working sufficient hours per CW requirements, children who are otherwise eligible but cannot be added to the AU until the next CW payment period 2. Be a mandatory or voluntary ES participant in good standing with program requirements, actively participating or waiting to be engaged in ES program activities Diaper supportive services may also be issued for participants who are: 1. In noncompliance and not yet financially sanctioned or removed from aid 2. Determined to have good cause for not meeting monthly participation requirements 3. In the process of curing a sanction or removal from cash aid 4. Exempt from ES but participating voluntarily 5. Excused 2nd Parents but participating voluntarily Diaper supportive services will not be issued to individuals who are: 1. Financially sanctioned or removed from cash aid and not in the process of curing the sanction/removal from cash aid 2. Exempt from ES and not participating voluntarily 3. Excused 2nd parents and not participating voluntarily 4. CW ineligible and only receiving cash aid for an eligible child (Child Only AU) 5. Receiving cash aid in a Pregnant Woman Only AU with no eligible children in the home 6. In an AU with a child not aided due to parent's failure to report birth of the child within required reporting timeframes and/or provide verifications required to add the child to the CW case Diaper supportive services will continue to be advanced until the first of the month in which the child reaches 36 months of age. Diaper supportive services will be discontinued if the participant opts out of the payment or is no longer eligible. Notification Requirements A timely Notice of Action (NOA) is required to be issued for supportive service approvals, denials and/or payment changes. When denying, decreasing, or discontinuing supportive services, a NOA must be issued at least ten calendar days prior to the effective date of the change. The ten days does not include the day the NOA is mailed or the effective date. A NOA is not required for approval of supportive services for one -time, short -term activities, such as Orientation/Appraisal. ES participants are required to notify their ECM at least ten calendar days before any anticipated changes affecting supportive services, except in emergency or exceptional situations. Procedure: Processing Guides 10-011.A1; 10-011.A2; Appendix A 10-011.A2 References: • MPP 42-750 • ACL 03-15; ACL18-38; ACL 21-04, ACL 22-80 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Supportive Services Number Page 10-011.A 4 of 4 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by July 31, 2027 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

Participants will have good cause for not participating if supportive services are not available. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to add eligibility factors for ancillary payments for qualifying ES participants enrolled in Self-Employment. Policy: Payment for supportive services must be made as soon as possible to allow for the individual’s participation in assigned ES activities. Payments, except for child care, will be advanced so that personal funds are not used to pay for ES related expenses. Supportive Service Types Supportive Services include ancillary, transportation and child care expenses. Specific policies related to child care are provided in CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) section 10-010. title: B. Behavioral Health Services
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page Behavioral Health Services 10-011.B 1 of 1 Revision Date: 07/01/2020 Background: Individuals participating in CalWORKs Employment Services (ES) are required to provide relevant information during Appraisal or regular case management in order to be assigned to appropriate ES activities. This may include information relating to physical and behavioral health, including, but not limited to, mental health and substance use issues, past or present domestic abuse issues or any other barrier that may affect an individual’s ability to participate in work activities. Purpose: The purpose of this material is to streamline and consolidate policies and procedures for Mental Health Services (MHS) and Substance Abuse Services (SAS), previously outlined in CPG 10-011.D and 10-011.E, under a new section entitled Behavioral Health Services (BHS). Policy: BHS Referral and Assignment ES participants can be referred to BHS as needed to address concerns impairing their ability to participate in assigned activities. BHS participants may be referred to MHS, SAS and/or Family Violence Services (FVS). Policies and procedures pertaining to FVS are found in CPG 40-100.O and Processing Guides 40-100.O1-O3. BHS may be assigned as an Initial Engagement activity at time of Appraisal for a period of four consecutive weeks (CPG 10-005.E). If it is determined that BHS activities are needed in excess of the initial four consecutive weeks, or at any time, the ECM will refer the individual to an Assessment/Reassessment and assign additional BHS activities on an ES plan. ES Plan for BHS The ES plan will include BHS activities determined as a result of the BHS assessment, including those related to a secondary diagnosis, appropriate employment accommodations or restrictions, supportive services and treatment requirements. Any prior diagnosis, evaluation, or assessment provided by the participant will also be considered in the development the ES plan. Noncompliance with BHS When the Employment Case Manager (ECM) determines that a participant in BHS activities is out of compliance with program requirements, the determination of whether the participant has good cause for Noncompliance will include consideration of whether the participant's BHS issue caused or substantially contributed to the failure to comply. The ECM will consult with the BHS provider to make this determination. Procedure: Processing Guide 10-011.B References: MPP 42-711, 42-716 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 07/31/2023

title: A. Employment Services Exemptions
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Exemptions Number Page 10-020.A 1 of 4 Revision Date: June 1, 2025 Background: CalWORKs (CW) customers are required to participate in Employment Services (ES) activities unless they are excused or exempt from participation. Excused or exempt customers may voluntarily participate in ES with certain exceptions. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to update policy to remove the once-in-a-lifetime ES exemption for truant teens per All County Letter (ACL) 23-30. ACL 23 -30 indicates that individuals who lose this exemption due to truancy and are required to participate in ES may receive this exemption again by resuming full-time school attendance if otherwise eligible. Policy has been updated to indicate that an ES exemption for truant teens can be reinstated if the student later complies with school attendance requirements. Policy: Excused from Participation The following individuals are excused from participation in ES activities: • Cal-Learn Participant: A pregnant or parenting teen who is subject to Cal -Learn Program requirements. • Second Parent: A second parent in a two- parent household with unemployment deprivation is excused from participation if the other parent is meeting required ES participation hours. • Non-Minor Dependent (NMD): A dependent or ward of the court who is age 18 to 21 and is meeting Assembly Bill (AB) 12 program requirements to receive extended CalWORKs benefits. • Parent/Optional Stepparent: A parent or optional stepparent is excused from participation if the other parent in the Assistance Unit (AU) is meeting the required participation hours. ES Exemption Criteria 1. Age: Individuals under age 16 or age 60 and older. 2. School Attendance: o Full-Time Student: An individual who is age 16, 17, or 18 and is attending high school full time or a vocational or technical school full time. Full -time status is determined by the school. Noncompliance with school attendance requirements will end the exemption and the truant student will be required to participate in ES. An exemption can be reinstated if the student later complies with school attendance requirements. o Post-Secondary Education: An individual who is age 16 or 17, has completed high school or equivalent, and is enrolled or planning to enroll in a post -secondary educational, vocational, or technical school training program. An e xemption cannot continue beyond the beginning of the school term without verification of enrollment. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Exemptions Number Page 10-020.A 2 of 4 3. Disability: An individual who has a disability that is expected to last at least 30 calendar days that significantly impairs their ability to be regularly employed or participate in ES activities. An exemption will be granted if medical verification includes: (1) a description of the disability, (2) the expected duration of the disability, (3) the extent to which the disability impairs the individual’s employment and/or participation in ES activities, and (4) indicates that the individual is actively seeking appropriate medical treatment. Medical verification must be from a doctor or health care professional that is licensed in the United States to diagnose/treat physical and mental impairments. An exemption will not be granted if the medical verification indicates the individual can meet ES participation requirements. An exemption should be reviewed at the time the condition is expected to end or earlier if there is reason to believe there has been a change in the condition. An exemption based on disability will be granted retroactively if the individual’s condition impaired their ability to be employed or participate in ES activities prior to the exemption request date and they were actively seeking treatment during that time based on the medical verification provided. 4. Aided Nonparent Caretaker Relative: A needy caretaker relative who has primary responsibility to care for a child who is either: (1) a dependent or ward of the court, (2) a Kin-GAP recipient, or (3) at risk of placement in foster care as determined by the County. An exemption will be granted if the County determines that the caretaking responsibilities are beyond normal day -to-day parenting responsibilities and impair the caretaker’s ability to be regularly employed or participate in ES activities. Verification may include court documentation or other statement from Child and Family Well Being (CFWB). 5. Care of an Ill or Incapacitated Household Member: An individual whose presence in the home is required due to the illness or incapacity of another (aided or unaided) member of the household. An exemption will be granted if the County determines that the caretaking responsibilities impair the caretaker’s ability to be regularly employed or participate in ES activities. Verification may include medical verification forms or other statement from a doctor/health care professional, such as Family Medical Leave Act (FMLA) documentation. An exemption will not be granted if medical verification indicates the individual can meet ES participation requirements, or if there is a second parent in the home who is ES sanctioned. 6. Care of a Child: An exemption may be given to only one parent at a time in a two-parent household. An exemption will not be given if the other parent is ES sanctioned. o Age 6 Months or Under: A parent or caretaker relative who has primary responsibility to personally provide care to a child 6 months of age or under will be granted a one-time exemption. The exemption may be reduced to the first 12 weeks or extended to the first 12 months on a case-by-case basis after the birth or adoption of the child based on factors such as the availability of child care. o Age 12 Weeks: An individual who has previously received the one- time exemption for caring for a child 6 months of age or under will be exempt for 12 weeks upon the birth or adoption of any subsequent children. The exemption may be extended to 6 months on a case-by-case basis based on factors such as the availability of child care. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Exemptions Number Page 10-020.A 3 of 4 o Age 0-23 Months: A parent or caretaker relative who has primary responsibility to personally provide care to a child 0-23 months of age will be granted a one- time exemption upon request. The exemption may be reinstated after a break in aid if the same child continues to meet the age criteria. The exemption may switch from one parent to the other only one -time if there is a change in caretaking responsibilities for the same child. The parent will not qualify for the exemption again if they move to a new AU. 7. Pregnancy: A pregnant customer can qualify for an exemption during any trimester of pregnancy with approved and timely medical verification. Pregnancy verification may include a sworn written statement or verbal attestation by the customer provided that the customer submits medical verification of the pregnancy within 30 business days. A 30-day pregnancy exemption will be granted upon receipt of a sworn written statement or verbal attestation. The exemption may continue for the duration of the pregnancy if medical verification is provided within the 30- day timeframe after the sworn written statement or verbal attestation is provided. This is not a CalWORKs time limit exemption, however, pregnant customers may be eligible for other time limit exemptions based on disability. 8. Volunteers in Service to America (VISTA) Participation: An individual who is a full-time volunteer in the VISTA Program, as verified by a copy of a Domestic Volunteers Statement or a written verification from the VISTA sponsor or the Federal Region IX ACTION/VISTA Office. Exemption Verification Customers are required to provide required documentation to establish a basis for an exemption. A range of documents may be accepted to verify the exemption if documentation meets the required criteria. If an individual prefers that the C ounty obtain this information on their behalf, the C ounty will have the individual sign a release that is compliant with the Health Information Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA). For more information about HIPAA, go to http://www.hhs.gov/ocr/privacy/. Exemption Period An e xemption will be granted prospectively based on the exemption request date and verification provided, with the exception of retroactive disability exemptions. An exemption will end when criteria is no longer met. Voluntary Participation Excused or exempt individuals may volunteer to participate in ES with the exception of individuals who are subject to Cal -Learn or NMD program requirements. Individuals who are exempt due to disability or care of an ill or incapacitated household member may volunteer in ES activities only to the extent permitted by the medical verification provided. Procedure: Processing Guide 10-020.A1 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Exemptions Number Page 10-020.A 4 of 4 References: Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 42-701,42-712; All County Letter (ACL) 12-72, 13-52, 15- 08, 19-45, 21-134, 22-55, 23-30 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by June 30, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: B. Employment Services Good Cause
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Good Cause Number Page 10-020.B 1 of 1 Revision Date: November 1, 2024 Background: A participant may be excused from Employment Services (ES) participation on a case- by-case basis due to G ood Cause (GC), when it is determined that there is a condition or other circumstance that temporarily prevents or significantly impairs the participant’s ability to be regularly employed or participate in ES activities. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to complete a sunset review, streamline policies, and remove GC procedures from the CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG). A corresponding Processing Guide (PG) has been created for this purpose. This update also adds additional employment related GC reasons outlined in All County Letter (ACL) 23-30. Policy: Good Cause Evaluation GC is intended to temporarily address a participant’s reason for noncompliance, allowing them to resolve barriers which are preventing success in assigned activities leading to self -sufficiency. ES participants are required to provide information substantiating GC to complete the evaluation. Good Cause Determination ES staff will evaluate GC criteria and document the outcome of the determination and continuing validity monthly and more often as needed depending on the nature of the request. If GC is determined, then ES staff will continue to engage and assist the participant in meeting monthly participation requirements. If GC is not determined, then ES staff will initiate the noncompliance process as described in CPG 10-025.A and PG 10-025.A1. Procedure: PG 10-020.B1 References: Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 42-713, 42-721; All County Letter (ACL) 17-08, 23-30 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by November 30, 2027 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: A. Employment Services Noncompliance and Sanctions
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Noncompliance and Sanctions Number Page 10-025.A 1 of 3 Revision Date: July 1, 2026 Background: An individual who is required to participate in Employment Services (ES) program activities as a condition of receipt of California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids (CalWORKs) benefits is subject to noncompliance and sanctions if they fail or refuse to comply with program requirements without good cause. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to update noncompliance and sanction policies from changes introduced by Senate Bill (SB) 119 and All County Letter (ACL) 26- 28. This revision includes several changes to noncompliance and sanction processes , such as establishing a period during which noncompliance and sanction cannot be applied once CalWORKs is approved, allowing multiple rescheduling of cause determination appointments, ensuring child care is secured prior to initiating noncompliance, and simplifying the sanction cure process. Policy: No Sanction Period (NSP) Effective July 1, 2026, m andatory ES participants are not subject to noncompliance and financial sanctions within the first 90 calendar days from the date they are approved for CalWORKs. This 90 - day NSP restarts with each CalWORKs approval. During the NSP, participants are eligible to receive necessary supportive services and resources to remove barriers affecting successful engagement and participation. After the NSP, the participant is subject to noncompliance and sanctions. Noncompliance Participants are subject to ES sanctions whenever they fail or refuse to comply with program requirements without good cause and subsequently fail or refuse to agree or comply with a compliance plan without good cause. Participants cannot be sanctioned for assignments not provided in writing. Noncompliance with program requirements includes a failure or refusal to: • Sign an ES plan • Participate in an assigned program activity • Provide required proof of satisfactory progress in an assigned program activity • Accept employment • Continue employment • Continue employment at the same level of earnings Good cause reasons supporting the failure or refusal to comply with program requirements must be evaluated and allowed if valid. Cause Determination (CD) A CD appointment must be scheduled within 20-calendar days of the sanction notice of action to provide the participant an opportunity to demonstrate that they have good cause for refusal or failure to comply County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Noncompliance and Sanctions Number Page 10-025.A 2 of 3 with the program requirements. The CD appointment may be rescheduled as needed within the 20 calendar day compliance period. If good cause is found, the sanction request will be rescinded. Compliance Plan If there is no good cause found for the failure or refusal to comply, the participant can agree to a Compliance Plan (CP) to avoid a sanction upon successful completion. To resolve the instance of noncompliance, the participant is required to: • Sign a WTW 32 Compliance Plan and • Satisfactorily perform the activity specified in the WTW 32 The timeframe of the CP cannot exceed the timeframe of the original activity that caused the instance of noncompliance, and the CP cannot exceed 60 calendar days. Sanctions for Two-Parent Assistance Units All noncompliance and sanction procedures must be applied independently to each adult in a two- parent Assistance Unit (AU). Participation by the second parent does not cure the first parent’s sanction. Each parent must cure their own sanction independently. Additionally, i f one parent is sanctioned, the second parent must begin or increase hours of participation required by the household to avoid being sanctioned as well, unless exempt or meeting good cause criteria. Sanction Effective Date An ES sanction is effective immediately after the 20-day CD period has ended and either: • No good cause has been found, or • No good cause has been found, and the participant does not agree to a CP The participant is considered sanctioned the day after the 20-day CD period has ended (21st day) and must meet requirements to cure a sanction even though the financial sanction does not start until the date reflected on the notice of action sent to them. Sanction Cure A sanction will end when the noncompliant participant contacts eligibility or ES staff to request to cure their sanction with an intent to participate in ES activities. The sanction cure r equest can be made verbally or in writing. The request date is considered the sanction cure contact date which determines the restoration of aid month. Restoration of Aid When a sanction is successfully cured, cash aid will be restored effective the first day of the month following the sanction cure contact date, if all other eligibility criteria is met. Sanction Curing After Break in Aid Sanctioned individuals who reapply for CalWORKs after a break in aid are automatically deemed as having requested to cure their sanction with an intent to participate in ES activities. The sanction is ended during the CalWORKs intake process , and aid is restored in the application month following existing CalWORKs eligibility requirements. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Employment Services Noncompliance and Sanctions Number Page 10-025.A 3 of 3 Procedure: Processing Guides (PG) 10- 025.A1 ES Noncompliance Process , PG 10 -025.A2 ES Cause Determination Process, PG 10-025.A3 ES Compliance Plan, PG 10-025.A4 ES Sanction Cure Process, PG 10-025.A1 Appendix A ES Noncompliance Process, PG 10-005.A1 ES Referral Process, and PG 10-020.B1 ES Good Cause. References: Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 42-721 All County Letter (ACL) 03-59; 04-47; 06-27; 25-78; 26-28 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by July 31, 2029. Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services

Compliance Plan If there is no good cause found for the failure or refusal to comply, the participant can agree to a Compliance Plan (CP) to avoid a sanction upon successful completion. To resolve the instance of noncompliance, the participant is required to: • Sign a WTW 32 Compliance Plan and • Satisfactorily perform the activity specified in the WTW 32 The timeframe of the CP cannot exceed the timeframe of the original activity that caused the instance of noncompliance, and the CP cannot exceed 60 calendar days. Sanctions for Two-Parent Assistance Units All noncompliance and sanction procedures must be applied independently to each adult in a two- parent Assistance Unit (AU). Participation by the second parent does not cure the first parent’s sanction. Each parent must cure their own sanction independently. Additionally, i f one parent is sanctioned, the second parent must begin or increase hours of participation required by the household to avoid being sanctioned as well, unless exempt or meeting good cause criteria. Sanction Effective Date An ES sanction is effective

title: H. Employment Services Grievances
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page Employment Services Grievances 10-030.H 1 of 2 Revision Date: 09/01/20 Background: Employment Services (ES) participants have the right to dispute any program requirement or assignment they believe to be in violation of, or inconsistent with, state law and regulations governing the ES program. Purpose: The purpose of this material is to update policies for ES Grievances by requiring a review by ES Contractors and Eligibility Operations, instead of the Appeals section, and creating a Processing Guide. Policy: Complaint Resolution When possible, ES complaints regarding regulations and/or processes should first be handled at the level of the Employment Case Manager (ECM) and ECM Supervisor. This also applies to other ES programs, such as Child Care and Cal-Learn. When the complaint cannot be resolved on an informal basis, the ECM and ECM Supervisor will inform participants of their right to file a formal grievance or request a state hearing. State hearings are offered as an alternative to the formal grievance process or to appeal the outcome of a formal grievance. Policies and Procedures related to state hearings are found in the Eligibility Policy and Procedure Guide. ES Grievance Process The formal ES Grievance Process is offered as a method to determine whether a program requirement or assignment is in violation of the ES plan or is otherwise inconsistent with ES program requirements. ES participants are required to participate in assigned ES activities during the Grievance process and are entitled to supportive services to enable participation. Individuals who fail to participate during the ES Grievance process, or any subsequent appeal, are subject to sanction pending the outcome of the process if they fail to participate as required. The ES Grievance Process cannot be used: •To appeal the outcome of a state hearing or the results of an ES Assessment/Reassessment. Individuals disputing the outcome of an ES Assessment/Reassessment are referred for a Third Party Assessment (CPG 10-005.G) •For individuals who have failed to successfully resolve an instance of noncompliance and are deemed sanctioned. Sanctioned individuals may request a state hearing to appeal a program requirement or assignment Procedure: Processing Guide 10-030.H.1 References: MPP 42-700, 42-721, 42-750 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page Employment Services Grievances 10-030.H 2 of 2 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 09/30/2023 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations

title: I. Sanctions and State Hearings
content: I. Sanctions and State Hearings Regulation State regulations require that when a participant believes that any program requirement or assignment is in violation of, or inconsistent with, state law and regulations governing the Welfare to Work (WTW) program, the County shall inform him/her of the right either to request a state hearing or to file a formal grievance. Reference: 10-030 H ‘Welfare to Work Grievance’. http://hhsa-pg.sdcounty.ca.gov/CalWORKS/10-030/Welfare-To-Work_Grievance/H_Welfare-to- Work_Grievance.htm Sanctions and State Hearings If an individual appeals his or her sanction through the State hearing process in a timely manner, the sanction may not be imposed until a hearing decision sustaining the county’s action is issued. The county must continue to pay cash aid and necessary childcare as long as the individual is otherwise eligible pending the hearing decision. If the county’s action is sustained, aid is discontinued effective the end of the payment month in which the hearing decision is received. Note: The Employment Case Manager (ECM) must make note of the request for a fair hearing and monitor for hearing results. The ECM summarizes all hearing-related activities in CalWIN Case Comments. Right to File an Appeal or Grievance Whenever a participant believes that any program requirement or assignment in this program is in violation of his/her WTW plan, the participant may request a state hearing pursuant to MPP Division 22 or utilize the county’s formal grievance procedure. If the participant is not satisfied with the grievance procedure, he/she may appeal the decision in accordance with state appeal procedures. Requirement to Participate Pending Outcome of Appeal Participants are required to participate in assigned WTW activities pending the outcome of the formal grievance procedure and/or any subsequent appeal. Participants are subject to sanctions only if they fail to participate during the period the grievance procedure is being processed. A participant cannot utilize the grievance procedure to appeal the results of an assessment. Appeals to the United States If a participant is not satisfied with the decision of a state fair hearing concerning on-the-job working conditions or worker’s compensation Department of Labor coverage, the participant can file an appeal with the United States Department of Labor, as provided by federal law. State Hearing Decision If the hearing decision is in favor of the… Then… County, cash aid that was paid is not considered an overpayment. The sanction is deferred and not imposed until after the receipt of the hearing decision. individual, the County must reimburse the individual for any necessary transportation and/or work-or-trainingrelated expenses that he or she paid out of pocket, or was obliged to pay, during the time the hearing decision was pending.

title: A. Community Service-Work Experience
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Community Service-Work Experience Number Page 10-050.A 1 of 3 Revision Date: January 1, 2021 Background: Employment Services (ES) participants must be assigned to employment, education and/or training activities leading to self -sufficiency which can include Community Service (CS), Work Ex perience (WEX) and barrier removal activities. Part icipants may receive necessary supportive services to ensure participation and satisfactory progress. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to consolidate CS and WEX in this section, remove all procedures from CalWIN Program Guide (CPG) and include them in the corresponding processing guide. Policy: Community Service CS is an ES training activity that is temporary and transitional, performed in the public or private nonprofit sector, under the close super vision of the activit y provider. Examples of potential CS sites are faith-based organizations, non-profit Social Service s agencies, homeless shelter s, schools, etc. The CS activity Is assigned to provide basic job s kills leading to employ ment while meeting a community need. Self-Initiated Community Service Participants can choose to participate in a self -initiated CS program. P articipation in self-initiated CS is only permitted if the activ ity meets the CS criteria. These participants are not requir ed to attend a CS Orientation. Work Experience WEX is an unpaid ES training activity performed in a public or private setting to assist ES participants who need work experience prior to being placed in employment . The purpose of WEX is to provide basic job skills or enhance current job skills in a position related to the participant's experience. Note: CS/WEX activities are lim ited to a maxi mum of 12-months in a lifetime and are covered by State Workers’ Compensation. Orientation All participants assigned to CS /WEX are required to attend an Orientation to understand their rights and responsibilities . All CS/WEX participants will be evaluated for the most appropriate site placement. Participants who are in a self-initiated CS do not need to attend the CS Orientation. The Employment Case Manager (ECM) will monitor the participant’s progress and job readiness each month to determine if a referral to Expanded Work Experience (EWE) or Expande d Subsidized Employment (ESE) is appropriate. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Community Service-Work Experience Number Page 10-050.A 2 of 3 Site Development: A CS/WEX site is a public or private non-profit site that agrees to supervise a specified number of ES participants and provide them with basic job skills or enhance existing job skills leading to employment ES Contractors in each region are responsible for: • Developing and monitoring CS/WEX sites • Providing CS/WEX placement services • Ensuring site compliance with Federal, State, and County regulations • Reporting accidents/injuries • Ensuring participants are placed in a timely manner ES Contractors are required to develop their own procedures for: • Development and maintenance of Regional Cooperative Agreements with the sites. A Cooperative Agreement is entered into be tween the ES Contractor and the site to ensure compliance with all rules. Activation and deactivation of worksites. Participation Hours CS and WEX participants can only complete the maximum number of hours per month allowed by the Fair Labor S tandards A ct (FLSA). S ee Processing Guide 10- 050.A for calculat ion instr uctions. I f a participant completes additional CS/WEX hours, those hours cannot be claimed. Participants who complete the maximum amount of CS/WEX hours, will be deemed as meeting core hourly requirements. H owever, participants must still co mplete additional hours in other approv ed activities to meet W TW average weekly parti cipation requirements. The process of “deeming core hours” applies only to CS and/or unpaid WEX activities. Accident procedures and Workers’ Compensation Coverage: Participants w ho are injured w hile participati ng in CS activit ies are co vered by W orkers’ Compensation which is provided by the State of California. Procedure: Processing Guide 10-050.A.1 References: MPP 42-701.2, 42-709.4, 42-716(2)(A) ACLs 13-56, 18-70 CPG 10-150.B Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by Dec 30, 2024 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Community Service-Work Experience Number Page 10-050.A 3 of 3 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations

title: A. Expanded Subsidized Employment Program
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Expanded Subsidized Employment (ESE) Number Page 10-150.A 1 of 2 Revision Date: July 1, 2019 Background: The Expanded Subsidized Employment (ESE) program provides subsidized employment opportunities to eligible i ndividuals. Participants are employed by ESE employers and receive subsidized wages that are countable as earned income for eligibility purposes. Purpose: This section has been updated to add new policies for the reinstatement of subsidies in certain situations and to incorporate clarification for sanctioned participants and timed -out Safety Net adults previously issued via CalWORKs Policy Inquiry 2017-05. Policy: Program Eligibility Eligible individuals include: • Active CalWORKs recipients who are participating in Employment Services (Welfare-to-Work) and deemed to be job ready • Sanctioned individuals who will cure their sanction through subsidized employment as part of their Sanction Cure Plan . Individuals must maintain compliance with Employment Services requirements to continue in a subsidized placement. Participants must maintain their eligibility to CalWORKs and continue to meet Employment Services requirements while in the ESE program, with certain exceptions: • Participants who become ineligible to CalWORKs due to ESE income may remain in the ESE program until their placement ends. • Participants who reach their CalWORKs time limit an d continue to receive CalWORKs Safety Net benefits for their child(ren) may remain in the ESE program until the Safety Net benefits end. If the CalWORKs discontinuance is due to ESE income , timed-out participants (Safety Net adults) may remain in ESE until their placement ends. Participants who become ineligible to CalWORKs or stop participating in Employment Services for any other reason will be discontinued from the ESE program and subsidies must end. Participation in ESE may resume with County approval if the individual’s CalWORKs eligibility is reinstated within 30 days of the discontinuance and ESE program eligibility criteria continues to be met. Subsidies cannot be paid for ineligible individuals or for any time period in which there was a break in CalWORKs aid. ESE Placement Participants are limited to a maximum of six months of subsidized employment, unless eligible to an extension. The placement must be an effective Employment Services activity that will lead to self - sufficiency. If the placement ends earlier than planned or the placement was not the best fit for the participant’s skills or the current job market, a subsequent placement may be allowed on a case-by-case basis. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Expanded Subsidized Employment (ESE) Number Page 10-150.A 2 of 2 ESE Extension The placement may be extended in three -month increments with County approval , for up to six additional months. An extension will only be granted if additional time will increase the likelihood of: • Participant obtaining unsubsidized employment with the participating employer, or • Participant obtaining specific skills and experiences relevant for unsubsidized employment for a particular field. The extension reason (criteria listed above) and approved timeframe must be documented in the case record. Participants may not exceed 12 months in subsidized employment and must meet ESE program eligibility criteria to be eligible for an extension . This includes participants who are no longer eligible to CalWORKs due to ESE income as well as timed-out Safety Net adults. Employers and Subsidies ESE employer s pay wages to participant s, withhold taxes, and provid e workers’ compensation coverage and paid sick leave for the duration of the employment, as required by State law. Subsidies are paid for the ESE wages of eligible participants and other allowable costs under the ESE program. Subsidies cannot be paid for ineligible individuals or for any time period in which there was a break in CalWORKs aid. Procedure: Processing Guide 10-150.A1 ESE Procedures Processing Guide 10-150.A4 ESE-EWE Monthly Reporting Procedures Impacts: Former ESE participants who lost CalWORKs eligibility due to ESE income are to be evaluated as current recipients if they reapply for aid within three calendar months of their subsidies ending. Contact CalWORKs Program staff to confirm the subsidy end date. References: MPP 42-716.8 ACIN I-24-18 ACL 12-15, 12-29, 13-81, 14-17, 14-81, 16-17, 16-95, 17-03 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by July 31, 2022. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations

title: B. Expanded Work Experience Program
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Expanded Work Experience (EWE) Number Page 10-150.B 1 of 2 Revision Date: July 1, 2019 Background: The Expanded Work Experience (EWE) program provides paid on -the-job training to eligible individuals in preparation for enrollment in the Expanded Subsidized Employment (ESE) program described in CPG 10 -150.A. Participants are assigned to EWE worksites and receive subsidized wages that are countable as earned income for eligibility purposes. Purpose: This section has been updated due to sunset review. Updates include n ew policies for the reinstatement of subsidies in certain situations and clarification t hat participants receive subsidized wages for the duration of their EWE assignment, but are not employees of the worksite. Policy: Program Eligibility Eligible individuals are CalWORKs recipients who are participating in Employment Services (Welfareto-Work) and need to enhance existing skills to become job ready and qualify for the ESE program . Eligible individuals have already acquired basic job skills through past employment or training activities, such as Community Service or unpaid Work Experience (WEX). Participants must maintain their eligibility to CalWORKs and continue to meet Employment Services requirements while in the EWE program. Participants who become ineligible to CalWORKs or stop participating in Employment Services for any reason will be discontinued from the EWE program and subsidies must end. Participation in EWE may resume if the individual’s CalWORKs eligibility is reinstated within 30 days of the discontinuance and EWE program eligibility criteria continues to be met . Subsidies cannot be paid for ineligible individuals or for any time period in which there was a break in CalWORKs aid. EWE Assignment Participants are given a short-term (six months or less) assignment at an established EWE worksite. EWE must be include d in the participant’s Welfare-to-Work (WTW) Plan and cannot be concurrent with any other training activity (such as Community Service or WEX) , or an ESE placement , at the same site. EWE assignments will be part -time (no more than 20 hours per week), with consideration for any other household income, to prevent ineligibility to CalWORKs due to EWE income. The individual’s progress and participation will be evaluated each month to ensure the assignment is an effective Employment Services activity that will lead to successful transition to ESE . If the assignment does not result in a successful transition to ESE or unsubsidized employment, a subsequent assignment may be given on a case-by-case basis if appropriate for the WTW Plan. EWE Extension The assignment may be extended in three -month increments, for up to six additional months, on a case-by-case basis. An extension may be granted if additional time in the assignment will enable the County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Expanded Work Experience (EWE) Number Page 10-150.B 2 of 2 participant to overcome employment barriers that are preventing his/her transition to the ESE program. The extension reason and approved timeframe must be documented in the case record. Worksites and Subsidies EWE worksites are established with local employers and agencies that provide participants with onthe-job training opportunities. Participants receive weekly wages for the duration of their EWE assignment, but are no t employe es of the EWE worksite. Participants may not receive subsidized wages from the EWE and ESE programs at the same time. Subsidies are paid for the EWE wages of el igible participants and other allowable program costs. Subsidies cannot be paid for ineligible individuals or for any time period in which there was a break in CalWORKs aid. Procedure: Processing Guide 10-150.B1 EWE Procedures Processing Guide 10-150.A4 ESE-EWE Monthly Reporting Procedures References: MPP 42-716.8 ACIN I-24-18 ACL 12-15, 13-81, 14-17, 14-81, 16-17, 17-03 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by July 31, 2022. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations

If the assignment does not result in a successful transition to ESE or unsubsidized employment, a subsequent assignment may be given on a case-by-case basis if appropriate for the WTW Plan. EWE Extension The assignment may be extended in three -month increments, for up to six additional months, on a case-by-case basis. An extension may be granted if additional time in the assignment will enable the County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Expanded Work Experience (EWE) Number Page 10-150.B 2 of 2 participant to overcome employment barriers that are preventing his/her transition to the ESE program. The extension reason and approved timeframe must be documented in the case record. Worksites and Subsidies EWE worksites are established with local employers and agencies that provide participants with onthe-job training opportunities. Participants receive weekly wages for the duration of their EWE assignment, but are no t employe es of the EWE worksite. Participants may not receive subsidized wages from the EWE and ESE programs at the same time. Subsidies are paid for the EWE wages of el igible participants and other allowable program costs. Subsidies cannot be paid for ineligible individuals or for any time period in which there was a break in CalWORKs aid. title: A. Wrap Around
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Wrap Around Number Page 10-160.A 1 of 2 Revision Date: March 1, 2025 Background: The Wrap Around program consists of Intensive Case Management services. It provides closely supervised intensive case management assistance to Employment Services (ES) participants from a team of professionals. Purpose: The purpose of the Wrap Around program is to remove barriers that are preventing the customer(s) from participation in ES activities, by providing intensive and supportive relationships between the family, Employment Case Manager (ECM) and other support systems such as schools and employers. Because the entire family is mentored, participants learn how to develop contingency plans for working parent issues. The health and well -being of the child and the entire family is considered to make the transition to work a positive experience for all family members. This material revision is due to sunset date review. No policy or procedure changes have been made. Policy: Target Populations • Currently sanctioned from ES within the last six months. • Individuals returning to ES activities from Behavioral Health Services treatment. • Cal-Learn families transitioning to ES. • CalWORKs families who have known barriers to self-sufficiency. • Other populations identified by the County. Program Services • Identification and recruitment of families to receive services. • Family assessment to identify barriers to self-sufficiency. • Using plan of action to remove barriers to self-sufficiency. • Coordination of all resources needed to achieve plan of action. • Retention services to follow up with participants six months after leaving the Intensive Case Management program. Length of Services Services are to be provided for a period of up to 90 days to each family. Exceptions to continue working with a family beyond 90 days may be requested. Partnerships ES sites will have documented collaborative agreements with organizations offering resources that may aid in the removal of barriers and support self-sufficiency for families. Procedure: None. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Wrap Around Number Page 10-160.A 2 of 2 References: None. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by March 31, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: CalWORKs Outcomes and Accountability Review (Cal-OAR)
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide CalWORKs Outcomes and Accountability Review (Cal-OAR) Number Page 10-170 1 of 4 Effective Date: October 1, 2023 Background: The CalWORKs Outcomes and Accountability Review (Cal-OAR) was established by SB 89 (statutes of 2017) as Welfare and Institutions Code (WIC) 11523 to facilitate continuous quality improvement in county CalWORKs programs and further customer engagement. Cal-OAR implements a local, databased program management system that collects, analyzes, and shares outcomes and best practices. The passage of AB 79 (Statutes of 2020) suspended Cal-OAR during State Fiscal Year 2020 -21 and changed the Cal-OAR structure into five-year cycles, with the first Cal-OAR cycle beginning on July 1, 2021, and ending on June 30, 2026. Purpose: The purpose of this new section is to add Cal-OAR policies to the CalWORKs Program Guide. Policy: Stakeholder Engagement A stakeholder workgroup was convened by the California Department of Social Services ( CDSS) to obtain recommendations regarding Cal -OAR components and implementation plan. Future activities for the workgroup include evaluating lessons learned and needed adjustments from the first Cal-OAR cycle, assessing the need for additional performance measures, establishing standard target thresholds for each process measure and, if needed, institut ing state-wide performance standards for outcome measure(s). Cal-OAR Continuous Quality Improvement (Cal-CQI) A continuous quality improvement process will be used to improve CalWORKs program processes and outcomes utilizing regular self-assessment, analysis, and ongoing data collection. The Cal-OAR Cal- CQI process consists of three main components: performance measures, a county CalWORKs Self - Assessment, and a CalWORKs System Improvement Plan. CDSS will work collaboratively with counties throughout Cal-OAR implementation, and on an ongoing basis . CDSS will provide technical assistance to ensure consistent reporting and accurate data entry across counties. During each five-year Cal-OAR Cal-CQI cycle, counties will: • Conduct a County Self-Assessment: Including local stakeholder engagement and developing a CalWORKs County Self-Assessment (Cal-CSA) Report • Develop a System Improvement Plan : Including peer review participation and developing a CalWORKs System Improvement Plan (Cal-SIP) Report • Implement & Evaluate Strategies for Improvement • Report Progress : Including continued peer review participation and dev eloping a Cal-SIP Progress Report Cal-OAR Performance Measures Cal-OAR performance measures were developed by CDSS, in consultation with the stakeholder workgroup, and will be used by counties for Cal-CSA and Cal-SIP development. CDSS will combine Statewide Automated Welfare Systems (SAWS) data, available CDSS data, and other statewide data County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide CalWORKs Outcomes and Accountability Review (Cal-OAR) Number Page 10-170 2 of 4 to calculate the county’s Cal-OAR performance measures. Measures will be calculated and reported in a staggered manner, based on data availability, over a five-year cycle. To support measure accuracy, counties will enter Cal-OAR data elements in the ir automated systems in an accurate and consistent manner. Measures are interrelated to support a holistic assessment of a county’s CalWORKs program and are not intended to be evaluated in isolation from the other measures. Cal-OAR performance measures are categorized as either process measures or outcome measures. During the first five-year cycle, both county and state-wide data baselines will be established for each of the process measures to compare with subsequent data sets. After the first cycle, target thresholds will be determined for process measures in consultation with counties and other st akeholders. Statewide standards may also be established for outcome measures, if needed. In addition to SAWS data, CDSS will calculate Cal -OAR performance measures using data obtained directly from the following state-level agencies/databases: • Employment Development Department (EDD) • Online CalWORKs Appraisal Tool (OCAT) • Medi-Cal Eligibility Determination System (MEDS) • California Department of Public Health (CDPH) • California Department of Education (CDE) • California Community Colleges Chancellor’s Office (CCCCO) The following are Phase 1 Cal-OAR performance measures: • Engagement Rate • Sanction Rate • Sanction Resolution Rate • Orientation Attendance Rate • Online CalWORKs Appraisal Tool (OCAT)/Appraisal Completion Timeliness Rate • First Activity Attendance Rate • Improved Literacy, Basic Skills, English Language Acquisition • Community College Progress Rate The following are Phase 2 Cal-OAR performance measures: • OCAT/Appraisal to Next Activity Timeliness Rate • Education and Skills Development Access Rate • Education and Skills Development Utilization Rate • Child Care Access Rate • Homeless Assistance and Housing Support Program Access Rate • Ancillary Services Access Rate • Transportation Provision Timeliness Rate • Subsidized to Unsubsidized Employment Rate • Educational Completion Rate • Home Visiting Transitions to Welfare-To-Work (WTW) Engagement Rate • Family Stabilization Transitions to WTW Engagement Rate County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide CalWORKs Outcomes and Accountability Review (Cal-OAR) Number Page 10-170 3 of 4 CalWORKs County Self-Assessment (Cal-CSA) Through the Cal-CSA process, Counties will conduct a comprehensive evaluation of their CalWORKs program performance based on the established performance measures, including identifying strengths and weaknesses of current program practices and resource deployment, how local operations and systemic factors affect program outcomes , and a reas of improvement to focus on in their Cal -SIP. Counties will actively engage and collaborate with local stakeholders while completing the Cal -CSA process and developing their CalWORKs County Self -Assessment (Cal -CSA) Report . CDSS will provide templates and tools to facilitate county analysis of performance measures alongside additional data elements. The County Director will approve the Cal-CSA prior to submission to CDSS. Client Satisfaction Surveys (CSSs) The CSSs were developed by CDSS in conjunction with stakeholders to assist counties in gathering feedback from CalWORKs and WTW customers to identify potential areas of improvement for CalWORKs service delivery. CDSS will issue three separate surveys to evaluate customer satisfaction during their first six -months on CalWORKs aid tied to specific WTW milestones : completing WTW Orientation, sign ing the first WTW plan, and after the first Semi -Annual Report (SAR 7) . All three surveys will be issued to customers by CDSS on a recurring basis for new customers. CDSS will provide counties with individual level survey results monthly and a quarterly report containing aggregate survey responses. Analysis of CSS results must be reported by counties in their Cal-CSA and Cal-SIP. CSS Incentive Payments Customers that complete the Cal-OAR CSS may receive a CSS incentive payment. CDSS will provide counties with a monthly list of customers who will each receive a $50 CSS incentive payment. CSS incentive payments are excluded from CalWORKs income or resource considerations. Counties should issue CSS incentive payments as Ancillary supportive services payments within 30 days of receiving the CSS incentive list from CDSS. CalWORKs System Improvement Plan (Cal-SIP) The Cal-SIP is the third component of the Cal-OAR CQI process. Counties, in partnership with CDSS, will identify measure(s) for improvement from their Cal-CSA, develop strategies to improve performance for their CalWORKs program regarding selected measure(s), monitor and evaluate the impact of implemented strategies on program performance , and document these processes in a Cal - SIP Report . CDSS and a third -party partner will support counties through measure selection and implementation. Peer Review As part of Cal-SIP development, counties will participate in a peer review process focused on the county’s selected measure(s) for improvement. Through peer review counties will share promising and best practices, d evelop ideas to innovate and refine their CalWORKs programs, discuss successes and challenges, troubleshoot obstacles, and design solutions with peer counties. Counties will document their peer review experience within the Cal -SIP Report, and annual Cal-SIP Progress Reports. Required Approvals The County Director will approve the Cal-SIP prior to submission to CDSS. Once CDSS has reviewed the Cal -SIP, C ounties will have their County Board of Supervisors or chief elected official, where County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide CalWORKs Outcomes and Accountability Review (Cal-OAR) Number Page 10-170 4 of 4 applicable, approve the Cal-SIP. Once the Cal -SIP is approved by the County Board of Supervisors and CDSS, the County will implement improvement strategies. Cal-SIP Progress Report Counties will also complete an annual Cal-SIP Progress Report to track and report measure and strategy implementation progress, including an overview of findings from the peer review process, indepth information regarding county successes, barriers in reaching performance goals and any necessary adjustments to improvement strategies. The County Director is required to approve the Cal- SIP Progress Report prior to submission to CDSS. Program Impacts: CalFresh: CSS Incentive Payments are considered nonrecurring lump -sum payment s and will be excluded from consideration as income for the CalFresh Program. CSS incentive payment s will be considered a resource in the month received , unless the CalFresh household is not subject to the resource test due to being Categorically Eligible (CE) or Modified Categorically Eligible (MCE). References: WIC Section 11523 ACIN I-49-18 ACL 19-40,19-108, 20-95, 22-42, 23-25 ACIN 1-60-21 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by October 31, 2026. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: A. Refugee Employment Services
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Refugee Employment Services Number Page 10-200.A 1 of 4 Revision Date: July 1, 2026 Background: State Law requires counties to administer Refugee Supportive Services (RSS) in accordance with the County Refugee Supportive Services Plan . The Refugee Employment Services (RES) program, implemented by the County of San Diego , provides in-depth case management and supportive services to help newly arrived refugee families and longer-term refugees who have been in the county for less than five years, quickly achieve economic self-sufficiency through employment. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to update the requirements for the Family Self-Sufficiency Plan (FSSP) and provide clarification on RES eligibility factors. Policy: CalWORKs recipients who meet RES eligibility criteria will be eligible to receive services to help obtain or retain employment. Participants who are not employment -ready will receive services through the CalWORKs Employment Services (ES) program. RES Eligibility Criteria To be eligible to receive RES, a participant must be: • A qualifying non -citizen who has been granted one of the designated immigration status es specified in the following section. • Residing in the United States for 60 months or less. • Sixteen years or older and not a full-time student in elementary or secondary school. • Employed or ‘Employment ready’ and actively seeking employment. RES Immigration Status and Eligibility Timeframes Qualifying refugees can receive RES for up to 60 calendar months. The following table includes a list of RES immigration statues and how to determine the RES 60- month beginning date. Immigration Status RES 60-Month Beginning Date Refugee, Special Immigrant Visa (SIV), Amerasians from Vietnam Date of Entry (DOE) Asylee Asylum status grant date Cuban and Haitian Entrants Date parole or other status was granted Human Trafficking and Crime Victims (refer to CalWORKs Program Guide 70- 100.A) • Trafficking Crime Victims Assistance Program (TCVAP) recipients: Application date • Non-TCVAP recipients: o Date of Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) Certification Letter for victims 18 years old and older o Date of ORR Eligibility Letter for victims under 18 years old County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Refugee Employment Services Number Page 10-200.A 2 of 4 Additional immigration statuses eligible for RES: Ukrainian and Non -Ukrainian Humanitarian Parolees paroled into the U nited States (U.S) between February 24, 2022 and September 30, 2023 , are eligible until the end of their parole term. These individuals’ spouses or unmarried children under the age of 21 who are paroled into the United States after September 30, 2023 are also eligible. Afghan Humanitarian Parolees paroled into the U.S. between July 31, 2021, through September 30, 2023, are potentially eligible until March 31, 2023, or the end of their parole term, whichever is later. Spouses or children of these individuals paroled into the U.S. after September 30, 2023 are also eligible. Verification of Immigration Status Staff will verify and/or validate qualifying immigration status by viewing the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) document ation. RES participants are not required to provide their Social Security number (SSN) to receive ES through the RES program. Definition of Employment Ready A participant will be considered employment ready, if they have skills that will lead to immediate gainful employment. For example, a participant who was a nurse in their home country has the skills and experience that will lead to gainful employment within one year. Services Available through RES Participants will be offered all services available to eliminate any barriers preventing the m from gaining employment. Below are services available through RES: • Development of a FSSP that establishes job-related experience and job retention services. • Activities that provide acculturation and life skill experiences. • In-depth case management, including employability assessment and translation services. • Referrals for barrier removal services such as mental health and conflict resolution. • English language training through a variety of avenues, such as Vocational English -as-Second Language (VESL) or local vocational training programs. • On-the-job training. • Monetary supportive services (CalWORKs recipients only). FSSP All RES participants will be required to complete the FSSP, in addition to an ES plan. The FSSP will assist the participant and staff to identify the services needed to address barriers and needs of the participant, as well as to establish income and resources necessary to achieve economic self - sufficiency. The FSSP must include each member of the family, includin g children. The FSSP will set measurable short- and long-term goals, steps, and strategies to obtain and retain employment based on the needs of the whole family. The FSSP must include the following: • A comprehensive assessment for each family member, including children. • Strengths and assets. • Stressors and barriers. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Refugee Employment Services Number Page 10-200.A 3 of 4 • A family budget, including itemized expenses and sources of income. • An Individual Employability Plan (IEP). • Short-term and long-term goals. • Referrals to services. A follow-up assessment must be completed at 6 and 12 months, which includes: • An assessment of progress and outcomes. • Documentation if the initial primary goal was met or not met. • Identification of any new barriers. • Offer of new referrals for resources. • Employment status, if employed, the number of months employed part -time or full-time, as well as the hourly wage. • A revised family budget. • A revised IEP. FSSP Exceptions A FSSP is not required for participants enrolled only in English as a Second Language (ESL) classes for purposes other than obtaining or retaining employment. For example, participants who are already employed and enroll in ESL to improve their English. Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) and TCVAP Recipients RCA and TCVAP recipients must participate in work -related activities unless exempt. Some TCVAP recipients may not possess a SSN or work authorization. As an alternative, job readiness, life skills, acculturation, and ESL activities may be assigned in preparation for future employment. 90-Day Retention The 90-day retention period begins with the start date of the RES participant’s first job. Follow-up is required to verify retention with RES participants 90 days from the start date of employment. Procedure: CalWORKs Processing Guide 10-200.A1 References: • County Refugee Program Guidelines https://www.cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/refugees/guidance/state-and-fed-regs • United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) Class of Admission Codes: https://sdcountycagov.sharepoint.com/sites/Eligibility/cfip/Desk_Aid_USCIS_Class_of_Admission_ Codes_Table_(03-11).docx • All County Letter (ACL) 22-102 • Policy Letter 21-06 • County Refugee Program Guideline CDSS County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Refugee Employment Services Number Page 10-200.A 4 of 4 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by July 31, 2029 Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services
