title: A. Restoration of Aid
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Restoration of Aid Number Page 40-125.A 1 of 5 Revision Date: June 1, 2024 Background: Assembly Bill (AB) 959 requires CalWORKs benefits to be restored when a complete Semi -Annual Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7) is provided in the month after a SAR 7 related discontinuance. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide guidance to staff when completing a restoration, when a case has discontinued. This section is being revised for Sunset Review. There is no policy change. Policy: CalWORKs benefits may be restored on a prorated basis, when a complete SAR 7 is received after the extended filing date and good cause does not exist. Restoration may also be considered when a case is set to discontinue for excess property or excess income. Once a case has discontinued, applicant rules are used to reestablish CalWORKs eligibility. The definition of restoration for the CalWORKs program refers to when an individual reapplies for aid in the same county within 12 months following a CalWORKs discontinuance. Completion of a new application and Statement of Facts are usually required. Requests for Restoration of Aid A restoration of aid may refer to a request for reevaluation of continuing CalWORKs eligibility when the Assistance Unit (AU) has received notification of an upcoming discontinuance or after the case has discontinued. Restoration of aid may also refer to the reevaluation of CalWORKs eligibility when a penalty or sanction has been imposed and the AU later complies with CalWORKs program or Employment Services participation requirements. Discontinuances of excess property or excess income may require an evaluation for restoration of aid: • If the AU provides verification and is within the resource and income limits prior to the discontinuance date, the discontinuance will be rescinded, and CalWORKs reinstated without a break in aid. • If the AU provides verification and is within the resource and income limits after CalWORKs has discontinued, the AU is required to reapply for benefits. Restoration after a SAR 7 Discontinuance When benefits have discontinued for failure to submit a complete SAR 7, aid may be restored if a complete SAR 7 is received during the month following the discontinuance and good cause does not exist. The restored benefits will be prorated based on the date the complete SAR 7 was received without requiring a new application or interview. The Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) Cycle and redetermination date will remain unchanged and recipient budgeting rules will apply. CalWORKs recipient rules will be used for restoration of aid following a discontinuance for failure to provide a complete SAR 7 . Continuing eligibility will first be established before benefits are restored. Restoration of aid will not be processed if information provided on the complete SAR 7 results in County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Restoration of Aid Number Page 40-125.A 2 of 5 ineligibility to CalWORKs. The AU may submit a new application, instead of a complete SAR 7. Good cause and restoration of aid will not be evaluated when the AU chooses to reapply for CalWORKs. Restored Benefits Scenario An AU is assigned to Cycle 1 and provides an incomplete May SAR 7 on June 6th. No income verification is provided and an adequate Y-NOA is issued timely. CalWORKs discontinues timely effective July 1st. Partial verification is provided on the extended filing date, July 2 nd. The remaining pending verification is provided on July 20th. The worker determines good cause does not exist. Outcome The May SAR 7 is considered complete as of July 20 th. CalWORKs eligibility will be restored, and benefits prorated as of July 20th. Good Cause When a complete SAR 7 is received in the month after a SAR 7-related discontinuance, the worker is required to first determine if good cause exists. Recipient budgeting rules and information provided in the complete SAR 7 will be used to determine ongoing CalWORKs eligibility. If Good Cause is established and a SAR 7 discontinuance is rescinded, benefits will be reinstated at the previous level without a break in aid, even if the new information provided on the complete SAR 7 results in a decrease in benefits. Timely notice is required before benefits can be decreased. Customers have the option to waive the 10-day notice requirement to avoid a CalWORKs overpayment. A signed waiver form is required before benefits can be decreased or discontinued without timely notice. If Good Cause then the CalWORKs discontinuance… exists, will be rescinded and benefits restored back to the first of the following month. does not exist, is valid and remains in place. Benefits will be restored and prorated based on the date the complete SAR 7 is received. Untimely Processing of SAR 7 Scenario An AU is assigned to Cycle 4 and submits an August SAR 7 timely on September 11th. The SAR 7 is processed as incomplete on September 28th and CalWORKs benefits are discontinued effective November 1st to allow for timely notice. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Restoration of Aid Number Page 40-125.A 3 of 5 A complete August SAR 7 is received on October 10 th. New income is reported, and it is determined that benefits for the new payment period will be a lower amount than what was previously issued. Outcome The worker determines good cause exists because a timely Y-NOA was not issued to discontinue CalWORKs at the end of the Submit Month. The November 1st discontinuance will be rescinded and benefits for the new payment period will be recalculated using the August SAR 7 information. An overpayment for October due to Administrative Error will be established for any overpaid benefits. Decreased Benefits at Restoration If information provided on the complete SAR 7 results in a decrease in benefits from the amount previously issued, timely notice is not required to restore aid at a lower amount. This is not considered a mid-period decrease in benefits as the payment period was disrupted when CalWORKs discontinued. Decrease Benefit at Restoration Scenario An AU of 3, Mom and her two children, has no income. The AU is assigned to Cycle 5 and fails to submit a September SAR 7. An X-NOA is issued timely, and CalWORKs discontinues on November 1st. On November 15 th, the AU submits a complete September SAR 7 with new income. Mom started a new job and now earns $1,000/month. The worker determines good cause does not exist. Outcome The September SAR 7 is considered complete as of November 15th. Benefits will be prorated effective November 15 th using Mom’s new earnings to calculate benefits for the new payment period, November - April. 10-day notice is not needed to restore benefits for November at a decreased amount. Late Receipt of SAR 7 Scenario An AU is assigned to Cycle 5 and fails to provide a September SAR 7. An X-NOA is issued timely and CalWORKs discontinues November 1st. The AU provides a complete September SAR 7 on the extended filing date, November 1st. An increase in income is reported and it is determined that benefits will decrease for the new payment period. Outcome The November 1 st discontinuance will be rescinded and benefits for November reinstated without a break in aid. Since timely notice to decrease benefits for November cannot be provided, benefits will be issued at the previous level. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Restoration of Aid Number Page 40-125.A 4 of 5 An overpayment for November due to Client Error will be established for any overpaid benefits. Denying Restoration of Aid If information on the complete SAR 7 results in ineligibility to aid, CalWORKs benefits cannot be restored, and the AU will be required to reapply for aid. Denying Restoration Scenario An AU of 2, Dad and one child, has no income. The AU is assigned to Cycle 6 and fails to submit an October SAR 7. An X -NOA is issued timely and CalWORKs discontinues on December 1st. On December 11th, the AU submits a complete October SAR 7 with new income. Dad started a new job and earns $3,500/month. The worker determines Good Cause does not exist. Outcome Although the AU provided a complete SAR 7 in the month following the SAR 7 discontinuance, aid cannot be restored because the AU has excess income and is no longer eligible to CalWORKs. Restoration of aid will be denied and a restoration denial NOA will be issued. Impacts to CalFresh If a complete CalWORKs SAR 7 is received in the month after the SAR 7 discontinuance and CalWORKs benefits are restored, Non-Assistance CalFresh (NACF) benefits will be converted to Public Assistance CalFresh (PACF) with timely notice. NACF after a CalWORKs/PACF Discontinuance Scenario A CalWORKs/PACF two -parent household is assigned to Cycle 4. A February SAR 7 is received in the Submit Month that is only signed by one parent. The AU later submits a February SAR 7 that is signed by the other parent on April 23rd and the February SAR 7 is now complete for CalWORKs. The worker determines Good Cause does not exist. Outcome The SAR 7 provided in the Submit Month is considered complete for CalFresh, but not for CalWORKs. CalWORKs and PACF discontinue at the beginning of the following Month (April1st) and PACF is converted to NACF April 1st. CalWORKs benefits will be restored effective April 23 rd and PACF benefits reinstated effective June 1st with timely notice. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Restoration of Aid Number Page 40-125.A 5 of 5 Procedure: CalWORKs Processing Guide 44-270.A1 References: • EAS 40-125.9, 40-171.21, 40-171.22 • ACL No. 12-25, 12-35, 12-49, 12-59, 13-17, 13-26, 13-28, 13-80, Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by June 30, 2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

Restoration after a SAR 7 Discontinuance When benefits have discontinued for failure to submit a complete SAR 7, aid may be restored if a complete SAR 7 is received during the month following the discontinuance and good cause does not exist. The restored benefits will be prorated based on the date the complete SAR 7 was received without requiring a new application or interview. The Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) Cycle and redetermination date will remain unchanged and recipient budgeting rules will apply. CalWORKs recipient rules will be used for restoration of aid following a discontinuance for failure to provide a complete SAR 7 . Continuing eligibility will first be established before benefits are restored. Restoration of aid will not be processed if information provided on the complete SAR 7 results in County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Restoration of Aid Number Page 40-125.A 2 of 5 ineligibility to CalWORKs. The AU may submit a new application, instead of a complete SAR 7. Good cause and restoration of aid will not be evaluated when the AU chooses to reapply for CalWORKs. Restored Benefits Scenario An AU is assigned to Cycle 1 and provides an incomplete May SAR 7 on June 6th. No income verification is provided and an adequate Y-NOA is issued timely. CalWORKs discontinues timely effective July 1st. Partial verification is provided on the extended filing date, July 2 nd. The remaining pending verification is provided on July 20th. The worker determines good cause does not exist. Outcome The May SAR 7 is considered complete as of July 20 th. CalWORKs eligibility will be restored, and benefits prorated as of July 20th. Good Cause When a complete SAR 7 is received in the month after a SAR 7-related discontinuance, the worker is required to first determine if good cause exists. title: A. Intra-Program Transfer (IPT)
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageIntra-Program Transfer (IPT) 40-183.A 1 of 1 Revision Date: November 29, 2016 Background: Foster care (FC) dependent children who are placed with relatives whom are not eligible to receive federal or state foster care payments may qualify for other cash benefits until age 18 or 21 as a non-minor dependent (NMD) under the state-funded Extended Foster Care (EFC) Program. Caretaker relatives of foster care children may also choose to receive CalWORKs assistance rather than Foster Care (AFDC-FC) payments. Their decision is documented by the Foster Care HSS. Policy: 40-183.A.1 Referral from Foster Care An Intra-Program Transfer (IPT) referral will be forwarded to the Family Resource Center (FRC) based on the caretaker relative’s zip code. Residency for the child is established by the court of jurisdiction. All IPT Referrals for children placed with relatives residing outside of San Diego County, including children placed with relatives outside of the state of California, shall be forwarded to the North Central FRC for processing. 40-183.A.2 Fraud Referrals CalWORKs staff shall exempt needy and non-needy caretaker relatives from a fraud referral when Child Welfare Services (CWS) has placed the child with the relative. Caretaker relatives shall not be subject to an investigation unless there is an actual basis on which to suspect fraud. Procedure: CPG Processing Guide 40-183.A.1 Program Impact/s: Other Programs Affected CalFresh: 63-223.3 and 63-243.2 Medi-Cal: Letter 810 and MPG 05.15.05 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by November 30, 2019. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations

title: B. Extended CalWORKs for Non-Minor Dependents (NMD)
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageExtended CalWORKs for Non-Minor Dependents 40-183.B 1 of 3 Revision Date: November 29, 2016 Background: Assembly Bill 12 requires that children who are under the responsibility of the County Child Welfare Services (CWS) or Probation Department at age 18 may remain in foster care as non-minor dependents (NMDs) until age 21 under the state-funded Extended Foster Care (EFC) Program. ACL 11-61 Policy: 40-183.B.1 CalWORKs Eligibility Criteria CalWORKs NMDs must: 1. Live with an approved relative caregiver who is not eligible for federal or state foster care payments 2. Meet EFC program requirements as determined by their CWS Social Worker. A NMD must: A. Meet at least one of the following eligibility conditions: 1. Be enrolled in, and working towards, completing high school or an equivalent program 2. Be enrolled in a post-secondary or vocational school at least half-time, or be enrolled for the next available term 3. Be participating in a program or activity that promotes employment or removes barriers to employment 4. Be employed at least 80 hours per month 5. Be incapable of participating in school or employment due to a documented physical, mental, or emotional condition B. Agree and adhere to the Mutual Agreement for EFC. If the NMDs voluntarily exit and later re-enter foster care, the NMD must adhere to a Voluntary Re-Entry Agreement for EFC rather than a Mutual Agreement. ACL 12-12 C. Cooperate with review hearings and complete the Six-Month Certification of EFC with their CWS Social Worker. The CWS Social Worker will provide a new Six-Month Certification of EFC every six months to document the NMD’s continuing eligibility. This documentation must be received in the first month of the new certification period to prevent CalWORKs discontinuance. ACL 11-78 Other household members, such as the relative caregiver or the NMD’s minor child(ren), are not eligible to extended CalWORKs. ACL 11-78 and 13-82E 40-183.B.2 CalWORKs Program Requirements NMDs must adhere to EFC Program requirements and are not subject to CalWORKs program requirements, such as: •Application, redetermination, or Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) •Face-to-face interview •Statewide Fingerprint Imaging System (SFIS) •CalWORKs income and property limits •California residence •Child Support enforcement •Maximum Family Grant (MFG) rule •Time on Aid (TOA) limits •Participation in Welfare-to-Work (WTW) or Cal-Learn programs ACL 11-78, 12-27, and 13-10 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageExtended CalWORKs for Non-Minor Dependents 40-183.B 2 of 3 NMDs may receive recurring special needs or Pregnancy Special Need (PSN) payments with verification. NMDs are not eligible to homeless assistance. ACL 13-82 40-183.B.3 County Payment Responsibility The county of jurisdiction retains CalWORKs payment responsibility for the NMD regardless of the county or state where the NMD lives. A NMD may receive CalWORKs while residing outside of California for the following reasons: •The NMD is placed with an approved relative who lives in another county or state; or •The approved relative with whom the NMD is currently placed moves to another county or state. ACL 11-78, 12-27, 13-10 and 14-33 40-183.B.4 Beginning Date of Aid (BDA) The BDA is the first day of the following month in which the Six-Month Certification of EFC is signed, and timely and adequate notice can be given to discontinue the NMD from the relative caregiver’s CalWORKs case. ACL 11-78 and 12-27 The BDA for NMDs who re-enter EFC is the date of placement with the approved relative caregiver; provided the Voluntary Re-Entry Agreement for EFC is signed by the CWS Social Worker and all eligibility criteria are met. ACL 12-27 40-183.B.5 Payment and Issuance Method The extended CalWORKs payment amount is equal to the Maximum Aid Payment (MAP) for a non-exempt Assistance Unit (AU) of one. The payment may be issued to the NMD via direct deposit or Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT). ACL 11-78 and 12-27 40-183.B.6 Overpayments Collection for extended CalWORKs overpayment claims may only occur via grant reduction while the NMD is actively receiving extended CalWORKs or if the NMD later receives CalWORKs for his/her own minor child(ren) due to the Hartley v. Lightbourne settlement. ACL 12-66 and 13-82 40-183.B.7 Inter-County Transfer The eligibility worker must initiate an inter-county transfer (ICT) to transfer CalWORKs payment responsibility after court jurisdiction is transferred to another county. ACL 12-27 and 13-10 40-183.B.8 Out-of-State Placement The eligibility worker will follow existing procedures under CPG 80-300.A for Interstate Compact on the Placement of Children (ICPC) cases. ACL 14-33 Procedure: CPG Processing Guide 40-183.B.1 Program Impacts: Automation How To #261 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageExtended CalWORKs for Non-Minor Dependents 40-183.B 3 of 3 Forms and Document Capture All manual forms and notices must be imaged in to CERMS References: AB 12 (http://www.leginfo.ca.gov/pub/09-10/bill/asm/ab_0001-0050/ab_12_bill_20100930_chaptered.pdf) AB 1712 (http://www.leginfo.ca.gov/pub/11-12/bill/asm/ab_1701-1750/ab_1712_bill_20120930_chaptered.pdf) AB 212 (http://www.leginfo.ca.gov/pub/11-12/bill/asm/ab_0201-0250/ab_212_bill_20111004_chaptered.pdf) ACIN I-37-14 (http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/lettersnotices/EntRes/getinfo/acin/2014/I-37-_14.pdf) ACL 11-61 (http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/lettersnotices/entres/getinfo/acl/2011/11-61.pdf) ACL 11-78 (http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/lettersnotices/entres/getinfo/acl/2011/11-78.pdf) ACL 12-12 (http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/lettersnotices/entres/getinfo/acl/2012/12-12.pdf) ACL 12-27 (http://www.cdss.ca.gov/lettersnotices/entres/getinfo/acl/2012/12-27.pdf) ACL 12-66 (http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/lettersnotices/entres/getinfo/acl/2012/12-66.pdf) ACL 13-10 (http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/lettersnotices/entres/getinfo/acl/2013/13-10.pdf) ACL 13-82 (http://www.cdss.ca.gov/lettersnotices/entres/getinfo/acl/2013/13-82.pdf) ACL 13-82E (http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/lettersnotices/entres/getinfo/acl/2013/13-82E.pdf) ACL 14-33 (http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/lettersnotices/entres/getinfo/acl/2014/14-33.pdf) EAS 40-181.C (http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/ord/entres/getinfo/pdf/3EAS.pdf) EAS 40-190.15 (http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/ord/entres/getinfo/pdf/3EAS.pdf) EAS 42-101.3 (http://www.dss.cahwnet.gov/ord/entres/getinfo/pdf/4EAS.pdf) Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by November 30, 2019. title: C. Approved Relative Caregiver (ARC) Program
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Approved Relative Caregiver (ARC) Program Number Page 40-183.C 1 of 6 Revision Date: February 1, 2022 Background: Per state regulations, the Approved Relative Caretaker (ARC) Program was developed by the State of California to make payments equal to the basic Foster Care (FC)/Home-Based Family Care (HBFC) rate for approved relative caregivers with whom a non-federally eligible foster child is placed. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to update references to the Maximum Aid Payment (MAP) and child support disregard amounts , due to increases in these amounts . The change to the child support disregard amounts is effective January 1, 2022. Policy: Eligibility for CalWORKs is not a requirement for receipt of the ARC payment . However, each ARC- eligible child must be assessed for CalWORKs eligibility in order to determine if CalWORKs funds will be used in the ARC payment. Additionally, participation in the ARC Program is not mandatory and families may choose to receive CalWORKs benefits only. FC Human Services Specialist (HSS) will determine eligibility to CalWORKs benefits and issue monthly ARC payments to ARC eligible children receiving CalWORKs. The ARC Program payment issued by FC will consist of CalWORKs and ARC funding. FC HSSs will also issue ARC payments to ARC eligible children not eligible to receive CalWORKs and the payment will consist of ARC funding only. ARC Program Eligibility Criteria To be eligible for the ARC Program, a child or Non -Minor Dependent (NMD) receiving ext ended CalWORKs benefits, must meet all of the following criteria: • Be placed with an approved relative whose home is approved or has a Resource Family Approval (RFA). o If there is a change in the caregiver’s address, a new home approval or RFA certificate must be on file for the new address o The caregiver’s home must be renewed within one calendar year to the end of the month the assessment was approved. For example, the caregiver was RFA certified on February 1, 2017, the RFA renewal must be completed by March 3, 2018 • Reside in California (Children in out of state placements are not eligible) • Be a dependent or ward of the California juvenile court. Children under a voluntary placement agreement may participate in the ARC Program for up to six months • Not be federally eligible under Title IV -E of the Social Security Act while placed with an approved relative caregiver • Be denied or discontinued from the FC Program • Have completed an ARC Program application (ARC 1) Application Requirements The ARC application is a “right to apply” application. The caregiver may submit this application at any FRC. The ARC Caregiver Rights and Responsibilities notice must be given to all ARC applicants along County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Approved Relative Caregiver (ARC) Program Number Page 40-183.C 2 of 6 with the ARC application and the caregiver must acknowledge that the rights and responsibilities notice was received on the ARC application. An ARC application is required for each child when: • A new approved relative caregiver applies for the ARC Program • There is a change in the approved relative caregiver regard less of whether the change occurred within the same home • A child becomes a dependent after a voluntary placement • A NMD receiving extended CalWORKs wishes to apply for the ARC Program Assistance Unit (AU) The AU in the ARC Program will consist of the child only. If the ARC child’s household includes: • A needy caretaker o When the ARC child is the only eligible child for a needy caretaker relative, the needy caretaker relative is still potentially eligible for CalWORKs and can apply separately for themselves • The child of an ARC eligible parenting teen o If eligible, the child of an ARC eligible parenting teen may receive CalWORKs , the child would be included in the AU of the needy or non-needy caretaker relative; this does not apply to NMD’s • A pregnant or parenting teen has the option to establish their own CalWORKs case at age 18 and those who establish their own CalWORKs case will not be eligible for the ARC Program If an ARC child’s biological parent moves into the approved relative caregiver’s home, even if it is a court specified placement, the approved relative caregiv er will no longer be eligible to the ARC Program, as the biological parent must apply for aid on behalf of the child. CalWORKs Eligibility Requirements When determining eligibility for the CalWORKs portion of the ARC payment, the following CalWORKs requirements will not apply: • Face-to-face or electronic (telephonic) interview • Photo-image of the approved relative caregiver • Immunization verification • School attendance verification • Cal-Learn participation • Employment Services participation • Redeterminations (It is considered sufficient that the social worker completes monthly visits and six-month review hearings) • Reporting o CalWORKs reporting requirements will not apply as ARC children meet with their social worker on a monthly basis. The FC eligibility staff should ensure that CalWORKs eligibility staff is notified of any changes that would render the child ineligible for CalWORKs benefits, such as if the child exits care • A Bureau of Public Assistance Investigations (BPAI) fraud investigation is only made if there is an actual basis of suspected fraud Note: The caretaker relative must comply with CalWORKs Program requirements if they or other children in the home receive CalWORKs benefits and do not participate in the ARC Program. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Approved Relative Caregiver (ARC) Program Number Page 40-183.C 3 of 6 Beginning Date of Aid (BDA) For an individual ARC-eligible child, the BDA is the date that the ARC application is signed and dated by the approved relative caregiver, date received by the agency, home approval or RFA certified, or the date of the child’s placement, whichever is later. If the child is discontinued from the F C Program, the BDA for the ARC Program is the date of the FC Program discontinuance. For example, the child received FC which discontinued on February 3, 2016, the beginning date of payment is on February 3, 2016. FC does not pay the date of discontinuance. If the child is no longer eligible to the ARC Program, the relative caregiver can submit a CW 8A form to add the child to an active CalWORKs case or a new CalWORKs application to request CalWORKs. Income and Resources Eligibility for the CalWORKs portion of the ARC payment is based on the child’s income and resources. Income eligibility is determined by applying the HBFC income requirements. If a child is determined eligible for CalWORKs, the CalWORKs portion of the ARC payment will be based on the regional county of jurisdiction. The CalWORKs portion of the ARC payment will be the exempt Maximum Aid Payment ( MAP) for an AU of one, do not subtract the income from the MAP or apply income disregards. The ARC payment would be offset by any social security income that an ARC child or NMD receives. An ARC child may retain up to $10,000 in income and property. Grant Calculation Payment for the ARC Program will consist of CalWORKs and ARC funding and will be prorated based on the beginning date of payment . These funding sou rces will be used to fund payments up to the amount equal to the HBFC rate. The caregiver will be paid based on the day the child is under the care of the caregiver. The county of jurisdiction will be responsible for issuing ARC payments (CalWORKs and ARC funding) even if the child is placed out of the county, as long as the child is placed in California. Starting with July 1, 2017 payment s, all ARC payments will be issued retrospectively instead of prospectively. For example, the July 2017 payment will be issued on June 31, 2017. The CalWORKs portion of the ARC payment will be exempt MAP for an AU of one and the ARC funding is the difference up to the HBFC rate. The income of the child will be offset against the ARC funding portion only. Any offsets, due to either income or some other factor will be applied after the prorated grant amount has been calculated. If the child is ineligible to CalWORKs funding, the ARC payment will consist of ARC funding only equal to the HBFC rate. If the child was receiving CalWORKs in another case prior to transitioning to the ARC Program, the CalWORKs income will be exempt from the ARC budget. For example, a CalWORKs payment in March 2022 for an eligible six-year-old child is the Exempt MAP of $638, plus ARC funds of $ 399, to bring the child’s total ARC payment up to the basic FC rate of $1,037 for the child’s age group. For CalWORKs funding the child must: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Approved Relative Caregiver (ARC) Program Number Page 40-183.C 4 of 6 • Be a U nited States citizen or eligible noncitizen. If the child is a noncitizen, they must m eet citizenship requirements defined under CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 42-400.D Eligible Non- Citizen Status, CPG 42 -400.E Battered Non-Citizens and CPG 70-100.A Human Trafficking and Victims of Serious Crimes/Child Citizenship Act • Not be a recipient of Supplemental Security Income/State Supplemental Payment (SSI/SSP) • Not have combined income and resources exceeding $10,000 in any given month Combined income and resources over $10,000 do not make the child ineligible to the ARC Program . However, the ARC payment will consist of ARC funding only equal to the HBFC rate. Retroactive Payments Children not already receiving CalWORKs, who complete an ARC application when the HSS has made a CalWORKs determination, will receive the ARC payment retroactive to the date of the ARC application. ARC Aid Codes • 2S – ARC Funding Option + federal CalWORKs • 2T – ARC Funding Option + state CalWORKs • 2U – ARC Funding Option + state CalWORKs (for NMDs) • 2P – ARC only • 2R – ARC only (for NMDs) Child Support Requirements Cooperating with child support is required unless there is good cause. If the child support packet is not returned, the ARC child remains eligible to full ARC payments. Child support cooperation requirements can be exempt when it has been determined that a referral to the Local Child Support Agency (LCSA) is not in the best interest of the child , including an increased risk of harm to the child or when cooperation would pose a barrier to family reunification efforts. Child support will be recoupable for the entire ARC payment with the exception of NMDs. For ARC cases that are referred to child support, the ARC caregiver will recei ve the appropriate child support disregard amount as discussed in CPG 43-200.D Child Support Payments. Special Payments An approved relative caregiver receiving ARC payments on behalf of an eligible child is not eligible to receive additional CalWORKs payments on behalf of the same child. These additional CalWORKs payments include payments for special needs, emergencies, ho meless assistance and pregnancy special needs. Overpayments Overpayments are established in the ARC Program when a caregiver receives payment for an amount or a time period in which the caregiver is ineligible to benefits. HSSs must establish an overpayment under the following situation: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Approved Relative Caregiver (ARC) Program Number Page 40-183.C 5 of 6 • The child begins to receive SSI/SSP, Social Security Agency (SSA) income or other income (earned or unearned) • The child’s combined monthly income and resources/property total more than $10,000 and the caregiver does not report it • The child has been absent from the caregiver’s home for more than 15 cumulative days in any given month (the period of absence includes the first day of the month) and the caregiver does not report it. An exception to this rule is if the child is hospitalized for any length of time Collection is prohibited under the following conditions: • The cost of collection exceeds the amount of the overpayment that is likely to be recovered by the county • The child was temporarily removed from the home or was a runaway and returned and payment was owed to the relative to maintain the child’s placement or to meet the child’s needs • The overpayment was exclusively the result of a county administrative error or both the county and the relative were unaware of the information which caused the overpayment • The relative did not have knowledge of, and did not contribute to, the cause of the overpayment • The caregiver timely reported information that reduced the ARC payment, but the county did not have sufficient time to adjust the amount before the payment was issued An overpayment established due to any income or benefit received by the child may only reduce the non-CalWORKs portion of the ARC payment. Non-income related overpayments, such as those established by an absence from the placement, should offset all portions of the ARC payment in equal proportion. Appeals Process An approved relative caregiver cannot appeal any reduction in their ARC payment that occurs as a result of a county opting-out of the ARC Program. This includes any reduction in payments following the presumed opt-out of counties in the event of a state-budget reduction. However, if there is a reduction in payments to an approved relative caregiver , as a result of some other determination unrelated to a county opting-out of the ARC Program, the caregiver retains existing appeal rights. Inter-County Transfers (ICT) The county of court jurisdiction will be the county with payment responsibility for the ARC Program. The county of court jurisdiction will make the ARC payment even if the child is placed out of county, as long as the child is placed in California. It does not matter if the county in which the child is placed is an ARC opt-in county or not. The regional MAP amount attributable to the CalWORKs portion of the ARC payment is based on the county of jurisdiction. As a result, an ICT may be necessary to transfer the child’s ARC/CalWORKs case from the county of residence to the county of court jurisdiction. Case transfer is initiated by using the CW 215 form or via electronic data transfer. Existing CalWORKs ICT procedures apply to the CalWORKs portion of the ARC payment. For new cases, residence is established by the county of jurisdiction, but CalWORKs cases for needy or non-needy caretaker relatives who receive CalWORKs for themselves and/or a child(ren) who is/are County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Approved Relative Caregiver (ARC) Program Number Page 40-183.C 6 of 6 not participating in the ARC Program would be established by the county of residence. Issuance ARC payments are not to be issued on the Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) Card. ARC payments are to be issued via warrant or direct deposit. ARC Payment in CalFresh Budget An ARC child may be eligible for CalFresh benefits. For CalFresh budgeting purposes, ARC payments shall be treated in the same manner as FC payments made to CalFresh households per CalFresh Program Guide (CFPG) 63-101.7 and 63-224.14. Continued Medi-Cal Eligibility If the ARC child is discontinued from the ARC Program, the child will receive continued Medi -Cal benefits under aid code 7J (under age 18) or 4M (age 18 and over until the age of 26). Procedure: N/A Impacts: CalFresh: 63-101.7 and 63-224.14 Medi-Cal: 05.15.05 Information from CalWORKs Program Memo No. 17-18, which states that FRC staff no longer process ARC cases has been incorporated into this material . As a result, CalWORKs Processing Guide 40 - 183.C.1 and Memo 17-18 are now obsolete. sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Approved Relative Caregiver (ARC) Program Number Page 40-183.C 1 of 6 Revision Date: February 1, 2022 Background: Per state regulations, the Approved Relative Caretaker (ARC) Program was developed by the State of California to make payments equal to the basic Foster Care (FC)/Home-Based Family Care (HBFC) rate for approved relative caregivers with whom a non-federally eligible foster child is placed. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to update references to the Maximum Aid Payment (MAP) and child support disregard amounts , due to increases in these amounts . The change to the child support disregard amounts is effective January 1, 2022. Policy: Eligibility for CalWORKs is not a requirement for receipt of the ARC payment . However, each ARC- eligible child must be assessed for CalWORKs eligibility in order to determine if CalWORKs funds will be used in the ARC payment. Additionally, participation in the ARC Program is not mandatory and families may choose to receive CalWORKs benefits only. FC Human Services Specialist (HSS) will determine eligibility to CalWORKs benefits and issue monthly ARC payments to ARC eligible children receiving CalWORKs. The ARC Program payment issued by FC will consist of CalWORKs and ARC funding. FC HSSs will also issue ARC payments to ARC eligible children not eligible to receive CalWORKs and the payment will consist of ARC funding only. ARC Program Eligibility Criteria To be eligible for the ARC Program, a child or Non -Minor Dependent (NMD) receiving ext ended CalWORKs benefits, must meet all of the following criteria: • Be placed with an approved relative whose home is approved or has a Resource Family Approval (RFA). o If there is a change in the caregiver’s address, a new home approval or RFA certificate must be on file for the new address o The caregiver’s home must be renewed within one calendar year to the end of the month the assessment was approved. For example, the caregiver was RFA certified on February 1, 2017, the RFA renewal must be completed by March 3, 2018 • Reside in California (Children in out of state placements are not eligible) • Be a dependent or ward of the California juvenile court. Children under a voluntary placement agreement may participate in the ARC Program for up to six months • Not be federally eligible under Title IV -E of the Social Security Act while placed with an approved relative caregiver • Be denied or discontinued from the FC Program • Have completed an ARC Program application (ARC 1) Application Requirements The ARC application is a “right to apply” application. The caregiver may submit this application at any FRC. The ARC Caregiver Rights and Responsibilities notice must be given to all ARC applicants along County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Approved Relative Caregiver (ARC) Program Number Page 40-183.C 2 of 6 with the ARC application and the caregiver must acknowledge that the rights and responsibilities notice was received on the ARC application. An ARC application is required for each child when: • A new approved relative caregiver applies for the ARC Program • There is a change in the approved relative caregiver regard less of whether the change occurred within the same home • A child becomes a dependent after a voluntary placement • A NMD receiving extended CalWORKs wishes to apply for the ARC Program Assistance Unit (AU) The AU in the ARC Program will consist of the child only. If the ARC child’s household includes: • A needy caretaker o When the ARC child is the only eligible child for a needy caretaker relative, the needy caretaker relative is still potentially eligible for CalWORKs and can apply separately for themselves • The child of an ARC eligible parenting teen o If eligible, the child of an ARC eligible parenting teen may receive CalWORKs , the child would be included in the AU of the needy or non-needy

title: D. CalWORKs Reunification Families
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageCalWORKs Family Reunification Program 40-183.D 1 of 2 Revision Date: August 1, 2018 Background: CalWORKs recipients, whose eligibility ends because their children were removed from the home by Child Welfare Services (CWS), may continue to participate in Welfare-to-Work (WTW) activities, and receive supportive services, if the CWS Social Worker or Juvenile Court deem services necessary to reunify the family. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to notify staff that Family Reunification (FR) families may receive Temporary Homeless Assistance (THA) benefits, if otherwise eligible, if the county determines that THA is necessary for reunification to occur. Policy: The CWS Social Worker, or the court, may authorize FR services for up to 180 days from the date the children are removed from the assistance unit (AU). The court may also grant the parent a good cause extension to the 180-day period. Eligibility to FR Services To receive FR services, all of the following conditions must be met: •A CWS Social Worker, or the court, have determined that the provision of FR services is necessary for family reunification •The child(ren) have been removed from the home and placed in out-of-home care •The AU had been receiving CalWORKs when the child(ren) was/were removed Note: SSI recipients, undocumented noncitizens, or timed-out parents are ineligible to FR services because they were not eligible to receive CalWORKs benefits When there are multiple children in the AU, but not all the children are removed, and the AU becomes ineligible to CalWORKs due to income, the parent(s) may be eligible to FR services if there is a court-ordered reunification plan for the child(ren) who were removed. THA Effective January 1, 2018, FR cases that are experiencing homelessness may be eligible for THA benefits, if the county determines these benefits are necessary for reunification and the family is otherwise eligible. Since THA only covers 16 days of temporary shelter assistance, staff should connect families to any additional housing interventions available including, but not limited to, Family Stabilization (FS) and the Housing Support Program (HSP) for further assistance. Additionally, once the children are returned to the home and are added back into the AU, the family may be eligible for Permanent HA, if otherwise eligible. WTW The court ordered reunification plan will be used to develop the WTW plan. Individuals who fail to participate in WTW activities or any other activities required under the FR plan are not subject to the WTW noncompliance or sanctioning process. WTW services will continue to be provided until the FR plan is terminated by the CWS Social Worker. Aid Codes Family Reunification cases will be identified under aid codes 4P or 4R. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageCalWORKs Family Reunification Program 40-183.D 2 of 2 •4P aid code (All Families): Provides for continuance of FR services (no cash aid) to all families except twoparent families. •4R aid code (Two Parent Households): Provides for continuance of FR services (no cash aid) to two-parent families. Eligibility for Medi-Cal FR parents are ineligible to cash-linked Medi-Cal through CalWORKs; therefore, an evaluation for Medi-Cal must be completed. Eligibility for CalFresh FR households do not receive a cash grant therefore FR families are eligible for Transitional CalFresh benefits (TCF) in the month in which CalWORKs benefits are reduced to zero when FR services begin. Periodic Report Reunification families are not required to submit a periodic report for CalWORKs. Redetermination Redetermination of eligibility will be made at six-month intervals in coordination with the Juvenile Court’s review of the family reunification plan. If they are determined eligible, the existing certification period will be changed to align with the reunification plan. When a family is reunified, a CalWORKs redetermination must be completed to reopen the CalWORKs case. Once a redetermination is completed, if they are eligible, CalWORKs benefits will be issued effective the first of the following month after the family is reunified. Procedure: CPG Processing Guide 40-183.D.1 Program Impacts: Automation BEnDS 1443 Forms and Document Capture All manual forms and notices must be imaged in to CERMS. References: Assembly Bill (AB) Nos. 429 and 236 EAS 42-7111.512, 80-301.3, 82-812.678; ACIN No. I-49-04; ACL Nos. 02-36, 03-52, 11-04, 16-98, and18-71 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by August 31, 2021. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations

title: E. Community Prisoner Adult Program
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Community Prisoner Adult Program Number Page 40-183.E 1 of 1 Revision Date: June 1, 2024 Background: The California Department of Corrections (CDC) operates the Community Prisoner Adult Program for low-risk adult inmates placed in community residential facilities where they are allowed to live with their pre-school age children. State regulations consider children residing with prisoner parents to be potentially eligible to CalWORKs, Medi-Cal, and CalFresh. Purpose: The section explains the policy for customers placed in community residential facilities. The purpose of this revision is to reformat the section to current standards and move the section from CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) section 40-100.Q to CPG 40-183.E. With this revision, 40-100.Q is obsolete. P olicy: Eligibility Incarcerated individuals are not entitled to CalWORKs benefits because the CDC provides for all of their basic needs. Children residing with prisoner adults are potentially eligible for CalWORKs and Medi-Cal benefits as the CDC does not provide for the children’s needs. These children may also be eligible to CalFresh benefits as a separate household. Normal eligibility determinations would need to be done for the children. Treatment of Income/Resources Incarcerated individuals are treated as excluded household members and are not entitled to CalWORKs benefits and are not included in the CW Assistance Unit (AU). Income and/or resources are excluded when determining CalWORKs eligibility or grant amount. Since prisoner adults must pay the facility for each child’s living expenses, there is no in-kind income attributed to the child’s AU. Case Payee Payments Prisoner adults are the case payee on the case. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by June 30, 2027. Approval for Release: R ick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: A. Deprivation
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Deprivation Number Page 41-400.A 1 of 2 Revision Date: August 1, 2024 Background: Deprivation of parental support or care is a separate and specific eligibility factor for CalWORKs. A child’s deprivation is based on the status of their natural or adoptive parent(s). There is no CalWORKs eligibility unless deprivation requirements are met. Purpose: This section outlines the CalWORKs policies on deprivation requirements. The purpose of this revision is for sunset review and reformatting to current standards. There is no policy change. Policy: Definition of a Parent A parent is defined as the natural or adoptive, married or unmarried, father or mother of a child. Deprivation for an adopted child is based on the status of the adoptive parent and not of the natural parents. In a one-parent adoption, deprivation is based on the absence of the second adopted parent. In cases where there is a question as to parentage concerning either parent, the matter will be referred to the Local Child Support Agency (LCSA) for resolution. Basis of Deprivation A child is considered deprived of parental support and care if: • Either parent is deceased. • Either parent is physically or mentally incapacitated. • The principal earner is unemployed. • Either parent is continually absent from the home in which the child is living. When the child is deprived of parental support or care for more than one reason, eligibility will be established on any basis of deprivation. However, the basis of deprivation due to unemployment should be used whenever possible because this permits federal participation. The basis for deprivation is to be determined: • At the time of application. • When processing Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) or once per payment period. Verification of Deprivation CalWORKs is not to be authorized until the requirements which establish deprivation are met and verified. Verification of deprivation is not required to approve an Immediate Need request. Termination of Deprivation When a basis for deprivation ends, and the family remains in need, determine if any other basis for deprivation exists. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Deprivation Number Page 41-400.A 2 of 2 For households with SAR reporting responsibilities: • Do not to take negative action based on changes in deprivation when a basis for deprivation ends mid-period. • Any change in deprivation is to be reported on form SAR 7 – Eligibility Status Report. • Changes in eligibility that result from the change in deprivation will be effective the first day of the next SAR payment period. If a SAR household reports a change mid-period and staff determined that the change reported qualifies the Assistance Unit (AU) for an exempt Maximum Aid Payment (MAP ), the change from non -exempt to exempt MAP is to occur the month following the report. For example, an AU of two consisting of a timed-out parent and two children. The AU is aided based on absent parent deprivation. The parent makes a voluntary mid -period report in October that they have been approved for Supplemental Security Income (SSI). Staff will change the basis of deprivation for this AU to incapacitated and allow the exempt MAP amount effective November 1. For Annual Reporting/Child Only (AR/CO) households: • No action will be taken based on changes in deprivation when a basis for deprivation ends mid - period, unless the change in deprivation is due to a change in the household composition. • Any change in deprivation is to be reported on the SAWS 2 Plus. • Any change in eligibility that results from a change in deprivation, except a change in the household composition, will be effective the first day of the next AR/CO payment period. • Timely and adequate notice is required when a change in deprivation due to a change in the household composition will result in a decrease or discontinuance of CalWORKs. References: Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 41-401, 41-403, 41-405 All County Letter (ACL) 03-18, 12-25 All County Information Notices (ACIN) I-58-13 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by August 31, 2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: B. Deprivation Due to Death
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Deprivation Due to Death Number Page 41-400.B 1 of 1 Revision Date: August 1, 2024 Background: Deprivation of parental support or care is a separate and specific eligibility factor for CalWORKs. A child’s deprivation is based on the status of their natural or adoptive parent(s). There is no CalWORKs eligibility unless deprivation requirements are met. Purpose: This section outlines the CalWORKs policies on deprivation due to death. The purpose of this revision is for sunset review and reformatting to current standards. There is no policy change. Policy: Deprivation due to death exists if either parent of a child is deceased. If one or both parents are deceased, the Assistance Unit (AU) would not be subject to child support enforcement requirements. Customers have the responsibility to provide the verification to establish deprivation. The following are acceptable verifications of the death of a parent: • A copy of the death certificate. • An award letter from the Social Security Administration based on the death of the parent. • A newspaper obituary of the parent’s death. • Other reliable documentation. A s worn statement is acceptable verification when no other evidence can be obtained . Existing verification available in any case record may be used. When credible evidence to establish the death of a parent is unobtainable , staff will evaluate for deprivation based on absence and a referral to the Local Child Support Agency (LCSA) will be completed. References: Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 41-420 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by August 31, 2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: C. Deprivation Due to Incapacity
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Deprivation Due to Incapacity Number Page 41-400.C 1 of 3 Revision Date: August 1, 2024 Background: Deprivation of parental support or care is a separate and specific eligibility factor for CalWORKs. A child’s deprivation is based on the status of their natural or adoptive parent(s). There is no CalWORKs eligibility unless deprivation requirements are met. Purpose: Thise section outlines the CalWORKs policies on deprivation due to incapacity. The purpose of this revision is for sunset review and reformatting to the current standards. There is no policy change. Policy: Deprivation due to physical or mental incapacity of a parent is deemed to exist when the parent of an otherwise eligible child has a physical or mental illness, defect, or impairment that reduces substantially, or eliminates the parent's ability to support or care for the child for a period which is expected to last at least 30 days. Criteria for Incapacity Incapacity deprivation exists if the incapacity meets at least one of the following criteria: • Prevents the parent from working full-time: o At a job in which they have normally worked. o On another job for which they have attained education, training, experience, or can be learned by on-the-job training. • The incapacity Is the reason employers refuse to employ the parent for the work they could do. This includes behavioral disorders which interfere with the securing and maintaining of employment. • Prevents the parent from accomplishing as much on a job as other employees and is the reason the parent is paid on a reduced basis even though working full time. • Qualifies the parent to be employed in a job which is rehabilitative, therapeutic or in a sheltered workshop not considered to be a full-time job. • Reduces substantially or eliminates the parent’s ability to care for the child. Determination of Incapacity When making a determination that incapacity exist s, staff will take into consideration the limited employment opportunities of the customer with the disability. The following are acceptable verification of incapacity: • A written statement, current award letter or copy of benefit payment from the agency authorizing the disability payment such as benefits from: o Social Security Administration (Disability based income). o State Disability Insurance Benefits. o Worker’s Compensation. o Supplemental Security Income (SSI)/State Supplemental Payment (SSP). Note: Receipt of SSI/SSP because of age (65+) does not establish deprivation based on incapacity. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Deprivation Due to Incapacity Number Page 41-400.C 2 of 3 • Medical verification form (such as, but not limited to; CW 61A Physical Capacities, CW 61B Mental Capacities, and 07-388 HHSA Authorization to Release Medical Information) or a written statement completed by a licensed healthcare provider that provides information sufficient to verify the incapacity that includes all of the following: o A diagnosis of the parent’s condition. o Explanation to which the condition prevents the parent form engaging in employment or why it reduces substantially or eliminates their ability to support or care for the child. o The duration of the condition. o The date of the next scheduled medical examination or appointment. o The name, address, and phone number of the healthcare provider. Note: Verbal statements can be accepted w hen there is a delay in obtaining a written statement for reasons beyond the customer’s control. A verbal statement from the physician, licensed or certified psychologist, or an authorized staff member with access to the customer’s medical records verifying incapacity will be accepted pending the written verification for up to 60 days. If a verbal statement is obtained, the journal entry must include all of the following: • The date the verification was obtained. • The name of the person who provided the verification. • The name of the staff who obtained the verification. Review of Incapacity The deprivation of incapacity does not exist when: • The verification provided does not meet the criteria. • The incapacity is expected to be less than 30 days. If deprivation due to incapacity cannot be established, staff will evaluate the case to determine if another basis of deprivation can be established. If an application was denied due to the incapacity is not expected to last at least 30 days, and later on it is established that the incapacity is to exceed 30 days, the denial will be rescinded and payment will be granted retroactively effective the appropriate beginning date of aid. Once d eprivation due to incapacity has been determined at application, it is required to be reestablished and reverified at the following times: • Annual redetermination when the duration of the incapacity is expected to last more than one year or is permanent. • 30 days prior to the end date of the incapacity when the duration of the incapacity is not expected to last more than one year. • When there is a reason to believe that there has been a change in the condition. o For example, during the Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) review, there is an indication that the incapacitated parent is now employed. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Deprivation Due to Incapacity Number Page 41-400.C 3 of 3 References: Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 41-430 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by August 31, 2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

Policy: Deprivation due to physical or mental incapacity of a parent is deemed to exist when the parent of an otherwise eligible child has a physical or mental illness, defect, or impairment that reduces substantially, or eliminates the parent's ability to support or care for the child for a period which is expected to last at least 30 days. Criteria for Incapacity Incapacity deprivation exists if the incapacity meets at least one of the following criteria: • Prevents the parent from working full-time: o At a job in which they have normally worked. o On another job for which they have attained education, training, experience, or can be learned by on-the-job training. • The incapacity Is the reason employers refuse to employ the parent for the work they could do. This includes behavioral disorders which interfere with the securing and maintaining of employment. • Prevents the parent from accomplishing as much on a job as other employees and is the reason the parent is paid on a reduced basis even though working full time. • Qualifies the parent to be employed in a job which is rehabilitative, therapeutic or in a sheltered workshop not considered to be a full-time job. • Reduces substantially or eliminates the parent’s ability to care for the child. Determination of Incapacity When making a determination that incapacity exist s, staff will take into consideration the limited employment opportunities of the customer with the disability. The following are acceptable verification of incapacity: • A written statement, current award letter or copy of benefit payment from the agency authorizing the disability payment such as benefits from: o Social Security Administration (Disability based income). o State Disability Insurance Benefits. o Worker’s Compensation. o Supplemental Security Income (SSI)/State Supplemental Payment (SSP). Note: Receipt of SSI/SSP because of age (65+) does not establish deprivation based on incapacity. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Deprivation Due to Incapacity Number Page 41-400.C 2 of 3 • Medical verification form (such as, but not limited to; CW 61A Physical Capacities, CW 61B Mental Capacities, and 07-388 HHSA Authorization to Release Medical Information) or a written statement completed by a licensed healthcare provider that provides information sufficient to verify the incapacity that includes all of the following: o A diagnosis of the parent’s condition. o Explanation to which the condition prevents the parent form engaging in employment or why it reduces substantially or eliminates their ability to support or care for the child. o The duration of the condition. o The date of the next scheduled medical examination or appointment. o The name, address, and phone number of the healthcare provider. Note: Verbal statements can be accepted w hen there is a delay in obtaining a written statement for reasons beyond the customer’s control. A verbal statement from the physician, licensed or certified psychologist, or an authorized staff member with access to the customer’s medical records verifying incapacity will be accepted pending the written verification for up to 60 days. title: D. Deprivation Due to Unemployment
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Deprivation Due to Unemployment Number Page 41-400.D 1 of 3 Revision Date: August 1, 2024 Background: Deprivation of parental support or care is a separate and specific eligibility factor for CalWORKs. A child’s deprivation is based on the status of their natural or adoptive parent(s). There is no CalWORKs eligibility unless deprivation requirements are met. Purpose: This section outlines the CalWORKs policies on deprivation due to unemployment. The purpose of this revision is for sunset review and reformatting to current standards . There is no policy change. This revision also combines previous sections of the CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 41 -400.D and 41- 400.E into one section. Additionally, specific situational examples were removed from the CPG, and a desk aid was created. Policy: Deprivation due to unemployment exists when the parent, in a two parent case, who is determined to be the Principal Earner (PE) meets the definition of unemployed or underemployed whether the individual is included or excluded from the Assistance Unit (AU) and the child(ren) would otherwise be deprived except that neither of the parents is deceased, incapacitated or absent from the home. Principal Earner In a home in which both parents of an eligible child are living , the PE is whichever parent earned the greater amount of income in the 24-month period prior to the date of eligibility for CalWORKs. When both parents qualify as PE and have earned an identical amount of income in the 24-month period, the customers will designate which parent is the PE. Once the PE has been determined, the designated parent continues to be the PE for each consecutive month the family receives CalWORKs due to the unemployment deprivation. Unemployed Parent (U-Parent) An unemployed parent is defined as one of the natural or adoptive parents with whom the child is living, who is designated as the PE, and meets one of the following conditions: • Is not employed. • Is employed less than 100 hours during the four-week (28-day) period prior to the date of eligibility for CalWORKs. Note: Unemployment deprivation can only be established due to the unemployment of the parent designated as the PE. The 100-hour policy does not apply to the parent who is not the PE. Hours of Employment The hours of employment is defined as the hours the customer spent providing a service or product, whether the customer is an employee or self -employed. Any hours spent working to acquire earned income, whether the customer receives the income or not, will be considered toward the 100 -hours policy. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Deprivation Due to Unemployment Number Page 41-400.D 2 of 3 A self-employed individual is considered fully employed when working 100 hours o r more per month. The 100 hours includes the time utilized for: • Contracting for jobs. • Making a product to be sold. • Travel time to and from a job site. Customers who are participating in an on-the-job (OJT) program or any similar work training activity, in which they are paid in a wage, are to be considered employed for the purpose of determining deprivation. Requirements in Establishing Deprivation Due to Unemployment To establish deprivation due to unemployment, the following requirements must be met: • Unemployment of the PE. o The PE has worked less than 100 hours during the four-week (28-day) period prior to the date of eligibility. The four -week period is to be adjusted daily to determine the four -week period in which the PE worked less than 100 hours. Note: When a customer applies for CalWORKs who recently lost CalWORKs eligibility due to Expanded Subsidized Income (ESE), they will be considered a current recipient for the purpose of establishing unemployment deprivation if they apply within three calendar months of the end of the ESE assignment. During the three calendar months period after the ESE ends, the 100 -hour rule is not applicable. • The PE who is apparently eligible for Unemployment Insurance Benefits (UIB) must apply for and accept any UIB to which they are entitled. When the PE does not comply with this requirement, the unemployment deprivation does not exist for the family. Note: The PE cannot be considered as unemployed due to their participation in a strike. Refer to Desk Aid – Unemployment Deprivation for examples in establishing deprivation due to unemployment. Change in Deprivation A family’s circumstances may change in such a way that deprivation needs to be reestablished . For example, the absent parent returns to the home , or a parent is no longer incapacitated . In such situations, the PE is to be determined, and hours of employment is determined according to the 100 - hour policy. Refer to the following CalWORKs Processing Guides for examples of reported changes related to deprivation: • 40-100.A3 – Treatment of Changes During the Application Process. • 44-270.A1 – Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) Procedures. When deprivation changes to unemployment, the previously incapacitated or absent parent must be referred to Employment Services unless otherwise exempt. Once deprivation due to unemployment has been determined at application, it is required to be reestablished at SAR and annual redetermination. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Deprivation Due to Unemployment Number Page 41-400.D 3 of 3 Note: The 100-hour policy applies to applicants only. Once the AU is determined eligible for CalWORKs with deprivation due to unemployment, the AU is no longer subject to the 100-hour rule as long as they receive continued aid. For example, the PE reported at annual redetermination that their work hours exceeded 100 hours. The family may continue to receive aid regardless of the number of hours the PE works provided the family meets all other conditions of CalWORKs eligibility. References: Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 41-440 All County Letter (ACL) 97-65, 12-25, 14-57 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by August 31, 2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: E. Deprivation Due to Absence
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Deprivation Due to Absence Number Page 41-400.E 1 of 3 Revision Date: August 1, 2024 Background: Deprivation of parental support or care is a separate and specific eligibility factor for CalWORKs. A child’s deprivation is based on the status of their natural or adoptive parent(s). There is no CalWORKs eligibility unless deprivation requirements are met. Purpose: The section outlines the CalWORKs policies on deprivation due to absence. The purpose of this revision is for sunset review and reformatting to current standards . There is no policy change. This revision renumbered and combined CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) sections 41-400.F, 41-400.G, and 41 -400.H into section 41-400.E. CPG sections 41 -100.F, 41 -400.G, and 41 -400.H become obsolete with the issuance of this material. Policy: Deprivation due to absence exists when the natural or adoptive parent continues to be physically absent from the child’s home. In addition, the nature of the absence results in an interruption or termination of the parent’s functioning as a provider of maintenance, physical care, or guidance for the child . The reason for the absence or the length of time that the parent has been absent is not a determining factor, instead the deciding aspect is if the absence precludes the parent from planning for the present support and care of the child. Continued Absence The continued absence of the parent from the home as defined above includes but is not limited to the following circumstances: • The parents are not married to each other and have not maintained a home together. • The absent parent: o Is not legally able to return to the home because of confinement in a penal or correctional institution. o Has been deported. o Has voluntarily left the country because of the threat of, or the knowledge that they are subject to deportation. • A parent has filed for or retained legal counsel for the purpose of filing an action for dissolution of marriage, an annulment, or for legal separation. • The court has issued an injunction forbidding the parent to visit the custodial parent or child. • The remaining parent has presented a sign, written statement that the other parent has left the family and that the nature of the absence constitutes continued absence of the parent. Refer to the Evidence of Continued Absence section of this material for more information. • One or both parents are physically out of the home and their whereabouts are unknown. Deprivation due to continued absence exist s as of the date that one of the mentioned circumstances occurs. A determination of continued absence must be determined even under the following circumstances: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Deprivation Due to Absence Number Page 41-400.E 2 of 3 • When the parent remains in contact with the child through regular or frequent visits. • When the child lives with each parent for alternating periods of time. • When a parent who is a convicted offender is permitted to live at home while serving a courtimposed sentence by performing unpaid public work or unpaid community service during the workday. Note: If the customer is in a jail program in which they live at the home and work at a regular job during the week and only spends weekends in jail, the absence must be considered temporary and is not considered continued. Therefore, there is no CalWORKs eligibility unless other deprivation exists. When questions arise regarding continued absence of a parent , various factors may be considered such as, but not limited to: • Does the parent provide day-to-day care and control of the child? • Do the parents maintain separate homes? • Do the parents have separate mailing addresses? • Do the parents maintain their money separately? • Do the parents have access to each other’s income or resources? • Is the parent absent due to hospitalization, attendance at school, visiting, vacationing, or trips made in connection with current or prospective employment? Temporary Absence Continued absence does not exist when: • A parent is physically absent from the home on a temporary basis such as visits, trips or temporary assignments undertaken in connection with current or prospective employment. • A parent is absent for the sole reason of performing active duty in the uniformed services of the United States such as: o Army o Navy o Airforce o Marine Corps o Coast Guard o National Oceanographic and Atmospheric Administration o Public Health Services of the United States Note: When the customer provides appropriate evidence to establish that continued absence would exist irrespective of the parent’s performance of active duty in the uniformed services of the United States, continued absence must be considered to exist. Evidence of Continued Absence The customer’s written statement on the application and the child support forms are considered sufficient evidence of the other parent ’s continued absence unless conflicting information is known to the county or reasonable doubt indicates that the deprivation due to absence is questionable. When the information presented is questionable, staff are required to further review the case to ensure deprivation due to absence exist. Examples of such conditions that may raise concern include but are not limited to the following: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Deprivation Due to Absence Number Page 41-400.E 3 of 3 • Verbal or written information provided by the customer is contradictory, incomplete, or not consistent. • Information provided by the customer or others, including information in the previous case record, leads to a reasonable doubt that continued absence exists. • Past history of non-compliance with the Local Child Support Agency (LCSA). If conflicting information is known to the county or reasonable doubt indicates further evidence is necessary, the written statement of the customer must be supported by at least one of the following: • Additional evidence demonstrating “continued absence” exists, which may include written statements of the absent parent or other persons with prior knowledge of the family relationship. • Evidence of the actions of the customer or the absent parent that clearly indicate not only the physical absence of the other parent but also the continued nature of the absence. If it is suspected that the absent parent is living in the home or deprivation due to absence is questionable, staff must confer with their supervisor to review the case circumstances, and when applicable, the case is to be referred to the Bureau of Public Assistance Investigations (BPAI). Refer to CPG 20-000.A – Integrity/Fraud Detection and Prevention and the associated CalWORKs Processing Guide 20-000.A1 for more information. Requirements to Cooperate with Child Support Regulations The child support cooperation requirement must be followed whenever the assistance unit (AU) has an absent parent. Refer to CPG 43 -200.A – Child Support/Referrals and Assignment of Rights and Cooperation Requirements for more information. References: Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 41-450 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by August 31, 2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services
