title: A. Assistance Unit
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Assistance Unit Number Page 41-500.A 1 of 3 Revision Date: December 1, 2024 Background: The Assistance Unit (AU) is defined as a group of related persons, living in the same home, who have been determined eligible for CalWORKs. An AU will be established when all eligibility factors have been determined. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to define the minimum requirements to establishing the AU, differentiate between the AU members, non-AU members and optional persons to the AU. This material revision is due to sunset date review. No policy or procedure changes have been made. Policy: Filing Unit Individuals required to be included on the Statement of Facts are considered the Filing Unit. In addition, optional persons must be included on the Statement of Facts when aid is requested for them and they are living in the home of an applicant child. The Filing Unit (also referred to as the “Family Unit” or “Big MAP” (Maximum Aid Payment)) includes all members of the AU plus certain non-AU members living in the home including: • The spouse of an aided child. • Ineligible undocumented noncitizens. • Fleeing felons. Persons receiving Supplemental Security Income/State Supplement ary Payment (SSI/SSP) are not included as filing unit members. Mandatorily Included Persons in the Filing Unit • Applicant child. • Siblings and half-siblings of the applicant child. • Parents of mandatory children. • A pregnant person, in a one-person unit (Pregnant Person Only – PPO). • The following adults, if seeking aid, when there is a child receiving SSI/SSP or the child is sanctioned by the Employment Services (ES) program: o The child’s parent(s). o Caretaker relative. o Stepparent or domestic partner of the child’s parent. • Senior parent of minor parent seeking aid for the minor parent’s child. • Sponsor of a documented noncitizen. • Spouse or California domestic partner of persons mandatorily included in the filing unit. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Assistance Unit Number Page 41-500.A 2 of 3 Optional Persons in the Filing Unit • A nonparent relative who has been determined to be the caretaker relative of the eligible child(ren). • Other eligible children, including but not limited to a grandchild, niece or nephew. • Alternatively Sentenced Parent (ASP)*. *An ASP is a parent who is a convicted offender permitted to live at home while serving a court - imposed sentence that precludes the parent from providing support through paid employment. Maximum Aid Payment The MAP level is determined by an evaluation of the AU’s status as either exempt or non-exempt. Eligible Child An eligible child is: • A member of an income eligible AU. • Deprived of parental support and care. • Under 18 years of age or an 18-year-old who meets the age requirements. Note: Effective January 1, 2016, a deceased child will continue to be included as a member of a family receiving CalWORKs for the month in which his or her death occurred, and the following month. Penalties Penalties may be assessed for immunization problem, school attendance problem, persons committing fraud. Also refer to CPG 41-500.E for Excluded Sanctioned Persons. The penalized person’s needs are not considered when determining the AU’s financial eligibility and computing the grant amount. However, the person remains in the AU as an active recipient. As an AU member, the person continues to receive cash-linked Medi-Cal, is required to participate in ES activities unless exempt and ha s time on aid counted against the Time On Aid (TOA) limit. All income of the penalized person is used in the AU’s eligibility and grant determination, and all appropriate income disregards are allowed. Procedure: None. Program Impacts: None. References: • EAS 82-800, 82-832.1. • ACLs No. 14-100, 15-18, 15-92. • ACINs No. I-02-16, I-13-16, I-03-20. • CFLs No. 14-15-60, 14-15-61. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by December 31, 2027. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Assistance Unit Number Page 41-500.A 3 of 3 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: B. Caretaker Relative Requirements
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Caretaker Relative Requirements Number Page 41-500.B 1 of 5 Revision Date: December 1, 2024 Background: The caretaker relative must be related to the applicant or eligible child. The caretaker relative may be any relation by blood, marriage or adoption who is within the fifth degree of kinship to the applicant or eligible child, and exercises responsibility for the day to day care and control of the child. Purpose: The purpose of this section is t o define the caretaker relative requirements. This material revision is due to sunset date review. No policy or procedure changes have been made. Policy: Caretaker Relative Defined The following rules apply to the designation of a caretaker relative in an Assistance Unit (AU): • A caretaker relative must be related to the applicant or eligible child. • A caretaker relative may be a parent or a non-parent caretaker. • A non-parent caretaker relative must be 18 years of age or older. • To be determined a caretaker relative, an eligible child must be living in the home of the caretaker relative. • A child is considered to be living in the home of a caretaker relative even when: o The child is under the jurisdiction of the court and is living in the home of a relative ( that is, receiving probation services or protective supervision). o The child’s legal custody is held by an agency that does not have physical possession of the child. • The caretaker relative can be any of the relatives listed below (See Relationship of a Caretaker Relative) when a child has been relinquished or adopted, or parental rights have been terminated. A Legal Guardian as Caretaker Relative A legal guardian is a person named by the court to be the guardian of a child. In order to receive CalWORKs benefits for the child and/or themselves, the legal guardian must meet the definition of a caretaker relative (above). Relationship of a Caretaker Relative The caretaker relative may be related by blood, marriage or adoption who is within the fifth degree of kinship to the applicant or eligible child as specified below: Relationship Type Relation Biological Relatives • Parent (mother or father). • Grandparent (including great and great-great). • Brother or sister (including half-sibling). • Uncle or aunt (including great and great-great). • Nephew or niece (including great and great-great). • First or second cousin. Step Relatives • Stepfather, stepmother or California domestic partner of a parent. • Stepbrother or stepsister. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Caretaker Relative Requirements Number Page 41-500.B 2 of 5 Spouses of Relatives A spouse or California domestic partner of a parent of any person named above even after marriage or domestic relationship has been terminated by death or dissolution or termination of the California domestic partnership. Adoptive Relatives A person who legally adopts the child or that person’s relatives as above in this table. Determining the Caretaker Relative • Generally, if the child is living with a parent, the parent is the caretaker relative. • If the child is not living with the parent, the applicant will be the caretaker relative. • Staff must determine which person(s) has responsibility for the care and control of the child for whom aid is being requested based on information supplied by the customer. • If the birth or adoptive parent is not the caretaker relative, but lives in the same home as the caretaker relative and the eligible child, the parent must be included in the AU. • The mandatory inclusion rules do not supersede the caretaker relative relationship requirement - the caretaker relative must have the acceptable degree of relatedness. Care and Control The responsibilities for care and control of the child may include but are not limited to responsibility for the following: • The well-being of the child (personal hygiene, clothing, medical and dental care, nutrition, etc.). • The child’s education or childcare (enrolls child in school, takes child to school, assists with child’s homework, attends parent-teacher meetings, etc.). • The discipline of the child (sets rules, curfew, monitors child’s behavior, etc.). • The religious, cultural and social well-being of the child (church attendance, involvement with community groups and organizations, such as, scouting, little league, school dances, movies, etc.). • Claiming the child as a tax dependent. Number of Caretaker Relatives An AU may have more than one caretaker relative . For example, a married couple each with a child from a prior relationship is each considered the caretaker relative for their respective child . However, an eligible child must have only one caretaker relative at a time. Minor Parent / Caretaker Relative A child who is a caretaker relative for their own or another child ( such as a sibling) must not be considered as a child in order to establish eligibility for a senior parent in the household. Changing Caretaker Relatives Only one needy caretaker relative can be aided within an AU at a time. When an AU relocates from the home of one needy caretaker relative to the home of another needy caretaker relative, the second caretaker relative cannot be aided until the first of the following month. Caretaker Relationship Verification • The relationship must be clearly documented in the case record as well as the evidence used to verify the relationship of the caretaker relative has to the applicant or eligible child. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Caretaker Relative Requirements Number Page 41-500.B 3 of 5 • When the evidence of relationship is incomplete, explorations must be continued to pursue verification to the point that a preponderance of evidence supports an approval or denial of aid. • The case record must document which kind(s) of evidence does or does not establish relationship - inconsistent or contradictory evidence should be referred to the Bureau of Public Assistance Investigations (BPAI). When Unable to Verify Relationship Procedures When evidence is not available to establish relationship, aid may be approved by a supervisor when all the following apply: • There is a non-parent caretaker relative. • The claim of relationship is not inconsistent or questionable. • The supervisor has determined a sworn statement by the caretaker relative affirms their relationship to the child. • The steps taken to acquire evidence of relationship and their outcome are documented in the case record. Acceptable Evidence of Relationship The following are examples of acceptable evidence of the caretaker relative’s relationship to a child: Type of Records Document Birth Records • Adoption papers or records. • Baptismal records of birth and parentage. • Birth certificate. Court Records • Court records of parentage. • Court support records. • Divorce papers or termination of California registered domestic partnership. • Juvenile Court records. Government Records • Bureau of Vital Statistics or local government records of birth and parentage. • Census records. • Native American Census records. • Child Support Agency paternity records. • Marriage licenses records or declaration of California registered domestic partnership. • Public Health records of birth and parentage. Miscellaneous • Church records (including a statement from a priest, minister, rabbi, imam or other holy person) of parentage or relationship. • School or day care center records. • Family Bible. • Insurance Policy. • Hospital or public health records of birth and parentage. • Outpatient care records (maintained by a hospital, clinic or physician). • Voluntary social service agency records. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Caretaker Relative Requirements Number Page 41-500.B 4 of 5 Alternating Caretaker Relative Living Arrangements for a Child • If a child stays alternately for periods of less than one month with each parent, the caretaker relative will be, in most situations the parent with whom the child stays for the majority of the time . The temporary absence of the caretaker relative or child does not affect this determination. • When a child alternates between parents for periods of more than one full calendar month, there is no temporary absence. The child is considered to be permanently absent from one parent when they are with the other parent. • The parent with whom the child stays for the minority of the time may be the caretaker relative if that parent can establish that they have majority of responsibility for care and control of the child. • The parent who has been determined to be the caretaker relative of a child, who stays with the other parent for an alternating period of one month or less , will remain the caretaker relative while the child is with the other parent. Equal Time Caretaker Relative Living Arrangements for a Child When the child spends an equal amount of time with each parent, and each parent exercises an equal share of care and control, the parent who applied for aid is considered the caretaker relative, provided the other parent is not currently applying for or receiving aid for the child. When Both Parents Apply for Aid as the Caretaker Relative When each parent has applied for aid, the caretaker relative is determined by the following order: • The parent designated in a current court order as the primary caretaker for purposes of public assistance under Civil Code Section 4600.5(h). • When a court order does not exist and only one parent would be eligible for aid, the parent who would be eligible is the caretaker relative. • When both parents would be eligible, the parents will designate one parent as the caretaker relative, the agreement will be documented by completing form CW 13 Caretaker Relative Agreement. • If the parents cannot reach agreement, the parent who first applied for aid for the child will be the caretaker relative. Death of a Parent Caretaker or Other Caretaker Relative When it is learned of the death of a parent caretaker or other caretaker relative of a child receiving CalWORKs benefits, and if the child is still eligible for CalWORKs, the staff will assist the new caretaker relative with the process needed to ensure that CalWORKs benefits continue for the child. If the child is no longer eligible for CalWORKs because they are living with a non-relative caretaker rather than a relative caretaker, the staff will inform the non -relative caretaker that Aid to Family with Dependent Children-Foster Care (AFDC-FC) benefits may be available for the child. If they wish to apply for Foster Care benefits at that time, the staff will refer them to the county’s Foster Care office. Procedure: Chart for Determining Relatedness of Caretaker Relatives The chart, located in Eligibility Essentials/CalWORKs/Desk Aid site, is available to help staff establish the correct caretaker relationship. Program Impacts: None. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Caretaker Relative Requirements Number Page 41-500.B 5 of 5 References: • EAS 82-808. • ACL No. 18-82. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by December 31, 2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: C. Temporary Absence
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Temporary Absence From The Assistance Unit Number Page 41-500.C 1 of 3 Revision Date: December 1, 2024 Background: Any member of an Assistance Unit (AU) may be considered temporarily absent when absent from the home for one full calendar month or less. A child may be considered to be living in the home of a caretaker relative even though the child or the caretaker relative is temporarily absent from the home. Purpose: The purpose of this section is t o define the factors to be considered when determining temporary absence status. This material revision is due to sunset date review. No policy or procedure changes have been made. Policy: Length of Temporary Absence Rules • Any member of the AU can be temporarily absent from the home for one calendar month or less. • One full calendar month is from the first day of the month through the last day of the month. • If the individual is absent for the entire month of February, the calendar month is not considered completed until a full 30 days has transpired. • A person confined in a correctional facility on the first of any month and expected to remain for one calendar month or more is to be considered permanently absent. Examples: • On February 2nd, an AU member leaves the home to visit other family and returns on March 16th . The person left after the 1st and was not gone for one calendar month . They would be considered temporarily absent. • On April 16th, an AU member leaves home due to a death in the family and does not return until June 3rd. The person was gone more than one calendar month (May) and is not eligible for aid in June. • In a non-leap year, an AU member leaves the home on February 1st. The person is not considered absent until March 3rd, after 30 days away from home. Evaluating for Length of Absence Exception Factors The following factors must be evaluated in determining exceptions to the one calendar month time limit for temporary absence. A single factor may not be conclusive: • The actual family circumstances (even if it is inconsistent with a court custody order). • The caretaker relative must continue to exercise responsibility for care and control of the child. • The absent person has the ability and intent to return. • In the case of an absent child, the caretaker relative has the ability to require the return of the child to the home. • The caretaker relative continues to contribute to the support of the child. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Temporary Absence From The Assistance Unit Number Page 41-500.C 2 of 3 Verification Verification is required to document the basis of any exception to the one full calendar month time limit for temporary absence described below. Documentation consists of a third -party verification and a journal entry explanation. Example: The AU reports that a child has been hospitalized. Verification is required to document the basis of the temporary absence. Acceptable evidence that a child is hospitalized may include, but is not limited to, the following: • An admittance documentation from the hospital. • A letter from the admitting medical doctor or other legally qualified medical professional. • Other documentation determined to be acceptable evidence that the child has been admitted to the hospital. The documentation must include the date the child was admitted to the hospital and, if possible, the anticipated duration of the hospital stay . If the child remains hospitalized beyond the anticipated duration of the hospital stay, a new verification is required. Reasons for Exceptions to the Length of Absence Time Limit The following situations are exceptions to the one full calendar month time limit for a temporary absence from the home. Reason for Absence Description Hospital Stay As of January 1, 2014: • Any AU member may be considered temporarily absent during a hospital stay. • A hospital stay may include any in -patient admission to a medical hospital, a psychiatric care facility, or drug or alcohol rehabilitation treatment facility. Employment • An AU member absent from the home because of work is temporarily absent for the duration of the job. • Absence from the home to search for a job does not qualify for this exemption. Institution of Higher Learning and Educational School (leading to high school diploma or equivalent) Vocational School (leading to a job) • An AU member who is away from home to attend one of these institutions is considered temporarily absent when there is no local school that provides the same preparatory opportunities. • Individuals who qualify for this exemption continue to be considered temporarily absent during the period they are in school or training. A Child with an Individualized Education Plan (IEP) • A child who is away from home to attend a school that meets their special needs is temporarily absent when there is no local school that can meet the child’s needs. A Child in a Licensed Group Home • When a child is in a licensed group home due to a crisis situation such as their parent: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Temporary Absence From The Assistance Unit Number Page 41-500.C 3 of 3 o Being hospitalized. o Being Incapacitated. o Receiving respite care services to maintain family stability is considered temporarily absent if Foster Care is not paying for the child’s care. • The caretaker relative continues to have care and control over the child. • This exemption is limited to the duration of the parent’s illness or the other family crisis. A child placed in out -of-home care by a Children’s Services Protective Services Worker • If the child’s family is considered to be a CalWORKs Family Reunification, then the child is considered temporarily absent for up to 180 days. • The absence may be extended by order of Juvenile Court. • The child continues to be considered temporarily absent until returned home or reunification services are terminated by the Juvenile Court. Procedure: None. Program Impacts: None. References: • EAS 82-812. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by December 31, 2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: D. Persons Included in the Assistance Unit
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Persons Included in the Assistance Unit Number Page 41-500.D 1 of 3 Revision Date: December 1, 2024 Background: The Assistance Unit (AU) is a group of related persons living in the same home who have been determined eligible for CalWORKs and for whom cash aid has been authorized. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to define the minimum requirements to establishing the AU, differentiate between the AU members, non-AU members and optional persons in the AU. This material revision is due to sunset date review. No policy or procedure changes have been made. Policy: The AU After the Filing Unit (refer to CPG 41-500.A) has been established, an AU will be established when all eligibility factors have been met, including those persons who meet the mandatory inclusion and optional person requirements. If a person, not otherwise excluded, is found to meet the eligibility requirements, they are considered an eligible person who must be added to the AU if not considered an optional person. The AU is also referred to as the “Little MAP (Maximum Aid Payment)”. These eligible individuals must be living in the same home at the time of initial family application, mid - period if their addition has no negative action to the grant amount, at the beginning of the Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) payment period for SAR cases, or the first of the month following the month the change was reported for Annual Reporting/Child-Only (AR/CO) cases. Minimum Requirements The AU is required to have at least one of the following: • An eligible child. • One non-minor dependent in their own AU of one. • A needy caretaker relative of a: o Supplemental Security Income/State Supplementary Payment (SSI/SSP) child. o Child who is eligible to receive federal Foster Care (aid code 42). o Kin-GAP child (aid code 4F or 4G). • A pregnant person. • A relative of a 16 or 17-year-old teen who is sanctioned by Employment Services (ES). Mandatory Inclusion The Mandatory Inclusion requirement means that a parent, sibling or half-sibling must be included in a Filing Unit and require s that an eligible parent, sibling or half -sibling must be included in the AU with the applicant or eligible child. An eligible child must be both deprived and needy, meaning that the child meets the requirements of all necessary linking and non-linking eligibility factors. Linking eligibility factors are those single conditions that link a customer to the program: blindness and deprivation of parental care or support. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Persons Included in the Assistance Unit Number Page 41-500.D 2 of 3 Non-linking eligibility factors are those factors that establish whether an individual is eligible to assistance under the program to which the customer is linked: age, property, residence, financial and institutional statuses. The AU must include the following persons when they are living in the same home and are eligible: • The applicant child(ren). • Any eligible sibling or half-sibling of the applicant child who meets the age requirement. • Any birth or adoptive parent of the applicant child, or of an eligible sibling or half-sibling who meets the age requirement, except for an Alternatively Sentenced Prisoner (ASP)*. *An ASP is a parent who is a convicted offender permitted to live at home while serving a court - imposed sentence that precludes the parent from providing support through paid employment. The application must be denied, or the case be discontinued, when a mandator ily included person refuses to be included in the AU or fails to provide required documentation to determine eligibility. Voluntary Maximum Aid Payment Exclusion Effective November 1, 2018, an AU may opt to receive full child support payments for a step/half-sibling of an eligible child in the AU, in lieu of CalWORKs for that step/half-sibling (refer to CPG 44-300.H). Optional Persons The following optional persons are those who are not otherwise required to be in the AU but can be included upon customer’s request: • Any non-parent relative who has been determined to be the caretaker relative of the child. • Any other eligible child, including but no t limited to, a grandchild or niece/nephew of the caretaker relative. • Any essential person (stepparent, California domestic partner of the eligible child’s parent, or ASP) meeting the identification of persons for claiming of financial participation requirements (refer to CPG 41-500.G). A person identified as an excluded person cannot be in the AU even if previously identified as a mandatorily included or optional person. When a change in the number of persons living in the home is reported, staff must: • Identify for the customer any person living in the home who may be included in the AU. • Explain the effect of including or excluding the optional person by describing the AU composition which will result in the maximum grant amount to which the family is eligible, considering the income and resources of each person who may be included. AU Determination • Staff determine who is mandatorily to be included or excluded from the AU. • Staff and customer together decide whether an optional person is included in the AU. Staff will use the mandatory inclusion regulations based on the circumstances unique to that family when determining an AU, ensuring no conflicts with other CalWORKs regulations. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Persons Included in the Assistance Unit Number Page 41-500.D 3 of 3 A child may be deprived of parental care or support for more than one reason. Before identifying a sibling or half-sibling as an eligible child, staff must evaluate non-linking factors. A sibling or half-sibling may meet a basis of deprivation but remain an ineligible child for inclusion in the AU. Combining Assistance Units Two or more AUs in the same home must be combined into one AU when any of the following is met: • A caretaker relative is married to another caretaker relative in another AU. • Two caretaker relatives in the home have separate children and have a child in common. • There is only one caretaker relative. Combining AUs Mid-Period When a voluntary mid-period change is made that would combine separate AUs, staff will compare the monthly grant for the combined AUs to the total combined monthly grants of the separate AUs and combine the AUs the first of the: • Month following the voluntary report, i f the combined AU's monthly grant would be higher than the total combined monthly grant of two separate AUs. • Next Payment Period, if the combined AU's monthly grant does not result in an increase to the total combined monthly grant of the separate AUs. Procedure: Desk Aid - Mandatory Inclusion in the Assistance Unit (AU) - Scenario Examples Refer to the desk aid, located in Eligibility Essentials, for mandatory inclusion examples. References: • EAS 82-800. • ACL No. 18-82. • ACIN No. I-03-20. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by December 31, 2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: E. Persons Excluded from the Assistance Unit
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Persons Excluded From The Assistance Unit Number Page 41-500.E 1 of 3 Revision Date: December 1, 2024 Background: Certain persons in the home are ineligible to CalWORKs if they are excluded by law, sanctioned, or have exhausted their CalWORKs time limit. These persons are not included in the assistance unit (AU). Purpose: The purpose of this section is t o define the non-AU members. This material revision is due to sunset review. No policy or procedure changes have been made. Policy: Persons Excluded by Law The following persons are excluded by Law: • A child living with their minor parent who is receiving Foster Care or Kin-GAP. • A person not meeting the citizenship/qualified non-citizen status requirements. • The father of an unborn child who is living in the home with the pregnant woman and who is: o Not the parent or caretaker relative of an eligible child in the household. o Not an essential person. • A person receiving Supplemental Security Income/State Supplemental Payment (SSI/SSP), Refugee Repatriate Payment (RRP), Foster Care or Kin-GAP. • A sponsored non-citizen whose needs are met by a sponsoring agency or by a sponsor’s deemed income. • The spouse of an eligible child, living with the child in the senior parent’s home, when there is no child in common, for whom deprivation exists. • A refugee eligible for and required to participate in an alternative project implemented pursuant to Section 412(e)(7) of the federal Immigration and Nationality Act 8 USC 1522(e)(7). • A person fleeing to avoid felony prosecution, custody or confinement after conviction for a crime or attempt to commit a crime that is a felony. o The existence of a warrant for arrest will be presumed to be evidence of fleeing, unless rebutted by other evidence sufficient to prove that the person had no knowledge that they are being sought by law enforcement. • A person in violation of a condition of probation or parole. o Violating a condition of probation or parole means a warrant for a crime, that violates a condition of probation or parole, has been issued, or an order has been issued revoking probation or parole. o The initial offense for which probation or parole was ordered does not need to have been a felony. • A non-minor dependent. o Non-minor dependents constitute an AU of one and are excluded from the AU of a needy or non-needy caretaker relative for CalWORKs purposes. Excluded Sanctioned Persons A sanction results when a person is taken out of the AU for failure to comply with program requirements. A person excluded from the AU due to a sanction is: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Persons Excluded From The Assistance Unit Number Page 41-500.E 2 of 3 • A parent, pregnant person, or caretaker relative who refuses to assign support rights, or fails to cooperate with the Child/Spousal Support requirements. • A person who fails to cooperate in the verification of their citizenship or non-citizen status. • A mandatory work registrant who fails or refuses without good cause to meet Employment Services (ES) program requirements. o When the participant is a principal earner, the second parent is also ineligible unless they are participating in, or exempt from, ES activities. Effective March 1, 2015, CalWORKs cases that include parents/caretakers who have been ES sanctioned for 12 consecutive months or longer, will be eligible to the solely state funded (K1/3F aid codes) program. Note: ES sanctioned persons will resume sanctioned status whenever there has been a break in aid. Intake staff must review the case to identify any adults in the potential AU who are currently serving a n ES sanction. The sanction status will remain for the non -compliant persons on the automated system at intake, when the cash assistance case is granted for other eligible members of the AU. The sanction status will remain until the person has cured their sanction by performing the activity that resulted in the sanction (CPG 10-025.A). • A customer or a child whose parent, caretaker relative, or legal guardian: o Refuses or fails to furnish a Social Security Number (SSN) or evidence of a completed application for a SSN. o Refuses or fails to cooperate in verifying a SSN. • A striker who is not a caretaker relative. Excluded CalWORKs Timed-Out Adults A CalWORKs timed-out adult is an adult who has been removed from the AU due to exceeding the 60- month CalWORKs time limit. Procedure: None. Impacts: None. References: • EAS 82-832.1. • ACLs No. 14-100, 15-18, 15-92. • ACIN I-02-16. • CFLs No. 14-15-60, 14-15-61. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by December 31, 2027. title: F. Pregnancy Based Assistance Unit
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Pregnancy Based Assistance Unit Number Page 41-500.F 1 of 3 Revision Date: June 1, 2025 Background: An Assistance Unit (AU) with a pregnant person and no other eligible child is referred to as an AU of one or a Pregnant Person Only (PPO) AU. A PPO may be eligible to receive CalWORKs and Pregnancy Special Need (PSN) payments, any time after medical verification of pregnancy is provided. Purpose: The purpose of this program guide section is to define the requirements to establishing a PPO AU. The purpose of this material revision is to incorporate the required referral to the Home Visiting Program (HVP) perinatal services for pregnant people receiving PSN payments. Policy: AU of One - PPO Applicant An AU of one can be established when a PPO meets all the following conditions: • Deprivation for the unborn is established. o Deprivation for the unborn child must be determined as if the unborn were a child (CalWORKs Program Guide [CPG] 41-400). o If deprivation does not exist, the application must be denied. • Medical verification of the pregnancy has been provided. o If unable to provide medical verification of pregnancy, the PPO will be allowed to submit a sworn statement, signed under penalty of perjury, to verify the pregnancy for aid and allow the PSN payment (CPG 44-200.C). o The sworn statement must include the PPO’s name, date of application, the declaration of pregnancy and the expected date of delivery. o If unable to provide a signed sworn statement, when NICE InContact is unavailable , a verbal attestation will be accepted, ensur ing the conditions under which the PPO is eligible are documented in case comments. o Medical verification of pregnancy must be submitted within 30 business days following submittal of the sworn statement, or verbal attestation, for benefits to continue. o Upon the expiration of the 30-day period, aid must continue if the PPO presents evidence of good-faith efforts to obtain and submit the medical verification. o If the medical verification is not submitted within 30 business days and there is no evidence of good faith efforts to comply, aid will be discontinued at the end of the month of the 30-day period with timely and adequate notice. o Should benefits continue beyond the end of the month of the 30-day period, an overpayment will be established for any subsequent aided months the PPO failed to comply. o Should circumstances preclude the PPO from obtaining the necessary documentation on their own, staff will assist the PPO, when it has been determined the PPO has made every attempt necessary to obtain the documentation, as outlined under CPG 22-000.B. • The pregnant person (and unborn child, when born, would be living with the PPO) would be eligible for CalWORKs. • The pregnant person cannot be included in another AU. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Pregnancy Based Assistance Unit Number Page 41-500.F 2 of 3 Example: a pregnant 17-year-old, living with their parents who are receiving CalWORKs for other children, is an eligible child on the parents' case, therefore, the 17-year-old cannot be aided in an AU of one. Eligibility for PPO A PPO may qualify for CalWORKs upon verification of their pregnancy, as defined above. Once a PPO is aided, they remain eligible based on the pregnancy until they become ineligible or the pregnancy ends. Note: Cal-Learn program eligibility for teens will be evaluated and a referral made if appropriate, as outlined under CPG 15-000. End of Pregnancy Reporting Requirements If the pregnancy ends prior to the esti mated delivery date, not resulting in the live birth of a child, the PPO is required to report verbally or in writing, within 30 days following the end of their pregnancy. Cash aid will discontinue, with timely and adequate notice, at the end of the month following the month in which the loss was reported. Prior to discontinuing aid, the PPO will be provided with information about, and referral to, mental health services, including, but not limited to, services provided by the Health and Human Services Agency, when appropriate. If the PPO fail s to report the loss within 30 days and benefits continued, overpayment s will be established for any subsequently aided months the PPO failed to comply. Pregnancy Special Need (PSN) In addition to the basic grant for the PPO meeting the criteria above, a PSN payment can be authorized for the duration of the pregnancy upon verification of pregnancy, as defined above. (CPG 44-200.C). A pregnant person receiving PSN payment is required to be referred to perinatal home visiting services administered by HVP, as outlined in CPG 10-009.A. Immediate Need and Homeless Assistance PPO who are unable to provide medical verification of pregnancy at application will be allowed to provide a sworn statement, or verbal attestation (when NICE inContact is unavailable), to be determined apparently eligible for Immediate Need and Homeless Assistance. Newborn Placed in Foster Care When a baby is born mid-period and immediately taken from the PPO by the Department of Child and Family Well Being (CFWB) and placed in Foster Care, the case will be discontinued mid -period as a county-initiated action at the end of the month in which the baby is placed in Foster Care , as the customer no longer has a CalWORKs eligible child in the home (CPG 44 -270.I.1.g), unless, CFWB recommends Family Reunification (FR) services. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Pregnancy Based Assistance Unit Number Page 41-500.F 3 of 3 Unaided Second Parent When the second parent of the unborn is living in the home at application, the application based on pregnancy is for the “family” (filing unit) that includes the pregnant person, the unborn, and the second parent. The second parent is excluded from the AU by law until the baby is born (CPG 41-500.E). The second parent’s income and property are considered in the eligibility and grant determination. Adding the Newborn and the Second Parent of the Newborn to the AU Upon notification of the birth of the child, eligibility for the newborn and second parent, if applicable, must be established prior to adding the newborn and the second parent to the AU. Refer to the following sections under CPG 44-270.H for additional information: • Newborns. • Adding the Newborn and the Second Parent to the PPO Case. Procedure: None. Program Impacts: Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) and Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program (TCVAP) RCA and TCVAP programs follow CalWORKs administrative rules with certain exceptions. CalWORKs program regulations apply to financial eligibility and payments for the RCA program, unless specifically superseded by RCA regulations. Unless otherwise provided, TCVAP customers will be provided cash assistance under the same conditions and to the same extent as the RCA program. Although RCA and TCVAP are intended for families without children, pregnant applicants, with no other eligible children, are eligible to apply for the CalWORKs program at any time during their pregnancy and are subject to the same medical verification requirements as CalWORKs customers. General Relief Persons in their first trimester of pregnancy will no longer be eligible to General Relief because they will now have linkage to CalWORKs (General Relief Program Guide 90-500.2.M). References: • Eligibility Assistance Standards (EAS) 44-211.6, 82-836. • All County Letters (ACLs) No. 14-04, 15-38, 21-134, 21-140, 23-83. • All-County Information Notices (ACINs) No. I-03-20, I-16-20. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by June 30, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: G. Identification of Persons for Claiming Financial Participation
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Identification of Persons for Claiming Financial Participation Number Page 41-500.G 1 of 2 Revision Date: December 1, 2024 Background: Once financial eligibility has been determined and a payment is to be issued, an evaluation must be made to determine whether the persons in the Assistance Unit (AU) are to be paid as federally eligible persons or essential persons. Purpose: The purpose of this section is t o define the Federal Financial Participation (FFP) category for each person in the AU. This material revision is due to sunset review. No policy or procedure changes have been made. Policy Determine Assistance Unit Members Claiming Status If an AU is determined to be financially eligible and an aid payment is to be issued, determine whether FFP is available for each person in the AU. For purposes of determining FFP, customers are categorized into two groups: • Federally eligible persons. • Essential persons. The following is a description of the categories of persons who must be included in each group. Federally Eligible Persons • Children. All children are federally eligible who are deprived of any parental support and care due to a parent’s: o Death. o Incapacity. o Continued absence. o Unemployment (when the parent meets federal eligibility conditions). • Adults. An adult in the AU is federally eligible when the adult is any of the following: o The caretaker relative of a federally eligible child, or of a child who is receiving Supplemental Security Income/State Supplementary Payment (SSI/SSP). o The second parent of a federally eligible child, or of a child who is receiving SSI/SSP. o The needy stepparent or California domestic partner of a parent of a federally eligible child, when the child’s parent in the home is incapacitated. • Pregnant Person. A person who meets all the following conditions is federally eligible: o Has no federally eligible children. o Has provided medical verification of the pregnancy. o Whose child, if born, and living with the previously pregnant parent would be federally eligible for aid in the month of payment. and is either: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Identification of Persons for Claiming Financial Participation Number Page 41-500.G 2 of 2 o Under the age of 19 and has not obtained a high school diploma or its equivalent. o The pregnancy has reached the three -month period (last trimester of pregnancy) immediately before the month of anticipated birth. If the child is born prior to the originally estimated date of birth, the anticipated month of birth is changed to the month in which the birth occurred, and federal financial participation is retroactively available for the three -month period prior to the month of birth. Essential Persons An essential person is a stepparent, California domestic partner of a parent or Alternately Sentenced Prisoner (ASP) who is not an otherwise federally eligible person and who is any of the following: • Related to a child determined to be federally eligible. • Related to a child who is either: o Receiving SSI/SSP. o Employment Services sanctioned but would otherwise be a federally eligible child. Procedure: None. Program Impacts: None. References: Eligibility and Assistance Standards (EAS) 44-209. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by December 31, 2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: H. Minor Parent Assistance Unit
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Minor Parent Assistance Unit Number Page 41-500.H 1 of 3 Revision Date: December 1, 2024 Background: A minor parent is a pregnant or parenting minor under age 18 who has never been married. The minor parent must be residing in an adult -supervised living situation. The minor parent requirement is also applicable to a minor parent who is an undocumented noncitizen or receives Supplemental Security Income/State Supplementary Payment (SSI/SSP) benefits. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to define the minor parent requirements. This material revision is due to sunset review. No policy or procedure changes have been made. Policy: Minor Parent Requirement To meet the minor parent (residence) requirement the minor parent must live with one of the following: • A senior parent. • A legal guardian. • An adult relative (a relative age 18 or older who is within the degree of relationship specified for caretaker relatives. • In a licensed home (a state licensed adult-supervised supportive living arrangement, which includes a group home or a maternity home). When a minor parent does not live in an appropriate living situation or meet one of the exceptions listed below, the minor parent and/or the minor parent’s Assistance Unit (AU) is ineligible for CalWORKs. If two or more sibling minor parents live with their unaided senior parent, a separate eligibility determination must be made for each minor parent. If both unmarried minor parents of the child live together, then each minor parent must be living in an appropriate adult -supervised living arrangement or meet one of the specified exceptions. If only one of the minor parents meets this condition of eligibility, only that minor parent and the child are aided. The minor parent who does not meet the minor parent provisions is excluded from the AU. Any income from that minor parent is counted in the budgeting process as a non-AU member. Exemptions to Minor Parent Requirements The minor parent and their dependent child are exempt from the minor parent requirement when any of the following conditions exist (an exception must exist for each senior parent): • Deceased. • Whereabouts Unknown. • Not allowed to Live in Home. • Health/Safety. • Live Apart for 12 Months. • Emancipation. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Minor Parent Assistance Unit Number Page 41-500.H 2 of 3 Minor Parent Claiming an Exemption When a minor parent claims to have an exemption take all the following actions: • Verify the exemption. • Grant CalWORKs if all other eligibility conditions are met. • Make a referral to the Department of Child and Family Well Being (CFWB) - Minor Parent Services (unless the minor is emancipated) - CFWB will complete assessments within 30 days of the referral (the referral should state that this is a minor parent investigation). Minor Parent Eligibility Determination When a minor parent is eligible to be included in their own AU, it is not necessary that the senior parent be present at the application/annual redetermination interview. It is the minor parent’s responsibility to complete the required forms and provide all other necessary information. All minor parents are required to complete a CW 25 - Supplemental Statement of Facts - Minor Parent and a SAR 23 - Supplement to the Statement of Facts during any of the following: • Application. • Annual redetermination. • When the minor has been living in a supervised setting and there is a change of address and/or living arrangement. Aid will be denied or discontinued when there is a failure or refusal to complete and return the CW 25 or SAR 23 after timely notification. Minor Parent Who Claims a Risk When a minor parent alleges that living with a senior parent/legal guardian will jeopardize the physical or emotional health or safety of themselves or their child, a referral must be made to CFWB to have the allegation supported. Also, staff must contact the CFWB Child Abuse Hotline at (858) 560-2191, or the State of California toll free number at (800) 344-6000 to report the safety concern. Refer to HHSA Chapter: Policy, Strategy and Program Development No. HHSA-H-1 on how to report suspected child abuse/neglect: http://insite.sdcounty.ca.gov/hhsa/Misc%20Policies/Child%20Abuse%20Reporting.pdf The referral must be documented in the case file. Minor Parent Risk Assessment The C FWB social worker will complete the risk assessment within 20 days . Immediate need risk assessments will be completed within 15 days. The CFWB portion of the CW 25 will be completed by the CFWB social worker. If the CFWB social worker determines that there is a safety issue, aid will be granted if all other eligibility conditions are met. If the CFWB social worker determines that there is not a safety issue, aid will be denied or discontinued if the minor parent does not meet the Minor Parent Requirement or other exception. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Minor Parent Assistance Unit Number Page 41-500.H 3 of 3 Responsible Adult as the Payee Unless the minor parent is exempt from the minor parent requirement, CalWORKs payments will be issued, on behalf of the minor parent, to the adult living in the home or to the licensed home. • Adult Refusal If the adult living in the home refuses to act as payee on behalf of the minor parent, the minor parent may be the payee. • Minor Parent Refusal or Failure to Cooperate If the minor parent refuses or fails to cooperate in obtaining verification of the adult's consent or refusal to act as payee on their behalf, the minor parent's AU is ineligible for CalWORKs. • Determination That Minor Parent Should Be Payee Whenever it is determined to be in the best interest of the minor parent and their child, the minor parent may be the payee of their case instead of the adult living in the home with the minor parent. Note: • Form CW 25A - Payee Agreement for Minor Parent is required as a condition of eligibility, when the minor parent lives in the home of a senior parent, legal guardian, or adult relative. • A CW 25A is not needed when the minor resides in an adult-supervised living arrangement. In this situation use the facility as the payee. Procedure: Questions & Answers - 41-500.H1 Minor Parent Requirement Refer to the document, located in Eligibility Essentials/CalWORKs site, for different examples of Minor Parent scenarios. Impacts: None. References: Eligibility and Assistance Standards (EAS) 89-201. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by December 31, 2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

If only one of the minor parents meets this condition of eligibility, only that minor parent and the child are aided. The minor parent who does not meet the minor parent provisions is excluded from the AU. Any income from that minor parent is counted in the budgeting process as a non-AU member. Exemptions to Minor Parent Requirements The minor parent and their dependent child are exempt from the minor parent requirement when any of the following conditions exist (an exception must exist for each senior parent): • Deceased. • Whereabouts Unknown. • Not allowed to Live in Home. • Health/Safety. • Live Apart for 12 Months. • Emancipation. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Minor Parent Assistance Unit Number Page 41-500.H 2 of 3 Minor Parent Claiming an Exemption When a minor parent claims to have an exemption take all the following actions: • Verify the exemption. • Grant CalWORKs if all other eligibility conditions are met. • Make a referral to the Department of Child and Family Well Being (CFWB) - Minor Parent Services (unless the minor is emancipated) - CFWB will complete assessments within 30 days of the referral (the referral should state that this is a minor parent investigation). Minor Parent Eligibility Determination When a minor parent is eligible to be included in their own AU, it is not necessary that the senior parent be present at the application/annual redetermination interview. It is the minor parent’s responsibility to complete the required forms and provide all other necessary information. All minor parents are required to complete a CW 25 - Supplemental Statement of Facts - Minor Parent and a SAR 23 - Supplement to the Statement of Facts during any of the following: • Application. • Annual redetermination. • When the minor has been living in a supervised setting and there is a change of address and/or living arrangement. Aid will be denied or discontinued when there is a failure or refusal to complete and return the CW 25 or SAR 23 after timely notification. title: I. Senior Parent Income
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Senior Parent Income Number Page 41-500.I 1 of 3 Revision Date: December 1, 2024 Background: The income and needs of the Senior Parents (SP) are to be applied in all income eligibility determinations, including the applicant/recipient income tests, as well as budget computations. Purpose: The purpose of this section is t o define the SP income requirements. This material revision is due to sunset review, and to update the examples with current Earned Income Disregard and Maximum Aid Payment (MAP) amounts. No policy or procedure changes have been made. Policy SP Income In cases where a Minor Parent (MP) lives with their parent(s), the income and needs of the SP must be considered: • The MP is to have their aid payment calculated using existing income and computation rules. • The SP’s income must be counted when determining the eligibility and aid payment for the MP’s Assistance Unit (AU). Ineligible MP When the SP’s income causes the MP’s AU to be ineligible, the MP’s case is denied/discontinued. All the MP’s income is considered available to the MP’s AU. Example of Ineligible MP AU Due to Excess SP Income • The persons residing together and receiving aid are the SP, a minor child, the MP and the MP’s child. The SP earnings are $3,500.00, which is the family’s only income. The family is nonexempt. • The eligibility/grant computation is as follows: $3,500.00 Gross Family Earned Income - 600.00 $600 Income Disregard $2,900.00 Nonexempt Earnings - $1,450.00 50% Earned Income Disregard $1,450.00 Total Net Nonexempt Income (round down) $ 1,416.00 MAP for an AU of 4 - 1,450.00 Total Net Nonexempt Income $ -0- Grant (AU ineligible) SP/MP Eligibility When considering a SP’s income results in the eligibility of the minor and the minor is either eligible to be included in their own AU or is eligible to be included in the SP’s AU, the SP’s income is considered, and the AU’s grant amount is: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Senior Parent Income Number Page 41-500.I 2 of 3 • The lesser of the potential grant amount of the MP’s AU MAP. • Plus any special needs for the MP’s AU less any overpayment adjustment. Example of Minor in Own AU (SP Excluded) • The persons residing together are the SP, the MP and the MP’s child. The SP is not in the AU. The SP earns $1,025.00. The MP has no income. The family is nonexempt. • The eligibility/grant computation is as follows: $1,025.00 Gross Family Earned Income - 600.00 $600 Income Disregard $ 425.00 Nonexempt Earnings - 212.50 50% Earned Income Disregard $ 212.00 Total Net Nonexempt Income (round down) $1,175.00 MAP for an AU of 3 - 212.00 Total Net Nonexempt Income $ 963.00 Potential Grant $ 930.00 MAP for an AU of 2 $ 930.00 Actual Grant Amount (lesser of potential grant or AU MAP) Example of MP in SP(s) AU • MP lives with both parents. title: A. Age Requirements and Pregnant-Parenting Teens
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Age Requirements and Pregnant/Parenting Teens Number Page 42-100.A 1 of 5 Revision Date: April 1, 2023 Background: Teens who receive aid as a dependent child and have no children of their own remain eligible for aid if they meet the education/training requirements that must be completed by the teen’s 19th birthday. The age of all children in the Assistance Unit (AU) must be verified, before granting aid. Continuing eligibility must also be reviewed for pregnant/parenting teens when turning age 18. Purpose: The purpose of th is section is to provide requirements for child age eligibility and eligibility for pregnant/parenting teens who turn age 18 years of age. This material revision is to reformat this section and to remove duplicate or obsolete policies. There are no policy or procedure changes. This revision also combines CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 42-100.B Pregnant and/or Parenting Teens and CPG 42-100.C Evidence of Age into this section, creating one singular section. Sections CPG 42-100.B CPG 42-100.C become obsolete with the issuance of this material. Policy: Age Requirement A child meets the age requirement for CalWORKs until the child’s 18th birthday. Eligibility may extend into the child’s 18th year if they meet the exceptions as listed below. Evidence of Age Verification of age is a condition of eligibility. The age of all eligible children must be verified. Acceptable Verification includes the following: • Birth/Hospital certificate, physician/midwife’s birth record • Baptismal certificate or church record of baptism • Confirmation papers or church record of confirmation • Indian agency records (when applicable) • United States (U. S.) government records of immigration or naturalization • Adoption decree • Passport • State or federal census record (if the date of birth appears on the document) • Other forms of verification not shown on this list ( such as school records when the school requires proof of birth before the child is enrolled). The Family Resource Center manager must approve this verification • Entries in a family Bible or other genealogical record or memorandum of customer • A sworn statement of an adult (other than the customer) if this statement is based on the adult’s personal knowledge, which substantiate s the age of the customer. This statement, made under penalty of perjury, must recount the specific facts upon which the adult’s knowledge is based, not the adult’s personal belief • Customer’s sworn statement, made under penalty of perjury , verifying the age of their child(ren), when none of the above listed evidence is available ; the sworn statement is to be used only as a last resort County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Age Requirements and Pregnant/Parenting Teens Number Page 42-100.A 2 of 5 Refer to CPG 42-400.C6 section for follow-up actions Unacceptable Age Verification Any evidence listed above, which does not appear to be substantive or genuine , such as certificates that have been filled in by the customer or any evidence that appears to have been altered. Note: Altered documents are a basis for fraud referral. Case Documentation The cases will be coded with the type of evidence provided for each child in the AU. If the code is not listed in the automated system, Case Comments will be made indicating the type of evidence provided to establish age, the pertinent evidence contained in such document(s) and the date the documentation was reviewed. Continuing Eligibility for 18-Year-Old Child A child who is 18 may be eligible to CalWORKs if any of the following provisions apply: • The child is a full-time student (as defined by the school) in high school • The child has not completed high school, and the child is in either a vocational or technical training program (which cannot result in a college degree) In addition: • The child is expected to finish the school/training program before reaching 19 years old • This requirement cannot be met by correspondence course work • A student enrolled in a full-time program is considered attending on a full-time basis until enrollment is terminated by the school or the student • For a child in receipt of Kin -GAP, the child and placement agency must sign a mutual agreement (KG 1) prior to or within the month the child reaches age 18 Disability Criteria Eligible 18 -year-olds who attend school full -time, or vocational/technical train ing program, and are considered disabled under this criterion , will be eligible for CalWORKs benefits in their parent’s/caretaker relative’s case, until they complete the program, turn 19 , or stop attending school full-time, whichever occurs first. The 18-year-old is considered disabled if meeting any of the following disability criteria: • Currently receiving , or has received in the past , Supplemental Security Income /State Supplementary Payment (SSI/SSP) • Currently receiving , or has received in the pas t, services through a Regional Center Program pursuant to the Lanterman Act • Currently receiving, or has received in the past, services at school in accordance with their Individual Education Plan (IEP) or under/pursuant to Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act ( for example, a section 504 Plan or Section 504 Accommodation Plan) Disability Verification The child’s disability verification may include the following: • Social Security Administration Award letter County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Age Requirements and Pregnant/Parenting Teens Number Page 42-100.A 3 of 5 • Statement from the Regional Center or school • Copies of the child’s IEP or Section 504 Accommodation Plan/Section 504 Plan When a child’s disability cannot be verified by using the criteria described above, the parent/caretaker relative can provide independent verification , or authorize the county to obtain documentation, from a health care provider or a trained, qualified learning disabilities evaluation professional of a current or past disability. Ineligible 18-Year-Old An 18-year-old child becomes ineligible when the child: • Graduates or completes the requirements for graduation from high school* • Completes the vocational/technical training program* • Drops out of high school or training and does not enter a high school or training program that meets the above conditions • Will not graduate before turning 19 and there is no mental or physical disability condition • Becomes 19 years of age *When an 18 -year-old completes their graduation requirements before their 19th birthday, eligibility ends when the requirements are met, regardless of the date of the formal graduation ceremony. If there are any questions about the graduation date, the AU must provide verification from the school of the expected end date. Example: Child will be 19 on June 10th. The graduation requirements are met on May 30th. The graduation ceremony takes place on June 15th. The child must be discontinued at the end of May. If the graduation requirements were met on June 5th, the child would be discontinued at the end of June. Acceptable School and Training Programs • High School : Includes high schools, adult high schools and General Educational Development (GED) course work sponsored by a local high school or community college • Vocational/Technical: Includes business schools, cosmetology schools, vocational programs offered through the junior college system ( if the program does not lead to a college degree), and Job Corps o A Technical school is one that provides instruction in the practical industrial, mechanical arts, or applied sciences o A Vocational school is one that provides instruction intended to prepare the individual for a career, trade, or occupation. Correspondence course work does not meet this requirement Pregnant/Parenting Teens A teen who is pregnant or a custodial parent and who is aided in their parent/caretaker relative’s AU, in accordance with mandatory inclusion requirements, may choose one of the following: • Remain a dependent child in their parent/caretaker relative’s case after they turn 18, provided they continue to meet the educational or training requirements • Have their own AU established on the first day of the month following the month in which they turn 18 (unless they turn 18 on the first day of the month, in which case the change is effective on th at date) County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Age Requirements and Pregnant/Parenting Teens Number Page 42-100.A 4 of 5 Informing Requirement Notice CW 2103 Reminder for Teens Turning 18 Years Old must be sent to all pregnant /parenting teens up to 60 days before the teen turns 18 to inform them of the options. This notice also instructs the senior parents/caretakers to provide the notice to the teen approaching age 18. These teens must be informed that: • Their grants will increase in most cases (and the parent/caretaker’s grant will go down or stop) if they start their own AU • They do not have to move out of their parent/caretaker’s home to start their own AU • Their CalWORKs Time -on-Aid (TOA) clocks will not start to run until they leave the Cal-Learn Program, if applicable Seamless Determination of Eligibility The transition for pregnant/parenting teens to their own AU must be as seamless as possible. If a pregnant/parenting teen requests an AU of their own, to aid in the transition into their own AU and ensure that there is no break in aid, the following steps must begin up to 60 days before the teen’s 18th birthday: • A copy of the latest application (SAWS 1) for the family contained in the case in which the teen was aided will be obtained; this is to be used to establish the separate AU • An interview will be scheduled with the teen • The teen will not be required to furnish any documentation previously provided to the county o This could include but is not limited to birth certificate, social security number ( SSN), identification, pay verification, vehicle registration, benefit award letter, etc. o If required by regulation, a release of information will be obtained from the teen’s parent/caretaker relative to secure sensitive information (such as senior parent information on child suppor t, medical records, absent parent information, etc.) from the parent /caretaker relative’s case file for the teen’s case o Documentation that is public record , such as the teen’s birth certificate , does not require obtaining a release of information from the teen’s parent/caretaker relative This is not considered an application but a transfer of aid. If the teen does not complete the eligibility requirements to establish their own AU, their aid is to be continued from the case in which they were originally receiving assistance, without a break in aid. Transition Eligibility Requirements Certain eligibility criteria are necessary to process the teen into their own AU. Listed below are some additional requirements when processing these types of cases: • The teen is required to attend Orientation • The teen may be required to sign a dditional documents such as the rights and responsibilities, statement of facts (SOF), etc. • The teen will be required to fill out the child support referral forms (CW 2.1/CW 2.1Q) and attend an interview with the Local Child Support Agency (LCSA) • The teen must present a photo identification in-person, as described in CPG 40-100.A County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Age Requirements and Pregnant/Parenting Teens Number Page 42-100.A 5 of 5 Income And Resources The teen will be treated as a recipient rather than as an applicant. However, the teen’s income, if any, will be budgeted in accordance with the Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) regulations. Underpayment - Overpayment • Underpayment: An underpayment will be provided to any pregnant/parenting teen who had previously been aided as a dependent child and had a break in aid between being aided in their parent/caretaker relative’s case and establishing their own case • Overpayment: Payments made to a teen parent as head of their own AU will be offset against any existing cash aid overpayment that may have occurred on the teen’s case o These payments will not be used to offset any supportive service overpayment Non-Minor Dependents (NMD) Refer to CPG 40-183.B for eligibility criteria for NMD. Procedure: • Processing Guide 40 -100.E5 Birth Certificate Request, In -Person Identity Verification and Third- Party Payment Process • To determine if the child who is turning 18 -years-old is attending school full -time, or to verify the disability, verification will be obtained in accordance with CPG 22 -000.B Request for Verification and CPG 42-100.F 18-Year-Old Students Impacts: Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) and Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program (TCVAP) Regulations relating to financial eligibility and payments apply to RCA/TCVAP unless specifically superseded by RCA/TCVAP regulations. References: • Eligibility and Assistance Standards (EAS) 40-105.5(b), 40-109.3, 40-171.11, 42-101, 42-111, 42- 762.21, 82-820 • All County Letter (ACL) No. 01-77 • All County Information Notice (ACIN) No. I-71-02 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by April 30, 2026. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services
