title: B. Income Eligibility and Budgeting
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Income Eligibility and Budgeting Number Page 44-270.B 1 of 7 Revision Date: May 1, 2025 Background: Budgeting is the activity used to compute the aid payment for a Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) Payment Period for which eligibility exists using the net nonexempt income, that is reasonably anticipated to be received in the SAR payment period. Budgeting is an activity separate from the determination of eligibility. All eligibility factors, including income eligibility are considered on a prospective basis. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide instructions on income eligibility and budgeting determination. This material revision is due to sunset date review and to renumber this section from CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 44 -270.F to 44 -270.B. Section CPG 44-270.F becomes obsolete with the issuance of this revision . This revision also removes CalWIN terminology. No policy or procedure changes have been made. Policy: Prospective Budgeting and Reasonably Anticipated Income • Prospective Budgeting: The use of income that the customer anticipates with reasonable certainty will be received in the upcoming SAR Payment Period. • Reasonably Anticipated Income: The specific amount of income that is reasonably certain to be received in the SAR Payment Period as determined by the customer and staff. This applies to both earned and unearned income. If the amount of income that will be received or when it will be received is not known, then the income cannot be reasonably anticipated. Income that is uncertain will not be used in the eligibility determination. Since the budget is never reconciled with actual income, it is critical for staff to obtain the necessary income verifications and enter detailed journal entries to document the determination of reasonably anticipated income. Income Eligibility at Initial Application The Assistance Unit ( AU) must first establish initial income eligibility to CalWORKs by passing the Applicant Test using the application month’s actual income, per CPG 44-100.A: • If the AU passes the Applicant Test, staff will determine the benefit amount for each month of the semi-annual period using reasonably anticipated income. • If the AU does not pass the Applicant Test but staff determines there may be eligibility within 60 days of the application date, another Applicant Test will be completed using the second month’s reasonably anticipated income. If the AU is eligible, CalWORKs will be approved effective the first of the month following the application month. See CPG 44-300.C regarding the beginning date of aid (BDA). Reminder: Cash aid received from another state is considered unearned income and will be used along with other actual and anticipated income to determine if the AU passes the Applicant Test. Staff will only budget cash aid from another state in the month(s) it is received and/or anticipated to be received. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Income Eligibility and Budgeting Number Page 44-270.B 2 of 7 Income Changes Prior to the Approval of Aid Applicants are required to report changes that affect their eligibility within five calendar days, per CPG 40-100.A. When there is a change in income that occurs during the initial application process prior to the approval of benefits, staff must consider the new information when determining eligibility to aid. If CalWORKs has not yet been approved, the new information must be considered regardless of whether the change occurred after the date of the initial interview. If a change in income occurs after CalWORKs has been approved, the AU will not be required to report the new information mid -period unless the total household income exceeds the Income Reporting Threshold (IRT). See CPG 44-270.C and 44-270.H for mandatory and voluntary mid-period reports. Continuing Income Eligibility Following the initial approval, continuing income eligibility will be determined using prospective budgeting and reasonably anticipated income based on information reported by the AU. It is critical for staff to enter a detailed journal entry regarding how income was evaluated and used (or not used) in the benefit determination. The journal entry must document any anticipated changes in income, including unstable income that the AU cannot reasonably anticipate will be received in the upcoming SAR Payment Period. Mid-Period Reports For income changes reported mid-period, staff will use the current month’s income (the month in which the change was reported) and any anticipated changes to determine if any mid-period action is required. See CPG 44-270.C for mandatory reports of income exceeding the IRT and CPG 44 -270.H for voluntarily reported income changes that result in an increase in benefits. SAR 7 – Eligibility Status Report and Annual Redetermination Reports Except for income verification at annual redetermination, AUs are required to provide information for the Data Month and to report any anticipated changes for the upcoming six months. Information for the Data Month is considered reasonably anticipated and will be used in the budget calculation, unless a change for the upcoming SAR Payment Period is anticipated. For income verification at annual redetermination refer to the section below. If there is no conflicting information, staff will accept the income and anticipated changes reported on the SAR 7 and at annual redetermination and use the information to determine benefits for the next SAR Payment Period. Income Verification at Annual Redetermination The AUs are required to provide verification of any income received during the 30 days prior to submission of the AU’s annual redetermination. There is no defined date or date range for submission under this provision. Staff must determine the relevant 30 -day period based on when the AU submits their annual redetermination or when a request for income verification is made using the CW 2200 Request for Verification form. This approach accounts for the various timeframes in which an AU may submit a complete annual redetermination , including verification of income, or when staff requests County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Income Eligibility and Budgeting Number Page 44-270.B 3 of 7 additional income verification if required and not originally submitted by the AU with their annual redetermination. Income verification must not be requested when the income is not reasonably expected to continue and will not be used to determine eligibility for the upcoming payment period. Verification of income received in the 30 days prior to submission of a n AU’s annual redetermination is not required if all the following apply: • The income source has stopped (job loss) or is not reasonably anticipated to continue. • The loss of income is not questionable. Note: The change to the 30-day period only applies to annual redetermination. There are no changes to income verification requirements at initial application, SAR 7, or at any other time during the certification period. Requesting Income Verification at Annual Redetermination The CW 2200 is the required form to use for requesting verification. Verification is not limited to a specific type and any verification that satisfies the verification requirement is acceptable. As a last resort, a sworn statement may be accepted as income verification when all other efforts to obtain sources of income verification have been exhausted. If complete income verification is not submitted with the annual redetermination, staff must send the CW 2200 to request verification of income received. When using the CW 2200, staff is required to list the specific date range for which the income verification is being requested to comply with adequate noticing requirements. To fulfill this requirement, staff must request income verification for the 30 days prior to the date listed on the CW 2200. If the c ustomer returns the CW 2200 with income verification that is outside of the 30 -day period listed on the form, but is sufficient for determining eligibility, staff must accept the verification. This rule is especially important when granting good cause because the request for verification may be much later than the date of the original submission of the annual redetermination. Request for Verifications that Cross Calendar Months The AU is required to provide verification of income received during the 30 days prior to submission of the AU’s annual redetermination or the 30 days prior to the date listed on the CW 2200. However, this 30-day period may not always fall within a calendar month. Therefore, the AU is only required to provide income verification for a specific calendar month when it is applicable to their case circumstances. Depending on when the AU submits their annual redetermination or when a request for verification is sent to an AU, the AU may provide income verification that crosses one or more calendar months. To determine the appropriate monthly income amount when income verification crosses calendar months, staff must convert the income to a monthly average using the weekly, bi - weekly, or semi-monthly conversion factors (refer to the Using Conversion Factors section below). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Income Eligibility and Budgeting Number Page 44-270.B 4 of 7 Rules for Anticipating Income • New Income: Income from a new source will only be considered reasonably anticipated if all the following apply: 1. The AU verifies that the income has been or will be approved or authorized within the upcoming SAR period, or the AU is otherwise reasonably certain that the income will be received within the SAR period. 2. The anticipated amount of the income is known and verified, or the AU is otherwise reasonably certain of the amount of the income. 3. The start date of the income is known and verified, or the AU is otherwise reasonably certain of the start date of the income. If the AU anticipates receiving income in the upcoming SAR Payment Period but does not have reasonable certainty of the dates and/or amounts expected to be received, the income cannot be considered reasonably anticipated and will not be used in the benefit determination for the upcoming SAR Payment Period. Unemployment Insurance Benefits (UIB) may not be reasonably anticipated based only on current claim information from the Employment Development Department (EDD) Real-Time Match, regardless if there are no issues to be resolved. Additional information, such as an Income Eligibility Verification System ( IEVS) report, is needed to determine whether any UIB income has actually been issued. The start date must be known and verified in order for the UIB income to be reasonably anticipated for the SAR Payment Period. • Fluctuating Income: When the AU’s monthly income fluctuates or the AU expects that the income received in the Data Month will change during the upcoming SAR Payment Period, staff must attempt to determine what amount of income is reasonably expected to be received. Only the income that the AU reasonably anticipates will be received during the upcoming SAR Payment Period may be used in the benefit determination. If the AU states that the Data Month income is not typical, explains why, and provides a reasonable estimate of future income, staff may budget the estimated income unless there is conflicting information. If the AU cannot anticipate an amount or if it is uncertain whether the income will be received in the upcoming SAR Payment Period, then no income can be reasonably anticipated or used in the benefit determination. The determination that income is too uncertain to anticipate must be done on a case-by-case basis. Staff must follow-up with the AU to determine what amount, if any, can be reasonably anticipated and document in a journal entry the basis for the amount agreed upon by the AU and staff. Refer to the Budgeting Fluctuating Income section below for additional information. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Income Eligibility and Budgeting Number Page 44-270.B 5 of 7 • Changing Income: If the AU reports an upcoming change or discontinuance in income but is uncertain when the change will take place or by how much the income will change, staff cannot reasonably anticipate this change and will continue to use the current income information in the benefit determination. Staff will advise the AU to report when the income actually changes or discontinues. Refer to the Budgeting Income That Stops or Starts Mid -Period section below for additional information. Using Conversion Factors Income that is received on a weekly or biweekly basis must be converted to a monthly amount if it is anticipated to be received in the upcoming SAR Payment Period. The income will be converted as follows: • Weekly Income: Add the four (or five) weekly checks together and divide by four (or five) to get an average weekly amount. Multiply this amount by 4.33. • Biweekly Income: Add the two (or three) biweekly checks together and divide by two (or three) to get an average weekly amount. Multiply this amount by 2.167. Each paycheck does not need to be the same amount . However, the AU must anticipate that their monthly income will continue at that level in order to convert the income into a monthly average. Note: If the income fluctuates and the AU cannot reasonably anticipate that their Data Month income will continue at the same amount, the weekly and biweekly conversion factors may not be used. Budgeting Stable Income When an AU has stable monthly income and does not expect any changes in the upcoming SAR Payment Period, the income reported at initial application, on the SAR 7, or at annual redetermination will be used in the benefit determination for the next SAR Payment Period. The conversion factors described under the Using Conversion Factors section will be used for income received on a weekly or biweekly basis. Budgeting Fluctuating Income When the AU anticipates its income for the upcoming SAR Payment Period will fluctuate from what was received in the Data Month, staff may use the following guidelines to determine what income amount can be reasonably anticipated: • Consider any changes in income from the Data Month that the AU reasonably anticipates for the upcoming SAR Payment Period. • Use the Data Month income until the AU reports a reasonably anticipated change. • Assist the AU in determining the amount of income that can be reasonably anticipated, including contacting the employer or other third party when a signed authorization for release of information is provided by the AU. • Consider past income from the previous SAR Payment Period (or comparable season if income fluctuates seasonally) if no third-party verification is available and no income changes have occurred or are anticipated. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Income Eligibility and Budgeting Number Page 44-270.B 6 of 7 If the AU reports their income fluctuates so much each month that no amount can be reasonably anticipated, and there are some months when no income is received, then no income would be budgeted in the benefit determination unless there is conflicting information. If information on the SAR 7 is unclear or questionable and the AU refuses to assist in providing required information or fails to provide information necessary to determine continuing eligibility, CalWORKs may be discontinued with timely and adequate notice. Note: If the AU is attempting to cooperate to the best of their ability but is unable to provide necessary information, the AU will not be considered “failing to cooperate” and CalWORKs cannot be discontinued for that reason. Budgeting Contract Income CalWORKs does not have special rules for budgeting annual contract/self-employment income. When an AU receives its annual income in a period shorter than one year, staff will budget the contract income as follows: If the AU receives... Then the contract income will be... CalWORKs and CalFresh averaged over 12 months and budgeted in accordance with the CalFresh rules explained in CFPG 63-251.4. CalWORKs only budgeted in accordance with the prospective budgeting and reasonably anticipated income rules. Note: Contract income that is not a household’s annual income and is not paid on an hourly or piecework basis will be prorated over the period that the income is intended to cover. Budgeting Income that Stops or Starts Mid-Period Income that the AU anticipates will begin or end in one of the months of the upcoming SAR Payment Period will only be counted in the month(s) that the income is reasonably anticipated to be received. Income that is beginning or ending will be treated differently depending on how certain the AU is that the income will begin or end: • If a customer currently has stable monthly income but has heard they may get laid off soon, staff will continue to budget the current income until additional information is known. Staff will instruct the customer to report when a lay -off notification is received or report in the month their income will actually decrease. • If a customer thinks they will be starting a new job in the next month or so but is not sure about the start date or hours, income from this new job cannot be reasonably anticipated and will not be used in the benefit determination. Staff will remind the customer of their responsibility to report within 10 days if the total household income exceeds their IRT ; or on the ir next SAR 7 or at annual redetermination if the income is not over their IRT. • If a customer is certain that their income will be ending or that new income will be starting in a certain month of the SAR Payment Period, staff will only budget the income for the months in which it is reasonably anticipated to be received. Staff will calculate two different grant amounts for the SAR Payment Period: One amount for the months in which the income will be received and one amount for the months in which the income will not be received. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Income Eligibility and Budgeting Number Page 44-270.B 7 of 7 Impacts: CalFresh Refer to CalFresh Program Guide 63-251 - Prospective Budgeting and Reasonably Anticipated Income. Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) and Trafficking, and Crime Victims Assistance Program (TCVAP) The RCA and TCVAP cash assistance programs follow the CalWORKs rules with certain exceptions. CalWORKs program regulations apply to financial eligibility and payments for the RCA program, unless specifically superseded by RCA regulations. Unless otherwise specified, TCVAP customers must be provided cash assistance under the same conditions, and to the same extent as the RCA program, per CPG 69-205.A and 70-100.A. Procedure: Desk Aid – Income Eligibility and Budgeting - Scenario Examples Refer to the desk aid, located in Eligibility Essentials, for income eligibility and budgeting examples. References: • Assembly Bill (AB) No. 6, 79. • Eligibility Assistance Standards (EAS) 40-181.2, 44-313. • Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 70-105. • All County Letters (ACLs) No. 12-25, 12-25 Errata, 19-10, 21-24. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by May 31, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Income Eligibility and Budgeting Number Page 44-270.B 1 of 7 Revision Date: May 1, 2025 Background: Budgeting is the activity used to compute the aid payment for a Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) Payment Period for which eligibility exists using the net nonexempt income, that is reasonably anticipated to be received in the SAR payment period. Budgeting is an activity separate from the determination of eligibility. All eligibility factors, including income eligibility are considered on a prospective basis. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide instructions on income eligibility and budgeting determination. This material revision is due to sunset date review and to renumber this section from CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 44 -270.F to 44 -270.B. Section CPG 44-270.F becomes obsolete with the issuance of this revision . This revision also removes CalWIN terminology. No policy or procedure changes have been made. Policy: Prospective Budgeting and Reasonably Anticipated Income • Prospective Budgeting: The use of income that the customer anticipates with reasonable certainty will be received in the upcoming SAR Payment Period. • Reasonably Anticipated Income: The specific amount of income that is reasonably certain to be received in the SAR Payment Period as determined by the customer and staff. This applies to both earned and unearned income. If the amount of income that will be received or when it will be received is not known, then the income cannot be reasonably anticipated. Income that is uncertain will not be used in the eligibility determination. Since the budget is never reconciled with actual income, it is critical for staff to obtain the necessary income verifications and enter detailed journal entries to document the determination of reasonably anticipated income. Income Eligibility at Initial Application The Assistance Unit ( AU) must first establish initial income eligibility to CalWORKs by passing the Applicant Test using the application month’s actual income, per CPG 44-100.A: • If the AU passes the Applicant Test, staff will determine the benefit amount for each month of the semi-annual period using reasonably anticipated income. • If the AU does not pass the Applicant Test but staff determines there may be eligibility within 60 days of the application date, another Applicant Test will be completed using the second month’s reasonably anticipated income. If the AU is eligible, CalWORKs will be approved effective the first of the month following the application month. See CPG 44-300.C regarding the beginning date of aid (BDA). Reminder: Cash aid received from another state is considered unearned income and will be used along with other actual and anticipated income to determine if the AU passes the Applicant Test. Staff will only budget cash aid from another state in the month(s) it is received and/or anticipated to be received. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Income Eligibility and Budgeting Number Page 44-270.B 2 of 7 Income Changes Prior to the Approval of Aid Applicants are required to report changes that affect their eligibility within five calendar days, per CPG 40-100.A. When there is a change in income that occurs during the initial application process prior to the approval of benefits, staff must consider the new information when determining eligibility to aid. If CalWORKs has not yet been approved, the new information must be considered regardless of whether the change occurred after the date of the initial interview. If a change in income occurs after CalWORKs has been approved, the AU will not be required to report the new information mid -period unless the total household income exceeds the Income Reporting Threshold (IRT). See CPG 44-270.C and 44-270.H for mandatory and voluntary mid-period reports. Continuing Income Eligibility Following the initial approval, cont

title: C. Mandatory Mid-Period Reports
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Mandatory Mid-Period Reports Number Page 44-270.C 1 of 3 Revision Date: July 1, 2024 Background: Under the Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) system, customers are required to report only certain changes mid-period. Purpose: This section provides instructions for evaluating any mandatory reported changes and if any mid-period action is required. The purpose of this revision is to incorporate changes to the continuing Financial Eligibility Test regulations. If the Net Non -Exempt Income (NNI), instead of the gross income, is reasonably anticipated to continue and exceeds the Tier 2 Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) , the Assistance Unit ( AU) is financially ineligible. This section is also being renumbered from CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 44-270.G to CPG 44-270.C. Section CPG 44-270.G becomes obsolete with the issuance of this material. Policy: Mandatory Reporting All CalWORKs customers are required to report the following changes within 10 calendar days of the date the change becomes known to the AU: • When income exceeds the IRT. • When an AU member has a change in fleeing felon status. • Violations of conditions of probation or parole. • Residence/address changes. AUs that include a pregnant person are required to report when a pregnancy ends prior to the estimated delivery date, not resulting in the birth of a child within 30 calendar days. This is a requirement for both Pregnant Person Only (PPO) AUs and AUs that include a pregnant person with other eligible children. Note: If the AU reports mid -period that income exceeds the IRT due to income of a new household member, then no mid-period action will be taken to decrease or discontinue CalWORKs since the report of income over IRT is based on a new household member and a voluntary report. Mid-period reports may be made in writing , by fax, online via email, by phone, or in -person to designated staff or at a Family Resource Center (FRC). Customers may also provide a Mid-Period Status Report (SAR 3) to report a change. Income Reporting Threshold The IRT is an income level that informs the AU when they are mandated to make a mid -period report of an increase in income. AUs with only unearned income, including disability-based unearned income, are not required to report mid-period when their income exceeds the IRT. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Mandatory Mid-Period Reports Number Page 44-270.C 2 of 3 AUs with earned income are required to report within 10 days when their total combined gross monthly income (earned and unearned) of all the members in the Family Maximum Aid Payment (MAP) exceeds the IRT. Income that must be reported includes: • Income for penalized, excluded, and timed-out individuals. • Income of individuals who are not in the AU but are included in the determination of eligibility. If the AU receives: • Earned income only or a combination of earned and unearned income, then the AU is required to report within 10 days when their household’s total income exceeds the IRT. • Unearned income only or no income, then the AU is required to report within 10 days only if they receive new earnings that would exceed the IRT when combined with other household income. Note: New unearned income is not required to be reported mid-period. Failure to make a timely report of income that exceeds the IRT may result in an overpayment per CalWORKs Program Guide ( CPG) 44-350.A Overpayment. If the failure to report income was done knowingly and intentionally, the customer may be subject to fraud prosecution, financial penalties, and potential disqualification from CalWORKs, as described in CPG 44-350.J Intentional Program Violation (IPV). Nonrecurring lump sum income is treated as property in the month received and for any subsequent months per CPG 44-100.A Income Definitions. Customers are not required to report mid-period when nonrecurring lump sum income is received. Two-Tiered IRT System The CalWORKs IRT will vary for each family due to the two-tiered system, which is used for both Annual Reporting/Child Only (AR/CO) and SAR AUs. A report of income over the IRT may result in either a mid-period decrease or discontinuance of CalWORKs. Effective June 1, 2020, the CalWORKs IRT is the lesser of the following: • Tier 1: 55% of the Federal Poverty Level ( FPL) for a family of three (regardless of the actual AU size) plus the amount of gross income last used in the CalWORKs benefit determination. • Tier 2: 130% of the FPL – The level likely to make a household ineligible for CalFresh benefits based on the household size: o The CalWORKs cases may remain open with a zero-basic-grant (ZBG), refer to CPG 44-300.D, if the AU’s NNI remains below the Tier 2 IRT amount. ZBG cases remain eligible for supportive services and/or CalWORKs special needs. o If the reasonably anticipated NNI will continue to exceed the Tier 2 IRT for the remainder of the payment period, the AU is determined to be financially ineligible and is to be discontinued at the end of the month in which timely and adequate notice can be provided. Refer to CPG 45-200 Resources and Desk Aids - CalWORKs Assistance Standards Chart for current IRT levels. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Mandatory Mid-Period Reports Number Page 44-270.C 3 of 3 Fleeing Felon Status and Parole/Probation Violations Customers are required to report within 10 days when it becomes known that a member of the AU: • Becomes a fleeing felon. • Violates a condition of parole or probation. Procedure: CalWORKs Processing Guide 44-270.C1. Impacts: None References: • ACL No. 12-25, 13-109, 14-100, 15-92, 19-76, 19-76E, 21-140, 23-96. • ACIN No. I-02-16. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by July 31, 2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: H. Voluntary Mid-Period Reports
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageVoluntary Mid-Period Reports 44-270.H 1 of 8 Revision Date: July 1, 2020 Background: State regulations state customers may voluntarily report changes any time. A voluntary report can never be late and there is no requirement for an Assistance Unit (AU) to report a voluntary change within 10 days. If the change is verified mid-period, the customer is not required to report the change again. However, gross income received in the Data Month must still be reported and verified. Mid-period reports may be made in writing, fax, online, email, by phone, in-person or on a Mid-Period Status Report. Purpose: This section is being revised to clarify the mid-period reporting rules for adding a newborn and second parent to an existing Pregnant Person Only (PPO) case. Policy: Action on Voluntary Reports Take action mid-period for a voluntary report when: •Verification has been provided that results in an increase in CalWORKs benefits; or •There is a request for discontinuance for an individual or entire AU. When mid-period action is not required or verification for a potential increase in benefits has not been received: •Changes will be entered in the data system for follow-up at the next SAR 7 or annual redetermination, whichever comes first. •A “No Change” Notice of Action (NOA) will be issued to the AU. The budget calculation must be included on the CalWORKs “No Change” NOA for the AU to see how the County determined that the reported change did not result in a mid-period increase in benefits. Establishing Effective Date of Benefit Increase The effective date of the increase in CalWORKs is based on when the change is reported and not when the change actually occurred. This is determined based on the type of change reported: If the voluntary report is a: •Decrease in income, CalWORKs benefits will increase effective the first of the month in which the change occurred or is reported, whichever is later. •New household member, CalWORKs benefits will increase the first of the month following the report of the change. Example 1: Verification received within 10-day timeframe Scenario An AU is in the January - June Payment Period (Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) Cycle 1). Mom voluntarily reports a decrease in income on March 25th. A request for verification was sent on March 28th with a 10-day due date of April 7th. The verification is provided timely on April 3rd. Outcome The grant will be recalculated for March – June and a supplemental payment will be issued for March no later than April 13th. The AU will also be notified of any changes in the Income Reporting Threshold (IRT). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageVoluntary Mid-Period Reports 44-270.H 2 of 8 Example 2: Verification received after 10-day timeframe Scenario Same scenario as Example 1 above; however, the requested verification is not received until April 10th after the 10-day due date. Outcome Since the verification was provided after the 10-day timeframe, April 10 th will be considered as the new report date and no supplemental payment will be issued for March. Benefits will be recalculated for April – June and a supplemental payment will be issued for April. The AU will also be notified of any changes in IRT. Example 3: Submit Month change reported on SAR 7 Scenario An AU is in the January - June Payment Period (SAR Cycle 1). A timely May SAR 7 is submitted on June 4th. A report is made that the June income will be lower than previously anticipated, and that the income will continue at that lower level. On June 7th, acceptable verification is provided of the decreased income. Outcome Benefits will be recalculated for the month of June and a supplemental payment issued if eligible. Benefits for the new SAR Payment Period, July - December, will be reevaluated and timely notification of any changes in IRT will be provided. Example 4: Decreased income reported for one month only Scenario An AU is in the January-June Payment Period (SAR Cycle 1). The current grant amount is based on the AU’s current earned income of $1,000/month. On March 25th, a report is made that two weeks of work were missed due to illness and the AU anticipates only receiving $500 for March. The regular monthly income of $1,000 will resume in April. Outcome Upon receiving timely verification of the decreased income, benefits will be recalculated for March only and a supplemental payment will be issued. Benefits for April, May, and June will remain at the previous level. Since the decrease in income for March was only temporary, the AU’s IRT will not be recalculated. Changes in Exempt and Non-Exempt Maximum Aid Payment (MAP) Status Mid-period action to change an AU’s exemption status will only be taken if the change will result in an increase to the CalWORKs grant. When the exempt MAP status is due to the receipt of certain disabilitybased income, a determination must be completed if CalWORKs will increase when using the new disability-based income together with the higher exempt MAP amount. If the change results in an overall decrease in CalWORKs, the MAP exemption status will remain unchanged and the lower MAP will be used until the next SAR Payment Period. Household Composition Changes If a change in household composition is voluntarily reported during the SAR Payment Period, midperiod action will be taken if the change results in an increase in benefits or if there is a request for discontinuance for an individual or the AU. The AU will continue to receive CalWORKs at their current level for the remaining months of the SAR Payment Period if the change results in a decrease in benefits, unless there is a change in eligibility due to other reasons. Verification must first be requested and evaluated, before benefits can be increased mid-period. The new individual must be eligible, and if added, must meet all linking and nonlinking eligibility factors before aid is authorized. When an AU voluntarily reports a new individual in the home: •First determine if the new individual, if added to the AU, would still meet all eligibility conditions County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageVoluntary Mid-Period Reports 44-270.H 3 of 8 •Then determine the effect the addition will have on the cash grant; if it would cause an increase or decrease to the grant amount, or if the addition would render the entire AU ineligible If the addition of the new individual would result in a(n): •Increase in aid but the new individual does not meet all eligibility conditions before aid is authorized, do not add the individual nor discontinue the existing AU mid-period •Decrease, add the new individual the first day of the next Payment Period, after all eligibility conditions have been met If the household does not report a new household member on the SAR 7 or at annual redetermination, and the addition of the individual would have resulted in a decrease in benefits, an overpayment will be established. AU Composition Due to Changes of Income Circumstances may change over time and this may result in a different AU composition mid-period, at SAR, or annual redetermination than the AU reported at the time of initial application. When the AU reports income in excess of the IRT in any month except the last month of the current payment period, the county will determine if the reported income is reasonably anticipated to continue and whether the AU's net nonexempt monthly income determined for the remainder of the current payment period will result in a lower grant amount or will exceed the income eligibility limits for CalWORKs. If the income is reasonably anticipated to continue and will result in a lower grant amount for the remainder of the payment period, the county will recalculate the AU’s grant amount for the remainder of the payment period. If the income is reasonably anticipated to continue to exceed the AU's income eligibility limits for the remainder of the payment period, the county will determine the AU financially ineligible and will discontinue the AU at the end of the month in which the AU first received the income that exceeded the AU's eligibility limits, with timely and adequate notice. When an AU is determined no longer financially eligible to CalWORKs due to a mandatory mid-period report of income over the CalWORKs limits, the county will discontinue the AU at the end of the month in which the AU first received the income that exceeded the AU's eligibility limits, with timely and adequate notice. If the income reported is not reasonably anticipated to continue, the report of income over the IRT will not affect ongoing benefits for the current payment period. When an AU reports income in excess of the IRT in the last month of the current payment period, the county will determine if the reported income is reasonably anticipated to continue. If the income will continue, the county will use that information together with the SAR 7 or SAWS 2 PLUS information to prospectively determine eligibility and cash aid amount for the next payment period. If the AU’s new income is reasonably anticipated to continue and will make the current AU ineligible, the county will determine if continued eligibility exists for any of the members of the current AU. Any change in deprivation reported on the SAR 7 or the SAWS 2 PLUS and any change in eligibility or the grant amount that results from the new AU shall also be effective the first day of the next payment period. Example 1: New household member reported mid-period Scenario An AU of 3, A Parent and two children, is in the January - June Payment Period (SAR Cycle 1). The AU has no income. In February, the parent voluntarily reports that the second parent has moved into the home and has income. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageVoluntary Mid-Period Reports 44-270.H 4 of 8 Outcome It was determined that adding the second parent to the AU will result in a decrease in benefits. A “No Change” NOA is sent to the AU and the information is noted as a Held Change for follow-up at the next SAR 7 or annual redetermination, whichever comes first. Example 2: Follow-up at SAR 7 Scenario Parent submits the May SAR 7 in June but does not report the second parent or that parent’s income on the SAR 7. The Human Services Specialist calls the parent regarding these omissions and the parent explains that the second parent left the home in April. Outcome Unless there is conflicting information, benefits for the upcoming SAR Payment Period (July - December) will continue to be calculated based on the AU of 3 with no income. The second parent’s three months in the home (February - April) will have no effect on the benefit level for this AU. Example 3: New household member results in Ineligibility Scenario An AU of 2, Parent and one child, are in the January-June Payment Period (SAR Cycle 1). In February, the parent voluntarily reports that the second parent moved into the home in February. The second parent has income. It was determined that adding the second parent to the AU will result in ineligibility to CalWORKs. Outcome No mid-period action will be taken and a CalWORKs “No Change” NOA, including the required budget, will be issued. The change will be noted in Held Change for followup at the next SAR 7 or at annual redetermination, whichever comes first. Medi-Cal will be evaluated for the second parent. CalWORKs will be discontinued effective June 30 th at the end of the SAR Payment Period after the second parent’s income is reported on the SAR 7 or redetermination. All household members will be evaluated for continuing eligibility to Medi-Cal. Request to Discontinue an AU/Optional Member An individual who left the home may request their own discontinuance from the AU. An optional AU member who no longer wants to receive CalWORKs may also request to be discontinued from the AU for their CalWORKs time clock to stop. Mid-period action will be taken to adjust benefits for the remaining AU members, per customer request, regardless of whether the AU had reported the change. Death of a Household Member There is no requirement for the AU to report that a household member is deceased until the next SAR or annual redetermination, whichever comes first. If a death of a household member is voluntarily reported by the AU or discovered through a third-party, county-initiated action must be taken to discontinue the deceased household member. When a death of a child is voluntarily reported, the child will continue to be included as a member of the AU in the month which the death occurred, and the following month (CPG 44-270.I). Newborns When the birth of a child is voluntarily reported mid-period and required verification has been provided, if adding the newborn to the AU will result in a(n): County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageVoluntary Mid-Period Reports 44-270.H 5 of 8 •Increase in aid; discontinue the pregnancy special need (PSN) payment at the end of the month. Add the newborn the first of the month following the report of the birth after PSN is discontinued. •Decrease or no change in aid; continue the PSN through the end of the payment period. The newborn will be added first month of the next SAR Payment Period after PSN ends. Example: Adding a newborn Scenario An AU of 2, pregnant Mom and her child, is in the January - June Payment Period (SAR Cycle 1). In February, Mom voluntarily reports that she gave birth in January. Outcome It was determined that adding the newborn will result in increase of aid. The newborn will be added to the AU effective March 1 st, pending required verification. PSN will be discontinued at the end of February. The newborn is deemed eligible to receive Medi-Cal effective January 1st, regardless of when verification is provided to add the newborn to the AU. Adding the Newborn and the Second Parent to the PPO Case For a PPO AU, if the second parent of the unborn child is living in the home, the second parent will be excluded from the AU until the child is born. If the second parent was not previously living in the home or was not included on the Statement of Facts at initial application, the second parent is required to complete the CW 8, interview, and provide all documentation/verifications. The newborn and second parent are treated distinctly, and a separate analysis may be required to determine how each would affect the grant for the existing AU. The newborn and second parent may be added to the case separately, when the circumstances allow, to maximize the cash aid. After all conditions of eligibility have been met and verification provided: •If adding the newborn to the existing AU results in a(n): oIncrease in cash aid, the newborn will be added the first of the month after the birth is reported; PSN will be discontinued at the end of the month in which the birth was reported (10-day notice is not required) oDecrease in cash aid, the newborn will be added the first day of the next SAR Payment Period; PSN will continue through the end of the current SAR Payment Period •If adding the second parent results in a(n): oIncrease in cash aid, the second parent will be added the first of the month after the birth is reported oDecrease in cash aid, the second parent will be added the first day of the next SAR Payment Period after the reported birth Notes: •Any income received by the second parent at application is considered when determining financial eligibility for the initial AU. Therefore, any income (under the AU’s IRT) received/reported by the second parent after the PPO case has been established is considered a voluntary mid-period report. All parents regardless of their age or marital status are responsible to the extent of their ability for the support and care of their children including an unborn child •When new household members are added to an existing AU, the AU is subject to the recipient financial eligibility test County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageVoluntary Mid-Period Reports 44-270.H 6 of 8 •If the addition results in a decrease and/or loss of deprivation, rendering the entire AU ineligible, the existing AU will continue unchanged until the end of the current payment period •Any change in eligibility or cash aid amount resulting from a change in deprivation will be effective the first day of the next SAR payment period Example 1: Second Parent in the Home at Application Scenario A PPO applying for CalWORKs. The second parent is in the home, employed parttime, working ten hours a week. CalWORKs is approved with unemployed parent deprivation. The SAR Payment Period is January through June. The income increased in February but remains under the AU’s IRT. Their child is born in March. The AU reports both changes in April. Outcome While both changes were reported in the same month, they need to be evaluated independently and only act on that which results in an increase to the cash aid. The newborn’s eligibility needs to be evaluated to determine linking (deprivation) and non-linking (financial status, etc.) factors and must look at whether the newborn is needy, thus a review of the new income. If the newborn maintains deprivation, and all other conditions of eligibility are met, the newborn may be added the first of the month following the reported birth. Then if adding the second parent would result in an increase to the cash aid, the second parent will also be added the first of the month following the reported birth, assuming all other conditions of eligibility are met. In this scenario, even though the change in income took place prior to the birth of the child, it occurred after the PPO AU was already established and under the IRT; therefore, the report is considered voluntary. As such, the income considered at application will be used when adding the newborn and second parent in determining the cash grant amount for the remainder of the payment period. As the change in income results in a decrease to the existing AU’s cash aid, the increased income will be deferred until the first of the following SAR payment period before taking action. Example 2: Second Parent Moves into the Home After the PPO is Established Scenario PPO AU approved with absent parent deprivation. The SAR payment period is January through June. The child was born in February. The second parent, employed part-time, moved into the home in March. The AU reports both changes in April. Outcome As deprivation has been established for the newborn, and all other conditions of eligibility are met for the AU, adding only the newborn would have a positive impact on the grant. In this scenario, because the second parent moved into the home after the PPO AU was already established, the newborn would be added mid-period while the second parent and the income would be added effective July 1, the first month of the following SAR payment period. After evaluating the second parent’s income and recalculating the cash grant for the remainder of the SAR payment period for an AU of three, it is determined that including the second parent’s income would cause a decrease in the grant, but it would not render the entire AU ineligible. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageVoluntary Mid-Period Reports 44-270.H 7 of 8 If adding the second parent and the income result in a decrease in cash aid for an AU of three, wait until the following SAR payment period before adding the second parent to the AU, assuming all eligibility conditions are met. Example 3: Employed Second Parent Moves into the Home After the PPO is Established Scenario PPO AU is granted in January with absent parent deprivation, and the SAR payment period is January through June. In April it was reported that the child was born in February, and the fully employed second parent moved into the home in March. Outcome Deprivation changes are not acted on mid-period. Therefore, each voluntary midperiod report must be determined separately and sequentially. Although deprivation existed at birth, the newborn no longer meets the financial eligibility criteria, as the income from the second parent exceeds the eligibility limit for an AU of three. As this results in a negative action to the case, the eligibility determination for the newborn and the second parent will be deferred until the following SAR payment period. The existing PPO AU maintains current eligibility, including the PSN payment, until the end of the current payment period. Had the birth been reported in February and the child added to the AU prior to the second parent going into the home, the AU of two would have remained eligible for the remainder of the SAR payment period. Combining AUs When a change in household composition results in combining separate AUs mid-period, a determination must be made if the change will result in an increase or decrease in aid for the separate AU. A comparison of the monthly CalWORKs grant of the combined AU to the total monthly grants of the separate AUs must be completed. If the monthly grant of the combined AU is: •Higher than the total month grants of the separate AUs, the AU will be combined effective the first of the month following the voluntary report. •Lower than the total monthly grants of the separate AUs, the AUs will be combined effective the first month of the next SAR Payment Period, after the change is reported on the SAR 7 or at the annual redetermination. If the two AUs have different SAR cycles, the AUs will be combined at the beginning of whichever SAR Payment Period comes first. Request for Special Need Payments When a customer voluntarily reports having a special need and verifications are provided, the special needs payment will begin effective the month that the request was made (if verification is received timely) and terminate at the end of the SAR Payment Period in which the special need is expected to end based on the verification. PSN may discontinue mid-period if adding the newborn will result in an increase to the CalWORKs grant. If the duration of the special need is: •Permanent, verification must be provided once per year, at annual redetermination or when the current verification expires. •Temporary, special need payments will be allowed through the end of the SAR Payment Period in which the special need is expected to end. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageVoluntary Mid-Period Reports 44-270.H 8 of 8 •Unknown, verification must be provided once per semi-annual period. sections.heading: 44-270Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR)
sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageVoluntary Mid-Period Reports 44-270.H 1 of 8 Revision Date: July 1, 2020 Background: State regulations state customers may voluntarily report changes any time. A voluntary report can never be late and there is no requirement for an Assistance Unit (AU) to report a voluntary change within 10 days. If the change is verified mid-period, the customer is not required to report the change again. However, gross income received in the Data Month must still be reported and verified. Mid-period reports may be made in writing, fax, online, email, by phone, in-person or on a Mid-Period Status Report. Purpose: This section is being revised to clarify the mid-period reporting rules for adding a newborn and second parent to an existing Pregnant Person Only (PPO) case. Policy: Action on Voluntary Reports Take action mid-period for a voluntary report when: •Verification has been provided that results in an increase in CalWORKs benefits; or •There is a request for discontinuance for an individual or entire AU. When mid-period action is not required or verification for a potential increase in benefits has not been received: •Changes will be entered in the data system for follow-up at the next SAR 7 or annual redetermination, whichever comes first. •A “No Change” Notice of Action (NOA) will be issued to the AU. The budget calculation must be included on the CalWORKs “No Change” NOA for the AU to see how the County determined that the reported change did not result in a mid-period increase in benefits. Establishing Effective Date of Benefit Increase The effective date of the increase in CalWORKs is based on when the change is reported and not when the change actually occurred. This is determined based on the type of change reported: If the voluntary report is a: •Decrease in income, CalWORKs benefits will increase effective the first of the month in which the change occurred or is reported, whichever is later. •New household member, CalWORKs benefits will increase the first of the month following the report of the change. Example 1: Verification received within 10-day timeframe Scenario An AU is in the January - June Payment Period (Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) Cycle 1). Mom voluntarily reports a decrease in income on March 25th. A request for verification was sent on March 28th with a 10-day due date of April 7th. The verification is provided timely on April 3rd. Outcome The grant will be recalculated for March – June and a supplemental payment will be issued for March no later than April 13th. The AU will also be notified of any changes in the Income Reporting Threshold (IRT). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number PageVoluntary Mid-Period Reports 44-270.H 2 of 8 Example 2: Verification received after 10-day timeframe Scenario Same scenario as Example 1 above; however, the requested verification is not received until April 10th after the 10-day due date. Outcome Since the verification was provided after the 10-day timeframe, April 10 th will be considered as the new report date and no supplemental payment will be issued for March. Benefits will be recalculated for April – June and a supplemental payment will be issued for April. The AU will also be notified of any changes in IRT. Example 3: Submit Month change reported on SAR 7 Scenario An AU is in the January - June Payment Period (SAR Cycle 1). A timely May SAR 7 is submitted on June 4th. A report is made that the June income will be lower than previously anticipated, and that the income will continue at that lower level. On June 7th, acceptable verification is provided of the decreased income. Outcome Benefits will be recalculated for the month of June and a supplemental payment issued if eligible. Benefits for the new SAR Payment Period, July - December, will be reevaluated and timely notification of any changes in IRT will be provided. Example 4:

title: I. County-Initiated Actions and Third Party Information
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page County-Initiated Actions and Third Party Information 44-270.I 1 of 3 Background: Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) and Annual Reporting/Child Only (AR/CO) rules require the County to take mid-period action on certain changes in eligibility, even if the action will result in a decrease or discontinuance of aid for the Assistance Unit (AU). MPP 44-316.33; ACL 12-25 and 12-49 Policy: 44-270.I.1 County-Initiated Actions The following requires mid-period action, depending if SAR or AR/CO: SAR AR/CO a. An adult in the AU reaches their CalWORKs time limit (CPG 15-100.A) X b. A sanction or financial penalty is imposed on an individual in the AU X X c. A Welfare-to-Work (WTW) sanction is removed from an individual who has complied with WTW program requirements X d. A financial penalty is removed from an AU that complies with CalWORKs program requirements X X e. A Cal-Learn participant earns a Cal-Learn bonus or sanction X f. A child in the AU reaches the CalWORKs age limit (CPG 42-100.A) X X g. A child in the AU is placed in Foster Care X X h. A Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) recipient reaches the RCA time limit X i. Aid is authorized for an individual who is currently aided in another AU X X j. Information from an eligibility status report is acted upon mid-period X k. State Hearing decision resulting in mandatory changes mid-period X X l. An AU becomes a Family Reunification case X X m. An AU member is no longer a California resident X X n. Information from a redetermination is acted upon mid-period X X o. An erroneous payment caused by incorrect or incomplete recipient reporting or incorrect action or lack of action by the county is corrected X X p. An individual in the AU is deceased Effective January 1, 2016, a deceased child will continue to be included as a member of the AU in the month in which his or her death occurred and the following month. X X q. An AU is transferred to a Tribal TANF program X X r. Cost-of-living adjustments (COLA) for Minimum Basic Standards of Adequate Care (MBSAC) including income in-kind, Maximum Aid Payment, and Social Security X X s. An individual is confined in a correctional facility on the first of a month and is expected to remain for a full calendar month or more X X t. A nine-month real property exemption expires (CPG 42-200.G) X X u. A non-minor dependent (NMD) is transferred into his/her own AU X X v. Recoupment for an overpayment begins via grant reduction X w. A Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program (TCVAP) recipient is no longer eligible to state-funded services or becomes eligible to federally-funded programs X X County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page County-Initiated Actions and Third Party Information 44-270.I 2 of 3 Reminder: Approval of Supplemental Security Income (SSI) is not a County-initiated action and does not require mid-period action for CalWORKs. 44-270.I.2 Third Party Information Information that becomes known to the County or is provided through a third party may not require mid-period action if the information was not required to be reported per SAR or AR/CO rules. Examples include: •Employment information received by the WTW Employment Case Manager (ECM) that does not put the AU over their Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) •Information about the AU that is reported by an anonymous source •Earnings information obtained via an Income and Eligibility Verification System (IEVS) match •Interest income or bank account information obtained via an Asset Match •Pregnancy or newborn information received by the Cal-Learn Case Manager (CLCM) ACL12-25 and 12-49 Procedure: A. County-Initiated Actions The eligibility worker will take mid-period action and re-evaluate eligibility at the end of the month in which the change occurred. See CPG 22-000.A for timely notice requirements and exceptions. If the change does not require County-initiated action, the worker will note the information as a Held Change to be evaluated at the next eligibility status report or redetermination, whichever comes first. B. Third Party Information The eligibility worker will first determine if the AU was required to report the information on the most recent eligibility status report, redetermination, or as a mandatory mid-period report, and ensure the information was acted on appropriately. The worker will take mid-period action, if necessary, to reevaluate eligibility for all affected months and allow for timely notice as outlined in CPG 22-000.A. If the information was not required to be reported, the worker will note the information as a Held Change to be evaluated at the next eligibility status report or redetermination, whichever comes first. Impacts: CalFresh: CFPG 63-285 References: Assembly Bill (AB) 6 Senate Bill (SB) 1041 MPP 44-316.33 All County Letters (ACLs): 12-25, 12-49, and 14-77 ACIN 1-13-16 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page County-Initiated Actions and Third Party Information 44-270.I 3 of 3 Release Date: April 26, 2016 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by April 30, 2019.

title: A. Vendor Payments
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Vendor Payment Number Page 44-300.A 1 of 2 Revision Date: November 1, 2023 Background: Vendor payments are payments issued directly to a third party, agency, or vendor such as property owner, manager, agent, or landlord that is supplying goods or services to the customer. Purpose: The purpose of this program guide section is to define the requirements on vendor payment. The section is being revised as part of a sunset review and to update the section to the current formatting standards. In addition, processes were transferred to the CalWORKs Processing Guide (CPG) 44- 300.A1. There is no policy change. Policy: Mandatory Vendor Payment Benefits must be issued by vendor payment for the following: • Home repairs under special shelter payment provisions • Rent and/or utility payment when a parent or caretaker is sanctioned for failure to meet Employment Services (ES) requirements and the sanction has been imposed for a minimum of three consecutive months or longer • Homeless Assistance (HA) payment when mismanagement of funds exists. Refer to CPG 44-200.D for more information The mandatory vendor pay ment will be in the form of a warrant to the vendor. T here is no service charge to the vendor. The Vendor Payment Agreement form is not required to start mandatory vendor payments. The mandatory vendor payments will start as soon as timely n otice requirements can be met. The mandatory vendor payment stops when the customer is no longer subject to mandatory vendor payment. For example, the customer is eligible for an ES exemption or has cured their sanction. Voluntary Vendor Payment All customers may request a vendor payment option to pay for their rent or HA. Only the customer can make a request for voluntary vendor payments. The Voluntary Vendor Payment Agreement form is required and it must be completed by the customer and the vendor. The voluntary vendor payments start on the date indicated on the agreement or as soon as timely notice requirements can be met. The customer may request to discontinue voluntary vendor pay at any time. The voluntary vendor payments will stop when there is a change in circumstance (address or vendor) and the customer has not provided a new Voluntary Vendor Payment Agreement form. All of the following conditions must be met in order for a voluntary vendor payment to be processed: • The Assistance Unit (AU) receives a CalWORKs grant • The CalWORKs grant is more than or equal to the amount of the requested vendor payment amount • The Vendor Payment Agreement has been completed County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Vendor Payment Number Page 44-300.A 2 of 2 Changes in Vendor Information or Rent Amount A new Vendor Payment Agreement is required when there is a change in vendor, address, or rent amount. The payee’s name, address, or rent amount must be changed when the new information is reported by the customer. When a change of address or vendor is reported, payments to the previous vendor must be discontinued. When the address remains the same, but the customer reports that the rent amount has changed, a new agreement form is needed to authorize the change of the vendor payment amount. Vendor Pay Notification Customers must be provided with t imely and adequate notice when starting or stopping vendor payments. Timely notice is also required to change from vendor payments to two party warrants. The vendors must be notified when vendor payments start or stop. However, vendor notification does not need to be timely. The vendor must be notified prior to the time an action takes place. Confidentiality Staff must not release any specific case information such as benefit amounts or status of case without the customer’s written authorization. Information can be released to the vendor concerning the status of a specific payment such as issued, returned, not issued, or duplicate warrant was issued to establish an overpayment. Refer to CPG 19-000.A for more information on confidentiality. Overpayments and Fraud The customer is responsible for all overpayments. The vendor is not responsible for overpayments, and they do not have appeal rights. If a vendor is convicted of knowingly and willingly assisting a customer to commit fraud, vendor payments will no longer be issued to them. Procedure: CalWORKs Processing Guide 44-300.A1 References: Eligibility and Assistance Standards (EAS) 44-303.3, 44-307 All County Letter (ACL) 97-66 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by November 30, 2026. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: B. Benefit Issuance
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Benefit Issuance Number Page 44-300.B 1 of 3 Revision Date: March 1, 2023 Background: CalWORKs benefits are issued monthly to customers via Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT), or an alternate method. Customers are required to be notified at application and redetermination of the available benefit issuance options. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to provide guidance for qualifying accounts when a CalWORKs customer chooses to receive their benefits via direct deposit. Policy: Benefit Issuance CalWORKs benefits, including supportive services payments for Employment Services, are issued to the Assistance Unit (AU) via their EBT cash account. To assist in deterring fraud via skimming and scamming, Direct Deposit is highly encouraged. A n alternate method for benefit issuance, such as a warrant may be approved on a case-by-case basis. A warrant may be issued if the payee has demonstrated their inability to use the EBT system due to a physical or mental incapacity or condition or other barrier s, and there is no available alternative. Issuance via a warrant should only be approved after all other available alternatives have been explored and explained to the customer. Verification of the condition and its expected duration is required. Benefit issuance to a third-party (vendor payment) may be necessary in certain situations (CPG 44-300.A). Direct Deposit A customer can request at any time to receive their CalWORKs benefits via direct deposit to a qualifying account. Direct Deposit is highly encouraged. A qualifying account is: • A demand deposit (an account that offers access to funds at any time without advance notice, such as a checking account) or savings account at an insured financial institution. The account is required to be offered directly by the insured financial institution on its website or through its branches and is in the name of the person(s) entitled to receive the CalWORKs benefits • A prepaid account, or a demand deposit/savings account offered by an entity other than an insured financial institution that meets all the following criteria: o The account is held at an insured financial institution o The account is set up to meet the requirements for direct deposit or pass -through deposit or share insurance payable to the CalWORKs customer by the Federal Insurance Corporation o The account is not attached to a credit or overdraft feature that is automatically repaid from the account unless the credit or overdraft feature has no fee, charge, or cost, whether direct, required voluntary, or involuntary or the credit or overdraft feature complies with the requirements for credit offered in connection with a prepaid account under the federal Truth in Lending Act o The account complies with all the requirements and provides the holder of the account with all the consumer protections that apply to an account under the rules in the Electronic Fund Transfer Act (EFTA) The purpose of determining a qualifying account is to protect against predatory actions by non- ba nk entities that may impose excessive overdraft fees. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Benefit Issuance Number Page 44-300.B 2 of 3 Benefit Availability CalWORKs benefits are available in the EBT cash account on a staggered basis over the first three calendar days of the month, based on case number: Ca lWORKs benefits that are issued via direct deposit are available in the payee's personal bank account on the first calendar day of the month. Electronic Theft (Skimming or Scams) Electronic theft occurs when a customer or authorized representative has physical possession of their EBT card and benefits are stolen electronically from the EBT cash account. Customers may be eligible to receive replacement cash benefits if all requirements are met within 90 days of the electronic theft. Refer to the CalWORKs Processing Guide 40-300.B2. S kimming Skimming involves the use of electronic equipment or other electronic methods to capture a customer’s EBT card information without the customer’s knowledge. A common example is the use of equipment installed on an ATM or third-party points of sale devices to capture the customer’s EBT card information. S camming Scamming involves deceiving or misleading a customer to unwittingly give their EBT account information that is then used to create a counterfeit card and steal the customer’s benefit. Scams are typically done via text messaging and phone calls R eplacement cash benefits for victims of electronic theft will not count as income or property for CalWORKs eligibility purposes in the month received or in the following month. Benefits cannot be replaced if the EBT card has been lost or stolen or if the customer provided their EBT card number and/or Personal Identification Number (PIN) to someone they know and the benefits were stolen by that person. Procedure: Eligibility Policy and Procedures Guide - EBT System for CalFresh, CalWORKs, General Relief and Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants Eligibility Operations Processing Guide Electronic Theft of Cash Aid Procedures BEnDS 6358 Replacement of Lost or Stolen Cash EBT Benefits CalWORKs Processing Guide 44-300.B1 Direct Deposit Procedures CalWORKs Processing Guide 44-300.B2 – Electronic Theft Procedures Program Impacts: Management Reporting Out-of-state benefit usage is monitored each month to ensure timely actions are taken when a customer is no longer a California resident. Monthly reports are available in the MR SharePoint site. Last Digit of Case Number Benefit Issuance Date 1, 2, or 3 1st day of the month 4,5,6, or 7 2nd day of the month 8,9, or 0 3rd day of the month County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Benefit Issuance Number Page 44-300.B 3 of 3 References: • MPP 16-000-16-801, 44-300-44-315 • ACL 13-67, 18-148, 22-82 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by March 31, 2026. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Benefit Issuance Number Page 44-300.B 2 of 3 Benefit Availability CalWORKs benefits are available in the EBT cash account on a staggered basis over the first three calendar days of the month, based on case number: Ca lWORKs benefits that are issued via direct deposit are available in the payee's personal bank account on the first calendar day of the month. Electronic Theft (Skimming or Scams) Electronic theft occurs when a customer or authorized representative has physical possession of their EBT card and benefits are stolen electronically from the EBT cash account. Customers may be eligible to receive replacement cash benefits if all requirements are met within 90 days of the electronic theft. Refer to the CalWORKs Processing Guide 40-300
