title: C. Beginning Date of Aid
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Beginning Date of Aid Number Page 44-300.C 1 of 3 Revision Date: November 1, 2023 Background: The Beginning Date of Aid (BDA) regulation is followed when granting an application for assistance. The BDA may vary for Assistance Unit (AU) members. The BDA cannot precede the date of application. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is for sunset review and to reformat the section to current standards. The section is also being renumbered from 44 -300.F to 44 -300.C. CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) section 44-300.F Maximum Family Grant (MFG) is now obsolete and removed from the CPG. There is no policy change to BDA with this revision. Policy: BDA for New Applications The BDA for new applications is the date of application or the date the customer meets all conditions of eligibility, whichever is later. The date of application means the date the county receives a signed and dated application. The date the application meets all eligibility conditions means the date all linking and non -linking factors of eligibility are met, even when the required verifica tion of the condition is received at a later date. Examples of the linking and non-linking factors are deprivation, age, citizenship, non-citizen status, residence, property, and income. Technical conditions of eligibility met at a later date are considered to be met on the application date when they are completed by the date of approval except for the verification of, or application for, a Social Security Number (SSN). The customer must provide the SSN or proof of application for SSN within 30 days following the application date. Refer to CPG 40 -100.B for the list of all technical conditions for CalWORKs. When the BDA is after the first of the month, the amount of aid will be prorated. When a case was erroneously denied, the de nial action is to be rescinded and the BDA will be the date the AU would have been eligible in accordance with the BDA regulation. In addition, retroactive corrective payments will be made to the family member when aid is not paid in accordance with the BDA regulations or when an application was erroneously denied. For example, a family applies for CalWORKs on November 10. All family members meet the eligibility requirements except for the youngest child who does not have a SSN. On November 20, aid was granted for everyone except the one child because verification of a completed SSN application has not been provided. On December 2, the county receives proof of an application for a SSN. The denial for the child will be rescinded and the BDA for the child is November 10. BDA for Person Being Added to the AU The BDA for persons being added to the AU will be based on Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) or Annual Reporting/Child Only (AR/CO) regulations and the impact to the grant amount will be considered. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Beginning Date of Aid Number Page 44-300.C 2 of 3 When a mandatorily included person being added to the AU results in: • Increase of grant – The BDA will be the first of the month after the change is reported and all conditions of eligibility have been met. • Decrease of grant for SAR household – the BDA will be the first day of the SAR Payment Period following the required reporting of the customer on the SAR 7 and all conditions of eligibility have been met. • Decrease of grant for AR/CO household – The BDA will be the first month following the month in which the change occurred. When a mandatory AU member is unreported, the BDA is the date the person meets all requirements for eligibility when they are required to be included in the AU. Eligibility conditions are considered to have been met from the first day of the month following the date the person was discovered in the home, providing the person is cooperating in meeting the eligibility conditions. When an optional person being added to the AU results in: • Increase of grant – The BDA will be the first of the month after the change is reported and all conditions of eligibility have been met. • Decrease of grant for SAR household – the BDA will be the first day of the SAR Payment Period following the required reporting of the customer on the SAR 7 and all conditions of eligibility have been met. • Decrease of grant for AR/CO household – The BDA will be the first month following the month in which the change occurred. The BDA for a person who was sanctioned will be the first of the month following the date the customer contacted the county to indicate their desire to cure the sanction after all the following conditions are met: • All conditions of eligibility. • The customer completed the necessary action to cure their Employment Services sanction by successfully complet ing the activities that resulted in the sanction, or another valid activity determined by the Employment Case Manager (ECM). Refer to CPG section 10-025.A – Employment Services Noncompliance and Sanctions for more information and refer to CalWORKs Processing Guide 10-025.A4 for example scenarios. When a newborn child being added to the AU results in: • Increase of grant for SAR household – The BDA will be the first of the month after the birth is reported and all conditions of eligibility have been met. • Decrease of grant for SAR household – The BDA will be the first day of the next SAR Payment Period after the change is reported on the SAR 7 and all conditions of eligibility have been met. • Increase of grant for AR/CO household – The BDA will be the first of the month after the birth is reported and all conditions of eligibility have been met. • Decrease of grant for AR/CO household – The BDA will be the first of the month after the birth is reported and all conditions of eligibility have been met. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Beginning Date of Aid Number Page 44-300.C 3 of 3 When the second parent of a newborn being added to the AU results in: • Increase of grant – The BDA will be the first of the month after the report of the birth and all conditions of eligibility have been met. • Decrease of grant for SAR household – The BDA will be the first day of the next SAR Payment Period after the report of the birth and all conditions of eligibility have been met. Note: There are instances when the second parent and the newborn will be added to the Pregnant Person Only (PPO) case separately. The newborn can be added to the AU prior to the second parent when adding the second parent (of a newborn) results in a decrease of the grant. Program Impacts: Medi-Cal When a customer receiving Medi -Cal requests CalWORKs, the customer must submit a CalWORKs application. The BDA is whichever of the following is later: the first of the month of application, or the first of the month in which the customer meets all CalWORKs conditions of eligibility. General Relief The BDA regulations will be followed when a customer receiving General Relief benefits applies for CalWORKs. The customer may receive CalWORKs benefits in the same month they receive General Relief when the customer meets all CalWORKs conditions of eligibility . Refer to CPG 44-100.C for information on how the General Relief income will be treated in the CalWORKs budget. References: Eligibility and Assistance Standards (EAS): 44-315.72, 44-317, 44-318 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by November 30, 2026. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: D. Amount of Aid
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Amount of Aid Number Page 44-300.D 1 of 3 Revision Date: March 1, 2025 Background: The term amount of aid refers to the cash aid granted to the Assistance Unit (AU) for a given month. When an aid amount is less than $10 but more than $0, the aid will not be issued to the customer but this is not a basis for denial or discontinuance. The CalWORKs case may remain active. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to include changes to the continuing Financial Eligibility Test regulation per Assembly Bill (AB) 172. AB 172 implements using the Net Non-Exempt Income (NNI), instead of gross income, when determining whether the AU remains financially eligible for CalWORKs. When an AU’s income exceeds the Maximum Aid Payment (MAP), but their NNI remains below the Tier 2 Income Reporting Threshold (IRT), the AU may be eligible for a Zero Basic Grant (ZBG) and their CalWORKs case will remain open. Policy: Staff are responsible for computing the amount of aid at application, annual redetermination, and when there is a change in income or other factors affecting the amount of aid to which the customer is eligible. The amount of aid is determined by computing the AU’s NNI and subtracting it from the MAP for the AU. For more information on income calculation, refer to CalWORKs Program Guide ( CPG) 44-100.K Income Eligibility. MAP The MAP is a set value determined in the Welfare and Institution Code (WIC) Section 11450. The MAP for each AU is based on all family members whose needs are considered in the payment month. There are two MAP levels: the higher level for an exempt AU and a lower MAP level for a non-exempt AU. An AU is considered exempt when at least one of the following conditions are met: • The non-parent caretaker relative is not included in the AU (non-needy caretaker relative). • Each parent (including minor parent , aided stepparent, and needy caretaker relative) is disabled and is receiving one of the following: o Supplemental Security Income (SSI)/State Supplemental Payments (SSP). o In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS). o State Disability Insurance (SDI). o Temporary Worker’s Compensation (TWC). o Temporary Disability Indemnity (TDI). • An AU without aided children and each parent is receiving any of the disability benefits mentioned above and the child is excluded due to: o Receiving SSI/SSP. o Employment Services (ES) sanction. o Receiving Foster Care. • The AU is a Pregnancy Person Only (PPO) case and the parent receives any of the disability benefits mentioned above. • Each adult or parent of a child is aided under Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Amount of Aid Number Page 44-300.D 2 of 3 An AU is considered a n on-exempt AU when none of the criteria above is met. Refer to CPG 45- 200 CalWORKs Assistance Standards Chart, for the MAP table. The MAP level is determined at the following times: • Initial application. • Annual redetermination. • When an Eligibility Status Report ( SAR 7) is processed and there is a change reported that could affect the AU status. • When adding a person to the AU. • When the customer requests a review of the AU status. • When the customer reports a change related to the AU status. • When an AU member is determined to be exempt from ES participation due to an incapacity or are required to provide care to another person in the household. When the AU status changes between exempt and non-exempt MAP, the following will be applied: • When the change is reported on the SAR 7, the change in MAP level will be effective the first day of the next Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) payment period. • When the change is reported mid-period and the change will increase the grant amount, the change in MAP level will be effective the first day of the month following the report of the change when the verification has been provided. This applies to SAR household s and Annual Reporting/Child Only (AR/CO) households. • When the change in household composition is reported mid-period for AR/CO households and the change results in a grant decrease, the county must provide the AU timely and adequate notice. • When the customer request s a review of the AU status mid- period, the MAP status change must not be applied to any months prior to the month to which the request was received. If the change will result in a grant increase, the change will be effective the first day of the month following the report of the change when the verification has been provided. For more information on mid-period changes in exempt and non-exempt MAP, refer to CPG 44-270.H Voluntary Mid-Period Reports. ZBG An aid payment will not be issued when the total monthly grant is less than $10 but more than $0 . Although no cash amount will be issued, the AU is considered to have received a cash aid payment and the family will remain eligible to all CalWORKs benefits and services. ZBG eligibility happens when any of the following occur: • The grant amount is $10 or less. • The grant amount for the AU is reduced to zero due to a penalty. • The grant amount for the AU is reduced to zero to adjust for a prior overpayment. • The grant based on On-The-Job-Training is diverted to the employer as a wage subsidy to offset the participant’s wages. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Amount of Aid Number Page 44-300.D 3 of 3 When an AU’s income exceeds the MAP, but their NNI remains below the Tier 2 IRT, the AU may be eligible for a ZBG . T heir CalWORKs case may remain open, and they may remain eligible for CalWORKs supportive services even though they are not eligible for a cash grant. Note: There is no change to the CalWORKs a pplicant test requirement. Customers applying for CalWORKs must initially pass the Applicant/Minimum Basic Standards of Adequate Care (MBSAC) Test and then pass the Recipient Test. Provided all eligibility requirements are met, customers receiving ZBG are eligible to all CalWORKs benefits and services, including: • Housing and Homeless Assistance. • ES supportive services including transportation assistance. • CalWORKs Stage 1 Child Care. • Pregnancy and other recurring and nonrecurring special needs. • Home Visiting Program services. • Eligibility to CalFresh and cash-linked Medi-Cal. Customers receiving a ZBG are required to adhere to mandatory report ing. Any changes to their household circumstances, including the addition of a new member or changes in income made outside of the SAR 7 and annual redetermination processes, are treated as mid- period reports and would not require a reapplication of aid. Overpayment Although customers will not receive grants less than $10, an aid amount of less than $10 can be used to offset an overpayment. When customers receive a grant of $10 or more, and it is later determined the correct entitlement was less than $10, the entire amount is an overpayment. For more information regarding ZBG, refer to the Zero Basic Grant Question and Answer document housed in the CalWORKs SharePoint. References: Eligibility and Assistance Standards (EAS): 44-300, 44-315, 89-110 All County Letter (ACL) No.: 19-76, 19-76EII, 23-96 All County Information Notice (ACIN) No.: I-09-98, I-53-20 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by March 31, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: E. Voluntary Maximum Aid Payment (MAP) Exclusion
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Voluntary Maximum Aid Payment Exclusion Number Page 44-300.E 1 of 7 Revision Date: October 1, 2025 Background: Effective November 1, 2018, Senate Bill (SB) 380 allows customers to elect to receive full child support payments for a step/half-sibling in lieu of CalWORKs for that child. Customers have the choice to opt in or out of this policy. Prior to November 1, 2018, c ustomers were not allowed to keep child support payments received in lieu of CalWORKs. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to complete a sunset review and to renumber t his section from CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) section 44-300.H to 44 -300.E. CPG section number 44 -300.H becomes obsolete with the issuance of this material. This revision also includes clarification that child support does not need to be court ordered for the child to be excluded. Policy: Eligibility Criteria An Assistance Unit (AU) may opt to exclude the needs of a step/half-sibling from the AU’s Maximum Aid Payment (MAP), to keep the full child support payments made to that child, when all of the following apply: • The step/half-sibling lives with at least one eligible child. • The step/half-sibling is a child for whom child support payments are received. • The amount of current child support received each month for the step/half-sibling is greater than the CalWORKs grant amount for that child (refer to the Child MAP section of this material). • The customer requests in writing that the step/half-sibling not to be included in the MAP. Note: If a verbal request is made, staff must explain that the request must be in writing. The customer must complete form CW 52 SB 380 Informing Notice and Child Support Payment Opt-In Form. Verbal request will not be processed. Child MAP The Child MAP is the amount used to determine if the monthly child support received by a child exceeds the CalWORKs grant amount that the child receives or would receive if approved at application. Th is amount is determined based on the MAP for the AU size , with the child included , minus the MAP for the AU without the child, plus the amount of the child support disregard. Note: The child support disregard pertains to the number of children in the AU, not based on the number of children receiving child support payments. Therefore, there would always be at least two children MAP for AU with the step/half-sibling MAP for AU without the step/halfsibling(s) $200 (Child Support Disregard amount) Child MAP County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Voluntary Maximum Aid Payment Exclusion Number Page 44-300.E 2 of 7 considered when identifying the appropriate child support disregard amount as an SB 380 child must reside with a CalWORKs eligible child. The child support disregard is only considered in the Child MAP calculation for the first child because the AU receives the child support disregard only once per month regardless of the number of child support payments received in that month. The Child MAP calculation is available for staff in Desk Aid SB 380 Child MAP Charts, located in the CalWORKs SharePoint under the Desk Aid section. This desk aid provides the Child MAP for one and multiple children participating in SB 380 based on the AU type (exempt or non-exempt) and the AU size. Note: The use of the child support disregard in the Child MAP calculation has no impact to the CalWORKs budget. The AU will still be entitled to the appropriate child support disregard amount in the CalWORKs budget if child support is collected/received/passed through for the eligible child in the AU. Step/Half-Sibling’s Needs The step/half-sibling’s needs are still considered for the family Minimum Basic Standards of Adequate Care (MBSAC) but removed from the AU’s MAP amount. The child is still considered part of the AU and remains otherwise eligible for all other programs and services (Child Care, Special Needs, etc.). Evaluations for SB 380 Criteria and Opt-In Effective Date The step/half-sibling’s exclusion is to be evaluated only at the following times: • Application. • Periodic report. • Annual redetermination. For applicants who those to opt in , t he effective date to exclud e the step/half -sibling is the date CalWORKs is approved. For recipients who choose to opt in, the effective date is the following month after the request was made if timely and adequate notice can be provided. If there is not enough time to issue a timely notice, the exclusion will start in two months. For example, if the customer requested on 2/23/2025, the effective date to exclude the child is 4/01/2025. The child is eligible to be excluded from the MAP If the amount of child support received is greater than the Child MAP The child is not eligible to be excluded from the MAP If the amount of child support received is equal to or less than the Child MAP County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Voluntary Maximum Aid Payment Exclusion Number Page 44-300.E 3 of 7 Reminder: Customers also have the option to waive the 10 -day notice requirement to decrease their benefits. A signed waiver form is required before benefits can be decreased without timely notice. Step/Half-Sibling Verification at Application If the customer requests to exclude a step/half -sibling at application, the child’s required verifications are still to be provided, within the current timeframes, as if the child were being included in the MAP . This will assist in meeting a 10-day timeframe of adding the child back to the MAP determination , if a future request is made mid-period. The application will not be delayed, nor denied, while gathering the step/half-sibling’s verification. The only documentation required prior to granting the request is verification that the child is related within the 5th degree of kinship to the caretaker relative, they are a step/half-sibling of an eligible child who is living in the same home, and the amount of monthly child support received for the child will exceed the amount of CalWORKs the child would receive if included in the AU’s MAP determination. Note: Other verifications may be needed for other program eligibility determinations, such as Medi-Cal eligibility and CalFresh budgeting. Adding Back the Step/Half-Sibling to the MAP Determination When a step/half -sibling is excluded from the MAP, t he child can only be added back to the MAP determination at any of the following times: • Periodic report. • Annual redetermination. • Mid-period report when the customer voluntarily reports that the child support payments have decreased or ended and the customer requests the child be added back. The request to add the child’s needs back to the MAP may be made on the SAR 7 (Eligibility Status Report), SAWS 2 Plus, AR 3 (Mid -Year Status Report AR/CO AUs), SAR 3 (Mid -Year Status Report SAR AUs), a written statement, or verbally reported by the customer. Verbal requests must be documented in Journal Entry, explaining the request and reported change (loss or decrease) of child support income. If the request is made at SAR 7 or annual redetermination and there is no decrease or loss of the child support payments, the child will be added effective the first of the month following the request date. If the request is made at mid-period: • The child will be added the month in which the decrease or loss of child support income was reported. • Verification of the loss or decrease of child support income is needed. • The grant will be increased within 10 days after receipt of the verification of the loss or decrease of the child support income. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Voluntary Maximum Aid Payment Exclusion Number Page 44-300.E 4 of 7 Child Support and Other Income Payments In addition to child support payments, other types of income from the absent parent , such as Social Security Administration (SSA)/Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) , may be credited as child support by the Department of Child Support Services (DCSS). Therefore, a ny child support payments and other income coming from the absent parent (e.g. SSA/SSDI), regardless if the payment is received separately or combined, if the total amount received exceeds the Child MAP, the child may also be eligible to be excluded from the MAP. Examples of income to be used to determine whether the child may be excluded from the MAP: 1. A step/half-sibling receives child support. The child also receives SSA from the custodial parent. Only the child support income would be compared to the Child MAP as the SSA income is from the custodial parent. Therefore, it is not considered child support. 2. A step/half-sibling receives both SSDI and child support from the absent parent. The amount from both sources would be compared to the Child MAP. Treatment of Income and Resources When a step/half -sibling’s needs are excluded from the MAP determination, the child’s income and resources are excluded. Any income of the child is considered to be intended for the care and support of that child, and not for the use of other members of the family. Mandatory Inclusion Regulations Mandatory inclusion regulations do not apply when the step/half-sibling is excluded due to the SB 380 regulations. Cooperation with Local Child Support Agency (LCSA) Cooperation with the LCSA is still required under SB 380 , unless the customer meet s existing good cause criteria. Refer to CPG 43-200 for more information on child support cooperation requirements. Allocated and Unallocated Child Support Orders If the child support is court ordered, a llocated child support orders are required to determine SB 380 eligibility. Customers are required to provide copies of the current child support order and Monthly Statement of Collections and Distributions. Customers may contact the LCSA for information about child support amounts allocated to , and collected on behalf of , their children. Customers with unallocated child support orders will need to have their child support orders modified to reflect a per child support allocation. Occasionally it is possible that the child support order might have been entered as unallocated, but it could be considered allocated if the information is included in an attachment to the court order using a calculation method or some other attached document. Below are examples of allocated versus unallocated court orders: Allocated The court order lists three children and has a net figure for support for all three. There is no language stating that the order is unallocated nor non-severable. The order includes a calculation method or other program printout with support for County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Voluntary Maximum Aid Payment Exclusion Number Page 44-300.E 5 of 7 three children, and the total sum matches the amount on the Judicial Council order form. Unallocated The court order lists three children and has a net figure for support for all three. There is no language stating that the order is unallocated nor non -severable. There is no attached support calculation. Unallocated The court order lists three children and has a net figure for support for all three. The order includes language that the order is non-severable. Attached to the order is a printout with support for three children, showing allocation amounts and the net support matches the order. Staff must ask customers if they have any additional pages or attachments with their child support order if the copies submitted as verification are not clear. If the customer does not have their court order or is unsure if there are additional pages/attachments, staff may reach out to the LCSA. The LCSA will be able to provide the information either over the phone, through email , or by providing a copy to the customer. If staff accept the verification from the LCSA over the phone, they must thoroughly document in a Journal Entry the details of the conversation and amount of child support received as well as the name, position (title), contact information and office name/location of the LCSA providing the verification. Child Support SB 380 requires that the child support payment must exceed the Child MAP. Therefore, proof of the amount of child support paid is required to determine eligibility to exclude the child’s needs from the AU’s MAP determination. Child support does not need to be received from the LCSA/DCSS in order for the child to be excluded. Proof of child support can be but is not limited to: • An allocated (per child) court order for child support. • Copies of checks received from the absent parent. • A written statement signed by the absent parent. • Monthly statements of child support sent by the LCSA/DCSS. • A sworn affidavit (as a last resort) in the absence of any of the documents listed above. Mid-Period Changes Certain circumstances will require action to add the excluded child into the AU’s MAP or discontinue the AU at SAR 7 /annual redetermination if the child loses their eligibility to participate in SB 380 . Examples of mid-period changes include, but are not limited to: • MAP Increases – When MAP levels increase, the Child MAP will also change. When new Child MAP amounts are calculated based on MAP increases, the excluded child’s amount of child support will be reviewed to see if eligibility for exclusion still exists. If the amount of child support received is less than the revised Child MAP, the next actions will depend on when the MAP change occurred: Time Period Action AU’s SAR 7 data month The child’s needs will be added back into the AU’s MAP determination. The customer’s request is not needed to add the child. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Voluntary Maximum Aid Payment Exclusion Number Page 44-300.E 6 of 7 AU’s month of annual redetermination The child’s needs will be added back into the AU’s MAP determination. The customer’s request is not needed to add the child. Mid-period The child will not be added. The amount of child support received will be re-evaluated at the next SAR 7 or annual redetermination. • Penalties and Eligibility – Teens with school attendance penalties for whom child support is being received are eligible to participate under the SB 380 policy. These teens are members of the AU and receiving a grant amount of $0. Any amount of child support received for that teen above $200 (child support disregard) would qualify them for participation in this policy. Once the penalty is lifted and the grant amount increases for that teen back to an amount above $200, a re-evaluation of eligibility will be done by determining whether the amount of child support they receive exceeds the Child MAP. After re-evaluating the teen’s eligibility, if they are no longer eligible to participate under this policy, action will be taken following the same policy as described above for MAP increases. • Child Turning 18 Years of Age – A step/half-sibling’s income is excluded as long as they remain a child/minor in their parent/caretaker relative’s CalWORKs case. When the step/half -sibling is discontinued from the CalWORKs case due to reaching the age limit, that step/half-sibling is now considered an adult for purposes of CalWORKs eligibility, and any child support arrearages received by the customer on behalf of that child/teen is considered unearned income to the AU. Impacts: CalFresh Impact Child support payments received for an eligible household member are treated as unearned income when determining CalFresh eligibility and benefit amounts. Medi-Cal Impact The step/half-sibling remains eligible for cash-linked Medi-Cal, as long as they are otherwise eligible. When the child is discontinued from CalWORKs, they will be reevaluated for Medi-Cal benefits. Forms Impacts • CW 52 - SB 380 Informing Notice and Child Support Payment Opt-In Form Customers must be informed of this policy in writing at application and each annual redetermination; and they must make their requests in writing - This form serves as notification to customers of the options available, and to allow them to submit their requests in writing • M40-171D – Basic Approval – Partial This Notice of Action (NOA) informs the customer that the child’s needs are not included in the AU’s MAP determination as requested, but that the child is eligible for Medi-Cal and CalFresh • M82-832H – CW 52 Request Deny This NOA is to be used to deny the request, to exclude a child’s needs in the AU’s MAP determination, because the child does not meet one of the specified eligibility criteria under SB 380 • M82-832G – Grant Change This NOA is to be issued when CalWORKs for a child has stopped because the customer has opted to receive the child support in lieu of CalWORKs County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Voluntary Maximum Aid Payment Exclusion Number Page 44-300.E 7 of 7 Procedure: • SB 380 Regulations Summary Desk Aid • SB 380 Child Maximum Aid Payment Charts These charts reflect the Child MAP by region, AU size and exempt/non-exempt AUs for single child and multi-child participation. They are available in Eligibility Essentials under CalWORKs – Desk Aids. • Questions and Answers - Voluntary Maximum Aid Payment Exclusion Provides policy clarification regarding SB 380 under specified circumstances. They are available in CalWORKs SharePoint under the Questions and Answers section. References: Manual Policy and Procedures (MPP) 44-133.5(.51-.55), 80-820 All County Letter (ACL) No. 18-82, 20-109, 20-115 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by October 31, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Voluntary Maximum Aid Payment Exclusion Number Page 44-300.E 1 of 7 Revision Date: October 1, 2025 Background: Effective November 1, 2018, Senate Bill (SB) 380 allows customers to elect to receive full child support payments for a step/half-sibling in lieu of CalWORKs for that child. Customers have the choice to opt in or out of this policy. Prior to November 1, 2018, c ustomers were not allowed to keep child support payments received in lieu of CalWORKs. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to complete a sunset review and to renumber t his section from CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) section 44-300.H to 44 -300.E. CPG section number 44 -300.H becomes obsolete with the issuance of this material. This revision also includes clarification that child support does not need to be court ordered for the child to be excluded. Policy: Eligibility Criteria An Assistance Unit (AU) may opt to exclude the needs of a step/half-sibling from the AU’s Maximum Aid Payment (MAP), to keep the full child support payments made to that child, when all of the following apply: • The step/half-sibling lives with at least one eligible child. • The step/half-sibling is a child for whom child support payments are received. • The amount of current child support received each month for the step/half-sibling is greater than the CalWORKs grant amount for that child (refer to the Child MAP section of this material). • The customer requests in writing that the step/half-sibling not to be included in the MAP. Note: If a verbal request is made, staff must explain that the request must be in writing. The customer must complete form CW 52 SB 380 Informing Notice and Child Support Payment Opt-In Form. Verbal request will not be processed. Child MAP The Child MAP is the amount used to determine if the monthly child support received by a child exceeds the CalWORKs grant amount that the child receives or would receive if approved at application. Th is amount is determined based on the MAP for the AU size , with the child included , minus the MAP for the AU without the child, plus the amount of the child support disregard. Note: The child support disregard pertains to the number of children in the AU, not based on the number of children receiving child support payments. Therefore, there would always be at least two children MAP for AU with the step/half-sibling MAP for AU without the step/halfsibling(s) $200 (Child Support Disregard amount) Child MAP County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Voluntary Maximum Aid Payment Exclusion Number Page 44-300.E 2 of 7 considered when identifying the appropriate child support disregard amount as an SB 380 child must reside with a CalWORKs eligible child. The child support disregard is only considered in the Child MAP calculation for the first child because the AU receives the child support disregard only once per month regardless of the number of child support payments received in that month. The Child MAP calculation is available for staff in Desk Aid SB 380 Child MAP Charts, located in the CalWORKs SharePoint under the Desk Aid section. This desk aid provides the Child MAP for one and multiple children participating in SB 380 based on the AU type (exempt or non-exempt) and the AU size. Note: The use of the child support disregard in the Child MAP calculation has no impact to the CalWORKs budget. The AU will still be entitled to the appropriate child support disregard amount in the CalWORKs budget if child support is collected/received/passed through for the eligible child in the AU. Step/Half-Sibling’s Needs The step/half-sibling’s needs are still considered for the family Minimum Basic Standards of Adequate Care (MBSAC) but removed from the AU’s MAP amount. The child is still considered part of the AU and remains otherwise eligible for all other programs and services (Child Care, Special Needs, etc.). E

title: A. Overpayment
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Overpayment Number Page 44-350.A 1 of 7 Revision Date: July 1, 2024 Background: An overpayment is any amount of any aid payment received by an Assistance Unit (AU) that they were not entitled to receive. An overpayment may be all, or a portion, of the payment. This includes payments issued for regular aid payment, Immediate Need, Homeless Assistance, Aid Paid Pending (APP) for a state hearing, or Employment Services (ES). Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide the requirements to establish overpayments. This revision is to incorporate the implementation of the Potential Intentional Program Violation (IPV) policy and establishment of claims resulting from IPVs. Policy: General All reasonable steps necessary to promptly correct and collect any known overpayments must be taken. The following are roles/guidelines for evaluating, establishing and collecting overpayments: • The Human Services Specialist ( HSS) determines and computes all overpayments and grant adjustments. o The HSS determines from whom (the adult liable individual) the overpayment can be collected. If the liable individual is no longer in the AU, the overpayment is referred to Office of Revenue and Recovery (ORR). Only after all efforts to collect from the liable individual are exhausted, can the overpayment be collected from the AU. Refer to CPG 44-250.G for additional information. • Quality & Eligibility Support Department (QESD) computes overpayments based on Bureau of Public Assistance Investigations ( BPAI) reports and the review/findings of Integrated Fraud Detection (IFD) reports. • BPAI investigates and evaluates cases with suspected fraud and determines whether to prosecute. • ORR demands repayment, establishes collection accounts, and seeks civil judgments for overpayments which can no longer be recouped by grant adjustment. • Suspected fraud overpayments that are not prosecuted by BPAI are evaluated by QESD for an Administrative Disqualification Hearing (ADH). Refer to CPG 44-350.J for additional information. Establishment of Overpayment Overpayments will be established based on the following: • Customer’s failure to report accurately and completely. • County error. • County inability to issue the correct grant amount due to 10 -day notice requirement when the customer reported timely, completely, and accurately. Late reporting applies to the timing of mandatory mid -period reports, as well as the timing of the submission of the SAR 7 Eligibility Status Report form or redetermination. An overpayment will be established based on mandatory reports of information impacting eligibility when the customer received a grant amount to which they were not entitled under Semi -Annual Reporting (SAR) and Annual County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Overpayment Number Page 44-350.A 2 of 7 Reporting/Child Only (AR/CO) rules, regardless of whether the customer reported timely, except as noted under the Overpayment Will Not Be Assessed section below. Overpayment Will Not Be Assessed Overpayment will not be assessed: • For Technical Overpayments (Refer to CPG 44-350.B). • Based on any differences between the amount of income the county reasonably anticipated the customer would receive during the payment period, and the income the customer actually received during that period, provided the customer’s reports were complete and accurate. • For changes which were not required to be reported, but that may be voluntarily reported. An overpayment cannot be assessed based on an AU failing to make a voluntary mid-period report, or when the required report does not impact eligibility. • For mid-period changes to deprivation, property or household composition, unless the changes are not reported on the following SAR 7 or at redetermination. The changes in deprivation, property and household composition are only required to be reported on the SAR 7 or at redetermination. Note: Customers may waive the 10 -day notice requirement to avoid incurring an overpayment. The HSS will explain and offer this option to the customer. Effective January 1, 2017, if a 10 -day notice of a reduction or termination of the benefits cannot be provided, no overpayment will be established for the following month after the AU timely reports a change in: • Income over the Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) for a SAR AU. • Income over the IRT or household composition for an AR/CO AU. Two-Year Overpayment Establishment and Calculation Timeframe Effective July 1, 2022, a non-fraudulent overpayment will only be established if all or a portion of the overpayment occurred within the 24 months immediately prior to the date of discovery. The date of discovery is the date it is determined by computation that an overpayment has occurred. The overpayment claim will be considered established as of the date of the initial demand letter or written notification. The date of discovery must be documented in a journal entry for the case reviewers to more easily determine that the established overpayment claim follows the 24-month establishment and calculation policy. When establishing an overpayment, any overpaid benefits that were paid or issued more than 24 months prior to the date of discovery must not be included when calculating the overpayment claim. For example, in July 2022 it is discovered that the AU was over paid benefits starting in June 2019 through May 2022. The overpayment claim is established in the same month. In this scenario, the HSS would only calculate an overpayment for August 2020 through May 2022 as those months fall within the 24 -month period fro m August 2020 through July 2022, when the county discovered the overpayment. The overpayment from June 2019 through July 2020 falls beyond the 24 -month timeframe and will not be included when the overpayment is calculated. Claims established prior to the implementation of this policy must not be recalculated, except for overpayment claims that have been later determined to be fraudulent. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Overpayment Number Page 44-350.A 3 of 7 The 24-month timeframe for establishing and collecting an overpayment does not apply to fraudulent overpayments. A fraudulent overpayment is classified as an IPV claim. For an already established nonfraudulent overpayment claim that is later determined to be fraudulent, the non-fraudulent overpayment claim must be reclassified as an IPV and may include overpayment months beyond the 24-month limit (refer to the Potential IPV Overpayment Type section below). Potential IPV Overpayment Type For cases involving suspected fraud to move forward with either a referral for prosecution or a request for an ADH, that include overpayments beyond the 24-month establishment period, two claims must be created, the original nonfraudulent claim and the Potential IPV claim for the portion of the overpayment beyond the 24-month establishment period. The Potential IPV claim must be created in a suspended status since collection is not allowed until an IPV has been found. A CW 377 CalWORKs Informational Notice Potential Intentional Program Violation (IPV) notice must be sent to inform the customer of the calculated Potential IPV overpayment amount beyond the 24 - month period. This notice must be sent at the time the case is referred for prosecution or a request is submitted for an ADH. If an IPV is substantiated through the criminal prosecution or ADH processes, the overpayment type must be reclassified from Potential IPV to IPV. Once the IPV claim is established, the appropriate IPV Notice of Action (NOA) and corresponding budget worksheet must be sent to the customer. If an IPV is not substantiated through the criminal prosecution or ADH processes, the Potential IPV overpayment claim must be deleted. Overpayment Adjustment An o verpayment adjustment will only be started at the beginning of a payment period. Benefit adjustments will be discontinued mid-period when the overpayment is completely recouped. However, complete recoupment of one overpayment in mid -period may permit the recoupment of another overpayment in the following month (that is, before the next payment period), the next overpayment recoupment may begin in mid -period as long as the amount b eing adjusted does not result in the benefits being decreased mid-period. Mandatory Reporting Per SAR and AR/CO rules, customers must report the following: • Fleeing felon status. • Probation/parole violations. • Income over the IRT. • Address changes, including moving out of state mid-period. Refer to CPG 44-260.D and CPG 44-270.G for complete mandatory reporting information. An overpayment will be calculated for failure to report any of the above, except for address changes when they do not involve a move out of state. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Overpayment Number Page 44-350.A 4 of 7 For mandatory mid-period reports, which either result in ineligibility or a decrease to the grant amount, but it is too late to provide a 10-day notice of adverse action, the benefits must be released for the next month at the previous (higher) level, then establish an overpayment, except as noted under the Overpayment Will Not Be Assessed section above. Voluntary Reporting Changes which are not required to be reported, but voluntarily reported, will not be considered when determining overpayments. When an AU voluntarily reports the acquisition of property in excess of the property limit, the customer’s benefits will not be discontinued mid-period. The AU will remain eligible for the entire period. A No Change NOA must be sent to the household. The customer must report the information on the next SAR 7 or redetermination. Voluntary changes need only be reported on the SAR 7 that follows the change. If the change is not reported when the SAR 7 is submitted, that is when the AU will be considered to have failed to report. In this case, the AU will be notified of an incomplete SAR 7 and the appropriate NOAs issued. If this is not done, any resulting overpayments will be recorded as Agency Error, with the overpayments established for the amount the AU was not entitled to receive, beginning the SAR Payment Period after the incomplete SAR 7 or redetermination were due. Recoupment • Any non -willful overpayment which occurred prior to April 2, 1982, will not be collected except through voluntary repayment. • For any willful overpayment which was discovered prior to April 2, 1982, if the maximum adjustment period did not expire prior to April 2, 1982, the adjustment will continue as long as necessary to recover the overpayment. • For any overpayment, which is discovered after April 2, 1982, the overpayment is to be recouped in accordance with regulations in effect on the date of discovery. • When the overpayment is determined to be due to excess property, the overpayment is to be recouped in accordance with CPG 44-350.F. • All reasonable steps necessary to promptly correct and collect all overpayments will be taken regardless of the overpayment amount - Refer to the Closed Cases and NOAs sections below for appropriate actions when the claim balance is less than the established threshold. Active Cases The amount that can be recovered is the total amount calculated. For active cases, the automated system initiates recoupment once an overpayment is established. Closed Cases If the CalWORKs program discontinues with outstanding overpayments (or if the overpayments are established for closed cases), the claims balance is automatically referred to ORR via the automated system / Revenue Plus Collection System (RPCS) interface. ORR staff will establish a collection account and will initiate collection activities on all outstanding overpayments as follows: • IPV or fraudulent: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Overpayment Number Page 44-350.A 5 of 7 o ORR will start collection activities on any remaining balance, regardless of the amount. • The amount of non-fraudulent overpayment is $250 or more: o Collection of overpayments will be demanded from any liable individual of the overpaid AU. o If the overpayment is being paid in installments, collection efforts must cease once the balance of the outstanding overpayment falls under $250. o The payment that takes the overpayment claim below $250 will be the last payment accepted, after which the remaining overpayment balance will be placed in a suspended status. Example: There is a repayment agreement of $30 a month for an overpayment of $900. After 21 payments, the balance is $270. The next payment of $30 brings the balance to $240. This is the last payment required and the claim will then be placed in suspended status. Any subsequent payments made on the remaining overpayment balance of $240 must be refunded. • If the amount of non-fraudulent overpayment is less than $250: o Collection of overpayments will not be demanded from any individual of the overpaid AU. o For newly closed cases claims totaling less than $250 will be placed in a suspended status. • The $250 overpayment threshold applies to each non -fraudulent overpayment claim, rather than the total overpayment figure resulting from multiple overpayment claims. • The $250 threshold for collection applies to all closed CalWORKs cases with overpayment claims, including claims related to ES Supportive Services. Refer to CPG 44 -350.M for information on discharging non -fraudulent overpayments, when the CalWORKs case has been closed and the individual(s) responsible for the overpayment has not received aid under CalWORKs program for 36 consecutive months or longer in California. Civil or Criminal Prosecution for CalWORKs Overpayments Effective July 1, 2019, a civil or criminal action will not be made against any individual based on alleged unlawful application for or receipt of public social services if the case record, or any consumer credit report used in the civil or criminal case f or the purpose of determining the overpayment, has not been made available to the individual or has been destroyed after the expiration of the three -year retention period. Procedure: To be able to start or continue collecting an overpayment after the case is discontinued, the AU must have been notified of the overpayment. Therefore, all closed CalWORKs cases must be thoroughly reviewed before being assigned to the closed case bank to ensure: • NOAs and budget worksheets have been sent to the AU for each claim. o The required NOA fields completed, the notices reviewed for information accuracy and the NOAs issued to the liable individual(s). • Refer to CPG 44-350.I section for Non-System Determined Claims. • A journal entry to document a complete and clear explanation of the reason for the overpayment and action taken. For overpayments not currently being collected, such as when the liable individual for the overpayment leaves the AU or the home of the AU, the unlocatable procedures must be followed: • If the overpayment was referred to ORR contact ORR to determine if the person is unlocatable and follow up/review ORR’s response within 30 days. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Overpayment Number Page 44-350.A 6 of 7 • An overpayment can only be collected from other members of the AU, after all efforts to collect from the person responsible for the overpayment have been exhausted. Refer to the Overpayment Threshold and Discharge Process Examples desk aid, located in Eligibility Essentials, for overpayment threshold and overpayment discharge examples. Impacts: Other Programs These overpayment regulations also apply to the Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) and Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Programs (TCVAP). NOAs • M44-352A, Notice of Overpayment and Demand. To be issued when the case discontinues, and the overpayment was never collected through grant reduction - For non-fraudulent claims less than $250, and the liable individuals are not recipients in another case, M44-350M must be issued instead. • M44-352G, Demand Overpayment. To be issued when the case discontinues, the overpayment was being collected through grant reduction, and there is a balance owing of $250 or more - For non-fraudulent claims less than $250, and the liable individuals are not recipients in another case, M44-350M must be issued instead. • M44-350M, Suspension of Overpayment. This NOA informs former customers that: o Overpayment claims less than $250 will be placed in a suspense status following the case discontinuance. o Collection of the overpayment will resume if the individual becomes a CalWORKs recipient. • M44-350N, Suspend Overpayment Recovery. This NOA informs former customers who are making payments (on a discontinued case), and once the outstanding balance drops under $250, that: o They should no longer make additional payments because the overpayment balance is less than $250. o Collection of the overpayment will resume if the individual becomes a CalWORKs recipient. References: • Assembly Bill (AB) No. 135. • Senate Bills (SB) No. 80, 726. • Welfare and Institutions Code (W&IC) 10851, 11004. • Eligibility and Assistance Standards (EAS) 44-350. • All County Letters (ACLs) No. 16-120, 19-102, 21-109, 23-19. • All County Information Notice (ACIN) No. I-72-19. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by July 31, 2027. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Overpayment Number Page 44-350.A 7 of 7 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: B. Definitions
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Definitions Number Page 44-350.B 1 of 4 Revision Date: July 1, 2024 Background: An overpayment is any amount of any aid payment received by an Assistance Unit (AU) that they were not entitled to receive. An overpayment may be all, or a portion, of the payment. This includes payments issued for regular aid payment, Immediate Need, Homeless Assistance, Aid Paid Pending (APP) for a state hearing, or Employment Services (ES). Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide overpayment terms definitions. This revision is to add the new Potential Intentional Violation (IPV) definition. Policy: Action for Civil Judgment: The action taken by a county official to take the customer or former customer to court. Administrative (Agency) Error Overpayment: An overpayment caused by error on the part of the county when all information necessary to a correct determination of the grant was in the possession of the county. Aid: The amount of assistance issued to a customer. Balancing: A method for the recovery of all or a portion of an overpayment by applying it against an underpayment. Claim ID: When a claim (over/under payment) is determined and authorized in the automated system, it is assigned an unique ID number (Claim ID) that is linked to the Eligibility Determination and Benefits Calculation (EDBC) run and historical data that resulted in the claim’s creation. Client Error Overpayment (Other Overpayment) : An overpayment which does not meet the criteria to be considered an administrative overpayment, a fraudulent overpayment, or an Intentional Program Violation (IPV). Collect: To recover CalWORKs funds which are overpaid to a person by using methods other than grant adjustment. Corrective Payment: A payment made to an AU when it is determined that the AU has been underpaid. This usually occurs as the result of a retroactive court order, delayed implementation of regulations, or the correction of a misinterpretation of regulations. Demand for Repayment : The notification to a customer or former customer that an overpayment occurred for which there is a right for judicial restitution. Where demand for repayment is appropriate, it may be used concurrently with other methods of adjustment. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Definitions Number Page 44-350.B 2 of 4 Discharge: An expungement process for non-fraudulent overpayments, when the CalWORKs case has been closed and the liable individual(s) has not received CalWORKs for 36 consecutive months or longer. This also includes “mass overpayments” resulting from negligence or major systematic error as defined by the California Department of Social Services (CDSS). The discharge process does not apply to Aid to Families with Dependent Children (AFDC) overpayments established prior to December 1, 1996. Extended Filing Date: The date the SAR 7 – Eligibility Status Report form must be received in order for the customer to have continued CalWORKs eligibility. The SAR 7 must be received by the end of the business day on the first working day of the payment period in order for the customer to continue eligibility without a break in aid. Fraud: Fraud exists when a person has: • Knowingly, and with the intent to deceive or defraud, made a false statement or representation to obtain benefits, obtain a continuance or increase of benefits, or avoid a reduction of benefits. • Knowingly, and with intent to defraud, failed to disclose a fact which, if disclosed, could have resulted in denial, reduction, or discontinuance of benefits. • Accepted benefits knowing that there was no eligibility for those benefits, or accepted any amount of benefits knowing that this was greater than the amount to which they were entitled. • Made statements which that individual did not know to be true for the purpose of obtaining benefits, continuing receiving benefits, or avoiding a reduction or denial of benefits. Grant Adjustment: Recovery of an overpayment by reducing the grant of a customer or AU. Intentional Program Violation (IPV): A determination made by a state or federal court, or pursuant to an Administrative Disqualification Hearing (ADH), that an individual has intentionally: • Made a false or misleading statement or misrepresented, concealed, or withheld facts, or • Committed any act intended to mislead, misrepresent, conceal, or withhold facts or propound a falsity, and • Committed these acts to establish or maintain CalWORKs eligibility, or to increase or prevent a reduction in the amount of the CalWORKs grant. Liable Individual: The person who is determined to be accountable for the claim (overpayment). This person will be responsible for payment on the claim via methods such as monthly grant recoupment, cash payments, or tax intercepts. Mass Overpayment: An overpayment caused by the same action or inaction that impacts either eight percent of the county caseload, or more than 1,000 AU’s within the county, whichever is greater. Month of Discovery: The month in which the county obtained, or could have obtained by taking prompt action, information sufficient to support a determination both that an overpayment occurred and the amount of such overpayment. Non-fraudulent Overpayment: An overpayment, which is not determined to be fraudulent. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Definitions Number Page 44-350.B 3 of 4 Overpayment: Any amount of aid an AU has received to which it is not eligible. This may be all or a portion of the aid payment. It includes but is not limited to, an Immediate Need payment, a Special Need payment, ES Supportive Services, or APP for a state hearing. Potential IPV: This is for cases involving suspected fraud when the county has sufficient evidence to move forward with either a referral for prosecution or a request for an ADH that include overpayment beyond the 24-month establishment period. The calculated Potential IPV amount must be the portion of the overpayment beyond the 24-month establishment period. Recoupment: Recoupment is the method of recovering an overpayment by grant adjustments, or voluntary grant offset from individuals or the AU. Recovery: A method of getting back CalWORKs funds which were overpaid. Methods of recovery include grant adjustment (recoupment), voluntary grant offset, voluntary cash recovery, demand for repayment, action for civil judgment and balancing. Regrouping: When the data (that is, discovery date, error type or claim amount) in a claim is changed in the automated system and EDBC is run again, a new EDBC number is assigned and the recalculated claim is assigned a new number based on the new EDBC run. The old claim number does not disappear within the system but is closed out as “recalculated.” This allows historical data to remain available for tracking purposes and to create an audit trail. Supplemental Payment: A payment issued to an eligible AU when the budget for the current month is recomputed as a result of a change in anticipated income, and determined that the customer is due a larger aid payment in order to receive the correct amount of CalWORKs for the month. Technical Overpayment: This overpayment occurs when all four of the following requirements apply: • The customer fails to meet a condition of eligibility for CalWORKs. Examples include, but are not limited to, failing to: o Secure a Social Security Number. o Assign support rights. o Meet the Sponsored Non-Citizen requirements. o Apply for potentially available income. o Apply for Unemployment Insurance Benefits. • The customer's failure to meet the condition of eligibility is caused by the state, county, or Human Services Specialist (HSS) error and not by the customer's error. • The amount of aid paid would have been the same had the customer met the condition of eligibility. • This overpayment is discovered, calculated or recouped after January 1, 1985. Note: Technical overpayments are not considered overpayments in the State of California: • Any technical overpayment which was discovered on or after January 1, 1985 cannot be considered an overpayment. • Recoupment of any technical overpayments, regardless of when they occurred or were discovered, stopped effective January 1, 1985. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Definitions Number Page 44-350.B 4 of 4 Underpayment: An Underpayment occurs when the customer receives less than the amount to which the AU is entitled in a given month or months. If an underpayment comes to the attention of the HSS, reasonable steps to correct the underpayment must be taken. Note: A payment due to a change in the current month's budget is not an underpayment; rather it is considered a supplement to the grant. Unlocatable: Means either of the following: • When the county is unable to determine the whereabouts of the caretaker relative. • When the county is able to locate the liable individual, but unable to execute a legal process to collect. Voluntary Cash Recovery: Repayment made voluntarily to the county by a customer who has incurred an overpayment. Voluntary Grant Offset : Voluntary repayment made to the county by a customer’s foregoing all or a portion of a grant for which he or she is eligible. Procedure: None. References: • EAS 44-350.2. • ACL No. 19-102, 23-19. • ACIN No. I-72-19. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by July 31, 2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: C. Investigation of Overpayment
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Investigation of Overpayments Number Page 44-350.C 1 of 3 Revision Date: February 1, 2025 Background: An overpayment is any amount of any aid payment received by an Assistance Unit (AU) that they were not entitled to receive. An overpayment may be all, or a portion, of the payment. This includes payments issued for regular aid payments, Immediate Need, Homeless Assistance (HA), or Aid Paid Pending (APP) for a state hearing. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide investigation of overpayment requirements. This material revision is for Sunset Date review. No policy or procedure changes have been made. Policy: Apparent Eligibility When CalWORKs and/or HA benefits are issued as an Immediate Need payment , based upon a determination that the AU is apparently eligible, and later it is discovered that the AU is not CalWORKs eligible, the existence of an overpayment will depend on whether the AU was eligible to CalWORKs when the payment was issued. Refer to CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 40-100.K for additional information. Income Income-related failure to report and county error overpayments will be determined based on the mandatory recipient reporting requirements under Semi -Annual Reporting (SAR) (CPG 44 -270) and Annual Reporting/Child Only (AR/CO) (CPG 44 -260) rules. Mandatory recipient reports include reporting on the SAR 7 Eligibility Status Report, the mandatory mid -period report of income over the Income Reporting Threshold (IRT), and customer reports on redetermination. If an AU fails to report income any time they are required to report , or staff fails to act correctly on a report, staff will: • Recalculate the benefits based on an accurate report and correct the county action. • Recreate case circumstances using the correct processing timeframes based on what the AU should have reported. If an overpayment results from this calculation, except as noted under CPG 44-350.A, the overpayment will begin as of the date that the change should have been made. Refer to CPG 44-350.F for more information. Property AUs are required to report property changes only on the SAR 7 or at redetermination. No overpayment will be assessed for any months in which the AU was over the property limit but was not required to report property, including property that first exceeded the limit in the Submit Month. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Investigation of Overpayments Number Page 44-350.C 2 of 3 • Property eligibility will be determined once per payment period , based on information provided on the SAR 7 or at redetermination. • AUs are required to report only when property exceeds the limit in the (SAR) Data Month. • If the property reported on the SAR 7 or at redetermination, together with property already used to establish eligibility, does not exceed the property limit, the AU is considered property eligible for the entire upcoming payment period. If an AU owned property that exceeded the resource limit in the Data Month of the payment period, and failed to report it on the SAR 7 or at redetermination, staff will redetermine the benefits the AU should have received based on an accurate report and correct county action, including a determination of whether the excess property (and failure to report it) was in good faith. However, if staff failed to act correctly on a report of property that was determined to exceed the limit, the assumption will be made that the AU would have spent down the resources prior to the discontinuance, and would have remained eligible. In this case, no overpayment will be established. If excess property was held in good faith, the amount of the excess property overpayment will be the lesser of: • The amount by which the excess property exceeded the property limit in the one month the property had the highest value. • The total amount of aid the AU received while they were over the property limit. Refer to CPG 44-350.F for more information. Failing to Report Property and Resources The AU must report all new property acquired since the last SAR 7 or redetermination. If the AU owned property that exceeded the property limit in the Data Month of the payment period and failed to report it on the SAR 7 , or at redetermination, the benefits will be recalculated and an overpayment will be established. Late SAR 7 An overpayment will be established when an AU submits a late, or incomplete, SAR 7 resulting in the receipt of more benefits than they were entitled to, because of the inability to issue 10-day notice. If the AU voluntarily reported an unverified change mid-period, and that change is not included on their next SAR 7, staff must attempt to resolve the discrepancy. If staff cannot, the SAR 7 must be considered incomplete. If the discrepancy is resolved late in the submit month, and staff does not have time to issue 10 -day notice of decreased benefits, benefits must be released at the higher level , and an overpayment assessed. The type of overpayment (Agency Error or Customer Error) will be based on the specific circumstances leading to the late/incomplete reporting by the AU, or late processing by staff: • If the AU provides the SAR 7 too late for a 10 -day notice, the resulting overpayment is considered a Customer Error overpayment, not an Agency Error overpayment. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Investigation of Overpayments Number Page 44-350.C 3 of 3 • However, if the AU reported timely, completely, and accurately, but staff was unable to issue the correct grant amount due to the 10-day notice requirement when processing the SAR 7, this will result as an Agency Error overpayment. Refer to CPG 44-350.A for more information. Note: To avoid overpayments when a 10 -day notice cannot be provided, if the AU signs a waiver (waiving their right to 10-day notification) to reduce the benefits, no overpayment will be established. Procedure: • Review the eligibility and grant factors to find what the correct grant amount should have been, and determine the apparent cause of the overpayment. • Calculate the overpayment. • Determine from whom (the liable individual) the overpayment may be recovered. Refer to the following sections under CPG 44-350.G for additional information: o Priority of Recovery. o Child Only Cases. o Minors in Overpaid Assistance Units. • Determine the recovery method and the amount to be recovered. • If appropriate , initiate any referrals to Bureau of Public Assistance Investigations (BPAI) for an investigation. Refer to CPG 20-000.A for fraud criteria. References: All County Letter (ACL) No. 16-120, 18-26. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by February 28, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: D. Aid Paid Pending
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Aid Paid Pending Number Page 44-350.D 1 of 1 Revision Date: February 1, 2025 Background: An overpayment is any amount of any aid payment received by an Assistance Unit (AU) that they were not entitled to receive. An overpayment may be all, or a portion, of the payment. This includes payments issued for regular aid payment, Immediate Need, Homeless Assistance (HA), or Aid Paid Pending (APP) for a state hearing. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide APP overpayment requirements. This material revision is for Sunset Date review. No policy or procedure changes have been made. Policy: APP a state hearing decision is a recoverable overpayment except to the extent that the claim is granted. However, the amount of a proposed overpayment adjustment which is stopped because of a customer’s timely request for a state hearing is not an overpayment. When a request for a state hearing is filed timely, all collection efforts on any disputed overpayment claims must be suspended pending the outcome of the hearing. If a customer has received APP at a higher amount, and then loses the hearing mid -period, their APP must end and aid will be decreased mid -period. Any amount of APP that the customer received, but was not eligible to, will be considered a Customer Error overpayment. Procedure: None. References: Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 22-022. Eligibility and Assistance Standards (EAS) 44-350.4. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by February 28, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services
