title: A. Refugee Cash Assistance
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Refugee Cash Assistance Number Page 69-205.A 1 of 6 Revision Date: October 1, 2025 Background: The Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) program is cash assistance provided to refugees who have been determined to be ineligible for CalWORKs or Supplemental Security Income/State Supplementary Payment (SSI/SSP) and who have resided in the United States (U.S.) for no longer than the eligibility time period outlined by federal regulations. In San Diego County, the RCA program is administered by Catholic Charities. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide RCA eligibility regulations. This revision is to inform of the reduction of the RCA eligibility period from 12 to 4 months for individuals whose eligibility start date is on or after May 5, 2025. Policy: RCA Eligibility Requirements Factors that must be considered when determining eligibility for RCA are: • Eligibility time period. • Refugee status. • Income and resources. • Attendance in an institution of higher education/training requirements. • Employment requirements (see CalWORKs Program Guide [CPG] 10-200.A Refugee Employment Services [RES]). • If applicable, RCA customers must provide the name of their sponsor or responsible Resettlement Agency (RA). • Customers who qualify for assistance under the CalWORKs program will be aided under CalWORKs. Those who do not qualify for CalWORKs will have their eligibility determined for RCA. • Documentation showing DT code of Admission and length of parole. Further verification will not be requested unless the information provided is unclear. Note: RCA customers are not subject to CalWORKs program requirements of deprivation, minor children in the home, or less than 100 hours worked in the application month. RCA Eligibility Determination Timeframe The eligibility of each RCA customer will be determined as promptly as possible within no more than 30 days from the date of application. The date of application is the beginning date of aid for RCA. Customers receiving RCA also receive full scope cash linked Medi-Cal benefits. RCA Noncitizen Status and Eligibility Time Period To be eligible to RCA, a customer must provide documentation issued by the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) or the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) indicating a Refugee Eligible Population (REP) status. Regardless of the date a customer applies for RCA benefits, the month of arrival/date of entry (DOE) as indicated on the USCIS document is the first month in determining eligibility. Staff can request additional verification or run a Systematic Alien Verification for County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Refugee Cash Assistance Number Page 69-205.A 2 of 6 Entitlements (SAVE) if the length of parole is unclear. For example, if a refugee customer’s DOE is January 2022 and they apply for RCA benefits in May 2022 their eligibility period would begin in January 2022 and end on December 31, 2022. They would be eligible for RCA from the application date to the end of the 12-month period. REPs who have surpassed their eligibility period are referred to as RCA time expired. RCA eligibility has changed over time as follows: • On or after October 1, 2021- Eligibility extended to 8 months. • On or after May 1, 2022- Eligibility extended to 12 months. • Beginning May 5, 2025, 4 months for individuals whose RCA eligibility start date is on or after May 5, 2025. REP Status Eligibility Time Period Start Date Paroled as a refugee or asylee under the section 212 (d)(5) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) and anyone presenting documents showing DT Code of Admission. DOE as indicated on USCIS documentation. Admitted as a refugee under section 207 of the INA. DOE as indicated on USCIS documentation. Granted Asylum under Section 208 of the INA. The date they are granted asylum. Victims certified by the ORR of severe forms of trafficking. The date they are certified by the ORR. Eligible family members of certified trafficking victims are eligible for RCA from the date of entry into the U.S. or the date the Derivative T Visa is issued, if already present in the U.S. Afghan Humanitarian Parolees (AHPs) October 1, 2021 or: • If they traveled to a Safe Haven – the date they entered the community, whichever is later. • If they did not travel to a Safe Haven – the DOE on USCIS documentation, whichever is later. Children born in the U.S. of refugee parents are considered time -expired based on the most recently arrived parent’s expiration date or 12 months from the child’s birth date, whichever occurs sooner. The month of arrival, as indicated on the USCIS Form I -94, or the month of birth is counted as the first month in determining time-eligibility. RCA time-expired refugees will be aided under other federal, state and/or county-funded programs, if otherwise eligible. Refugee children who have been legally adopted by U.S Citizens are not eligible for RCA assistance. RCA Income Eligibility and Aid Payments County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Refugee Cash Assistance Number Page 69-205.A 3 of 6 Unless specifically superseded by RCA regulations, cash aid payments under RCA follow CalWORKs program regulations relating to financial eligibility and payments including recurring special needs payments and Pregnancy Special Needs (PSN) payments. RCA cus tomers are not eligible to Immediate Need payments. However, if a customer reports an emergency need for benefits, staff will speed up the process by issuing the initial grant to the customer on an immediate need basis when apparently eligible. RCA Sponsors Some applications for cash assistance may be made when the sponsor is unable or unwilling to meet the total needs of the refugee(s) for whom they have accepted responsibility. When this occurs, aid is to be granted in an amount sufficient to meet the unmet needs as determined by the CalWORKs standard. If, following the loss of contact with a sponsor and after the granting of aid to the refugee, the RA secures a new sponsor for the refugee who accepts the responsibilities of sponsorship and meets the needs of the refugee(s) in full, in accordance with th e CalWORKs standard of assistance, cash assistance will be terminated. Only if the subsequent sponsor fails to meet the full needs of the refugee will the refugee again be potentially eligible to cash assistance. RCA Income Income for the RCA program is determined based on CalWORKs program regulations (see CPG Section 44-100 Income) for determining need and computing the assistance payment, with the following exceptions: • The sponsorship deeming provisions in the CalWORKs program do not apply to RCA cases. • Any Reception and Placement (R&P) cash received by a refugee after their arrival into the U.S. is exempt for the RCA program. RCA Resource Limits RCA follows the real and personal property resource limits of the CalWORKs program (see CPG Section 42-200.B Property Resource Limit), with the following exceptions: • The sponsorship deeming provisions in the CalWORKs program are not applied to RCA cases. • Any resources remaining in the customers’ country of origin are not considered in determining resource eligibility. • Any R&P income treated as resources for the CalWORKs program received by a refugee after their arrival into the U.S. will be exempted from consideration when determining resource eligibility. Assistance Units (AUs) for RCA The following individuals will be in the same AU: • Refugee parents and their children under 18 years of age. • Married refugee couples without children. The following individuals will be in their own AU: • Single adult refugees and minor refugees emancipated pursuant to state law (unemancipated minor refugees will not be established in their own AU). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Refugee Cash Assistance Number Page 69-205.A 4 of 6 Note: U.S. Citizen children born of a refugee and a U.S. Citizen are not eligible for assistance or services funded by the Refugee Resettlement Program (RRP)/RCA benefits if the household unit includes the U.S. Citizen parent. In these cases, the refugee paren t may be eligible for RCA and the U.S. Citizen parent and the children, if eligible, may be aided under the CalWORKs program. Mandatory Social Security Agency (SSA) Referrals All aged, blind, or disabled refugee applicants will be referred to the appropriate SSA District Office to apply for SSI/SSP. This program is a primary resource for refugees who meet the eligibility requirements. Application for and receipt of SSI/SSP is mandatory, if determined eligible. Refugee Employment Services (RES) All RCA customers will be referred to the RES program within 30 days of the RCA application being approved unless exempt. Refer to CPG 10-020 Exemptions and Good Cause for applicable exemption and good cause criteria. Also, as a condition of continued receipt of RCA, a nonexempt customer who is employed 32 hours a week or less is required to accept part -time employment-directed services, provided that such services do not interfere with the customer’s job. Full Time Students and RCA Refugees are ineligible for RCA if they are full -time students in a college program at an institution of higher education. A student is considered to be full time when attending: • 12 semester hours or 12 quarter hours for institutions using standard semester, trimester, or quarter hour systems. • 24 semester hours or 36 quarter hours per academic year for institutions using credit hours to measure progress and not using semester, trimester, or quarter hour systems. • 24 clock hours per week for institutions using clock hours. • A program that includes both credit and clock hours and the number of credit hours per term divided by 12 plus the number of clock hours per week divided by 24 is equal to or greater than one. • A series of courses or seminars which equal 12 semester hours or 12 quarter hours in a maximum of 18 weeks. • The work portion of a cooperative education program in which the amount of work performed is equivalent to the academic workload of a full-time student. An “Institution of Higher Education” is defined as a: • Public or private nonprofit educational institution which provides: o An educational program which awards an associate, baccalaureate, graduate, or professional degree. o At least a two-year program which is acceptable for full credit toward a baccalaureate, graduate, or professional degree. o At least a one-year training program which leads to a certificate or degree and prepares students for gainful employment in a recognized occupation. • For profit institution (privately owned) of higher education which provides at least a six -month program of training to prepare students for gainful employment in a recognized occupation. • Post-secondary vocational institution which is a public or private nonprofit educational institution County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Refugee Cash Assistance Number Page 69-205.A 5 of 6 and provides at least a six-month program of training to prepare students for gainful employment in a recognized occupation. There are a few exceptions to the student eligibility rule. The following students would be considered eligible to RCA benefits: • Refugees enrolled and participating in training programs offered at an institution of higher education on a full-time basis as part of an employability plan developed by Employment Services (ES). • RCA customers enrolled and participating in training programs offered at an institution of higher education on less than a full-time basis as part of an employability plan developed by ES. • An employed RCA customer who was a licensed professional in their home country and in need of professional refresher training in the U.S., or other services, in order to qualify and practice their licensed profession in the U.S. Note: The training may consist of full -time attendance in a college or professional training program if the training: • Is approved as part of the individual’s employability plan as developed by ES. • Does not exceed one year (If there is no documentation available, a sworn statement will be accepted as verification). • Is specifically intended to assist the individual in becoming relicensed in their profession and if completion can realistically be expected to result in relicensing. Voluntary Quit As a condition of eligibility for RCA benefits, customers must have not voluntarily quit employment, or refused an offer of suitable employment, without good cause, within 30 days prior to the application date. As a condition of continued receipt of RCA, a nonexempt customer will not, without good cause, voluntarily quit employment. Reporting Requirements RCA customers with eligibility start dates on or after May 5, 2025, who are eligible to receive up to 4 months of aid, are not required to submit a n Eligibility Status Report ( SAR 7). Customers whose eligibility began prior to May 5, 2025, and who remain eligible to receive up to 12 months of aid, are required to submit a SAR 7. Refer to CPG 44-270.A Semi-Annual Reporting. Termination of Aid RCA benefits will be discontinued under the following circumstances: • A sponsor is meeting the full needs of the refugee or refugee family. • The customer marries a U.S. Citizen or other non-refugee, including a time-expired refugee, who is able to meet the refugee’s needs. • The customer becomes time expired. • The customer fails to register for RES and meet educational/training requirements without good cause. • 100% of federal funding for cash assistance ceases. • A refugee becomes a full-time student in a college program in an institution of higher education and does not meet an exception to full-time student ineligibility. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Refugee Cash Assistance Number Page 69-205.A 6 of 6 Procedure: Refer to CalWORKs Processing Guide 69-205.A1 Refugee Cash Assistance Processing Guide. References: Eligibility and Assistance Standards 69-205 – 69-217. All County Letter No. 02-37, 12-25, 24-27. All County Information Notice No. I-88-04. All County Welfare Directors Letter from May 27, 2022, May 2, 2025. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by October 31, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: A. Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program
chapter: 70-100 Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program (TCVAP)
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program Number Page 70-100.A 1 of 7 Revision Date: October 1, 2025 Background: The Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program (TCVAP) is a state funded program established to provide public social services and healthcare services to noncitizen victims of human trafficking and to noncitizen victims of domestic violence and other serious crimes. Per Senate Bill (SB) 1569, customers qualifying under TCVAP provisions will be eligible for benefits and services to the same extent as individuals who are admitted to the United States (U.S.) as refugees. Potentially eligible customers can include families with minor children, single victims, or married couples without children. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide eligibility criteria for non -citizens under the TCVAP, and to inform staff of regulations and procedures for determining eligibility . This revision is to implement the reduction of the TCVAP cash assistance benefit eligibility period from 12 to 4 months for individuals whose eligibility start date is on or after May 5, 2025. Policy: Benefits and Services Available to TCVAP Customers Once it is determined that the customer is eligible to TCVAP services, they are potentially eligible to cash aid under the following state funded programs: • TCVAP CalWORKs for families with minor children. • TCVAP Cash Assistance for single adults or families without children. Applications and Processing Timeframes CalWORKs program forms will be used for both TCVAP CalWORKs and TCVAP Cash Assistance eligibility determinations. The eligibility of each TCVAP application will be determined as promptly as possible but no later than: • 45 days from the application date for TCVAP CalWORKs cases. • 30 days from the application date for TCVAP Cash Assistance. Time Limits Specific program time limits are as follows: • TCVAP CalWORKs eligible adult customers are subject to the 60-month time limit (effective May 1, 2022) for the CalWORKs program. • TCVAP Cash Assistance customers who are not eligible to CalWORKs are subject to the 4 -month time limit of the Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) program. TCVAP Cash Assistance is continuous with no time stoppers. Note: If the time limit changes for either the CalWORKs or RCA program, the time limit will also apply to TCVAP time limits. TCVAP Cash Assistance Time Reduction County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program Number Page 70-100.A 2 of 7 TCVAP Cash Assistance customers who applied for benefits on or after May 5, 2025, will have an eligibility period of 4 months. TCVAP customers who applied for benefits prior to May 5, 2025, continue to have an eligibility period of up to 12 months. Income and Resource Limitations TCVAP CalWORKs customers must meet CalWORKs program requirements including income, resource limitations, and work registration requirements, except for the requirement to have or apply for a Social Security Number (SSN). Income and resource limits for TCVAP Cash Assistance customers will be considered on the same basis as in the RCA program for determining need and computing the assistance payment. Income and resources for the RCA program are considered on the same basis a s the CalWORKs program unless specifically superseded by RCA regulations. Refer to CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 69-205.A RCA Program. The sponsorship noncitizen provisions that apply in the CalWORKs program do not apply to TCVAP customers. Human Trafficking Eligibility for TCVAP Forms of Human Trafficking are defined as any of the following: • Sex trafficking in which a commercial sex act is induced by force, fraud, or coercion, or in which the person induced to perform such an act has not reached 18 years of age. • The recruitment, harboring, transportation, provision, or obtaining of a person for labor or services through the use of force, fraud, or coercion for the purpose of subjection to involuntary servitude, peonage, debt bondage, or slavery. Determining Trafficking Victim Status For purposes of determining eligibility for a victim of human trafficking for TCVAP, a sworn statement by the victim or a representative (if the victim is not able to competently make a sworn statement) is sufficient to verify trafficking status, if at least one item of additional evidence is provided, including, but not limited to: • Police, government agency, or court records or files. • News articles. • Documentation from a social services, trafficking, or domestic violence program, or a legal, clinical, medical, or other professional from whom the customer has sought assistance in dealing with the crime. • A statement from any other individual with knowledge of the circumstances that provided the basis for the claim. • Physical evidence. • A copy of a completed visa application. • Written notice from the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) of receipt of the visa application. If the victim cannot provide additional evidence, a sworn statement is sufficient to make an eligibility determination as long as the customer’s status is not deemed questionable. The sworn statement must contain the customer’s declaration under penalty of perjury that they are a victim of human trafficking. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program Number Page 70-100.A 3 of 7 Once it has been determined that the customer meets the definition of a victim of human trafficking, at least one of the eligibility conditions below must be met for TCVAP eligibility: • An I -914 application for T Nonimmigrant status (T Visa) has been filed with USCIS and the application has not been denied. • The customer is preparing to file an application for a T Visa. • Steps are being taken to meet the eligibility conditions for federal benefits. • The customer is a person for whom "continued presence" in the U.S. has been requested by federal law enforcement because they are assisting or willing to assist in the investigation or prosecution of human traffickers. Note: "Continued Presence" is a status that allows victims assisting law enforcement to remain in the country during the course of a criminal investigation. Additional Documentation (T Visa) The following documentation may be useful in determining whether a customer has filed for a T Visa: • A confirmation receipt or letter from USCIS verifying an application has been filed. • A copy of the application for a T Visa (form I-914). If a customer has not yet filed for a T Visa, the customer’s statement that they intend to file or are taking steps to become federally eligible will be acceptable. Documentation may also include statements from persons in official capacities, (for example , law enforcement officials or victims’ advocates) who are assisting the victim with the T Visa application or steps to becoming eligible. Termination of Eligibility for TCVAP Services Eligibility for state -funded services for CalWORKs and Cash Assistance for trafficking victims will be terminated if the customer meets any of the conditions below: • The customer's application for a T Visa has been “ultimately administratively denied”. • An application for a Visa has been "ultimately administratively denied" when an appeal of the Visa denial has been unsuccessful or the time to appeal the denial has passed without an appeal having been filed, whichever comes first. • The customer has not applied for a T Visa within one year of the date of application for cash assistance. • If the customer has not filed for a T Visa within a year of their application for benefits but federal law enforcement has made a request for continued presence on behalf of the customer, the customer will continue to be eligible for benefits and services. • When a TCVAP customer is certified as a trafficking victim by the federal Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR), the customer is eligible to federal benefits and the case will need to be transferred to a federally funded program. • The customer reaches the time limits for the program. Case Transfer to Federally Funded Programs Families with children will transition from a state -funded aid code to a federal funded CalWORKs aid code once their ORR certification is received and their 4-month TCVAP eligibility period has ended. • TCVAP CalWORKs customers transferring to a federal aid code do not start a new CalWORKs eligibility period. The 60-month time limit does not start over. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program Number Page 70-100.A 4 of 7 Single adult cases or married couples without children will transition to a new 4-month period of federal RCA and eligibility begins once ORR certification letter is received. o These customers will be referred to Catholic Charities to be evaluated for RCA benefits. Note: In cases where a TCVAP customer is transferred to a federally funded program, any family members who hold a derivative visa will also be transferred to a federal aid code. Serious Crime Victims Eligibility for TCVAP In determining serious crime victim’s eligibility for TCVAP benefits and services, verification must be provided indicating that the customer has filed a formal application for a U Visa (Form I -918 and required supplements) with USCIS. See below for acceptable forms of documentation. Noncitizen Victims of Serious Crimes Federal Law Federal law defines noncitizen victims of serious crimes as persons who meet all of the following criteria: • Have suffered substantial physical or mental abuse as a result of having been victims of criminal activity involving or similar to, the following violations: rape; torture; trafficking; incest; domestic violence; sexual assault; abusive sexual contact; sex work; sexual exploitation; female genital mutilation; being held hostage; peonage; involuntary servitude; slave trade; kidnapping; abduction; unlawful criminal restraint; false imprisonment; blackmail; extortion; manslaughter; murder; felonious assault; w itness tampering; obstruction of justice; perjury; or attempt, conspiracy or solicitation to commit any of the above mentioned crimes. • Possess information concerning criminal activity (or in the case of a noncitizen child under the age of 16, the parent, guardian, or adult representing the child). • Have been helpful, are being helpful, or are likely to be helpful to a federal, state, or local law enforcement official, prosecutor, or judge or to other federal, state, or local authorities investigating or prosecuting criminal activities described above (or in the case of a noncitizen child under the age of 16, the parent, guardian, or adult representative of the noncitizen is helpful). Acceptable Documentation (U Visa) Acceptable documentation for verifying that an application for a U Visa has been filed or that U Visa Interim Relief was requested includes, but is not limited to any of the following: • A confirmation receipt or letter from USCIS verifying that a request has been filed. • The Notice of Action (form I -797) approving a U Visa or request for U Visa Interim Relief (U Visa Interim Relief is acceptable only if a request for U Visa Interim Relief was requested before October 17, 2007). • A form I-797 which serves as a fee receipt for an employment authorization request based on a n U Visa application. • A copy of the Petition for U Nonimmigrant status (Form I-918). • An Employment Authorization Document (EAD) issued under Category “A19” or “A20” for an approved U Visa petitioner. Note: A sworn statement cannot be accepted as proof of eligibility for victims of domestic violence and other serious crime victims. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program Number Page 70-100.A 5 of 7 Termination of Eligibility for TCVAP Services Eligibility for state-funded services for victims of serious crimes will be terminated when the customer’s application for a U Visa has been ultimately administratively denied, or when the program time limitation has been reached, whichever comes first. Unlike trafficking victims, victims of domestic violence and other serious crimes are ineligible for federally funded programs, regardless of being issued an U Visa. Derivative “T” and “U” Visas Certain family members (derivatives) of victims of trafficking or serious crimes may be eligible for TCVAP benefits and services. The following visa types are eligible for TCVAP CalWORKs or TCVAP Cash Assistance benefits and services provided they meet all other program criteria. • Victim of Trafficking: o T-2: Spouse. o T-3: Children. o T-4: Parent(s) (if the principal applicant was less than 21 years of age when the T Visa application was filed). o T-5: Sibling(s) less than 18 years of age. • Victim of a Serious Crime: o U-2: Spouse. o U-3: Children. o U-4: Parent (if the principal applicant was less than 21 years of age when the U Visa application was filed). o U-5: Sibling(s) less than 18 years of age. For a noncitizen who is already in the U.S. on the date that the Derivative T Visa is issued, the date of entry for purposes of benefits and services is the notice date on form I-797, Notice of Action of approval of the individual’s Derivative T Visa. For a noncitizen individual who enters the U.S. on the basis of a Derivative T Visa, the date of entry for purposes of benefits and services is the date of entry stamped on the individual’s passport or I -94 Arrival Record. Eligibility Criteria for TCVAP Cash Assistance Individuals determined eligible to TCVAP Cash Assistance are entitled to benefits and services to the same extent as refugees and are subject to the same requirements (outside of legal status) as RCA customers with the following exceptions that include, but are not limited to: • Eligibility for Other Programs – TCVAP customers who: o Are applying for benefits under these provisions will not be required to apply for Supplemental Security Income/State Supplemental Payments (SSI/SSP), as it would be inappropriate to impose a requirement for which it is known there is no eligibility. o Qualify for assistance under the Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants (CAPI) will be aided under CAPI. o Qualify for assistance under the state CalWORKs program will be aided under the state CalWORKs program. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program Number Page 70-100.A 6 of 7 o Are not already receiving CalFresh and Medi -Cal, will be informed that they can apply for CalFresh and Medi-Cal at the same time. Reporting Requirements It is the customer’s responsibility to notify the county when they have a change in immigration status such as administrative denial of their T or U Visa application or if they become certified by the ORR. TCVAP cash assistance customers with eligibility start dates on or after May 5, 2025, who are eligible to receive up to 4 months of aid, are not required to submit a n Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7). Customers whose eligibility began prior to May 5, 2025, and who remain eligible to receive up to 12 months of aid, are subject to SAR 7 requirements, unless they meet the definition of an Annual Report/Child Only (AR/CO) case. Refer to CPG 44-260.A Annual Reporting. Overpayments An overpayment will be computed if a customer receives more months of aid than they were not eligible to. Medi-Cal Coverage TCVAP CalWORKs customers are certified eligible to Medi-Cal under the CalWORKs aid code. TCVAP Cash Assistance customers are eligible for state funded Medi-Cal. Employment/Training Requirements and Exemptions TCVAP CalWORKs customers must participate in Employment Services (ES) activities to the same extent as other CalWORKs participants. However, it is likely that the TCVAP population will not have EADs because of their immigration status. An EAD, also known as a work permit, authorizes a noncitizen to work in the U.S. for a period of time, usually one year. An EAD can be granted at the same time a T or U Visa is granted. ES staff will ask the customer if they are authorized to work in the U.S. Once a person ha s entered the U.S. in a nonimmigrant status, they are usually restricted to the activity or reason for which they were allowed entry into the country. Compliance with certain registration, employment and employment directed education/training requirements will not be required if the customer does not have work authorization from USCIS. In addition to the exemptions from appropriate applicable work registration and employment and training requirements, an exemption will be available to TCVAP customers if physical or psychological trauma related to or arising from the victimization impedes their ability to participate in ES. The exemption must be verified with a physician's written statement that the illness or injury is serious enough to temporarily prevent their entry into an appropriate employment, education and/or training program. Procedure: CalWORKs Processing Guide 15-100.A1,70-100.A1, and 70-100.A2. Desk Aid – TCVAP Application Process. Did You Know – Cash Aid Services for the Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program (TCVAP). Impacts: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program Number Page 70-100.A 7 of 7 • CalFresh Program Guide: 63 -155 Battered Noncitizens, Victims of Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes. • Medi-Cal Program Guide 05.08.10 Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program (TCVAP). • Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants (CAPI) Program Guide: 99 -101.2 Non -Citizen/Citizen Status. References: • Welfare and Institutions Code (W&IC) 18945. • Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 70-102, 70-103, 70-104, 70-105. • All-County Letters (ACL) No. 06-60, 07-45, 07-45E, 08-15, 09-49, 12-25, 13-25,17-01. • All-County Information Notices (ACIN) No. I-41-07, I-07-15. • All-County Welfare Directors Letters (ACWDL) dated May 27,2022, May 5, 2025. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by October 31, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program Number Page 70-100.A 1 of 7 Revision Date: October 1, 2025 Background: The Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program (TCVAP) is a state funded program established to provide public social services and healthcare services to noncitizen victims of human trafficking and to noncitizen victims of domestic violence and other serious crimes. Per Senate Bill (SB) 1569, customers qualifying under TCVAP provisions will be eligible for benefits and services to the same extent as individuals who are admitted to the United States (U.S.) as refugees. Potentially eligible customers can include families with minor children, single victims, or married couples without children. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide eligibility criteria for non -citizens under the TCVAP, and to inform staff of regulations and procedures for determining eligibility . This revision is to implement the reduction of the TCVAP cash assistance benefit eligibility period from 12 to 4 months for individuals whose eligibility start date is on or after May 5, 2025. Policy: Benefits and Services Available to TCVAP Customers Once it is determined that the customer is eligible to TCVAP services, they are potentially eligible to cash aid under the following state funded programs: • TCVAP CalWORKs for families with minor children. • TCVAP Cash Assistance for single adults or families without children. Applications and Processing Timeframes CalWORKs program forms will be used for both TCVAP CalWORKs and TCVAP Cash Assistance eligibility determinations. The eligibility of each TCVAP application will be determined as promptly as possible but no later than: • 45 days from the application date for TCVAP CalWORKs cases. • 30 days from the application date for TCVAP Cash Assistance. Time Limits Specific program time limits are as follows: • TCVAP CalWORKs eligible adult customers are subject to the 60-month time limit (effective May 1, 2022) for the CalWORKs program. • TCVAP Cash Assistance customers who are not eligible to CalWORKs are subject to the 4 -month time limit of the Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) program. TCVAP Cash Assistance is continuous with no time stoppers. Note: If the time limit changes for either the CalWORKs or RCA program, the time limit will also apply to TCVAP time limits. TCVAP Cash Assistance Time Reduction County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program Number Page 70-100.A 2 of 7 TCVAP Cash Assistance customers who applied for benefits on or after May 5, 2025, will have an eligibility period of 4 months. TCVAP customers who applied for benefits prior to May 5, 2025, continue to have an eligibility period of up to 12 months. Income and Resource Limitations TCVAP CalWORKs customers must meet CalWORKs program requirements including income, resource limitations, and work registration requirements, except for the requirement to have or apply for a Social Security Number (SSN). Income and resource limits for TCVAP Cash Assistance customers will be considered on the same basis as in the RCA program for determining need and computing the assistance payment. Income and resources for the RCA program are considered on the same basis a s the CalWORKs program unless specifically superseded by RCA regulations. Refer to CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 69-205.A RCA Program. The sponsorship noncitizen provisions that apply in the CalWORKs program do not apply to TCVAP customers. title: SN 26-04 2026 Covered California (CA) Renewal for Advanced Premium Tax Credit (APTC) to Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI)
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Special Notice 2026 Covered California Renewal for Advanced Premium Tax Credit to Modified Adjusted Gross Income Number Page 26-04 1 of 7 Effective Date: October 1, 2026 Background: During Open Enrollment when information reported at renewal results in potential eligibility to Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) or Non- MAGI Medi-Cal, a California Healthcare Eligibility, Enrollment, and Retention System (CalHEERS) Advanced Premium Tax Credit (APTC) to MAGI referral is generated and sent to the county to make a final eligibility determination. Purpose: The purp ose of this S pecial Notice (SN) is to provide staff with guidance on processing APTC to MAGI renewal referrals during the Open enrollment period. Open enrollment for Covered Cal ifornia will run from November 1, 2026, through January 31, 2027. Effective October 1, 2026, Covered California cases will go into renewal mode. Current members may begin renewing or switching plans on this date. Procedure: When an APTC to MAGI referral is received, customers are placed in a Carry Forward Status (CFS) hold to prevent a loss of coverage while a Medi -Cal evaluation is in process. If Medi -Cal eligibility is established, the benefits will be granted effective the first day of the month of transition ( January 1, 2027). Refer to Medi -Cal Program Guide (MPG) section 04.02.22F Processing Transitioning Cases from APTC to Medi-Cal for more information on CFS. Multiple Referrals Received When multiple referrals with the same MAGI case numbers are received for different Benefit Months, review each referral to determine if it meets the APTC to MAGI Renewal criteria. Review each referral received on or after October 1, 2026, to determine if any have a Benefit Month prior to 01/2027. • If multiple referrals are received and any indicate a Continuing Run Reason with a Benefit Month of 10/2026, 11/2026 or 12/2026, treat the referral as a regular APTC to MAGI referral and use the earliest Initiated Date as the application date. Assign the application to the regular Family Resource Center (FRC) caseload bank and follow the standard application processing guidelines. • If one or more referrals are received and all have a Benefit Month of 01/2027 with a Renewal Run Reason, treat the referral as an APTC to MAGI Renewal Referral. Assign the application to the appropriate “FRC CalHEERS DPC Hold” caseload bank through November 30, 202 6, and hold for processing until December 1, 2026. Note: The Document Processing Center (DPC) will continue to clear and register applications for Referrals and will assist FRCs with Determination Changes upon request. When referring Determination Changes to the DPC, include the correct application date and indicate whether the MAGI Referral is a Renewal or a regular APTC to MAGI. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Special Notice 2026 Covered California Renewal for Advanced Premium Tax Credit to Modified Adjusted Gross Income Number Page 26-04 2 of 7 Referral Types: Renewal APTC to MAGI referral: Renewal APTC to MAGI referrals are dated October 1 – December 31, 2026, and will display a Run Reason of Renewal – manual renewal with a Benefit Month of 01/2027. Determination Change APTC to MAGI referral: A normal Determination Change APTC to MAGI referral will be dated any time of the year and will display a Run Reason of Continuing with the Benefit Month starting the first of the month following the discontinuance of APTC. Required Action for DPC: Caseload bank assignment instructions are valid through November 30, 2026. After this date, DPC shall no longer place CalHEERS referrals in the “CalHEERS DPC Hold” caseload banks and will resume the regular FRC bank assignment process. All other instructions in this SN will remain in effect for renewal related APTC to MAGI referrals. To register a 2026 Renewal APTC to MAGI Referral, DPC staff must: • Complete a case clearance • Identify if the CalHEERS referral meets the Renewal APTC to MAGI criteria • Register an application in CalSAWS using the date the referral was received • Complete a Journal Entry (JE) and include Renewal APTC to MAGI Referral • Assign the referral to the appropriate FRC caseload below: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Special Notice 2026 Covered California Renewal for Advanced Premium Tax Credit to Modified Adjusted Gross Income Number Page 26-04 3 of 7 Renewal APTC to MAGI Referral Processing: Renewal APTC to MAGI Referrals must not be processed until December 1, 2026, due to CalHEERS functionality. Processing cases prior to this date will result in a disruption to the customer’s APTC benefits. Step Actions 1 Enter the case number and open the Case Summary page. On the Display field enter 01/01/2027 and click View to see the application information in the Medi-Cal Program block. Last Name First Name CalSAWS Caseload Office CC CalHEERS DPC Hold Bank 37LS09420S Centre City, Metro EC CalHEERS DPC Hold Bank 37LS023A0Q El Cajon LG CalHEERS DPC Hold Bank 37LS032X0S Lemon Grove NC CalHEERS DPC Hold Bank 37LS053H0R North Coastal NCE CalHEERS DPC Hold Bank 37LS012W0Y North Central NE CalHEERS DPC Hold Bank 37LS0C4H0R Northeast NI CalHEERS DPC Hold Bank 37LS06480R North Inland, Fallbrook, Ramona SE CalHEERS DPC Hold Bank 37LS0F3M0S Southeastern SR CalHEERS DPC Hold Bank 37LS045Y0S Chula Vista SRNC CalHEERS DPC Hold Bank 37LS3KOI0T National City County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Special Notice 2026 Covered California Renewal for Advanced Premium Tax Credit to Modified Adjusted Gross Income Number Page 26-04 4 of 7 2 Click Inter-Agency Transfer (IAT) Summary on the Task Navigation Bar to view CalHEERS referrals. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Special Notice 2026 Covered California Renewal for Advanced Premium Tax Credit to Modified Adjusted Gross Income Number Page 26-04 5 of 7 3 From the IAT Summary page, select the Initiated Date Hyperlink with Benefit Month of 01/2027 to view the MAGI Referral Detail page. 4 The MAGI Referral Detail page allows you to view application details such as household composition, tax household, requesting status, program information (MAGI/APTC/Non-MAGI), and Authorized Representatives (ARs). Additional information and verifications can be viewed by clicking on the hyperlink for each case member listed under the Case Members block to display the MAGI Person Detail page. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Special Notice 2026 Covered California Renewal for Advanced Premium Tax Credit to Modified Adjusted Gross Income Number Page 26-04 6 of 7 5 The MAGI Determination Summary page will reflect information on the CFS from CalHEERS. To lift a Carry Forward hold, staff must update customer information in CalSAWS, request MAGI for the appropriate benefit month(s), accept and authorize the Eligibility Determination and Benefit Calculation (EDBC) results. This will send a disposition transaction to CalHEERS to lift the CFS. 6 Once results have been accepted, complete a JE and send the appropriate Notice of Action (NOA). Note: Customers who are transitioning to Medi -Cal from a Qualifying Health Plan (QHP) with APTC may request retroactive coverage. Refer to MPG 04.02.10I for additional information. Required Action for FRCs - Determination Changes Within the context of a case, go to the IAT Summary page. The Search Results Summary will display all referrals received. Determine whether the Determination Change will be processed as a Renewal or Regular APTC to MAGI Referral. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Special Notice 2026 Covered California Renewal for Advanced Premium Tax Credit to Modified Adjusted Gross Income Number Page 26-04 7 of 7 Example A - The Determination Change is treated as a regular APTC to MAGI referral with an application date of 10/02/2026. Example B – The Determination Change is treated as a Renewal APTC to MAGI referral with a Beginning Date of Aid of 01/01/2027. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by September 30, 2027. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: SN 26-03 Family Members Base Allocation Amount for 2026-2027
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice Family Members Base Allocation Amount for 2026-2027 Number Page 26-03 1 of 1 Effective Date: July 1, 2026 Background: The Family Members Base Allocation (FMBA) amount is updated annually per Section 1924(d) of the Social Security Act. Purpose: To inform staff of the new FMBA amount for 2026-2027. Policy: The FMBA amount is used when determining how much income an institutionalized or Home and Community-Based Services (HBCS) spouse may allocate to family members. Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 10.05.04 Allocation/Deeming and Special Case Situations for Long Term Care (LTC) and MPG 05.18.01 Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS). Procedure: Effective July 1, 202 6, the updated FMBA amount of $2, 705 must be used to calculate allocations to spouses and dependent family members of an institutionalized or HCBS spouse. A ny allocations for the month of July and ongoing where the 2025-2026 amount of $2,644 was used must be recalculated. Automation Impact: Until the FMBA is updated in the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS), use a manual budget to calculate the FMBA and override to the appropriate aid code or Share of Cost (SOC). The manual budget must be imaged to the case record, and all case actions must be documented in a journal entry. The following manual budgets for LTC cases are available in the CalSAWS Template Repository are: • Allocation/Special Deduction Worksheet A (MC 176W). • Share of Cost Determination MFBUs with LTC Person Included - LTC (MC 176M-LTC). The following manual budget for HCBS cases is available in the Eligibility Forms Library (EFL): • HHSA Budget Steps for HCBS Spousal Impoverishment (14-152). References: All County Welfare Directors Letter (ACWDL) 26-09 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 06/30/2027. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: SN 26 01 2026 Federal Poverty Levels (FPL) and Maintenance Need Standards
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice 2026 Federal Poverty Levels (FPL) and Maintenance Needs Standards Number Page 26-01 1 of 3 Effective Date: March 1, 2026 Background: The FPLs and maintenance needs standards are used to determine eligibility for Medi-Cal programs and are adjusted annually to reflect changes in the cost of living. The statewide Average Private Pay Rate (APPR) for Nursing Facility Level of Care (NFLOC) services is used to calculate a Period of Ineligibility (POI) when an institutionalized customer transfers nonexempt property for less than fair market value. The Minimum Monthly Maintenance Needs Allowance (MMMNA) and Community Spouse Resource Allowance (CSRA) are used to calculate allocations in Spousal Impoverishment determinations. The Supplemental Security Income/State Supplementary Payment (SSI/SSP) grant levels, In -Kind Support and Maintenance (ISM) values, Federal Benefit Rate (FBR), SSI Standard/Parent Allocation amounts, and Pickle Disregard Chart are used to compute Pickle Program eligibility. The Tuberculosis (TB) income standard and standard child allocation are used in eligibility evaluations for the TB program who are ineligible to other Medi -Cal programs and whose income falls within specific limits. Purpose: To provide 2026 FPL, APPR, MMMNA, CSRA, SSI/SSP grant levels, ISM, FBR values, TB standards and procedures. Policy: The effective dates for the 2026 FPL values below are based on the coverage groups listed. Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 11.1A for the updated values. Effective Date Coverage Group Retroactively to January 1, 2026 Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) methodologies and Medicare Savings Programs (MSP) with: • Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB). • Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary (SLMB). • Qualified Individual (QI-1) who do not receive Title II Retirement, Survivors, and Disability (RSDI) income. Retroactively to March 1, 2026 MSPs with customers receiving Title II RSDI income. Effective April 1, 2026 Aged, Blind, and Disabled (ABD) FPL programs and the 250% Working Disabled Program (WDP). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice 2026 Federal Poverty Levels (FPL) and Maintenance Needs Standards Number Page 26-01 2 of 3 The Maintenance Needs Assistance Standards below are effective January 1, 2026. Maintenance Needs 2026 Values APPR $14,440 per transfer MMMNA $4,067 CSRA $162,660 FBR • $994 for an individual. • $1,491 for a couple. SSI Standard Parent Allocation Standard Child Allocation • $994 for one ineligible parent living with a child. • $1,491 when both ineligible parents live with a child. • $497 maximum for each ineligible child. Pickle Disregard/Multiplier and SSI Payment Values Refer to MPG 11.1A TB $2,073 Procedure: 2026 FPL Increases Use the increased 2026 FPL values when determining eligibility for: • D enials and discontinuances back to the specified effective date for each coverage group. • R equests from a beneficiary, their parent or legal guardian, or Authorized Representative (AR), to retroactively evaluate eligibility for: o Individuals eligible to Advanced Premium Tax Credits (APTCs) who did not enroll in a Qualified Health Plan (QHP) nor pay a premium. o Individuals with a Share of Cost (SOC). Note: Individuals who had out of pocket expenses for covered medical or dental services and are redetermined eligible to either a lower or zero SOC with the 2026 FPLs may be eligible for retroactive medical out-of-pocket expense reimbursements. Refer to MPG 04.02.10J Beneficiary Reimbursement Process for more information. Do not calculate periods of ineligibility for disqualifying transfers made between January 1, 2024, and December 31, 2025. MMMNA and CSRA Use the updated M MMNA and CSRA figures when determining the spousal income and property allocation to the community spouse. SSI/SSP Grant Levels, ISM V alues, FBR, SSI Standard/Parent Allocation Amounts, and Pickle Disregard Chart Use the updated 2026 values to calculate Pickle Program eligibility. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice 2026 Federal Poverty Levels (FPL) and Maintenance Needs Standards Number Page 26-01 3 of 3 TB Income Standards, FBR, Standard Child Allocation Use the updated 2026 values when determining eligibility to the TB Program. Note: When determining retroactive eligibility for any of the above programs, use the FPLs and related charts for that month and year. FRCs must review and act on cases that did not authorize in the batch run; the lists will include instructions on how to process these cases. title: SN 26-02 Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) Outreach
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach Number Page CW 26-01 CF 26-02 MC 26-02 GR 26-01 CAPI 26-01 CMS 26-01 1 of 4 Effective Date: March 1, 2026 Background: San Diego County’s Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) campaign provide s outreach which is intended to provide customers with information to access potentially eligible tax credits, free tax preparation, and other filing services and resources. EITC payments and credits may have impact to Self -Sufficiency Services (SSS) programs such as California Work Opportunity and Responsibility for Kids (CalWORKs), CalFresh, Medi -Cal, General Relief (GR), Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants (CAPI) and County Medical Services (CMS). Purpose: To provide guidance on treatment of EITC payments and credits for SSS programs and outreach resources available for eligibility staff to provide to customers who are potentially eligible to tax credits, free tax preparation, and other filing services and resources. Policy: Treatment of Income from EITC EITC payments are exempt for CalWORKs, CalFresh, CAPI, Medi-Cal and CMS. For General Relief , EITC payments are counted as unearned income in the month received. If a customer received GR during 2025, and the customer receives the EITC, review the case for potential unreported earnings since EITC is for earned income. EITC related payments and credits that customers may receive are EITC, CalEITC, Foster Youth Tax Credit (FYTC), Expanded Young Child Tax Credit (EYCTC). Treatment of Property from EITC payments The table below outlines the treatment of Property for payments received from EITC. Program Treatment of Property CalWORKs and CalFresh Exempt resources for 12 months, starting with the month that the payment is received. Medi-Cal EITC payments are exempt as property in the month following the month of receipt. General Relief Refund retained by the customer in the month following receipt is considered personal property. CAPI EITC payments are exempt as property in the month following the month of receipt. CMS Any portion of the refund retained by the beneficiary in the month following receipt is considered exempt personal property. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach Number Page CW 26-01 CF 26-02 MC 26-02 GR 26-01 CAPI 26-01 CMS 26-01 2 of 4 Procedure: FRCs and ES Staff If customers report EITC payments or credits, treat the income and property as listed in this notice. Distribute the EITC postcards to c ustomers at all contacts and encourage them to contact 2 -1-1 to receive free assistance with filing their taxes and claim available tax credits. If additional postcards are needed, they can be ordered through XEROX printing services. References: All County Information Notice (ACIN) No. I-01-26 Resources: CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 44-100.C and 44-100.H2 CalFresh Program Guide (CFPG) 63-203 and 63-204. Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 09.06.01,10.02.01 and Desk Aid 56 MAGI Eligibility Groups and Aid Codes General Relief Program Guide (GRPG) 90-400.5F CAPI Program Guide (CAPI) PG 99-103.2B and 99-104.4B CMS Program Guide (CMSPG) 06.01.02A and 06.04.03H Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by March 31, 2027. title: SN 25-07 Social Security Administration (SSA) Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA) 2026
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide/CalFresh/Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice Social Security Administration – Cost-of-Living Adjustment Number Page CalWORKs 25-04 CalFresh 25-03 Medi-Cal 25-07 1 of 3 Effective Date: January 1, 2026 Background: Social Security Administration ( SSA) recipients will receive a 2.8 percent Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) effective December 31, 2025, and payable January 1, 2026. In addition, starting January 2026 the Medicare Part B premium will increase to $202.90 per month. Policy: New Applicants The actual amount of the SS A benefit, including the COLA increase, must be used for eligibility and budgeting purposes beginning in January 202 6. The SS A budgeted amount for January will be considered reasonably anticipated income for applications received in November and December 2025. Treatment of SSA COLA for Ongoing Semi-Annual Reporting (SAR) Customers The SSA COLA is considered a mid- period county-initiated action. As a result, a decrease in CalWORKs/CalFresh benefits may occur effective January 1, 2026, with timely and adequate notice. Income Reporting Threshold (IRT) Requirements CalWORKs customers are required to report if the increase in SSA benefits combined with earned income results in exceeding their IRT. If income exceeding the IRT is reported an evaluation is required to determine if the customer is still eligible to benefits. If CalWORKs discontinues due to exceeding the IRT, the CalFresh households (HH) are eligible to Transitional CalFresh (TCF). CalFresh HHs must report if the increase in SSA benefits combined with all other income receive d results in exceeding the HH’s IRT. If income exceeding the IRT is report ed, then an evaluation is required to determine if the HH is still eligible to benefits. Treatment of SSA COLA for CalWORKs Annual Reporting/Child Only (AR/CO) Cases The only cases where this action will not be considered mid- period are those AR/CO cases with a December 2025 redetermination. For those cases, include the updated SSA benefit amount in budgeting for the upcoming AR/CO period. Timely and Adequate Notice As with any adverse action, timely and adequate notice is required to decrease benefits . If unable to change the January 2026 CalWORKs grant/CalFresh allotment, take the appropriate action to decrease benefits the first of the following month after timely adequate notice can be provided. Recalculate January 2026 benefits using the increased SSA benefits and Medicare Part B premium amounts; and if the calculation results in a decrease, an overpayment/overissuance will need to be established as appropriate. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide/CalFresh/Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice Social Security Administration – Cost-of-Living Adjustment Number Page CalWORKs 25-04 CalFresh 25-03 Medi-Cal 25-07 2 of 3 Treatment of SSA COLA for Non-MAGI Medi-Cal Eligibility Groups The increase will not be applied to the Aged, Blind, and Disabled Federal Poverty Level (ABD FPL) and Medicare Savings Programs (MSPs) until April 1, 2026. Effective January 1, 2026, all medically needy cases with Title II income must have the share of cost (SOC) adjusted to reflect the COLA. Medicare Part B Disregard the income equal to the amount of the customer’s Medicare Part B premium when determining eligibility for the ABD FPL program, regardless of the state’s payment of the premium. This income disregard is applied to the budget as long as the countable income remains within the ABD FPL program limits. Note: Customers who are evaluated as Medically Needy (MN) must pay the premium before receiving the deduction. Procedure: When updating the SSA benefit amount the calculation is to be completed as follows: When Medicare Part B is not paid by the customer: Step Action 1 Use the previous SSA Title II benefit amount. 2 Multiply the amount by 1.028. 3 Round down to the next lower dollar (remove the cents). 4 Final amount will be the new anticipated SSA benefit amount. When Medicare Part B is paid for by the customer: Step Action 1 Add the 2005 Part B premium ($185) to the 2024 net Title II benefit amount. 2 Multiply the amount by 1.028. 3 Round down to the next lower dollar (remove the cents). 4 Subtract the 2026 Part B premium and round down to the next lower whole dollar. 5 Final amount will be the new anticipated SSA benefit amount. Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 11.1A Assistance Standards for updated premium values. Impacts: Automation A COLA mass update will run on December 6, 2025, automatically adjusting SSA benefit amounts and Medicare Part B premiums for open SSA and Medicare expense records in CalSAWS. On December 13, 202 5, a batch Eligibility Determination Benefit Calculation (EDBC) run will occur and effective January 2026 CalWORKs/CalFresh benefits will reflect the SSA benefit and Medicare premium increases. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs Program Guide/CalFresh/Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice Social Security Administration – Cost-of-Living Adjustment Number Page CalWORKs 25-04 CalFresh 25-03 Medi-Cal 25-07 3 of 3 The automatic adjustment will not occur on cases where there was a discrepancy including manual overrides. Case list reports requiring action will be shared when available. Cases not included in the COLA run will require staff to manually update the information in the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) to reflect in the January 2026 benefits. Other Programs Affected The SSA COLA also applies to Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) and Trafficking and Crime Victims Assistance Program (TCVAP). References: All County Information Notice (ACIN) No. I-56-25. All County Welfare Directors Letter (ACWDL) 25-22, 25-26. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by December 31, 2026. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: SN 25-06 2025 Covered California (CA) Renewal for Advanced Premium Tax Credit (APTC) to Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI)
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice 2025 Covered California (CA) Renewal for Advanced Premium Tax Credit (APTC) to Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) Number Page 25-06 1 of 7 Effective Date: November 1, 2025 Background: During Open Enrollment ( November 1, 2025 – January 31, 2026), when information reported at renewal results in potential eligibility to Medi -Cal (MAGI or Non -MAGI), a California Healthcare Eligibility, Enrollment, and Retention System (CalHEERS) Advanced Premium Tax Credit (APTC) to MAGI referral is generated and sent to the county to make a final eligibility determination. Purpose: To provide guidance for processing APTC to MAGI renewal referrals during the Open Enrollment period. Effective October 1, 2025, Covered CA cases will go into renewal mode. Procedure: When an APTC to MAGI referral is received, customers are placed in a Carry Forward Status (CFS) hold to prevent a loss of coverage while a Medi -Cal evaluation is in process. If Medi -Cal eligibility is established, the benefits will be granted effective the first day of the month of transition ( January 1, 2026). Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) section 04.02.22F for more information on CFS. Multiple Referrals Received When multiple referrals with the same MAGI case numbers are received for different Benefit Months, review each referral to determine if it meets the APTC to MAGI Renewal criteria. Review each referral received on or after October 1, 2025, to determine if any have a Benefit Month prior to January 1, 2026. • If multiple referrals are received and any indicate a Continuing Run Reason with a Benefit Month of 10/2025, 11/2025 or 12/2025, treat the referral as a regular APTC to MAGI referral and use the earliest Initiated Date as the application date. Assign the application to the regular Family Resource Center (FRC) caseload bank and follow the standard application processing guidelines. • If one or more referrals are received and all have a Benefit Month of 01/2026 with a Renewal Run Reason, treat as a APTC to MAGI Renewal Referral. Assign the application to the appropriate “FRC CalHEERS DPC Hold” caseload bank through November 30, 2025, and hold for processing until December 1, 2025. Note: The Document Processing Center (DPC) will continue to clear and register applications for Referrals and will assist FRCs with Determination Changes upon request. When referring to the DPC, include the correct application date and indicate whether the MAG I Referral is a Renewal or a regular APTC to MAGI. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice 2025 Covered California (CA) Renewal for Advanced Premium Tax Credit (APTC) to Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) Number Page 25-06 2 of 7 Referral Types: Renewal APTC to MAGI referral: Renewal APTC to MAGI referrals are dated October 1 – December 31, 2025, and will display a Run Reason of Renewal – manual renewal with a Benefit Month of January 1, 2026. Determination Change APTC to MAGI referral: A normal Determination Change APTC to MAGI referral will be dated any time of the year and will display a Run Reason of Continuing with the Benefit Month starting the first of the month following the discontinuance of APTC. Required Action for DPC: Caseload bank assignment instructions are valid through November 30, 2025. After this date, DPC shall no longer place CalHEERS referrals in the “CalHEERS DPC Hold” caseload banks and will resume the regular FRC bank assignment process. All other instructions in this memo will remain in effect for renewal related APTC to MAGI referrals. To register a 2025 Renewal APTC to MAGI Referral, DPC staff must: • Complete a case clearance • Identify if the CalHEERS referral meets the Renewal APTC to MAGI criteria • Register application in CalSAWS using the date the referral was received • Complete Journal Entry and include Renewal APTC to MAGI Referral • Assign the referral to the appropriate FRC caseload below: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice 2025 Covered California (CA) Renewal for Advanced Premium Tax Credit (APTC) to Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) Number Page 25-06 3 of 7 Renewal APTC to MAGI Referral Processing: Renewal APTC to MAGI Referrals must not be processed until December 1, 2025, due to CalHEERS functionality. Processing cases prior to December 1, 2025, will result in a disruption to the customer’s APTC benefits. Step Actions 1 Enter the case number and open the Case Summary page. On the Display field enter 01/01/2026 and click View to see the application information in the Medi-Cal Program block. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice 2025 Covered California (CA) Renewal for Advanced Premium Tax Credit (APTC) to Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) Number Page 25-06 5 of 7 3 From the IAT Summary page, select the Initiated Date Hyperlink with Benefit Month of 01/2026 to view the MAGI Referral Detail page. 4 The MAGI Referral Detail page allows you to view application details such as household composition, tax household, requesting status, program information (MAGI/APTC/Non-MAGI), and Authorized Representatives (ARs). Additional information and verifications can be viewed by clicking on the hyperlink for each case member listed under the Case Members block to display the MAGI Person Detail page. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice 2025 Covered California (CA) Renewal for Advanced Premium Tax Credit (APTC) to Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) Number Page 25-06 6 of 7 5 The MAGI Determination Summary age will reflect information on the CFS from CalHEERS. To lift a Carry Forward hold, staff must update customer information in CalSAWS, request MAGI for the appropriate benefit month(s), accept and authorize the Eligibility Determination and Benefit Calculation (EDBC) results. This will send a disposition transaction to CalHEERS to lift the CFS. 6 Once results have been accepted, complete a Journal Entry and send the appropriate Notice of Action (NOA). Note: Customers who are transitioning to Medi-Cal from a Qualifying Health Plan (QHP) with APTC may request retroactive coverage. Refer to MPG 04.02.10I for additional information. Required Action for FRCs - Determination Changes Within the context of a case, go to the IAT Summary page. The Search Results Summary will display all referrals received. Determine whether the Determination Change will be processed as a Renewal or Regular APTC to MAGI Referral. Purpose: To provide guidance for processing APTC to MAGI renewal referrals during the Open Enrollment period. Effective October 1, 2025, Covered CA cases will go into renewal mode. Procedure: When an APTC to MAGI referral is received, customers are placed in a Carry Forward Status (CFS) hold to prevent a loss of coverage while a Medi -Cal evaluation is in process. If Medi -Cal eligibility is established, the benefits will be granted effective the first day of the month of transition ( January 1, 2026). Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) section 04.02.22F for more information on CFS. Multiple Referrals Received When multiple referrals with the same MAGI case numbers are received for different Benefit Months, review each referral to determine if it meets the APTC to MAGI Renewal criteria. Review each referral received on or after October 1, 2025, to determine if any have a Benefit Month prior to January 1, 2026. • If multiple referrals are received and any indicate a Continuing Run Reason with a Benefit Month of 10/2025, 11/2025 or 12/2025, treat the referral as a regular APTC to MAGI referral and use the earliest Initiated Date as the application date. Assign the application to the regular Family Resource Center (FRC) caseload bank and follow the standard application processing guidelines. • If one or more referrals are received and all have a Benefit Month of 01/2026 with a Renewal Run Reason, treat as a APTC to MAGI Renewal Referral. Assign the application to the appropriate “FRC CalHEERS DPC Hold” caseload bank through November 30, 2025, and hold for processing until December 1, 2025. Note: The Document Processing Center (DPC) will continue to clear and register applications for Referrals and will assist FRCs with Determination Changes upon request. When referring to the DPC, include the correct application date and indicate whether the MAG I Referral is a Renewal or a regular APTC to MAGI. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice 2025 Covered California (CA) Renewal for Advanced Premium Tax Credit (APTC) to Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) Number Page 25-06 2 of 7 Referral Types: Renewal APTC to MAGI referral: Renewal APTC to MAGI referrals are dated October 1 – December 31, 2025, and will display a Run Reason of Renewal – manual renewal with a Benefit Month of January 1, 2026. Determination Change APTC to MAGI referral: A normal Determination Change APTC to MAGI referral will be dated any time of the year and will display a Run Reason of Continuing with the Benefit Month starting the first of the month following the discontinuance of APTC. Required Action for DPC: Caseload bank assignment instructions are valid through November 30, 2025. After this date, DPC shall no longer place CalHEERS referrals in the “CalHEERS DPC Hold” caseload banks and will resume the regular FRC bank assignment process. All other instructions in this memo will remain in effect for renewal related APTC to MAGI referrals. title: SN 25-03 2025-2026 Family Members Base Allocation Amount
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice 2025/2026 Family Members Base Allocation Amount Number Page 25-03 1 of 1 Effective Date: July 1, 2025 Backg round: The Family Members Base Allocation (FMBA) amount is used when determining how much income an institutionalized or Home and Community -Based Services (HBCS) spouse may allocate to family members. Pur pose: To inform staff of the new FMBA amount. Po licy: Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 10.05.04 Allocation/Deeming and Special Case Situations. Pr ocedure: Effective July 1, 2025, use the updated FMBA amount of $2,644 to calculate allocations to spouses and dependent family members of an institutionalized or HCBS spouse. Recalculate any allocations for the month of July and ongoing where the 2024-2025 amount of $2,555 was used. Aut omation Impact: Until the FMBA is updated in the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS), complete a manual budget to calculate the FMBA and override to the appropriate aid code or Share of Cost (SOC). Image the manual budget and make a detailed journal entry for all case actions taken. Ref erences: ACWDL 25-11 Su nset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 06/30/2026. Appr oval for Release: Rick Wanne, Dir ector Self-Sufficiency Services

title: SN 25-02 2025 Federal Poverty Level and Statewide Average Private Pay
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Special Notice 2025 Federal Poverty Level and Statewide Average Private Pay Rate for Nursing Care Facilities Number Page 25-02 1 of 2 Effective: 03/01/2025 Background: The Federal Poverty Levels (FPLs) used to determine financial eligibility for Medi-Cal programs, are adjusted annually to reflect changes in the cost of living. The Statewide Average Private Pay Rate (APPR) for Nursing Facility Level of Care (NFLOC) services is used to calculate the Period of Ineligibility (POI) when an institutionalized customer transfers non-exempt property for less than fair market value. Purpose: To provide staff with the 2025 FPL and APPR values and procedures. Policy: Use the updated 2025 FPL values referenced in Medi -Cal Program Guide (MPG) 11.1A Assistance Standards when determining eligibility for the appropriate programs. • For applicants and beneficiaries of the Medicare Savings Programs (MSP), Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB), Specified Low -Income Medicare Beneficiary (S LMB), and Qualified Individual (QI-1) who do not receive Title II Retirement Survivors and Disability Insurance (RSDI) income, apply the new FPLs retroactively to January 1, 2025. • For MSP customers with Title II RSDI income, apply the new FPLs effective March 1, 2025. • For Aged, Blind, and Disabled (ABD) FPL program and the 250% Working Disabled Program (WDP), the new FPLs are effective April 1, 2025. • For individuals with Medi-Cal eligibility based on Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) methodologies, apply the new FPLs retroactively to January 1, 2025. Effective January 1, 2025, the APPR for NFLOC is $13, 656. Do not review or request information for transfers made on or after January 1, 2024. Only transfers made during the look -back period are considered. The look-back period is the 30 months prior to January 2024. The review period decreases by one month for each month that passes after January 1, 2024. Procedure: Review all denials and discontinuances back to the specified date for each group to re -evaluate eligibility based on the updated 2025 FPLs. Upon request from the beneficiary, their parent or legal guardian, or their Authorized Representative (AR), retroactively adjust eligibility in the following circumstances: • Advance Premium Tax Credit (APTC) eligible individuals who did not enroll in a Qualified Health Plan (QHP) or did not pay a premium. • APTC eligible individuals who enrolled in a QHP and paid a premium but have Medi-Cal covered medical or dental expenses that were not covered by their QHP during the retroactive period. • Individuals with a share of cost (SOC) who are redetermined eligible with a zero or a lower SOC when using the 2025 FPLs, who had out of pocket expenses for covered medical or dental services may be eligible for retroactive Medi -Cal out-of-pocket expense reimbursements (Conlan). Refer to MPG 04.02.10J Beneficiary Reimbursement Process (BRP) for more information. Use the 2025 APPR when calculating any POI if the date of application or date of institutionalization (whichever is more recent) occurs in 2025 and a disqualifying transfer of property was made during the County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Special Notice 2025 Federal Poverty Level and Statewide Average Private Pay Rate for Nursing Care Facilities Number Page 25-02 2 of 2 look-back period in 2023 or earlier. Refer to Special Notice (SN) 23- 06 Attachment A - Decreasing Look-Back Period. Automation Impact: The 2025 FPL tables were updated in the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) on February 13, 2025. A Batch update occurred on March 1, 2025, to update the MSP values. The new FPL values will be effective April 1, 2025. An Exception List will be sent to Family Resource Centers (FRCs) for action on cases that did not automatically authorize along with instructions on how to process these cases. References: ACWDL 25-01 and 25-02 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 02/28/2026. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services
