title: SN 25-01 Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) Outreach
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach Number Page CW 25-01 CF 25-02 MC 25-01 GR 25-01 CAPI 25-01 CMS 25-01 1 of 6 Effective Date: February 1, 2025 Background: San Diego County’s Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) campaign continues to provide services annually. These materials are provided to supplement EITC outreach efforts and are revised to reflect changes each tax year. Purpose: The purpose of this Special Notice is to provide revised federal EITC, California EITC (CalEITC) as well as other tax credit income limits , maximum credit amounts, and their impact on self -sufficiency programs. This material also provides resources to assist customers to access tax credits for which they are potentially eligible. Policy: Age and General EITC Eligibility California tax filers may qualify for either federal and/or state EITC depending on their income, age, and number of children. Refer to Appendix B for income limits and credit amounts. Federal EITC Eligibility: • Have earned income and adjusted gross income within certain limits but must be at least $1. • Have a valid SSN. • Meet qualifying child rules if any dependent children are claimed. • Live in the United States for more than half the tax year. • Requires the Schedule EIC form available on the EITC webpage or by calling the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) at 800-829-1040. CalEITC Eligibility: • Available to qualified tax filers ages 18 to 65 without qualifying children or any age with qualifying children. • Have a valid Social Security Number (SSN). • Have earned income and adjusted gross income of at least $1 and less than $31,950. • Meet qualifying child rules if any dependent children claimed. • Live in California for more than half the tax year. • Requires the Franchise Tax Board (FTB) 3514 form available on the CalEITC website or by contacting the FTB by phone at 800-852-5711. Note: California taxpayers may qualify for state credits even if they do not qualify for federal credits. Foster Youth Tax Credit (FYTC) Eligible current and former foster youth who file their California state tax return and claim the FYTC will receive up to $1,154 in tax credits. The credit amount is adjusted for inflation annually and phases out County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach Number Page CW 25-01 CF 25-02 MC 25-01 GR 25-01 CAPI 25-01 CMS 25-01 2 of 6 gradually as income rises above $31,950. The FYTC is awarded per eligible individual . An individual may qualify for FYTC if they meet all the following criteria: • Qualify for the CalEITC. • Age 18 through 25 at the end of the 2024 tax year. • In foster care at age 13 or older and placed through the California foster care system. Expanded Young Child Tax Credit (YCTC) For the 2024 tax year, the YCTC has been increased to $1,154 per family. To qualify, families must: • Have at least one child under six years old at the end of the tax year. • File a California state tax return. • Meet the CalEITC eligibility criteria. Beginning with the 2022 tax year, earned income is no longer a requirement for eligibility to YCTC. However, eligible families must still meet CalEITC and YCTC requirements. If filing for prior years, customers must have at least $1 of earned income to qualify. Procedure: Free Tax Preparation Services Free tax preparation services are available for low to moderate income individuals. Customers can call 2-1-1 for more information or log on to: • https://211sandiego.org/ • https://www.myfreetaxes.org/ MyFreeTaxes.com is operated by United Way Worldwide and offers free state and federal tax preparation and filing services. For the 2024 tax year, tax filers will have the option to choose to file “By Myself,” “With Assistance” or “I’m Not Sure”. Based on their selection, the information will be routed to the appropriate tax preparation model through a virtual assistant software, or in -person drop off. Services are free for households with earnings less than $60,000 for in person help or $66,000 or less if filing with virtual help. • https://www.getyourrefund.org/en For the 2024 tax year, United Way has partnered with Code for America to provide virtual free tax credit services with IRS certified volunteers for household with earnings less than $66,000. • https://www.eitc.irs.gov • https://www.irs.gov/ • www.ftb.ca.gov/caleitc • https://www.sco.ca.gov/eo_vita.html The IRS Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) Program offers free tax assistance to households with income of $ 60,000 or less. For the 2024 tax year, these services will be offered to qualifying individuals virtually or in-person with an appointment. EITC Postcards The County of San Diego’s Community Action Partnership (CAP) and local nonprofit agency Dreams for Change will coordinate distribution of EITC postcards and virtual EITC presentations to various County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach Number Page CW 25-01 CF 25-02 MC 25-01 GR 25-01 CAPI 25-01 CMS 25-01 3 of 6 Family Resource Centers (FRCs) and Employment Services (ES) sites as requested. Postcards (see Appendix A) will be distributed to ES, Refugee Employment Services (RES), Public Health Clinics, City and County libraries, schools, and Child Care contractors. In addition, a flyer (Appendix B) containing postcard information with VITA site locations and phone numbers is being distributed via Short Message Service (SMS) message to CalWORKs, CalFresh and Medi-Cal customers and is available on the sandiegocounty.gov website. EITC publications: • Strengthen state and county efforts to promote the EITC to our customer population. • Target families and individuals who qualify for EITC. • Educate and assist families on how to access EITC. FRC, ES, RES and Child Care Staff Action FRC and contracted staff will distribute the EITC postcards to customers at all contacts and encourage them to contact 2-1-1 to receive free assistance to file their taxes and claim EITC and other available tax credits. If additional postcards are needed, FRC and ES Managers, or their designees, may contact the CAP at (619) 338-2799. Impacts: CalWORKs and CalFresh • Income Federal and state EITC payments, whether received as advanced payments or as a single payment, are exempt as income in determining CalWORK s and CalFresh eligibility or benefits level (CalWORKs Program Guide [CPG] 44-100.C and CalFresh Program Guide [CFPG] 63-224). • Resource EITC payments and refund payments are exempt resources for 12 months, starting with the month that the payment is received (CPG 44-100.H2; CFPG 63-203, and 63-204). Medi-Cal • Income EITC payments received as tax refunds or advanced payments are exempt from consideration as income (Medi-Cal Program Guide [MPG] 10.02.01 and Desk Aid 56 - Modified Adjusted Gross Income [MAGI] Income and Deduction Types). • Resource The asset test for Non-MAGI Medi-Cal was eliminated effective January 1, 2025. General Relief (GR) • Income GR considers EITC payments as unearned income in the month received (General Relief Program Guide [GRPG] 90-400.5F). If a customer received GR during 2024, and the customer receives the EITC, review the case for potential unreported earnings since EITC is for earned income. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach Number Page CW 25-01 CF 25-02 MC 25-01 GR 25-01 CAPI 25-01 CMS 25-01 4 of 6 • Resource Any portion of the refund retained by the customer in the month following receipt is considered personal property (GRPG 90-400.5F). Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants (CAPI) • Income CAPI exempts EITC from consideration as income in the month received . (CAPI Program Guide [PG] 99-103.2B). • Resource CAPI exempts EITC as a resource for 12 months following the month of receipt (CAPI PG 99 - 104.4B). County Medical Services (CMS) • Income CMS exempts EITC as income in the month received . (County Medical Services Program Guide [CMSPG] 06.01.02A). • Resource Any portion of the refund retained by the beneficiary in the month following receipt is considered exempt personal property (CMSPG 06.04.03H). References: All County Information Notice (ACIN) No. I-67-24 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by February 28, 2026. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services Appendix A Appendix B Appendix B

title: SN 24-04 January 2025 Social Security Administration (SSA) Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA) and Related Changes
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Special Notice January 2025 Social Security Administration (SSA) Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA) and Related Changes Number Page 24-04 1 of 2 Effective: January 1, 2025 Background: The annual Cost of Li ving Adjustment (COLA) occurs for Social Security Administration (SSA) Title II payments, Supplemental Security Income (SSI)/State Supplementary Payments (SSP), the In- Kind Support and Maintenance (ISM) levels for computing Pickle eligibility, Pickle Disregard computation chart, Federal Benefit Rate, Medicare Premiums, Substantial Gainful Activity (SGA) and the SSI standard and parental allocation amounts. Purpose: To provide guidance for processing the 2025 SSA COLA and update the Medi -Cal Assistance Standards chart with 2025 values. Policy: Effective January 1, 2025, payments for SSA Title II Retirement, Survivors, and Disability Insurance will receive a 2.5 percent COLA increase. Non-MAGI Eligibility Groups This increase will not be applied to the Aged, Blind, and Disabled (ABD) Federal Poverty Level (FPL) and Medicare Savings Program (MSP) until April 2025. MAGI Eligibility Groups The Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) eligibility groups will not be affected at this time. The California Healthcare, Eligibility, Enrollment and Retention Systems (CalHEERS) will not run a COLA update until the FPLs are updated in April 2025. The Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) will notify affected MAGI beneficiaries about the change when CalHEERS runs the COLA update. title: SN 24-03 - 2024/2025 Family Member Base Allocation Amount
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Special Notice 2024/2025 Family Members Base Allocation Amount Number 24-03 Page 1 of 1 Effective Date: 8/1/2024 Background: The Family Members Base Allocation (FMBA) amount is used when calculating how much income an institutionalized or Home and Community Based Services (HCBS) waiver spouse can allocate to family members. Purpose: To inform staff of the annual FMBA amount. Policy: Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 10.05.04 Allocation/Deeming and Special Case Situations. Procedure: Effective 7/1/2024 use the updated FMBA amount of $2,555 to calculate allocations to spouses and dependent family members of an institutionalized or HCBS spouse. Recalculate any allocations that used the 2023-2024 amount of $2,465 for the month of July and onward with the new amount. Automation Impact: The FMBA update is scheduled for a September change release. Until the FMBA is updated in the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS), complete manual budget allocations and manually override to the appropriate aid code or Share of Cost (SOC). Image the manual budgets into CalSAWS and make detailed journal entries. References: ACWDL 24-07 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 6/30/2025 Approval for Release: Ouseopat for: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: SN 24-02 - 2024 Federal Poverty Level and Statewide Average Private Pay Rate for Nursing Facilities
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Special Notice 2024 Federal Poverty Level and Statewide Average Private Pay Rate for Nursing Care Facilities Number Page 24-02 1 of 2 Effective Date: 3/1/2024 Background: The Federal Poverty Levels (FPLs) used in determining financial eligibility to Medi -Cal programs are adjusted annually to allow for changes to the cost of living. The Statewide Average Private Pay Rate (APPR) for N ursing Facility Level of C are services (NFLOC) is used to calculate the period of ineligibility (POI) for institutionalized customers who make a transfer of assets for below fair market value. Purpose: To provide staff with the 2024 FPL and APPR values and procedures. Policy: Use the updated 2024 FPL values when determining eligibility for the appropriate programs referenced in Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 11.1A Assistance Standards: • For applicants and beneficiaries of the Medicare Savings Programs (MSP): Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB), Specified Low -Income Medicare Beneficiary (SLMB), and Qualified Individual (QI) who do not receive Title II Retirement Survivors and Disability Insurance (RSDI) income, the new FPL values must be applied retroactively to January 1, 2024. • For MSP customers who are receiving Title II RSDI income, apply the new FPL values retroactively to March 1, 2024. • For individuals who are eligible for Aged, Blind, and Disabled (ABD) FPL programs and 250% Working Disabled Program (WDP), apply the updated FPL values effective April 1, 2024. • For customers whose Medi-Cal eligibility is based upon Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) methodologies, apply the FPLs retroactively to January 1, 2024. Effective January 1, 2024, the APPR for NFLOC is $12,608. Do not review or request information for transfers made after January 1, 2024. Procedure: Review all denials and discontinuances back to the date specified for each gr oup and r e-evaluate eligibility based on the revised FPLs. Upon request from the beneficiary, the beneficiary’s parent o r legal guardian, or the beneficiary’s authorized representative, staff must retroactively change eligibility for the following circumstances: • Advanced Premium Tax Credit (APTC) eligible indiv iduals who did not enroll in a Qualified Healt h Plan (QHP) or did not pay a premium. • APTC eligible individuals who enroll in a QHP and pay a premium but have Medi-Cal covere d medical or dental expenses that were not covered by their QHP during the retroactive period. • Individuals with a Shar e-of-Cost (SOC) who are redetermined eligible to zero SOC or lower SOC when using the 2024 FPLs, who had out of pocket expenses for covered medical or dental services may be eligible for retroactive Medi-Cal out-of-pocket expense reimbursements (Conlan). Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 04.02.10J Beneficiary Reimbursement Process for more information. Use the 2024 APPR when calculating a disqualifying transfer of property made during the 30- month look-back period in 2023 or earlier. Refer to Special Notice 23- 06 for more information about how asset elimination affects the look-back period for a POI. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Special Notice 2024 Federal Poverty Level and Statewide Average Private Pay Rate for Nursing Care Facilities Number Page 24-02 2 of 2 Automation Impact: The California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) applied the FPL changes on March 2, 2024, with the correct effective dates for each group listed above. Four lists were generated by CalSAWS to assist in case processing and were uploaded to SharePoint here. Calculate each uncompensated transfer manually using form MC 176 PI and the updated APPR amount. When a POI is determined, send the MC 176 PI and related documentation to the Department of Health Care Services ( DHCS) via secure email for review at NonMAGIinbox@dhcs.ca.gov within 10 days . Once approved, request the restriction code 951 via a 14-28 to the MEDS operator. References: ACWDL 24-02 and 24-05 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 12/31/2026. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: SN 24-01 Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach Number Page CW 24-01 CF 24-02 MC 24-01 GR 24-01 CAPI 24-01 CMS 24-01 1 of 6 Effective Date: February 1, 2024 Background: San Diego County’s Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) campaign continues to provide services annually. The outreach materials are provided to supplement EITC outreach efforts and are revised to reflect changes each tax year. Purpose: The purpose of this Special Notice is to provide revised federal EITC, California EITC (CalEITC) as well as other tax credit income limits, maximum credit amounts, and their impact on self -sufficiency programs. This material also provides resources to assist customers to access tax credits for which they are potentially eligible. Policy: Age and General EITC Eligibility California tax filers may qualify for either federal and/or state EITC depending on their income, age, and number of children. Refer to Appendix B for income limits and credit amounts. Federal EITC Eligibility: • Must have earned income and adjusted gross income within certain limits but must be at least $1. • Must meet certain basic rules. For example, have a valid Social Security Number (SSN). • Must meet qualifying child rules if any dependent children are claimed. • Must live in the United States for more than half the tax year. • Claiming the federal EITC requires the Schedule EIC form available on the EITC webpage or by calling the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) at 800-829-1040. CalEITC Eligibility: • CalEITC is available to qualified tax filers ages 18 to 65 without qualifying children or any age with qualifying children. • Must have an SSN or an Individual Tax Identification Number (ITIN) for undocumented individuals. • Must have earned income and adjusted gross income of at least $1 and less than $30,950. • Must meet qualifying child rules if any dependent children claimed. • Must live in California for more than half the tax year. • Claiming the CalEITC requires the FTB 3514 form available on the CalEITC website or by contacting the Franchise Tax Board by phone at 800-852-5711. Note: California taxpayers may qualify for state credits even if they do not qualify for federal credits. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach Number Page CW 24-01 CF 24-02 MC 24-01 GR 24-01 CAPI 24-01 CMS 24-01 2 of 6 New Foster Youth Tax Credit (FYTC) Eligible current and former foster youth who file their California state tax return and claim the FYTC will receive up to $1,117 in tax credits. The credit amount is adjusted for inflation annually and phases out gradually as income rises above $ 30,950. The FYTC is awarded per eligible individual. An individual may qualify for FYTC if they meet all the following criteria: • Qualify for the CalEITC. • Were age 18 through 25 at the end of the 2023 tax year. • Were in foster care at age 13 or older and placed through the California foster care system. Expanded Young Child Tax Credit (YCTC) The YCTC has been expanded for the 202 3 tax year. The YCTC increased to $1,083 per family. Families must have at least one child under six years old at the end of the tax year and must file a California state tax return and meet the requirements of the CalEITC. Beginning in the 202 3 tax year, taxpayers do not need to have earned income to be eligible if they otherwise meet CalEITC requirements. If filing for prior years, customers must have at least $1 of earned income to qualify. Procedure: Free Tax Preparation Services Free tax preparation services are available for low to moderate income individuals. Customers can call 2-1-1 for more information. Customers can also log on to: • https://211sandiego.org/ • https://www.myfreetaxes.org/ MyFreeTaxes.com is operated by United Way Worldwide and offers free state and federal tax preparation and filing services. For the 2023 tax year, tax filers will have the option to choose to file “By Myself,” “With Assistance” or “I’m Not Sure”. Based on their request, the information will be routed to the appropriate tax preparation model through a virtual assistant software, or in -person drop off. Services are free for households with earnings less than $60,000 for in person help or $66,000 or less if filing with virtual help. • https://www.getyourrefund.org/en For the 2023 tax year, United Way has partnered with Code for America to provide virtual free tax credit services with IRS certified volunteers for household with earnings less than $66,000. • https://www.eitc.irs.gov • https://www.irs.gov/ • www.ftb.ca.gov/caleitc • https://www.sco.ca.gov/eo_vita.html The IRS Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) Program offers free tax assistance to households with income of $60,000 or less. For the 2023 tax year, these services will be predominantly virtual or will require an appointment due to the COVID-19 pandemic. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach Number Page CW 24-01 CF 24-02 MC 24-01 GR 24-01 CAPI 24-01 CMS 24-01 3 of 6 EITC Postcards The County of San Diego’s Office of Equitable Communities- Community Action Partnership (CAP) and local nonprofit agency Dreams of Change will coordinate the distribution of EITC postcards and virtual EITC presentations to various Family Resource Centers (FRCs) and Employment Services (ES) sites as requested. Postcards (see Appendix A) will be distributed to ES, Refugee Employment Services (RES), Public Health Clinics, City and County libraries, schools, and Childcare contractors. Post cards are available in all threshold languages. In addition, a flyer (Appendix B) containing postcard information with VITA site locations and phone numbers is being distributed via SMS message to CalWORKs, CalFresh and Medi-Cal customers and is available on the sandiegocounty.gov website. These EITC publications: • Strengthen state and county efforts to promote the EITC to our customer population. • Target families and individuals who qualify for EITC. • Educate and assist families on how to access EITC. FRC, ES, RES and Child Care Staff Action FRC and contracted staff will distribute these postcards to c ustomers at all contacts and encourage them to contact 2-1-1 to receive free assistance to file their taxes and claim EITC and other tax credits available to them . If additional postcards are needed, FRC /ES Managers, or their designee s, may contact the Office of Equitable Communities- Community Action Partnership (CAP) at (619) 338-2799. Impacts: CalWORKs and CalFresh • Income Federal and state EITC payments, whether received as advanced payments or as a single payment, are exempt as income in determining CalWORKs and CalFresh eligibility or benefits level (CPG 44- 100.C; CFPG 63-224, 63-224). • Resource EITC payments and refund payments are exempt resources for 12 months, starting with the month that the payment is received (CPG 44-100.H2; CFPG 63-203, 63-204). Medi-Cal • Income EITC payments received as tax refunds or advanced payments are exempt from consideration as income (MPG 10.02.01 and Desk Aid 56 – MAGI Income and Deduction Types). • Resource The Asset test for Medi-Cal was eliminated effective 1/1/2024. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach Number Page CW 24-01 CF 24-02 MC 24-01 GR 24-01 CAPI 24-01 CMS 24-01 4 of 6 General Relief (GR) • Income General Relief considers EITC payments as unearned income in the month received (GRPG 90 - 400.5F). If a customer received General Relief during 202 3, and the customer receives EITC, the case must be reviewed for potential unreported earned income since EITC is for earned income. • Resource Any portion of the refund retained by the customer in the month following receipt is considered personal property (GRPG 90-400.5F). Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants (CAPI) • Income CAPI exempts EITC from consideration as income in the month received (CAPI PG 99-103.2B). • Resource CAPI exempts EITC as a resource for 12 months following the month of receipt (CAPI PG 99 - 104.4B). County Medical Services (CMS) • Income CMS exempts EITC as income in the month received (CMSPG 06.01.02A). • Resource Any portion of the refund retained by the beneficiary in the month following receipt is considered exempt personal property (CMSPG 06.04.03H). Automation: On the Income List section, enter the Income as Miscellaneous Type: Tax/Refunds/Rebates/Credits. CalSAWS will count this entry as countable income for the General Relief program and will exempt as income for the CalWORKs, CalFresh, Medi-Cal, CAPI, and Refugee Cash Assistance. References: All County Information Notice No. I-74-23 All County Information Notice No. I-74-23E Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by February 28,2025. title: SN 23-05 Adult Expansion for Individuals Ages 26 to 49
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice Adult Expansion for Individuals Ages 26 to 49 Number Page 23-05 1 of 2 Effective Date January 1, 2024 Background: Senate Bill (SB) 184 expands full scope Medi-Cal (MC) eligibility to California (CA) residents that are ages 26 to 49 regardless of immigration status. Purpose: To provide adult expansion policies and the informational material available to promote this change. Policy: Beginning January 1, 2024 all customers may receive full scope benefits regardless of age, citizenship, or immigration status. There are no new aid codes for this expansion. Customers will be placed in their applicable Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) and/or Non-MAGI aid codes. Attachment A provides a crosswalk from restricted to full scope MAGI and Non- MAGI aid code categories. Retroactive requests for months prior to January 1, 2024, will be evaluated based on regulations in effect prior to implementation of Adult Expansion. Examples: Scenario A customer applies and turns 50 in January 2024 and requests retroactive coverage. Outcome Grant restricted scope for any of the three retroactive months. Scenario A customer applies and turns 26 in January 2024 and requests retroactive coverage. Outcome Grant full scope benefits under the Young Adult Expansion for any of the three retroactive months. Scenario A customer applies who is 46 in January 2024 and requests retroactive coverage. Outcome They will be eligible to restricted scope for November 2023 and December 2023. Beginning January 2024, they will be eligible full scope benefits. Managed Care Plans (MCP) Adult Expansion customers may enroll in a MCP beginning January 1,2024. Those who do not select a MCP will be auto enrolled in a plan and will be able to make changes to their plan by contacting Health Care Options at 1-800-430-4263. The following notices have been mailed by the Department of Health Care Services (DHCS): • M edi-Cal MCP Enrollment Notice mailed on December 1, 2023 explaining what a MCP is, the requirement of enrolling in a health plan, and how to enroll. • M edi-Cal Choice Packets mailed in November 2023. Procedure: Citizenship and immigration status verification requirements have not changed. Staff must continue to grant customers Reasonable Opportunity Period (ROP) to obtain and verify citizenship status. If … Then continue full scope benefits … after the ROP the customer fails to provide citizenship/immigration verification, enter the appropriate citizenship/immigration status fields in the CalSAWS and check MEDS for aid code. a signed MC 13 is not returned, enter the appropriate citizenship/immigration status County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice Adult Expansion for Individuals Ages 26 to 49 Number Page 23-05 2 of 2 fields in the CalSAWS and check MEDS for aid code. The following resources are available: • How To 102 guidance on adding or updating citizenship status in CalSAWS. • Desk Aid 115 Non-Immigrant Visas and California Residence. • Desk Aid 116 Common Employment Authorization Document (EAD) Category Codes. sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice Adult Expansion for Individuals Ages 26 to 49 Number Page 23-05 1 of 2 Effective Date January 1, 2024 Background: Senate Bill (SB) 184 expands full scope Medi-Cal (MC) eligibility to California (CA) residents that are ages 26 to 49 regardless of immigration status. Purpose: To provide adult expansion policies and the informational material available to promote this change. Policy: Beginning January 1, 2024 all customers may receive full scope benefits regardless of age, citizenship, or immigration status. There are no new aid codes for this expansion. Customers will be placed in their applicable Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) and/or Non-MAGI aid codes. Attachment A provides a crosswalk from restricted to full scope MAGI and Non- MAGI aid code categories. Retroactive requests for months prior to January 1, 2024, will be evaluated based on regulations in effect prior to implementation of Adult Expansion. Examples: Scenario A customer applies and turns 50 in January 2024 and requests retroactive coverage. Outcome Grant restricted scope for any of the three retroactive months. Scenario A customer applies and turns 26 in January 2024 and requests retroactive coverage. Outcome Grant full scope benefits under the Young Adult Expansion for any of the three retroactive months. Scenario A customer applies who is 46 in January 2024 and requests retroactive coverage. Outcome They will be eligible to restricted scope for November 2023 and December 2023. Beginning January 2024, they will be eligible full scope benefits. Managed Care Plans (MCP) Adult Expansion customers may enroll in a MCP beginning January 1,2024. Those who do not select a MCP will be auto enrolled in a plan and will be able to make changes to their plan by contacting Health Care Options at 1-800-430-4263. The following notices have been mailed by the Department of Health Care Services (DHCS): • M edi-Cal MCP Enrollment Notice mailed on December 1, 2023 explaining what a MCP is, the requirement of enrolling in a health plan, and how to enroll. • M edi-Cal Choice Packets mailed in November 2023. Procedure: Citizenship and immigration status verification requirements have not changed. Staff must continue to grant customers Reasonable Opportunity Period (ROP) to obtain and verify citizenship status. If … Then continue full scope benefits … after the ROP the customer fails to provide citizenship/immigration verification, enter the appropriate citizenship/immigration status fields in the CalSAWS and check MEDS for aid code. a signed MC 13 is not returned, enter the appropriate citizenship/immigration status County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice Adult Expansion for Individuals Ages 26 to 49 Number Page 23-05 2 of 2 fields in the CalSAWS and check MEDS for aid code. The following resources are available: • How To 102 guidance on adding or updating citizenship status in CalSAWS. • Desk Aid 115 Non-Immigrant Visas and California Residence. • Desk Aid 116 Common Employment Authorization Document (EAD) Category Codes. Note: Desk Aid 105 is obsolete with the issuance of this notice. Automation Impact: The California Healthcare Eligibility, Enrollment, and Retention System (CalHEERS) and CalSAWS have been programed to grant full scope benefits effective January 1, 2024. CalSAWS began transitioning existing customers and sending advance notices on November 1, 2023, for January 2024 eligibility. Unsuccessfully transitioned case exception and online correspondence report will be shared after automation run. Informational Material: Flyers have been posted to the Community Partner Resource Toolkit and Medi-Cal Program websites and can be ordered through Xerox Print Services. References: ACWDL 23-08 W&IC 14007.8 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 01/31/2025. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Dire

title: SN 23-06 Asset Elimination
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice Asset Elimination for Non-Modified Adjust Gross Income (MAGI) Number Page 23-06 1 of 4 Effective Date January 1, 2024 Background: Assembly Bill (AB) 133 signed into law July 27, 2021, eliminates the asset test to determine eligibility for Non-Modified Adjust Gross Income (MAGI) Medi-Cal Programs in two phases. Phase 1 was implemented on July 1, 2022, which increased asset limits for all Non-MAGI programs to $130,000 per individual and $65,000 for each additional member (up to 10). Phase 2 is effective as of January 1, 2024, to eliminate the asset test completely for Non- MAGI programs including Long Term Care (LTC) and Medicare Savings Programs (MSP). Purpose: To provide asset elimination policies when determining eligibility to all Non-MAGI programs. Policy: Beginning January 1, 2024, all customers both new intake applications and ongoing cases, will be evaluated without requiring verification of assets when determining eligibility. Treatment of income for Non-MAGI programs as noted in the Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) Article 10 have not changed. Request information only to verify the income amount received from income producing assets and frequency of distributions. • Customers denied in December 2023 for reason of Over Property must be re-evaluated for eligibility January 2024 and ongoing. • Customers denied for the reason of over property in the past 6 months prior to implementation will receive a one-time outreach letter by early March 2024, to inform them of the new regulations and encourage them to reapply. Procedure: Income Producing Assets Reference table below for clarification of Income Producing Assets as it relates to Asset Elimination. Asset Type Description Annuities Any undistributed balance is no longer considered . Customers are no longer required to take any period distributions from an annuity as a condition of eligibility. Individual Retirement Arrangements (IRAs), Retirement Plans for customers that are Self-Employed (formerly known as Keoghs) and Work Related Pension Funds The cash value of these plans is no longer considered. Customers are no longer required to receive any periodic payments from these funds as a condition of eligibility and are not considered as unconditionally available income. Income from Real Property Property utilization is no longer a requirement. Trusts A t rust principal is no longer considered . Continue to request trust documentation to review the terms of the trust regarding distributions. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice Asset Elimination for Non-Modified Adjust Gross Income (MAGI) Number Page 23-06 2 of 4 Interest and Dividend Income The value of the asset for which Interest or Dividend s income is received are not considered. Estate Recovery The Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) will continue to seek repayment from the estates of deceased Medi -Cal customers who meet the criteria as stated in MPG Section 16.03. Asset information for Estate Recovery purposes should not be requested from customers. Refer all E state Recovery inquiries to: • Estate Recovery website https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/services/Pages/TPLRD_ER_cont.aspx. • DHCS Third Party Liability and Recovery Division ER@dhcs.ca.gov or (916) 650-0590. Overpayments Follow MPG 16.02 when establishing overpayments due to income and failure to report other health coverage discovered. Overpayments due to excess property must not be established on or after January 1, 2024. Spousal Impoverishment (SI) Effective January 1, 2024, Community Spouse Resource Allowance (CSRA) no longer applies for purposes of SI provisions. Customers requesting Medi-Cal evaluation prior to implementation date will be subject to verify property and will have CSRA applied to determine eligibility . Apply the Minimum Monthly Maintenance Needs Allowance (MMMNA) when evaluating under SI provisions. The MMMNA will continue to be updated by DHCS annually. Transfer of Assets, Period of Ineligibility (POI) and Asset Verification Program (AVP) Transfers of property completed after January 1, 2024, are no longer required to be verified. This includes transfers of lumps sums and income such as from mortgages, loans, and annuities. Review transfer of assets to determine if customers requesting LTC services and their responsible relatives made asset transfers for less than fair market value during the look back period prior to January 1, 2024, as referenced in MPG 09.07.01 using the AVP repor t. Request administrative verification if the AVP report is not: • R eturned within 20 calendar days. • S ufficient to complete the POI evaluation. Note: Only request and utilize the AVP report to determine POI during the lookback period. The number of months that will require review in the look back period decreases by one month for each month that passes after January 2024. Example: Scenario Customer applies April 2024 and is requesting LTC services Outcome The look back period would be 27 months from 10-2021 to 12-2023 as it would only include any months prior to January 2024. Please refer to Attachment A- Decreasing Look Back Period. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice Asset Elimination for Non-Modified Adjust Gross Income (MAGI) Number Page 23-06 3 of 4 Undue Hardship All cases must be reviewed for undue hardship when evaluating POI or OBRA 93 trusts. • Reference MPG 09.07.01 and 09.13.03 when evaluate undue hardship during a POI. • Reference MPG 09.14.4C when evaluating undue hardship for OBRA 93 trusts. Automation Impact: The California Statewide Welfare System (CalSAWS) has been programed and updated to no longer count or display property in the Medi-Cal eligibility determination beginning January 1, 2024. Client Correspondence and Forms Notices and forms relating to property will be available for use in CalSAWS for Retroactive Medi-Cal determinations. Updates on all other forms related to asset elimination will be shared as they are released. Renewal forms have been updated and no longer include asset information. The following forms have been obsoleted: • Medi-Cal General Property Limitations (MC 007) • Sneede v. Kizer Property Worksheet (MC 175-3 P) • Medi-Cal Property Assessment Application (MC 176 PA-A) • QMB/SLMB/QI Property Worksheet, Adult (MC 176 P-A QMB/SLMB/QI) • QMB/SLMB/QI Property Worksheet, Child (MC 176 P-C QMB/SLMB/QI) • Period of Ineligibility for Nursing Facility Level of Care Worksheet (MC 176 P-I) • QDWI Property Worksheet (MC 176 QDWI-2) • Supplement to Statement of Facts—Pickle Eligibility Determination (MC 210 B) • Property Assessment Statement of Facts (MC 210 PA) • Medi-Cal Potential Overpayment Reporting Worksheet—Property Total Ineligibility or Ineligibility for a Specific Level of Services (MC 224 B) • Tuberculosis Program Property Worksheet-Adult (MC 278 TB) • Pickle Resource Worksheet (DHCS 7037) • MC 210 PS Property Supplement • MC 322 Real and Personal Property- Supplement to Medi-Cal Mail-in Application AVP report The last monthly batch for AVP will occur December 2023 as they will become obsolete for renewals. Weekly reports will continue for requests made for customers seeking LTC services and their responsible relatives. title: SN 23-07 January 2024 Social Security Cost of Living Adjustment and Related Changes
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Special Notice January 2024 Social Security Administration (SSA) Cost of Living (COLA) Adjustment and Related Changes Number 23-07 Page 1 of 2 Effective Date: 1/1/2024 Background: The annual Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA) occurs for Social Security (SSA) Title I payments, Supplemental Security Income (SSI)/State Supplementary Payment (SSP) payments, the In-Kind Support and Maintenance (ISM) levels for computing Pickle eligibility, 2023 Pickle Disregard computation chart, Federal Benefit Rate, Medicare Premiums, Substantial Gainful Activity (SGA), and the SSI standard and parental allocation amounts. Purpose: To provide guidance for processing the 2024 SSA COLA and update the Medi-Cal Assistance Standards chart with 2024 values. Policy: There will be a 3.2 percent COLA increase to SSA Title II Retirement, Survivors, and Disability Insurance payments effective January 1, 2024. This increase will not apply to Federal Poverty Level (FPL) programs (Aged and Disabled FPL, Blind FPL, and Medicare Savings Programs) until April 2024. The California Healthcare Eligibility, Enrollment, and Retention System (CalHEERS) is not running a COLA update until the FPLs are updated in April, so Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) cases will not be affected at this time. The Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) will notify affected MAGI beneficiaries when CalHEERS runs the COLA update next year. Beneficiaries may contact the county for a re-evaluation back to January 1, 2024, if they were impacted. Do not apply the COLA prematurely to FPL and MAGI based programs. Program Impact/s: The California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) applied the COLA and completed a mass update of Medi-Cal cases over the weekend of December 02, 2023. Cases that did not have the SSA income or Medicare Part B premium amounts) updated must be reviewed and authorized. The lists will be available on SharePoint. NOTE: Cases that are in the continuous coverage group were not authorized in the COLA run and must be reviewed during their annual renewal month. title: SN 23-03 2023 Statewide Average Private Pay Rate for Nursing Facility Services
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice 2023 Statewide Average Private Pay Rate (APPR) for Nursing Facility Level of Care Services Number Page 23-03 1 of 1 Effective Date 04/01/2023 Background: The Statewide Average Private Pay Rate (APPR) for Nursing Facility Level of Care (NFLOC) services is used when calculating the period of ineligibility (POI) for transfers of non-exempt property which are less than fair market value (FMV). Purpose: To provide staff with the updated APPR figure and procedure. Policy: Effective January 1, 2023, the APPR amount for NFLOC services is $11,576. • The 2023 APPR figure must not be used to recalculate periods of ineligibility for NFLOC if the date of application or the date of institutionalization occurred before January 1, 2023. Procedure: Use the updated APPR figure when determining a POI that occurs in 2023 due to an uncompensated transfer of property as referenced in Medi-Cal Program Guide 09.07.01. Automation Impact: Calculate each uncompensated transfer manually using form MC 176 PI and updated APPR amount . When a POI is determined enter the begin and end date on the Display Sanction/POI/Penalty Detail Screen to transmit the restriction code 951 to MEDS. Image form MC 176 PI into the CalWIN Electronic Records Management System (CERMS) and enter detailed case comments. References: ACWDL 23-06 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 04/30/2024. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: SN 23-02 2023 Medicare Catastrophic Coverage Act Spousal Impoverishment Caps and Federal Poverty Levels23
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice 2023 Medicare Catastrophic Coverage Act Spousal Impoverishment Caps and 2023 Federal Poverty Level (FPL) Increase Number Page 23-02 1 of 3 Effective Date 02/01/2023 Background: The federal poverty levels (FPLs) used in determining financial eligibility to Medi -Cal programs are adjusted annually to allow for changes to the cost of living. The Community Spouse Resource Allowance (CSRA) is the amount of countable property a community spouse is allowed to retain when they have an institutionalized or Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) spouse applying for Medi-Cal benefits. The Minimum Monthly Maintenance Nee ds Allowance (MMMNA) is the income allocation from the institutionalized/HCBS spouse’s income to the community spouse. The CSRA and MMMNA are also updated annually. Purpose: To provide staff with the 2023 FPL, CSRA, and MMMNA values and procedures. Policy: 2023 CSRA and MMMNA Effective January 1, 2023, the CSRA and MMMNA amounts are as follows: CSRA $148,620 MMMNA $3,716 2023 FPL Increases Use the updated 2023 FPLs values when determining eligibility for the appropriate programs referenced in Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 11.1A Assistance Standards: • For applicants and beneficiaries of the Medicare Savings Programs (MSP): Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB), Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary (SLMB), and Qualified Individual (QI) who do not receive Title II Retirement Survivors and Disability Insurance (RSDI) income, the new FPL values must be applied retroactively to January 1, 2023. • For MSP customers who are receiving Title II RSDI income , apply the n ew FPL values retroactively to March 1, 2023. • For individuals who are eligible for Aged, Blind, and Disabled (ABD) FPL programs and 250% Working Disabled Program (WDP), apply the updated FPL values effective April 1, 2023. • For customers whose Medi-Cal eligibility is based upon Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) methodologies, apply the FPLs retroactively to January 1, 2023. Procedure: 2023 CSRA and MMNA Use the updated CSRA and MMMNA standards when determining spousal impoverishment for an institutionalized or HCBS spouse. 2023 FPL Increases Review all denials and discontinuances back to the date specified for each group and re -evaluate eligibility based on the revised FPLs. Upon request from the beneficiary, the beneficiary’s parent or legal guardian, or the beneficiary’s authorized representative, staff must retroactively change eligibility for the following circumstances: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice 2023 Medicare Catastrophic Coverage Act Spousal Impoverishment Caps and 2023 Federal Poverty Level (FPL) Increase Number Page 23-02 2 of 3 • Advanced Premium Tax Credit (APTC) eligible individuals who did not enroll in a Qualified Health Plan (QHP) or did not pay a premium. • APTC eligible individuals who enroll in a QHP and pay a premium but have Medi-Cal covered medical or dental expenses that were not covered by their QHP during the retroactive period. • Individuals with a Share-of-Cost (SOC) who are redetermined eligible to zero SOC or lower SOC when using the 2023 FPLs, who had out of pocket expenses for covered medical or dental services may be eligible for retroactive Medi-Cal out-of-pocket expense reimbursements (Conlan). Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 04.02.10J Beneficiary Reimbursement Process for more information. • Optional Targeted Low-Income Children’s Program (OTLICP) eligible children. OTLICP premiums have been reduced to $0 as of July 1, 2022. Note: When determining retroactive eligibility for months in 2022, use the FPLs and related charts for 2022. Automation Impact: An Exception List will be sent to Family Resource Centers (FRCs) for action on cases that do not automatically authorize when California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids Informati on Network (CalWIN) updates with the new 2023 amounts along with instructions on how to process these cases. FRCs will be notified when these lists are placed on the SharePoint website under Medi-Cal Report to review and process Notices of Action (NOAs) he ld in the print queue. 2023 CSRA and MMNA Staff must use BEnDS 49130 Spousal Impoverishment Provisions until the CSRA and MMMNA values have been updated in CalWIN when determining spousal impoverishment. 2023 FPL Increase The FPL tables were updated in CalWIN on the weekend of February 18, 2023. The following case types were included in the FPL COLA run: • Non-MAGI. • Mixed (MAGI and Non-MAGI). • APTC and Non-MAGI. The following case types were excluded from the FPL COLA run: • MAGI only. • Mixed (MAGI and APTC). • Pre-ACA (no evaluation for MAGI completed). References: ACWDLs 23-01, 23-03 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 03/31/2024. title: SN 23-01 Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach Number Page CW 23-02 CF 23-03 MC 23-01 GR 23-01 CAPI 23-01 CMS 23-01 1 of 4 Effective Date: February 1, 2023 Background: San Diego County’s Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) campaign continues to provide services annually. These materials are provided to supplement EITC outreach efforts and are revised to reflect changes each tax year. Purpose: The purpose of this Special Notice is to provide revised federal EITC, California EITC (CalEITC) as well as other tax credit income limits, maximum credit amounts, and their impact on self -sufficiency programs. This material also provides resources to assist customers to access tax credits they are potentially eligible for. Policy: Age and General EITC Eligibility California tax filers may qualify for either federal and/or state EITC depending on their income, age, and number of children. Refer to Appendix A for income limits and credit amounts. F ederal EITC Eligibility: • Must have earned income and adjusted gross income within certain limits, but must be at least $1 • Must meet certain basic rules. For example, have a valid Social Security Number (SSN) • Must meet qualifying child rules if any dependent children are claimed • Must live in the United States for more than half the tax year • Claiming the federal EITC requires the Schedule EIC form available on the EITC webpage or by calling the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) at 800-829-1040 C alEITC Eligibility: • CalEITC is available to qualified tax filers ages 18 to 65 without qualifying children or any age with qualifying children • Must have an SSN or an Individual Tax Identification Number (ITIN) for undocumented individuals • Must have earned income and adjusted gross income of at least $1 and less than $30,000 • Must meet certain Internal Revenue Service (IRS) basic rules such as having an SSN or ITIN • Must meet qualifying child rules if any dependent children claimed • Must live in California for more than half the tax year • Claiming the CalEITC requires the FTB 3514 form available on the CalEITC website or by contacting the Franchise Tax Board by phone at 800-852-5711 N ote: California taxpayers may qualify for state credits even if they do not qualify for federal credits. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach Number Page CW 23-02 CF 23-03 MC 23-01 GR 23-01 CAPI 23-01 CMS 23-01 2 of 4 New Foster Youth Tax Credit (FYTC) Eligible current and former foster youth who file their California state tax return and claim the FYTC will receive up to $1,083 in tax credits. The credit amount is adjusted for inflation annually and phases out gradually as income rises above $25,000. The FTYC is awarded per eligible individual. An individual may qualify for FYTC if they meet all the following criteria: • Qualify for the CalEITC • Were ages 18 through 25 at the end of the 2022 tax year • Were in foster care at age 13 or older and placed through the California foster care system Expanded Young Child Tax Credit (YCTC) The YCTC has been expanded for the 2022 tax year. The YCTC increased to $1,083 per family. Families must have at least one child under six years old at the end of the tax year and must file a California state tax return and meet the requirements of the CalEITC. Beginning in the 2022 tax year, taxpayers do not need to have earned income to be eligible if they otherwise meet CalEITC requirements. If filing for prior years, customer must have at least $1 of earned income to qualify. Procedure: Free Tax Preparation Services Free tax preparation services are available for low to moderate income individuals. Customers can call 2-1-1 for more information. Customers can also log on to: • https://211sandiego.org/ • https://www.myfreetaxes.org/ MyFreeTaxes.com is operated by United Way Worldwide and offers free state and federal tax preparation and filing services. For the 2022 tax year, tax filers will have the option to choose to file “By Myself,” “With Assistance” or “I’m Not Sure”. Based on their request, the information will be routed to the appropriate tax preparation model through a virtual assistant software, or in -person drop off. Ser vices are free for households with earnings less than $60,000 for in person help or $66,000 or less if filing with virtual help. • https://www.getyourrefund.org/en For the 2022 tax year, United Way has partnered with Code for America to provide virtual free tax credit services with IRS certified volunteers for household with earnings less than $66,000 • https://www.eitc.irs.gov • https://www.irs.gov/ • www.ftb.ca.gov/caleitc • https://www.sco.ca.gov/eo_vita.html The IRS Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) Program offers free tax assistance to households with income of $60,000 or less. For the 2022 tax year, these services will be predominantly virtual or will require an appointment due to the COVID-19 pandemic. EITC Postcards The County of San Diego’s Community Action Partnership (CAP) and local nonprofit agency Dreams for Change will coordinate distribution of EITC postcards and virtual EITC presentations to various County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach Number Page CW 23-02 CF 23-03 MC 23-01 GR 23-01 CAPI 23-01 CMS 23-01 3 of 4 Family Resource Centers (FRCs) and Employment Services (ES) sites as requested. Postcards (see Appendix B) will be distributed to ES, Refugee Employment Services (RES), Public Health Clinics, City and County libraries, schools, and Child Care contractors. I n addition, a flyer (Appendix A) containing postcard information with VITA site locations and phone numbers is being distributed via SMS message to CalWORKs, CalFresh and Medi-Cal customers and is available on the sandiegocounty.gov w ebsite. Th ese EITC publications: • Strengthen state and county efforts to promote the EITC to our customer population • Target families and individuals who qualify for EITC • Educate and assist families on how to access EITC FRC, ES, RES and Child Care Staff Action FRC and contracted staff will distribute these postcards to c ustomers at all contacts and encourage them to contact 2-1-1 to receive free assistance to file their taxes and claim EITC and other tax credits available to them . If additional postcards are needed, FRC /ES Managers, or their designees, may contact the Community Action Partnership at (619) 338-2799. Impacts: CalWORKs and CalFresh • Income Federal and state EITC payments, whether received as advanced payments or as a single payment, are exempt as income in determining CalWORKs and CalFresh eligibility or benefits level (CPG 44- 100.H2; CFPG 63-224, 63-224) • R esource EITC payments and refund payments are exempt resources for 12 months, starting with the month that the payment is received (CPG 44-100.H2; CFPG 63-203, 63-204) Medi-Cal • Income EITC payments received as tax refunds or advanced payments are exempt from consideration as income (MPG 10.02.01 and Desk Aid 56 – MAGI Income and Deduction Types) • R esource Actual EITC payments are exempt property in the month following the month of receipt (MPG 09.06.01M) General Relief (GR) • Income General Relief considers EITC payments as unearned income in the month received (GRPG 90- 400.5F). If a customer received General Relief during 2022, and the customer receives EITC, the case must be reviewed for potential unreported earned income since EITC is for earned income County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalWORKs/CalFresh/Medi-Cal/General Relief/Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants/County Medical Services Program Guide Special Notice Earned Income Tax Credit Outreach Number Page CW 23-02 CF 23-03 MC 23-01 GR 23-01 CAPI 23-01 CMS 23-01 4 of 4 • Resource Any portion of the refund retained by the customer in the month following receipt is considered personal property (GRPG 90-400.5F) Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants (CAPI) • Income CAPI exempts EITC from consideration as income in the month received (CAPI PG 99-103.2B) • R esource CAPI exempts EITC as a resource for 12 months following the month of receipt (CAPI PG 99- 104.4B) County Medical Services (CMS) • Income CMS exempts EITC as income in the month received (CMSPG 06.01.02A) • R esource Any portion of the refund retained by the beneficiary in the month following receipt is considered exempt personal property (CMSPG 06.04.03H) Automation: • On the Collect Unearned Income Detail window Type field, select Earned Income Tax Credit: actual money received as earnings/refund from the drop-down menu. CalWIN will count this entry as countable income for the General Relief program and will exempt as income for the CalWORKs, CalFresh, Medi-Cal, CAPI, and Refugee Cash Assistance. References: All County Information Notice No. I-87-22 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by February 29, 2024. Approval for Release: R ick Wanne, Director Self-S ufficiency Service EITC Income Limits 2022 CalEITC Income Limits: 2022 Federal EITC Income Limits: • Individuals/families earning $1- $60,000 per year can get free tax assistance and may qualify to claim the federal tax credits • Individuals/families earning $1- $30,000 may be eligible for additional state tax credits • Undocumented ITIN filers • Photo ID • Social Security Card or ITIN for yourself and any dependents • Income documents including any W2s or 1099s • Bank account information for direct deposit • School tuition or student loan interest statements • Dates of health coverage for yourself and any dependents How To File Call 2-1-1 or go to myfreetaxes.org to see if you qualify and make an appointment. Tax preparation services are available in multiple languages. In-person and virtual online assistance is available. If you don’t help filing your taxes, you can still file online at no cost, if you qualify, by going to myfreetaxes.org. This program is brought to you by the San Diego County EITC Coalition and the following partners: FILE YOUR TAXES FOR FREE! ¡Reciba asistencia gratuita para la declaración de impuestos en línea or en un centro de Asistencia Voluntaria para los impuestos (VITA, por sus siglas en inglés)! Usted puede calificar para recibir el Crédito Tributario por Ingreso del Trabajo (EITC por sus siglas en inglés) y el Crédito Tributario por Hijos (CTC por sus siglas en inglés); los cuales corresponden a créditos tributarios federales que pueden significar un reembolso mayor. El EITC de California (CalEITC) y el Crédito Tributario por Hijos Menores (YCTC, por sus siglas en inglés) corresponden a créditos tributarios estatales que pueden reembolsarle aún más dinero. También existen otros créditos tributarios. ¡Nuestros preparadores de impuestos de confianza comprobarán si tiene derecho a estos créditos en su declaración de impuesto! Call 2-1-1 or visit myfreetaxes.org to learn more! Receive free tax filing assistance online or at a VITA (Volunteer Income Tax Assistance) site! You may qualify for the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) and Child Tax Credit (CTC), which are federal tax credits that can put money back in your pocket. The California EITC (CalEITC) and Young Child Tax Credit are state tax credits that can give you even more money back. Other tax credits are available too. Our trusted tax preparers will check if you qualify for these credits on your tax return! ¡Llame al 2-1-1 o visite myfreetaxes.org para obtener más información! ¿Quiénes son elegibles? • Los individuos o familias que ganen entre $1 y $60,000 al año pueden obtener asistencia tributaria gratuita y pueden calificar los créditos tributarios federales • Los individuos o familias que ganen entre $1 y $30,000 pueden calificar para creditos tributarios estatales adicionales • Los contribuyentes indocumentados con ITIN Qué necesitarás • Identificación con foto • Tarjeta de Seguro Social o ITIN de usted y sus dependientes • Documentos de ingreso, incluyendo formularios W2 o 1099 • Información de la cuenta bancaria para el depósito directo • Declaraciones de la matrícula escolar o de los intereses de los préstamos estudiantiles • Fechas de la cobertura médica para usted y sus dependientes Cómo declarar Llame al 2-1-1 o visite myfreetaxes.org para ver si cumple los requisitos y para que obtenga una cita. Asistencia disponible en persona y virtual en línea. Los servicios de preparación de impuestos están disponibles en varios idiomas. Si cumple con los requisitos y no necesita ayuda para declarar sus impuestos, puede hacerlo en línea sin costo alguno visitando myfreetaxes.org. For example, have a valid Social Security Number (SSN) • Must meet qualifying child rules if any dependent children are claimed • Must live in the United States for more than half the tax year • Claiming the federal EITC requires the Schedule EIC form available on the EITC webpage or by calling the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) at 800-829-1040 C alEITC Eligibility: • CalEITC is available to qualified tax filers ages 18 to 65 without qualifying children or any age with qualifying children • Must have an SSN or an Individual Tax Identification Number (ITIN) for undocumented individuals • Must have earned income and adjusted gross income of at least $1 and less than $30,000 • Must meet certain Internal Revenue Service (IRS) basic rules such as having an SSN or ITIN • Must meet qualifying child rules if any dependent children claimed • Must live in California for more than half the tax year • Claiming the CalEITC requires the FTB 3514 form available on the CalEITC website or by contacting the Franchise Tax Board by phone at 800-852-5711 N ote: California taxpayers may qualify for state credits even if they do not qualify for federal credits. title: SN 22-10 January 2023 Social Security Administration Cost of Living Adjustment and Related Changes
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Special Notice January 2023 Social Security Administration (SSA) Cost of Living (COLA) Adjustment and Related Changes Number 22-10 Page 1 of 2 Effective Date: January 1, 2023 Background: The annual Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA) for Social Security Administration (SSA) Title II benefits is 8.7 percent and is effective January 1, 2023. There are also annual updates to the Supplemental Security Income (SSI)/State Supplementary Payment (SSP) payment rate, the In-Kind Support and Maintenance levels (ISM) for computing Pickle eligibility, the 2023 Pickle Disregard computation chart the Federal Benefit Rate, Medicare Premiums, Substantial Gainful Activity (SGA), and the SSI standard and parental allocation amounts. Purpose: To provide guidance for processing the 2023 SSA COLA and update the Medi-Cal Assistance Standards chart with 2023 values. Policy: There will be an 8.7 percent COLA increase to SSA Title II Retirement, Survivors, and Disability Insurance payments effective January 1, 2023. This increase will not apply to Federal Poverty Level (FPL) programs (Aged and Disabled FPL, Blind FPL, and Medicare Savings Programs) until April 2023. The California Healthcare Eligibility, Enrollment, and Retention System (CalHEERS) is not running a COLA update until later in 2023, so Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) cases will not be affected at this time. The Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) will notify affected MAGI beneficiaries when CalHEERS runs its COLA update next year. Beneficiaries may contact the county for a re- evaluation back to January 1, 2023, if they were impacted. The suspension of negative actions due to the public health emergency applies to processing the COLA change. Do not apply negative actions including increases in Share of Cost until the end of the public health emergency. Use the updated 2023 Maintenance Need Assistance Standards chart values for the following: • SSI/SSP Payment cash grant levels for determining Pickle eligibility • ISM for determining Pickle eligibility Pickle disregard computation chart Federal Benefit Rate • SSI standard and parental allocation amounts Medicare Premiums • SGA Procedure: Use the updated Maintenance Need Assistance Standards chart when evaluating the appropriate programs. Do not apply the COLA prematurely to FPL and MAGI based programs. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Special Notice January 2023 Social Security Administration (SSA) Cost of Living (COLA) Adjustment and Related Changes Page 2 of 2 Program Impacts: Automation The California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids Information Network (CalWIN) applied the COLA and completed a mass update of Medi-Cal cases over the weekend of December 03, 2022. Cases that exception out of the authorization must be reviewed and authorized. The exception list will be available on SharePoint. Some Client Correspondence will be held online and must be reviewed for appropriateness prior to mailing. Program will send the list to Family Resource Centers via email. References: ACWDLs 22-29, 22-30, and 22-31. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 12/31/2023. Approval for Release: Ou Elagot sor Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: SN 22-09 - TB Program Income Limit
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Special Notice 2022 Tuberculosis (TB) Program Income Limit Number 22-09 Page 1 of 1 Effective Date: 1/1/2022 Background: The TB Program provides medical assistance for individuals infected with tuberculosis who are ineligible to other Medi-Cal programs and whose income and resources fall within specific limits. Purpose: To inform staff of the new TB Program income limit. Policy: Effective 1/1/2022, the income limit for the TB Program is $1,767. If Human Service Specialists (HSS) are made aware of an individual denied for exceeding the income limit since 1/1/2022 or the property limit since 7/1/2022, re-evaluate using the new income or property standard. title: SN 22-07 Increase to the Reasonable Compatibility Threshold in CalHEERS
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice Increase to the Reasonable Compatibility Threshold in the California Healthcare Eligibility, Enrollment and Retention System (CalHEERS) Number 22-07 Page 1 of 2 Effective Date 07/01/2022 Background: To determine eligibility for Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) Medi-Cal, California Healthcare Eligibility, Enrollment and Retention System (CalHEERS) electronically compares self-attested income with the Federal Data Services Hub (FDSH), to determine if the self-attested income reported by applicants and beneficiaries are reasonably compatible. CalHEERS makes individual determinations based on income tax and household compositions and identifies when income is at or below the MAGI Federal Poverty Level (FPL) or a reasonable compatibility threshold as electronically verified (e- verified). Purpose: To notify staff of the temporary increase to the MAGI and Medi-Cal Access Program (MCAP) income reasonable compatibility threshold from 10% to 20% from July 2022 through the end of the Public Health Emergency (PHE) unwinding period. This temporary increase will allow continued coverage for customers and reduce requests for a reasonable explanation or additional income verification from the customer. Policy: The reasonable compatibility threshold increased temporarily to 20% effective 7/1/2022 for MAGI and MCAP. Staff are to accept results when income is e-verified and must not request further income verification at application, change in circumstance or annual redetermination (RV) (when RV's are reinstated). Customers may report self-attested income via CalHEERS or by contacting the county. Note: The federal poverty levels (FPL) remain unchanged. Procedure: When a referral from CalHEERs is received or when staff enter self-attested income in CalWIN and the CalHEERS Business Rules Engine (BRE) is run and the determination eligibility response (DER) is received: • If the income was found to be reasonably compatible and is e-verified for any household member, accept the results. • If the results are not reasonably compatible for any other household member, request a reasonable explanation or additional verification as noted in MPG 4.07 to determine eligibility to MAGI Medi-Cal. Note: When the BRE is initiated after the implementation date, the 20% threshold will be applied back to the date of application, and any retroactive month/s if a request is received. Example: Application is received June 12, 2022, with a request for retroactive month of May 2022. The Human Services Specialist (HSS) processes the application on July 30, 2022, and self-attested income is e-verified within the new threshold. Since the CalHEERs BRE was initiated in July when the threshold increased, customer is also eligible for May 2022 and June 2022. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice Increase to the Reasonable Compatibility Threshold in the California Healthcare Eligibility, Enrollment and Retention System (CalHEERS) Number 22-07 Page 2 of 2 Automation Impact: No impact. With Release 22.6 implementation, CalHEERS allows the MAGI reasonable compatibility threshold by 20% for MAGI and MCAP. References: ACWDL 22-17 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 12/31/2023. Approval for Release: t fox Rick Wanne, Director Self Sufficiency Services

title: SN 22-05 2022 Medicare Savings Programs Property Limit
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice 2022 Medicare Savings Program Property Limit Number 22-05 Page 1 of 2 Effective Date 07/01/2022 Background: The Medicare Savings Programs (MSP) are the Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB), Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary (SLMB), Qualifying Individual (QI), and Qualified Disabled and Working Individual (QDWI) programs. These programs assist individuals with low income and assets in paying some or all their Medicare premiums, deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance. Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide section 05.13 for policy on MSP programs. Purpose: To provide staff with the 2022 MSP Property limit. Policy: Effective January 1, 2022, MSP property limits have increased to $8,400 for an individual and $12,600 for a couple. Note: Effective July 1, 2022, the asset limits for Non-MAGI programs have increased to $130,000 for an individual and $65,000 for each additional household member up to a maximum of 10 people. These increased limits apply to Non-MAGI programs including Long Term Care (LTC) and MSPs. Procedure: Use the increased 2022 MSP property limit when determining eligibility for the appropriate programs. Offices will be provided with an MSP Denial/Discontinuance report. Staff must review each individual and take the following actions: • Rescind the MSP denial or discontinuance action. • Re-run EDBC and capture the MSP evaluation back to the denial/discontinuance date. • Review Wrap-up to ensure that countable resources are evaluated against the 2022 MSP property limits from January 2022 to June 2022. • Issue the appropriate Notice of Action (NOA). • Enter detailed case comments regarding actions taken on the case. Automation Impact: PPM 61924 was implemented on June 27, 2022, updating the California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids Information Network (CalWIN). References: ACWDL 22-06 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 7/31/2025. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice 2022 Medicare Savings Program Property Limit Number 22-05 Approval for Release: It for: Rick Wanne, Direc Self-Sufficiency Services Page 2 of 2

title: SN 22-06 2022-2023 Family Members Base Allocation Amount
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice 2022/2023 Family Members Base Allocation Amount Number 22-06 Page 1 of 1 Effective Date July 1, 2022 Background: The Family Members Base Allocation (FMBA) amount is used when determining how much income an institutionalized or Home and Community Based Services (HBCS) spouse may allocate to family members. Purpose: To inform staff of the new FMBA amount. Policy: Effective July 1, 2022, the FMBA amount is $2,289. Procedure: Effective July 1, 2022, use the updated FMBA to calculate allocations to spouses and dependent family members of an institutionalized or HCBS spouse. For cases that used the 2021-2022 amount of $2, 178, recalculate the FMBA with the updated amount of $2,289. Automation Impact: Until the FMBA is updated in the California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids Network (CalWIN), calculate the FMBA manually and override to the appropriate aid code or share-of-cost (SOC). Image the manual budgets into the CalWIN Electronic Records Management System (CERMS) and enter detailed case comments regarding all case actions taken. References: ACWDL 22-16 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 6/30/2023 Approval for Release: li Elay at for: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency
