title: SN 13-09 Health Care Reform Medi-Cal and Low Income Health Program Addendum A - MAGI Eligibility Requirements
content: Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice (SN) 13-09, Addendum A December 09, 2013 Subject HEALTH CARE REFORM (HCR) MEDI -CAL AND LOW INCOME HEALTH PROGRAM Effective Upon receipt Reference MEDIL I 13 - 12 Purpose To inform staff of:  Eligibility requirements for MAGI Medi -Cal and Advance Premium Tax Credit (APTC) programs.  Special processing requirement for Disability Determination Services Division (DDSD) cases. Instructions will be provided in future program material on:  County Medical Services (CMS)  Low Income Health Program (LIHP)  Refugee Medi-Cal Assistance (RMA) Background MPG SN 13 -09 provided HCR requirements that affected our application business process and LIHP transition information to Medi- Cal. Under Health Care Reform, also known as the Affordable Care Act, eligibility to the expanded Medi -Cal programs and APTC will be calculated using a household’s Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI). Beginning January 1, 2014, single adults wit hout children, ages 19-64, with income at or below 138% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) , will be eligible to MAGI Medi-Cal. Enrollment began October 1, 2013; if eligible, coverage starts as soon as January 1, 2014. If income exceeds 138% FPL, but is under 400% FPL, individuals may qualify for APTC. APTC is a federal assistance program used to assist individuals and families obtain health insurance by redu cing the monthly premium amount . Covered California offer s four different health plan levels that provides a range of premiums and benefit levels with the applicants ’ share of health care costs ranging from 10% - 40%. These are:  Platinum  Gold  Silver  Bronze If enrolled in a silver -level Covered California health plan and their income is above 138% FPL but under 250% FPL, consumers may also receive cost-sharing reductions (CSR). If an application is submitted to the County, H SS staff are responsible for processing APTC/ CSR applications prior to transferring case information and/or documents to Covered California. California Healthcare, Eligibility, Enrollment, and Retention System (CalHEERS) is a new web -based portal for applications for MAGI and APTC programs. CalHEERS is used by Covered California and all California Counties. It is expected that effective January 1, 2014, CalHEERS and CalWIN will interface with worker entries completed in CalWIN. The Business Rules Engine (BRE) in CalHEERS is similar to EDBC in CalWIN, with the addition of calling the federal data hub. The program rules are programed into the BRE to evaluate income and household composition and determine eligibility to the various extended programs. The BRE will call the federal data hub to electronically verify certain data elements reported by the client. Required Action If an application for Medi -Cal is dated prior to January 1, 2014, the HSS must evaluate the application for the current Medi-Cal programs. If not eligible to current Medi-Cal, HSS must evaluate for the expanded health care programs. This evaluation includes:  Applications assigned to Health Care Reform ( HCR) specialized caseload banks  Applicant immigrants under 5 years of legal permanent resident status who do not qualify for LIHP due to immigration status  DDSD pending applications that are currently not eligible to Medi -Cal or LIHP Refer to Processing Guide 11 - CalHEERS Application P rocessing for detailed instructions. Applications dated January 1, 2014 and later will first be evaluated under MAGI rules. Non-MAGI Medi-Cal Non-MAGI Non-MAGI Medi -Cal is the new term for the existing Medi -Cal programs that will not follow MAGI rules. Asset tests wi ll continue to be required for non-MAGI Medi-Cal. Undocumented immigrants remain eligible for emergency assistance and restricted scope Medi-Cal if all eligibility requirements are met. Minor consent continues to exist. There are no changes in eligibility rules for this program at this time. Sneede v. Kizer continues to apply to the non -MAGI Medically Needy program. Non- MAGI Categories Non-MAGI categories includes:  Supplemental Security Income (SSI)  Foster Care  Aged (65 or over), Blind, Disabled  Long Term Care (LTC)  Home and Community Based Waiver  Medically Needy (MN)  250% Working Disabled  Disabled Adult Child not entitled to Medicare  Pickle Program  CalWORKs deemed eligible MAGI Medi-Cal MAGI Under MAGI eligibility, the asset test, linkage and deprivation requirements are eliminated. Below is a table of the MAGI Medi -Cal groups and the new adult category: MAGI Group Description Childless Adults Individuals between 19 and 64 years of age Parents and Caretaker Relatives Parents and caretaker relatives with a dependent child Children Infants and children under age 19 Pregnant Women Pregnant and post-partum women for pregnancy services or full scope benefits Open enrollment periods do not apply to MAGI Medi-Cal, which can be applied for at any time. Federal Data Hub The CalHEERS BRE automatically interfaces with the hub to verify certain data elements. The hub is not a separate system from CalHEERS. The purpose of the hub is to improve reliability. For MAGI Medi-Cal, the hub will attempt to verify:  Citizenship  SSN  Income Hub results will either be “Reasonably Compatible” or “Not Reasonably Compatible” for each requirement. Requirement If “not reasonably compatible” then … If “reasonably compatible” then … Citizenship paper verification of citizenship is required. No further verification is required. SSN verification of SSN is required. Income paper verification of income is required. Citizenship: An individual must be a US Citizen or an Eligible Non -Citizen to receive full scope MAGI Medi-Cal. Current Citizenship and verification requirements will follow existing Medi -Cal rules. Refer to MPG 07.02.02 for a list of acceptable verifications. SSN: As a condition of eligibility to full scope MAGI Medi -Cal, each applicant is required to provide a SSN. SSN and verification requirements follow existing Medi -Cal rules. Refer to MPG 04.11 for a list of acceptable verifications. Note: All current ex parte requirements remain the same. If the federal data hub returns a “not reasonably compatible” finding, an ex parte review of all available information and verifications already available to the county must be conducted prior to requesting additional verification. Each ex parte review must be documented in case comments. Refer to MPG 04.07.12 for information on the ex parte process. Immigrants Immigrants eligible to Full-Scope Medi-Cal are:  Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR’s)  Permanent Residence Under Color of Law (PRUCOL)  Asylees  Refugees  Cuban and Haitian entrants  Certain battered spouses and children  Victims of Trafficking  Individuals granted conditional entry  Individuals granted withholding of deportation/ removal  Individuals paroled into the U.S. for at least one year Qualified Immigrants under 5 years of Legal Permanent Resident status are eligible to receive state-only full-scope Medi-Cal. Undocumented Immigrants:  Adults and children will be included in the MAGI Medi -Cal expansion.  If all other eligibility requirements are met, undocumented immigrants will continue to receive: a) Restricted/ limited scope benefits includ ing State funded Long Term Care (LTC) b) Pregnancy –related services for: 1. Prenatal care 2. Labor and delivery 3. Up to 60 days of post-partum care 4. Family planning services  Immigrants with temporary status, temporary visas or those who do not intend to stay permanen tly such as foreign visitors and students are typically not eligible unless they establish that they intend to reside in California permanently and they meet all other eligibility requirements. If eligible to MAGI Medi -Cal, they may be eligible to the sam e level of benefits as undocumented aliens. Self- Attestation Self-attestation is when an individual is stating that something is true. Unless questionable, s elf-attestation is acceptable for MAGI Medi -Cal for:  Age  Date of birth  Family size  Pregnancy Self- attestation i s not allowed for MAGI Medi-Cal for residency or income (unless income is reasonably compatible with the hub). Residency To be eligible, an individual must be a resident of California with the intent to reside. Residency and verification requirement s will follow existing Medi -Cal rules. Refer to MPG 04.07.05 for acceptable residency verification. Other Documents and Verifications Current Medi -Cal program requirements for accepting other documents and verifications will stil l be required for MAGI Medi -Cal, unless otherwise specified. Eligibility forms such as the MC 13 Statement of Citizenship, CW 2.1 N A Child Support Notice & Agreement, CW 2.1Q Support Questionnaire, etc. will still be required for MAGI Medi-Cal. Disability Determination Service Division (DDSD) The DDSD disability compliance process is only related to non-MAGI Medi-Cal. If a client claims disability and is approved for MAGI, the worker will attempt to obtain a DDSD packet. If the applicant refuses to comply or does not comply with the DDSD process, it does not impact their MAGI eligibility. Current DDSD pending applications cannot be denied if approved for MAGI Medi-Cal. A final DDSD state evaluation must be received and processed prior to HSS taking action on the DDSD case. Determining Household Composition Household composition under MAGI methodology is determined differently from non-MAGI Medi-Cal rules. The following categories need to be identified to determine the size of the MAGI household composition:  Tax filer  Tax dependent  Non-tax filers If the individual is Then, the MAGI household includes ... the ... Tax filer tax filer and his/ her tax dependents. Tax dependent the same individuals as in the household of the tax filer who claimed the tax dependent. Note: The tax dependent rule does not apply to:  Tax dependents who are not the children, or spouse of the tax filer  Common children living with both parents who file separately  Children claimed as tax dependent by a noncustodial parent If the above exemptions apply, follow the nontax filers rules below. Non-tax filers adult individual and:  His/ her spouse  Their natural, adopted and/or step children child plus:  His/her natural, adopted, and/or step parent  Their natural, adopted, and/or step minor siblings Rules for non-filers mirror those for filers Married couples: Married couples living together are included in each other’s household regardless of their filing status. Sneede v. Kizer: Sneede v. Kizer rules do not apply under MAGI Medi -Cal. When determining eligibility for MAGI Medi-Cal, the parent-for-child rules that apply to Medi-Cal will also extend to step-parents. If the step-parent is in the same tax filing household as the stepchild, the step -parent’s income is counted towards the stepchild for MAGI Medi-Cal purposes. Determining Income Income countable for tax purposes will be used to determine eligibility to MAGI Medi-Cal. To be eligible for MAGI Medi -Cal the applicant’s total countable income must be within the following Federal Poverty Levels (FPLs): MAGI Group FPL Childless Adults Up to 138% FPL Parents and Caretaker Relatives Up to 138% FPL Children Up to 250% FPL Pregnant Women 0-138% FPL (full scope) 139% - 200% FPL (pregnancy services only) Income and income deductions: Many of the same expense deductions allowed on an i ncome tax return for both self -employment and employer -based taxes are also allowed for MAGI Medi-Cal. Desk Aid 56 : Income and Income Deductions provides a comparison of income and deductions for non- MAGI, MAGI and APTC. Exempt income: Many o f the income exemptions listed i n MPG 10.3 , will exist under MAGI rules as long as the income is exempt for tax filing purposes. The followin g income types are also ex empt from MAGI income evaluations:  Child support received  Veteran’s Benefits  Educational Assistance Unconditionally available income: Applying for unconditionally available income continues to be a requirement for MAGI Medi-Cal. If the applicant submits ... Then verification of application for the unconditionally available income ... the MC 210, SAWS 2, SAWS 2 Plus or MC 321 is required the single streamlined application is not required as DHCS will accept the single streamlined application attestation that the applicant has applied for unconditionally available income based on the Rights & Responsibilities section on the application. Income Verification: If verification of income is returned from the hub as “Not Reasonably Compatible” then verification is needed. Note: Ex parte review shall be conducted prior to requesting additional verifications. Acceptable types of verification have not changed. Refer to MPG 04.07.02. Self-Employment Income: The hub may also verify taxable self-employment income. If individual has ... Then the worker will determine self-employment income by... worked long enough to file a federal tax re turn for the previous year and it represents their current income using income and deductions claimed on the previous year’s taxes (1040, line 12 of schedule C) worked for less than a year at the business, or not long enough to file a tax return in the previous year, or the tax returns do not reflect current income  adding together gross self - employment income and any profit made from selling business property or equipment over the period of time the business has been in operation within the last year  subtracting business expenses allowed by the Internal Revenue Service Establishing the Date of Application The date of application for MAGI Medi -Cal benefits shall be established using the following guidelines based on date received by Covered California from applicant: If application is submitted... Then the date of application will be the... to Covered California and sent to the County as a Quick Sort transfer date that application is transferred by Covered California. Example: Covered California received a call from an applicant on Friday, 10/11/13 at 6pm. Applicant was Quick Sort transferred to S an Diego County same day. D ate of application will be 10/11/2013 on-line in CalHEERS date the application was submitted to Covered California. Example: Application was submitted electronically through Covered California on Saturday, 10/12/2013. Date of application will be 10/12/2013. By all other pathways date of application will follow current application process. Example: Application is received at FRC as face -to-face. The d ate of application will be the date the applic ant submitted the application to that FRC. Example: Application is received via My Benefits CalWIN. Date of application will follow established processing guidelines. Refer to Medi-Cal SN 10 -17 Electronic Medi-Cal and Food Stamp Applications - Phase 2- Benefits CalWIN and One E-App Request for Additional Information/ Verification Timeframe to request additional verifications remain the same including following ex parte requirements. Refer to MPG 04.07.12 for process requirements. Processing Deadlines Processing deadlines remain the same. If the application is ... Then it must be processed within ... a regular application 45 days based on disability 90 days Refer to MPG 04.02.17 B Advance Premium Tax Credit Programs APTC and CSR APTC helps reduce insurance costs for individuals and families. It may be taken in advance or when taxes are filed. Eligibility for the credit is determined based on the information provided by the applicant. Starting January 1, 2014, any individual who meets the following requirements may be eligible for APTC:  No other Health Coverage incl uding Medi -Cal (and no offer of affordable employer coverage)  Resident of California  Citizenship/ Immigration  Household Composition  Social Security Number  Income 139% to 400% of FPL Applicants must file a tax retu rn for the year in which they receive the credit. Example: if a client receives a premium tax credit in 2014, the client must file a 2014 tax return in spring 2015. Cost Sharing Reductions (CSR) can provide assistance in paying out - of-pocket costs like deductibles and co-pays. Enrollment Period Applicants must apply for b enefits during Open Enrollment or experience a qualifying life event. The initial Open E nrollment started October 1, 2013 and runs through March 31, 2014. If they have enrolled by December 15 , 2013 , coverage may begin as soon as January 1, 2014. Starting in 2014, annual Open Enrollment will be October 15 through December 7. A qualifying life event is when an applicant has a life change that may impact eligibility such as:  Birth of a child  Moving to a new state  Marriage or divorce  Loss of Minimum Essential Coverage  Moving to a new plan area  Release from incarceration Citizenship To be eligible to APTC, applicants must be U.S. Citizens or Legal Permanent Residents. Undocumented aliens are not eligible to APTC. Undocumented parents of citizen or lawfully present children are eligible for APTC and subsidies on behalf of their children but not for themselves, if the parents file taxes. Self- Attestation Unless questionable, self- attestation is acceptable for:  Age  Date of birth  Family size  Household income  Residency  Pregnancy Federal Data Hub For APTC, the hub will attempt to verify:  Citizenship  SSN  Income Hub results will either be “Reasonably Compatible” or “Not Reasonably Compatible” for each requirement. Requirement If “Not Reasonably Compatible” then … If “reasonably compatible” then … Citizenship paper verification of citizenship is required. No further verification is required SSN verification of SSN is required. Income paper verification of income is required. Household Income Countable and excluded i ncome for the APTC program are the same as they are for MAGI Medi-Cal. Household Composition While countable and e xcluded income are based on the same factors for APTC and MAGI Medi -Cal, they may differ for each household based on the members counted in the APTC unit vs. the MAGI Medi - Cal unit. For APTC/SCR, the household composition is based on the taxpayer and all of his/her claimed tax dependents. Note: Applicants are ineligible to APTC if they are legally married - filing separately, whether living together or not. Impact Aid Codes A final listing of aid codes will be provided once received from DHCS. Appeals Impact A client has the right to request an appeal on any actions taken that affect Medi-Cal eligibility. Appeals will not conduct appeals for APTC and CSR cases. Automation Impact The processing of a MAGI/APTC case must be completed in CalHEERS until the CalWIN and CalHEERS interface is available. Forms Impact Refer to Medi-Cal S N 13 -09 Health Care Reform Medi -Cal and Low Income Health Program for forms impact. ACCESS Impact No Impact Imaging Impact Refer to Medi-Cal SN 13 -09 Health Care Reform Medi -Cal and Low Income Health Program for imaging impact. CalFresh or CalWORKs Program Impact CalWORKs and CalFresh Program will issue guidance under separate cover when information becomes available from the California Department of Social Services (CDSS). Quality Control (QC) Impact Effective with the January 2014 review month, QC will cite the appropriate error on any case that does not comply with the requirements outlined in this letter. sections.text: Medi-Cal Program Guide Special Notice (SN) 13-09, Addendum A December 09, 2013 Subject HEALTH CARE REFORM (HCR) MEDI -CAL AND LOW INCOME HEALTH PROGRAM Effective Upon receipt Reference MEDIL I 13 - 12 Purpose To inform staff of:  Eligibility requirements for MAGI Medi -Cal and Advance Premium Tax Credit (APTC) programs.  Special processing requirement for Disability Determination Services Division (DDSD) cases. Instructions will be provided in future program material on:  County Medical Services (CMS)  Low Income Health Program (LIHP)  Refugee Medi-Cal Assistance (RMA) Background MPG SN 13 -09 provided HCR requirements that affected our application business process and LIHP transition information to Medi- Cal. Under Health Care Reform, also known as the Affordable Care Act, eligibility to the expanded Medi -Cal programs and APTC will be calculated using a household’s Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI). Beginning January 1, 2014, single adults wit hout children, ages 19-64, with income at or below 138% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) , will be eligible to MAGI Medi-Cal. Enrollment began October 1, 2013; if eligible, coverage starts as soon as January 1, 2014. If income exceeds 138% FPL, but is under 400% FPL, individuals may qualify for APTC. APTC is a federal assistance program used to assist individuals and families obtain health insurance by redu cing the monthly premium amount . Covered California offer s four different health plan levels that provides a range of premiums and benefit levels with the applicants ’ share of health care costs ranging from 10% - 40%. These are:  Platinum  Gold  Silver  Bronze If enrolled in a silver -level Covered California health plan and their income is above 138% FPL but under 250% FPL, consumers may also receive cost-sharing reductions (CSR). If an application is submitted to the County, H SS staff are responsible for processing APTC/ CSR applications prior to transferring case information and/or documents to Covered California. California Healthcare, Eligibility, Enrollment, and Retention System (CalHEERS) is a new web -based portal for applications for MAGI and APTC programs. CalHEERS is used by Covered California and all California Counties. It is expected that effective January 1, 2014, CalHEERS and CalWIN will interface with worker entries completed in CalWIN. The Business Rules Engine (BRE) in CalHEERS is similar to EDBC in CalWIN, with the addition of calling the federal data hub. The program rules are programed into the BRE to evaluate income and household composition and determine eligibility to the various extended programs. The BRE will call the federal data hub to electronically verify certain data elements reported by the client. Required Action If an application for Medi -Cal is dated prior to January 1, 2014, the HSS must evaluate the application for the current Medi-Cal programs. If not eligible to current Medi-Cal, HSS must evaluate for the expanded health care programs. This evaluation includes:  Applications assigned to Health Care Reform ( HCR) specialized caseload banks  Applicant immigrants under 5 years of legal permanent resident status who do not qualify for LIHP due to immigration status  DDSD pending applications that are currently not eligible to Medi -Cal or LIHP Refer to Processing Guide 11 - CalHEERS Application P rocessing for detailed instructions. Applications dated January 1, 2014 and later will first be evaluated under MAGI rules. Non-MAGI Medi-Cal Non-MAGI Non-MAGI Medi -Cal is the new term for the existing Medi -Cal programs that will not follow MAGI rules. Asset tests wi ll continue to be required for non-MAGI Medi-Cal. Undocumented immigrants remain eligible for emergency assistance and restricted scope Medi-Cal if all eligibility requirements are met. Minor consent continues to exist. There are no changes in eligibility rules for this program at this time. Sneede v. Kizer continues to apply to the non -MAGI Medically Needy program.

VTR Value of the One-Third Reduction WD Working Disabled WIC Women, Infants, and Children WRE Work Related Expense Definitions The table below shows the common terms used in the Medi-Cal program along with a definition. Term Definition Accelerated Enrollment The AE program provides immediate, temporary, full-scope, zero SOC Medi- Cal coverage to children under 19 who are new to Medi-Cal and applied for Medi-Cal through California Health Eligibility, Enrollment, and Retention System (CalHEERS). Accurately Reflect A reasonable determination of current income based on what the customer reported on the Statement of Facts when compared to provided verifications. If … Then … There is a discrepancy between the amounts of income declared and the amounts reflected on the verification, Use the best judgment as to the correct amount of current income. Not able to determine the correct income, Consult the supervisor. Still not able to make a reasonable determination of income, or the discrepancy would result in ineligibility to a Medi-Cal program, Contact the customer to clarify. Document the determination in Case Comments. Adequate Consideration The receipt of cash or property, which is fair and reasonable under the circumstances considering the net market value of property that is sold, converted, or transferred. Adoptions Assistance Program Removes or reduces barriers to the adoption of children who otherwise would remain in long-term foster care. Adult A person meeting any of the criteria below: •21 years of age or older •Blind or disabled MN 18 to 21 years of age, living in the home of a parent, and not currently enrolled in school •MN or MI 18 to 21 years of age, not living in the home of a parent or caretaker relative, not claimed as a tax dependent of his/her parent(s), and not receiving out-of-home care from a public agency •14 to 18 years of age not living in the home of a parent or caretaker relative and does not have a parent, caretaker relative, or legal guardian handling any of his/her financial affairs. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageDefinitions 1.1 6 of 23 Term Definition Adverse Action An action taken which discontinues Medi-Cal eligibility or increases an MFBU’s SOC, or reduces the scope of benefits (for example, zero SOC to premium OTLICP and full-scope to restricted). The following are not considered to be an adverse action: •Discontinuance due to any of the following reasons: oDeath, for a one-person MFBU oThe whereabouts of the beneficiary is unknown, and the post office has returned HHSA mail sent to the beneficiary indicating no forwarding address oAdmission to an institution, which renders the beneficiary ineligible. oThe beneficiary also has Medi-Cal eligibility under another identity or category, or in another county or state, or will have such dual eligibility as of the first of the coming month if discontinuance action is not taken oReceipt of the beneficiary’s clear and signed written statement that does either of the following: ▪States that the beneficiary no longer wants Medi-Cal benefits ▪Gives information that requires discontinuance and includes the beneficiary’s acknowledgement that he/she knows Medi- Cal will stop due to this information •Increase in an MFBU’s SOC due to either of the following: oThe voluntary inclusion of eligible family members who currently are not receiving benefits under any Medi-Cal program. oReceipt of the beneficiary’s clear and signed written statement which gives information which requires an increase in SOC and includes the beneficiary’s acknowledgement that the increase must be the consequence of supplying such information. Aged & Disabled Federal Poverty Level Program Provides zero SOC Medi-Cal to qualified aged or disabled individuals throughout the State of California. Aged, Blind, or Disabled People age 65 or older, or considered legally blind, or with a disability (as classified by SSA or DDSD). People in the Aged, Blind, or Disabled category receive greater income deductions which may mean a lower SOC. Aging and Independence Services Serves older adults, disabled persons, those at risk of abuse, people with HIV or AIDS, and others who would be at risk of institutionalization. Aid Category People who apply for Medi-Cal must have their eligibility evaluated according to the regulations governing the category to which the person or family is linked. Aid Code Used to determine the types of services for which Medi-Cal beneficiaries are eligible and the funding source: state, federal, or a combination of both. All County Welfare Directors Letter DHCS provides county public social services agencies with ACWDLs regarding new or changed policies and/or procedures used in determining eligibility for Medi-Cal benefits. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageDefinitions 1.1 7 of 23 Term Definition Applicant The individual or family either: •Making an application for aid •On whose behalf an application is made •Requesting a restoration or reapplication Approval of Eligibility Applicants who meet conditions of eligibility and their applications are approved for Medi-Cal based on an eligibility determination. Authorized Representative Person or organization authorized by a customer to apply for any of the health care programs and to perform the duties required to establish and maintain eligibility. Automated Eligibility Verification System Enables providers to verify eligibility via the telephone. Beneficiary An individual who becomes eligible for Medi-Cal under a specific category. Benefits Identification Card Card used to access the California Eligibility and Claims Management System to verify eligibility and SOC payment or obligation. Board and Care Nonmedical, community-based residential care for individuals who can care for themselves; meals and supervision are provided. Breast and Cervical Cancer Treatment Program Provides cancer treatment for eligible low-income California residents who are screened by the cancer detection program and found to need treatment for breast and/or cervical cancer. Bureau of Public Assistance Investigations Preventing, detecting, deterring, and prosecuting fraud or for those who obtain public aid they are not eligible to protects the interests of those in genuine need and conserves taxpayer resources. Burial Insurance Insurance, which by its terms can only be used to pay the burial expenses of the insured. California Department of Aging Administers programs that serve older adults, adults with disabilities, family caregivers, and residents in long-term care facilities throughout the State. California Department of Social Services Responsible for the oversight and administration of programs serving California’s most vulnerable residents. CalWIN Online, real-time computer program that supports the administration of public assistance programs. CalWORKs Program that provides temporary assistance in the form of cash aid and services to needy families with minor children. Caretaker Relative A relative who provides care and supervision to a child. The caretaker relative may be any relation by blood, marriage, or adoption who is within the fifth degree of relationship to the dependent child. Cash-Based Medi-Cal Medi-Cal benefits which are based upon a determination of eligibility for a cash grant. Cash Grant The money payment made to a person eligible for CalWORKs or SSI/SSP. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageDefinitions 1.1 8 of 23 Term Definition Categorically Eligible The person has met the requirements for the program, without requiring a separate determination. Certification Date for Claims Clearance The date in which the beneficiary met his/her SOC. Certification Effective Date The date the person is certified to receive Medi-Cal benefits. Certification for Medi-Cal The determination that a person is eligible for Medi-Cal and has no SOC, has met the SOC, or is in LTC and has a SOC that is less than the cost of LTC at the Medi-Cal rate. Child A person under the age of 21 except that the following people are considered adults: •Blind or disabled MN 18 to 21 years of age, living in the home of a parent, and not currently enrolled in school •MN or MI 18 to 21 years of age, not living in the home of a parent or caretaker relative, not claimed as a tax dependent of his/her parent(s), and not receiving out-of-home care from a public agency •14 to 18 years of age not living in the home of a parent or caretaker relative and does not have a parent, caretaker relative, or legal guardian handling any of his/her financial affairs. An unborn is considered a child for Medi-Cal purposes. Child Health and Disability Prevention Program The community-based program for early identification and referral for treatment of people under 21 years of age with potentially handicapping conditions. Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) CHIP provides health coverage to eligible children. CHIP provides federal funding to states to initiate and expand health assistance to uninsured lowincome children with income too high to qualify for Medi-Cal, but too low to purchase private insurance.is administered by states, following federal requirements. Medicaid law under Title XIX was amended to allow state the option to expand coverage to uninsured children through Medi-Cal which is now a coverage group in OTLICP and was previously known as Healthy Families, AIM, and Medi-Cal’s FPL programs for children. The aid code would determine the funding source depending on the title that the aid is provided: Title XIX: Medi-Cal OTLICP Title XXI: CHIP Client Identification Number Unique identifier assigned to beneficiaries by MEDS. Combination Cases An MFBU, which contains more than one assistance program for eligible people. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageDefinitions 1.1 9 of 23 Term Definition Common-Law Marriage A common-law marriage is established when: •A man and a woman both agree by written and verbal statement that they are husband and wife. The words must be in the present tense and must express intent to assume the relationship of husband and wife at the time involved and not at some future time. •The parties must have the capacity to enter the agreement. This means that they must be of sound mind and of the minimum age. •There must be cohabitation (living together as husband and wife and hold themselves out to the public as husband and wife) following the verbal or written statement. If these facts are established and the state where it occurred recognizes common-law marriages, a marriage is in existence which is valid for all purposes in California and which can only be dissolved by formal divorce even in the state in which it was created. See Desk Aid 112 to validate which states recognize common-law marriages. Community Property Property acquired by either spouse during marriage unless the property was acquired as separate property or with funds that can be identified as separate property. Community Spouse The spouse of an institutionalized individual who is not in LTC. Community Spouse Resource Allowance A spouse who continues to reside in the community after the other spouse has entered a long-term care facility is entitled to retain a portion of the couple’s resources. Competent A person able to act on one’s own behalf in business and personal matters. Comprehensive Prepaid Health Plan A PHP that is required by contract with the State to provide full scope benefits available under the Medi-Cal program. Contiguous Property Adjacent or adjoining property that is not separated by a road, street, right of way, or in any other manner from property being considered. Continuous Eligibility for Children Provides no SOC Medi-Cal benefits to certain children up to the age of 19. Conversion of Property Changing the property from one form to another without changing ownership. County Agency Either an administrative division of a county government or a non-county organization that has a contract with the county to act on the county’s behalf. County Dollar Error Rate Medi-Cal dollars paid in error in the eligibility quality control sample divided by the Medi-Cal dollars paid in the sample. County Medical Services A county-funded program for adults 21 through 64 years of age who are ineligible for Medi-Cal. County Welfare Department Agency that provides social welfare services to citizens in need to include, but are not limited to, cash, food assistance, employment services, and medical needs. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageDefinitions 1.1 10 of 23 Term Definition Covered California Service that connects Californians with health insurance under the Affordable Care Act. Cuban-Haitian Entrant Program Provide asylum and humanitarian assistance to people subject to persecution in their homelands. Assistance which helps refugees adapt to their new country, become economically self-sufficient, and ultimately participate in and contribute to their new communities. Current Market Rental Value Income from rental property minus allowable expenses. Current Market Value Real property determined by the assessed value of the most recent property tax assessment or value established through an appraisal by a qualified real estate appraiser. Deficit Reduction Act of 2005 Act made changes in mandatory spending under legal entitlements and tax laws to achieve savings in the federal budget and outlay. Department of Child Support Services Establishes child and medical support orders, enforces/modifies child and medical support orders, and collects and distributes child and spousal support payments. Department of Developmental Services Provides services and support to individuals with developmental disabilities. Department of Health Care Services The state agency charged with administering the Medicaid program for the Federal government. Disabled Adult Children Person who became permanently disabled before the age of 22 and is now over the age of 22. Disability Determination Services Division DDSD is responsible for evaluating medical and employment data to determine if a customer meets the federal definition of disability. “Inability to engage in any substantial gainful activity by reason of a medically determinable physical or mental impairment which can be expected to result in death or has lasted or can be expected to last for a continuous period of not less than twelve months.” Disability Insurance Benefits Provides support when a person is unable to work. Disproportionate Share Hospital System of payment for the operating costs of acute care hospital inpatient stays. Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnosis, and Treatment Comprehensive and preventive child health program for individuals under the age of 21. Eligibility and Assistance Standards The portion of the MPP published by the CDSS which includes regulations pertaining to the CalWORKs and SSP programs. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageDefinitions 1.1 11 of 23 Term Definition Eligibility Services A service provided by HHSA relating to the initial and continuing determination of a person’s or family’s Medi-Cal eligibility. Employment Development Department Administers the Job Service, Unemployment Insurance, Disability Insurance, and Workforce Investment Act. Employment Training Services Provides a comprehensive range of employment and training services in partnership with local agencies. Encumbrances of Record Obligations for which property is security as evidenced by a written document. Entrant Medical Assistance Certain refugees for whom assistance is authorized with documentation for USCIS. Estimated Date of Confinement The due date or estimated calendar date when a baby will be born. Family Member The following people living in the home: •A child or sibling children •The parents (married or unmarried) of the sibling children •The stepparents of the sibling children •The separate children of either unmarried parent or the parent or stepparent. If there are no children, family member means a single person or a married couple. Family Resource Center Facility offering self-sufficiency services. Federal Financial Participation Federal Medicaid matching funds paid to the State for allowable expenditures for Medicaid services or administrative costs. Federal Poverty Level An income limit based on the official poverty level as defined by the Federal Office of Management and Budget and revised annually. Federal Poverty Level for the Blind Program covers blind individuals pursuant to Title XVI who have not yet or cannot meet the Title II criteria for disability based upon blindness. Federal Qualified Health Center All organizations receiving grants under Section 330 of the Public Health Service Act. Former Foster Youth Provides full, no cost Medi-Cal for people who were in foster care on their 18th birthday and who were released from foster care due to age. Franchise Tax Board The department that collects state personal income taxes and bank and corporation taxes for the State of California. Health and Human Services Agency Principal agency for protecting the health of all Americans and providing essential human services, especially for those who are least able to help themselves. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageDefinitions 1.1 12 of 23 Term Definition Health Care Options Gives health care services through networks of organized systems of care. Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act Federal law that mandates that each state has the capacity to exchange data with the Medicare program and which contains provisions that require state Medicaid programs to use standard, national codes for electronic transactions related to the processing of health claims. Mandates certain standards and practices about privacy of consumer health information. Health Insurance Premium Payment Program Enrollment of a beneficiary in a group health plan which is cost effective. Heirloom Any item of personal property, other than cash or securities, which has substantial sentimental value, has been owned by a family for at least two generations, and has the intention to be retained by the family in succeeding generations. Home Real or personal property, fixed or mobile, located on land or water, in which a person or family lives. Hospital Outstation Hospitals contracting with the Hospital Council to have workers stationed in their facilities to process Medi-Cal and CMS applications for inpatients and patients scheduled for admittance. Immigration Reform and Control Act Granted amnesty to certain undocumented immigrants who entered the United States before January 1, 1982 and have resided there continuously. Impairment Related Work Expenses Deduction for out-of-pocket expenses for items such as medicine, medical supplies, medical devices, service animals, and disposable items such as bandages and syringes when figuring the amount of earned income. Income and Eligibility Verification System The federally mandated system established to obtain, use, and verify information relevant to determination of eligibility and SOC. In-Home Supportive Services The social services program, which provides necessary personal and domestic care so that an aged, blind, or disabled person may remain in their own home. In-Kind Support and Maintenance Unearned income that is not cash or a check when someone else pays for or provides food and/or shelter. Inmate A person living or confined in an institution. Excluded from this definition are people residing at a facility for vocational training or educational purposes, and people temporarily in an institution pending more suitable arrangements, such as children in a local agency facility pending foster care placement. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageDefinitions 1.1 13 of 23 Term Definition Institution An establishment which provides food and shelter to four or more people unrelated to the proprietor and in addition provides some treatment or services which meet needs beyond the basic provision of food and shelter. Institution Definition Medical Any public or private acute care hospital, acute psychiatric hospital, intermediate care facility, skilled nursing facility, or other medical facility licensed by an officially designated state standard setting authority. Mental Diseases An institution primarily engaged in providing diagnosis, treatment, or care for people with mental illness. Non-medical Any institution providing non-medical residential care, custodial care, custody, or restraint. This includes penal institutions. Private A proprietary or nonprofit facility managed and controlled by an individual, private association, or cooperation. Public An institution that is the responsibility of a government unit or over which a governmental unit exercises administrative control. Excluded from this definition are medical facilities and publicly operated community residences. Tuberculosis An institution which is primarily engaged in providing diagnosis, treatment, or care of people with tuberculosis, including medical attention, nursing care, and related services. . Institutionalized Spouse Beginning on the date of application an institutionalized spouse is one who is all the following: •Applying for Medi-Cal after January 1, 1990 •Beginning a continuous period of institutionalization after September 20, 1989, as an inpatient in a medical institution, nursing facility, or applying for or receiving Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) •Is expected to remain in the medical institution, nursing facility, or receive HCBS for a continuous period of at least 30 consecutive days as evidenced by a statement signed and dated by the physician of the institutionalized spouse. Non-receipt of nursing facility level of care for a full calendar month is considered a termination of a continuous period of institutionalization •Has a community spouse •Is not AFDC-MN Intermediate Care Facility A facility which provides services to patients who: •Require protection and supportive care above board and care level •Do not require continuous supervision by a licensed registered or vocational nurse •Do not have an illness, injury, or disability for which hospital or skilled nursing facilities are required County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageDefinitions 1.1 14 of 23 Term Definition Interprogram Transfer A transfer of eligibility from one aid category to another aid category, in which the first digit of the aid code changes. Intraprogram Status Change A change in a person’s or family’s eligibility from one aid category to another aid category, in which the first digit of the aid code remains the same. Kinship Guardian Assistance Program Support payments for foster children who have been placed in long-term foster care with a relative caregiver. Letter of Authorization Proof of eligibility that occurred at least 12 months prior to the current month. Life Insurance A contract for which premiums are paid during the lifetime of the insured and on which the insuring company pays the face amount of the policy to the beneficiary upon the death of the insured. Life insurance may also be purchased by a single premium or by letting dividends accumulate. Limited Service Status The beneficiary’s use of Medi-Cal is limited because of enrollment in a comprehensive PHO, improper usage of service, application as a child under Minor Consent services, or participation in a pilot project conducted by the State. Linked Meeting the SSI/SSP requirements of age, blindness, or disability. Long-Term Care Spouse An institutionalized spouse regardless of the date of admission to the LTC facility. Long-Term Care Status Inpatient medical care, which lasts for more than the month of admission and is expected to last for at least one full calendar month after the month of admission. Manual of Policies and Procedures Provides clarification to county social services staff on policies and procedures for making eligibility determinations for the Medi-Cal program. Issued by CDSS. Marriage The state of being married, including a common-law marriage (for further details on legal common-law marriage, see common-law marriage). Medi-Cal California’s medical assistance program and the benefits available under that program. Medi-Cal is the California state plan version of the federal Medicaid program. Medi-Cal Dollar Error Rate Standard The statewide dollar error rate tolerance level established by the State to measure county performance in the accurate determination of Medi-Cal eligibility and SOC for MN and MI beneficiaries. Medi-Cal Eligibility Quality Control •Federally mandated review of Medi-Cal cases to ensure proper determination of eligibility. •State mandated review of Medi-Cal cases within individual counties to ensure proper determination of eligibility. Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System State information system that supports the operations of the Medi-Cal program that contains sub-systems and files for beneficiary eligibility. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageDefinitions 1.1 15 of 23 Term Definition Medi-Cal Eligibility Division Information Letter Information letter used to provide clarification and implementation of Medi-Cal regulations, policy, and procedures to assure that Medi-Cal eligibility is determined accurately and timely. Medi-Cal Eligibility Procedures Manual State manual that provides clarification to county social services staff on procedures for making eligibility determinations for the Medi-Cal program. Issued by DHCS. Medi-Cal Family Budget Unit The people who will be included in the Medi-Cal eligibility and SOC determination. Medi-Cal Only Eligibility A person’s or family’s eligibility for Medi-Cal benefits that has been determined independently of an eligibility determination for any other aid or benefit program. Medically Needy Person or Family A person or family eligible under the MN program. These people are linked to a federal program. Medi-Cal Program Guide County manual that provides instruction to County eligibility staff on regulations, policies, and procedures for making eligibility determinations for the Medi-Cal program. Medicare Catastrophic Coverage Act Created to preserve the assets of the aged due to catastrophic illness. Minimum Basic Standard of Adequate Care The amount necessary to provide a CalWORKs family with basic needs as specified in the EAS manual. Minor Consent Services Services related to: •Sexual assault •Drug or alcohol abuse for children 12 years of age or older •Pregnancy •Family planning •Venereal disease (sexually transmitted diseases designated by the State) for children 12 years of age or older •Mental health care for children 12 years of age or older who are mature enough to participate intelligently and which is needed to prevent the children from seriously harming themselves or others or because the children are the alleged victims of incest or child abuse. Minor Parent A parent who meets the definition of a child and has his/her children living in the home. Modified Adjusted Gross Income MAGI is the term for Medi-Cal that uses tax rules to determine eligibility. Multiple Dwelling Unit Any dwelling with more than one separate living unit, which normally would include, as a minimum, a bathroom and a kitchen. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageDefinitions 1.1 16 of 23 Term Definition Multipurpose Senior Service Program Provides social and health care management for frail elderly customers who are certifiable for placement in a nursing facility but who wish to remain in the community. National School Lunch Program Federally assisted meal program operating in public and nonprofit private schools and residential childcare institutions that provides nutritionally balanced, low-cost, or free lunches to children each school day. Newborn Automatic Number Assignment If parents choose to have a SSN automatically assigned to their newborn child, federal law requires the inclusion of at least one parent’s SSN on the birth record. Nonrecurring Lump Sum Payment A payment accrued over more than one calendar month and not expected to be received again in the future. It does not include the amount of the monthly benefit for the month the lump sum is received. For instance, a Social Security lump sum payment would have the current month payment subtracted from the lump sum payment to determine the amount of the lump sum. See Desk Aid 56 for treatment in MAGI determinations. Notice of Action Notification that provides customers with clear communication for accurate eligibility status, the reasons why actions are taken, and appeal rights. Nursing Facility An intermediate care facility or a skilled nursing facility. Obligate To incur a cost for health care services. Office of Refugee Resettlement Provides people in need with critical resources to assist them in becoming integrated members of American society. Optional Targeted Low- Income Children’s Program Provides medical coverage for children through 19 years of age with family income below 266% FPL. This program also includes California’s CHIP expansion. Other Health Coverage Any benefit for health-related services or entitlements for which a Medi-Cal beneficiary is eligible under any private, group, or government insurance program. Other PA Recipient A person eligible for Medi-Cal under one of the categories in the Other PA program. Overpayment The receipt of Medi-Cal benefits or a portion of benefits when there is no eligibility. Parent The natural or adoptive parent of a child. Patient A person receiving individual professional services directed by a licensed practitioner of the healing arts towards maintenance, improvement, or protection of health, or the alleviation of disability or pain. Payment Verification System A monthly match that provides information on RSDI benefits, UIB, and SDI. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageDefinitions 1.1 17 of 23 Term Definition People Living in the Home •Includes all the following: oPeople physically present in the home oPeople temporarily absent from the home because of hospitalization, visiting, vacation, trips in connection with work, or because of similar reasons to an 18 to 21-year-old as shown below oPeople away at school or vocational training who will resume living in the home as evidenced by the person returning home for vacations, weekends, and at other times. •A temporary absence is normally one in which the person leaves and returns to the home in the same month or the following month. •A child temporarily absent from the home is living in the home if the parent continues to have responsibility for the care and control of a child until the court removes this responsibility or the parent voluntarily relinquishes it. •An 18 to 21-year-old or unmarried minor parent living on the parent’s property is not living in the parent’s home if both following conditions exist: oThe 18 to 21-year-old or unmarried minor parent does not receive any support from the parents oThe building the 18 to 21-year-old or unmarried minor parent lives in would be considered other real property of the parents. •A person whose institutional status results in ineligibility Perinatal Care Network Works with families eligible for pregnancy related Medi-Cal to make sure that women get prenatal care and other services they need. Permanently Residing Under Color of Law Noncitizen permanently residing in the United States who is not under a direct, final order of deportation. Personal Care Services Program Provides services such as housekeeping, meal preparation, bathing, toileting, and grooming. Personal Property Possession or interests, exclusive of real property, that may be easily transported or stored; including but not limited to cash on hand, bank accounts, notes, mortgages, deeds of trust, cash surrender value of life insurance, motor vehicles, uncollected judgements, an interest in a firm in receivership, a lawsuit, patents, and copyrights. Point of Services Device used to verify recipient eligibility, clear SOC liability, reserve Medi-Cal services, and submit and adjudicate pharmacy claims online. Prepaid Health Plan Contracts between an insurer and subscriber or a group of subscribers whereby a specified set of health benefits is provided in return for a periodic premium. Presumed Maximum Value Presume that the value of support and maintenance does not exceed a certain maximum amount. Presumptive Disability Presumes that a person is disabled while a more formal determination of their disability is under consideration. Presumptive Eligibility Program allows qualified Medi-Cal providers throughout the state to provide their low-income patients immediate, temporary Medi-Cal coverage for prenatal care. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageDefinitions 1.1 18 of 23 Term Definition Primary Care Case Management Plan Any person or organization who: •Has entered into a contract with DHCS on a capitalized or risk sharing basis, or both, to provide or arrange for the provision of health care services •Meets the requirements for participation in the Medicaid program on an atrisk basis. Program for All Inclusive Care for the Elderly A comprehensive service package that permits the elderly to continue living at home while receiving services rather than be institutionalized. Proof of Eligibility Verification on the period to which a person is eligible for Medi-Cal, including retroactive eligibility. Public Agency An administrative division of local, state, or federal government, or an organization that has a contract to act in behalf of the local, state, or federal government. Public Assistance Recipient A person or family receiving assistance under the CalWORKs, SSI/SSP, or Refugee Assistance programs. Public Funds Money provided by a local, state, or federal government. Publicly Operated Community Residence A facility designed and planned to serve no more than 16 residents, which is serving 16 or fewer residents. The facility provides food and shelter and must provide some additional services such as: •Social services •Help with personal activities •Training in socialization and life skills. Excluded from this definition are: •Residential facilities located on the grounds or immediately adjacent to any large institution or multi-purpose complex •Educational or vocational training facilities •Correctional or holding facilities for people detained under the penal system •Medical treatment facilities. Qualified Disabled Working Individual An individual who meets the eligibility criteria for the QDWI program specified in MPG 5.13.6. Qualified Disaster A natural disaster is designated as qualifying disaster by federal, state, or local agencies or certain other personal hardship. Qualified Individual An individual who meets the eligibility criteria for the QI program specified in MPG 5.13.5. Qualified Medicare Beneficiary An individual who meets the eligibility criteria for the QI program specified in MPG 5.13.3. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageDefinitions 1.1 19 of 23 Term Definition Railroad Retirement Board Administers a federal retirement benefit program covering the nation’s railroad workers. Real Property Land and improvements, which generally include any immovable property attached to the land and any oil, mineral, timber, or other rights related to the land. Reapplication An application for Medi-Cal only eligibility made in the same county as a previous application, if the previous application was denied or withdrawn or Medi-Cal only eligibility based on the previous application has been discontinued for more than 12 months. Reasonable Opportunity Period Defined as the time needed for the customer to obtain valid documentation. Recipient A person or family receiving aid under a PA program or the Other PA program. Redetermination The review of a person’s or family’s Medi-Cal eligibility. Refugee Cash Assistance A 100% federally funded program that provides social services and cash assistance for a limited time. Refugee Medical Assistance A 100% federally funded program that provides up to eight months of health care coverage to certain noncitizens who are considered refugees under the Immigration and Naturalization Act. Registered Domestic Partner Registered legal relationship available to same-sex couples, and to certain opposite-sex couples in which at least one party is at least 62 years of age. It affords the couple the same rights, protections, and benefits, and is subject to the same responsibilities, obligations, and duties under law as married spouses. Relative •A parent (1 st degree), grandparent (2nd degree), sibling (3rd degree), a great-grandparent (3rd degree), uncle or aunt (3rd degree), nephew or niece (3rd degree), great-great-grandparent (4th degree), great-uncle or aunt (4th degree), great-great-great-grandparent (5th degree), great-great uncle or aunt (5th degree), or a first cousin once removed (5th degree) •A stepfather, stepmother, stepbrother, or stepsister •A spouse even after the marriage has been terminated by death or dissolution but not by annulment •A person (or his/her relatives) who legally adopts the child Example: If Anne and Betty are cousins, Betty’s children are first cousins once removed to Anne and Anne’s children are first cousins once removed to Betty. Anne’s children and Betty’s children are second cousins. Renal Dialysis The process of filtering the blood, the way kidneys normally do, using a machine. Repayment The recovery of an overpayment in response to a demand by DHCS. Residence The place in which a person or family lives or is physically present if the person or family has no present intention of leaving. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageDefinitions 1.1 20 of 23 Term Definition Responsible Relative A relative who is responsible to contribute to the cost of health care services received by a Medi-Cal beneficiary. Restoration The approval of Medi-Cal only eligibility for a person or family in the same county as that in which they were previously eligible for Medi-Cal only, if the effective date of the approval occurs within 12 months of the end of the previous period of eligibility. Retirement, Survivor’s, and Disability Insurance Program operated by SSA that provides a monthly income to certain people based on payroll contributions made via Social Security taxes. Satisfactory Immigration Status An immigration status that makes the individual eligible for full-scope benefits under the applicable program. Separate Property Any item that is to be considered separate property under California Property Law. Generally, separate property is acquired by an individual by any method prior to marriage, after obtaining an interlocutory, or final judgment of dissolution, or while voluntarily separated, or at any time by gift or inheritance, or purchases made with funds that are separate property or with funds from the sale of separate property. Share of Community Property To determine Medi-Cal eligibility, share of community property is to be treated as if each spouse owns one-half of the community property. Share of Cost A person’s or family’s net income more than their maintenance need that must be paid or obligated toward the cost of health care services monthly before the person or family may be certified. Share of Encumbrance That portion of any encumbrances attributed to each portion of jointly owned property. Single Point of Entry Provides a uniform, centralized process for the receipt, processing, and tracking of applications. Skilled Nursing Facility A health facility or a distinct part of a hospital, which provides skilled nursing care and supportive care to patients whose primary need, is for skilled nursing care on an extended basis. It provides 24-hour care and, as a minimum, includes nursing, dietary, pharmaceutical services, and an activity program. Social Security Administration Independent agency of the United States federal government that administers Social Security, a social insurance program consisting of retirement, disability, and survivor’s benefits and Medicare. Social Security Health Insurance Claim Number Number assigned by the SSA to an individual identifying them as a Medicare beneficiary. Social Security Number A nine-digit number issued to U.S. citizens, permanent residents, and temporary (working) residents which primary purpose is to track individuals for taxation purposes. Social Worker Helping people overcome problems to make their lives better. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageDefinitions 1.1 21 of 23 Term Definition Special Agricultural Workers Immigrants who performed labor in perishable agricultural commodities for a specified period and were admitted for temporary and then permanent residence under a provision of the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986. Specified Low- Income Medicare Beneficiary An individual who meets the eligibility criteria for the QI program specified in MPG 5.13.4. State Data Exchange The data system by which the federal government provides information to the State regarding the eligibility of SSI/SSP applicants and recipients. State Disability Insurance Provides partial wage replacement to eligible workers who are unable to work because of a disability. Stepparent A person who is married to the parent of a child and who is not the natural or adoptive parent of the child. Substantial Gainful Activity Disabled People who were once determined disabled by SSI/SSP, became ineligible for SSI/SSP because of SGA, and still have the medical impairment which was the basis of the SSI/SSP disability determination. Supplemental Security Income/State Supplemental Program The federal and state payments, respectively, which are based on need, and are paid to aged, blind, or disabled people. Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements Automated verification process to provide federal, state, and local benefit issuing agencies and institutions with immigration status information which will assist them in determining an individual’s eligibility. Therapeutic Wages Wages earned by an individual when all the following conditions are met: •A physician who does not have a financial interest in the LTC facility in which the individual resides, and who oversees the individual’s case, prescribes his work as therapy for the individual. •The individual must be employed by the same LTC facility in which he/she resides. •The individual’s employment does not displace any existing employees. •The individual has resided in a LTC facility continuously since September 1979. Third Party Liability The responsibility of insurers for payment of claims which relate to injuries or trauma sustained by recipients becaise of fault or negligence of third parties (for example, auto accident claims). The State is responsible for assuring the use of third-party assets or for detection and collection of third-party liability payments. Title II Social Security benefits that provide monthly payments to aged, blind, or disabled people who have a previous earnings history. Payments are also paid to certain dependents and survivors. Recipients are not automatically eligible to receive Medi-Cal. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageDefinitions 1.1 22 of 23 Term Definition Title IVA CalWORKs. This program is administered by State agencies. Families receiving assistance through this program are automatically eligible to Medi- Cal. Title XVI SSI cash grant program. SSA administers the program that provides cash assistance to aged, blind, and disabled people whose income and resources are below certain levels. California has a SSP. People receiving SSI/SSP assistance are automatically eligible to Medi-Cal. Title XVII Medicare. This program is administered by SSA and provides health insurance to almost all aged individuals and certain disabled individuals. Medicare recipients are not automatically eligible to receive Medi-Cal. Title XIX Medicaid program. This program is administered by the state and federal agencies. The single agency in California is DHCS. In California, the program is called Medi-Cal. Title XXI Children’s Health Insurance Program (see above), which is a coverage group under OTLICP. Total Parenteral Nutrition Feeding a person intravenously, bypassing the usual process of eating and digestion. Transfer of Property A change of ownership whereby a person no longer holds the title to, or beneficial interest in, property. Transitional Medi-Cal Comprehensive preventive care services for families who lost their cash based Medi-Cal due to earnings. Tuberculosis Contagious bacterial infection that mainly involves the lungs but may spread to other organs. Unemployment Insurance Benefits Provides temporary financial assistance to eligible workers who are unemployed through no fault of their own. United States Citizenship and Immigration Services Federal government agency that oversees lawful immigration to the United States, and citizenship services. Unmarried Parents Parents who are living together with their common child and the parents are not married to each other. Value of the One-Third Reduction An amount equal to one-third of the applicable Federal Benefit Rate is considered the value of the in-kind support and maintenance. Verification The process of obtaining acceptable evidence, which substantiates statements made by the customer. Women, Infants, and Children WIC provides Federal grants to States for supplemental food, health care referrals, and nutrition education for low-income pregnant, and postpartum women, and to infants and children up to age five who are found to be at nutritional risk. Working Disabled Program Disabled individuals who work and have income that is too high to qualify for other Medi-Cal categories can have up to 250% of the federal poverty level in countable income and still receive Medi-Cal benefits. Enrollees pay a monthly, sliding-scale premium for this coverage. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageDefinitions 1.1 23 of 23 Term Definition Work Related Expenses A standard deduction or an itemized deduction for ordinary and necessary expenses attributable to a customer’s job. Procedure: See above. Program Impacts: None. References: None. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by June 30, 2023 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations
