title: Section 1 Confidentiality
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageConfidential Information 2.1.1 1 of 2 Revision Date: September 1, 2019 Background: Confidentiality regulations were created to protect customers against identification, exploitation, or stigma that could result from the release of information identifying them as having applied for or received public assistance. These regulations are outlined in the State CDSS Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) Division 19-000. MPG Article 2, Section 1 provides staff with policies and procedures regarding the confidentiality of HHSA Medi-Cal case records and release of information to qualified agencies, people, and Medi-Cal providers. The unauthorized release and possession of confidential information is a violation of MPP confidentiality regulations and can be prosecuted as a misdemeanor. Purpose: This section is revised to include information from Medi-Cal Memo 15-35 and to update to the current format. Policy: Policy and Procedures Governing Confidentiality: HHSA employees are encouraged to respond to inquiries by providing information regarding HHSA policies and procedures. However, care must be taken to preserve the confidentiality of HHSA case records. All reference to “case records” includes all documents, forms, and communications, including those stored electronically. Prior to the release of confidential information to other agencies or individuals, review the policies and procedures detailed in this Article, the Confidentiality Eligibility Policies and Procedures Guide (EPPG), and, when necessary, MPP 19-000. Unauthorized disclosure of confidential information by a County employee is a misdemeanor and may lead to criminal or civil liability for both County employees and the County. The County may also take disciplinary action against the employee. Information that Is Confidential: All information in case records, including names, addresses, and eligibility information about the circumstances of any customer, including whether that person is a customer, is confidential and must be safeguarded. This applies to all information obtained from, for, and about all customers, whether received in writing or orally. Do not disclose confidential information for any purposes not directly related to the administration of public social services programs or as noted in this Article. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageConfidential Information 2.1.1 2 of 2 Information that Is Not Confidential: Statistical information and social data which is not identified with an individual may be released. Examples of information that may be released include, but are not limited to, such information as statements on the number of beneficiaries, total expenditures per program or administration, average grant amount figures, and other general information about the caseload. Avoiding a Breach in Confidentiality for ACA Cases: When any of the following items are entered in CalWIN for an individual, the individual will be added to the CalHEERS case and the family could receive notices with their information: •“Yes” for the field “In Home” •“Yes” for “Requesting Assistance” •Added to the “Tax Filer” window. If the individual is not in the home or is not requesting, confidential information may be released erroneously to or about this individual. To prevent a breach in confidentiality, carefully review entries for every individual listed in a case and ensure that these entries are populated with the appropriate values. Procedure: Follow the policies above to maintain confidential information. Other Program Impacts: None. References: MPP 19-000 MEPM 2H Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 09/31/2022. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageHandling of Case Records 2.1.2 1 of 2 Revision Date: September 1, 2019 Background: Case records are the original and permanent records of HHSA and are maintained for reference and audit purposes to document eligibility. Case records and original documents should be at the assigned Family Resource Center (FRC) or electronically stored in the imaging system and CalWIN. Unless approved by the FRC Manager, no case record, whether hard copy or electronic copy, will be removed from HHSA. The customer’s case record must only contain facts relevant to the case. Purpose: This section is updated to the current format. Policy: Routing of Case Records for Official Use: When requested, case records may be routed to other divisions or administrative staff for official use (for example, QESD, BPAI, DHCS Investigations, Appeals, Fiscal, Internal Investigations, etc.). The routing of case records to other divisions or administrative staff for official use does not require approval from the FRC Manager. State and Federal Quality Control may view HHSA records for their reviews without prior approval. The requests for cases may be made directly to the FRC or through the Corrective Action Coordinator. MEDS Screens: DHCS’ policy is that only individuals who have a MEDS ID may view MEDS screens, including MOPI. The table below shows what to do if a request is received to view MEDS screens or screen prints. If the requestor is a … Then … Customer, Authorized Representative (AR), Representative, Conservator Deny the request. Provider Refer to MPG 14.4. Procedure: Follow the policies above to maintain confidential information. Other Program Impacts: None. References: MPP 19-000 ACWDL 08-04 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 09/31/2022. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageHandling of Case Records 2.1.2 2 of 2 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageRelease of Information 2.1.4 1 of 3 Revision Date: September 1, 2019 Background: Confidential information may only be released for either reason below: •For the purposes directly connected with the administration of public social services program •As authorized by the customer. This section will not prohibit the release of information to other public agencies to the extent required for verifying eligibility. Document in the case record all information and the disposition of the request. Purpose: This section is updated to the current format. Policy: Authorized Disclosure List: Confidential information may only be released without the consent of the customer for purposes directly connected with the administration of public social services programs except as specified under MPG 2.1.6 Law Enforcement Officials. In addition to HHSA staff of this county and their counterparts in other counties or states, the following agencies and/or people are authorized to receive or exchange confidential information without the consent of the customer when the request is for a purpose connected with the administration of the public social services program. The list is not intended to be complete and/or result in the automatic disclosure of information to people or agencies on the list. The list provides a quick reference of people and agencies that most frequently make authorized inquiries. •Auditor and Controller (County, State, and Federal) •County Counsel (except for investigations of Worker’s Compensation claims or other questionable situations) •Department of Health and Human Services (County, State, and Federal) •Department of Health Care Services (State and Federal) •District Attorney – BPAI, FSD, Welfare Employee Fraud Prosecutions, Child Support Prosecutions only •Grand Jury •Housing Authorities •Juvenile Probation Department (for billings on AFDC Foster Care cases) •Mental Health Services •Revenue and Recovery •Social Security Administration Contact HHSA Eligibility Operations Medi-Cal Program when there is doubt as to the propriety of releasing any program specific information. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageRelease of Information 2.1.4 2 of 3 Required Authorization Prior to Release: Unless otherwise provided under “Telephone Authorization,” all authorizations must be written and must be obtained by the worker prior to the release of confidential information to agencies and people not listed on the Authorized Disclosure List. Under no circumstances release medical (health) information from the case based on the customer’s oral authorization. Written authorization from the customer is always required prior to releasing medical information to a third party. Refer to MPG 2.1.6 Privileged Communication – Physician/Patient about additional requirements to release medical information from a case record. Written Authorization: The following guidelines apply to written authorizations: •Must be signed and dated by the customer •Must include a description of the information to be disclosed •Must include a description of the purpose of the disclosure. “At the request of the individual” or similar language may be accepted if the customer does not wish to describe the purpose of the request •Must identify the name of the individual or organization authorized by the customer to receive such information •Expires one year from the date signed unless expressly limited to a shorter period •May be revoked by the customer at any time •Accept photocopies of the written authorization. Telephone Authorization: Accept telephone authorization in lieu of written authorization where the circumstances ensure that the customer has positively identified himself/herself to the County. Acceptable items of identification may include case number, driver’s license number, Social Security number, or date of birth. The following guidelines apply to telephone authorizations: •Is temporary and good for only that phone call •Does not apply to medical (health) information from a case •Should be followed by a written authorization •Must be documented in the case •The customer’s oral agreement to provide a written authorization must be documented in the case along with the date that the release form was sent to the customer. Procedure: Follow the policies above to maintain confidential information. Other Program Impacts: None. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageRelease of Information 2.1.4 3 of 3 References: MPP 19-000 MEPM 2H County Policy Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 09/31/2022. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageRelease to Customer or Authorized Representative 2.1.5 1 of 3 Revision Date: September 1, 2019 Background: This section provides instructions for what information may be released to a customer and/or their Authorized Representative (AR). Purpose: This section is updated to the current format. Policy: Information Which May Be Released: Information contained in applications or other documents made or kept by HHSA may be released to the customer or his/her AR only if both Conditions 1 and 2 are met: Condition 1: •The customer has authorized the release of the information; And Condition 2: •The information was provided solely by the customer (for example, income verifications); or •The customer authorized HHSA to obtain the information (for example, bank verification requests). Information Which May Not Be Released: Information provided confidentially to HHSA by a third party and not provided solely by the customer will not be reviewed or disclosed to the customer or his/her AR. This includes: Type Description Guidelines DHCS Investigations/ BPAI Reports All reports, summaries, and other confidential communications or information obtained by DHCS Investigations/BPAI in the process of investigation of an alleged fraud. Do not release or allow customer or his/her AR to view. Note: If DHCS Investigations/BPAI reports plan to be or are being offered as evidence in a State Fair Hearing, they are subject to customer and/or AR review to permit preparation for the hearing. Informant Identity The identity of the informer. •Do not disclose to the customer or his/her AR •Refer questions to DHCS Investigations. Other Privileged Communication: The following information is classified as other privileged communication. Handle such information as follows: Type Description Disclosed Only When Physician/Patient Confidential communication from a physician Specific written consent from the patient is obtained. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageRelease to Customer or Authorized Representative 2.1.5 2 of 3 Physician/Patient Confidential communication from a physician and the physician requested that the report not be released to the patient Physician’s consent to release and specific written consent form the patient is obtained. Lawyer/Customer Matters of confidential communication between a lawyer and customer Specific written consent from the customer is obtained. However, make no contact with the customer about privileged communications when they have legal counsel in any matter in which the County is a party (for example, State Fair Hearing or petitions for judicial review). Husband/Wife Confidential communication between husband and wife during their marital relationship Written consent from both husband and wife is obtained, even if the marriage has terminated. Income Eligibility Verification System (IEVS): Case information obtained through IEVS requires special handling to protect the confidentiality of IEVS information which may have been mismatched to the customer. Follow the guidelines below in handles IEVS reports: If the IEVS reports … Then … Verify information previously reported by the customer, •The report is classified as verifications authorized by the customer •Information on the report may be released to the customer. Do not appear to pertain to the customer, Contain previously unreported information, •The report is classified as information provided confidentially by a third party •Information on the report may not be released until the discrepancy has been clarified and the accuracy confirmed. For IEVS reports with a discrepancy, enough information from the reports may be provided to the customer to allow the customer to obtain additional verification and/or clarification. Example: EDD reports a match of SSN to a UIB recipient. The name does not match, and the customer claims no UIB income. The EDD Field Office number from the report may be provided to the customer to aid EDD in clarifying the discrepancy. The name of the UIB recipient shown on the report may not be released. Requests for Photocopies/Printouts from Case Record: Process requests for items in the case record from the customer or as authorized by the customer as follows: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageRelease to Customer or Authorized Representative 2.1.5 3 of 3 If the request is … Then … For a specific item or items in the case record (for example, birth certificate, ID, SSN card, etc.), Provide photocopies or printouts of the requested item(s). A general request (for example, the case file), Do not provide photocopies or printouts. Procedure: Follow the policies above to maintain confidential information. Other Program Impacts: None. References: MPP 19-000 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 09/31/2022. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageRequests for Information from Other Entities 2.1.6 1 of 5 Revision Date: September 1, 2019 Background: This section provides instructions for what information may be released to another entity Purpose: This section is updated to the current format and adds information from Memo 18-07, which is now obsolete. Policy: General Guidelines: Use the following guidelines when handling requests for information from specific groups and/or individuals: If the request for information is … Then … Questionable or unreasonable (not related to the responsibilities of the requesting office), Step Action 1 Obtain a written statement about the request and circumstance of the request from the requesting entity. 2 Forward the written statement to the FRC Manager for review and approval/ disapproval of the request. When necessary, the FRC Manager will forward the request to the Chief for further review and approval/ disapproval. On a closed case, Refer the requesting entity to Access. On an active case, Process the request for information for entities and people not listed on the Authorized Disclosure List using the procedures below. Absent Parents, Family, or Friends: Obtain a written consent from the customer prior to releasing information to absent parents, the customer’s family, or friends. In handling such request, follow the procedures below: Step Action 1 Do not acknowledge to the requesting person that the customer or the customer’s child(ren) have applied for or are receiving aid or services. 2 Advise the requesting person that he/she must submit a written request for any information including his/her address and phone number. 3 Notify the customer of the request for information upon receipt of the written request. If the customer … Then … Wants to provide the information directly to the requesting person, Document resolution in the case. Is willing to provide the written County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageRequests for Information from Other Entities 2.1.6 2 of 5 authorization for the release of the requested information, Step Action 1 Request proof of identity from the requesting person. 2 Obtain written authorization for release of information from the customer. 3 Process the request for information only when the identity of the requestor and written authorization from the customer are received. Does not want to provide the information to the requesting person, Do not release any information to the requesting person. The requesting person, at his/her own discretion, may contact the DA or private attorney and use legal recourse. If an absent parent claims that the aided parent has kidnapped, abused, or neglected the child(ren), refer the case to Child Welfare Services for appropriate action. Report the claim to the Child Abuse Hotline (858-560-2191). Provide the absent parent with the hotline number for future use. Board of Supervisors and Other Legislative Entity: Refer all inquiries from the Board of Supervisors or other legislative entities to the FRC Manager for resolution. These inquiries may include, but are not limited to: •General request for information on program or FRC procedures •Request based on complaints by a customer about HHSA handling of his/her case •Request based on an anonymous complaint about case handling or to a customer. Follow the procedures below for processing such inquiries: Step Action 1 Determine if the inquiry can be responded to or issue is resolved without releasing confidential information about a customer. If … Then … Yes, Provide general program information or information about FRC procedures. No, Proceed to Step 2 as the customer’s authorization for release of information is required. 2 Determine if the Board of Supervisors or Legislative entity received a written request/ inquiry for assistance from the customer about his/her application or eligibility for public social services. If … Then … County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageRequests for Information from Other Entities 2.1.6 3 of 5 Yes, Obtain a copy of the written request/inquiry for assistance from the Board of Supervisors or Legislative entity and proceed to Step 3. No, Obtain oral or written authorization from the customer and proceed to Step 3. 3 Respond to the inquiry with the proper authorization documentation on file, releasing only information enough to answer such an inquiry. Proceed to Step 4 only if the issue or result cannot be resolved. 4 Contact the Chief for additional clarification and direction needed to respond to the inquiry. Businesses: Release of information to businesses is only authorized when HHSA has a written and dated authorization from the customer. Valid business inquiries may include grant and address information to establish a customer’s credit but do not include inquiries to pursue collection on a delinquent account. Defense Attorney: Refer requests from defense attorney, including Legal Aid Society and the Public Defender, which does not include a customer authorized release, to EO for an explanation on how to subpoena records. Law Enforcement Officials: Confidential information about a customer may be released to a state or local law enforcement agency only in the course of investigations, prosecutions, civil/criminal proceedings directly related to the administration of the Medi-Cal Program. All types of information, written or oral, is confidential and is not open to examination other than for purposes directly connected with the administration of the Medi-Cal Program, such as conducting or assisting an investigation, prosecution, or civil/criminal proceeding related to the administration of the Medi-Cal Program. The non-disclosure policy applies to all requests for information, including those from other government agencies, the courts (unless ordered by the court to do otherwise), and law enforcement officials. Follow the procedures for processing inquiries from law enforcement officials below. If the inquiry is … Then … Associated with an investigation, prosecution, civil/criminal proceeding directly related to the administration of the Medi-Cal Program, Release the information to the requesting law enforcement official. Customer’s consent is not required. For information from a Medi-Cal case record of a deceased customer, Do not release the information to the requesting law enforcement official. For information from a Medi-Cal case record of customers with Do not release the information to the requesting law enforcement official. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageRequests for Information from Other Entities 2.1.6 4 of 5 outstanding felony and/or misdemeanor arrest warrants, Refer questions in this regard to DHCS Investigations. Medi-Cal Providers: Limited beneficiary eligibility information will be given to Medi-Cal providers when requested. Medi- Cal providers include: •Hospitals •Primary Care Clinics •Managed Care Plans •Private Providers •County Medical Services (CMS) If the eligibility information requested is within the last 12 months, encourage the provider to use the POS system to verify eligibility. Refer to MPG 14.3 if the information requested is for a period over one year from the date of the request. Process requests received from Medi-Cal providers as shown below: If the Medi-Cal provider is asking for … Then … Client Identification Number (CIN) or Benefits Identification Card (BIC) information, Date of Birth, Other health coverage, Medicare coverage, Any restricted status, Provide the information. Eligibility status for specific month(s), Indicate if the individual is eligible or ineligible, share of cost, and LTC status. Reason for ineligibility, Do not release the information, unless written authorization from the beneficiary is in the case. Third-Party Contracted Staff/Application Assistors at Hospitals: Third-Party contracted staff/application assistors at hospitals may act as the agent of a Medi-Cal provider (including hospitals) for certain authorized activities. Information cannot be provided without a signed release from the customer. Public Administrator: In San Diego County, the Public Administrator is the Indigent Burial Officer and operates the Indigent Burial Program as an agent of HHSA. Information from Medi-Cal records may be released to the Public Administrator when the information is needed for the operation of the Indigent Burial Program. Consent of the customer is not required. Private Organizations/People: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageRequests for Information from Other Entities 2.1.6 5 of 5 Inform private organizations and people not on the Authorized Disclosure list who request information, including whether a person is receiving or has received aid, about regulations about confidentiality of case records. Often, general statistical or specific program information can resolve the inquiry. Evaluate all unauthorized inquiries for referral to other agencies or offices. Refer media inquiries directly to the FRC Manager, who will refer the media to the Office of Public Relations. Research Organization: Before gaining access to case records, research organizations or graduate students conducting research for a thesis or term paper must have prior approval from an assistant deputy director from EO. The Knowledge Center has responsibility for submitting research proposals to the assistant deputy director. Other Requests: Refer confidential questions or requests for release of information not addressed in this Article to the FRC Manager for review. Unauthorized disclosure of confidential information may render the County and/or staff liable for criminal and civil suits. Procedure: Follow the policies above to maintain confidential information. Other Program Impacts: None. References: W&I 10850.3d and 10850.7c MPP 19-000 MEPM 2H ACWDLs 08-04 and 00-43 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 09/31/2022. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageInspection of Case Records 2.1.7 1 of 2 Revision Date: September 1, 2019 Background: Authorized people requesting review, as well as those authorized to make the inspection, must agree to the HHSA review procedures listed below before being allowed access to the case record. Authorized people requesting review in preparation for a State hearing will be subject to these HHSA review procedures. If a more extensive review is requested, the customer should be referred to the Appeals section to schedule an appointment. Purpose: This section is updated to the current format. Policy: Processing Requests for Inspection of Case Records: Forward all requests for inspection of case records (except for those from customers/Ars during an appeal) to Regional Support. This applies to requests on closed and active cases. Upon receipt of the request, Regional Support will coordinate with the FRC that has the assigned case and the customer or his/her AR for the case inspection. HHSA Case Review Guidelines: Guidelines on inspection of case records are as follows: •The complete case record, including case comments, will be made available for inspection, except for privileged information which may not be released to the customer or his/her AR. •For case comments, a thorough review of case comments must be conducted and any comments which contain privileged information must be removed prior to the case inspection. •Privileged information which may not be released if required consent has not been obtained, must be removed from the case before any review by the customer or his/her AR. •Case inspection will be permitted only during normal working hours. •FRCs will make a private room available for record review where staff and customer and/or AR may discuss case contents. •No case will be made available unless a staff member is present during the entire period of examination except for requests made to the Appeals section for cases in the State hearing process. •The reviewers will not be permitted to remove, alter, photocopy, print, or photograph anything in case records. Reviewers may photocopy or print items necessary to prepare for the State Hearing for cases in Appeals. •The reviewers will be permitted to make notes on what they see in the case record. •Requests for photocopies or printouts of specific items will be processed. •Requests for photocopies or printouts of general requests (for example, the case file) will not be processed. •Provide printed MPG sections upon request. Provide the url (web address) to the Medi-Cal Program Guide if the customer and/or AR request viewing at a location other than the FRC. Purpose: This section is updated to the current format. Policy: To protect the confidentiality of an individual public assistance customer, the individual must be given the opportunity to provide needed information or verifications in a manner which does not identify the individual as a public assistance customer. Before a collateral contact is initiated, inform the customer of his/her option to obtain the needed information himself/herself without any requirement to use county forms or form letters. Except for CDHS/BPAI staff, the customer’s written consent must be obtained prior to initiating collateral contacts. Procedure: Follow the policies above to maintain confidential information. Other Program Impacts: None. References: County Policy Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 09/31/2022. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations

sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageConfidential Information 2.1.1 1 of 2 Revision Date: September 1, 2019 Background: Confidentiality regulations were created to protect customers against identification, exploitation, or stigma that could result from the release of information identifying them as having applied for or received public assistance. These regulations are outlined in the State CDSS Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) Division 19-000. MPG Article 2, Section 1 provides staff with policies and procedures regarding the confidentiality of HHSA Medi-Cal case records and release of information to qualified agencies, people, and Medi-Cal providers. The unauthorized release and possession of confidential information is a violation of MPP confidentiality regulations and can be prosecuted as a misdemeanor. Purpose: This section is revised to include information from Medi-Cal Memo 15-35 and to update to the current format. Policy: Policy and Procedures Governing Confidentiality: HHSA employees are encouraged to respond to inquiries by providing information regarding HHSA policies and procedures. However, care must be taken to preserve the confidentiality of HHSA case records. All reference to “case records” includes all documents, forms, and communications, including those stored electronically. Prior to the release of confidential information to other agencies or individuals, review the policies and procedures detailed in this Article, the Confidentiality Eligibility Policies and Procedures Guide (EPPG), and, when necessary, MPP 19-000. Unauthorized disclosure of confidential information by a County employee is a misdemeanor and may lead to criminal or civil liability for both County employees and the County. The County may also take disciplinary action against the employee. Information that Is Confidential: All information in case records, including names, addresses, and eligibility information about the circumstances of any customer, including whether that person is a customer, is confidential and must be safeguarded. This applies to all information obtained from, for, and about all customers, whether received in writing or orally. Do not disclose confidential information for any purposes not directly related to the administration of public social services programs or as noted in this Article. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageConfidential Information 2.1.1 2 of 2 Information that Is Not Confidential: Statistical information and social data which is not identified with an individual may be released. Examples of information that may be released include, but are not limited to, such information as statements on the number of beneficiaries, total expenditures per program or administration, average grant amount figures, and other general information about the caseload. Avoiding a Breach in Confidentiality for ACA Cases: When any of the following items are entered in CalWIN for an individual, the individual will be added to the CalHEERS case and the family could receive notices with their information: •“Yes” for the field “In Home” •“Yes” for “Requesting Assistance” •Added to the “Tax Filer” window. If the individual is not in the home or is not requesting, confidential information may be released erroneously to or about this individual. To prevent a breach in confidentiality, carefully review entries for every individual listed in a case and ensure that these entries are populated with the appropriate values. Procedure: Follow the policies above to maintain confidential information. Other Program Impacts: None. References: MPP 19-000 MEPM 2H Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 09/31/2022. title: Section 01 - County of Responsibility
content: Article 3 Section 1 – County of Responsibility Table of Contents TITLE MPG CITE Overview 03.01.01 Family Composition • Persons With a Family • Persons Without a Family 03.01.02 Out-of-Home Placement • Public Agency/Government Representative • Private Agency/State Employed Person • Persons Placed in State Hospitals • Placement in Long Term Care after Release from a State Hospital • Long-Term Care – Incompetent/Incapacitated Individuals 03.01.03 General Situations • Public Assistance • Deceased Persons • Persons Absent from the State • Courtesy Applications • Persons Under 21 Years of Age 03.01.04 03.01.01 County of Responsibility A. Overview The procedures contained in this section are administrative guidelines provided by the Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) to county staff to process Medi-Cal applications and to ensure that benefits and services remain accessible to applicants, beneficiaries, and representatives acting on behalf of the applicants/beneficiaries. The objective of these procedures is to provide counties with information to administer the Medi-Cal program in a coordinated and efficient manner within the state and grant benefits promptly. In resolving County of Responsibility issues, staff shall consider criteria such as: •The age of the applicant/beneficiary and his/her representative; •The physical and mental condition of the applicant/beneficiary; MEM PROC. 3B •The travel distance of the applicant/beneficiary and his/her representative; •The possible delay in the processing of the application and eligibility determination that may create an undue hardship for the applicant/beneficiary and/or his/her representative 03.01.02 Family Composition A. Persons with a Family For individuals whose eligibility is determined as part of a family or based on family income, the County of Responsibility is one of the following: •The county of physical presence if the family’s residence is unclear, or •The county in which the family’s principal residence is located Example: An individual is involved in an automobile accident and hospitalized in County A. The individual is expected to remain hospitalized for less than 30 days. The individual has an intact family consisting of a spouse and two children living in County B. The County of Responsibility shall be County B. For individuals in Long Term Care that have a public guardian/conservator or are incompetent, the County of Responsibility is determined in accordance with MPG 03.01.03, Items D and E. MEM PROC. 3C B. Persons without a Family A. For persons whose eligibility is not determined as part of a family, nor based on family income, the County of Responsibility is the county where the person lives and maintains residence. Example: The Joneses have a home in County A. Mr. and Mrs. Jones decide to end their marriage. Mr. Jones lives in County B and Mrs. Jones and the children remain in the home in County A. County A is responsible for Mrs. Jones and the children. County B is responsible for Mr. Jones because Mr. and Mrs. Jones are no longer living together. In this situation, there is no “marital tie” and Mr. Jones' income is not used to determine Mrs. Jones' or the children's share of cost. When a person's residence or identification is unclear, the County of Responsibility is determined by the physical presence of the individual. The person shall be treated as a person without a family. 03.01.03 Out-of-Home Placement A. Public Agency/ Government Representative A government representative is an employee of an administrative agency of a local, state, or federal government. The employee may be a public guardian/conservator or social worker who has placement responsibility of the person. If… Then the County of Responsibility is where the… a person is placed by a government agency/representative into a foster care home, board and care home, or a facility placement agency is located if the public agency is the appointed guardian/ conservator of the person the county where the foster care home, board and care home, or a treatment facility is located accepts a transfer of guardianship/ conservatorship beneficiary is living. The County of Responsibility remains with the placement county until the county agencies work out the transfer/ jurisdiction agreement B. Private Agency/State Employed Person When a person is placed into a board and care home, group home, or treatment facility by a •guardian, •person employed by a private agency, or •the state to act as guardian/conservator for the person The County of Responsibility shall be where the board and care home or treatment facility is located, unless a person’s eligibility is based on the family’s income or is determined as member of an MFBU which includes the family. C. Persons Placed in State Hospitals Persons placed in state hospitals by a county mental health agency or a Regional Center for the developmentally disabled shall have their Medi-Cal eligibility determined by the county in which the state hospital is located, unless the person's eligibility is determined as part of a family or based on family income. In this case, the County of Responsibility is determined in accordance with MPG 03.01.02, item A D. Placement in Long-Term Care after Release from a State Hospital Persons released from a state hospital and placed in a long-term care facility will have their Medi-Cal eligibility determined by the county in which the long-term care facility is located, with the following exceptions: If… Then ... the person(s) has a public guardian or conservator in the county that originally placed the person into the state hospital that county remains the County of Responsibility, unless the county in which the long-term care facility is located agrees to accept guardianship or conservatorship of the person The person’s eligibility is determined as part of a family or based upon family income the County of Responsibility is determined in accordance with MPG 03.01.02, item A E. Long-Term Care – Incompetent/ Incapacitated Individuals If the applicant/beneficiary's community spouse, family member or representative lives in another county within the State of California, staff is expected to work with the applicant/beneficiary or his/her representative to expedite the application/redetermination process. Assistance for the applicant/beneficiary and/or his/her representative shall include but not limited to: •Reviewing the Statement of Facts •Gathering Information •Determining eligibility •Issuing benefits Refer to Article 4, Section 2 for procedures dealing with Authorized Representatives and Representatives for incompetent individuals (key persons). The county where the community spouse or applicant/beneficiary's representative resides shall be the County of Responsibility. The responsible county is not determined by the county residence/location of the Authorized Representative appointed by a competent community spouse, responsible relative, or other knowledgeable representative. If ... Then ... a non-institutionalized community County A shall: spouse resides and maintains a home in County A and he/she applies in County A for the incompetent institutionalized spouse who is in an LTC facility in County B •accept the application •assist the community spouse in gathering information •determine eligibility for the institutionalized spouse County A, where the noninstitutionalized community spouse lives, shall retain the case for continued eligibility since the institutionalized spouse is unable to provide information the individual is in a hospital in County A and is being released to an LTC facility in County A. The individual is incompetent and unable to apply for Medi-Cal on his/her own. The individual's adult child, who lives in County B applies for benefits in County B on behalf of the LTC parent County B shall: •accept and process the application •assist the adult child in gathering information •determine eligibility for the individual in LTC County B shall retain the case because the adult child is the beneficiary's representative acting on the beneficiary's behalf for continued eligibility in reporting changes County B shall: •accept the application •contact County A and forward the application/ information to County A the individual is in a hospital in County A and is being released to an LTC facility in County A. The individual is competent, but incapacitated. The individual's adult child, who lives in County B applies for benefits in County B on behalf of the LTC parent County A shall: •accept and process the application •assist the LTC applicant in gathering information •determine eligibility for the individual in LTC 03.01.04 General Situations A. Public Assistance For people eligible for Medi-Cal under CalWORKs or SSI/SSP, the County of Responsibility is established by the regulations of the specific public assistance program. B. Deceased Persons The County of Responsibility for a deceased person is the county where the person was living at the time of death. Example: A person was admitted to a hospital in County A to receive emergency medical treatment. The person died in the hospital. The person was living in County B at the time of death. County B is the county responsible for taking the application; determining eligibility, and issuing benefits for the deceased person. If the deceased person's family or representative applies in any county within the state, the county in which the applicant’s representative applies in shall accept the application and process the application under the courtesy application procedures. C. Persons Absent from the State Persons who are absent from the state but retain California residence, in accordance with MPG Article 7, Se ction 5, have their Medi-Cal eligibility determined by the county which would have been the County of Responsibility prior to the person's absence from the state. D. Courtesy Application A courtesy application is an application made in a county other than the County of Responsibility. The county in which an applicant or his/her representative applies for benefits is the county responsible for making the initial eligibility determination even if it is not the applicant’s county of residence. The county in which the individual or his/her representative applies must accept and process the application. If all of the information required for making the eligibility determination is available, the county shall: Step Action 1 Review application for completion. If … Then … complete complete Step 2 and 3 incomplete complete Step 4 2 Issue benefits promptly before the case information and verifications are transferred to the beneficiary’s residence county, the County of Responsibility. 3 Follow the procedures outlined in Article 3, Sect ion 2 to process an Inter-county Transfer via an eICT. 4 Forward the application and all information collected within 15 days from the date of application to the County of Responsibility for follow-up and completion of the initial eligibility determination. Example: An individual lives in County A and becomes ill in County B. The individual is immediately admitted to a hospital in County B. County B has an outstationed eligibility worker at the hospital who receives a Medi-Cal referral from the hospital staff. The individual, with the worker’s assistance, can complete the Application (SAWS1), Statement of Facts (MC 210), and provide County B with the sufficient information to determine initial eligibility. County B shall grant the individual's benefits before transferring the continued eligibility case responsibility to County A, the beneficiary's county of residence. E. Persons Under 21 Years of Age When determining the County of Responsibility for a person under 21 years of age, parental control and the person's tax dependent status shall be evaluated. Parental control for the purposes of determining the County of Responsibility is the authority of the parent(s) to make decision on the child's behalf, whether or not the control is actually exercised. A child who is away at school but returns home on some weekends, holidays, or vacations and is subject to parental control is considered temporarily absent from the parents' household, regardless of the duration of the absence. When ... Then … a person who is under age 21 is living away from home, and claimed by his/her parents as the County of Responsibility is where the claiming parents live (except for Minor Consent dependent for tax purposes applications) if the parents live in the State a person is between age 18 and 21, living in California but his/her parents, who claim the child as a tax dependent, live out-of-state. the County of Responsibility is where the child lives but the parents must complete the MC 210, provide the county with information/verification, and cooperate with county staff in the child's eligibility determination process. The county where the child is physically present shall contact the child's parents and ask the parents to complete the application and grant benefits to the child if eligibility conditions are met The applicant is under age 21, living away from home and does not have information on his/her tax dependent status the application for Medi-Cal shall be accepted in the county where the applicant lives

title: Section 02 - Intercounty Transfers
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageIntercounty Transfers 03.02 1 of 5 Revision Date: 04/01/2021 Background: When a Medi-Cal beneficiary moves permanently from one county to another within the state, the beneficiary’s Medi-Cal benefits must be transferred to the new county with no interruption in benefits. The process of transferring responsibility for a beneficiary’s Medi-Cal benefits from one county to another is called an Intercounty Transfer (ICT). The statewide Electronic Intercounty Transfers (eICT) system connects all California counties, allowing Human Services Specialists (HSS) to electronically perform an ICT of a case from one county to another regardless of the system that county is using for eligibility determinations. The eICT automates the processes that are essential to the transfer of beneficiary benefits throughout California counties. Purpose: This section was updated to incorporate recent changes to the ICT process for when only part of a household moves to another county along with general clarifications on ICTs. In addition, a sunset review was completed, and obsolete information has been removed. Policy: •Medi-Cal beneficiaries have the option to report a change of county residence in person, in writing, electronically, or by phone. •The Receiving County must not require the individual to complete a new application or a full eligibility review until the next redetermination (RV) date, as established in the case by the Sending County. •HSSs in both Sending and Receiving Counties must ensure all Medi-Cal cases remain active throughout the ICT period with no interruption in benefits. The Sending County may not terminate their case until the effective date in the new county is confirmed. A. Initiating an ICT When a Medi-Cal beneficiary reports a permanent change of county residence, the county that received the notification (Sending or Receiving) must initiate an ICT, using the eICT system, within 7 business days. B. Incoming ICTs The ICT Liaison(s) at each Family Resource Center (FRC) will monitor the receipt of ICTs through the CalWIN system. Access staff will forward any ICTs received via email or telephone to the FRC for processing. C. Outgoing ICT Attachments These documents must be included when sending the ICT: •Current Statement of Facts and supplements (Request for Tax Household Information (RFTHI), RV Forms, etc.) •Identification verification and Social Security numbers •Case Comments for past 12 months County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageIntercounty Transfers 03.02 2 of 5 •Latest Notices of Action (NOA) for eligibility or share of cost (SOC) •Other health coverage information •Income verifications •Citizenship information •MC 05 Veterans Referral Form •Copy of Disability Determination Services Division (DDSD) decision or verification of incapacity •Authorized Representative form(s) D. ICT Transfer Period The Receiving County must complete the ICT no later than the first available benefit month following the 30 days after the beneficiary’s initial notification of their change in residence. The beginning date of aid in the Receiving County is determined by the date the ICT is received. Example: The beneficiary contacts the Sending County on Wednesday, January 10 to report that they are moving to a new county. The Sending County must initiate the ICT within seven business days or, in this instance, no later than Friday, January 19. This ICT must be completed by the next available benefit month which falls after the 30 th day from the beneficiary’s initial notification that they have moved. In this scenario, the beneficiary’s ICT must be processed and completed by the Receiving County, effective March 1. E. Reasons for Not Initiating an ICT An ICT is not required if the beneficiary: •Reports the loss of California residency •Sends in a written request to discontinue Medi-Cal benefits •Is incarcerated •Is ineligible due to institutional status •Is deceased •Is an incompetent long-term care (LTC) individual and the Representative (aka Key Person) or Conservator resides in San Diego County and requests that the case not be transferred. F. Annual RV If an annual RV is due or overdue at the time an address change is reported, the county must not delay initiating the ICT. It is the Receiving County’s responsibility to process the redetermination. G. Managed Care Health Plans (MCHP) If a beneficiary requires non-emergency care and is still enrolled in an MCHP in the county from which they moved, the Medi-Cal Managed Care Ombudsman may be contacted to complete an expedited disenrollment. The Ombudsman can be contacted by the beneficiary or County staff at 1- 888-452-8609 or MMCDOmbudsmanOffice@dhcs.ca.gov. For urgent requests, the Department of Healthcare Services (DHCS) website contains a fillable form for use by County staff: http://dhcs.ca.gov/MCOmbudsman. Emergency services are covered regardless of which plan the beneficiary is assigned. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageIntercounty Transfers 03.02 3 of 5 H. Whereabouts Unknown If a beneficiary contacts either county to report a new address within 30 days of discontinuance for whereabouts unknown, the Sending County must restore the case without a break in aid, and then initiate an ICT to the Receiving County. I. Part of Household Moves Out of County Sending County The Sending County must initiate a manual ICT when a beneficiary reports to either county that they are permanently moving to a new county and are no longer being claimed as a member of the tax household in the Sending County. The Sending County will send the manual ICT within seven business days of notification of the move. The manual ICT process is completed outside of CalWIN so Sending and Receiving Counties must maintain clear and timely communication regarding the status of the ICT. The following documents must be sent securely when initiating a manual ICT: •MC 360 – to include a description of household composition and the contact information for San Diego (manual ICTs only) •Current Statement of Facts and supplements (RV Forms, etc.) •Identification verification and Social Security numbers •Tax filing information •Case Comments relevant to the eligibility determination •Income verifications •Citizenship information During the manual ICT process, the beneficiary will remain active on the Sending County’s case until the Receiving County confirms active Medi-Cal in their county. Once eligibility is established, the Sending County will complete a change in circumstance redetermination for the remaining household members. Receiving County The Receiving County must complete a change in circumstance redetermination after they receive the manual ICT. Information should be obtained through the ICT material received and an ex parte review if necessary. Additional information must only be requested from the beneficiary when necessary and related to the change in circumstances. If the beneficiary who moved out of the household was not the primary contact in the Sending County, the Receiving County must review the Rights and Responsibilities and obtain a signed penalty of perjury statement from the beneficiary for the new case. Exceptions to Manual Processing •If the Sending County receives new and complete information regarding the beneficiary who is moving to the new county (new address, tax filing status, current income, etc.), they will establish a new case and redetermine Medi-Cal eligibility. The Sending County will then initiate the ICT using the eICT automated process. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageIntercounty Transfers 03.02 4 of 5 •An ICT is not initiated if the County is informed of the beneficiary’s move but the address in the new county is not known. An ex parte review must be completed to determine if the new address is available. If the new address is not available, send an MC 355 to the beneficiary at their last known address. If the mail is returned as undeliverable, the beneficiary will be discontinued for whereabouts unknown, and a NOA must be sent to the last known address. •If an individual beneficiary moves to a new county, but they continue to be claimed as a tax household member in their former county, this is not considered an ICT, and they will remain active on the existing case. The county will update the address for the individual only, so they are able to enroll in a health plan in the new county. Temporary Move The ICT process will not be initiated when a family member temporarily moves out of the home to attend school or obtain health treatments outside the county of residence. J. Retroactive Requests The Receiving County is responsible for processing retroactive benefits requests. If the request requires a budget calculation for a period in which the beneficiary was active in the previous county, staff should contact Medi-Cal Program for assistance with obtaining information from the other county. K. Other ICT Types An ICT is required for the following case types: •Aid Code 38 (discontinued CalWORKs) The Receiving County will complete a change in circumstance redetermination using ex parte. •Transitional Medi-Cal •Former Foster Youth •In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS) linked The Sending County worker must complete a Medi-Cal evaluation. If the beneficiary is eligible to ongoing benefits, a Medi-Cal only ICT must be initiated. •Craig v. Bonta The Sending County must notify the Receiving County by sending an MC 360. There is no CalWIN case for these individuals, so ICT documents are not required. •CalWORKs If the Receiving County does not approve a CalWORKs ICT, a Medi-Cal only ICT must be processed. Procedure: Find How-To instructions for the eICT process on the Eligibility Essentials site under CalWIN and Systems Support: HT172 Send an Inter-County Transfer HT173 Cancel an Inter-County Transfer HT174 Request an Inter-County Transfer References: Eligibility Policy and Procedure Guide (EPPG) 01-04 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageIntercounty Transfers 03.02 5 of 5 ACWDLs 03-12, 04-14, 16-10,18-02 and 18-02E Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 03/31/2024

title: Section 01 - Conditions of Eligibility
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageConditions of Eligibility 04.01 1 of 3 Effective Date: 8/1/2021 Background: Medi-Cal applicants must meet several conditions of eligibility. The eligibility and linkage factors to be evaluated are identified in this section. Although there are no income limits for Non-MAGI Medi-Cal some applicable conditions of eligibility must be met before an application for Medi-Cal can be approved, while some must not delay approval. Purpose: This section provides a brief description of each condition of eligibility, if the conditions must be met prior to granting, and refers to the appropriate MPG sections in which the specific requirements for each condition are addressed. This section was updated to note that verification of specific conditions of eligibility must not delay approval. Policy: A. Residence An applicant must be a California resident to be eligible for Medi-Cal. Refer to MPG Article 7, Section 5 for residence requirements. B. Citizenship United States (U.S.) Citizenship/National or legal resident status is not required for eligibility for Medi- Cal benefits. However, the citizenship/immigration status of the applicant determines the level of benefits (full scope or restricted) for which the applicant is potentially eligible depending on their age. MPG Article 7, Sections 1, 2, and 3 define U.S. citizen and non-citizen categories and specify the level of benefits for which the customer is potentially eligible. MPG Article 04.07.13 contains guidance for the reasonable opportunity period to provide citizenship verification. C. Property Limits As a condition of eligibility for Non-MAGI Medi-Cal the total net nonexempt property of the applicant’s Medi-Cal Family Budget Unit (MFBU) must not exceed the property limit established by the Medi-Cal program. MPG Article 9 specifies what property is included in the property reserve and assists the Human Services Specialist (HSS) with the determination of total net nonexempt property. Factors to be considered include the evaluation of: •ownership •availability •spend down •transfer or conversion of property D. Social Security Number (SSN) All applicants who are eligible for full scope benefits are required to provide a SSN within 60 days of application as a condition of eligibility for Medi-Cal. MPG Article 4, Section 11 lists acceptable verification of SSNs and describes referral procedures when the applicant does not have, or is unable to verify, their SSN. Do not delay approval of the application pending verification of the SSN if the customer is otherwise eligible. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageConditions of Eligibility 04.01 2 of 3 E. Unconditionally Available Income (UAI) All applicants are required to apply for any UAI to which they appear eligible. MPG Article 4, Section 12 defines UAI and describes application, cooperation and verification requirements for applicants who must apply for such income. Do not delay approval of the application pending verification of application for UAI if the customer is otherwise eligible. F. Linkage to Public Cash Assistance People who receive a cash grant in certain public assistance cash programs are automatically eligible for Medi-Cal. MPG Article 5, Section 1 identifies public assistance programs that automatically qualify recipients for Medi-Cal benefits. G. Linkage AFDC, ABD, or MI Persons who have linkage to Aid to Families with Dependent Children (AFDC), Aged, Blind, or Disabled (ABD), or Medically Indigent (MI) are eligible for Medi-Cal if all other conditions of eligibility are met. MPG Article 5, Sections 2, 3, and 5 define linkage to these programs. These sections also provide eligibility and verification requirements for applicants who qualify under one or more of these categories. H. Institutional Status The determination of eligibility and the period of eligibility are affected by the institutional status of certain Medi-Cal applicants. MPG Article 6 clarifies situations in which the applicant’s Medi-Cal eligibility is affected by their institutional status. I. Medical Support Referral Medically Needy Only (MNO) applicants, requesting Medi-Cal for a child born out of wedlock or with an absent parent, must cooperate with the Department of Child Support Services (DCSS) by assigning and locating the absent parent and provide information about possible medical support and payments available through a third party. Referral procedures are outlined in Article 4, Section 18. Applicants who refuse to cooperate with the Medical Support Enforcement Program without good cause will be ineligible members of the MFBU. Do not delay approval of the application for completion of the support packet if the customer is otherwise eligible. J. Application for Medicare Customers must apply for Medicare if they have potential eligibility and have 60 days from the date they are informed of the requirement to apply to provide proof of approval or denial. Allow good cause for the verification if the customer has not received a response from the Social Security Administration (SSA). Do not delay approval of the application pending verification of their application status. More information about Medicare can be found in MPG Article 15, section 4. K. Other Health Coverage Customers must supply Other Health Coverage (OHC) information at application and redetermination and report changes to the county within ten days. Most OHC information is obtained and entered in the Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System MEDS through data match (see MPG 15.01 for more information). Do not delay approval pending OHC if the customer is otherwise eligible. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageConditions of Eligibility 04.01 3 of 3 L. Veteran’s Information Customers who indicate that they are veterans must apply for veteran’s benefits through the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The referral process is in MPG article 4, section 12. Do not delay approval pending Veteran’s Information if the customer is otherwise eligible. M. Third Party Liability Customers who have a lawsuit due to accident or injury must provide third party liability information. More information is in MPG 15.03.01. Do not delay approval pending third party liability information if the customer is otherwise eligible. Procedure: Do not delay Medi-Cal approval for verification of SSN, OHC, veteran’s information, third party liability, application for UAI, Citizenship, Satisfactory Immigration Status (SIS), and Medicare if the customer is otherwise eligible. Follow up with the customer after granting requesting verifications using the redetermination timeframes and contact rules and allow 30 days for response (60 days for Medicare and SSN). If there is no response, discontinue only the individuals in the case that were required to provide and failed to comply. References: MEM 50074, 50168(a)(1), 50175, 50185, 50186, 50207, 50404, 50408(a), 50409, 50141 ACWDL 96-27, 07-12, 19-13 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 8/31/2024 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: Section 02 - Application Processing Requirements
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Application Procedures Number Page 04.02.01 1 of 7 Revision Date: October 1, 2025 Background: The application process begins when a customer or Authorized Representative (AR) applies for Medi- Cal benefits by telephone, mail, electronically, or by attending a face-to-face interview. When a request is received without a Statement of Facts (SOF), an Initial Application for CalFresh, Cash Aid, and/or Medi-Cal/Health Care Programs (SAWS 1) application form is filled out and the customer or AR is given a Single Streamlined Application (SSApp) with a reasonable time to submit. Purpose: This section has been revised to include new guidance from the Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) on the acceptance of electronic signatures collected and submitted by a third party. Policy: As part of the application process, all Medi -Cal customers must be informed of their rights and responsibilities. The customer’s Medi-Cal eligibility and share of cost (SOC) determination is made after the customer has applied, completed the SOF, and provided all essential information and verifications. Customers may submit the completed SOF and required verifications by mail, electronically, or in person. Applications and sworn statements may also be completed telephonically. Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 04.07.01 for further guidance on verification requirements. Procedure: A. SAWS 1 A completed SAWS 1 begins the application process by establishing the date of application and months of potential retroactive eligibility. When a SOF is used, the application cannot be denied due to an incomplete or missing SAWS 1. If an individual is deceased or unable to apply on their own behalf, a SAWS 1 may be filed by any of the following: • The customer’s guardian, conservator, or executor • An adult who is in the customer’s household or family • A person who knows the customer’s need to apply • A public agency representative • Someone acting responsibly for the customer if the customer is a minor or incapacitated B. Ways to Apply An individual may apply for Medi-Cal benefits by: • Calling Access at (866) 262-9881 to request a mail-in application • Calling 2-1-1 to apply over the phone with a 2-1-1 San Diego agent • Visiting a Family Resource Center (FRC) or outstation site to request a mail -in application or faceto-face/telephone interview • Submitting an electronic application through BenefitsCal or Covered California (CA) • Applying through the Perinatal Care Network (PCN) • Making the request while receiving aid under another Public Assistance (PA) program County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Application Procedures Number Page 04.02.01 2 of 7 • Faxing or emailing the Document Processing Center (DPC) Electronic Signatures (e -signatures) outside of BenefitsCal and Covered CA, are only acceptable on Medi-Cal forms when collected by the following software companies: • Adobe Sign • Clio Draft (formerly Lawyaw) • DocuSign • Nitro • PandaDoc Note: A typed signature collected outside of the above listed e -signature programs is not acceptable. Refer to MPG 04.02.22 for applications submitted with a typed signature. Insufficient Information Received When an application is unsigned or does not include the information necessary to evaluate eligibility (ex. name and address only) , or form MC 171 Medi -Cal Long -Term Care Facility Admission and Discharge Notification is received and the customer does not have an active or pending case, DPC will register the application and mail an application packet along with form 14 -85 HHSA Reminder Notice. The registered application is then assigned to the corresponding FRC for follow up. Refer to FRC/Office Required Actions 04.02.01F for guidance on follow up actions. C. Date of Application The date of application for Medi-Cal benefits will be established using the following guidelines: If the request is made… then the date of application is the date the… over the phone, phone request is made. in person, SAWS 1 is signed by the customer. by mail, County receives the Medi-Cal application or SAWS 1. online through Covered CA, application is submitted. to the Covered CA call center and the call is transferred to the County as a Quick Sort Transfer, request was transferred by Covered CA to the County, even if a voice mail message is left for Access staff to return. Example 1: Covered CA received a call from a customer on Friday, 3/21/25 at 6 pm. The call was Quick Sort transferred to San Diego County on the same day. The date of application will be 3/21/25. Example 2: Covered CA received a call from a customer on Sunday, 3/23/25. The call was Quick Sort transferred to San Diego County but since the County was not open for business, the customer was able to leave a voice mail message. The date of application will be 3/23/25. online through BenefitsCal, application is received. If received after 5 PM, the application date is the next business day. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Application Procedures Number Page 04.02.01 3 of 7 Applications from Covered CA Advanced Premium Tax Credit (APTC) beneficiaries transitioning to Medi-Cal will reflect the initial application date from the last Covered CA open enrollment or special enrollment. The DPC will register the application using the date the referral was initiated. Note: The date of application will always be the earlier of the two dates when the SOF and SAWS 1 are received separately. D. Processing Requests for a Face-to-Face or Telephone Interview When a customer requests Medi-Cal at an FRC or outstation site, and chooses to attend a face-to-face or telephone interview: Step Action 1 Ask the customer to complete and sign a SAWS 1 to preserve the date of application. 2 Schedule an appointment according to office procedures. 3 Complete the application registration process and assign the pending case to the central pending case bank based on office procedures. 4 Provide the customer with a Medi -Cal application packet and form 14 -85 HHSA which serves as the first contact request for application. Note: FRC staff may screen the customer at the time of request and provide any supplemental forms that may be required. 5 Inform the customer that if Medi-Cal eligibility is approved and they are eligible to enroll in a health plan, the Health Care Options (HCO) packet will arrive by mail for the customer to choose a health plan. If the customer would like assistance with the ir Medi-Cal managed care health plan enrollment or changes, they can contact HCO via phone at 1-800-430- 4263 or by visiting an FRC. 6 Ask the customer if they would like to apply for CalFresh in addition to Medi -Cal. If the customer is interested in applying for CalFresh, inform them to expect an interview within 30 days and they can choose to do so over the phone (refer to CalFresh Prog ram Guide (CFPG) 63-103). The CalFresh interview may be scheduled with the Medi -Cal application to streamline the application process. 7 Complete a journal entry documenting all case actions taken and image the SAWS 1 and form 14-85 HHSA in Hyland if not system generated. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Application Procedures Number Page 04.02.01 4 of 7 Actions to take on the day of the appointment: If the customer… then… does not attend and no contact is made by the customer to reschedule, • send a second 14-85 HHSA ten days from the date the first 14 -85 HHSA was issued • if the customer does not provide an application by the second due date, deny the application and send denial Notice of Action (NOA) does not attend but contact is made by the customer to reschedule, • schedule an appointment according to office procedures • if the customer does not attend the interview, deny the application after two contacts (allow 10 -calendar days for each) have been made attends the face-to-face or telephone interview, process the application as follows. If the application is… then… complete, evaluate for eligibility and notify the customer of the determination. Complete the eligibility determination within the 45- day or 90-day period as specified in MPG 04.02.17. incomplete, follow the two 10-day timeline specified in MPG 04.07.12A to request needed information/verification. E. Processing in Person Requests at FRC for a Mail-In Application Upon an in-person request for a mail-in application, take the following actions to provide the customer with the necessary information at the time of the request: Step Action 1 Explain to the customer that they can apply for Medi -Cal via mail, electronically, or attend a telephone or face-to-face interview. 2 Ask the customer to complete and sign a SAWS 1 to preserve the date of application. Hospital and Community Support Services (HCSS) staff will process the SAWS 1 requests received for their office. 3 Complete the application registration process and assign the pending case to the central pending case bank based on office procedures. 4 Provide the customer with the Medi -Cal application packet and form 14 -85 HHSA which serves as the first contact request for application. Note: Staff may screen the customer at the time of request and provide any supplemental forms that may be required. 5 Inform the customer that if Medi-Cal eligibility is approved and they are eligible to enroll in a health plan, the HCO packet will arrive by mail for the customer to choose a health plan. If the customer would like assistance with their Medi -Cal managed ca re health plan enrollment or to make changes, they can contact HCO via phone or by visiting an FRC. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Applicants Rights and Responsibilities Number Page 04.02.03 1 of 4 Revision Date: 04/01/2021 Background: All applicants must be informed of their rights and responsibilities. The Rights and Responsibilities for Medi-Cal form (MC 219) was updated to reflect new rules and changes in accordance with the Affordable Care Act (ACA). Purpose: This section is revised for the sunset review, no policies or procedures were changed. Policy: Each applicant must be informed of their rights and responsibilities under the Medi -Cal program even if it appears that the applicant is ineligible. As part of the applicant’s rights, information that must be supplied to the applicant includes: • Copy of the Right and Responsibilities form (MC 219) • Information on general Medi-Cal property limits (MC 007 and MC 005, if applicable) • Income Eligibility Verification System (IEVS) information Additionally, evaluate the applicant’s potential eligibility to other Public Assistance (PA) programs, such as CalWORKs and CalFresh only when requested. Refer the applicant to apply for Supplemental Security Income/State Supplementary Payment (SSI/SSP) if they appear eligible to that program. The applicant would only be evaluated for County Medical Services (CMS) if they are not eligible to Medi - Cal. Procedure: 04.02.03A Inform Applicant of Rights All Medi-Cal applicants shall be provided with the following information: Requirement Description MC 219 – Rights and Responsibilities Give or send the MC 219, “Important Information for Persons Requesting Medi- Cal”, to the applicant. Document in case comments that the information was provided to the applicant. It does not have to be returned by the applicant. For CalWORKs applicants who are determined ineligible to CalWORKs but wish to apply for Medi -Cal only, the signed SAWS 2 Plus is an acceptable replacement of the MC 219. Give applicants who request Medi-Cal after a CalFresh only application the MC 219. MC 007 – General Property Limits Give t he MC Information Notice 007 to all applicants who are subject to a property evaluation. All applicants shall be informed of their right to reduce nonexempt excess property within the month of application, provided the applicant receives adequate consideration. Adequate consideration applies only to an institutionalized individual after January 1, 1990. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Applicants Rights and Responsibilities Number Page 04.02.03 2 of 4 Ways to Reduce Excess Property Provide options as to how excess property may be reduced and how adequate consideration may be obtained to establish eligibility in the month of application. Do this as soon as there is an indication that the applicant may be ineligible because of excess property. Such options shall include, but are not limited to: • Paying medical or other bills • Purchasing exempt items • Paying off mortgages or car loans • Making home repairs or improvements to property • Borrowing against the cash values of nonexempt property and life insurance policies and then reducing the proceeds by receiving adequate consideration • Informing the applicant that the cash surrender value of nonexempt life insurance policies and any other asset will be considered unavailable as the applicant continues to make a good faith effort to liquidate the asset • Setting aside up to $1,500 for the individual’s bur ial as a designated Burial Fund Refer to MPG 09.01.09 for more information on reduction of excess property (spend down). IEVS The Single Streamlined Application informs Medi-Cal applicants that their Social Security number (SSN) will be used to access State and Federal information on income and resources. Explain to the applicant that: • the SSN will be used to match information provided to the State by employers, Employment Development Department ( EDD) and financial institutions, • although applicants who are not U nites States citizen and who request restricted benefits are not required to provide a SSN, their SSN will be used to access income and resource information if the applicant voluntarily provides a SSN or if the SSN is available through a prior case record, • information received through IEVS is used to ensure that the eligibility and share of cost (SOC) determination is correct and that the information may be verified through collateral contacts when discrepancies are found. Health Care Options (HCO) Inform the applicant that if Medi-Cal eligibility is approved and they are eligible to enroll in a health plan, the Health Care Options (HCO) packet will arrive by mail for the customer to choose a health plan. If the applicant would like to obtain assistance with their Medi -Cal managed care health plan enrollment or make changes, the customer can: • Contact HCO by telephone • Walk-in to any Family Resource Center (FRC) 04.02.03B Review of Potential Eligibility for Other PA Programs When reviewing the application, evaluate the applicant’s apparent eligibility for CalWORKs, CalFresh, and SSI/SSP.
