sections.text: Article 4, Section 5 – Immediate Medical Need Table of Contents TITLE MPG CITE General 4.05.01 Actions Required Upon Identification of IMN 4.05.02 4.05.01 Immediate Medical Need A. General This section provides instructions for identification of Medi-Cal immediate need situations and requirements for expediting the immediate need applicants’ eligibility determination. Procedures for issuance of immediate need Medi-Cal ID cards are included in MPG Article 14, Section 2. MPG LTR 446 (4/01) MEM 50177 B. Background State DHCS policy requires that when an applicant has an immediate medical need (IMN), the worker must expedite the applicant’s eligibility determination. This policy further states that women who are pregnant are automatically considered to have an IMN, whether or not they plan to carry their pregnancy to term. These policies are applied equally to all applicants and beneficiaries who have an IMN, including those with OHC or coverage through the County Medical Services (CMS) program or Low-Income Health Program (LIHP). MPG LTR 798 (7/13) MEPM 4J County Policy C. Definition An IMN exists when an applicant, or any family member for whom application is made, indicates any of the following conditions or circumstances at any time during the application process: •pregnancy •a hospital or nursing home admission is planned within the next ten working days •a doctor, dentist, clinic, or other medical appointment is scheduled or necessary within the next ten working days and the provider refuses treatment without the Medi-Cal ID card •a prescription must be filled within the next ten working days •a referral (HHSA:CMS-5) from a CMS Program Case Manager of from CMS medical staff indicates an immediate need The applicant’s statement of any of the above conditions or circumstances, verbally or otherwise, is to be accepted for purposes of determining that an IMN exists. MPG LTR 446 (4/01) 4.05.02 Actions Required Upon Identification of IMN A. Required Actions Workers and staff assigned to the rescheduling of appointments must be alert to any indication that an IMN exists and reschedule the new appointment within the IMN timeframe. Applicants with an IMN are not required to specifically request that their eligibility determination be expedited. Immediate need procedures, as identified below, are followed whenever an IMN is identified. MPG LTR 446 (4/01) B. Preapplication When an IMN is identified at pre-application, and potential eligibility exists, the applicant must be scheduled for an immediate need intake appointment. Every effort should be made to schedule the immediate need intake appointment as soon as possible within ten working days to permit completion of the eligibility determination in time to meet the specific requirements of the IMN situation. The worker shall remind the applicant that all required verifications, information, and completed forms must be provided at the intake interview so that an eligibility determination can be made at that time. Cards will be issued the same day for any eligible person with an IMN. If the applicant indicates that any of the required verifications are not available, or that additional assistance with completion of the forms is required due to illiteracy or for other reasons, the applicant will be asked to do the best he/she can and that additional assistance will be provided by available staff. MPG LTR 446 (4/01) MEM 50185 County Policy C. IMN Identified Between Preapplication and Intake If an applicant with a scheduled intake appointment contacts the reschedule clerk to request an earlier appointment due to an IMN, every effort should be made to provide an earlier appointment. MPG LTR 446 (4/01) D. Eligibility Requirements Not Met at Intake If an IMN was identified at pre-application or during the intake, and the worker is unable to certify eligibility because of missing information/verifications, the worker will review the remaining requirements with the applicant and offer assistanc

title: Section 07 - Verification and Documentation Procedures
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification Requirements Number Page 04.07.01 1 of 3 Revision Date: February 1, 2025 Background: Customers are responsible for providing the documents necessary to determine eligibility for the Medi- Cal program. Purpose: This section has been revised to incorporate changes regarding the elimination of the asset test to establish Medi-Cal eligibility on initial applications and ongoing cases effective January 1, 2024. Policy: As part of the application/renewal process, staff must explain verification requirements to the customer, evaluate the customer’s ability to obtain verification and assist in obtaining the verification whenever necessary. For applications received prior to implementation, continue to follow policies and procedures regarding property verification requirements. A. Verification Required Before Approval Certain information provided by the customer on the Statement of Facts (SOF) must be verified prior to approving the application. Information which must be verified prior to approval includes: • Income. • Income deductions (only required to allow the deductions). • Real and personal property (for Non-Modified Adjusted Gross Income [MAGI] Medi-Cal applications dated prior to January 1, 2024). • Age (refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide [MPG] 04.07.01C for more information). • Blindness/disability (Non-MAGI only). • Legal responsibility for a child (if child is applying alone, except for Minor Consent). • Substantial Gainful Activity (SGA) (Non-MAGI only). Verification requirements for application of Unconditionally Available Income ( UAI) and United States (U.S.) Citizenship/Satisfactory Immigration Status (SIS) can be met after approval of the application. Refer to MPG 04.12.01 and 04.07.13 for more information. B. Verification Required within 60 Days Eligibility may be established prior to recei ving the following information, if all other eligibility requirements have been met, provided that approval occurs within 60 days from the date of application: • Social Security Number (SSN) or application for a SSN. • Medicare entitlement. The following individuals are exempt from the SSN requirement: • Deemed Eligible infants. • Customers requesting Minor Consent services. • Refugees applying for Refugee Medical Assistance/Entrant Medical Assistance (RMA/EMA). • Customers who do not claim U.S. Citizenship or SIS and do not have work authorization. Refer to MPG 04.11 for detailed information on SSN requirements. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification Requirements Number Page 04.07.01 2 of 3 C. Self-Attestation Self-attestation is when the individual states that something is true and correct. Unless questionable, self-attestation is acceptable for: • Age. • Date of birth. • Family size. • Residency. • Pregnancy. D. Electronic Verifications (e-verified) for Use in Non-MAGI Determinations When the verifications below are e-verified, they may be used to determine Non-MAGI eligibility: • Citizenship. • Identity. • Immigration status. • SSN. • Medicare. • Incarceration. • Deceased. • Disability. Note: For clarification on whether an application must be run through the California Healthcare, Eligibility, Enrollment, and Retention System (CalHEERS) Business Rules Engine (BRE), refer to MPG 04.02.22. E. Telephone/Electronic Signature Accept telephonically recorded and electronic signatures as well as handwritten signatures transmitted via fax or email for any form that must be signed for the Medi -Cal program. Please refer to Self- Sufficiency Services Processing Guide – Telephonic/ Electronic Signatures for methods of accepting telephonic/electronic signatures. A sworn statement may be signed telephonically under penalty of perjury if a customer must provide a sworn statement for purposes of written verification, electronic verification was not successful , and other methods of paper verification are unavailable. F. Verifications for Retroactive Medi-Cal When “no change” is reported on the MC 210A Retroactive Medi-Cal Request form, no verification is required beyond what is used to determine current and ongoing Medi -Cal eligibility. If a change is reported, verification is required. G. Verifications for Renewals Items that must be re -verified at re newal are those which have not been previously verified or are subject to change. If the verification was previously unavailable, research to see if that verification is now available. Refer to MPG 04.15 for more information on renewal requirements. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification Requirements Number Page 04.07.01 3 of 3 H. Additional Verifications Do not request verification of items not listed in MPG 0 4.07 or a cross-referenced section, which specifically addresses the item unless it is considered necessary to ensure correct eligibility determination in a specific case. In those instances, indicate the nature of the additional verification requested and the reason for the request in a Journal Entry (JE). Procedures: None Program Impacts: None References: 22CCR 50101, 50167, 50168, 50169, 50185 MEPM 4M, 24-B MEPM Letter 274, Letter 285 ACWDL 06-15, 07-12, 08-03, 08-26, 08-29, 08-54,19-13, 19-17, 20-17, 21-12, 22-25 MEDIL I 13-12, 14-16, 14-23, 14-31, 23-57 Clarifications from DHCS Processing Guide 01-Medi-Cal Annual Redetermination Desk Aid 08- Medi-Cal Verification Requirements Chart Desk Aid 97-Verification Processing Guidelines for CF-CW-MC Applications Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by February 29, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification of Income Number Page 04.07.02 1 of 8 Revision Date: October 1, 2025 Background: Non-exempt income of a customer must be verified prior to approval of an application or renewal. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide guidance on income verifications and policy changes due to the discontinuance of Equifax Verify Current Income (VCI) effective January 1, 2025, and the elimination of the requirement to apply for other Unconditionally Available Income (UAI) effective June 1, 2025. Policy: A. Earned Income Acceptable verifications of earned income include but are not limited to: Verification Type Example One Paystub A document from an employer that details the customer’s earnings and deductions for a specific pay period providing a breakdown of gross pay, taxes, and net pay. It does not have to be dated within the last 30 days if: • it is the most recent available. • i t accurately reflects the amount reported on the application or redetermination form. Additional paystubs may be requested if the income reported is inconsistent with that of the one submitted. Refer to Medi-Cal Desk Aid 33 Paycheck and Other Income Stubs General Information. Note: A discrepancy does not exist if the income reported on the application is clearly “net” earnings. Income Tax Return A copy of the previous year’s federal income tax return that accurately reflects current income. Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 04.07.02D. Statement from Employer A signed letter from the employer that shows the gross amount and date of payment. Employer Statement Form GEN 111 may also be used to assist the customer with obtaining this verification. If none of the above are available, refer to MPG 04.07.10 for the use of sworn statement s or the Statement of Facts (SOF) in lieu of a sworn statement. B. Self-Employment Income Acceptable verification of self-employment income includes but is not limited to: • Receipts showing gross earnings and expenses. • Business records or Profit and Loss (P&L) statements. These records are not required to be for the entire year. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification of Income Number Page 04.07.02 2 of 8 • A copy of the most recent federal income tax return and the appropriate schedule below: o Schedule C – Profit or Loss from Business. o Schedule D – Capital Gains and Losses. o Schedule F – Profit or Loss from Farming. Refer to MPG 04.07.02D for information on how to use the federal income tax return for purposes of self-employment income verification. Accept any records that are available and accurately reflect the customer’s stated net income from their business. C. Unearned Income Acceptable verifications for unearned income include but are not limited to: • An award letter or the most recent Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA) increase notice. • Income Eligibility and Verification System/Payment Verification System ( IEVS/PVS) reports. Refer to MPG 16.01 for information. • A current bank statement for unearned income that is direct deposited*. • A copy of a check or paystubs*. • A signed statement from the person or organization providing the income. • A SOF or a sworn statement for income received from the United States g overnment can be used as verification pending receipt of verification from the appropriate government agency when one of the above items cannot be provided. Refer to MPG 10.02.01 for information on unearned income. *The following must be considered f or customer’s receiving income from the Social Security Administration (SSA): • The amount shown may be the net amount if Medicare premiums are being deducted or an overpayment is being collected. • Do not require copies of checks issued by the United States government. Ask the customer if they are paying for Medicare or repaying an overpayment. • Verification of this amount may be necessary if IEVS is not available. • Health care premiums may be allowed as a deduction and overpayment deductions may be considered unavailable income. Refer to MPG 10.01 and MPG 10.06. D. Use of Federal Income Tax Return to Verify Income A copy of the previous year’s federal income tax return (IRS 1040 or 1040-SR) is acceptable verification of income if it reflects the income reported on the SOF. When using form 1040/1040-SR, the procedures below must be followed: • Count the positive gross amounts that are reported in the i ncome section (Lines 1- 8) of the tax return. • Do not count the income reported on the tax return that is no longer being received. • Treat negative amounts reported in the income section as zero. • Use the positive income amounts, divided by 12 (or the number of months it was received), as the average monthly gross income figures. • Use the average monthly gross income figures to compute the correct level of benefits unless there is a discrepancy with the income reported on the SOF. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification of Income Number Page 04.07.02 3 of 8 • Small discrepancies due to a pay increase or COLA may be clarified over the phone. A Journal Entry must be completed. The most accurate amount between the income reported on the 1040/1040-SR and the amount reported on the SOF will be used. • Request current information to clarify significant discrepancies other than those due to a pay increase or COLA. Note: When a customer is reporting self -employment income, f ollow MPG 10.05.03 procedures for using Schedule C or F as verification. Example 1: A customer applies for Medi -Cal and reports income from a job of several years and spousal support. The SOF indicates that they earn $2,000 per month and receive $165 in monthly spousal support. They provide the previous year’s tax return as verification of income which confirms the information reported on the SOF. The tax return is used to compute eligibility as follows: Step Action Calculation 1 Review Line 1 (wages, salaries, tips) on IRS Form 1040. $24,000 per year. 2 Review Line 2a (alimony [spousal support] received) on IRS Form Schedule 1. $2,000 per year. 3 Calculate gross earnings by dividing each line by 12. • Gross earned income = $2,000 per month. • Gross unearned income = $166.66 per month. Example 2: A customer a pplies for Medi -Cal and the SOF indicates earning s of $4,000 per month. Previous year’s tax return is provided as verification of income. The tax return reflects both earnings and unemployment benefits. The customer explains that they received unemployment benefits for one month and received income from employment for the remainder of the year (11 months). They continue to work at the same job. The tax return is used to compute eligibility as follows: Step Action Calculation 1 Review Line 1 (wages, salaries, tips) on IRS Form 1040/1040-SR. $46,000 per year. 2 Review Line 7 (unemployment compensation) on IRS Form Schedule 1. $200 per year. 3 Calculate gross earnings by dividing Line 1 by 11 (the number of months he had earnings). • Gross earned income = $4,181.81 per month • Because the unemployment benefits have stopped, they will not be counted toward determining his Medi-Cal Non-Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) eligibility. E. Income from S-Corporations S-Corporations are corporations that elect t o pass their corporate income, losses, deductions, and credits through to their shareholders for federal tax purposes. The shareholders are the n required to report the flow-through of income and losses on their personal tax returns. Customers can provide tax County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification of Income Number Page 04.07.02 4 of 8 returns from the previous year as verification of income received from an S -Corporation. The amount entered as income or loss is the amount that should be used when evaluating Medi-Cal eligibility. If the customer claims the loss is not reflected on the previous year’s tax return, they can provide one of the following: • A Schedule K-1 from the previous year along with a sworn statement that explains the cause of the change, the income amount, and the expected portion of loss for the current year, documenting that the customer is the sole distributor of the profit/loss for the corporation. • A profit/loss statement, along with a sworn statement that confirms the anticipated profit/loss for the current year based on tax filing rules. • If documentation is unavailable and all other verification attempts are unsuccessful, a signed and dated sworn statement that explains the c ause of the change in income, the income amount, and the expected portion of loss for the year can be accepted as a last resort. F. In-Kind Income Verification is only required if the customer claims the amount is lower than the allowable standard. A written statement from the provider is acceptable. Refer to MPG 11.1A Appendix A Assistance Standards Chart. G. Fluctuating Income Fluctuating income may be verified by using paystubs, copies of checks, or a signed statement which includes the gross income amount and pay frequenc y from the person or organization making the payments. H. Tip Income Acceptable verifications of tip income are the amount reported on the paystub or by the customer. If a discrepancy exists regarding the amount reported, the customer may sign a sworn statement clarifying the reason. I. Temporary Worker’s Compensation An award letter from the insurance company or other entity which identifies the payments as temporary, indicates the amount, and the schedule of the payments may be accepted. J. Veterans Assistance (VA) Acceptable verifications of VA or Aid and Attendance Payments are: • A completed Military Verification and Referral Form (MC 05). • Documentation in the Journal that the VA check was viewed. • A VA Benefit Summary Letter or VA Award Letter. K. Veterans Education Benefits Acceptable verifications of Veterans Education Benefits are: Verification Type Example General Issue (GI) Bill. The VA Benefit Summary Letter or VA Award Letter is acceptable evidence to document the type, amount, and frequency of payments. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification of Income Number Page 04.07.02 5 of 8 Post 9/11 GI Bill. Post 9/11 GI Bill payments are identified as VA Chapter 33 payments. The VA Benefit Summary Letter/VA Award Letter is acceptable evidence to document the type, amount, and frequency of payments. Veterans Educational Assistance Program (VEAP). Verify receipt of payments under the VEAP program by completing the MC 05. On the MC 05, include a request for the Office of Military and V eterans Affair (OMVA) to identify under which program educational benefits are being issued. L. Interest or Dividends Acceptable verifications of interest or dividends include but are not limited to: • T ax documents showing the amount of interest/dividend income paid to the individual for the prior tax year. • Current bank statement showing the deposit of interest/dividend income. • Account statement. • Payment record. M. Child/Spousal Support Acceptable verifications of child/spousal support include but are not limited to: • Court documents. • Department of Child Support Services (DCSS) records. • Sworn statement from the absent parent. • Copy of the check. N. Educational Grants/Loans Educational grants/loans may be verified by viewing the Financial Aid papers provided by the college/university and documenting the information in the case record. O. Net Income from Property Acceptable verifications of net income from property include but are not limited to: • Lease or sales agreement. • Bookkeeping records. • Tax documents – Profit and Loss statements detailing allowable expenses. • Bank statements showing deposits of income from rental property. P. Unconditionally Available Income (UAI) The requirement to apply for UAI has been eliminated as a condition of Medi -Cal eligibility. Eligibility staff should continue to inform customers of any potential income from available resources. Refer to MPG 04.12 for more information. Q. Zero Income Not Electronically Verified (e-verified) When a customer reports zero income, the information is run through the California Healthcare Eligibility, Enrollment, and Retention System (CalHEERS) Business Rule Engine (BRE). If the income is e-verified, eligibility staff must accept the results. Refer to 04.07.02S Reasonable Explanation and MPG 04.02.22 for more information. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification of Income Number Page 04.07.02 6 of 8 R. VCI for Income Verification Equifax’s VCI service was added as one of the sources in the Federal Data Services Hub (FDSH) for electronic verification of employment. E ffective January 1, 2025, this service has been discontinued until further notice. VCI service data with employment information that was retrieved prior to the discontinuance date will remain available and can be used as a standalone verification of income for ex parte only when reasonably compatible (at or below the program limit) with the attested income. Note: Staff may not use Equifax’s The Work Number service to verify income in Medi -Cal only cases, however The Work Number results can be used for verification if found in a multi -program case file during the ex parte review. S. Reasonable Explanation Customers can provide a verbal or written explanation to resolve discrepancies between their self - attested income and information received through electronic data sources at application, change in circumstance (CIC), or annual renewals. If the reasonable explanation resolves an income discrepancy, continue with the Medi-Cal evaluation without requesting further verification. Attempt to contact a customer and provide a list of reasonable explanations as an opportunity for the customer to resolve income discrepancies. The list includes but is not limited to the following: • Loss of Job. • Decrease in job hours. • Commission based work. • Fluctuating income. • Seasonal Income. • Self-employment Related Reasons. • Change in Marital Status. • Household member moving in or out of home. • H omelessness. • Victim of Identity Theft. • Victim of Natural Disaster. • Intimate Partner Violence. • Other. CalHEERS is automated to include a dropdown menu with reasonable explanation options for customers who appear to be MAGI eligible and meet the following criteria: • Their self-attested MAGI Medi-Cal Current Monthly Income (CMI) and/or MAGI Medi -Cal Reasonably Projected Annual Income (RPAI) or Projected Annual Income (PAI) in under the income limit but is “Pending” verification; and • They are attesting to a countable income greater than $0; and • Their MAGI Medi -Cal Household (HH) Composition does not include an individual that is “Not Verified for CMI, RPAI, and PAI. Note: “Not verified” means the call to the hub was unable to be completed. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification of Income Number Page 04.07.02 7 of 8 If a customer selects a predefined reasonable explanation (excluding “Other”), that reasonable explanation will be considered valid and the income will be verified without requiring further follow -up. If “Other” is selected, the income will remain in a “Pending” status, and the case will be sent to the county via the Determination Eligibility Response (DER) for manual verification. If the customer is successfully contacted and provides a reasonable explanation that resolves the discrepancy, a determination will be sent to CalHEERS through an Eligibility Determination Request (EDR) as “REX- Confirm”, which will resolve the discrepancy automatically. If the “Other” reasonable explanation is denied, the determination will be returned via the EDR as “REX -Deny”, which will indicate that the explanation does not resolve the discrepancy. Additional verification must be requested. The functionality for reasonable explanation for MAGI customers will be in CalHEERS. The functionality for Non-MAGI customers will be in CalSAWS. The automation of reasonable explanation in CalHEERS does not limit a customer’s ability to provide a reasonable explanation in person, by phone or any other means outside of CalHEERS. Eligibility staff should document and provide the reasonable explanation in CalSAWS for Non-MAGI customers or MAGI customers who did not update their information in CalHEERS. For MAGI customers, t his information will be submi tted to CalHEERS via an EDR. This functionality is exclusively for CalHEERS and CalSAWS. Customers applying through BenefitsCal, via paper, or over the phone will follow existing business processes for a reasonable explanation if the income is not reasonably compatible. Journal entries should include the reasonable explanation provided and whether the discrepancy was resolved. If the discrepancy was not resolved, include details of the attempts to resolve, including the request of form DHCS 7103 Request for Additional Income Information for Medi-Cal along with the MC 355 Request for Information or CW 2200 Verification Checklist when unable to contact the customer. If the customer does not provide the DHCS 7103, do not deny or discontinue for failure to provide, continue the normal process of requesting income. A reasonable explanation does not require a telephonic, electronic, or written signature when reported on a signed SOF. Refer to Desk Aid 130 – Reasonable Explanation. Procedures: None Program Impacts: None References: 22CCR 50101, 50167, 50185 MEPM 4M MEPM Letter 274 ACWDLs 01-50, 19-17, 22-08, 22-22, 24-19, 25-15 MEDIL I 24-29, I 25-06 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by September 30, 2028. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification of Income Number Page 04.07.02 8 of 8 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification of Income Deductions Number Page 04.07.03 1 of 3 Revision Date: 04/01/2021 Background: Verification of expenses is only required to allow the deduction from the total countable income. Purpose: Included with the reformatting, this section is updated to remove the use of form DHCS 6155 -Health Insurance Questionnaire. Policy: 04.07.03A Verification of Expenses Verification of expenses is NOT required as a condition of eligibility. 04.07.03B Guardian/Conservator Fees When a guardian/conservator asserts that reasonable court approved fees exist and they have provided verification that the customer has income from which fees are an allowable deduction, take the following actions: Step Action 1 Request: • A copy of the court order authorizing payment of fees from the customer’s account to the guardian/conservator. The order must include the amount of the fee and the month for which the fee is authorized, AND • A written statement from the guardian/conservator describing the services provided during the month, how the fee was calculated, including hours spent on the conservatee’s affairs and the rate being charged as well as any other costs included in the fee. 2 Review the verifications requested in Step 1 and determine whether the fee amount is reasonable: If fee is… Then… Reasonable, Proceed to step 4 Not reasonable, Proceed to step 3 Presume the fees billed in the statement are reasonable provided that the amount matches the amount shown in the court order and there is no circumstance which leads the Human Services Specialist (HSS) to question the fee amount. Examples of questionable fees which may require further review and documentation include: • Fees for personal services • Charges for services not related to the administration of the conservatees estate • Fees which vary from month to month when there is no change in income, property, etc. and there is no court activity County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification of Income Deductions Number Page 04.07.03 2 of 3 3 Request a written statement from the guardian/conservator to clarify fees determined to be questionable. The statement needs to address why the: • P ersonal services are required • F ees fluctuate from month to month when t here is no change in income, property, etc. and there is no court activity • F ees are higher than what is normally charged for similar service The guardian/conservator must be given a reasonable time to respond. The share of cost (SOC) is to be calculated without the fee deduction until the reasonableness of the fee is verified. 4 Calculate the SOC with the fee deduction 04.07.03C Dependent Care Deduction The dependent care deduction shall encompass the cost of childcare or the cost for care of an incapacitated person. The cost of childcare or care of an incapacitated person will be verified by viewing: • Receipts • Cancelled checks • Signed statement from the person or organization receiving the payment Additionally, if the cost of care is for an incapacitated person, the incapacity must be verified with a written statement from a physician. The statement must specify that the person requires care due to the incapacity. Set an alert on the case to review the incapacity or discontinue allowing the deduction based on the information on the statement. When the incapacity is permanent, the review and reverification will be obtained at the annual redetermination. 04.07.03D Health Insurance Premium Acceptable verifications of health insurance premiums are: • Information about coverage Procedures: None Program Impacts: None References: 22CCR 50101, 50167, 50185 MEPM 4M MEPM Letter 274 ACWDL 13-12 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification of Income Deductions Number Page 04.07.03 3 of 3 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 04/30/2024. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification of Real and Personal Property Number Page 04.07.04 1 of 4 Revision Date: February 1, 2025 Background: As a condition of eligibility for Medi- Cal, verification of real and personal property is required before approval of applications or retroactive benefit months prior to January 1, 2024. Purpose: This section has been revised to incorporate changes regarding the elimination of the asset test to establish Medi-Cal eligibility for initial applications and renewals beginning on or after January 1, 2024. Policy: Verification of real and personal property must meet certain criteria to be considered acceptable. For applications received prior to January 1, 2024, c ontinue to follow policies and procedures regarding property verification requirements. A. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification of California Residency Number Page 04.07.05 1 of 3 Revision Date: August 1, 2026 Background: Following the implementation of Accelerated Enrollment (AE), the Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) has enhanced the residency verification process in the California Healthcare Eligibility, Enrollment and Retention Systems (CalHEERS) to align with state and federal eligibility policy. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide updated guidance on California residency verification requirements. Policy: Medi-Cal applicants must verify California residency prior to the approval of their application. Residency must also be verified whenever one of the following conditions exists: • The customer is absent from the state for more than 60 days. • The customer is absent from the state for less than 60 days and claims to be a resident of California and the County has evidence to the contrary A Post Office (P.O) Box address is acceptable as a mailing address, but it does not meet the residency requirement when listed as the customer’s physical address. A. Electronic Verification (e-verification) of California Residency E-verification must be attempted for every adult at initial application. If the primary applicant is successfully verified, that verification will be applied to all other household members who live with the primary applicant, and do not have conflicting residency information. Applicants whose residency cannot be e -verified and who meet all other Medi -Cal eligibility requirements must be granted AE. Eligibility staff must request manual verification before a final Medi- Cal determination can be made. B. Who Must Provide Verification of Residency Every Medi-Cal applicant must verify their California residency except: • Children whose parents are also applying for Medi-Cal. o The parents’ residency will also establish their children’s residency. • The spouse of a person who has verified their California residency, unless the spouse lives at another address and is requesting Medi-Cal. • Adults or children who are in the care of a government agency in California; provided that the eligibility worker has verified that the person is the responsibility of the agency. • Minor Consent customers. • Customers transitioning to Medi-Cal directly from a cash-based public assistance program with no break in aid, f or example, those coming from Transitional Medi -Cal (TMC), Edwards or Craig v. Bonta aid codes, unless there is evidence that contradicts the residency determination of the cash program. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification of California Residency Number Page 04.07.05 2 of 3 o The journal entry must document that the customer is transitioning directly to Medi -Cal from a cash-based public assistance program. C. Verification of California Residency The following are acceptable forms of residency verification: • A current and valid California driver’s license or California identification card. • Rent, mortgage, or utility bill showing the applicant’s name and California address. • A current and valid California motor vehicle registration. • Employment records showing the applicant is employed in California. • Documentation showing registration with a California employment agency (public or private). • Evidence of school enrollment for self or children in California. • Evidence showing that customer receives public assistance other than Medi -Cal, at an address in California. • Voter registration in California. • A sworn statement or affidavit signed under penalty of perjury. Note: A sworn statement or affidavit alone is not sufficient to verify residency and must be supported by other credible evidence. Customers who are unhoused may provide a letter from a shelter or a community organization they are involved with in addition to their sworn statement. D. Evidence to the Contrary Evidence to the contrary refers to any information available to eligibility staff that contradicts a customer’s California residency claim. This evidence may include, but is not limited to, information or documents which show the customer: • Entered the state for a visit or other temporary purposes. • At the time of application, has plans to leave California to return to another state or country. o For example, a customer that has a return airline ticket and has not previously established nor continuously maintained residency in California. • Has a spouse and/or minor children remaining in another state or country that lived with the customer immediately prior to their arrival in California. • Entered the state solely to obtain medical care and does not intend on establishing California residency. • Possesses a Border Crossing Card or visa of a temporary nature, such as a B1 or B2 visa. • Operates a business or keeps a home outside of California. • Has motor vehicles registered in another state or country. • Has children attending school in another state or country. • Receives public assistance from another state or country. E. Statement of Residency Customers must declare that they meet both of the following conditions at application: • The customer does not own a principal residence outside of California. • The customer is not receiving Public Assistance outside of California. If a customer claim s they have an out-of-state principal residence, as defined per Medi -Cal Program Guide ( MPG) 09.04, then request verification supporting that the customer is a California resident. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification of California Residency Number Page 04.07.05 3 of 3 Make an eligibility determination based on all the information available and narrate the determination in a journal entry. The exception to this is in cases with an unmarried couple living together with a common child; only the person completing the applic ation must make the required residency declarations. F. Questionable Residency If a customer’s California residency remains questionable after all verifications have been reviewed, initiate a fraud referral. Staff must complete a detailed journal entry to support the reason for the referral. Refer to Medi-Cal Processing Guide 19 – Fraud Prevention for additional guidance. Procedure: None Automation: CalHEERS and the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) implemented updates to the residency verification process, making verification a mandatory requirement before a final Medi- Cal eligibility determination can be made. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification Not Available Number Page 04.07.10 1 of 2 Revision Date: February 1, 2025 Background: This section provides guidance to determine if income or property verification is unavailable. Purpose: This section has been revised to incorporate changes regarding the elimination of the asset test to establish Medi-Cal eligibility on initial applications and ongoing cases beginning on or after January 1, 2024. Policy: A. General Verifications of income or property are to be considered unavailable when any of the following, or similar, conditions exist: • Attempts to obtain the verification would put the customer in some bodily danger or would result in loss of employment. • Records were destroyed (for example by fire or flood). • The source of the verification is uncooperative. Note: For applications received prior to implementation, continue to follow policies and procedures regarding property verification requirements. B. Reasonable Attempt When a customer states verification is unavailable, evaluate whether the customer has made reasonable attempts to obtain the verification. A reasonable attempt to obtain the verification must be made by either the customer or staff. The attempt may be made by telephone or in writing to the verification source. All actions taken to obtain verification must be documented in a Journal Entry (JE). The requirement to contact the verification source may be waived if the customer states contact would jeopardize employment or put the customer in danger of physical harm. In this circumstance, the customer must complete a sworn statement describing their situation whereby attempting to get verification may jeopardize them physically or lead to loss of employment. C. Use of Sworn Statement When staff determines that verification is unavailable, a sworn statement from the customer, dated and signed under penalty of perjury, must be obtained. A JE must be included that documents the steps taken to obtain the verification and why it was not available in any other form. D. Submission Methods Sworn statements may be submitted by telephone, mail, in person, of by other commonly available electronic means such as fax and email. Telephonic and electronic signatures are acceptable for sworn statements. Please refer to the Eligibility Operations Processing Guide – Telephonic/Electronic Signatures for methods of accepting telephonic/electronic signatures. Other PA cases include other Medi-Cal, CalFresh (CF), General Relief (GR), California Work Opportunities and Responsibility to Kids (CalWORKs), Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants ( CAPI), County Medical Services (CMS), In- Home Supportive Services (IHSS), and Foster Care (FC) cases. Purpose: Included with the reformatting, this section is updated to include information implemented by the Affordable Care Act (ACA), previously issued in Special Notice (SN) 13-09 Addenda A & D. Policy: 04.07.11A Ex Parte Overview Use the ex parte process when determining Medi-Cal eligibility at application, redetermination or when a change in circumstance occurs that affects Medi -Cal eligibility. Ex parte is the process whereby a Medi-Cal only determination is made without the involvement of the customer. Under ex parte, attempt to complete the Medi -Cal evaluation based on information/verifications included in any of the following: • An active PA case(s) • A PA case that closed within the last ninety (90) days • Other PA case records of beneficiaries and their immediate family members that have been obtained within the last 12 months and are not subject to change (such as Identification, and Social Security Card) Always attempt to obtain needed information/verification by means of the ex parte process prior to: • Denying a case for failure to provide for applicants • Requesting the information/verification from beneficiaries Ex Parte for Applicants Necessary verifications may be requested from applicants after initiating an ex parte review. Always attempt to locate needed information/verification by means of an ex parte review, prior to requesting it from the applicant. Ex Parte For Beneficiaries When a change that affects ongoing eligibility is reported, always attempt to locate needed information/verification by means of an ex parte review, prior to requesting it from the beneficiary. When the ex parte process reveals a change in circumstance that requires a referral or updat e of information to other agencies, the beneficiary must complete the appropriate forms. If phone contact is unsuccessful, send the beneficiary an MC 355 requesting the information/ verification(s) and allow 30 days for a response. If the requested information/verification is not received by the due date without good cause, the individual or case must be discontinued effective the end of month in which the adequate and timely discontinuance NOA requirement is met. Program Impacts: None References: ACWDL 01-36, 01-39, 6-16, 08-07, 08-27,08-27E, 08-29, 08-54, 11-23, 11-27, 18-25 Clarification from DHCS as of 12/1/08 SN 01-08, 01-12, 02-10 MEDIL I 20-13 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 04/30/2024. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Request for Citizenship/Identity Verification Required Under Deficit Reduction Act (DRA) of 2005 Number Page 04.07.13 1 of 6 Revision Date: February 1, 2025 Background: With the passage of the Deficit Reduction Act (DRA) of 2005, individuals who claim United States (U.S.) Citizenship status and who request Medi -Cal benefits must provide acceptable evidence of their Citizenship and Identity (CIT/ID). Purpose: This section was updated to incorporate updated policy regarding the Medi -Cal Adult Expansion that went into effect January 1, 2024. Policy: A. General Staff must assist customer s in obtaining evidence of CIT/ID . Reasonable and heightened assistance must be provided depending on the customer’s circumstances. B. Actions Required Before Requesting Before contacting the customer to request verification of U.S CIT/ID, follow the steps below to determine if they are exempt from the verification requirements, the requirements have been met through the Birth Record Data Match via the Medi -Cal Eligibility Data System ( MEDS), or are electronically-verified (everified) through the Federal Data Services Hub (FDSH) in Covered California. Step Action 1 Determine if the customer is exempt from the U.S. CIT/ID verification requirements, as specified in MPG 07.02.02B. If individual is… then… exempt, • document in a Journal Entry (JE), • ensure that MEDS has appropriate coding(s), • no further action is required. not exempt, go to Step 2. 2 Determine if the customer has already provided acceptable verifications of CIT/ID by: • Performing an ex parte review of county eligibility case records and databases, including documents in the Hyland Imaging system. • Reviewing the verifications that are attached to the application form. • Contacting other counties if there is prior history of benefits in another county shown on the INQM screen of MEDS. If acceptable CIT/ID verification from the individual has… then… already been provided, • issue form DHCS 0011 Proof of Acceptable Citizenship or Identity Documents if acceptable verifications are attached to the application, County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Request for Citizenship/Identity Verification Required Under Deficit Reduction Act (DRA) of 2005 Number Page 04.07.13 2 of 6 • ensure that MEDS has appropriate coding(s), • document actions taken in a JE. not been provided, go to Step 3. 3 Determine if a Social Security Administration ( SSA) CIT/ID verification match was performed by reviewing the CITIZENSHIP -DOC: TYPE and IDENTITY- DOC: TYPE fields on the INQE screen of MEDS. If SSA CIT/ID verification match was… then… performed, follow the procedures found in MPG 07.02.07. not performed, proceed to Step 4. If MEDS is not working properly, report issue to the MEDS Liaison. 4 Determine if the customer was born in California. If the customer was born… then… in California, initiate a Request Match History in the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS). Go to Step 5. in another U.S. state, go to section C below, titled “Required Action When Requesting CIT/ID Documents.” 5 Review result of the Request Match History request. If the result is… then… a match, • verify match on MEDS and notify the customer that the citizenship verification requirement has been met via DHCS 0006 Proof of Citizenship or Identity Needed for Medi-Cal Applicants and Beneficiaries Who Are U.S. Citizens or Nationals, as specified in MPG 07.02.05E, • document in JE, • if evidence of identity is still needed, proceed to section C below, titled “Required Action When Requesting CIT/ID Documents”. is not a match, go to section C below, titled “Required Action When Requesting CIT/ID Documents.” C. Required Action When Requesting CIT/ID Documents The following procedures must only be applied to individuals who meet all the following conditions: • Are not exempt from the DRA CIT/ID verification requirements. • Have not provided acceptable verifications of CIT/ID. • Cannot be verified through the birth record data match or the SSA CIT/ID verification match. • T he results of the SSA CIT/ID verification match, if one was completed, was not discrepant. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Request for Citizenship/Identity Verification Required Under Deficit Reduction Act (DRA) of 2005 Number Page 04.07.13 3 of 6 Once staff has determined that the customer meets all the above conditions, take the following actions: Step Action 1 Attempt to contact the customer by phone and advise them of the need to obtain and provide the required documentation. If phone contact was … then issue full scope benefits if otherwise eligible and… not successful, proceed to Step 2. successful and the customer states they are making attempts to obtain CIT/ID documents, establish the Reasonable Opportunity Period (ROP), refer to section 04.07.13E and go to Step 4. successful but the customer states they will not be providing the required CIT/ID documents, update the Citizenship Status record to undocumented. 2 Send the following forms: • DHCS 0006 - Proof of Citizenship or Identity Needed f or Medi -Cal Applicants and Beneficiaries Who Are U.S. Citizens or Nationals • DHCS 0003 - Affidavit of Reasonable Effort to Get Proof of Citizenship Include form DHCS 0004 Request for California Birth Record for individuals who were born in California with an unsuccessful birth Record Match. This form can be completed for the customer at a Family Resource Center (FRC) or by telephone. Note: The DHCS 0003 is not a required form to establish a ROP. 3 Attempt a 2nd telephone contact if the customer fails to respond to the written contact within ten (10) days and advise them of the need to provide the required documentation. If the phone call was … then issue full scope benefits if otherwise eligible and… not successful, update the Citizenship Status record to undocumented and go to Step 6. successful and the customer states they are making attempts to obtain CIT/ID, establish the ROP and go to Step 4. successful but the customer states they will not be providing the required CIT/ID documents, update the Citizenship Status record to undocumented and go to Step 6. 4 Enter the ROP Due Date on the Citizenship Status Detail page to reevaluate based on the customer’s circumstances and ROP. Refer to 04.07.13F for establishing good faith effort. Note: Set the ROP period to six months from the application or annual renewal date if the customer is unable to specify a timeframe that they will need in order to obtain the required document(s). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Request for Citizenship/Identity Verification Required Under Deficit Reduction Act (DRA) of 2005 Number Page 04.07.13 4 of 6 5 Follow up and notify the customer as appropriate. Reminder: If staff can reach the customer, determine the appropriate follow-up timeframe based on the customer ’s circumstances, establish good faith effort to provide, and set a ROP. 6 Document all actions taken to assist the customer in meeting the CIT/ID verification requirements by entering a JE. These include, but are not limited to: • All efforts made to contact the customer. • Advising the customer of the need to provide evidence of CIT/ID. • Good faith effort made by the customer to obtain evidence of CIT/ID. • Extensions of the ROP. • Follow-up required. • Receipt of evidence of CIT/ID. • Actions taken because of the customer’s inability, refusal, or failure to provide the required documents. • Good cause determination for the customer’s inability, refusal, or failure to provide the required documents. D. Providing Assistance 1. Reasonable Assistance Customers must be provided with reasonable assistance in obtaining and providing acceptable evidence of CIT/ID. Examples of reasonable assistance include, but are not limited to: • Explaining how to provide evidence of good faith effort to obtain documents. • Reviewing and explaining acceptable evidence of CIT/ID. • Determining the possible acceptable documents that may be available to the customer based on individual circumstances. • Providing any available resources to obtain the required documentation, such as the name, address, and telephone number of the vital statistics agency for their state of birth. Staff can find the vital statistics office contact information at S:\Enterprise\Medi-Cal Spreadsheets and Forms\Citizenship Reasonable Assistance Resources. • Using the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlement ( SAVE) system to verify C itizenship for Naturalized Citizens. • Submitting birth information to MEDS for a birth record data match for all customer s born in California. • Reviewing county eligibility files and records to locate evidence of CIT/ID documents that have already been provided. • Reviewing MEDS to determine prior history of public assistance in another county and contacting that county to determine if acceptable documentation of CIT/ID is available. Note: The county does not provide financial assistance for customers to pay for documents. 2. Additional Heightened Assistance Customers incapable of acting on their own behalf to provide acceptable evidence of CIT/ID must be given additional assistance. This includes customers who are: • Homeless. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Request for Citizenship/Identity Verification Required Under Deficit Reduction Act (DRA) of 2005 Number Page 04.07.13 5 of 6 • Amnesia victims. • Mentally impaired. • Physically incapacitated. In addition to providing reasonable assistance: • Contact any known family members who may have CIT/ID documents for the incapacitated person. • Contact any known current or past health care providers, such as long-term care facilities, to see if they have any acceptable evidence of CIT/ID. • Contact other social services agencies within and outside of the county that are known to have assisted the customer to obtain acceptable evidence of CIT/ID. • Follow the Diligent Search procedures in MPG 04.09, if applicable, to assist the customer to obtain the necessary evidence of CIT/ID. E. Setting the ROP ROP of CIT/ID is defined as the time needed for the customer to obtain valid documentation of CIT/ID based on the individual’s: • Circumstances. • Ability to obtain that documentation. • Good faith effort. When considering whether to extend the ROP: • Make the determination on a case-by-case basis, depending on how much time the customer needs to obtain the required information. • Follow up with the customer as needed to ensure that acceptable documentation is in the case file or to provide additional time, if needed. • Issue full scope benefits to customers claiming to be U.S. Citizens, if otherwise eligible and have not presented the required evidence of CIT/ID or stopped making a good faith effort to obtain and provide the required verification. Exception: When a SSA CIT/ID verification match is performed and the result shows a mismatch, the ROP shall be limited to 90 days. The 90- day period starts seven ( 7) days from the date that the staff mails the Information Notice Unable to Verify U.S. Citizenship/Identity Through the Social Security Administration MC 239 DRA-6 notifying the customer of the mismatch. The customer will have 90 days to resolve the mismatch or to provide the required DRA CIT/ID documents. Refer to MPG 07.02.07 for guidance. F. Establishing Good Faith Effort Good faith effort to provide evidence of CIT/ID is defined as demonstration of effort to obtain and provide satisfactory documents to meet the evidence of CIT/ID requirement. Customers may self-attest or provide written statements of their efforts to obtain evidence of CIT/ID . Accept any reasonable information provided by the customer including any basis for a determination that the customer is or is not making a good faith effort. Allow additional time for the customer to acquire the documents when they are demonstrating a good food effort to provide. Examples of good faith effort include, but are not limited to: • Oral or written statements of: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Request for Citizenship/Identity Verification Required Under Deficit Reduction Act (DRA) of 2005 Number Page 04.07.13 6 of 6 o Efforts taken to obtain documentation. o Update of progress made in obtaining evidence of U.S. CIT/ID. o Explanation of attempts to locate two persons who could attest to the customer’s U.S. Citizenship. • Providing a copy of a: o Letter, email, or a receipt for the requested document from the agency issuing the document. o Document request sent to the issuing agency or other appropriate entity. o Document along with documentation that an original or certified copy of the document requested. o Copy of a check, receipt, or other documentation indicating that a CIT/ID document has been ordered. Staff must make a detailed JE which include dates to indicate how much time the individual will need to obtain the required documents and an appropriate follow up timeframe. Procedure: None Program Impacts: CalSAWS Job Aids: • Vital Statistics • Citizenship and Sponsorship – Add or Edit References: ACWDL 07-12, 08-03, 09-27, 09-65, 23-08 Clarification from DHCS SN 07-04, 07-04 Addendums A & B County policy Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by February 29, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Document Handling of Citizenship/Identity Verification Number Page 04.07.14 1 of 4 Revision Date: February 1, 2025 Background: Customers attesting to be United States ( U.S.) C itizens/Nationals must provide verification of their Citizenship and Identity (CIT/ID). A photocopy, fax, scanned or other copy of a document must be accepted to the same extent as an original, unless questionable. Purpose: To provide guidance on the verification requirement of CIT/ID for U.S. Citizens/Nationals, remove references to the California Welfare Information Network (CalWIN) system and incorporate references to the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS). Policy: A. General U.S. Citizens/Nationals may satisfy the requirement by: • M ailing the documents to the Document Processing Center (DPC). • S ubmitting documents to staff at any: o Family Resource Center (FRC). o Federal Qualified Health Centers (FQHC) or a Disproportionate Share Hospitals (DSH). B. Role of FQHCs and DSHs FQHC and DSH staff assisting a Medi-Cal customer with the initial application process or renewal, upon receipt of verifications of U.S. CIT/ID, are authorized to: • View and photocopy the documents. • Complete form DHCS 0005 Receipt of Citizenship or Identity Documents for each CIT/ID document they receive and view (if an original or certified copy of the document was provided). • Mail the original DHCS 0005(s) and copies of the CIT/ID document(s) to the DPC . The mailing address is: Health and Human Services Agency ERA/DPC P.O. Box 939043 San Diego, CA 92193-9043 FQHC/DSH staff have the option to hand deliver the documents, along with the application to any FRC. C. Reception Role Staff are authorized to view and copy CIT/ID documents and must accept the documents when customers submit them at a FRC. When an original or certified copy of a CIT/ID document is submitted by Medi-Cal customers (excluding those in the Breast and Cervical Cancer Treatment Program [ BCCTP]) at a FRC reception, staff are not required to complete the DHCS 0005 when all steps outlined below are taken: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Document Handling of Citizenship/Identity Verification Number Page 04.07.14 2 of 4 Step Action 1 Clear the customer information in CalSAWS. 2 Determine whether the document is an original or certified copy by the issuing agency. 3 Photocopy the original document. 4 Stamp the copy. The stamp must indicate that the document is a copy of an original or certified copy ( for example “PHOTOCOPIED FROM ORIGINAL”) and contain all the following information: • Date • Worker number (if applicable) • Staff name • FRC address and phone number 5 Scan the stamped copy into the Hyland Imaging System. 6 Provide the customer with the stamped copy as a receipt. 7 Return the original CIT/ID document(s) to the customer. Do not staple any receipts to the original document. Staff are required to complete and sign the DHCS 0005 when the CIT/ID documents are submitted by a BCCTP customer. Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 04.07.16 for details. D. Human Services Specialist (HSS) Role 1. Processing Documents Submitted Through FQHCs or DSHs When evidence of CIT/ID are viewed and form DHCS 0005 is completed by FHQC/DSH staff, the form along with copies of the evidence documents are transferred directly from FQHC/DSH staff to the FRC. Under no circumstances must staff accept an original DHCS 0005 from a customer. Upon receipt of documents: Step Action 1 Review each packet for completeness. Every document must be accompanied by a corresponding original DHCS 0005 form. 2 Complete the DHCS 0011 Proof of Acceptable Citizenship or Identity Documents if the original DHCS 0005 is complete and accurate, and the CIT/ID document received are acceptable evidence as specified in MPG 07.02.04. 3 Mail the original DHCS 0011 to the customer. 4 Upload the following to the Hyland Imaging System: • Original DHCS 0005 • Copy of DHCS 0011 • Copy of the evidence 5 If the original DHCS 0005 was not included in the packet or the DHCS 0005 is incomplete, follow up with the FQHC/DSH staff and apply the following: If the FQHC/DSH staff states that a copy of the DHCS 0005 or document is… then inform the FQHC/DSH staff that … on file, they may complete another DHCS 0005 form and forward it, along with a copy of the initial DHCS 0005 and document. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Document Handling of Citizenship/Identity Verification Number Page 04.07.14 3 of 4 not on file, the packet cannot be processed . FQHC/DSH staff have the option of contacting the customer to re -submit the required original CIT/ID documents or refer the customer to FRC staff. 2. Processing Documents Submitted at FRC Reception Upon receipt of the CIT/ID documents forwarded from reception: Step Action 1 Review the CIT/ID document to confirm if it is acceptable evidence as specified in MPG 07.02.04. If the CIT/ID document received is… then… acceptable, complete form DHCS 0011 and go to Step 3. not acceptable, contact the customer and request the required original CIT/ID documents. 2 Mail the original DHCS 0011 to the customer. 3 Upload the following to the Hyland Imaging System: • Copy of DHCS 0011 • Copy of the evidence • Original DHCS 0005 (if made available) 3. Processing Documents Submitted to an HSS When evidence of CIT/ID are submitted directly to the HSS (either in person or by mail): Step Action 1 Review the CIT/ID document received to confirm it is acceptable evidence of CIT/ID. 2 Complete and issue form DHCS 0011. 3 Return the original(s) to the customer (within two business days if received by mail). 4 Provide the original DHCS 0011 to the customer. 5 Image a copy of the DHCS 0011 and stamped CIT/ID. 6 Document the date and means by which the original document was returned (for example, Certificate of Naturalization returned to John Doe by mail on 1/1/06) in a Journal entry. Note: Do not complete a DHCS 0005 if all the steps above were taken. Procedure: None Program Impacts: None County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Document Handling of Citizenship/Identity Verification Number Page 04.07.14 4 of 4 References: ACWDL 07-12, 08-03, 08-26, 08-29, 08-54, 23-08 Clarification from DHCS SN 07-04, 07-04 Addendum A & B County Policy 42CFR435.406(f) Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by February 29, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Processing Changes to Medi-Cal Contact Information Number Page 04.07.15 1 of 2 Revision Date: 04/01/2021 Background: The Medi-Cal Contact Information Form is no t required for Managed Care Health Plans (MCHPs) to inform the County of changes in a beneficiary’s contact information (address, telephone number, etc.). Purpose: This section is updated for the sunset review; no other changes have been made. Policy: 04.07.15A MCHPs can inform the County of changes by phone, fax, or email. The information provided to the County must be sufficient to identify the beneficiary’s case record; including name, identification number, date of birth and former name (when a name change is being reported) and former phone number (when a phone number change is being reported) before changes are made. No changes are made if the information provided to the County is insufficient to identify the case record. Procedure: 04.07.15B MCHPs will contact the County to inform them of the updates and whether the beneficiary has approved providing the updated information to the County. If the provision to update the County ... Then … Has been approved by the beneficiary, Immediately input the information into the case record, and no verification or beneficiary contact is required. Has not been approved by the beneficiary, Verify the new information before making changes by: 1. Looking for the same changes made to other county cases for the same beneficiary or their immediate family members including, CalWORKs, and CalFresh cases that are currently open or have closed within the last 90 days. 2. If unable to verify the changes made to any of the case records, then attempt to contact the beneficiary to verify the updated information using the beneficiary’s preferred method of contact. 3. If no confirmation/verification is received, make no changes. Note: Document in the case comments that the updates were provided by an MCHP. References: ACWDL 15-30 Sunset Date: This letter will be reviewed for continuance by 04/30/2024. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Processing Changes to Medi-Cal Contact Information Number Page 04.07.15 2 of 2 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Processing Verification of Citizenship/Identity for Breast and Cervical Cancer Treatment Program (BCCTP) Number Page 04.07.16 1 of 3 Revision Date: February 1, 2025 Background: The Breast and Cervical Cancer Treatment Program (BCCTP) provides full scope, zero SOC Medi-Cal benefits to uninsured women and men under age sixty -five (65) who are screened through an authorized provider and found in need of treatment for breast and/or cervical cancer, including some precancerous conditions. With the implementation of Adult Expansion, effective January 1, 2024, individuals who are otherwise eligible to Medi -Cal will receive full scope benefits regardless of immigration status for state-funded Medi-Cal programs. The BCCTP is administered by the California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS). Purpose: This section describes the responsibilities that the Sacramento BCCTP unit has in the Deficit Reduction Act (DRA) process. Additionally, it describes the county’s responsibilities upon receiving an original or certified copy of a United States (U.S.) Citizenship or Identity (CIT/ID) document for a BCCTP customer. This section has been updated to remove reference to restricted scope benefits under State- funded BCCTP. Policy: A. General In compliance with the Federal DRA of 2005, individuals attesting to be U.S. Citizens/Nationals applying for benefits under the BCCTP must provide original proof or certified copy of CIT/ID documents upon request. The se requirements do not apply to individuals whose benefits are established through BCCTP accelerated enrollment. However, evidence of CIT/ID must be provided to determine on-going Medi-Cal eligibility or at time of annual renewal. A BCCTP customer may satisfy the requirement by mailing the documents to the Sacramento BCCTP office or by having the original /certified copies inspected by the Sacramento BCCTP unit, a Family Resource Center (FRC), Federal Qualified Health Centers (FQHC), or Disproportionate Share Hospital (DSH). B. Sacramento BCCTP Unit Role The Sacramento BCCTP unit serves as a point of contact for all DRA and program related questions for BCCTP customers and will: • Inform BCCTP customer s of the CIT/ID requirements under DRA and consequences for noncompliance. • Instruct customers to present a copy of the letter concerning the DRA requirements to the County. • Receive copies of the DHCS 0005 Receipt of Citizenship or Identity Documents and the BCCTP customer’s documentation from the counties, FQHCs or DSHs. • Verify that the documentation is on the list of acceptable DRA documents. • Issue form DHCS 0011 Proof of Acceptable Citizenship or Identity D ocuments to the BCCTP customer once verified. • Perform all Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS) transactions to indicate that documentation for CIT/ID has been verified. • Determine if the BCCTP customer is: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Processing Verification of Citizenship/Identity for Breast and Cervical Cancer Treatment Program (BCCTP) Number Page 04.07.16 2 of 3 o E xempt from or has met the CIT/ID requirements via California Birth Record Data Match. o M aking a good faith effort to provide documentation. C. County Responsibilities BCCTP customers have the option to submit originals or certified copies of their CIT/ID documents to any FRC, regardless of their county of residence. The county i s responsible for reviewing the CIT/ID documents to determine that they are originals or copies certified by the issuing agency and forwarding copies of the documents to the Sacramento BCCTP unit. The county will not determine whether documents submitted are on the list of acceptable DRA documents. Take the following actions: Step Action 1 Determine if the individual is a BCCTP customer as follows: If the individual… then… states that they are participating in the BCCTP, proceed to Step 2. Presents a copy of the BCCTP DRA notification letter, proceed to Step 2. does not indicate that they are a BCCTP participant, clear MEDS and proceed to Step 2 if the customer is active with BCCTP aid code of 0N, 0P, or 0V. 2 Review the document and determine if it is an original or a copy certified by the issuing agency. 3 Make a photocopy of the original or certified CIT/ID document. 4 Complete and sign the DHCS 0005 form for each CIT/ID documents provided by the BCCTP customer/Authorized Representative (AR). 5 Return the original documents to the individual. 6 Provide the individual with a copy of the completed and signed DHCS 0005 form. 7 Mail or fax copies of the documents and DHCS 0005 form(s) to the BCCTP unit. Fax Transmissions: Department of Health Care Services ATTN: Breast and Cervical Cancer Treatment Program-DRA Fax number: (916) 552-9440 United States Mail: Department of Health Care Services Breast and Cervical Cancer Treatment Program – DRA MS 4611 P.O. Box 997417 Sacramento, CA 95899-7417 If faxing, a phone call must be made to (800) 824- 0088 to notify staff prior to faxing to comply with Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA). 8 File copies of the documents viewed and the signed DHCS 0005(s) in the Family Resource Center (FRC) designated centralized location. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Processing Verification of Citizenship/Identity for Breast and Cervical Cancer Treatment Program (BCCTP) Number Page 04.07.16 3 of 3 Additionally, if the BCCTP customer has questions regarding the BCCTP process, including any that are related to the DRA requirements, refer them to the Eligibility Specialist (ES) identified on the BCCTP DRA Notice or the BCCTP toll-free number at (800) 824-0088. Procedure: None Program Impacts: None References: ACWDL 08-25, 23-08 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by February 29, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification Requirements Number Page 04.07.01 1 of 3 Revision Date: February 1, 2025 Background: Customers are responsible for providing the documents necessary to determine eligibility for the Medi- Cal program. Purpose: This section has been revised to incorporate changes regarding the elimination of the asset test to establish Medi-Cal eligibility on initial applications and ongoing cases effective January 1, 2024. Policy: As part of the application/renewal process, staff must explain verification requirements to the customer, evaluate the customer’s ability to obtain verification and assist in obtaining the verification whenever necessary. For applications received prior to implementation, continue to follow policies and procedures regarding property verification requirements. A. Verification Required Before Approval Certain information provided by the customer on the Statement of Facts (SOF) must be verified prior to approving the application. Information which must be verified prior to approval includes: • Income. • Income deductions (only required to allow the deductions). • Real and personal property (for Non-Modified Adjusted Gross Income [MAGI] Medi-Cal applications dated prior to January 1, 2024). • Age (refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide [MPG] 04.07.01C for more information). • Blindness/disability (Non-MAGI only). • Legal responsibility for a child (if child is applying alone, except for Minor Consent). • Substantial Gainful Activity (SGA) (Non-MAGI only). Verification requirements for application of Unconditionally Available Income ( UAI) and United States (U.S.) Citizenship/Satisfactory Immigration Status (SIS) can be met after approval of the application. Refer to MPG 04.12.01 and 04.07.13 for more information. B. Verification Required within 60 Days Eligibility may be established prior to recei ving the following information, if all other eligibility requirements have been met, provided that approval occurs within 60 days from the date of application: • Social Security Number (SSN) or application for a SSN. • Medicare entitlement. The following individuals are exempt from the SSN requirement: • Deemed Eligible infants. • Customers requesting Minor Consent services. • Refugees applying for Refugee Medical Assistance/Entrant Medical Assistance (RMA/EMA). • Customers who do not claim U.S. Citizenship or SIS and do not have work authorization. Refer to MPG 04.11 for detailed information on SSN requirements. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Verification Requirements Number Page 04.07.01 2 of 3 C. Self-Attestation Self-attestation is when the individual states that something is true and correct. Unless questionable, self-attestation is acceptable for: • Age. • Date of birth. • Family size. • Residency. • Pregnancy. D. Electronic Verifications (e-verified) for Use in Non-MAGI Determinations When the verifications below are e-verified, they may be used to determine Non-MAGI eligibility: • Citizenship. • Identity. • Immigration status. • SSN. • Medicare. • Incarceration. • Deceased. • Disability. Note: For clarification on whether an application must be run through the California Healthcare, Eligibility, Enrollment, and Retention System (CalHEERS) Business Rules Engine (BRE), refer to MPG 04.02.22. E. Telephone/Electronic Signature Accept telephonically recorded and electronic signatures as well as handwritten signatures transmitted via fax or email for any form that must be signed for the Medi -Cal program. Please refer to Self- Sufficiency Services Processing Guide – Telephonic/ Electronic Signatures for methods of accepting telephonic/electronic signatures. A sworn statement may be signed telephonically under penalty of perjury if a customer must provide a sworn statement for purposes of written verification, electronic verification was not successful , and other methods of paper verif
