title: Section 08 - Residency Requirements
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide California Residency and Customer Address Number Page 04.08.01 1 of 4 Revision Date: August 1, 2026 Background: A customer must reside in the state of California to be eligible for Medi-Cal. They must maintain up to date contact information to ensure they receive important information about their benefits and eligibility. Customers are required to report changes to their address information within ten days of the change. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to define residency requirements, explain how a customer may establish residency in California, and specify required actions when a customer uses a Post Office (P.O.) Box or a Commercial Mail Receiving Agency (CMRA) address . This section includes new guidance on updating customers’ addresses based on information received from reliable third- party sources. This section was reformatted and renumbered. Policy: A. Establishing California Residency California residency is a condition of eligibility for Medi -Cal and must be verified at initial application. Once California residency is established, it continues until residency is established in another state or country as defined by Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 04.08.03. If staff become aware of information that contradicts the customer’s claim of California residency, verification must be requested. If the information provided does not resolve the discrepancy, a fraud referral will be initiated. If a determination is made that the customer is not a resident of the state, staff must clearly narrate all facts in the journal entry. B. Use of P.O Box, CMRA or Alternate Address to Establish California Residency Although customers must meet residency requirements, they are not required to have a fixed address. A P.O. Box or CMRA address can be used as a mailing address, but it does not satisfy the residency requirement. C. Job Commitment or Seeking Employment California residency may be established during the period of employment or while seeking employment even if they plan to return to a residence in another state when they reside in California. A person who commutes to California for employment while living in another state or country is not considered a resident of California. D. Households with Separate Residences Household members may establish separate residences with no break in marital or familial ties. In these situations, only household members who meet the California residency requirements are eligible for Medi-Cal. E. Children Living with Their Parents Children living with their parents will have their residency determined as that of their parents. Parents who do not meet the California residency requirements may establish California residency for their children if both of the following conditions are met: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide California Residency and Customer Address Number Page 04.08.01 2 of 4 • The parents: o Intend for their children to remain in California on a permanent basis. o Have arranged for the children to remain in California independent of the parents. F. Unusual Circumstances California residency may be established when a customer: • Is on parole from a correctional facility or other institution. • Is living within the boundaries of California on land owned or leased by the Federal Government. • Receives Public Assistance from another state or county if the issuing agency knows that the customer is a resident of California and sen ds the benefits directly to a California address in the customer’s name. G. Acceptable Address Sources for Medi-Cal Only Cases To ensure that eligible customers do not lose coverage when their address changes, staff must act on updated in-state address information from the following reliable third-party sources: • Mail returned to the county by the United States Postal Service (USPS) with an in-state forwarding address. • The USPS National Change of Address (NCOA) database, and • Updated member address information received by a Medi-Cal Managed Care Plan (MCP), provided that the information was directly from or verified with the member to the MCP. If… then… the county receives an updated in-state address for the primary applicant from a reliable thirdparty source, staff must update the mailing and physical address in the case record for all household members who share the same mailing and physical address as the primary applicant. a household member, such as an adult child or spouse, has a different address on record, their address will not be updated unless the county has been informed that they now reside at the same address. the county receives an updated in-state address from a reliable third- party source for someone other than the primary applicant, and the update does not indicate if it applies to the entire household, staff must follow the process outlined in Medi- Cal Processing Guide 46 Address Discrepancies and Loss of Contact . If the customer does not respond, the address cannot be updated. The case record must retain the last known address confirmed by the customer. In cases where customers have separate mailing and physical addresses or a P.O. Box, the address may be updated as follows: If… then… the physical and mailing address in the case record are different at the time the in- state address update is received, staff must only update the mailing address. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide California Residency and Customer Address Number Page 04.08.01 3 of 4 the mailing address is a P.O. Box, and the physical address is different in the case record at the time the in -state address update is received, staff must not update either address. Follow the good faith effort processes outlined in Medi-Cal Processing Guide 46 Address Discrepancies and Loss of Contact. the updated address indicates a P.O. Box as the forwarding address, staff must not treat the P.O. Box as an in -state forwarding address. The addresses must not be updated. Staff must follow the good faith effort processes outlined in Medi -Cal Processing Guide 46 Address Discrepancies and Loss of Contact. Note: When the updated address is outside of the county, staff must complete an intercounty transfer (ICT) if no other eligibility information is needed. Refer to MPG 03.02 for guidance on ICTs. There should be no interruption in benefits during this process. For cases where more than one program is activ e, staff must follow the program hierarchy before updating the case. Refer to CalWORKs Program Guide (CPG) 42-400.A and CalFresh Program Guide (CFPG) 63-152 for guidance. H. Vulnerable or Sensitive Cases: Staff must not update the address for families with a domestic violence flag in the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) until they can confirm the address change through the Address Discrepancies procedures outlined in Medi-Cal Processing Guide 46. If the household does not report the change voluntarily, staff must verify it a t the next renewal. Eligibility shall not be discontinued for not reporting an address change. If staff are unable to confirm the new address, the address on the case record must remain as the last known address confirmed by the customer. Staff must not update the address for customers who are incarcerated or for cases in which a household member is incarcerated. Staff must confirm the newly updated address using the process outlined in the Ex Parte Unsuccessful in Medi-Cal Processing Guide 46. I. Address Updates for the Safe at Home (SAH) Program Staff may only change the address for customers in the SAH program when the customer provides and confirms the new address directly and indicates their participation in the SAH program has been terminated. Procedures: Refer to Medi-Cal Processing Guide 46 Address Discrepancies and Loss of Contact. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Students Number Page 04.08.02 1 of 2 Revision Date: August 1, 2026 Background: Customers residing in California for purposes of attending school may meet Medi -Cal residenc y requirements. Similarly, customers may remain Medi-Cal eligible if they leave California temporarily to attend school in another state. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide guidance when determining California residency for customers who are living in California to attend school and those who attend school out-of-state. This section was reformatted and renumbered. Policy: A. Students Who Come to California to Attend School Students from another state or country who are residing in California while attending school may qualify for Medi-Cal if they are a resident of California. Students who commute into California to attend school from another state or country do not meet the California residency requirement. If a student applies for Medi -Cal and is receiving Medicaid in another state, their benefits must be discontinued as soon as administratively possible. An eligible student cannot receive Medicaid coverage in more than one state at the same time. All other Medi -Cal eligibility rules and requirements apply in cases with customers who come to California to attend school. B. Students Attending School in Another State Students who leave California to attend school temporarily in another state must report their temporary leave to the county. Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS) must continue to reflect the California address to which they plan to return. Temporary absence from California does not have a specific timeframe requirement, however a 60- day absence may lead to a presumption that the customer is no longer a California resident. Absences over 60 days may require additional follow-up. Students attending school in another state can choose to discontinue benefits in California and apply for Medicaid in the state where they are attending school. If this occurs, Medi-Cal must be discontinued as soon as administratively possible. C. Impact to Parent/Caretaker Relatives of Out-of-State Students Students who move out -of-state to attend school have no impact on the family Medi -Cal case if the student is still claimed as a tax dependent by their parent (s). Students who are claimed as tax dependents must provide the applicable tax household and income information when they apply for Medi-Cal. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Students Number Page 04.08.02 2 of 2 When a student who temporarily moves out of state is the only child on the case, their parent(s) will maintain their parent/caretaker linkage if the student meets the requirements to be considered a dependent child. These requirements are: • The child meets the age requirements. • The parent(s) remain the primary caregiver(s) and is/are financially responsible for the child. • The child is still considered to be residing with their parents. D. Out-of-State Coverage Medi-Cal covers emergency services for customers who are temporarily absent from the state. When emergency services are received out -of-state, the provider must agree to accept Medi -Cal and must meet the requirements for becoming a Medi -Cal provider. Emergency services are provided in the United States. Only emergency services requiring hospitalization are provided in Canada and Mexico. Procedures: None Program Impacts: None References: ACWDL 15-23 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by July 31, 2029. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Temporary Absence and Loss of California Residency Number Page 04.08.03 1 of 2 Revision Date: August 1, 2026 Background: Individuals may be temporarily absent from the state of California without affecting their residency status depending on the duration of the absence. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide guidance on the treatment of temporary absences and loss of California residency. This section was reformatted and renumbered. Policy: A. Absence for 60 Days or Less Customers who are temporarily absent from the state of California for a period of 60 days or less will not have their residenc y status affected. Staff will p resume an absence of 60 days or less to be a temporary absence unless there is evidence to the contrary. Staff must a ccept applications or redeterminations from customers who are temporarily absent from the state for 60 days or less. B. Absence for More than 60 Days When a customer is absent from the state for more than 60 days, staff will presume they intend to establish residency outside of California, unless they provide a written statement which states both: • An intent to return to California. • The existence of one of the following circumstances: o Illness or emergency which prohibits the customer’s return to California. o The customer lives with family members who are California residents and are physically present in the state. o The customer maintains California housing arrangements. When a customer is absent from the state for more than 60 days, staff must request verification of residency. C. Loss of California Residency A customer is considered to have loss of California residenc y when they leave the state and take any of the following actions in another state: • Purchases, leases, or rents a residence. • Becomes employed. • Obtains an out-of-state driver’s license. • Applies for aid in another state. The loss of residenc y will be considered verified unless there is evidence to the contrary. When a customer loses residency, Medi-Cal benefits will be discontinued effective the last day of the month in which residency was terminated or the last day of the following month, whichever allows for sufficient 10-day notice. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Temporary Absence and Loss of California Residency Number Page 04.08.03 2 of 2 D. Death During Absence from the State A customer who dies during an absence from the state will be considered a resident of California if there is evidence that they met the residency requirements at the time of death. Procedures: None Program Impacts: None References: ACWDL 93-29, 95-47, 26-04 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by July 31, 2029. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Loss of Customer Contact Number Page 04.08.04 1 of 3 Revision Date: August 1, 2026 Background: Medi-Cal may be denied or discontinued for loss of contact only after reasonable attempts are made to contact the customer. Staff must confirm contact information any time they speak with a customer by phone or in person. This includes confirming the physical and mailing address and any phone number or email contact information previously provided. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide guidance on the process when a Medi-Cal customer’s mail is returned as undeliverable. This section was reformatted and renumbered. Policy: Upon receipt of returned mail or any indication that a customer has moved without reporting a change of address, staff must make reasonable attempts to contact the customer. A. Phone Contact Requirements When mail is received as undeliverable, staff must make at least two attempts to contact the customer by phone. If contact is made, staff must: • Confirm the customer’s address. • Update the case address if necessary. • Document the contact in a journal entry. If unable to reach the customer on the first attempt or there is no phone number on file , staff must complete a detailed journal entry. Returned Mail Information When mail is returned, staff must ensure that it was sent to the intended address by reviewing the completeness and accuracy of the address on the returned mail and comparing it to the information on the customer’s case record. If there are no errors or missing information, staff must attempt to contact the customer via two methods (ex. phone and mail). Complete a detailed journal entry. If the original mail contains errors or missing information (ex. incorrect zip code, missing apartment number) or was not sent using the most up to date contact information, staff must correct the information and resend the documents to the corrected address. A detailed journal entry must be completed. If mail is returned for any of the reasons below, staff must follow the procedures outlined in Processing Guide 46 - Address Discrepancies and Loss of Contact: • An in-state address is received from a data source not identified as reliable. • Conflicting addresses are received. • An out-of-state address is received. • Whereabouts are unclear due to undeliverable mail and no forwarding address is provided by the United States Postal Service (USPS). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Loss of Customer Contact Number Page 04.08.04 2 of 3 Imaging Returned Mail The contents or envelopes of undeliverable mail do not need to be imaged if the information is already stored in the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS). When mail is returned to the office as undeliverable, document the following in a detailed journal entry: • Type of mail (NOA, form, letter, etc.,). • Address the mail was sent to. • Date the mail was sent. • Date the mail was returned. • Safe at Home (SAH) status if applicable, along with confirmation that the customer is utilizing the confidential post office (P.O.) Box. 90-Day Cure Period Customers have 90 days from the date of discontinuance to have their Medi-Cal eligibility reestablished if their whereabouts become known and they remain in-state. Rescind eligibility back to the date of the discontinuance without requesting additional inf ormation to verify eligibility, unless there is other information that indicates that the customer may not meet all eligibility requirements. Exempt From Discontinuance Loss of contact is not a basis for discontinuing Medi-Cal benefits for the following programs: • Former Foster Youth (FFY). • Children eligible for Continuous Eligibility for Children (CEC). • Deemed Eligible Infants (under 1 year). • Medi-Cal Access Program (MCAP). • Pregnant beneficiaries. • Beneficiaries in their 12-month postpartum period. Procedures: Refer to Medi -Cal Processing Guide 46 for procedures on reviewing cases when an address discrepancy exists or there is a loss of customer contact. Program Impacts: CalFresh cases should not be discontinued for Whereabouts Unknown. When discontinuing Medi -Cal for one of the undeliverable mail situations above, ensure the action taken in CalSAWS does not affect the CalFresh benefits. References: MEDIL I23-11E ACWDL 25-06 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by July 31, 2029. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Loss of Customer Contact Number Page 04.08.04 3 of 3 Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: Section 09 - Diligent Search
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Diligent Search Number Page 04.09.01 1 of 5 Revision Date: October 1, 2026 Background: Customers may need assistance in providing information necessary for an eligibility determination due to amnesia, being in a comatose condition, or any other condition that impedes them from acting on their own behalf when no qualified representative is available. Purpose: This section provides guidance for processing an application through a diligent search process. The section has been updated for sunset review and to include examples of qualified representatives. Policy: Eligibility staff must complete the diligent search process regardless of whether the customer’s identity is known. Diligent search involves the process of searching for a customer’s identity, available income, and available resources when the customer is unable to assist in the application process and there is no qualified representative to complete the Statement of Facts (SOF) or act on their behalf. Examples of qualified representatives in rank order are: • S pouses. • G uardians. • C onservators. • E xecutors. • I ndividuals with legal authority such as Power of Attorney. • R elatives or persons with sufficient knowledge of the applicant’s circumstances. • R epresentatives of a public agency or county department. Action cannot be taken on an application until ineligibility has been determined or a diligent search and a referral to the State Programs-Disability Determination Services Division (SP-DDSD), if appropriate, have been completed. Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 05.04 DDSD Referrals for additional guidance. A. Diligent Search Overview Eligibility staff must take the following actions in the diligent search process: • Determine and document the customer’s competence. • Refer customers between the ages of 21 and 64 to the SP-DDSD for a disability determination. • Conduct a reasonable search of all available information. • Determine eligibility based on diligent search findings. • Refer customers to the public guardian or conservator’s office, if appropriate. B. Determining and Documenting a Customer’s Competency Before completing a diligent search, eligibility staff must determine the customer’s competency to confirm if they are capable of handling their own affairs. Eligibility staff will assess the c ustomer’s competence based on their ability to adequately respond to routine questions asked as part of the eligibility determination process. This assessment is not considered a legal or medical determination. Refer to MPG 04.02.05B Competency for steps to take when conducting a competency determination. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Diligent Search Number Page 04.09.01 2 of 5 Some examples of cases that require a diligent search process involve customers who are deceased, comatose or have amnesia. The determination of incompetence must be documented in the journal entry. C. Referral for a Disability Determination Individuals with a condition that impedes them from acting on their own behalf must be referred to the SP-DDSD unless they appear to be under the age of 21 or over the age of 64. The eligibility staff making the referral must sign the Authorization for Release of Information (MC 220) and write "person is comatose" or "person is deceased" as applicable on the face of the form. A Disability Determination and Transmittal (MC 221) and Applicant's Supplemental Statement of Facts for Medi -Cal (MC 223) must be completed with all available information. D. Diligent Search – Identity When a hospital staff member has attempted and is unable to establish the identity of a customer who is comatose, amnesiac, or lacks mental competency , eligibility staff must document all reasonable attempts in a journal entry. If the customer is deceased and law enforcement officials are involved, information on identity must be requested from the appropriate agency. E. Diligent Search – Income and Property For customers whose identity is known, conduct a diligent search by reviewing the following: • Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS) search by Social Security Number (SSN) or, if unavailable, by name and county. • The Income and Eligibility Verification System (IEVS) abstract to: o Verify Social Security benefits or by calling 1-800-772-1213. o Verify wages, Unemployment Insurance/Disability Insurance (UI/DI) information. o Identify the existence of any interest-bearing accounts. • Verification of Veteran's Administration (VA) benefits via the Military Verification and Referral ( MC 05). • Bank statements that show an automatic deposit with the source of the income identified. • The Asset Verification Program (AVP) for customers who appear to be over the age of 65. • Additional third-party contacts (must be fully documented in the journal entry). • Verification of vehicle registration through a written request to the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV). • Property search via the County Assessor's Office website or by calling the County Assessor's Office to determine if the customer has any real property in San Diego County. • If the customer’s personal effects indicate a specific bank account, staff must use the Release of Information-Financial Institution (CW 60) to request information for all accounts belonging to the customer. If the banking institution confirms that the customer owns stocks, bonds, or mutual funds, staff must contact a recognized stock exchange broker to determine their current sales value or establish the current selling price through current listings. • If information contained in the personal effects, such as a passbook or check register, provides an account balance, staff may use this information in determining eligibility. • If the bank refuses to provide the requested information, the effort must be documented in a journal entry. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Diligent Search Number Page 04.09.01 3 of 5 When requesting any of the above information, staff must include a cover letter indicating that the customer is comatose or deceased and cannot sign a release of information form. Also include that there is no person authorized to act on behalf of the customer and the County is trying to establish the individual’s Medi-Cal eligibility. F. Determine Eligibility Based on Findings An eligibility determination based on the results of a diligent search will be completed the same way as any other determination. • R esidency requirements are considered to be met in the absence of information to the contrary. • Only the income and resources discovered through diligent search will be considered available. • If the customer is the only person who has access to the income or resources, these accounts are considered unavailable until staff is notified otherwise. • Restricted/limited scope benefits must be granted if unable to obtain acceptable citizenship/identity documents to verify Satisfactory Immigration Status (SIS) or United States (U.S) citizenship status at the end of the diligent search process. Upon completion of the Medi -Cal eligibility determination, the Supervising Human Services Specialist (SHSS) must approve the eligibility staff’s determination by countersigning the SOF. G. Referral to Public Guardian or Conservator Customers who are unable to act on their own behalf and have no qualified representative must be referred to the Public Guardian or C onservator’s Office. If the public guardian’s office accepts responsibility, eligiblity will be determined based on the information provided by that office. If the Public Guardian’s office does not respond or accept responsibility, staff must document the attempt in a journal entry and proceed with the diligent search process. Referrals must be submitted on the Health and Human Services Agency ( HHSA) Public Guardian website: • https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/hhsa/programs/ais/Services/Public-Guardian.html When a customer is deceased, a referral must be submitted to the HHSA Public Administrator: • https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/hhsa/programs/ais/Services/Public- Administrator.html Note: Staff must not delay referrals to the Public Guardian or C onservator’s Office even if the customer’s medical records, financial information, and other evidence of the customer 's inability to manage their affairs are unavailable. H. Acting on Changes Diligent search efforts will end if at any time during the application to determine eligibility the customer’s condition changes or a friend/relative is found and the information can be obtained in the usual manner. The case record must be updated to reflect the customer’s verified identity and eligibility status. Any previously disregarded income and property must be reviewed for availability. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Diligent Search Number Page 04.09.01 4 of 5 If the customer … then … remains eligible and a Medi -Cal Client Index Number (CIN) has been assigned, retain the CIN and update the aid code if there is a change in eligibility status. is found to be ineligible, deny or discontinue the case with timely and adequate notice. Note: If the friend /relative is unable to supply the information or is non- cooperative, then they do not meet the qualified representative criteria, and the diligent search effort must continue. Refer to MPG 04.02.05 Persons Who May Complete and Sign the Statement of Facts (SOF) for additional information. Automation: Processing Diligent Search Cases The following information must be entered in the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) for diligent search cases: • Name - John C. Doe or Jane C. Doe for those whose name is unknown. • Aid Code - When the customer’s age is unknown, use the following aid codes: If the customer’s age appears to be … then use aid code … Under 21, 82 Over 21-64, 38 Over 21 -64 and in an Intermediate Care Facility/Skilled Nursing Facility (ICF/SNF). 53 65 or over 14, 17 or 13 when in ICF/SNF • Birth Date - When the customer’s age is unknown, use “01” for the month, “01” for the day, and the following for the year of birth: If the estimated age is … then use the current year minus… Under 21, 10 years. Between 21 and 64, 40 years. 65 or over, 70 years. • SSN – Must be left blank if unknown. MEDS will assign a pseudo number. • Medicare Beneficiary Identifier (MBI) Number - Must be left blank if unknown. • Address – The Family Resource Center (FRC) Post Office (P.O) Box processing the case must be used. Program Impacts: None References: All County Welfare Directors Letters (ACWDLs) 94-62, 02-28, 11-11, 12-17 Medi-Cal Eligibility Procedures Manual (MEPM) 4I, 22C, 22C-1, 22C-7 Medi-Cal Eligibility Division Information (MEDILs) 20-33, 20-33E, 26-04 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by September 30, 2029. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Diligent Search Number Page 04.09.01 5 of 5 Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services

Diligent Search – Identity When a hospital staff member has attempted and is unable to establish the identity of a customer who is comatose, amnesiac, or lacks mental competency , eligibility staff must document all reasonable attempts in a journal entry. If the customer is deceased and law enforcement officials are involved, information on identity must be requested

title: Section 10 - Child Health and Disability Prevention Program
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageChild Health and Disability Prevention (CHDP) Program 4.10.1 1 of 2 Revision Date: January 1, 2020 Background: The Child Health and Disability Prevention (CHDP) program is a State program of health screening for children in California which incorporates the federally mandated Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnosis, and Treatment (EPSDT) program. CHDP is available to all Medi-Cal beneficiaries under the age of 21. This section provides an explanation of the purpose and provisions of CHDP. This section is updated to the current format and updates procedures. Purpose: The purpose of screening is the earliest possible detection, correction, and prevention of problems in health and development, which are potentially handicapping or could lead to more serious medical problems. Policy: A. Provisions: Health screening is a series of evaluations by physicians or paramedical staff, such as pediatric nurses or nurse practitioners, supervised by a physician. The screening evaluation includes health and development history, physical examinations, developmental assessment, vision and hearing tests, dental inspection, lab tests appropriate for age and population groups, immunizations, nutritional assessment, and other tests as needed. Also, children 3 years of age and older can be referred to a dentist for a yearly checkup, preventive dental care, and needed treatment. Under EPSDT, the above tests are done at periodic intervals according to the age of the child. The screener must explain the results of the screening to the parent/caretaker of the child and make a referral for diagnosis and treatment to the appropriate source of medical care when necessary. B. Availability: Lists of CHDP providers of medical and dental screenings by geographical area are available to each FRC and on the internet. The lists include physicians and dentists who provide CHDP services as well as the local health department. Contracted Health Care Plan (HCP) providers must provide CHDP services to all eligible children who are enrolled in the HCP. Procedure: See above. Program Impacts: None. References: ACWDL 81-30 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by December 31, 2022. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageChild Health and Disability Prevention (CHDP) Program 4.10.1 2 of 2 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageWorker Responsibilities 4.10.2 1 of 2 Revision Date: January 1, 2020 Background: State rules require that all Medi-Cal applicants who are under 21 years of age or are responsible for children under 21 years of age and all eligible pregnant women be informed of CHDP services. Workers must: •Inform all eligible Medi-Cal applicants/beneficiaries of CHDP services •Make referrals to CHDP •Document the informing/referral procedures Purpose: This section is updated to the current format and updates procedures. Policy: A. Application: The DHS PHE-265-CHDP must be included in the Supplemental Application Packet when the application includes children under the age of 21. B. Intake: Ensure that the applicant has been informed of CHDP benefits and make referrals to CHDP for all eligible people who request CHDP services. C. Intake Referrals: Enter a ‘Y’ or ‘N’ in the mandatory fields on the Collect CHDP/Social Services Request window, CHDP tab. Enter a ‘Y’ in one of the following fields to make a referral for CHDP services: •Regular checkups and Dental Services through CHDP •Medical Services only through CHDP •Dental Services only through CHDP •Assistance with Doctor’s Appointment for Checkup or Assistance with Transportation D. Documentation: The entries above document that the CHDP information was provided to the applicant/beneficiary. E. Continuing: The CHDP informational brochure is included in all Medi-Cal and CalWORKs redetermination packets. Follow the actions in Procedure, below. Procedure: Step Action 1 Explain the information contained in the brochure as part of the redetermination process. 2 Complete the CHDP/Social Services Request window, CHDP tab, to document that the beneficiary received the required information and was either referred to or rejected CHDP services. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageWorker Responsibilities 4.10.2 2 of 2 Program Impacts: None. References: ACWDL 81-30 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by December 31, 2022. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations

title: Section 11 - Social Security Number Requirements
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageSocial Security Number (SSN) Requirement Introduction 4.11.1 1 of 2 Revision Date: June 1, 2020 Background: Every person requesting Medi-Cal who has a Social Security Number (SSN) at the time of application is asked to provide it regardless of immigration status. The applicant can indicate if they have a SSN in Section D on the MC 13. Purpose: 04.11.01A This section establishes procedures for the following: •Situations where the customer is unable to provide or does not have a SSN •SSN validation process •SSN validation error resolution procedures 1.Policy: 04.11.01B As a condition of eligibility for full-scope Medi-Cal benefits, each customer must either provide acceptable verification of SSN or cooperate in obtaining a SSN. The following customers are exempt from this requirement: •Infants under the Deemed Eligibility program •Refugees under Refugee Medical Assistance/Entrant Medical Assistance (RMA/EMA) program 2.Procedure: 04.11.01C SSN Verification Verification must be received within 60 days of the date of application but not necessarily prior to the approval of eligibility. NOTE: Human Services Specialists (HSS) must apply SB 87 regulations before requesting SSN verification from a customer and attempt to verify the SSN through the ex parte process outlined in MPG 4.7.12. Acceptable SSN verification includes: •Social Security card •SSA form series OA-702 •SSA award letter •SSN notification letters for IRCA aliens •Medicare card •SSA check showing the applicant’s name and SSN with the letters A, HA, J, T or M following the SSN •Income Eligibility Verification System (IEVS) applicant report with a code “A” or “W” in the SSN-VER field 04.11.01D Cooperation Verification Acceptable verifications of cooperation include: •Completed application for a Social Security card Form SS-5 •MC 194 referral form annotated by a SSA official indicating that a completed form has been submitted •Form SSA-2853 “MESSAGE FROM SOCIAL SECURITY” signed by an official of the hospital where the baby was born oNote: this form is not required for newborns qualified for Deemed Eligibility •Proof of their attempt to apply for the number when SSA has not accepted the SSN application because of lack of documentation as outlined in MPG 04.11.02E County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageSocial Security Number (SSN) Requirement Introduction 4.11.1 2 of 2 04.11.01E Restricted Benefits Non-citizens eligible only for restricted benefits are NOT required to provide a SSN as a condition of eligibility. The HSS will leave the SSN field blank in CalWIN. MEDS will issue a pseudo-SSN for the MEDS record. If a non-citizen … Then … eligible for restricted Medi-Cal claims to have a SSN but refuses to provide it, •grant eligibility if all other eligibility requirements are met •submit a referral to the State Medi-Cal investigator if there is reason to believe that they are withholding any information relevant to their Medi-Cal eligibility or SOC provides a SSN, use the SSN: •on form MC221 •to obtain an IEVS via 14-28 •for any other mandated purposes NOTE: Under no circumstances should a HSS knowingly submit an incorrect or fraudulent SSN to MEDS. Program Impacts: No Impact to other programs References: ACWDL 17-01 MEDIL 10-03 MPG Letter 750 (04/12) Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by May 31, 2023 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageReferral to Social Security Administration (SSA) 4.11.2 3 of 2 Revision Date: June 1, 2020 Background: This section describes the policies for referring customers to SSA for a Social Security number (SSN). Purpose: This section is re-written in the new format. Policies have been updated to remove references to Immigration Reform and Control Act (IRCA) aliens. Procedures are moved to Processing Guide 31. Policy: When to Refer to SSA: Refer customers to SSA in the following situations when the: •Customer cannot provide an acceptable SSN verification •Customer does not have a SSN •SSN is not validated by SSA and the case review and/or customer states the County information is correct •Customer’s date of birth does not match SSA files and the customer has proof of the correct date of birth. Who to Refer to SSA: The following people will be referred to SSA if they meet the criteria outlined above: •United States (U.S.) citizens •Immigrants that can provide SSA with one of the following documents: oAR 3 oAR 3a oI-94 oI-95 oI-151 oI-181a/b oI-184 oI-185 oI-186 oI-551 oI-688 oI-688A oSW434 Failure to Cooperate in Applying for and/or Providing the SSN: Examples of failure to cooperate include, but are not limited to, when the customer: •States that he/she will not provide the SSN if available or will not apply for SSN on his/her own behalf or a child’s •Refuses to provide information to SSA that is accessible to him/her •Fails to return the MC 194 after he/she was instructed to apply/reapply for the SSN County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageReferral to Social Security Administration (SSA) 4.11.2 4 of 2 •Fails to obtain and submit the documentation required by SSA within 30 days of the date that the original SSN application was submitted but not accepted by SSA for lack of documentation. See Processing Guide 31 when the client has refused to apply for or provide the SSN. Procedure: Referral Procedures: See Processing Guide 31 to refer the customer to SSA. Form MC 194 Not Accepted Due to Lack of Evidence: See Processing Guide 31 when SSA indicates on the MC 194 that the application for SSN was submitted but not accepted due to lack of evidence. Form MC 194 Accepted by SSA: See Processing Guide 31 when the customer returns the MC 194 indicating that the SSN application was accepted. Responses to Request for SSN: See Processing Guide 31 when the customer responds to the requests for the SSN indicating that he/she has not received the SSN. Program Impacts: None. References: Medi-Cal Eligibility Procedures Manual 4M(II)A Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by May 31, 2023 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageSocial Security Number Validations 4.11.3 1 of 3 Revision Date: June 1, 2020 Background: The Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) has initiated a process in which the Social Security numbers (SSNs) of Medi-Cal beneficiaries are matched against Social Security Administration’s (SSA) records. This process is called validation. The process has two parts, the validation process and the referral process. Process Function Validation A daily match of all invalidated SSNs currently on the Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS). Referral Ongoing matching of people referred to SSA for either a replacement SSN card or an initial application. Includes those people who could not be “validated” in the daily process. Note: The referral process will update MEDS on a daily basis. Purpose: This section is re-written in the new format. No policies or procedures are changed, though procedures are moved to Processing Guide 32. Policy: Validation Error Resolution: To resolve invalidated SSNs, compare the invalidated data with the case record to determine where the error is. To compare the invalidated data with the case record data to determine if errors were made in the information forwarded to the state, check for: •Incorrect SSN (for example, SSN belongs to another family member) •Transposition of a number in the SSN •Incorrect digit(s) in the SSN •Incorrect spelling of the first and/or last name •Use of maiden name instead of married name •Use of nickname or the use of two surnames for any of the children •Incorrect gender and/or date of birth If … Then … Errors are found in either the CalWIN or MEDS record, •Correct the information in CalWIN •Submit 14-28 to MEDS operator to have the MEDS record corrected. No errors are found in either the CalWIN or MEDS record, Contact the beneficiary to verify the information by: •Requesting to view SSN card •Questioning the beneficiary if he/she used another name when County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageSocial Security Number Validations 4.11.3 2 of 3 applying for a SSN •Requesting date of birth verification to compare with the month and year shown on the report. The SSA/DHCS data match compares SSN in the following method and order: 1. First six letters of the last name 2. First letter of first name 3. Gender 4. Year and month of birth If any of these fields do not match, SSA notifies DHCS of those SSNs that were not validated. Specific data element(s) that caused the mismatch are not identified. Continue to check data elements after discovering inaccuracies to prevent duplicate invalidated SSN reports. All corrections will be processed through MEDS and will be included in the next State Validation file submittal to SSA. If the … Then … Record returns as “validated,” The State files will be updated accordingly. Beneficiary indicates that the worker has the correct information, Refer the beneficiary to SSA as outlined below. Referral Error Resolution: See Processing Guide 32 to resolve invalidated SSNs or discrepancies in the SSN information. Second MC 194 Returned: SSA may respond with either of the following when they return Form MC 194 for a beneficiary that has been referred to SSA a second time: •SSA is revising its record to match the State record for each discrepant item •SSA is not revising its record for at least one item but may be revising other items. If SSA is revising their record, no action is necessary. See Processing Guide 32 if SSA is not revising its record. Procedure: See above. Program Impacts: None. References: Medi-Cal Eligibility Procedures Manual 4M(II)A Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by May 31, 2023 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageSocial Security Number Validations 4.11.3 3 of 3 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageMedi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS) Impact 4.11.4 1 of 2 Revision Date: June 1, 2020 Background: MEDS will receive information from all the validation processes. This information will be compared to the MEDS database and this exception message will be generated: SS30 – SSN citizenship and identity validation. Purpose: This section is re-written in the new format. No policies or procedures are changed, though procedures are moved to Processing Guide 33. Policy: Referral Processing: If the Social Security Administration (SSA) and MEDS information is not consistent enough to validate the Social Security Number (SSN) the following will occur: •An alert is added to the MEDS beneficiary record •MEDS Name Cross Reference File is also updated to include the name and birth date from the referral record. If the … Then the MEDS beneficiary record … Beneficiary information is consistent, Is updated to show that the SSN was validated. SSA and MEDS information is not consistent enough to validate the SSN, Has an alert added to show the error. Referral Alerts: Referral alerts are issued when: •Follow-up action is needed for MEDS •Information obtained from the referral may be useful to the worker. Referral alerts will appear in CalWIN as MEDS Exceptions. For a listing of these messages, see Desk Aid 107. Procedures: Validation Process: See Processing Guide 33 for the validation process. SSN Changes: See Processing Guide 33 for SSN changes. Date of Birth Changes: See Processing Guide 33 for date of birth changes. Date of Birth Changes Previously Reported: See Processing Guide 33 for when the beneficiary has reported a date of birth change and the new date of birth was entered in CalWIN. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageMedi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS) Impact 4.11.4 2 of 2 Program Impacts: None. References: Medi-Cal Eligibility Procedures Manual 4M(II)A Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by May 31, 2023 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations

title: Section 12-Unconditionally Available Income
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Unconditionally Available Income (UAI) Number Page 04.12.01 1 of 1 Revision Date: October 1, 2025 Background: Income is unconditionally available when the customer just needs to accept or claim it, without meeting any additional conditions beyond being eligible. Purpose: This section has been revised to incorporate guidance on the elimination of the requirement to apply for other benefits, often referred to as UAI, as a condition of Medi-Cal eligibility. Policy: Effective June 1, 2025, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) has eliminated the requirement for individuals to apply for other benefits as a condition of eligibility for all Medi-Cal programs. The elimination of the requirement to apply for other benefits specifically applies to benefits that are income or cash-based only. Do not request that customers apply for UAI or other benefits that include but are not limited to: • Social Security benefits (for example, retirement or disability benefits from the Social Security Administration [SSA]). • Unemployment Insurance Benefits (UIB). • Pensions. • Veteran’s benefits (for example, disability compensation, pensions, or education assistance). • State Disability Insurance (SDI). Although customers are no longer required to apply for UAI, continue to inform Medi -Cal customers about potential income from other available sources. For guidance on other conditions of eligibility, refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 04.01. References: ACWDL 11-25, 19-13, 24-19, 25-03 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by September 30, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Social Security Benefits Number Page 04.12.02 1 of 2 Revision Date: October 1, 2025 Background: Title II Retirement Benefits refers to the federal Old- Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance (OASDI) program. Social Security consists of two separate parts, Retirement and Disability Insurance. Under OASDI, monthly benefits are paid to retired workers, their spouses and dependent children, and survivors of deceased workers (spouses, dependent children, and dependent parents). Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) replaces a portion of a worker’s income when a medical condition ends in death or prevents them from working for at least 12 months. Under SSDI, monthly benefits are paid to disabled workers who have not yet reached retirement age and their families. Purpose: This section has been revised to provide guidance on the elimination of the requirement to apply for other Unconditionally Available Income (UAI). Policy: Although it is no longer a condition of eligibility, all Medi-Cal customers who meet the criteria below are considered potentially eligible for OASDI . I nform Medi -Cal customers about potential income from available sources. To apply for Social Security benefits, the customer must be: • At least 61 years and 9 months of age and want to start receiving benefits in the next three months. • Widow or widower. • Surviving divorced spouse. • Surviving unmarried child under 18. Note: Applying for OASDI benefits before full retirement age reduces monthly payments which may result in a significant lifetime income loss. Social Security Administration (SSA) Application Process The customer can file for SSA by: • Applying online at www.socialsecurity.gov. • Calling 1-800-772-1213 to make an appointment. • Applying in person. Procedures: None References: ACWDL 11-25, 24-19 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by September 30, 2028. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Social Security Benefits Number Page 04.12.02 2 of 2 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Unemployment Insurance Benefits (UIB) Number Page 04.12.03 1 of 3 Revision Date: October 1, 2025 Background: UIB is a program which provides income to eligible individuals who are out of work. Purpose: This section was revised to provide updated guidance on the elimination of the requirement to apply for other Unconditionally Available Income (UAI). Policy: Although it is no longer a condition of eligibility , inform Medi-Cal customers who are considered potentially eligible for UIB how to apply for benefits through the Employment Development Department (EDD) except for individuals who: • Have not worked in employment covered by the Unemployment Insurance Compensation Law in the past 19 months. • R eceive UIB, have a claim pending, or have exhausted their UIB. • R eceive disability insurance benefits. • Are ill or injured as specified in the Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 04.12.04. • Were previously denied or discontinued from UIB and have had no subsequent employment which would change the previous EDD determination. • Are fully employed (working at least 40 hours per week). • Do not have Satisfactory Immigration Status (SIS). • Are full-time students. • Are children under 16 years of age with no work history. • Are minor consent applicants. A. Eligible Claimants Eligible claimants applying in California must have earned a minimum of $900 during a 12-month base period within the last 19 months and must: • Not have quit their job without good cause. • Not have been fired for cause. • Be able to work and available for employment. • Be seeking employment. B. UIB Application Process The customer can file a UIB claim by: • Applying online at edd.ca.gov/unemployment/apply. • Completing a paper Unemployment Insurance (UI) Application (Form DE 1101). • Telephone: (800) 300-5616 (English) (800) 326-8937 (Spanish) (800) 815-9387 (TTY) (800) 547-3506 (Chinese) (800) 547-2058 (Vietnamese) County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Unemployment Insurance Benefits (UIB) Number Page 04.12.03 2 of 3 C. EDD Real-Time Match The EDD Real-Time Match provides on-line access to EDD files. It can be used to determine: • If the customer is potentially eligible to receive UIB/State Disability Insurance (SDI). • If the customer has filed a recent claim. • The Weekly Benefit Amount (WBA). The current claim information from the EDD Real-Time Match can be used to verify a claim, under the condition that the information does not conflict with what the customer has stated. If there is a discrepancy with what the customer has stated, or with the Income Eligibility Verification System (IEVS) information, attempt to clarify the discrepancy utilizing reasonable explanation. If the customer is unable to provide a reasonable explanation, staff must obtain the UIB verification from the customer before approval. Refer to MPG 04.07.02S for additional guidance on reasonable explanation. D. UIB Award Notice Approximately 10 days after the application for UIB has been filed, the claimant will receive a computer printout from EDD. The print -out is titled "California Award." This print -out does not necessarily mean that the claimant will be entitled to receive UIB. The claimant may subsequently be denied UIB because of information obtained during the follow -up telephone interview, information from the previous employer, etc. Should the claimant be found ineligible for UIB, they will receive a denial notice indicating the reason for ineligibility. When the claimant is found eligible, they will receive UIB benefits. E. UIB Payments When a claimant is found to be eligible, UIB will normally be paid the third week after the application is filed. The initial payment will generally be for one week’s benefits. Benefits are issued either by check, EDD debit card, or direct deposit. The claimant can request a printout of their payment history by calling 1-866-333-4606 or online (www.edd.ca.gov/). Payment history will be mailed out by EDD within 10 days. UIB is paid every two weeks thereafter. The same WBA will generally be paid for each week of unemployment throughout the duration of the claim. However, adjustments to the WBA will be made when either: • Wages more than $25 occur. • SDI eligibility occurs. • Other internal adjustments are necessary. F. Interstate Claims The Interstate Benefit Payment Plan allows a person residing in one state (the agent state) to claim benefits from another state (the liable state) if they earned wages covered by Unemployment Compensation in the liable state. These claims are called Interstate Claims. The benefits are paid in approximately eight weeks by the liable state. EDD (including real-time match) does not have Interstate Claims information. Verification of benefit amounts can be obtained through documents in the customer’s possession, or by writing to the unemployment insurance office in the other state. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Unemployment Insurance Benefits (UIB) Number Page 04.12.03 3 of 3 G. Extended UIB During periods of high unemployment, California has a special program for claimants whose regular benefits have expired or have been exhausted. This is the California Extended Duration (Cal -Ed) program. The Federal Government has a similar program of extended benefits known as Federal Extended Benefits (FED-ED). The maximum amount of an extended claim is 50 percent of the original (parent) claim. The WBA remains the same as the parent claim. If the customer has received UIB recently , inform them to contact EDD if they wish to pursue further benefits. It takes approximately two weeks to process each claim. There are no requirements to serve a waiting week, and payment will be made for the effective date of the claim. If at any time the wage earner becomes eligible to regular UIB, EDD will terminate the Extended Unemployment Insurance claim and require the claimant to file a new claim for UIB. Procedure: Inform customers of potential eligibility to UAI and apply any income received to the ongoing Medi-Cal budget. Program Impacts: None References: ACWDL 24-19 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by September 30, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Disability Insurance Benefits (DIB) Number Page 04.12.04 1 of 2 Revision Date: October 1, 2025 Background: DIB is a program which provides income to eligible people who cannot work because of illness or injury not caused by their job. Purpose: This section has been revised to include new guidance on the elimination of requirement to apply for Unconditionally Available Income (UAI). Policy: Although it is no longer a condition of eligibility for Medi-Cal, inform customers of their potential eligibility and provide guidance on how to apply for benefits. A. Eligible Claimants In general, eligible claimants applying in California must have earned a minimum of $300 during a twelve-month base period and must: • H ave an incapacity which was not incurred on the job. • B e under treatment by a physician at the present time. • H ave a statement from a physician verifying incapacity. • H ave earned a minimum of $75 in a quarter within the base period. Note: Pregnancy may qualify as an incapacity if it prevents the individual from working. After childbirth, an individual may receive DIB for six weeks, regardless of prior eligibility. B. DIB Application Process The process below outlines a DIB claim submission. • Complete applicant section on form DE-250. • Submit form DE-250 to their doctor to complete the physician section. • Mail the application to the DIB Field Office. When the DIB Branch of the Employment Development Department (EDD) processes the application, the customer can submit the approval notice as verification of the claim amount. DIB is paid according to the number of days disabled rather than weekly. Benefits are issued either by check, direct deposit, or EDD debit card. The customer can request a printout of their payment history by calling 1 -800-480-3287 or online (www.edd.ca.gov/). Payment history will be mailed out by EDD within 10 days. C. Voluntary DIB Plan If a customer qualifies for DIB and worke d for an employer with an EDD -approved private insurance carrier or self-insured plan, they may be eligible for Voluntary DIB Plan benefits. Income received from Voluntary DIB Plan must be reported timely. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Disability Insurance Benefits (DIB) Number Page 04.12.04 2 of 2 Procedure: None Program Impacts: None References: ACWDL 11-25, 24-19 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by September 30, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Veterans Benefits Number Page 04.12.05 1 of 3 Revision Date: October 1, 2025 Background: Veterans’ benefits offer support which include healthcare, disability compensation, pension, education, home loans, insurance, and burial benefits and are administered by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). San Diego County has established the Office of Military and Veterans Affairs (OMVA) which is a section of the Health and Human Services Agency ( HHSA). OMVA provides services for military veterans, their dependents, and survivors who are entitled to benefits through the VA, State of California, and other applicable agencies. Purpose: This section was revised to include new guidance on the elimination of the requirement to apply for other Unconditionally Available Income (UAI). Policy: VA benefits such as disability compensation, pensions, or education assistance are considered UAI. Although it is no longer a condition of eligibility for Medi-Cal, inform customers of their potential eligibility and provide guidance on how to apply for benefits. The requirement to apply for veterans’ health benefits remains in place whenever a member of the household is a veteran of military service, the spouse, or a dependent of a veteran. Only the person refusing to apply for and accept VA health benefits is considered ineligible for Medi-Cal. A. MC 05 Referral Procedure Complete the Military Verification and Referral Form (MC 05) using the information provided on the application even if the VA benefit verification has been provided. The form does not require a signature from the customer. Complete this form at intake and redetermination for each customer when they: • Indicate they have military service. • Are in receipt of VA benefits. • Have a spouse, parent, stepparent, or child who is not in receipt of benefits, but have served in the United States military for any period. • Have a dependent who has applied for or expects to receive VA benefits. • Have a dependent (including stepchild) who is receiving VA pension, disability , or educational benefits. • Are a disabled veteran or the dependent of a disabled or deceased veteran. • Are currently receiving VA disability benefits and their disability has worsened. • Are a veteran residing in a long-term care (LTC) facility. Mail completed MC 05 forms to the OMVA at Mail Stop O-273--ATTN: OMVA. See Medi-Cal Desk Aid 93: How to Complete the MC 05. Note: Do not delay approval pending the return of the MC 05 from OMVA if all other requirements have been met. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Veterans Benefits Number Page 04.12.05 2 of 3 The MC 05 is not required when: • The individual is on active duty in the military. • The individual's service was limited to the Merchant Marine, National Guard, or Reserves. • No legal relationship exists between the customer and the veteran or paternity cannot be established. • A previous MC 05 completed by OMVA states that no future benefits are available to the veteran. • A copy of a complete MC 05 was returned by OMVA within the last 45 days. • The veteran cannot be identified by at least one of the following: o Social Security Number and Date of Birth. o Military serial number. o VA claim number. When a referral is not submitted, make a journal entry documenting the reason. B. OMVA MC 05 Response OMVA will process all MC 05s on a flow basis, unless identified as a priority. The average response time for return of the MC 05 is one week after receipt , depending on the volume of referrals received. After the OMVA representative has determined eligibility to VA benefits, a copy of the MC 05 will be sent to the Document Processing Center (DPC) and imaged to the case. C. Aid and Attendance (A&A) Benefits Under certain conditions, veterans, spouses/widows of veterans, dependent s and "Gold Star" parents (parents who lost a child in military action) who receive VA benefits may be entitled to additional monthly payments if they have severe physical or mental disabilities. The additional entitlement is called A&A benefits. To qualify for A&A benefits, it must be demonstrated that the veteran, spouse/widow, or parent cannot feed or dress themselves, care for their needs, or remain out of bed all day. Blindness or confinement in an LTC facility also qualifies for A&A entitlement. D. Unusual Medical Expenses Under an injunction from the Sherman v. Griepentrog lawsuit, disregard that portion of a needs-based VA pension or needs -based compensation that is the direct result of an Unusual Medical Expense (UME) when determining a customer’s share of cost (SOC). Approval will not be delayed pending verification of UME. The amount of VA benefits, which is not otherwise exempt, will be counted as income when determining the SOC. When the MC 05 is returned, indicating the amount paid for UME, disregard that portion of the VA pension and if appropriate, readjust the SOC for previous months. E. VA Claims Initiated by OMVA The OMVA accesses HHSA files to identify Medi-Cal customers who are in LTC facilities. A Medi -Cal customer in LTC may be interviewed by OMVA staff to determine potential eligibility to VA benefits, including VA A&A payments. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Veterans Benefits Number Page 04.12.05 3 of 3 If the customer appears potentially eligible for VA benefits or A&A payments, the OMVA will assist them with filing a VA claim. OMVA will complete and forward a copy to the Family Resource Center (FRC). Once a claim has been filed, it may take up to six months for the VA to determine eligibility. Do not call OMVA to inquire about the status of a claim during the six -month period. If an eligibility determination has not been received by the end of the period, contact OMVA to inquire about the status of the claim. Procedure: None Program Impact: None References: MEM Proc. 10J ACWDL 95-29, 05-08, 16-04, 24-19, 25-03 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by September 30, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Unconditionally Available Income (UAI) Number Page 04.12.01 1 of 1 Revision Date: October 1, 2025 Background: Income is unconditionally available when the customer just needs to accept or claim it, without meeting any additional conditions beyond being eligible. Purpose: This section has been revised to incorporate guidance on the elimination of the requirement to apply for other benefits, often referred to as UAI, as a condition of Medi-Cal eligibility. Policy: Effective June 1, 2025, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) has eliminated the requirement for individuals to apply for other benefits as a condition of eligibility for all Medi-Cal programs. The elimination of the requirement to apply for other benefits specifically applies to benefits that are income or cash-based only. Do not request that customers apply for UAI or other benefits that include but are not limited to: • Social Security benefits (for example, retirement or disability benefits from the Social Security Administration [SSA]). • Unemployment Insurance Benefits (UIB). • Pensions. • Veteran’s benefits (for example, disability compensation, pensions, or education assistance). • State Disability Insurance (SDI). Although customers are no longer required to apply for UAI, continue to inform Medi -Cal customers about potential income from other available sources. For guidance on other conditions of eligibility, refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 04.01. References: ACWDL 11-25, 19-13, 24-19, 25-03 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by September 30, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Social Security Benefits Number Page 04.12.02 1 of 2 Revision Date: October 1, 2025 Background: Title II Retirement Benefits refers to the federal Old- Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance (OASDI) program. Social Security consists of two separate parts, Retirement and Disability Insurance. Under OASDI, monthly benefits are paid to retired workers, their spouses and dependent children, and survivors of deceased workers (spouses, dependent children, and dependent parents). Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) replaces a portion of a worker’s income when a medical condition ends in death or prevents them from working for at least 12 months. Under SSDI, monthly benefits are paid to disabled workers who have not yet reached retirement age and their families. Purpose: This section has been revised to provide guidance on the elimination of the requirement to apply for other Unconditionally Available Income (UAI). Policy: Although it is no longer a condition of eligibility, all Medi-Cal customers who meet the criteria below are considered potentially eligible for OASDI . I nform Medi -Cal customers about potential income from available sources. To apply for Social Security benefits, the customer must be: • At least 61 years and 9 months of age and want to start receiving benefits in the next three months. • Widow or widower. • Surviving divorced spouse. • Surviving unmarried child under 18. Note: Applying for OASDI benefits before full retirement age reduces monthly payments which may result in a significant lifetime income loss. Social Security Administration (SSA) Application Process The customer can file for SSA by: • Applying online at www.socialsecurity.gov. • Calling 1-800-772-1213 to make an appointment. • Applying in person. Procedures: None References: ACWDL 11-25, 24-19 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by September 30, 2028.
