title: Section 13 - Denial/Discontinuance Requirements
content: Article 4 Section 13 –Denial/Discontinuance/Restoration Requirements Table of Contents TITLE MPG CITE Request for Withdrawal/Discontinuance 04.13.01 Denial/Discontinuance Due to Lack of Information 04.13.02 Loss of Contact 04.13.03 Rescission of Denial/Discontinuance 04.13.04 Restoration of Full-Scope Medi-Cal 04.13.05 04.13.01 Request for Withdrawal/Discontinuance A. General The following procedures will apply whenever an applicant/beneficiary or person authorized to act on behalf of the applicant/beneficiary requests withdrawal of an application for Medi-Cal or requests discontinuance of Medi-Cal benefits. An applicant/beneficiary may withdraw his/her application for Medi-Cal or request discontinuance of Medi-Cal benefits by: •Indicating the request on Form MC 215; •Submitting a signed statement indicating the request for withdrawal/discontinuance; or •Making an oral request for withdrawal/discontinuance. MPG LTR 631 (5/08) B. Processing Request for Withdrawal or Discontinuan ce When the request is ... Then the worker will ... Written •deny/discontinuance the case; •send the appropriate NOA to the client; •retain a copy of the written request, along with the NOA, in the case file. Oral •ask that the request be made in writing; •document in case comment of the oral request and that written confirmation has been requested; •deny/discontinue the case; AND •send appropriate NOA. It is not necessary to wait for the written request before the case is denied/discontinued. When the written request is received, it is to be filed with a copy of the NOA. MPG LTR 631 (5/08) C. Timely Notice Requirement Timely notice is not required when the beneficiary provides a clear and signed written request for discontinuance of Medi-Cal benefits. Adequate notice is required. Timely notice is required when only an oral request is made and the worker is unable to obtain a written request from the beneficiary. MPG LTR 631 (5/08) D. Disputed Requests for Withdrawal or Discontinuan ce If the applicant/beneficiary fails to return a written request for withdrawal/discontinuance and later disputes the oral request, and there is not other basis for denial/discontinuance, the worker will immediately rescind the action. Otherwise, the action will be considered valid. MPG LTR 631 (5/08) 04.13.02 Denial/Discontinuance Due to Lack of Information A. General Applications are NOT to be denied solely because the worker has not received all required verifications within given deadlines unless the applicant/beneficiary is not cooperating within his/her ability or limitations. The following procedures must be followed when Medi-Cal benefits are to be denied or discontinued due to lack of information. MPG LTR 631 (5/08) B. Worker Assistance In addition to following the 10/10 timeframe when requesting for information/verifications necessary to complete eligibility determination, the worker is required to review the applicant/beneficiary’s ability to obtain the required verifications and offer assistance as necessary in obtaining verifications. The type of worker assistance required varies depending on the limitation of the applicant/beneficiary. In some situations, assistance in identifying the address of the verification source may be all that is needed. In others, the worker may need to obtain the applicant/beneficiary’s written authorization and request the verification on behalf of the applicant. MPG LTR 631 (5/08) C. Denials Due to Lack of Information Prior to denying an applicant for failure to provide essential information, the worker must: Step Action 1 Provide the applicant with a list of outstanding verifications and allow the applicant at least 10 calendar days to provide. The worker must extend the 10-day deadline if the applicant indicates that he/she may have difficulty in providing the verifications by the given deadline. If an extended deadline is agreed to, the worker will document that fact in CalWIN. 2 When the deadline has passed and verifications are still missing, provide the applicant with a 2nd request for information/verifications. Allow the applicant another 10 calendar days to provide. If, at the end of the second deadline, there is no contact from the applicant and no apparent reason of a need for a longer period in which to obtain the verifications, the worker will deny the application failure to provide essential information. When denying the application for failure to provide essential information, the worker must: •Determine which member of the MFBU lacks the required information AND whether the denial action applies 1) solely to that person or 2) to that person AND those for whom he/she is responsible, or 3) to the entire MFBU; AND •Determine whether the remaining MFBU members are still linked to the program. If not, then they will be denied as Medi-Cal linkage does not exist. MPG Letter 684 (08/09) D. Applicant Provides After Denial The following procedures shall apply when applicant contacts the County after denial within a specified timeframe. When… Then… Applicant contacts within 30 days of denial notice date AND request for more time Evaluate the applicant’s reason fore requiring additional time. The worker will allow additional time if it appears that the applicant is making a good faith effort to obtain the verifications, and/or the delay is beyond the applicant’s control. The contact with the applicant and the worker decision must be documented in the case file. If an extended period is allowed and verifications are not provided by the deadline, a second denial NOA is to be sent. If the verifications are provided and eligibility exists, the original denial is to be rescinded. Verifications are received within 30 days of denial notice date Consider the verifications as timely and rescind the denial, if otherwise eligible. If some verifications are still missing, the worker must document the case file and send a note to the applicant stating that the original denial stands. A copy of the note is to be filed in the case. If all verifications are provided but ineligibility exists for a different reason, a second denial NOA must be sent. Contacts are made or verifications received more than 30 days after the denial notice date The denial will stand and the applicant shall be advised to reapply. However, the supervisor may approve rescission of the denial under extenuating circumstances. Extenuating circumstances could include an applicant who has been hospitalized, or had a similar family emergency, and contacts the worker within a day or two after the emergency is over. The applicant must be advised of the decision either orally or in writing. The worker must document the oral contact in case comment or retain a copy of any written contact in case file. MPG LTR 569 (01/05) E. Discontinua nce Due to Lack of Information A second phone contact attempt is required before Medi-Cal benefits may be discontinued for failure to provide reason. The phone contact attempts are to be made as follows: •Make the first phone contact attempt on the day that a written request for the missing item(s) is mailed. •Make the second phone contact on the fifth business day after the written request for the missing item(s) was mailed or when partial items are received from the first request. •If only partial items are provided after two attempted phone contacts have been made, a courtesy phone contact is suggested to clarify what is needed. The worker must document all phone contacts, and/or attempted phone contacts, in the case. In addition to the phone contact, workers are encouraged to mail out the Reminder Flyer 14-76 HHSA (DISC) to promote the importance of health coverage and to encourage beneficiaries to return the forms. Reminder: Workers are precluded from requesting certain information from a Medi-Cal beneficiary to complete an eligibility review. Workers are not to request information which: •has been previously provided within 12 months from the date the eligibility determination was made; and •is not subject to change; •is available for verification by the worker (for example, in an other PA case file); or •is not absolutely necessary. The worker will follow the same general procedures as used at application in evaluating the beneficiary’s need for assistance in obtaining verifications needed for redetermination or upon change of eligibility or share of cost factors. Certification for Medi-Cal shall not be delayed or discontinued pending verifications from a person who is currently eligible unless the beneficiary refuses to cooperate. MPG LTR 569 (01/05) Revision Date: 08/01/2022 Background: An application for Medi-Cal may be denied or an active Medi-Cal case discontinued for loss of contact only after reasonable attempts are taken to contact the customer. The Human Services Specialist (HSS) must confirm contact information any time they speak with a customer by phone or in-person. Purpose: This section has been updated to provide guidance on the process when a Medi-Cal customer’s mail is returned as Undeliverable. In addition, the section has been reformatted and updated for sunset review. Policy: Upon receipt of returned mail or another indication that a customer has moved without reporting a change of address, the HSS will make reasonable attempts to contact the customer. Phone Contact Requirements Prior to proceeding with the undeliverable mail process below, the HSS must first attempt to contact the customer phone. Additionally, a second contact is required once the MC 355 has been mailed to the customer. 1. First attempt If contact is made… -Confirm the customer’s address -Update the case address if necessary -Document the contact in Case Comments If unable to reach the customer… -Proceed with the undeliverable mail process below 2. Second attempt Make a second attempt to contact the customer by phone after the MC 355 is sent, according to the undeliverable mail process below. If contact is made… -Confirm the customer’s address -Update the case address if necessary -Document the contact in Case Comments Note: If there is no phone number on file, add a case comment and continue with the undeliverable mail process below. Requirements for Processing Undeliverable Mail When mail is returned to the county as undeliverable, the HSS will take the following steps: 1. Enter a case comment that includes the… -Type of mail (Notice of Action [NOA], form, letter) -Address the mail was sent to -Date the mail was sent -Date the mail was returned -Safe at Home (SAH) status if applicable County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageLoss of Contact 04.13.03 1 of 11 2. Conduct an Ex Parte Review -Review all available information in California Healthcare Eligibility, Enrollment and Retention System (CalHEERS), Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS) or through an immediate family member’s* California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids (CalWORKs)/CalFresh case to confirm the undelivered mail was sent to the appropriate address -For SAH participant, attempt to verify the new address via the SAH Program Administrator -If an updated address is located, indicate in the case comments where the address was found, and attempt to send the previously undelivered mail to the customer at the new address *An “immediate family member” is an individual within the customer’s Medi-Cal household with whom they were living according to last known information. 3. Send the MC 355 -If unable to locate a more recent address using ex parte, the HSS will send an MC 355 to the customer’s last known address, with a 30-day deadline to return the requested information -The MC 355 will request only the customer’s current address and any other information necessary to determine eligibility -If the United States Postal Service (USPS) provides a forwarding address, the HSS will also send the MC 355 requesting the missing information to the forwarding address, even if it is out of state 4. When information is not returned by the customer When the MC 355 is returned as undeliverable, the customer does not return the information requested on the MC 355 or does not confirm their updated address by the MC 355 due date and after the required additional county contact, the HSS will follow the guidelines below for redetermination based on the customer’s individual circumstances. This guidance applies to all members of a household where the address is unknown, and not just the primary applicant/case name. USPS has not provided a forwarding address or has provided an out-of-state forwarding address The HSS will discontinue with a timely 10-day NOA when all the following apply: -The USPS provides no forwarding address or an Out-of-State forwarding address -The HSS has made the required additional attempt to contact after sending the MC 355 -An updated address is not confirmed by the customer within the 30-day deadline The timely 10-day NOA must be sent to the last known address (not the forwarding address) and must list the missing information that is needed to determine eligibility and include the 90-day cure period language. USPS has provided an in-state forwarding address If a Medi-Cal only customer (excluding SAH participant) does not confirm the new address after the MC 355 has been sent and additional required contact has been attempted, the HSS will: -Update the case record of the Medi-Cal only customer with the in-state forwarding address provided by the USPS -If the address is in another county, the HSS will initiate an intercounty transfer (ICT) for the Medi-Cal only customer when no other information is needed beyond the updated address County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageLoss of Contact 04.13.03 2 of 11 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide -The Medi-Cal only customer will not be discontinued if the only thing required is an updated address If the customer is eligible for both Medi-Cal and other public social services programs, such as CalWORKs and CalFresh, or the customer is a SAH participant, and does not confirm the new address, the HSS will not update the case record with the in-state forwarding address provided by the USPS or perform an ICT. The address on the case record remains the last known address confirmed by the customer. If more information than the updated address is needed to determine ongoing eligibility, the HSS will discontinue the customer with a timely 10-day NOA when all of the following apply: -The USPS provides an in-state forwarding address -The HSS requires more information than the updated address to determine ongoing eligibility -The HSS has made the required additional attempt to contact after the MC 355 is sent -The customer has not responded to the MC 355 by the 30-day deadline Reminders for processing undeliverable mail -Undeliverable mail resulting from a returned annual renewal form may be received early enough to conduct the undeliverable mail activities prior to the annual renewal due date. Depending on when the HSS receives the undeliverable annual renewal form, it is possible for customers to receive an additional month(s) of eligibility beyond their annual renewal month to allow the 30- day due date for the MC 355 and the10-day NOA -If an undeliverable annual renewal form is received after the customer has been discontinued for no renewal, the HSS must reinstate eligibility without a break in coverage, then follow the steps outlined above -If the original mail that was returned as undeliverable is a discontinuance NOA unrelated to whereabouts unknown, a NOA informing a customer about an increase in their share-of-cost or a NOA informing them of an adverse change to their eligibility, the HSS must reinstate eligibility to the previous level without a break in coverage, then follow the steps outlined above -Evaluate for good cause if the customer contacts the HSS after discontinuance 5. 90-Day Cure Period If the customer provides all information necessary to determine eligibility within 90 days of the discontinuance date, the HSS will make a redetermination using the existing the 90-Day Cure Period process. Exempt From Discontinuance Loss of contact is not a basis for discontinuing Medi-Cal benefits for the following programs: -Former Foster Youth (FFY) -Children eligible for Continuous Eligibility for Children (CEC) -Deemed Eligible Infants (under 1 year) -Medi-Cal Access Program (MCAP) -Pregnant beneficiaries -Beneficiaries in their 12-month postpartum period -Aid types where the county does not control the Medi-Cal record such as Supplemental Security Income/State Supplementary Payment (SSI/SSP), KinGAP, or Adoption Assistance Number PageLoss of Contact 04.13.03 3 of 11 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageLoss of Contact 04.13.03 8 of 11 Program Impacts: CalFresh cases should not be discontinued for Whereabouts Unknown. When discontinuing Medi-Cal for one of the undeliverable mail situations above, ensure the action taken in CalWIN does not affect the CalFresh benefits. References: ACWDL 22-09 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 08/31/2025 04.13.04 Rescission of Medi-Cal Denial/Discontinuance A. Requirement The worker must rescind the denial/discontinuance of the Medi- Cal case when any of the following conditions apply: •A state hearing decision orders rescission of the denial/discontinuance; •The worker receives an Out of Hearing Resolution from Appeals instructing the worker to rescind the denial/discontinuance; or •The worker/ES determines that the denial/discontinuance was in error. MPG LTR 11 (04/88) 04.13.05 Restoration of Full-Scope Medi-Cal A. General The following procedures apply whenever an applicant or beneficiary provides acceptable evidence of citizenship/identity after “limited scope benefits are granted. MPG LTR 631 (05/08) B. Restoring Full-Scope Applicants or beneficiaries who receive “limited scope” Medi-Cal for failure to provide evidence of citizenship/identity will have their full scope eligibility restored back as follows: If documents are provided And if… Then full-scope shall be restored to… Good cause exist the month that limited scope eligibility began Within one year of application/redetermination date Good cause does not exist 1st of the month in which the document is received More than one year of application/redetermination date 1st of the month in which the document is received. MPG LTR 631 (05/08) C. Establishing Good Cause Good cause exists when the applicant or beneficiary is unable to provide acceptable evidence of citizenship and/or identity for reasons beyond his/her control or knowledge. Examples of good case in these cases include but are not limited to: •A prior belief that the documents did not exist or were unattainable. •Mental or physical impairment that was an impediment to obtaining the documents; •Securing the documents could result in physical danger or familiar discord. Refer to MPG 04.21.01 for general information on good cause. MPG LTR 803 D. Recoupment of Previously Paid Expenses Applicants or current beneficiaries who paid for medical or dental care while obtaining their citizenship and identity documents may be reimbursed by Medi-Cal for these expense. In these cases, the applicant or current beneficiary shall be referred to the California Department of Health Services Beneficiary Services at 916-403-2007 for more information. MPG LTR 631 (05/08) E. Outstanding Expenses For medical and dental bills that have not yet been paid and if warranted under the good cause provision as specified above in MPG 4-13-5B, an eligibility letter of authorization (MC 180) will issued upon request to facilitate the payment of services render by providers more than one year after the month of services. Refer to MPG 14-3-1 for procedures on completion of MC 180. MPG LTR 631 (05/08)

General The following procedures will apply whenever an applicant/beneficiary or person authorized to act on behalf of the applicant/beneficiary requests withdrawal of an application for Medi-Cal or requests discontinuance of Medi-Cal benefits. An applicant/beneficiary may withdraw his/her application for Medi-Cal or request discontinuance of Medi-Cal benefits by: •Indicating the request on Form MC 215; •Submitting a signed statement indicating the request for withdrawal/discontinuance; or •Making an oral request for withdrawal/discontinuance. MPG LTR 631 (5/08) B. Processing Request for Withdrawal or Discontinuan ce When the request is ... Then the worker will ... Written •deny/discontinuance the case; •send the appropriate NOA to the client; •retain a copy of the written request, along with the NOA, in the case file. Oral •ask that the request be made in writing; •document in case comment of the oral request and that written confirmation has been requested; •deny/discontinue the case; AND •send appropriate NOA. It is not necessary to wait for the written request before the case is denied/discontinued. When the written request is received, it is to be filed with a copy of the NOA. MPG LTR 631 (5/08) C. Timely Notice Requirement Timely notice is not required when the beneficiary provides a clear and signed written request for discontinuance of Medi-Cal benefits. Adequate notice is required. Timely notice is required when only an oral request is made and the worker is unable to obtain a written request from the beneficiary. MPG LTR 631 (5/08) D. Disputed Requests for Withdrawal or Discontinuan ce If the applicant/beneficiary fails to return a written request for withdrawal/discontinuance and later disputes the oral request, and there is not other basis for denial/discontinuance, the worker will immediately rescind the action. Otherwise, the action will be considered valid. MPG LTR 631 (5/08) 04.13.02 Denial/Discontinuance Due to Lack of Information A. General Applications are NOT to be denied solely because the worker has not received all required verifications within given deadlines unless the applicant/beneficiary is not cooperating within his/her ability or limitations. The following procedures must be followed when Medi-Cal benefits are to be denied or discontinued due to lack of information. MPG LTR 631 (5/08) B. Worker Assistance In addition to following the 10/10 timeframe when requesting for information/verifications necessary to complete eligibility determination, the worker is required to review the applicant/beneficiary’s ability to obtain the required verifications and offer assistance as necessary in obtaining verifications. The type of worker assistance required varies depending on the limitation of the applicant/beneficiary. In some situations, assistance in identifying the address of the verification source may be all that is needed. In others, the worker may need to obtain the applicant/beneficiary’s written authorization and request the verification on behalf of the applicant. MPG LTR 631 (5/08) C. The worker must extend the 10-day deadline if the applicant indicates that he/she may have difficulty in providing the verifications by the given deadline. title: Section 15 - Renewal
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAnnual Renewal - Overview of Requirements 04.15.01 1 of 3 Revision Date: September 1, 2026 Background: Beneficiaries must have a renewal (RE) completed every 12 months to evaluate ongoing Medi-Cal eligibility. Purpose: This section is revised for the sunset review; no policy or procedures have been changed. Policy: Medi-Cal customers must have their eligibility renewed every 12 months. The Affordable Care Act (ACA) of 2010 changed the process to allow for automated annual REs, a 90-day cure period for failure to provide, advancement of the annual RE due date when a change in circumstances (CIC) occurs, and the required use of pre-populated RE forms. Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) Administrative Renewal Two months prior to the RE due month, an administrative process takes place when California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) sends Electronic Health Information Transfer (eHIT) transactions to the California Healthcare Eligibility Enrollment, and Retention System (CalHEERS) to initiate the electronic verification process for MAGI RE. If CalHEERS confirms eligibility, CalSAWS will: •Receive eligibility results from CalHEERS along with a Notice of Action (NOA). •Authorize the case during the overnight batch process. •Advance the RE date to 12 months from the original RE month. •Generate a journal entry. If CalHEERS does not confirm MAGI eligibility for all household members, CalSAWS will generate and send the pre-populated Medi-Cal Renewal form (MC 216) to the customer approximately 60 days prior to the renewal due date. Renewal Packet Required A renewal packet is required for Non-MAGI cases and MAGI cases that do not auto-renew. The customer or person authorized to act on their behalf must complete the renewal forms and provide the verifications necessary to redetermine eligibility. Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) section 04.15.03 for information on the forms required at RE. Information to be Verified The following information must be verified at RE: •Disability or blindness that is not previously known (when determining Non-MAGI linkage). •Legal responsibility for a child applying alone. •Countable income based on programs evaluated. •Status and value of non-exempt property for Non-MAGI customers. •Immigration status (if a change is reported). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAnnual Renewal - Overview of Requirements 04.15.01 2 of 3 Staff must not request information that is not relevant to ongoing eligibility or was previously provided and not subject to change such as date of birth, SSN or United States (U.S.) citizenship. Original documents are not required. Photocopies of all verifications are acceptable. Telephone Information RE information may be obtained over the phone as long as it is clearly documented in the CalSAWS case. A telephonic signature is required and the customer must be informed that they are making their statements under the penalty of perjury. Social Security Number (SSN) It is not necessary to re-verify the SSN at RE. However, if the customer’s SSN was not previously verified electronically, the customer will be given 30 days to provide verification or proof of application for the SSN. Citizenship When a customer reports a change in their citizenship status at RE, verification is required when ex parte or electronic verification is unavailable. Completion of the RE will not be delayed and the customer will be allowed a 90-day reasonable opportunity period (ROP). Income Eligibility Verification System (IEVS) An IEVS report will only generate during annual RE or CIC when there is a discrepancy. When a Recipient IEVS is received, staff must determine whether it matches the information provided by the customer. If there are no discrepancies, no further action is required. If the information does not match, staff will follow up with the customer to obtain verifications. Refer to Medi-Cal Processing Guide 19 - Fraud Prevention. Adding a Person Customers may add a person to their Medi-Cal case at RE by completing the appropriate section on the RE form or by providing the individual’s information over the phone. The information is entered in CalSAWS and run against the Hub (if applicable). An ex parte review must be completed prior to requesting paper verifications. Splitting Cases When a household member (such as an adult child) leaves the home or begins filing their own taxes, it becomes necessary to split them from the original case and open them on a case of their own. The individual who is being placed on a separate case must remain active while eligibility is redetermined. Procedure: Medi-Cal Renewal procedures can be found in Processing Guide 01 - Medi-Cal Annual Renewals and Change in Circumstances Redeterminations. Program Impacts: None References: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAnnual Renewal - Overview of Requirements 04.15.01 3 of 3 ACWDLs 06-16, 06-17, 07-12, 08-03, 11-30, 11-23, 20-17, 25-16 W&I Code 14005.37 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by August 31, 2029. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageChange in Circumstances Redeterminations 04.15.02 1 of 2 Revision Date: September 1, 2026 Background: A Change in Circumstances (CIC) redetermination is completed when the county receives information about a change to a customer’s circumstances that may affect their eligibility for Medi-Cal benefits. This information might be reported by the customer or come from another source such as the CalFresh and California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids (CalWORKs) programs, Covered California, the Social Security Administration (SSA), Asset Verification Reports (AVP), or the Income Eligibility Verification System (IEVS). Purpose: This section was added to provide guidance on CIC regulations including the latest renewal (RE) completion flexibility for hard-to-reach populations. Policy: CIC Redetermination Criteria The following circumstances require a CIC redetermination: •A customer reports a change (e.g. income, tax filing status) outside of their regular annual RE that requires a reevaluation of Medi-Cal eligibility. •Eligibility is evaluated for another program and the information can be used to determine Medi-Cal eligibility. •There is a change in citizenship or immigration status. •A customer loses eligibility to a particular Medi-Cal category, e.g. aged out of Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI), Supplemental Security Income (SSI), or CalWORKs. Hard to Reach Individuals Staff must complete a CIC redetermination and advance the RE date whenever contact is made with a hard-to-reach customer who confirms the information in their case is current and correct. Examples of hard-to reach individuals include those who are: •Unsheltered or without a fixed address. •Aged, Blind, or Disabled. •Victims of natural disaster. •Living in remote areas. •Incarcerated individuals. •Migrant workers. Non-MAGI CIC To advance the annual RE date for Non-MAGI customers, current information and verification for both income and property are required. When a Non-MAGI customer reports a change in income that we are able to confirm through another case, but there is no current property information available, the income will be updated for Medi-Cal but the RE date will not be advanced. Staff will not request property verifications until renewal. CalWORKs Discontinued for No RE When a family is discontinued from CalWORKs for failure to complete the annual RE, they are placed County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageChange in Circumstances Redeterminations 04.15.02 2 of 2 on Aid Code 38, pending a Medi-Cal CIC redetermination. The following actions are required to complete a Medi-Cal evaluation: •Complete an ex parte review prior to requesting information from the customer. •Obtain the Request for Tax Household Information (RFTHI) form by phone or mail. •Run the family through the California Healthcare Eligibility, Enrollment, and Retention System (CalHEERS) Business Rule Engine (BRE) to complete the redetermination. Note: If unable to obtain by phone, staff must mail the RFTHI during the month after CalWORKs discontinuance and allow 60 days for return of the RFTHI. The RE month is set to 12 months after the month of CIC determination for Medi-Cal only. Consumer Protection Programs The annual RE date will not be reset when a customer is already active or is placed into the following consumer protection programs because of the CIC: •Continuous Eligibility for Children (CEC). •Deemed Infants. •Transitional Medi-Cal (TMC). •Continuous Eligibility (CE) for Pregnant Women. Procedure: Medi-Cal RE procedures can be found in Processing Guide 01 – Medi-Cal Annual Renewals and Change in Circumstances Redeterminations. Program Impacts: Automation See CalSAWS Tip - Medi-Cal Change in Circumstances Redetermination. References: ACWDLs 06-16, 06-17, 07-12, 08-03, 11-30, 11-23, 20-17, 25-16 MEDIL I 25-13 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by August 31, 2029. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageSetting the Annual Renewal Date 04.15.03 1 of 3 Revision Date: September 1, 2026 Background: The annual renewal (RE) is a full eligibility review that is conducted once every 12 months. The RE month in California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) is generally set 12 months from the first day of the application month. However, if the applicant is not Medi-Cal eligible in the month of application, the RE month is set 12 months from the approval month. The approval month is the first month in which the applicant meets all eligibility criteria. A change in circumstances (CIC) redetermination is completed when information is received from the customer or another program that can be used to establish ongoing Medi-Cal eligibility. Purpose: This section is revised for the sunset review; no policy or procedures have been changed. Policy: Setting the RE due month The RE date is set to 12 months from the month of approval. When Medi-Cal household members have different initial eligibility months, the RE month will be set based on when the first member was determined eligible. Disability Determination Services Division (DDSD) Applicants When an applicant claims a disability and no other Medi-Cal linkage exists, a disability packet must be sent to DDSD for evaluation. If DDSD confirms the applicant’s disability, the annual RE date will be set to 12 months from the first month of Medi-Cal eligibility. Categorically Eligible (CE) Parents receiving Medi-Cal only benefits through their California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids (CalWORKs) case are not required to complete a separate Medi-Cal only annual RE as long as they cooperate with all requirements and complete the CalWORKs annual renewal. CalWORKs Approved When a family has Medi-Cal only and later applies and is approved for CalWORKs, the RE date will be set to12 months from the CalWORKs application month for any family members that remain Medi-Cal only. Deemed Eligible Infants Infants who are receiving Medi-Cal under Deemed Eligibility (DE) will have their RE month set to that of other Medi-Cal household members. If there are no others receiving Medi-Cal only, the RE due month will be set to the month of the infant’s first birthday. Transitional Medi-Cal (TMC) Individuals receiving Medi-Cal under TMC are not required to complete an annual RE while they are receiving TMC benefits. A redetermination of eligibility for other Medi-Cal programs must be completed County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageSetting the Annual Renewal Date 04.15.03 2 of 3 by the last month of the TMC period. Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 05.07 – Transitional Medi-Cal. The RE month will be set as follows: If... then... all Medi-Cal Family Budget Unit (MFBU) members are receiving TMC and their annual RE is due before their TMC period expires, the RE month is the last month of the TMC period. Example: Original RE month: 07/11 TMC expires: 10/11 New RE month: 10/11 all MFBU members are receiving TMC and their annual RE is due after their TMC period expires, the original RE month remains. all MFBU members are receiving TMC with different TMC expiration dates, the RE month is the last month of the TMC period that will end first. •This RE month will apply to all other MFBU members. •At the end of the other MFBU member’s TMC period, eligibility must be redetermined for that individual using information from the existing case. some MFBU members are receiving TMC and others are not, the RE month of the other non-TMC MFBU members will be applied. Actions that do not Change the RE Month Once the RE month is established, the following events will not change it: •Customer submits the RE packet within 90 days after Medi-Cal has been terminated AND is found eligible. •Customer submits the RE packet more than 90 days after discontinuance date, but good cause exists AND benefits are restored without a break in aid. •The packet is returned and processed within the two months prior to the RE month. Procedure: Medi-Cal RE procedures can be found in Processing Guide 01 - Medi-Cal Annual and Change in Circumstances Redeterminations. References: ACWDLs 06-16, 06-17, 11-23, 11-33, 14-15, 14-18, 14-22, 19-17 WIC 14005.07 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by August 31, 2029. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageSetting the Annual Renewal Date 04.15.03 3 of 3 Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAnnual Renewal - Required Forms 04.15.04 1 of 2 Revision Date: September 1, 2026 Background: Renewal (RE) information is requested using forms that may be completed by phone, in person, or electronically, including telephonically recorded signatures as well as handwritten signatures transmitted via fax or email. Purpose: This section is revised for the sunset review; no policy or procedures have been changed. Policy: Acceptable Annual Renewal RE Forms Federal law requires that annual RE forms are pre-populated with case information that customers are asked to confirm or update if inaccurate. Accept any of the following forms as the Statement of Facts (SOF) for the annual RE process. Form Number Used For MC 216 Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) cases that do not auto renew. California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) will send the MC 216 to the customer. MC 210 RV Non-MAGI cases including Long Term Care (LTC). MC 217 Cases that include both MAGI and Non-MAGI aid types (mixed households). MC 250 A Former Foster Youth (FFY) who are turning 26 years old. SAWS 2 Plus Accepted as a substitute for any of the above annual RE forms. Annual RE Packet The table below identifies forms that must be included in the Medi-Cal annual RE packet: Form Number Title MC 019 MC Information Notice – Medi-Cal Information for Beneficiaries RE Statement of Facts Medi-Cal Annual Renewal Form, based on the specifics of the case MC 219 Important Information for Persons Requesting Medi-Cal 16-64 HHSA Voter Preference Form Voter Registration CA Voter Registration Form Pub 13 Your Rights Under California Public Benefits Program Pamphlet MC 372 Breast and Cervical Cancer Treatment Program (BCCTP) Brochure GEN 1365 Notice of Language Services Envelope Postage Paid Envelope 09-98 HHSA* CalFresh Flyer for Medi-Cal (for non-LTC cases) CF 285* Application for CalFresh Benefits (for non-LTC cases) 14-116 HHSA* Medi-Cal Redetermination Packet Coversheet 20-44 HHSA* Civil Rights Information 16-157-A HHSA Text Message Service Agreement N/A* San Diego Gas and Electric CARE Program Application County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAnnual Renewal - Required Forms 04.15.04 2 of 2 * Indicates county required forms Mailing Date The first step in the annual RE process is to complete an ex parte review. MAGI cases will run against the federal data hub as part of the ex parte review. When verifications are required after the ex parte review, the Medi-Cal Annual Redetermination Notice and annual RE packet are automatically mailed to the customer at least 60 days prior to the RE due date. Due Date The annual RE form is considered “timely” if the County receives it by the last day of the RE month. Forms for Non-MAGI and Low-Income Subsidy (LIS) Extra Help Households at RE The Non-MAGI Screening Packet includes the forms below and is provided to Non-MAGI and LIS Extra Help Medi-Cal customers including those who are subject to a property evaluation. Form Number Title Pub 10 Non-MAGI Medi-Cal Programs Brochure MC 604 IPS Additional Income and Property Information Needed for Medi-Cal MC 007 Medi-Cal General Property Limitations DHCS 7077 Notice Regarding Standards for Medi-Cal Eligibility DHCS 7077-A Notice Regarding Transfer of a Home for Both a Married and Unmarried Applicant/Beneficiary APTC/CSR Brochure – “Covered CA Can Help You Get Affordable Health Coverage” Postage paid pre-addressed return envelope Procedure: Medi-Cal RE procedures can be found in Processing Guide 01 - Medi-Cal Annual and Change in Circumstances Redeterminations. Program Impacts: None References: ACWDLs 06-16, 11-23, 19-17, 20-21, 20-22 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by August 31, 2029. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAnnual Renewal - Return Requirements 04.15.05 1 of 3 Revision Date: September 1, 2026 Background: Customers must return annual renewal (RE) information electronically, telephonically or through the mail. Purpose: This section is revised to include the latest RE completion flexibility related to ex parte. Policy: RE Returned Timely When the customer returns the RE forms or provides the information timely (by the last day of the RE month), staff must review them to determine whether additional information/verifications are needed to complete the eligibility determination. Additional Information is Not Needed: If … then … there are no changes reported and on-going eligibility exists, •the case is certified for a new 12-month period based on the original RE month. •the Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS) must be reviewed after the RE is complete to ensure the most recent RE information is transmitted to MEDS. the customer is determined ineligible to Non-Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI), or any MAGI group, refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 04.15.06 for additional guidance on cases transitioning between MAGI and Non-MAGI. reported changes result in the customer(s) moving from zero share of cost (SOC) to SOC Medi-Cal or a SOC increase, •the new or increased SOC is applied on the 1 st of the month for which timely notice can be given, •the customer must be provided with a notice of action (NOA) about the restoration and the change to SOC, •MEDS must be reviewed after the RE is complete to ensure the most recent RE information is transmitted to MEDS. If the customer returns incomplete forms after the NOA cutoff date but prior to the last day of the RE month, the failure to provide discontinuance must be rescinded. The customer will be notified that benefits are restored and processing of the RE must continue. Ex Parte RE Packet Requirement Flexibility This flexibility allows staff to complete the annual RE via ex parte (if successful), even after an RE packet is sent to a Medi-Cal customer. If able to verify any missing or pending information, the RE can be completed without waiting for the customer to sign and return the form. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAnnual Renewal - Return Requirements 04.15.05 2 of 3 Note: This flexibility may only be applied if there is a positive or no change to eligibility. A negative action cannot be taken based solely off an ex parte review without verification. Complete Forms but Additional Information Needed When the customer returns the RE forms timely and additional information/verifications are needed, complete an ex parte review, attempt to obtain a reasonable explanation to clarify income discrepancies, and request missing information/verifications using the Medi-Cal Request for Information form (MC 355). Allow 30 days for the return of additional information/verifications. Returned within 90 days of RE Discontinuance Date When the RE packet is returned within 90 days after the discontinuance date (for example, RE due July 2025, RE packet submitted August 10, 2025), staff must review and determine whether the customer provided all necessary information and remains Medi-Cal eligible before rescinding. If the RE packet is incomplete or only partial information is received during the 90-day cure period, a courtesy call must be made to inform the customer of what is still missing (a MC 355 is not issued). The discontinuance will only be rescinded if the verifications are received prior to the end of the period and the customer remains Medi-Cal eligible. Returned more than 90 days after RE When the RE packet is returned more than 90 days after the discontinuance date, Medi-Cal will not be restored unless it is determined the customer had good cause for not submitting the information timely and remains eligible for Medi-Cal. Good cause includes but is not limited to: •Customer is unable to read or complete the RE forms without assistance because they are not available in the written language they understand. •The postal service failed to deliver the RE packet in a timely manner. •Physical/mental illness or incapacity prevented the customer from submitting the forms in a timely manner. Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 04.21 for general information on good cause. RE Not Returned When a customer fails to return the forms or provide the information to the county by the last day of the RE month and the packet was not returned by the post office as undeliverable, the case will automatically discontinue on the last day of the RE month. Note: Two contact attempts are required prior to discontinuing for failure to cooperate with annual RE. RE Returned as Undeliverable When the RE packet is returned undeliverable by the post office, staff must make reasonable attempts to contact the customer. Prior to discontinuing the case, staff will: •Complete an ex parte review of the information available in the various systems for the customer and immediate family members* to determine the most current contact information. •Mail the MC 355 and allow the customer 30 days to provide if ex parte is unsuccessful. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAnnual Renewal - Return Requirements 04.15.05 3 of 3 •Attempt to contact the customer by phone, or their preferred method during the 30 days. •Complete a detailed journal entry that includes the following: oThe date mail was sent/returned. oThe document that was returned. oThe address that was used. •Image a copy of the Returned Mail Notification or the return envelope and its contents into the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) case. Note: For purposes of the eligibility determination, immediate family members are defined as any of the individuals who make up the Medi-Cal household. To use an address provided by immediate family members, it must be more recent than the one already on file. If the MC 355 is undeliverable or not returned by the customer, the case must be discontinued and a NOA sent that contains the missing information needed to determine eligibility, including a valid address. If the customer’s whereabouts become known, the RE packet must be sent to the new address with 30 days allowed for return. Procedure: Medi-Cal RE procedures can be found in Processing Guide 01 - Medi-Cal Annual and Change in Circumstances Redeterminations. Program Impacts: None References: ACWDLs 06-16, 07-24, 14-15, 14-18, 14-22, 16-23, 19-17 MEDIL I 25-12 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by August 31, 2029. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageTransitions between Modified Adjusted Gross Income and Non- Modified Adjusted Gross Income 04.15.06 1 of 4 Revision Date: September 1, 2026 Background: Customers who are no longer eligible for Medi-Cal under their current program must be evaluated for all other programs following the Medi-Cal hierarchy prior to being referred to Covered California. Purpose: This section is revised for the sunset review; no policy or procedures have been changed. Policy: Soft Pause Customers must be evaluated for all Non-Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) programs before they are discontinued from MAGI Medi-Cal and referred to Covered California. During the evaluation, individuals will remain in their existing MAGI aid code to the extent possible. This is referred to as a “Soft Pause”. The purpose of the Soft Pause is to protect the customer from an adverse action while they are being evaluated for Non-MAGI or other Consumer Protection Programs (CPP), including: •Continuous Eligibility for Children (CEC). •Deemed Eligible Infants (DE). •Transitional Medi-Cal (TMC). •Continuous Eligibility for Pregnant Women. •Former Foster Youth (FFY). •4-Month Continuing Medi-Cal. If for some reason the customer cannot be left in their existing aid code, they must be placed in aid code 38 for full scope or 58 for restricted benefits until the evaluation is complete. Individuals will enter Soft Pause due to a: •Move from MAGI to Advance Premium Tax Credits/Cost-Sharing Reductions (APTC/CSR). •Move from non-premium MAGI to premium MAGI. •Move from full scope MAGI to restricted scope MAGI. •Move from full scope MAGI to Pregnancy Related Medi-Cal. •Loss of MAGI eligibility for reasons such as turning 65 years old, becoming Medicare eligible, or an income increase that puts them over the income limits. The Soft Pause will be lifted after the Non-MAGI or CPP eligibility evaluation is completed. If the customer indicates they only want to be evaluated for Covered California, they must be run through the California Healthcare Eligibility, Enrollment, and Retention System (CalHEERS) Business Rules Engine (BRE) to determine eligibility. If the individual is found eligible, the Soft Pause will be lifted. The customer may contact the Covered California Service Center at (800) 300-1506 for assistance with completing the plan enrollment process. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageTransitions between Modified Adjusted Gross Income and Non- Modified Adjusted Gross Income 04.15.06 2 of 4 Non-MAGI Medi-Cal Evaluation To determine Non-MAGI eligibility, an ex parte review must be completed using all available information. When ex parte is successful, the customer will be evaluated for Non-MAGI and approved if eligible. When the customer is ineligible to Non-MAGI or would have a share of cost (SOC), they must be referred to Covered California. If eligibility cannot be determined through ex parte, the Non-MAGI Screening Packet for Beneficiaries must be mailed to the customer allowing 30 days for return: Form Number Title Pub 10 Non-MAGI Medi-Cal Programs Brochure MC 604 IPS Additional Income and Property Information Needed for Medi-Cal MC 007 Medi-Cal General Property Limitations DHCS 7077 Notice Regarding Standards for Medi-Cal Eligibility DHCS 7077-A Notice Regarding Transfer of a Home for Both a Married and Unmarried Applicant/Beneficiary APTC/CSR Brochure – “Covered CA Can Help You Get Affordable Health Coverage” Postage paid pre-addressed return envelope The customer must be contacted at least once after mailing the packet, to remind them to return the information. A detailed journal entry is required. If the MC 604 IPS information is not received after 30 days, MAGI Medi-Cal will be discontinued with a timely Notice of Action (NOA) and the Soft Pause released. The customer will be referred to Covered CA and evaluated for APTC/CSR as appropriate. If the customer provides the information prior to it taking effect, the discontinuance will be rescinded and a Non-MAGI evaluation completed. Individuals have the option of having only SOC Medi-Cal, SOC Medi-Cal and Covered California, or only Covered California. Customers who choose to discontinue their SOC Medi-Cal will be mailed a timely discontinuance NOA. Note: SOC Medi-Cal does not meet Minimum Essential Coverage (MEC). Customers Discontinued from Non-MAGI Medi-Cal Individuals who are no longer eligible to Non-MAGI as a result of an annual renewal (RE) or change in circumstances (CIC) redetermination must be evaluated for MAGI Medi-Cal prior to discontinuance if potentially eligible. This includes an ex parte review to determine if the tax household information is available in the case record. If this information is not available, a Request for Tax Household Information (RFTHI) form must be sent and the customer allowed 30 days to provide. When there is no eligibility to MAGI, the CalHEERS BRE will not be run. RFTHI The RFTHI can be completed by phone, in person, or electronically. Telephone recorded signatures as well as handwritten signatures transmitted via fax or email are accepted. The customer is not required County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageTransitions between Modified Adjusted Gross Income and Non- Modified Adjusted Gross Income 04.15.06 3 of 4 to submit any supporting documentation with the completed RFTHI form. The form is only to acquire information to be verified through the federal data hub and available state data sources. Documentation will only be required if the: •CalHEERS BRE response does not verify the information. •Electronic verification through the BRE finds the information not reasonably compatible. •Information cannot be verified via an ex parte review. When the RFTHI information is provided, staff will run the case through the CalHEERS BRE and either: •Approve MAGI if the customer is determined eligible or, •Refer to Covered California if the customer is not eligible to MAGI and discontinue the Non-MAGI Medi-Cal with timely notice. RFTHI is Missing Information or Not Returned If the RFTHI is provided, but there is not enough information to determine MAGI eligibility, the Medi- Cal Request for Information (MC 355) must be sent and the customer given 30 days to provide. If the customer does not return the RFTHI or provide the information during the 30-day period staff will: •Complete an ex parte review to attempt to verify the information. •Contact the customer by their preferred method of communication (phone or mail) and provide a 10-day deadline following the contact. •Document the attempted contact with a detailed journal entry. •Discontinue the customer with timely notice if not received. Customers have a 90-day cure period to provide the information. Information that is Not Reasonably Compatible: When the CalHEERS BRE returns results that are not reasonably compatible (for example, income) and the information is not verified via ex parte, staff will send the MC 355 to request paper verifications and allow the customer 30 days to provide. During the 30-day period, the customer must be contacted at least once via their preferred method of communication (phone or mail) to remind then to return the information. A detailed journal entry is required. If the information is provided prior to the discontinuance date, staff will rescind the discontinuance and evaluate for MAGI. When the information is not received, staff must attempt to contact the customer to obtain the information and if unsuccessful, discontinue with timely notice. Procedure: Medi-Cal RE procedures can be found in Processing Guide 01 - Medi-Cal Annual and Change in Circumstances Redeterminations. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageMixed Household Renewals 04.15.07 1 of 3 Revision Date: September 1, 2026 Background: A mixed household is defined as a household with at least one member who is receiving Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) Medi-Cal benefits and at least one member who is receiving Covered California (CA) benefits. Medi-Cal customers have their annual renewal (RE) set for 12 months from their initial application date or most recent redetermination of eligibility. Covered CA re-determines eligibility for the next benefit year during the annual open enrollment period. Purpose: This section is revised for the sunset review; no policy or procedures have been changed. Policy: Annual RE Due Date MAGI vs Covered CA Annual MAGI Medi-Cal and Covered CA REs and are separate processes that may not occur concurrently depending on the Medi-Cal RE month. The Covered CA portion of the mixed household population will have their benefits renewed every January while the Medi-Cal portion will be renewed at the annual RE due date. If the RE dates are not aligned, any changes reported on the case via the Covered CA RE will be reported to the Medi-Cal program as a change in circumstances (CIC) for the MAGI customers. Annual RE for Mixed Households with the Same Date For mixed households with the same due date, the Medi-Cal annual RE process will initiate the RE for both the MAGI and Covered CA programs. Annual REs for Mixed Household with Different Dates When a Medi-Cal RE occurs prior to the Covered CA RE, the transaction will be treated as a CIC for the Covered CA program. The RE information will be sent electronically from California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) to the California Healthcare Eligibility, Enrollment and Retention System (CalHEERS) and CalHEERS will update the customer’s Covered CA account. Those who remain eligible and enrolled in a Covered CA plan will go through the Covered CA annual RE process once it occurs. If the Covered CA RE occurs prior to the Medi-Cal RE, the Covered CA RE will be treated as a CIC for Medi-Cal eligible case members. Any new information received by Covered CA as part of their RE will be sent electronically to CalSAWS. County Responsibility for Mixed Household Processing Counties are responsible for Medi-Cal eligibility determinations and ongoing case management for mixed household cases. Covered CA customers who belong to a mixed household may complete their annual RE using several methods, including: •Completing it online in CalHEERS. •Contacting the Covered CA service center. •Contacting the County. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageMixed Household Renewals 04.15.07 2 of 3 Note: Covered CA staff are only able to complete Covered CA related information for the RE but will refer customers to the county if there are any changes reported that impact Medi-Cal eligibility. Procedure: Medi-Cal RE procedures can be found in Processing Guide 01 - Medi-Cal Annual and Change in Circumstances Redeterminations. Program Impacts: None References: ACWDL 14-38 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by August 31, 2029. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services

sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAnnual Renewal - Overview of Requirements 04.15.01 1 of 3 Revision Date: September 1, 2026 Background: Beneficiaries must have a renewal (RE) completed every 12 months to evaluate ongoing Medi-Cal eligibility. Purpose: This section is revised for the sunset review; no policy or procedures have been changed. Policy: Medi-Cal customers must have their eligibility renewed every 12 months. The Affordable Care Act (ACA) of 2010 changed the process to allow for automated annual REs, a 90-day cure period for failure to provide, advancement of the annual RE due date when a change in circumstances (CIC) occurs, and the required use of pre-populated RE forms. Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) Administrative Renewal Two months prior to the RE due month, an administrative process takes place when California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) sends Electronic Health Information Transfer (eHIT) transactions to the California Healthcare Eligibility Enrollment, and Retention System (CalHEERS) to initiate the electronic verification process for MAGI RE. If CalHEERS confirms eligibility, CalSAWS will: •Receive eligibility results from CalHEERS along with a Notice of Action (NOA). •Authorize the case during the overnight batch process. •Advance the RE date to 12 months from the original RE month. •Generate a journal entry. If CalHEERS does not confirm MAGI eligibility for all household members, CalSAWS will generate and send the pre-populated Medi-Cal Renewal form (MC 216) to the customer approximately 60 days prior to the renewal due date. Renewal Packet Required A renewal packet is required for Non-MAGI cases and MAGI cases that do not auto-renew. The customer or person authorized to act on their behalf must complete the renewal forms and provide the verifications necessary to redetermine eligibility. Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) section 04.15.03 for information on the forms required at RE. Information to be Verified The following information must be verified at RE: •Disability or blindness that is not previously known (when determining Non-MAGI linkage). •Legal responsibility for a child applying alone. •Countable income based on programs evaluated. •Status and value of non-exempt property for Non-MAGI customers. •Immigration status (if a change is reported). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAnnual Renewal - Overview of Requirements 04.15.01 2 of 3 Staff must not request information that is not relevant to ongoing eligibility or was previously provided and not subject to change such as date of birth, SSN or United States (U.S.) citizenship. Original documents are not required. Photocopies of all verifications are acceptable. Telephone Information RE information may be obtained over the phone as long as it is clearly documented in the CalSAWS case. A telephonic signature is required and the customer must be informed that they are making their statements under the penalty of perjury. Social Security Number (SSN) It is not necessary to re-verify the SSN at RE. However, if the customer’s SSN was not previously verified electronically, the customer will be given 30 days to provide verification or proof of application for the SSN. Citizenship When a customer reports a change in their citizenship status at RE, verification is required when ex parte or electronic verification is unavailable. Completion of the RE will not be delayed and the customer will be allowed a 90-day reasonable opportunity period (ROP). Income Eligibility Verification System (IEVS) An IEVS report will only generate during annual RE or CIC when there is a discrepancy. When a Recipient IEVS is received, staff must determine whether it matches the information provided by the customer. If there are no discrepancies, no further action is required.
