sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Refugee Medical and Entrant Medical Assistance Number Page 05.08.01 1 of 3 Revision Date: June 1, 2026 Background: Refugee Medical Assistance and Entrant Medical Assistance (RMA/EMA) is a special federal program that provides time limited eligibility to refugees, asylees, victims of human trafficking, domestic violence and other serious crimes, and other special immigrant/entrants who are not otherwise eligible to federally funded Medi -Cal. The program is authorized by the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) but is administered by California counties. Purpose: This section has been reformatted and revised to incorporate the Iraqi and Afghan Special Immigrants non-citizen category and to provide guidance on the new time limits for RMA/EMA that went into effect May 5, 2025. Policy: Newly admitted refugees, asylees, victims of human trafficking, and other special immigrants must be evaluated for RMA/EMA if they are determined to have no other linkage to Medi-Cal programs, including: • Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) • Non-MAGI with a Share of Cost (SOC) • California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids (CalWORKs) linked Medi-Cal • Supplemental Security Income/State Supplementary Payment (SSI/SSP) • United States (U.S.) citizen children of refugees/entrants if it decreases or eliminates their SOC Note: Households can be mixed with some individuals in RMA/EMA and others in regular Medi -Cal programs. Program Income Limits If otherwise eligible, refugees/entrants with income: • below 200% of the Federal Poverty Limit (FPL) are eligible to zero SOC Medi-Cal • over 200% of the FPL are eligible with a SOC Non-Citizen Status Applicants must meet the federal definition of “refugee” or “entrant” and provide the name of their resettlement agency and proof of status from one of the following categories: • Conditional Entrant • Refugee • Asylee • Amerasian • Iraqi and Afghan Special Immigrants (SI) • Ukrainian SI • Victim of human trafficking, domestic violence or other serious crimes • Permanent Resident Status (n ew permanent residents who were formerly in one of the categories listed above) • Cuban/Haitian Entrants County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Refugee Medical and Entrant Medical Assistance Number Page 05.08.01 2 of 3 Refer to Medi-Cal Desk Aid 78 Common Immigration Documents for a list of acceptable documentation. Time Limits The RMA/EMA time limit is established by the date of entry/admission into the U.S. The current time limits are listed in the table below. If the U.S. entry/admission date is… then the time limit is… prior to May 5, 2025, 12 months. on or after May 5, 2025, 4 months. Students in Higher Education Full-time students in an institution of higher education are ineligible for RMA/EMA unless it is part of an employability plan developed by a county welfare department, county contractor or is part of a plan for an unaccompanied minor. Income and Resources The income and resources reported at the time of signing the application are considered in the evaluation (unless there is a decrease). The following income is exempt when determining RMA/EMA eligibility: • Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) • In-kind services provided by a sponsor or resettlement agency • Resources remaining in the refugee’s/entrant’s county of origin • Sponsor’s income or resources • Income earned after the date of application RMA and Advanced Premium Tax Credits (APTC) Refugees/entrants with income above the MAGI 138% FPL and below 200% FPL are potentially eligible to zero SOC Medi-Cal and APTC simultaneously and must be offered the opportunity to either enroll in APTC or continue with zero SOC Medi-Cal for their remaining RMA/EMA time limit. title: Section 10 - Pickle Benefits
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page Pickle Special Notice Report (503 Lead File Report) 05.10.01 1 of 2 Revision Date: 12/01/2019 Background: The Lynch v. Rank court order mandates specific requirements for both the DHCS and County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency related to identification, maintenance of lists, annual notification and review of individuals potentially eligible to Pickle benefits. In addition to the reformatting, this section has been revised for clarification. Policy: A. Actions Taken SSA Actions During the month of December each year, the Social Security Administration (SSA) notifies DHCS of all SSI/SSP recipients scheduled for discontinuance as a result of the Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA). These beneficiaries must be evaluated for no Share of Cost (SOC) Medi-Cal, through the Pickle Amendment. DHCS Actions DHCS will initiate extended Medi-Cal benefits for all persons on the report provided by SSA by placing these beneficiaries in Craig v. Bonta aid codes; 1E aged, 2E blind or 6E disabled. During the last two weeks of December, DHCS sends the Pickle Amendment Notice (Pickle Annual Stuffer) to Medi-Cal beneficiaries on the SSA discontinuance report. The notice advises individuals that they may be eligible to Medi-Cal benefits without a share of cost (SOC) under the Pickle Amendment and to contact their county social services office to apply. County Actions By the first or second week of January, DHCS sends the Pickle Special Notice (SN) report of all individuals discontinued from SSI/SSP due to the Title II COLA to the county. These beneficiaries are also placed on the county’s Exception Eligibles report and will remain on the report until a Pickle Amendment review or an ABD Medi-Cal Linkage determination has been completed. Procedures: B. Review Procedures A Pickle Amendment evaluation is mandatory for every individual on the Pickle SN report. An individual may also contact the county to request a Pickle evaluation. Medi-Cal programs under this Amendment are: •Pickle •Disabled Adult Children (DAC) •Disabled Widow(er) (DW) It is important to screen for potential eligibility for all three programs. If the individual is eligible to Pickle, DAC or DW at the same time, grant the DAC program first. When the individual doesn’t meet the criteria for Pickle, DAC, or DW, review for other Medi-Cal program eligibility. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page Pickle Special Notice Report (503 Lead File Report) 05.10.01 2 of 2 C. Pickle Amendment Review A Pickle Amendment eligibility review is required: •At initial application •At redetermination •In the month after a Social Security Title II COLA •Upon request •Following a break in aid The only exceptions are those individuals discontinued by SSA due to death or are incarcerated in a correctional facility. Program Impacts: The report is loaded into SharePoint by Automation for processing. References: ACWDL 02-05, 10-02 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 12/31/2022 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operation County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page Pickle Amendment Notice (Pickle Annual Stuffer) 05.10.02 1 of 2 Revision Date: 12/01/2019 Background: In December of each year, DHCS mails Pickle Annual Stuffer notices to active Medi-Cal beneficiaries in aid codes 14, 17, 24, 64, and 67 who: •Currently receive Title II Retirement, Survivor’s and Disability Insurance Social Security Benefits •Have been discontinued from the SSI/SSP program in the last three years •Were determined ineligible during the Pickle screening process the previous year The Pickle stuffer notice informs these beneficiaries to contact the county if they would like to apply for zero SOC Medi-Cal through the Pickle Amendment. This section has been reformatted and procedures moved to Processing Guide 29. Policy: The beneficiaries who receive the Pickle Annual Stuffer are aged, blind, and disabled and must be evaluated for Medi-Cal eligibility through the Pickle amendment. When determined ineligible, evaluate for all other ABD linked Medi-Cal Programs. A. Annual Pickle Amendment Reviews By terms of the Lynch v. Rank court order, the Pickle Amendment reviews must be completed during the months of January through March of each year. Each potentially eligible Pickle individual must receive a Pickle Medi-Cal notice from DHCS for three consecutive years. One year of ineligibles will be purged each year. Persons on the Pickle SN report must have their eligibility to Pickle reevaluated each year at the time of the annual Title II COLA. The individual’s name will appear on the Pickle SN report when a Pickle determination was not completed in the previous year or the individual was not eligible for Pickle through the Pickle Amendment for the previous year. The avenues in which the staff are notified to process individuals on the Pickle SN report are: 1) The Pickle SN report is uploaded to Share Point by Automation 2) Individual brings their Pickle amendment notice in to the FRC 3) Individual calls Access with questions about the Pickle amendment notice Procedures: Screen the individual for potential Pickle eligibility and determine if the beneficiary has an active county Medi-Cal case. Follow the procedures outlined in Processing Guide 29. When the Pickle determination is complete. Submit a HHSA 14-28 MEDS On-Line Request, checking the “Remove Pickle Indicator” box. This removes the individuals name from the Pickle SN report for the next year. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page Pickle Amendment Notice (Pickle Annual Stuffer) 05.10.02 2 of 2 Program Impacts: None References: California Code of Regulations (CCR) Title 22, Section 50247 ACWDL 87-75, 94-86, 95-45, 06-31, 10-01 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 12/31/2022 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page Pickle Program 05.10.03 1 of 3 Revision Date: 12/01/2019 Background: The Craig v. Bonta court order mandates individuals discontinued from SSI/SSP continue to receive full scope, zero SOC Medi-Cal until an eligibility determination is completed. Basic Medi-Cal eligibility requirements addressed in this section cover only those eligibility requirements that are different for Pickle eligible individuals and must be followed when evaluating the Pickle program. Included with the reformatting, this section has been revised to provide clarifications to the Pickle program. Policy: A. Pickle Eligibility Criteria An individual must meet all of the following criteria to be eligible to Pickle: •Currently receiving Social Security II benefits •Received Social Security Title II and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) and/or State Supplementary Payment (SSP) benefits simultaneously in any month after April 1977 •Discontinued from SSI/SSP after April 1977 •Received a Social Security Title II Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) since being discontinued from SSI/SSP and would be entitled to receive SSI/SSP benefits if the COLA was disregarded B. Pickle Handbook The DHCS issued Pickle Handbook sections, referenced in Desk Aid 92, include information and instructions necessary to determine Pickle eligibility and comply with the Craig v. Bonta and Lynch v. Rank court orders. C. Worksheets and Notice Of Action (NOA) Reminders •A NOA is required when approving or discontinuing Pickle, DAC, and DW benefits •If a NOA does not generate, a manual NOA must be used and saved in the case file •The Pickle Amendment worksheets are in the Electronic Forms Repository (EFR) and on the DHCS forms website, the NOAs are located on the MEDS Homepage EFR/DHCS Website DHCS 7019 Financial Eligibility Worksheet (Pickle Child) DHCS 7020 Screening Worksheet DHCS 7021 Financial Eligibility Worksheet DHCS 7029 Pickle Disregard Computation DHCS 7037 Pickle Resources Worksheet DHCS 7044 Statement of Living Arrangements DHCS 7075 Pickle Needs Test MC 210B Supplemental to Statement of Facts (Pickle) County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page Pickle Program 05.10.03 2 of 3 MEDS Homepage DHCS 7026 Denial/Discontinuance (Pickle/DAC) DHCS 7027 Pickle/DAC Approval D. Screening Process The steps below are followed when evaluating for Pickle, DAC, and DW: Step 1 Screen individuals for Age, Blindness, or Disability Step 2 Identify receipt of Social Security Title II income Step 3 Review MEDS Pickle Tickler Field Step 4 Review Program Specific Criteria Step 5 Determine eligibility Step 6 Notices of Action and Case Narratives E. Pickle Amendment Property Rules The Property rules used for Pickle, DAC, and DW are based on SSI rules. The treatment of property is very similar to traditional Medi-Cal with a few differences. The differences include: •Individuals cannot spend down excess property to become eligible within the month •Property Limits oPickle Couple $3,000 oPickle Individual $2,000 oPickle Child – Allow the property limit for his/her parents of $3,000 and then allow the property limit for an individual of $2,000 DHCS 7037 form may be used to evaluate the Pickle individual’s property. The table below shows definitions of certain items of property. These items are excluded from the property reserve, regardless of their value. Term Definition Examples Household Goods Items of personal property, found in or near the home that are used on a regular basis; and items needed by the householder for maintenance, use and occupancy of the premises as a home. Furniture, appliances, electronic equipment, personal computers, television sets, carpets, cooking and eating utensils, and dishes. Personal Effects Items of personal property ordinarily worn or carried by the individual and articles otherwise having an intimate relation to the individual. Clothing, personal jewelry, wedding and engagement rings, books, musical instruments, items of cultural or religious significance, prosthetic devices, and wheelchairs. Items acquired or held because of their value or as an investment are not considered household goods or personal effects for purposes of this exclusion. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page Pickle Program 05.10.03 3 of 3 F. Items of Unusual Value There is no property limit for items of unusual value. Procedures: G. Pickle Program Income The income computation for Pickle, DAC, and DW varies for each program. The Pickle Disregard Computation determines the dollar amount to be disregarded from the Social Security Title II benefit amount due to the COLA. See Processing Guide 29 for Pickle procedures. Program Impacts: None References: California Code of Regulations (CCR) Title 22, Section 50247 ACWDL 05-28 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 12/31/2022 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page Disabled Adult Children (DAC) Program 05.10.04 1 of 2 Revision Date: 12/01/2019 Background: Public Law 99-643 amended the Social Security Act to provide categorical zero SOC Medi-Cal to a limited group of former SSI/SSP recipients who receive Title II benefits as "Disabled Adult Children." These persons’ eligibility must be determined through the Pickle Amendment using DAC rules. Included in the reformatting, this section is being updated to align with Pickle Handbook Section 6 - DAC, and the procedures moved to Processing Guide 29. Policy: A. DAC Eligibility Criteria In order to be eligible to the Medi-Cal DAC program the individual must: •Be at least 18 years old •Deemed disabled by Social Security before 22 years of age •Previously received SSI/SSP benefits on the basis of blindness or disability, which began before reaching 22 years of age •Actively receiving Retirement, Survivors, Disability Insurance (RSDI) childhood disability benefits due to their disability •Discontinued from SSI/SSP due to becoming eligible on or after July 1, 1987 to RSDI childhood disability benefits or because of an increase to those benefits B. Exception to Title II COLA Requirement Persons identified by DHCS as potentially eligible to Medi-Cal though the Pickle amendment under the Disabled Adult Children (DAC) rules, are not required to have received a Title II COLA since their discontinuance from SSI/SSP. Note: Beneficiaries who are discontinued from SSI/SSP due to admission to a long-term care facility will not be included in the DAC extended eligibility process. Important Reminder – Screen for potential eligibility for all three programs; Pickle, DAC, and DW. If the individual is eligible to Pickle, DAC, and DW at the same time, grant the DAC program first. C. Notifications The Pickle amendment notice sent by DHCS, informs these individuals that they are eligible to a Medi-Cal evaluation under the Pickle Amendment. MPG 05.10.02 A NOA is required when approving or discontinuing Pickle, DAC, and DW benefits. MPG 05.10.03 D. Screening Process When screening for Pickle, DAC, and DW, follow the steps in MPG 05.10.03. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page Disabled Adult Children (DAC) Program 05.10.04 2 of 2 E. Pickle Amendment Property Rules The Property rules used for Pickle, DAC, and DW are based on SSI rules. See MPG 05.10.03 for the treatment of property when evaluating for DAC. Procedures: F. DAC Income Determination When determining DAC eligibility: •Disregard the entire amount of Social Security Title II income received as childhood disability benefits •Disregard any subsequent COLA received as childhood disability benefits when completing the Pickle Needs Test worksheet •Include any income from any other sources when completing the budget worksheet See Processing Guide 29 for Pickle procedures. Program Impacts: None References: California Code of Regulations (CCR) Title 22, Section 50247 ACWDL 93-30, 94-86, 02-05, 10-01 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 12/31/2022 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page COBRA Disabled Widows (DW) 05.10.05 1 of 2 Revision Date: 12/01/2019 Background: The Consolidated Omnibus Reconciliation Act of 1985 (COBRA '85) established criteria to be used in restoring and continuing Medi-Cal eligibility for disabled widows if their 1983 RSDI COLA resulted in a loss of their eligibility for SSI/SSP payments. Included in the reformatting, this section is being revised to align with previous sections for clarity, and the procedures moved to Processing Guide 29. Policy: A. DW Eligibility Criteria Individuals must meet all of the following criteria to be eligible to DW program: •Between the ages of 50 - 64 •Eligible for and currently receiving any widow(er)s benefits under Title II Section 202 •Not entitled to Medicare Part A hospital insurance •Ineligible for SSI/SSP benefits due to the receipt of Title II widow(er)s benefits. B. Consolidated Omnibus Reconciliation Act (COBRA) COBRA 1985 Persons who met the criteria for zero SOC Medi-Cal under COBRA '85 provisions were given a deadline of July 1, 1988 to apply at their local welfare department. Although no COBRA applications were received in San Diego County, there is the possibility that a COBRA '85 Medi-Cal beneficiary could move to San Diego County and request transfer of his/her case. In this event, Pickle Handbook, Section 5 specifies information which must be provided from the original county of responsibility to San Diego County. C. Omnibus Reconciliation Act (OBRA) OBRA 1987 The Omnibus Reconciliation Act of 1987 (OBRA '87) amended the Social Security Act to extend Medi-Cal coverage to a new group of disabled widow(er) s. The amendment allows DW between the ages of 60 and 64 who lose SSI/SSP benefits as a result of becoming entitled to or receiving an increase in Title II benefits, to continue their Medi-Cal eligibility until they become eligible for Part A Medicare benefits. Eligibility under this provision was effective July 1, 1988. Unlike COBRA '85 legislation, OBRA '87 does not establish an application deadline for potential eligibles. Potential OBRA '87 eligible DW are notified in their SSI/SSP discontinuance notice of their potential eligibility and are advised to apply at their local welfare department. OBRA 1990 The Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1990 (OBRA-90) created a new group of Medi-Cal eligibles. Section 5103 of OBRA-90 extended Medi-Cal coverage to disabled widows age 50-59 that become ineligible to SSI/SSP benefits because of entitlement to or an increase in certain Title II widows insurance benefits. OBRA-90 mandated zero SOC Medi-Cal coverage for this group of disabled widows until Medicare begins for them. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page COBRA Disabled Widows (DW) 05.10.05 2 of 2 D. Alert Messages and Notifications DWs become eligible for Medicare Part A two years after the onset of disability. At that time, they become ineligible for the DW program. Beginning in December 1994, the DHCS Data System Branch sends MEDS alert messages concerning DW individuals who need to be terminated in two months from the DW program because of the impending receipt of Medicare Part A. These individuals are re-evaluated under another Medi-Cal program. The alert message will read, "Medicare Part A in Two Months: Re-evaluate for other category." A NOA is required when approving or discontinuing Pickle, DAC, and DW benefits. MPG 05.10.03 E. Screening Process When screening for Pickle, DAC, and DW, follow the steps in MPG 05.10.03. F. Pickle Amendment Property Rules The Property rules used for Pickle, DAC, and DW are based on SSI rules. See MPG 05.10.03 for the treatment of property when evaluating for DAC. G. DW Financial Eligibility Determination The individual is first evaluated to determine potential eligibility for the DW program. When determining DW eligibility: •Disregard the entire amount of the Title II, Section 202 benefits only - Form DHCS 7089 (Screening Worksheet) oTitle II, Section 223 (disability) payments are to be counted •Use the SSI/SSP payment standard that is in effect for the month that eligibility is being determined – MPG 11.01A Procedures: Refer to Processing Guide 29 References: California Code of Regulations (CCR) Title 22, Section 50247 ACWDL 93-30, 94-86, 02-05, 10-01 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 12/31/2022 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page Title II and Title XVI Overlapping Payments 05.10.06 1 of 1 Revision Date: 12/01/2019 Background: Effective December 1, 1987, a change in rules for overlapping Title II SSA disability and Title XVI (SSI/SSP) payments was made. If the person is granted SSI/SSP first, and Title II benefits are approved several months later retroactively, that person is still potentially Pickle eligible. This section has been reformatted, no other changes have been made. Policy: In these instances, the Pickle applicant may have been required to reimburse the SSI/SSP program for any benefits received; however, he/she is still to be considered to have been eligible for and entitled to receive both SSA and SSI/SSP in the same month. This provision does not apply to persons who are determined ineligible for SSI/SSP for reasons other than receipt of SSA benefits. Example: Jack Overlap applied for SSI/SSP and SSA disability on June 19, 1990. The Social Security Administration computed and approved the SSI/SSP grant before computing the SSA payments. Consequently, Jack began receiving SSI/SSP benefits effective June 19, 1990. His SSA benefits were approved in October 1992 with an effective date of June 1990. It was determined that his SSA payments were marginally more than his SSI/SSP payments. As a result, his SSI/SSP benefits were discontinued effective October 31, 1992, and he was required to pay back the SSI/SSP received. Jack is considered to be potentially Pickle eligible at the time of the January 1993 SSA cost of living increase and a Pickle Amendment eligibility determination must be completed. Program Impacts: None References: California Code of Regulations (CCR) Title 22, Section 50247 ACWDL 93-30, 94-86, 10-01, 02-05 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 12/31/2022 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations

title: Section 11 - Medi-Cal Coverage Foster Care and AAP-AAC
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAdoption Assistance Payments (AAP), Foster Care, Kinship- Guardian Assistance Program (KinGAP), and Unaccompanied Refugee Minor (URM) 5.11.01 1 of 4 Revision Date: September 1, 2022 Background: Children who have been adopted from foster care, placed in foster care supervision, or unaccompanied refugee minors, may be eligible for Medi-Cal. This section provides policies to determine Medi-Cal eligibility for these children. Purpose: This section is updated to provide clarification regarding out of state non-Title IV-E Foster Care placements in California (CA). Policy: Basic Criteria: To receive Medi-Cal under any aid code children must meet the following basic Medi-Cal criteria: 1. Meet institutional status requirements (Article 6 and Medi-Cal Eligibility Procedures Manual (MEPM) 6D). •Children placed at Napa State Hospital (a public mental institution under Welfare and Institutions Code (WIC) Sections 601 and 300) are under medical care, and not custodial care and may be eligible for Medi-Cal. •Custodial care means maintenance provided by a psychiatric institution to individuals whose condition does not warrant medical treatment. •Medical treatment includes psychotherapy, counseling, rehabilitation training, or other forms of medical treatment. 2. Not be under a penal hold. Because of the complexity of the penal system and the many types of penal holds certain clarifications are addressed below. They are not all inclusive and variations must be clarified on an individual basis. Hold Type Clarification Under Arrest Children, who have committed crimes, and who are detained and admitted to hospitals or held in Juvenile Hall (detained under WIC Section 602) prior to and/or after a detention order being signed, are under arrest. Medical treatment involving minor children requires legal consent of either the parent/guardian or some other agency or individual who has authority to give such consent. A law enforcement agency cannot obtain such authority without one of the following: •Placing the child under arrest •The parents formally surrendering their authority to the law enforcement agency •Court action. Hold Pending Hearing, Arraignment, Trial, or Sentencing Children released on bail are not considered “held” unless bail is revoked. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAdoption Assistance Payments (AAP), Foster Care, Kinship- Guardian Assistance Program (KinGAP), and Unaccompanied Refugee Minor (URM) 5.11.01 2 of 4 Serving a Sentence •Children who are placed on parole or probation pursuant to a dispositional order under WIC Section 602 are not considered to be under a penal hold and may be eligible to Medi-Cal. They may be in Juvenile Hall awaiting placement in a Foster Care or group home or placed in a youth service program (for example, Rite of Passage or Boys Republic). •Children sentenced to serve terms under the California Youth Authority or sentenced to specific time to be spent in Honor Camps are under a penal hold and ineligible to Medi-Cal. •Children sentenced to a term of incarceration who are temporarily placed in a Foster Home pending available space in the detention center are ineligible to Medi-Cal. Placement in Mental Institution Under a Pre- Trial or Pre-Sentencing Observation Order or Who Are Sentenced to Such an Institution •Children placed at Camarillo or other State Hospitals must be evaluated to determine if they are still under a penal hold (ineligible) or have been placed on probation (potential eligibility). •Children discontinued from Medi-Cal under any program must be evaluated for eligibility under other Medi-Cal programs. Adoption Assistance Payments (AAP): Children may receive a federally funded adoption assistance subsidy under Title IV-E or a statefunded subsidy per state guidelines. Payments to the parents of an eligible child with special needs can take the form of either one-time (nonrecurring) or ongoing (recurring) adoption assistance. Children receiving AAP payments are not always eligible to receive Medi-Cal if residing in California. AAP children from another state residing in California may receive Medi-Cal and must be assessed individually and, if eligible, granted under the appropriate Interstate Compact on Adoption and Medical Assistance (ICAMA) aid code. The dependent status of the child is not a factor in determining Medi-Cal eligibility. Each child is in his/her own Medi-Cal Family Budget Unit (MFBU). The income and resources of the parents and siblings are not considered in the child’s Medi-Cal eligibility determination. AFDC-Foster Care (FC): Children placed in foster care supervision may receive a federally funded payment under Title IV-E or a state-funded, non-Title IV-E payment per state guidelines. Some children might not be eligible for a payment, but might still be eligible for Medi-Cal. Children placed under foster care supervision are not always eligible to receive Medi-Cal. Each case must be assessed individually and, if eligible, granted under the appropriate aid code. The dependent status of the child is not a factor in determining Medi-Cal eligibility. Each child is in his/her own MFBU. The income and resources of the parents and siblings are not considered in the child’s Medi-Cal eligibility determination. Non-foster care children from out of state placed in a CA medical and mental health facility, boarding school, educational institution, or other parent or legal guardian’s home is considered a CA resident and potentially eligible to Medi-Cal. Kinship-Guardian Assistance Program (KinGAP): KinGAP establishes a separate payment rate for children who are leaving the foster care system and are placed with relatives who obtain guardianship. KinGAP consists of two components – a federally-funded component and a state-funded component. To qualify for the KinGAP Program, a child must have: •Been removed from the parental home pursuant to a voluntary placement agreement or the result of a judicial determination to the effect that continuation in the home would be contrary to the welfare of the child and been adjudged a dependent child of the juvenile court pursuant to WIC Section 300, or a ward of the juvenile court pursuant to WIC Section 601 or 602 •Been residing for at least 6 consecutive months in the approved home of the relative while under the jurisdiction of the juvenile court or under a voluntary placement agreement or of a previously approved relative guardian •A written binding agreement entered into by the relative guardian and the county welfare agency, probation department, or Title IV-E tribal agency, prior to the establishment of the guardianship •A kinship guardianship established pursuant to WIC Sections 366.26, 360, or 728(d), and dependency dismissed pursuant to WIC Section 366.3, or wardship terminated pursuant to WIC Section 738(e) concurrently or subsequently to the establishment of the kinship guardianship. Each KinGAP child is in his/her own MFBU, even if there are other siblings or a needy caretaker relative in the home. Unaccompanied Refugee Minor (URM): The Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) provides full scope Medi-Cal without a share of cost to children in the URM Program, if otherwise eligible. The URM Program provides culturally and linguistically appropriate child welfare, foster care, and independent living services to minors who do not have parents in the United States (U.S.), or who enter the U.S. unaccompanied by a parent, an immediate adult relative, or an adult having documentable legal evidence of custody of the minor. These children are placed into the URM Program by the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR). URM children do not enter the state’s child welfare system because they are not usually removed from the home of a parent or legal guardian due to abuse, neglect, or through a voluntary agreement. For Medi-Cal purposes, URM children are treated like foster care children. Unlike foster care regulations, ORR regulations do not require that URM children be placed in the care and custody of the state. ORR regulations require states to ensure legal responsibility, including legal custody and/or County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAdoption Assistance Payments (AAP), Foster Care, Kinship- Guardian Assistance Program (KinGAP), and Unaccompanied Refugee Minor (URM) 5.11.01 4 of 4 guardianship, is established for each URM child. This section provides the policies to determine Medi-Cal eligibility for these children. Purpose: This section is added for the Unaccompanied Refugee Minor (URM) requirements. Policy: URM Application Process: Social Workers (SWs) from the URM service providers submit Medi-Cal applications to the County on behalf of children placed with their agency in the URM Program. Typically, Medi-Cal applications that are mailed in will be accompanied by a coversheet that identifies the individual applying as a representative of the URM service provider. In addition, the application must include an approval letter from ORR to confirm that the child is a federal URM Program participant, if the child is in any of the following immigration statuses: •Asylee •Cuban/Haitian entrant •Victim of human trafficking (T visa) •Non-citizen victims of domestic violence and other serious crimes who have been granted a U visa •Youth who have been granted Special Immigration Juvenile Status The ORR does not provide URM youth who are in refugee status with an approval letter. The SW will provide a verification letter from CDSS as proof of URM Program eligibility for refugees. Because URM youth are to be treated like foster care children for Medi-Cal eligibility purposes, the Medi-Cal application must include the following: •A completed MC 250/MC 250A form •A copy of the URM Designation letter from ORR or URM Approval letter from CDSS Other information needed for the case record includes: •A SSN (Note: Do not delay or deny services for otherwise eligible URM youth who fail to furnish their SSN. If an applicant has not been issued a SSN, normal rules for obtaining a SSN apply. Update the MEDS record when SSN information is provided.) •Immigration status information and/or an immigration document (Note: Do not delay or deny services for otherwise eligible URM youth who fail to furnish their immigration status. Update the MEDS record when immigration status is provided.) Medi-Cal Eligibility and Immigration Status Information: All eligible children in California under the age of 19 receive full scope Medi-Cal regardless of immigration status, but verification of immigration status is still required for children with satisfactory County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageUnaccompanied Refugee Minor (URM) 5.11.02 2 of 4 immigration status (SIS) because State law requires the department to maximize federal financial participation to the fullest extent possible. Verify the immigration status of URM youth using the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) system unless the Federal Data Services Hub, via the California Healthcare Eligibility, Enrollment and Retention System (CalHEERS), has already verified their status. Immigration status information or an immigration document for the URM youth will be provided along with the URM designee letter when available. Youth in the URM Program are eligible to full scope Medi-Cal regardless of immigration status. If immigration status information is not available at the time of application, do not delay establishing eligibility during the verification process if the URM youth is otherwise eligible. Nevertheless, if the immigration status of a URM applicant cannot be verified at the time of application, follow up with the service provider. Verify the immigration status of URM youth in accordance with policy. County of Responsibility: For purposes of Medi-Cal eligibility, the county of responsibility for URM youth is the county in which the youth resides. Therefore, the instructions on the back of the MC 250 form do not apply to URM cases. Foster Care Maintenance Payments: Youth in the URM Program do not receive assistance payments through the counties. The only benefits URM youth will access through the county is Medi-Cal under aid code 45 or 4M. All other services and benefits are provided through the URM service providers. These URM services are funded through ORR, through CDSS administered contracts with the three URM Program service providers. Extended Foster Care: URM youth are eligible for the URM version of extended foster care if they are between the ages of 18 and 21, and meet all eligibility requirements. URM youth who do not meet extended foster care eligibility requirements should be placed into aid code 45 for Medi-Cal purposes. Former Foster Youth: URM youth who meet Former Foster Youth (FFY) Program eligibility requirements are eligible to continue receiving full scope Medi-Cal under the FFY Program. When the worker learns that a FFY eligible URM youth has exited their URM placement (at age 18 or older), the worker will transition the youth into the Medi-Cal program for FFY and assign the 4M aid code even if the youth’s whereabouts are unknown. When URM youth age out of the FFY Program at age 26, follow the FFY age out process. Annual Redetermination: Follow Medi-Cal Foster Care and FFY annual redetermination rules for the URM youth. At annual redetermination, contact the URM service provider for individuals who are not in the FFY Program. The service provider must verify URM Program eligibility status prior to complete an annual redetermination. When the worker is notified of a change in circumstances resulting in a youth exiting URM foster care placement between 18 and 21 years of age, or when the URM youth turns 21 years of age, use the MC 250A form and transition the youth into aid code 4M. Upon transition into aid code 4M, send out the Notice of Action (NOA) MC 239 FFY-4, informing the beneficiary of continued Medi-Cal coverage. Also use this NOA to inform youth exiting foster care at age 18, or older, that they have been automatically moved into the FFY Program. Once the URM youth is transitioned into aid code 4M, send the NOA MC 239 FFY-3 at annual redetermination, advising them of their continued enrollment in the FFY Program. Even if the NOA is returned to the County due to loss of contact, the youth must be left in 4M, until age 26. When there is a loss of contact with a 4M beneficiary, move the youth into fee-for-service Medi-Cal if they are in a managed care plan. Because there is no MEDS transaction for workers to move a beneficiary from managed care to fee-for-service Medi-Cal, submit these requests to the Medi-Cal Managed Care Division Office of the Ombudsman. Do not terminate eligibility for aid codes 45 or 4M provided to URM youth prior to age 26 unless it is verified that the youth is deceased or not a California resident. If a URM youth is a Medi-Cal beneficiary on the date he/she becomes an inmate of a public institution, Medi-Cal benefits are suspended; not terminated. URM Beneficiaries and Managed Care: The Medi-Cal provided the URM youth is fee-for-service Medi-Cal or optional managed care. This means that URM youth in non-County Organized Health System counties, are in fee-for-service Medi- Cal unless they opt into a managed care plan. URM beneficiaries receiving fee-for-service Medi-Cal will not receive a Health Care Options (HCO) packet unless one is requested. If the individual chooses to opt into a managed care plan, he/she will need to select a health care provider. To join a managed care plan, or to get more information about a managed care plan, direct beneficiaries or the service providers to contact HCO at 1-800-430-4263 or Health San Diego at 619-515-6584. Inter-County Transfers: Follow Medi-Cal Inter-County Transfer (ICT) rules for URM beneficiaries. Do not use the Foster Care ICT process for the URM population. Medi-Cal URM youth or their service provider must promptly notify the County of any change in circumstances including a change in county of residence. Upon notification of a change in county of residence, initiate an ICT. The original county of residence must County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageUnaccompanied Refugee Minor (URM) 5.11.02 4 of 4 update MEDS to reflect necessary changes to the Current Residence Address and Res-County date fields. Do not require the URM service provider to submit a new application for Medi-Cal in the new county of residence for a URM beneficiary who is already on Medi-Cal. The case will remain active in the sending county until the receiving county has taken over the record. Counties must work together to ensure there is no break in coverage or benefits during the transition from one county to another. Purpose: This section is re-written in the new format. Policy: When retroactive Medi-Cal is requested for a child placed in California by another state, obtain the following information, if not already obtained, from the placing state: •Date the child moved to California •Written verification that the child is federally eligible for AAP or AFDC-FC. The statement must include the following: oName of child and of the adoptive/foster parent oChild’s SSN, date of birth, and address oCertification of Title IV-E federal eligibility to AAP/AFDC-FC oTermination date of Medicaid benefits from the placing state oOHC oFor AAP cases, the adoption agreement termination/renewal date and a statement that the adoption agreement is on file with the placing state. oFor AFDC-FC cases, the name of the agency in the placing state with responsibility for care and custody of the child and verification that the child is receiving an AFDC-FC grant. Do not grant retroactive Medi-Cal prior to the month the child moved to California, or three months prior to the month the MC 250 is dated, whichever is later. Procedure: Follow the rules above to determine eligibility for Medi-Cal for children in these programs. Program Impacts: Other Programs Affected Foster Care References: Title 22, Sections 50148, 50193, and 50197 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 9/30/2021. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations

sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAdoption Assistance Payments (AAP), Foster Care, Kinship- Guardian Assistance Program (KinGAP), and Unaccompanied Refugee Minor (URM) 5.11.01 1 of 4 Revision Date: September 1, 2022 Background: Children who have been adopted from foster care, placed in foster care supervision, or unaccompanied refugee minors, may be eligible for Medi-Cal. This section provides policies to determine Medi-Cal eligibility for these children. Purpose: This section is updated to provide clarification regarding out of state non-Title IV-E Foster Care placements in California (CA). Policy: Basic Criteria: To receive Medi-Cal under any aid code children must meet the following basic Medi-Cal criteria: 1. Meet institutional status requirements (Article 6 and Medi-Cal Eligibility Procedures Manual (MEPM) 6D). •Children placed at Napa State Hospital (a public mental institution under Welfare and Institutions Code (WIC) Sections 601 and 300) are under medical care, and not custodial care and may be eligible for Medi-Cal. •Custodial care means maintenance provided by a psychiatric institution to individuals whose condition does not warrant medical treatment. •Medical treatment includes psychotherapy, counseling, rehabilitation training, or other forms of medical treatment. 2. Not be under a penal hold. Because of the complexity of the penal system and the many types of penal holds certain clarifications are addressed below. They are not all inclusive and variations must be clarified on an individual basis. Hold Type Clarification Under Arrest Children, who have committed crimes, and who are detained and admitted to hospitals or held in Juvenile Hall (detained under WIC Section 602) prior to and/or after a detention order being signed, are under arrest. Medical treatment involving minor children requires legal consent of either the parent/guardian or some other agency or individual who has authority to give such consent. A law enforcement agency cannot obtain such authority without one of the following: •Placing the child under arrest •The parents formally surrendering their authority to the law enforcement agency •Court action. Hold Pending Hearing, Arraignment, Trial, or Sentencing Children released on bail are not considered “held” unless bail is revoked. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAdoption Assistance Payments (AAP), Foster Care, Kinship- Guardian Assistance Program (KinGAP), and Unaccompanied Refugee Minor (URM) 5.11.01 2 of 4 Serving a Sentence •Children who are placed on parole or probation pursuant to a dispositional order under WIC Section 602 are not considered to be under a penal hold and may be eligible to Medi-Cal. They may be in Juvenile Hall awaiting placement in a Foster Care or group home or placed in a youth service program (for example, Rite of Passage or Boys Republic). •Children sentenced to serve terms under the California Youth Authority or sentenced to specific time to be spent in Honor Camps are under a penal hold and ineligible to Medi-Cal. •Children sentenced to a term of incarceration who are temporarily placed in a Foster Home pending available space in the detention center are ineligible to Medi-Cal. Placement in Mental Institution Under a Pre- Trial or Pre-Sentencing Observation Order or Who Are Sentenced to Such an Institution •Children placed at Camarillo or other State Hospitals must be evaluated to determine if they are still under a penal hold (ineligible) or have been placed on probation (potential eligibility). •Children discontinued from Medi-Cal under any program must be evaluated for eligibility under other Medi-Cal programs. Adoption Assistance Payments (AAP): Children may receive a federally funded adoption assistance subsidy under Title IV-E or a statefunded subsidy per state guidelines. title: Section 12 - Special No-Cost Programs for Pregnant Women and Children
content: Article 5 Section 12 – Special Zero Share-of-Cost Programs for Children and Pregnant Women Table of Contents TITLE MPG CITE Overview 05.12.01 Income Disregard Program and the Asset Waiver Provision 05.12.02 133% Program 05.12.03 100% Program 05.12.04 Targeted Low-Income Children’s Program 05.12.05 Property Disregard 05.12.06 Long Term Care 05.12.07 Income Treatment and Deductions 05.12.08 Miscellaneous 05.12.09 Desk Aids and Processing Guidelines RESOURCE TITLE Processing Guidelines • TLICP CalWIN Entries Desk Aid • Children’s Special Zero SOC Program Aid Codes • Period of Eligibility • Children’s Special Zero SOC Program Flow Chart • Children’s Special Zero SOC Q & A LMS Training • Targeted Low Income Training (Type “TLICP” on the LMS search field to register and complete the training.) 05.12.01 Overview A. Overview This section provides regulations for the following programs which are applicable to cases that contain children (ages 0-19) and/or pregnant women: •Income Disregard •133% Program •100% Program ACWDL 12-33 •Targeted Low Income Children’s Program (TLICP) MPG LTR 771 (12/12) 05.12.02 Income Disregard A. Overview The Income Disregard Program provides zero share-of-cost Medi-Cal coverage to eligible infants under the age of one year and pregnant women. To qualify for the Income Disregard Program, the MFBU must have net nonexempt income that that exceeds the Medi-Cal maintenance need level but is not over 200% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL). MPG LTR 316 (10/95) MEM PCOC. 5F B. Pregnant Women Eligibility for pregnant women begins with the first day of the month of self-declaration of pregnancy. The pregnant woman may request a retroactive Medi-Cal evaluation (see 05.12.09.B). Pregnant women who qualify for no SOC benefits receive pregnancyrelated services regardless of their citizenship or alien status. Pregnancy services include: •Prenatal care •Labor •Delivery •Postpartum care •Family planning Pregnant women may also be eligible to non-pregnancy related services with a SOC under the MI/MN program. If eligibility is maintained through the month of birth, eligibility continues through the 60-day postpartum period. Benefits will be discontinued at the end of the month in which the 60-day postpartum period ends. If a pregnant minor does not qualify under regular Income Disregard regulations they must be evaluated using the Parental Income Disregard provision. ACWDL 03-34 C. Infants up to Infants up to one year of age may be eligible to full-scope benefits or benefits limited to the treatment of emergency medical conditions One Year of Age depending upon their citizenship status. Eligibility begins at birth and continues through the month of their first birthday, if eligibility is otherwise maintained during this period. NOTE: Under Continued Eligibility for pregnant women or Deemed Eligibility for infants, eligibility cannot be ended during the pregnancy or, for the infant, prior to the first birthday due to an increase in income. If the infant is active in the Income Disregard Program and loses eligibility, evaluate the child for Deemed Eligibility or Continuous Eligibility for Children (CEC) prior to taking any negative action. Approve for Deemed Eligibility or CEC if eligible. 05.12.03 133% Program A. 133% Program The 133% program provides zero SOC Medi-Cal coverage to otherwise eligible children beginning at age one up to end of the month of the child’s 6th birthday. To qualify for this program, the net nonexempt income of the MFBU must exceed the Medi-Cal maintenance need level but not be over 133% of the FPL. Scope of benefits will depend on their citizenship status. The following aid codes will be used: Aid Code Scope of Benefits 72 Full Scope 74 Limited Scope MPG LTR 534 (11/03) ACWDL 90-34 90-61 05.12.04 100% Program A. 100% Program The 100 Percent Program provides zero SOC Medi-cal coverage to eligible children at age six to the end of the month of the child’s 19 th birthday. To qualify for this program, the net non-exempt income of the MFBU must not exceed 100 percent of the federal poverty level. Scope of benefits will depend on their citizenship status. The following aid codes will be used: Aid Code Scope of Benefits ACWDL 91-61 7A Full Scope 7C Limited Scope MPG LTR 534 (11/03) County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide Number Page Targeted Low-Income Children’s Program (TLICP) 05.12.05 1 of 3 Issue Date: 4/23/2015 Effective Date: Upon Receipt Background: TLICP is a property disregard program that provides coverage for children who would have previously been enrolled in the HFP. Eligibility to the different programs is based on age. The below chart describes how the age groups are determined: Begin End At birth The end of the month of the child’s 1st birthday At age one The end of the month of the child’s 6th birthday At age six The end of the month of the child’s 19th birthday Continuous Eligibility for Children (CEC) applies to the TLICP refer to MPG 5.15.05. A. Aid Codes and Income Limits: To qualify for TLICP, the net non-exempt income of the MFBU must be as follows: Age Group Percent Level Aid Code Premium? 0-1 Above 200% - up to 250% (PRE-ACA) H1 No 0-1 Above 208% - up to 266% T5 No 0-1 Above 208% - up to 266% Undoc T0 No 1-6 Above 133% - up to 150%(PRE-ACA) H2 No 1-6 Above 142% - up to 160% T4 No 1-6 Above 142% - up to 160% (Undoc) T9 No 1-6 Above 160% - up to 266% T3 Yes 1-6 Above 150% - up to 250%(PRE-ACA) H3 Yes 1-6 Above 160% - up to 266% (Undoc) T8 Yes 6-19 Above 133% - up to 160% T2 No 6-19 Above 133% - up to 160% T7 No 6-19 Above 100% - up to 150%(PRE-ACA) H4 No 6-19 Above 160% - up to 266% T1 Yes 6-19 Above 160% - up to 266% (Undoc) T6 Yes 6-19 Above 150% - up to 250%(PRE-ACA) H5 Yes Aid codes H3 and H5 are Pre-ACA premium payment aid codes. Aid codes T1, T3, T6 and T8 Are MAGI TLICP premium payment aid codes. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide Number Page Targeted Low-Income Children’s Program (TLICP) 05.12.05 2 of 3 There are no restricted scope aid codes for pre-aca TLICP. If an applicant fails to provide citizenship/identity documentation at the end of their reasonable opportunity to provide period, they must be re-evaluated for limited scope Medi-Cal with a SOC. MAGI Based TLICP has aid codes for undocumented children. B. Premiums Premiums are $13 per child monthly, with a maximum of $39 per family monthly. When workers approve a beneficiary for one of the TLICP premium payment aid codes, the information will be transmitted to MAXIMUS via MEDS. Beneficiaries may pay premiums in the following forms: •Cash, check, Western Union •Electronic Funds Transfer •Credit Card Transactions MAXIMUS is the administrative vendor of premium payment collection and will be known as the Medi-Cal Premium Payment Section (MPPS). The MPPS will: •Maintain premium payment case files •Bill beneficiaries •Send overdue payment notices •Notify counties when a beneficiary on a premium payment aid code has not paid premiums for 60 days •Verify when a beneficiary previously discontinued for non-payment of premiums has paid and should be reinstated. C. Non-Payment of Premiums (NPP) Condition The Non-Payment of Premium Condition is when a beneficiary is two monthly payments past due. A reminder letter is mailed by the MPPS prior to 60 days past due. Upon receipt of notification of NPP, discontinue the beneficiary with timely notice. Beneficiaries are billed until they pay past due payments or are discontinued from TLICP. Premium Payment is a condition of eligibility for premium payment aid codes. No reevaluation of Medi-Cal is required when a beneficiary is discontinued from a premium based aid code for NPP. D. Reinstate TLICP Discontinued Due to NPP Beneficiaries can reinstate TLICP prior to termination, or within 30 days of termination by paying their past due premiums. After 30 days discontinuance, the customers must re-apply. If discontinued customers are determined eligible for TLICP with a premium again, they will be billed for all past due premiums. Procedures for reinstatement of premium based TLICP is in the NPP and Premium Refund/Waiver Processing Guide sections C, D, and E. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide Number Page Targeted Low-Income Children’s Program (TLICP) 05.12.05 3 of 3 E. Requests for Discontinuance of TLICP •The request for discontinuance must be in writing and documented in the case file. •Discontinuances of TLICP can only be made for the future months and cannot be made retroactive to the client’s request unless a change in circumstance reported timely makes the individual eligible for a non-premium aid code. F. Premium Refund/Waiver Requests The MPPS must continue billing the beneficiary until the Premium aid code is discontinued in MEDS. TLICP beneficiaries with premiums can request a waiver or refund of premiums in the following conditions: •They are found retroactively eligible to a non-premium aid code. They can request a refund of the premiums paid for the months where they are eligible for a nonpremium aid code. •A beneficiary requests discontinuance of a premium based aid code and the discontinuance is not effective the last day of the request month (example: client requests discontinuance in May 2014, but the worker does not take action until July 2014, the refund request would be for June 2014 and July 2014 paid premiums). Submit a premium refund/waiver request if the discontinuance is not processed by the end of the month of request, even if the beneficiary has not paid because the MPPS will still bill for the months where the client shows active in MEDS on a premium aid code. If the client goes back on a premium aid code within a year, the MPPS will bill the beneficiary for past due payments. Instructions for submitting Premium Refund/Waiver requests can be found in the NPP and Premium Refund/Waiver Processing Guide. G. American Indian/Alaskan Native Premium Waivers American Indians/Alaskan Natives who are eligible to receive or have received service from an Indian Health Service/ Tribal 638/ Urban Indian Health Program or through a referral to a Contracted Health Services, are eligible to a premium waiver for TLICP Premium-based aid codes. Initiate the premium waiver process for these individuals following the directions in the NPP and Premium Refund/Waiver Processing Guide section G. References: ACWDLs 12-33, 14-29, 14-29E, 14-43, and 15-10 MPG LTR 771 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 4/23/2018. 05.12.06 Property Disregard A. Overview The Income Disregard, 133% and 100% program offer a property disregard option that will be applied in the following situations: •When the property reported exceed the MFBU’s property limit. •In situations where a pregnant women request pregnancy related services and the only pending verifications are property verifications. •Property verifications will delay benefits for children (ages 0-19). Workers must inform applicants of the property disregard option at application or when made aware that the family is for a child (age 0- 19) or pregnant woman. If the pregnant woman wants full-scope benefits for herself and/or the rest of her family, she must reduce her family assets to the property limit in order to establish non Asset Waiver Provision Medi-Cal eligibility. NOTE: Workers must not require verification on any property listed on the MC 210, property utilization verification or completion of supplemental property forms. MPG LTR 555 (05/04) ACWDLs 89-50 89-103 89-104 94-07 95-28 95-52 98-06 B. Aid Codes The following aid codes must be used for property disregard cases: Aid Code Program Level of Benefits 47 200% Full Scope 69 200% Restricted 44 200% (Pregnancy) Full Scope 48 200% (Pregnancy) Restricted 8P 133% Full Scope 8N 133% Restricted 8R 100% Full Scope 8T 100% Restricted 05.12.07 Long Term Care A. Overview A child who is an inpatient receiving continuous services which begin before and continue beyond the age of eligibility to the following programs, will be entitled to extended eligibility under the program they ACWDL 89-105 qualify until the end of the month in which the continuous stay ends, as long as the family remains eligible: •Income Disregard •133% Program •100% Program •TLICP Inpatient services are defined as any medical facility in which the child stays over 24 hours, including long-term care (LTC) and acute care facilities. Children receiving continuous inpatient services must be re-evaluated for the 133% program at age six and at 6 month intervals until the continuous period ends. Workers must set a case alert to re-evaluate the child. Any MFBU with a share-of-cost (SOC) that contains an LTC person, must have the SOC listed for the LTC person. A pregnant woman in LTC who is not disabled and is eligible under the special programs must have zero SOC. Any SOC will be assigned to the other members of the MFBU who are not LTC. Any non-pregnancy related services received by her in the LTC facility may be applied towards the MFBU's SOC. MPG LTR 771 (12/12) 05.12.08 Income Treatment and Deductions A. Income This section includes the treatment of income for Income Disregard, 133%, 100% and TLICP program. Income from exempt property is counted in the budget except in the below situations: •is unavailable in accordance with MPG Article 10.01.04, •exempted by specific court order or statute •Interest income from a revocable or irrevocable burial trust or reserve which is exempt as property shall not be counted, if the family provides documentation that the burial trust or reserve meets the exemption criteria and that the interest income is left to accumulate and become part of the separate identifiable burial fund. •Interest income from disaster or emergency assistance payments is also exempt. Rental income from real property is counted in the budget, and must ACWDLs 89-50 94-07 be verified as follows: •Applicants/recipients must be provided the opportunity to state any expenses relate to rental income by completing the questions on the MC 210 S-P that relate to rental expenses. •The Asset Waiver applicant/recipient will not have to provide verification of the property other than what is necessary to establish the income and expense amounts. NOTE: Workers must review IEVS for all applicants regardless if the applicants/recipients meet the Asset Waiver provision requirements. IEVS provides income information including interest income from property. MPG LTR 771 (12/12) B. Deductions This section includes the treatment of deductions for Income Disregard, 133%, 100% and TLICP program. Allowable income deductions are the same as AFDC-MN programs (including excluded child allocations) outlined in MPG 10.06.04 except for the following: •Health insurance premiums •Deductions allowed for ABD persons under the MI/MN programs (MPG 10.06.03). NOTE: When these deductions are allowed in the MI/MN case they must be added back when completing the budget evaluation for the programs mentioned above. MPG LTR 771 (12/12) ACWDL 89-50 94-07 C. Parental Income Disregard Under the Parental Income Disregard Program provision, income from a parent of a pregnant minor who live together in the home is to be disregarded if the pregnant minor is not eligible using regular Income Disregard rules. This applies to all pregnant minors, including a pregnant minor between the ages of 18 and 21 and claimed as a tax dependent by her parents, even though she does not live in the home of the parents (e.g. she is temporarily away at college). The Parental Income Disregard provision must be used if the parent refuses to provide verification of income, but provides sufficient information about the minor. ACWDL 89-50 94-07 When the parental income is disregarded, the parent(s) will not be counted in the maintenance need level when comparing income to 200% of the FPL. D. Medi-Cal Family Budget Unit Children (age 0-19) and pregnant women in TLICP, 100%, 133% and Income Disregard program will be included in the special program MFBU and The MI/MN program MFBU with a share-of-cost as an ineligible person. Property Disregard children (0-19) and pregnant women in 100%, 133% and Income Disregard Program will only be included in the special program MFBU. NOTE: The child may link parents to AFDC-MN for Medi-Cal eligibility purposes. MPG LTR 771 (12/12) ACWDL 94-07 05.12.09 Miscellaneous A. Adding Newborns No application forms are required to add a newborn to the Medi-Cal case regardless of whether the child is Deemed Eligible or not. See MPG 04.02.16 for more information on adding newborns. According to Deemed Eligibility rules, an infant is to be placed in the same category of aid as the mother. Therefore, if the mother received Medi-Cal in the month of birth (see MPG 5-15) through the Income Disregard Program, the newborn will be added to the Income Disregard Program case. For more information, see MPG 05.15.02. If the mother did not meet her SOC in the month of birth, a statement of citizenship/alien status and application for SSN must be obtained for the infant. For more information, see MPG 5-15 I don’t think this applies any longer. Need to research. MI/MN MFBU The newborn must be added to the MI/MN MFBU as an ineligible person when he/she will be issued benefits through the Income Disregard MFBU. If the entire MI/MN MFBU is ineligible (e.g., no linkage for parents, no other children), the newborn's PDTL linkage code must be entered. MPG LTR 541 (11/03) ACWDL 03-45 03-49 B. Retroactive Requests The following programs may be applied in retroactive evaluations: •Income Disregard •133% Program •100% Program •TLICP NOTE: TLICP may not be applied to retroactive applications dated prior to 1/1/2013. In some cases, a woman applicant may not be pregnant at the time of application but may have been pregnant or in the postpartum period for one or more of the retroactive months. Likewise, an infant may be over one year of age at the time of application but may have been under one year of age for all or part of the three-month retroactive period. These situations need to be evaluated for retroactive Deemed Eligibility, Income Disregard and Asset Waiver benefits. MPG LTR 771 (12/12) ACWDL 94-07 03-49 C. Retroactive Repayment of SOC Beneficiaries who previously met or were obligated to pay their SOC and were subsequently determined eligible in the same month of eligibility for the Income Disregard program are entitled to an adjustment (refund/reduction of the billed amount). If the family met its SOC but the beneficiary had no expenses for that month (received no benefits), he/she would not be eligible for a refund. If the beneficiary ... Then ... had expenses in a month and the share of cost was not met, the county should issue the appropriate Income Disregard program card. states that he/she does not wish a refund but prefers an adjustment to a future month's SOC, follow the procedures outlined in Article 12 of the Medi-Cal Program Guide. Beneficiary’s must be provided with the following: If the date of service … Then the beneficiary should be given … Less than 12 months the SOC Medi-Cal Provider Letter (MC 1054) containing the "Old SOC County I.D." and the "New Non-SOC County I.D." Older than 12 months a retroactive Medi-Cal card containing the original SOC, county I.D. and an MC 1054. These documents must be given to the provider for processing. Once the provider's claim for services has been reimbursed by the fiscal intermediary, the provider must refund the appropriate amount to the beneficiary if the met SOC was paid. If the SOC was obligated but not paid, the provider reduces the amount billed to the beneficiary by the appropriate amount. D. Minor Consent Pregnant minors who apply for minor consent services may qualify for either the Income Disregard or the Asset Waiver provision. Pregnant minors are to be issued a no SOC limited service card under the appropriate aid code. Remember, minor consent applicants are never required to verify pregnancy. MPG LTR 541 (11/03) E. Sneede As in the other percentage programs, workers are to determine Sneede MBUs first. MBUs of children born after September 30, 1983 who are at least six years old and who have a share-of-cost should be evaluated for the 100% program. MPG LTR 414 (12/98) F. MEDS Alerts The following MEDS alerts will generate: Alert Description 9524 Generated towards the end of the 11th month from which the MEDS record was established stating that the woman appears to be no longer eligible for the Income Disregard or Asset Waiver program. The worker will be responsible for terminating the MEDS record. If the woman becomes pregnant again within 12 months the worker can reactivate the MEDS record through a restoration of benefits; however, no subsequent alert will be generated. 9525 Generated every 6 months beginning with the last month of eligibility to remind the worker to check the child's inpatient status, send a notice of action, or that a termination action should be taken if MEDS has no termination date. 9526 Generated when the child is past the appropriate age and every 6 months thereafter when eligibility has not been reconfirmed by the worker. It will inform the worker that eligibility has been terminated on MEDS.
