sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Overview of Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) Waivers and Programs Number Page 05.18.01 1 of 6 Revision Date: March 1, 2026 B ackground: Home and Community -Based Services ( HCBS) w aivers and programs provide certain services to eligible Non-Modified Adjusted Gross Income (Non- MAGI) individuals with skilled nursing care needs who wish to remain at home or in the community setting . These programs prevent individuals from having to enter a nursing facility or medical institution . Waiver administrators , Care -Coordinating Agencies (CCA), Aging Independence Services (AIS) , and In- Home Supportive Services (IHSS) determine eligibility and enroll customers to HCBS waivers and programs and may notify the county when a customer is approved for a waiver. The goal is to increase enrollment by applying the special rules when determining eligibility. P urpose: This section provides an overview of the HCBS w aivers and p rograms including s pousal impoverishment (SI) provisions for the HCBS population. References to property determinations for current evaluations were added due to the reinstatement of the property evaluation for Non-Modified Adjusted Gross Income (Non-MAGI) Medi-Cal effective January 1, 2026. P olicy: A. HCBS Waivers and Programs There are currently five HCBS waivers in effect in San Diego: • HCBS for the Developmentally Disabled ( HCBS-DD) – commonly known as the D epartment of Developmental Services (DDS) Waiver. • Home and Community-Based Alternatives (HCBA). • Multipurpose Senior Services Program (MSSP). • Assisted Living Waiver (ALW). • Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS). HCB S programs include but are not limited to: • IHSS Community First Choice Option (CFCO). • Program of All-inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE). • Senior Care Action Network (SCAN) Fully Integrated Dual Eligible Special Needs Plan. A customer may initiate the HCBS waiver or program request by: • Making a written or verbal request. • Answering “yes” to one of the following questions on the application or renewal form: - “Does anyone in your household need help with long-term care or home and community-based services?” - “Do you want information on the Personal Care Services Program, an in-home care program for aged, blind, or disabled persons (also called In-Home Supportive Services)?” • Contacting a waiver administrator or a CCA that works with the waiver administrator. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Overview of Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) Waivers and Programs Number Page 05.18.01 2 of 6 B. Institutional Deeming Most HCBS waivers and programs allow for the application of special rules under Non-MAGI Medi-Cal, also known as the institutional deeming process. Before applying i nstitutional deeming, Medi -Cal eligibility must first be determined by including the property and income of all household members based on Medi-Cal hierarchy. This includes the application of SI provisions when appropriate. Refer to Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 05.18.01C for guidance on SI provisions. Institutional deeming rules must be applied to individuals who are ineligible due to excess property or would have a Share of Cost (SOC). Institutional deeming applies to the following households: • Married HCBS participants with no community spouse ( for example, if the other aged or disabled spouse is institutionalized). • Married couples and both spouses are HCBS waiver or program participants. • HCBS participant c hild 20 years or younger with family income or property that makes them ineligible to no SOC Medi-Cal. Institutional Deeming requirements: • Each HCBS participant is treated as institutionalized and in a Medi-Cal Family Budget Unit (MFBU) of one. They may link other family members who request Medi -Cal such as those on Public Assistance (PA). • Community property is split equally between spouses a

content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAged and Disabled Federal Poverty Level Programs 05.19.01 1 of 3 Revision Date: 12/01/2020 Background: Known under the Affordable Care Act (ACA) as Non-Modified Adjusted Gross Income (Non-MAGI) category, the Aged and Disabled Federal Poverty Level (A&D FPL) Program provides zero Share of Cost (SOC) Medi-Cal to eligible aged or disabled individuals throughout the State of California. The A&D FPL Program was established January 1, 2001. Purpose: This section identifies potentially eligible A&D FPL individuals and describes instructions to determine eligibility and level of benefits. This section has been updated to include the new income limit of 138% of the FPL and remove the program income disregard of $230 for individuals, $310 for couples and is effective December 1, 2020. This section was also updated with changes to how the Medicare Part B deduction is applied to the A&D FPL budget effective December 1, 2020. Policy: A potentially eligible A&D FPL individual is aged or disabled, but not residing in a Long-Term Care (LTC) Facility. There is no age limit for those in the disabled category therefore disabled children may be evaluated for this program. Blind individuals may also be eligible to the A&D FPL Program if they meet the aged or disabled criteria. When applicants are blind and not in receipt of Title II disability benefits, evaluate for the Federal Poverty Level for the Blind (FPLB) program, refer to MPG 05.19.02. A. Income Eligibility Requirements Non-MAGI income rules apply to A&D FPL income evaluations including allocating to other public assistance (PA) spouses (Refer to MPG Article 10 for income guidelines). Effective 12/1/2020, the individual’s net non-exempt income must be at or below 138% of the FPL for the applicable family size after deductions. Also effective 12/1/2020, do not apply the standard deductions ($230 for an individual and $310 for a couple) in A&D FPL Program evaluations. For definitions and examples, see Desk Aid 88. B. Property Standards Non-MAGI property rules apply to the A&D FPL property evaluation. Refer to MPG Article 9. C. Application Process Effective January 1, 2014, Medi-Cal applicants, are screened for eligibility to MAGI Medi-Cal as part of the Medi-Cal hierarchy application process. See Desk Aid 74 for the Medi-Cal hierarchy when determining eligibility. When no eligibility to MAGI Medi-Cal exists, Medi-Cal applicants, not residing in LTC, will be screened for eligibility to the A&D FPL Program. The order of evaluation when determining A&D FPL eligibility is as follows: 1. Pickle 2. A&D FPL/Aged, Blind, or Disabled Medically Needy (ABD MN) Zero SOC 3. Federal Poverty Level for the Blind 4. Aged, Blind and Disabled Medically Needy (ABD MN) SOC 5. 250% Working Disabled County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAged and Disabled Federal Poverty Level Programs 05.19.01 2 of 3 A&D individuals are potentially eligible to three months of retroactive benefits when eligibility requirements are met in the preceding months. D. Deductions Apply all applicable non-MAGI income deductions including the $20.00 any income, health insurance premiums, and, where the customer has earned income, the $65.00 and one-half earned income deductions. Effective December 1, 2020, deduct the Medicare Part B Premium amount whether it is paid by the customer or the state. Do not remove the Medicare Part B premium deduction from the A&D FPL budget when the state begins paying the premium. ABD applicants in licensed board and care (B&C) may be evaluated for the A&D FPL Program and are eligible to all B&C deductions. They are entitled to receive either the personal care service (PCS) deduction or the income deduction for excess B&C (MPG 10.06.08). These deductions will be used in the A&D FPL income evaluation. E. Case Composition A&D FPL eligible individuals will be in their own Medi-Cal Family Budget Unit (MFBU) and eligible couples will remain together in one MFBU. A&D FPL eligible individuals and couples will be ineligible members in the MFBU for other family members applying for or receiving Medi-Cal benefits. The income of the A&D FPL individual(s) is included in the other family member’s budget and the maintenance need level for the family will include the A&D FPL individual(s). If a couple is eligible, both spouses will be on the A&D FPL Program; however, if both spouses cannot qualify as a couple for the A&D FPL Program, either spouse can apply separately to qualify. The spouse that chooses not to be in the A&D FPL Program may choose not to be on Medi-Cal or may qualify through the MN Program with a SOC. It is possible for spouses to be in two different programs. A&D FPL individuals may be determined eligible to the Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB) program or the Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary (SLMB) program. See Desk Aid 88 for examples of different A&D FPL households. F. Level of Benefits A&D FPL eligible individuals who are United States (US) Citizens, US Nationals or immigrants with Satisfactory Immigration Status (SIS) will receive full-scope benefits. A&D FPL eligible immigrants without SIS will receive restricted benefits. The following aid codes are used for this program: •1H Full-Scope FPL Aged Individuals •6H Full-Scope FPL Disabled Individuals •1U Restricted FPL Aged Individuals •6U Restricted FPL Disabled Individuals Note: A&D FPL eligible blind individuals are linked as either aged or disabled. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAged and Disabled Federal Poverty Level Programs 05.19.01 3 of 3 G. Redeterminations and Period of Eligibility Eligibility for the A&D FPL program must be redetermined annually. Regular Medi-Cal redetermination procedures are followed for this program. At redetermination, all A&D Medi-Cal beneficiaries, except for Pickle/Disabled Adult Child (DAC) beneficiaries, will be evaluated using Non- MAGI program regulations. Procedure: N/A Program Impacts Forms and Document Capture Discontinue use of form MC 176AD. A new manual budget form will be issued shortly. References: ACWDL 01-18, 02-38, 06-41, 09-28, 20-02, and 20-18 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 12/31/2023. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageFederal Poverty Level for the Blind 05.19.02 1 of 2 Revision Date: 08/01/2018 Background: This program covers blind individuals pursuant to Title XVI who have not yet or cannot meet the Title II criteria for disability based upon blindness. This section is being updated to the new format, no other changes were made. Purpose: This section is to provide guidelines for the Federal Poverty Level Program for the Blind (FPLB). Policy: The Federal Poverty Level Program for the Blind (FPLB) mirrors the eligibility criteria for the A&D FPL Program, except the linkage is based on blindness and the income limit may be higher for couples. Aid code 2H is effective July 1, 2009. A. General Rule FPLB is available for blind individuals whether they previously applied for or received SSI/SSP and were denied or discontinued or applied for Medi-Cal-only. FPLB is available for the following blind individuals who: •Have not met or who cannot meet the Title II criteria for disability based blindness •Meet the Title XVI criteria for blindness •Allege that they have blindness and who are waiting disability evaluations •Have had medical determination verified by a doctor A person is considered to be blind if there has been a medical determination verified by a doctor that they have either of the following conditions: •Central visual acuity if no more than 20/200 with corrections •Tunnel vision, which is a limited field of 20 degrees or less Any disability determination based upon blindness would only change retroactively, when it would have a positive effective for all family members living in the home. The effective date of the positive retroactive change would go back to the onset date of disability for the Medi-Cal recipient or July 1, 2009. Persons eligible under FLPB must meet the property, citizenship, alien status, residency, institutional status, and cooperation requirements specified in MPG Articles 4, 6, 7 and 9. They must also meet the SOC requirement in MPG 12.01. B. Case Composition FPLB eligible individual(s) will be in their own MFBU and eligible couples will remain together in one MFBU. FPLB eligible individuals and couples will be ineligible members of the MFBU of other family members applying for or receiving Medi-Cal benefits. The income of the FPLB individual(s) will be included in the other family members’ budget and the maintenance needs level for the family will include the FPLB individual(s). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageFederal Poverty Level for the Blind 05.19.02 2 of 2 FPLB individuals may be determined eligible to the QMB program or the SLMB program. C. FPLB Income Limit As stated above, the eligibility criteria for the FPLB Program mirrors the A&D FPL Program except that linkage is based on blindness and the income limits may be higher for couples. The income limits for the FPLB Program must be the greater of: •The Supplemental Security Income/State Supplementary Payment (SSI/SSP) rates, or •100 percent of FPL plus the standard deduction (A&D FPL Disregards) Note: On years where the SSI/SSP payment rate is higher than 100 percent of FPL plus the standard deduction, the income limit must be the SSI/SSP payment rate. The income limit for FPLB will be updated annually. Procedure: N/A Program Impacts: Automation: CalWIN functionality does not evaluate for FPLB eligibility. Follow the FPLB Processing Guidelines located in Eligibility Essentials website when completing an FPLB evaluation. References: ACWDL 09-18, 09-20, 09-28, 12-11 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 08/31/2021 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page250 Percent Working Disabled (250% WD) Program 05.19.03 1 of 5 Revision Date: 08/01/2018 Background: This program was implemented and intended to promote self-sufficiency and encourage the disabled to seek employment without fear of losing essential health care. The State has elected to impose a monthly premium on a sliding scale instead of a SOC for those eligible to the 250% WD Program. In addition to reformatting this section, procedures have been moved to Processing Guide 28 and the appendices to Desk Aids. Purpose: This section provides guidelines for the 250% WD Program. Policy: The 250% WD Program is an optional program. The individual may choose to participate in either a SOC program to which they are eligible or the 250% WD Program. A. Eligibility Criteria All applicants/beneficiaries must: •Meet all non-financial Medi-Cal program eligibility requirements •Meet the federal definition of disability as defined in federal law for Social Security disability programs, except that Substantial Gainful Activity (SGA) rules don’t apply •Work as defined in MPG 05.19.03E below •Have net non-exempt countable income less than 250% of the FPL •Have net non-exempt property within Medi-Cal limits •Meet the eligibility requirements of the SSI/SSP program as outlined MPG 05.19.03I and N below •Pay a monthly premium based on net countable income •Not residing in LTC Reporting responsibilities are the same for the 250% WD Program as other Medi-Cal programs. 250% WD beneficiaries are entitled to a state Medicare Part B buy-in. Disabled individuals who are working and have been previously denied SSDI benefits by Social Security based on the capacity to perform SGA or insufficient work quarters shall be evaluated for Medi-Cal eligibility under the 250% WD Program. B. SSDI Requirements for 250% WD When the applicant/beneficiary’s gross earnings are below the SGA limit, they must be referred to apply for SSDI. Note: If the gross earnings of a 250% WD beneficiary decrease below SGA, the beneficiary is then required to apply for SSDI. C. Aid Code Adults and children in the 250% WD Program are placed in aid code 6G. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page250 Percent Working Disabled (250% WD) Program 05.19.03 2 of 5 D. Definition of a Child For the 250% WD Program, a child must be unmarried and not be the head of a household and either under the age of 18 or under the age of 22 and a student regularly attending school, college or a training that is designed to prepare him/her for a paying job. E. Work Requirements “Work” is undefined for the purposes of this program and there is no minimum work requirement in order to qualify. However, the individual must be able to prove they are working or temporarily unemployed as follows: •Full time work •Part time work •Self-employment with countable earnings at or below the 250% of the FPL •Receiving earned in-kind income •Receiving unemployment F. 250% Working Disabled Case Composition The Medi-Cal household composition is determined as follows: If the 250% WD eligible is a… Then… Child or adult His/her own MFBU Couple and both are 250% WD eligible Couple will be together in one MFBU Couple and only one is eligible Each spouse will have their own MFBU Parent WD eligible child will be in a separate MFBU Note: All cases must be evaluated for good cause before discontinuance. Good cause includes: •Hospitalization •Inability to work that is directly related to the disability •Former worksite closure •Loss of transportation If good cause exists and the beneficiary meets all other eligibility requirements, continue the eligibility of the beneficiary for two months following the month that the work ceased. G. 250% WD Net Non-exempt Income Exceptions Income is determined in accordance to MPG 10.01 with the following exceptions: •In-Kind Income – use SSI program requirements for treating in-kind support and maintenance (ISM) as unearned income. ISM rules and chart may be found in Desk Aid 89. •Disability Income – All disability income, including worker’s compensation, of the working disabled individual is disregarded (e.g., federal, state or private disability income). •Impairment Related Work Expenses (IRWE) – IRWE also applies to the 250% WD Program. •Spousal/Parental Deeming – Spousal/parental deeming based on SSI methodology applies to the 250% WD Program. Use form MC 338J to assist in this computation. •Child Support – One third of child support received by an applicant who is a child is disregarded. The remainder is treated as unearned income. •Social Security income based on disability converted to Social Security retirement – Recipients of Social Security income based on disability may become eligible for increased County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page250 Percent Working Disabled (250% WD) Program 05.19.03 3 of 5 benefits when they reach retirement age or have some other qualifying event. All Social Security income based on disability that converts to Social Security income based on retirement is exempt including, but not limited to: oSocial Security Disability Benefits, including any increases (cost of living) oDisabled Widow/er’s Benefits oDisabled Adult Child (DAC) Benefits Note: Retirement income from sources other than Social Security is not exempt. Verify that the Social Security disability income converting to Social Security retirement income doesn’t include retirement income from other sources such as public or private retirement. Refer to BEnDS #752 for detailed CalWIN instructions on exempting income. H. 250% WD Net Non-exempt Property The property amount for a 250% WD applicant is determined in accordance with MPG 09.02. The following items are exempt: •Retirement arrangements authorized under the Internal Revenue Code oIndividual Retirement Accounts (IRAs) oWork related pension funds for income when employment ends, which are administered by an employer or union, including such plans as Deferred Compensation Plans and Thrifts Plans oPlans for self-employed individuals such as KEOGH Plan •Retained Earned Income which is defined as earned income held in a separate identifiable account and not comingled with other resources. NOTE: There is no maximum limitation on the amount that an individual can keep in their separately identifiable account as exempt retained income. I. SSI/SSP Property To meet the SSI/SSP property test, the net non-exempt property of an individual or child must be at or below the Medi-Cal property level for one. If there is a spouse, net non-exempt property must be below the Medi-Cal property level for two. Form MC 338C is available for the property determination. J. Non-Citizen Eligibility to the 250% WDP Non-Citizens lawfully residing in the United States and were receiving SSI on August 22, 1996, meet the SSI non-citizen status and may be eligible to the 250% WDP. Note: Non-Citizens who are or would be eligible to restricted-scope Medi-Cal benefits are not eligible for the 250% WDP. Procedures: K. Determine Disability A person is considered disabled if he/she meet the criteria in Title II or Title XVI of the Social Security Act. Refer to Processing Guide 28 for procedures to follow when an applicant has not had a disability determination or it is no longer current. In situations where the applicant’s DDSD packet has already been submitted, do not submit a new DDSD packet. When an individual moves from one program to another, a new referral is not needed. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page250 Percent Working Disabled (250% WD) Program 05.19.03 4 of 5 L. Application Processing The 250% WD Program is an optional program that staff should offer when a working and disabled person is not eligible to MAGI or Non-MAGI zero SOC programs. Applicants/beneficiaries may choose to participate in either a SOC program to which they are eligible or the 250% WD Program. 1. Provide the 250% WD Comparison Brochure (14-110 HHSA) to the individual and allow the individual to choose which program they prefer. 2. When notified of their choice, place the individual in the appropriate aid code. M. Reports Temporary Unemployment Continue the 250% WDP benefits for up to 26 weeks. The timeline for measuring the period of unemployment will begin the date the 250% WDP beneficiary reports their unemployment or the date the worker verifies unemployment through IEVS. Refer to Processing Guide 28 for steps to take when the applicant/beneficiary reports temporary unemployment. N. Determine if Income is at or Below 250% FPL To determine whether the applicant(s) are below the 250% FPL and meet the SSI/SSP income test, only consider the income for the 250% WD individual, their spouse and/or their parents (if a child). The following forms are associated with the budget computations: •MC 338 – 250 Percent Income Test Worksheet for the 250% WD Program •MC 338B – 250% and the SSI/SSP Income Test Worksheet for the 250% WD Program-Child applying with or without Ineligible Parent(s) O. Determine Premium Amount The monthly premium will be determined using the net non-exempt income level criteria outlined in 05.19.03F and using the 250% WD Premium Payment Chart (Desk Aid 91). Refer to Processing Guide 28 when 250% WD beneficiary reports a change in income. P. 250% WD Program Approvals See Processing Guide 28 for required actions. Q. Discontinue for Failure to Pay Premiums Discontinuances are processed by DHCS when full premiums have not been paid for two consecutive months excluding retroactive months. Refer to Processing Guide 28 for procedures. R. Collection of Premiums Premium payments will be returned to the DHCS, Third Party Liability Branch (TPLB). TPLB will process premiums as they are received. If a partial premium for a month is received, it will be deposited and reported to MEDS. MEDS program logic will be able to recognize both full and partial premium payments allowing for multiple premium payments to be made for each month. Program Impacts: Forms: MC 338 and 14-110 HHSA Comparison Brochure are available in the EO Forms Repository County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page250 Percent Working Disabled (250% WD) Program 05.19.03 5 of 5 References: ACWDL 00-16, 00-51, 01-14, 02-34, 02-39, 04-30, 09-28, 09-29, 09-33, 11-38, 11-41, 17-23, 17-31 18-05 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 08/31/2021 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operation

sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAged and Disabled Federal Poverty Level Programs 05.19.01 1 of 3 Revision Date: 12/01/2020 Background: Known under the Affordable Care Act (ACA) as Non-Modified Adjusted Gross Income (Non-MAGI) category, the Aged and Disabled Federal Poverty Level (A&D FPL) Program provides zero Share of Cost (SOC) Medi-Cal to eligible aged or disabled individuals throughout the State of California. This section has been updated to include the new income limit of 138% of the FPL and remove the program income disregard of $230 for individuals, $310 for couples and is effective December 1, 2020. This section was also updated with changes to how the Medicare Part B deduction is applied to the A&D FPL budget effective December 1, 2020. title: Section 20 - Safe Arms for Newborns
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page Safe Arms For Newborns 05.20.01 1 of 3 Revision Date: 05/01/2018 Background: The Safe Arms for Newborns Law was enacted to provide for the health and safety of unwanted newborn children. Under this law, any child less than seventy-two hours old, who is voluntarily surrendered to an employee on duty at a public or private hospital emergency room, will be determined eligible to Medi-Cal. The law also requires that the hospital taking physical custody provide a medical screening examination and any necessary medical care to the child. Included with the reformatting, this section is being updated to include application process clarifications issued in ACWDL 03-26E. Purpose: This section provides instructions regarding the processing of cases under the Safe Arms for Newborns Law. Policy: The Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) has issued instructions for hospitals and for county Medi-Cal eligibility staff regarding the Safe Arms for Newborn Law. A. Hospital Instructions DHCS has instructed hospitals as follows: •Upon taking physical custody of surrendered newborns, give these children a medical screening examination and provide them any necessary medical care. •The hospital employee taking physical custody of the newborn must enter the identification number from the child’s hospital ankle bracelet in the “ID number” field in the top right corner of the MC 356, “SAFE ARMS FOR NEWBORNS Medical Questionnaire.” •The hospital taking physical custody of the newborn must offer the person surrendering custody the MC 356. •The person surrendering the child is not required to complete or return the MC 356. •The parent names may not be requested. •A hospital that receives a surrendered newborn must initiate a request for Medi-Cal for that child no later than the following business day. B. County Instructions DHCS has instructed counties as follows: •County eligibility staff are responsible for completing the application and SOF. •When actual names and birth dates are unavailable, use the health facility identification information and estimated date of birth, if available, in establishing the Medi-Cal eligibility record. •For the purposes of this program, assume that the newborn is a United States citizen. •A child support referral to the Department of Child Support Enforcement is not required. •Upon granting, provide the health facility with the information necessary to obtain reimbursement for care provided to the newborn as soon as eligibility is established. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page Safe Arms For Newborns 05.20.01 2 of 3 C. Period of Eligibility Under this law, eligibility begins the day of surrender and extends through the last day of the following month. However, if a child is surrendered on the last day of the month, eligibility may continue through the third month. For example, if a child is surrendered to a hospital on the March 15, eligibility extends through April 30. If the surrender date is March 31, eligibility may be extended through May 31. In no circumstance will coverage under this category extend past the last day of the third month. Newborns determined eligible to the Safe Arms for Newborns Program are not eligible to continuing Medi-Cal benefits through the Deemed Eligibility Program for infants or the Continuous Eligibility for Children Program. Continuing eligibility for the child will be established under normal program criteria at the time that the child either enters the foster care system or is placed with a responsible relative or caretaker. D. Aid Code These children are to be placed in a new zero share of cost aid code 2A. This aid code will be used by DHCS to track cases opened under the Safe Arms for Newborn Law. E. Surrendered Newborns Not Covered Under the Safe Arms for Newborns Program Surrendered newborn babies, not covered under the Safe Arms for Newborns Program, are handled on a case-by-case basis using formerly established procedures. Refer to Desk Aid 87 for case examples. Procedure: F. County Required Action When processing a request for Medi-Cal for a surrendered newborn less than seventy-two hours old and the actual name and date of birth of the newborn are unavailable; complete the application and SOF as an immediate need using the hospital identification information and estimated date of birth. For example, if the hospital has assigned a name for identification purposes, such as “Baby Doe BBB” or “Abandoned Baby AAA,” these are acceptable and searchable on MEDS. Names cannot contain numbers, only letters can be used. Important Note: Treat these cases as confidential cases. •Do Not use parent’s name, social security number, or dates of births, if known. •The case number assigned is not to be used once Safe Arms for Newborns eligibility ends. •Do Not bank these cases to continuing. •Intake is responsible for holding the case for the period of eligibility. Program Impact/s: Automation: In the "Selected" group box for all programs, click the Emergency checkbox. Then select the Safe Arms for New Borns Benefits checkbox. References: ACWDLs 01-48, 03-26, 03-26E County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number Page Safe Arms For Newborns 05.20.01 3 of 3 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 05/31/2021 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations

title: Section 21 - In-Home Supportive Services
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageIn-Home Supportive Services (IHSS) 05.21.01 1 of 3 Revision Date: 06/01/2021 Background: In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS) provides homemaker and personal care assistance to lowincome customers who need assistance in their home so they can remain independent. These inhome services are provided by independent providers/IHSS providers/homemakers. Customers applying for or receiving IHSS must have a Medi-Cal eligibility determination completed before in-home services are authorized. IHSS Programs The following programs provide in-home services: •IHSS Plus Option (IPO) (Aid Code 2L) •Personal Care Services Program (PCSP) (Aid Code 2M) •IHSS Residual (Aid Code 2N) •Community First Choice (CFCO) (Aid Code 2K) IHSS aid codes are reported to the Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS) via the Case Management Information and Payrolling System (CMIPS) and NOT entered by the Medi-Cal Human Services Specialist (HSS) into CalWIN. Purpose: This section is updated to add the IHSS-CFCO program and clarifications from All County Welfare Directors Letter (ACWDL) 20-15 regarding the Beneficiary Reimbursement Process (also known as the Conlan process). Policy: IHSS Programs: IHSS Plus Option (IPO) (Aid Code 2L) To qualify for IPO, Medi-Cal eligibility is required. Customers not receiving Supplemental Security Income/State Supplemental Program (SSI/SSP), or another Medi-Cal linked cash-based program (for example: Foster Care, CalWORKs, Refugee Cash Assistance [RCA], Adoptions Assistance Program [AAP]) must be determined eligible for federally funded full-scope Medi-Cal and qualify for in-home services through a Needs Assessment completed by an IHSS Social Worker. Personal Care Services Program (PCSP) (Aid Code 2M) To qualify for PCSP, customers not receiving SSI/SSP, or Medi-Cal linked to a cash-based program must be determined eligible for federally funded full-scope Medi-Cal and be found in need of personal care services through a Needs Assessment completed by an IHSS Social Worker. IHSS Residual (Aid Code 2N) IHSS Residual Program services will be available to customers who are eligible under current IHSS regulations but are not eligible for federally funded full-scope Medi-Cal. Community First Choice (CFCO) (Aid Code 2K) The CFCO program is an alternative for PCSP and IPO customers. CFCO provides home and community-based attendant services and supports for customers who are eligible for Medi-Cal, meet County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageIn-Home Supportive Services (IHSS) 05.21.01 2 of 3 specific income criteria and the Nursing Facility Level of Care (NFLOC). CFCO customers are eligible to be evaluated under Medi-Cal Spousal Impoverishment (SI) Provisions, if applicable. See MPG 05.18.01 for the SI Provisions eligibility and Doctor’s Verification process. Case Processing: Application The Single Streamlined Application and related forms are used to complete the Medi-Cal determination. The Medi-Cal application packet must contain Disability Determination Services Division (DDSD) forms for cases in which the applicant’s disability has not already been determined. Redetermination The MC 210RV and related forms are used to complete the annual redetermination. Share-of-Cost (SOC) Customers with a SOC are treated as Medically Needy customers with a SOC. The SOC may be met with any medical service (including payments to the IHSS provider) and out-of-pocket expenses for personal services. IHSS Plus Option Income Payments made under the IHSS Plus Option are exempt as income and property. These exempt payments include: •Caregiver wages that are paid to a parent of an IHSS Plus Option minor child recipient for services provided to that child •Caregiver wages that are paid to a spouse of an IHSS Plus Option recipient for services provided to that recipient •Restaurant meal allowances from IHSS for the IHSS Plus Option recipient •The advance payments made to IHSS Plus Option recipients to pay their caregivers directly for services provided under the IHSS Plus Option In-Home Caregiver Wages In-home caregiver wages received by a spouse/parent for the care of their spouse or minor child in receipt of federal, state, or local government in-home services program are exempt as income and property for Medi-Cal purposes. This exemption includes payments received by a parent or spouse of an IHSS Residual recipient. In-Home Care Services Payments Payments made by the Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) to an in-home care recipient for the purpose of purchasing in-home care services, including restaurant meals, are exempt as income and property for Medi-Cal purposes. Procedure: Application Complete a Medi-Cal eligibility determination using Medi-Cal rules, forms, and Notices of Actions (NOAs) for all applicants or recipients of IHSS. The IHSS Needs Assessment can be completed by the IHSS Social Worker at any time during this process. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageIn-Home Supportive Services (IHSS) 05.21.01 3 of 3 Hospital & Community Support Services HSSs Process IHSS related Medi-Cal referrals according to the procedures outlined in MPG 4.2, MPG 4.3, and Medi-Cal Processing Guide 02 CMIPS II Interface Activities. Aged & Disabled Federal Poverty Level (A&D FPL) Program The Medi-Cal determination is separate from the IHSS determination. Determine potential eligibility to the A&D FPL according to the policies outlined in MPG 5.19. Disability Determination Services Division (DDSD) For cases that require a disability determination, follow the DDSD requirements outlined in MPG 5.4. CalWORKs Discontinuance When a CalWORKs recipient, who is also receiving IHSS, is discontinued and has no other MediCal eligibility, contact the IHSS Social Worker to request a copy of the DDSD determination. If the DDSD determination shows that the recipient is disabled and the reexamination date has not passed, use that determination for Medi-Cal eligibility. Redetermination Each Family Resource Center (FRC) is responsible for completing the annual redetermination of these cases according to the procedures outlined in MPG 4.15 and Medi-Cal Processing Guide 02 CMIPS II Interface Activities. Beneficiary Reimbursement Process (BRP) IHSS beneficiaries who are Medi-Cal eligible and paid an out-of-pocket expense for the excess SOC can file a claim to request reimbursement. See MPG 04.02.10J for the BRP (also known as the Conlan process). For scenarios where Spousal Impoverishment (SI) provisions are involved, see Processing Guide 25. Program Impacts None. References: ACLs 05-05, 05-05E, 07-11 ACWDLs 05-21, 05-29, 07-02, 07-05, 15-02, 17-25, 18-19, 20-15 County Policy Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 06/30/2024. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: Section 22 - Hospital Presumptive Eligibility
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Hospital Presumptive Eligibility (HPE) Number Page 05.22 1 of 3 Background: The Patient and Pro tection and Affordable Care Act of 2010 required implementation of Hospital Presumptive Eligibility (HPE) effective January 1, 2014. Qualified hospitals can determine HPE for certain Medi-Cal eligible individuals based on preliminary information. HPE provides temporary, no share-of-cost, PE Medi-Cal benefits based on self-attested information collected by authorized hospital personnel from the individual. Policy: Eligibility Requirements: To qualify for the HPE program, individuals must be a California resident, not be currently enrolled in Medi-Cal, and meet the income and household composition requirements for one of the ACA eligibility groups. The ACA eligibility groups are:  Former foster care children between the ages of 18 and 26 who received Foster Care on their 18th birthday  Children, ages 0 to18  Parent/ caretaker relatives  Pregnant women  New Adults (ages 19 to 64, not pregnant at time of application, not enrolled in Medicare, and not eligible for any other mandatory group) HPE Application: The HPE application is a one-page application that is based on the individual’s attestation about their state residence, income and family size. HPE eligibility determination is made in real-time. Authorized hospital personnel review the application and input the individual’s information online via the HPE online portal. Once the application is submitted online, an electronic match verifies that the individual is not currently receiving Medi-Cal benefits using the MEDS system. MEDS will provide a response and makes an HPE eligibility determination. HPE paper applications are not acceptable and must be submitted online only. If the individual is eligible for HPE, the authorized hospital personnel will provide an “Immediate Need Eligibility Document”. HPE beneficiaries will not receive a Benefits Identification Card (BIC); therefore, the “Immediate Need Eligibility Document” can be used as a BIC. HPE Denials A HPE application can be denied if applicant attests to any of the following:  Not being a California resident  Having income over the limit for their coverage group  Being currently enrolled in Medi-Cal  Already having received HPE benefits based on limitations set by DHCS If MEDS shows a… Then MEDS will… pending application with HX18 transaction (Covered California application) or EW18 transaction (county application) not automatically terminate. transaction with either HX20 or EW20 automatically terminate. Coverage Group PE Enrollment Period Permitted Former foster youth, age 18 to 25 One every 12 months Children, age 0 to 18 Two every 12 months Parents and caretaker relatives One every 12 months New Adult Group- age 19 through 64, not pregnant, not enrolled in Medicare, and not eligible for any other group One every 12 months Pregnant Women One per pregnancy Aid Code Description FPL Level of Benefits P1 Infants, up to age 1 At or below 208% Full P2 Parent/Caretaker relative At or below 109% Full P3 Adults At or below 138% Full P4 Pregnant women At or below 213% Limited to ambulatory prenatal services H6 Infants age 0 to 1 209 – 266% Full H7 Children age 1 to 5 At or below 142% Full H8 Children age 6 to18 At or below 133% Full H9 Children age 1 to 5 143 – 266% Full H0 Children age 6 to 18 134 – 266% Full County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Hospital Presumptive Eligibility (HPE) Number Page 05.22 2 of 3 HPE Enrollment Period and Limitations The HPE period begins on the day the applicant is determined eligible for PE and ends on the last day of the following month, if a Medi-Cal application is not submitted for ongoing eligibility. If a Medi- Cal application is submitted prior to the last day of the PE period, PE will continue until a final determination is c ompleted. HPE providers are required to provide HPE enrolled individuals an insurance affordability application (also known as a Medi-Cal application) prior to leaving the hospital. MEDS is programmed to automatically terminate HPE beneficiaries who reach their PE period unless MEDS has a record of a pending application. HPE enrollment period limitations are as follows: Note: If an applicant is not eligible for PE due to exceeding t he related enrollment limitation, a full Medi-Cal application s hall be processed, including an evaluation of the need for a retr oactive application. Aid Codes The following HPE aid codes are used by hospitals to issue HPE benefits to eligible individuals based on description and FPL: 4E Former foster care youth age 18 through 25 No income screening Full County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Hospital Presumptive Eligibility (HPE) Number Page 05.22 3 of 3 Procedure: Medi-Cal applications submitted from HPE beneficiaries must be processed in accordance with our business application processing procedures making sure HPE aid codes are updated on MEDS upon case disposition. Other Program Impacts: None References: ACWDL 14-14 MEDIL I 15-26 MEDIL I 15-31 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 04/30/2019. Release Date: 04/11/2016

title: Section 1 - Institutional Status
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageInstitutional Status 06.01.01 1 of 5 Revision Date: 2/1/2023 Background: This section provides staff with instructions for the determination of Medi-Cal eligibility for people in institutions. Inmates of a public institution who apply for Medi-Cal must be evaluated. Residence in a public institution does not disqualify applicants from Medi-Cal in and of itself. However, if the inmate meets all other eligibility standards, eligibility must be granted and immediately suspended until they are no longer considered inmates of a public institution (see MPG 06.02.05 for suspension policies). Inmates who receive inpatient care off the grounds of the facility who are otherwise Medi-Cal eligible are eligible to the Medi-Cal Inmate Eligibility Program ((MCIEP), see Article 6, section 2). MCIEP is limited to services inmates receive off the grounds of the institution. Residents of specific inmate facilities, such as the Male Community Reentry Program (MCRP) and Custody to Community Transitional Reentry Programs (CCTRP), are considered inmates of a public institution. This section was updated with the clarification that MCRP and CCTRP residents are no longer considered inmates of a public institution when they reach the third phase of the program. Policy: A. Definition of Public Institutions The following are identified as public institutions: •State or Federal prisons •Correctional facilities •County, city, or tribal jails •Detention centers •California Youth Authority (CYA) camps •Residential facilities located on the grounds of or adjacent to any large public institution •Correctional or holding facilities for prisoners or individuals being held under court order as witnesses •Detention facilities, camps, training schools, or any other facility for children determined to be delinquent •Education or vocational training institutions that provide an accredited program for its residents •Alternative custody facilities where the residents are serving their sentence in a community setting (for example, CCTRP, Enhanced Alternative Custody Program (EACP), Female Offender Treatment and Employment Program (FOTEP), MCRP, and county work furlough Programs) NOTE: People who reside in public institutions to receive educational or vocational training provided by the facility (for example, a state school for the blind) are not considered “inmates” of a public institution.. B. Facilities that are not Public Institutions County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageInstitutional Status 06.01.01 2 of 5 The following facilities are not public institutions: •A medical institution •An intermediate care facility •A publicly operated residence that serves no more than 16 residents •A child care facility that accommodates no more than 25 children •An institution for intellectually disabled people or persons with related conditions (chronic disability attributed to cerebral palsy, epilepsy, or any other condition other than mental illness closely related to intellectual disability). Eligibility and placement are usually through the San Diego Regional Center •A community care facility which is maintained and operated to provide 24-hour non-medical care for children and/or adults, including but not limited to, the physically handicapped, mentally impaired, incompetent persons, and neglected or abused children C. Individuals Considered Inmates of a Public Institution 1. An inmate in a prison or a county, city, or tribal jail Note: This includes inmates being held prior to arraignment, conviction, or sentencing. It does not include individuals who are out on bail or their own recognizance 2. An individual, who is incarcerated, but who can leave prison or jail on work release or work furlough and must return at specific times (work furlough) 3. A minor in a juvenile detention center prior to his or her disposition (judgment) due to a criminal activity of the minor 4. A minor who is placed in a detention or correctional facility after detention, including a youth ranch, forestry camp, or home which is part of the criminal justice system 5. A minor placed on juvenile intensive probation by a juvenile court with specific conditions of release, including residence in a juvenile detention center 6. A minor placed on probation by a juvenile court or on juvenile intensive probation to a secure treatment facility contracted with the juvenile detention center if the secure treatment facility is part of the criminal justice system 7. Residents of alternative custody facilities where the inmate serves their sentence in a community setting (for example, CCTRP, MCRP, or work furlough). NOTE: Individuals in county facilities may be eligible to MCIEP if otherwise Medi-Cal eligible. CCTRP and MCRP residents who are in phase three or four of the program are no longer considered inmates of a public institution D. Individuals Not Considered Inmates of a Public Institution 1. An individual who, after arrest but before booking, is escorted by police to a hospital for medical treatment and held under guard 2. An individual in prison or jail who transfers temporarily (one to two months) to a halfway house or residential treatment facility prior to a formal probation release order 3. An individual who is released from prison or jail, but who is on probation, parole, or release order with one of the following conditions: •Home arrest •Work release •Community service •Outpatient treatment County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageInstitutional Status 06.01.01 3 of 5 •Inpatient treatment 4. An individual released from prison or jail under a court probation order due to a medical emergency 5. A minor held in a juvenile detention center for care, protection, or in the best interest of the child if: •It is prior to disposition (judgment), and •There is a specific plan for that minor that makes the stay at the detention center temporary (one to two months) •This could include those juveniles awaiting placement but still physically present in juvenile hall 6. A minor placed on probation or juvenile intensive probation by a juvenile court, with home arrest restrictions 7. A minor placed on probation or juvenile intensive probation to a secure treatment facility which contracts with the juvenile detention center, if the secure treatment facility is not part of the criminal justice system. This includes juveniles who become wards of the court and are placed in a 24-hour non-medical residential facility, which provides counseling and other rehabilitative services 8. A minor placed on probation or juvenile intensive probation with treatment in one of the following as a condition of probation: •A psychiatric hospital •A residential treatment center •As an outpatient 9. Individuals with tuberculosis who are under an order of detention in one of the following facilities to protect public health: •A residential treatment center •A skilled nursing facility •A county, city or tribal jail awaiting placement for treatment 10.Individuals in a CCTRP or MCRP program who have reached phase three or four of the program E. Suspension of Benefits When an inmate of a public institution applies for Medi-Cal, they must be evaluated. If the inmate is Medi-Cal eligible, benefits must be granted and immediately suspended until release. NOTE: If an applicant reports an address that is known to be a CCTRP, EACP, FOTEP, or MCRP, Human Services Specialists (HSS) must verify the institutional status of the applicant. Some of these facilities have more than one program and some program residents may be considered inmates of a public institution, and some may not. CCTRP and MCRP have four phases. Once inmates reach the transitional phase three, they are no longer considered inmates of a public institution and their eligibility must be granted or existing benefits unsuspended as of their phase 3 start date. The HSS may accept the phase listed on application cover letters from CCTRP and MCRP as verification of the phase. The HSS can also accept the customer attestation of the phase three start date. If the customer is unsure of the phase three start date, use the report date as the start date. F. Medi-Cal Eligibility for Penal Codes Related to Competency to Stand Trial County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageInstitutional Status 06.01.01 4 of 5 Penal Code Description Eligibility 1367 Applies to individuals charged with a misdemeanor, but who are incompetent to stand trial. Provides that “A person cannot be tried or adjudged to punishment while that person is mentally incompetent.” If a judge finds reason to believe that a defendant may be incompetent to stand trial, they may order that the defendant be referred for 72-hour treatment and evaluation. During the evaluation period, the defendant is entitled to Medi-Cal benefits if otherwise eligible. If the result of the evaluation is that the individual is to be placed in a mental health facility for treatment, they may be entitled to receive Medi-Cal benefits if otherwise eligible. 1370 Applies to individuals charged with a serious felony who are placed in a mental health facility because they were determined incompetent to stand trial. If an individual is still determined to be incompetent after the placement period, a Murphy Conservatorship may be established. An individual under a Murphy Conservatorship is eligible to Medi-Cal benefits if otherwise eligible. 1372 Applies to defendants who have regained competency. When a defendant returns to court with a certification that competence has been regained, the court will determine if the person is to be released on bail. An individual released on bail is eligible to receive Medi-Cal benefits if otherwise eligible. If not released on bail and incarcerated, the individual would not be eligible for Medi-Cal benefits. References: MEPM 6A, 6B, 6C, 6I ACWDL 93-55, 14-26 MPG LTR 492, 808 MEDILs 17-23, 18-10, 22-15 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 2/28/2026 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageInstitutional Status 06.01.01 5 of 5 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Incarcerated Customers – State Prison Pre-Release Applications Number Page 06.02.01 1 of 2 Revision Date: 8/1/2024 Background: The Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) entered into an agreement with the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation (CDCR) to facilitate the completion , and submission, of Medi-Cal applications for incarcerated individuals , prior to their release. The intent of this agreement is to allow i ncarcerated individuals timely access to Medi-Cal benefits upon their release. Purpose: To provide policy guidance for the State Prison Pre-Release application program. Policy: A. Eligibility Pre-release applications are submitted to the county by State Prison Staff via the Transitional Case Management Program (TCMP), around 90 days prior to release. These applications must be processed using existing Medi-Cal policies and procedures, however, submission of an application earlier than 90 days prior to release is not grounds for denial. The incarcerated individual must be evaluated for the month of release, and the beginning date of aid will be the first of the month of release. B. Verifications The chart below summarizes how common eligibility verification requirements can be met as part of the pre - release application process: Verification Requirement Household Size The household size is based on the household of the incarcerated individual upon release. Income Reported income must be verified using current Medi -Cal rules (reasonable compatibility with the Federal Data Services Hub information), however if the income is not reasonably compatible and the i ncarcerated individual cannot resolve discrepancy due to incarceration, grant eligibility based on the customer’s statement and resolve the discrepancy upon their release using the existing request for information timelines. Identity Verification that the incarcerated person in custody from the cover sheet or statement from the facility can be used to verify identity if there is no other evidence available (e.g. Social Security Administration (SSA) verification) or if there is no contradicting evidence to what is stated on the application. Deficit Reduction Act (DRA) Citizenship and Identity Verification is required but consider that eligibility can be granted pending verification of citizenship and identity. Asset Verification (Non-MAGI) Verification may be obtained after release if the reported property does not make the applicant ineligible. Follow existing request for information timelines to obtain verification after release. Residence Incarcerated status may be used to verify California residence if all the following applies: • No other evidence is available. • CDCR confirms that the applicant is in custody in a CA correctional facility (statement on the cover letter). • The incarcerated individual declares an intent to reside in CA. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Incarcerated Customers – State Prison Pre-Release Applications Number Page 06.02.01 2 of 2 • There is no evidence to suggest the incarcerated individual will not be a CA resident in the month of release. Social Security Number (SSN) Must be verified in accordance with regular Medi-Cal rules. Household Tax Filer Status Tax Filer Status must be determined based on existing Medi-Cal rules. If the incarcerated individual is... Then... a member of a household, and returning to that household, add the incarcerated individual back to the active family case effective the month of release. single, or tax filing status is uncertain, treat the individual as a single individual. C. Confidentiality • During incarceration, share information only with the authorized representative listed on the single streamlined application (usually the TCMP worker listed on the cover letter). • After release, share information only with the individual, and or entity listed on the CDCR form 7385 -A (if provided). Procedure: Process State Prison Pre -Release applications using procedures in Processing Guide 13 – Incarcerated Customers References: ACWDLs 09-16, 14-26, and 24-04 MEDIL 16-19 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 8/31/2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Incarcerated Customers – State Prison MCIEP Number Page 06.02.02 1 of 2 Revision Date: 8/1/2024 Background: The California Prison Health Care Services (CPHCS) is responsible for the cost of medical care of individuals incarcerated in California state prisons. Federal Medicaid funds are available to pay for inpatient medical care received by incarcerated individuals outside of the correctional facility. The Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation (CDCR), the Department of HealthCare Services (DHCS) and CPHCS have developed the State Prison Medi-Cal Inmate Eligibility Program (MCIEP) to obtain the maximum number of federal dollars for the medical care of incarcerated individuals. When an incarcerated individual receives inpatient medical care: • CPHCS staff forwards applications, verifications, and medical records for State Program Disability Determination Service Division (DDSD) applications to DHCS. • DHCS performs eligibility determinations and forwards eligibility information to CPHCS. NOTE: All eligibility determinations for State Prison MCIEP are completed by DHCS. Purpose: Provide information about State Prison MCIEP and the county’s role. Policy: A. Eligibility Requirements Incarcerated individuals are eligible to MCIEP if they meet the following criteria: • Are incarcerated in a California State Prison. • Receive inpatient hospital services off the grounds of the correctional facility. • Are hospitalized for 24 hours or more. • Receive allowable inpatient hospital services. • Meet all Medi-Cal eligibility requirements such as linkage, deprivation, alien/citizenship status, income and property. B. Aid Codes When an individual incarcerated in a state prison is found eligible to MCIEP, DHCS will place the beneficiary in one of the following aid codes: • F1 - Title XIX, Medi-Cal Zero Share of cost (SOC) State Incarcerated Individuals. • G1- Title XIX, Medi-Cal SOC State Incarcerated Individuals. • F2 - Title XIX/Title XXI Medi-Cal Zero SOC Undocumented State Incarcerated Individuals. • G2 – Title XIX/Title XXI Medi-Cal SOC Undocumented State Incarcerated Individuals. C. County Participation As part of the state prison MCIEP, DHCS refers the following i ncarcerated individuals to the county via the MCIEP transmittal form when: • Case clearance of an incarcerated individual reveals an open Medi-Cal case for the individual. • Infants are born to MCIEP eligible incarcerated individual. • MCIEP beneficiaries are released from prison while on the MCIEP program. The below chart lists required actions related to state MCIEP: Situation Action County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Incarcerated Customers – State Prison MCIEP Number Page 06.02.02 2 of 2 A parolee is released from Prison while eligible to MCIEP. Complete an ex parte review and redetermination. Infant is born to MCIEP eligible incarcerated individual. When an incarcerated individual is MCIEP eligible at the time of the ir infant’s birth, the child is automatically deemed eligible for Medi -Cal without a separate application. There is an open Medi-Cal case for incarcerated individual. When DHCS notifies the county of an MCIEP applicant that is active on a county Medi -Cal case, suspend the incarcerated individual, reevaluate the rest of the case members, and send timely notice for any changes. There is interaction with the prerelease application process. If a MCIEP beneficiary requests a pre -release application from the county through the pre- release application process, that new application must be denied, and the ex parte determination completed since the applicant already has active Medi-Cal through MCIEP. A parolee applies for Medi-Cal. MCIEP beneficiaries released from custody within 12 months of their MCIEP application are not required to complete a new Medi -Cal application. When a case clearance at the county reveals that an applicant has eligibility under MCIEP, request the case file from DHCS and complete the ex parte determination. Request the case file via secure email to MCIEP@dhcs.ca.gov. Procedure: Procedures for processing the MCIEP referrals received from DHCS can be found in Processing Guide 13 – Incarcerated Customers, Section 3. References: ACWDLs 11-27, 14-26, and 24-04 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 8/31/2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Incarcerated Customers – County Jail Pre-Release Applications Number Page 06.02.03 1 of 1 Revision Date: 8/1/2024 Background: State law allows counties to assist individuals incarcerated in county jail with their applications for health insurance affordability programs and clarified that counties can process applications for incarcerated individuals while they are in custody . Customers incarcerated in a correctional facility who apply for Medi -Cal must be evaluated. Residence in a correctional facility does not disqualify applicants from Medi-Cal, however if otherwise eligible their eligibility must be suspended until they are no longer incarcerated. This section was updated to include the requirement to notify the Sheriff’s department of the outcome of the eligibility determination. Purpose: To provide policy guidance related to county jail pre-release applications. Policy: Pre-release applications are submitted around 90 days prior to the applicant’s release, are processed using existing Medi -Cal policies and procedures, and the incarcerated individual is evaluated for the month of release. The county jail may submit an application at any time, do not deny an application if submitted earlier than 90 days prior to release. Follow the state pre -release verification guidance in 06.02.02.C when processing county jail pre-release applications. Forward applications for individuals incarcerated in county jails releasing to other counties to the county of release. When an application is received for a customer active in another county, request an inter-county transfer. Notify the Sheriff Department of the result of the application and if the eligibility determination is not expected to be complete prior to the customer’s release date via secure email. Refer to processing guide 13 – Incarcerated Customers, section 2 for more detailed information. Procedure: When processing county pre -release applications, follow procedures in Processing Guide 13 – Incarcerated Customers, Section 2. References: ACWDLs 14-26, 22-27, and 24-04 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 8/31/2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Incarcerated Customers – County MCIEP Number Page 06.02.04 1 of 2 Revision Date: 8/1/2024 Background: The County Medi-Cal Inmate Eligibility Program ( MCIEP) provides limited Medi -Cal coverage to otherwise eligible individuals incarcerated in county jail , who receive acute inpatient hospital services provided off the grounds of the county correctional facility. The Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) provided procedures for reporting Social Security Income (SSI) Medi-Cal eligible MCIEP applicants to S ocial Security Administration (SSA) . SSA now has their own method for gathering this information, so t his section was revised to remove the requirement to send MCIEP applicant information to SSA. Purpose: To provide policy guidance related to county MCIEP. Policy: A. Eligibility MCIEP is limited scope Medi -Cal coverage that covers incarcerated customers for inpatient care received off the grounds of the facility. To be eligible for County MCIEP, an individual incarcerated in a county jail must be otherwise eligible for Medi-Cal (following the current Medi-Cal policies, procedures, and order of evaluation). NOTE: Incarcerated customers are not eligible to Advanced Premium Tax Credits (APTC). B. Verifications Existing Medi-Cal verification rules apply to MCIEP applications. The chart below lists clarifications received from The Department of Health Care Services ( DHCS) and modifications of the policy allowed for MCIEP applicants: Subject Policy Household Size • The household size is based on the household of the incarcerated individual , including their family at home. • The parent of an incarcerated juvenile may claim the child as a tax dependent , if the child lived with their parents for more than half the year. Income For Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) evaluations c ount all known income for the incarcerated individual, including: • Income from a spouse at home in the applicant’s tax household. • Income in jail accounts including retirement pensions, Veteran’s Administration funds, donations or wages received while incarcerated. • Income shown in Income and Eligibility Verification System (IEVS). • Income reported on the application. In-Kind Income For Non-MAGI evaluations, housing, utilities, food and clothing provided by the facility are considered in-kind income. Identity Verification that the incarcerated individual is in custody from the cover sheet can be used to verify identity if there is no other evidence available (e.g. SSA verification) and there is no contradicting evidence to what is stated on the application. Deficit Reduction Act Citizenship and Identity Verification is required but remember that eligibility can be granted pending verification of citizenship and identity. Residence Incarceration Status may be used to verify California residence if no other verification is available. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Incarcerated Customers – County MCIEP Number Page 06.02.04 2 of 2 C. Annual Redetermination The Period of Eligibility for MCIEP is 12 months. In carcerated individuals will remain active on MCIEP as long as they are incarcerated and otherwise eligible to Medi-Cal. Annual Redetermination requirements apply to in carcerated individuals covered under MCIEP. Changes in circumstances, such as aging out of the MAGI new adult group , must be processed according to existing redetermination policy. If the individual becomes Medi -Cal ineligible, MCIEP must be discontinued with timely notice. D. Notice of Action Notice of Action for MCIEP must be sent to the authorized representative, not the incarcerated individual. E. Interaction with Suspension of Benefits When an incarcerated individual is suspended from Medi- Cal due to incarceration and subsequently receives inpatient care services, they may be placed on the MCIEP aid code based on their previous Medi-Cal aid code. F. Incarcerated Individuals Released while MCIEP Active A new application is not required. Verify continuing eligibility through an ex parte review and Medi-Cal eligibility redetermination. G. County of Responsibility The county of responsibility for County MCIEP is the county where the individual is incarcerated. If San Diego receives an MCIEP application for an individual incarcerated in another county, workers will complete the courtesy application process by forwarding the application, and all information collected, to the county of responsibility within 15 days of the application date. If the incarcerated individual has a suspended Medi -Cal case in another county, coordinate with that county to lift the suspense, and then process the MCIEP application. Only the county that im plemented the suspense can lift it. Procedure: When processing MCIEP applications, follow the application procedures in P rocessing Guide 13 – Incarcerated Customers, Section 4. References: ACWDLs 13-18, 14-26, 24-04 MEDILs 16-23, 17-20 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 8/31/2027. Approval for Release: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Incarcerated Customers – County MCIEP Number Page 06.02.04 3 of 2 Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Incarcerated Customers – Suspending Benefits for County and State Incarcerated Individuals Number Page 06.02.05 1 of 2 Revision Date: 8/1/2024 Background: Suspense policy requires that rather than terminating Medi-Cal eligibility, it must be suspended for incarcerated individuals who were Medi-Cal eligible at the time of incarceration. The suspense policy started with juveniles and expanded to adult county and state incarcerated individuals effective 1/1/14. Suspension does not apply to adults incarcerated prior to 1/1/14. This section was updated to include new suspension timeframes and policies related to the Support Act. Purpose: To provide policy guidance related to suspending benefits for incarcerated individuals. Policy: A. Eligibility Incarcerated customers who were active Medi -Cal at the time of their incarceration must have their benefits suspended during incarceration and then restored without a new application upon release. Suspense is not required until the incarcerated individual has been in custody for more than 28 days. No suspense is required if the customer is released by the 28 th day of incarceration. The suspense is active the date of incarceration or the date the county is notified plus ten-day notice. Workers can accept customer statement of release date. B. Time limit There is no time limit for suspense and incarcerated individual s must remain suspended for the duration of their incarceration, however if an incarcerated individual is suspended for over a year, a redetermination is required at release if their eligibility has not been redetermined within a year of release. C. Pre-Release Applications If an incarcerated individual applies for Medi -Cal they can have that eligibility evaluated, granted if otherwise eligible for Medi-Cal, and then immediately suspended for the duration of their incarceration. D. Removing the Suspension Eligibility must be restored for suspended incarcerated individuals without a new application, effective the date the County receives the report that the customer has been released, or the date they are no longer considered incarcerated. The suspense lift must be processed within one day of notification. If the suspense lasted longer than a year, a redetermination must be completed using the ex parte process. E. Redetermination Customers in cases by themselves are not required to complete an annual redetermination while incarcerated and their eligibility must not be discontinued unless they are no longer incarcerated or deceased. Suspended customers in cases with family may be discontinued if the family is found no longer Medi -Cal eligible during redetermination. This includes cases discontinued for failure to complete the annual redetermination. Suspended individuals may be transitioned to new aid codes when there is a change in circumstances such as aging-out of a Medi-Cal aid code. If an individual has been suspended for more than one year, they must complete a redetermination upon release if they haven’t had their eligibility redetermined within a year of release. F. Notice of Action County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Incarcerated Customers – Suspending Benefits for County and State Incarcerated Individuals Number Page 06.02.05 2 of 2 Suspense notices must be sent to the home in cases where the incarcerated person is in a case with family, to the jail when the customer is in a case by themselves, or an authorized representative if applicable. G. Inter-County Transfer (ICT) Some incarcerated individuals in San Diego may have active or suspended benefits in another county. When San Diego workers receive notice that a customer active in another county is incarcerated in San Diego, contact the other county and let them know of the incarceration date so the other county can suspend benefits. When an incarcerated individual has suspended benefits in another county is set to release in San Diego, request the other county lifts the suspension and sends an ICT. Procedures: Procedures for processing suspensions are in Processing Guide 13 – Incarcerated Customers, section 5. References: ACWDLs 13-18, 14-26, 21-22, 22-26, and 24-04 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 8/31/2027. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Incarcerated Customers – Incarceration Verification Program Number Page 06.02.06 1 of 2 Revision Date: August 1, 2026 Background: Federal law states that federal funds cannot be used for medical services provided to incarcerated individuals, except for covered inpatient services received off the grounds of the correctional facility. The Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) implemented the Incarcerated Verification Program ( IVP) using the Nationwide Prisoner Match (NPM) system to identify individuals who must have their eligibility suspended due to incarceration. Purpose: To provide policy guidance related to the IVP. This section was revised to include changes to the IVP process. Policy: A. NPM Matching Process The NPM matches Medi -Cal beneficiary information with the Social Security Administration’s (SSA) Prisoner Update Program System database which contains data from jails, prisons and incarceration facilities. The NPM is the system for identifying individuals who must be suspended due to incarceration. The below table summarizes the IVP process. Step Action 1 DHCS completes a Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS) data match with the NPM and California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation (CDCR) to identify incarcerated Medi-Cal beneficiaries. 2 DHCS verifies the incarceration status of the matches through correctional facility websites and a third-party historical incarceration data network. 3 DHCS sends the county the list of verified incarcerated customers. This list is incorporated into the monthly NPM list published on the monthly reports section of the Management Reporting SharePoint. 4 Human Service Specialists suspend eligibility and notify the customer per suspense requirements in Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 06.02.05. B. Incarcerated Juveniles The IVP focuses on incarcerated adults and does not include juveniles (individuals under age 21). Incarcerated juveniles are considered temporarily absent from the home and still part of the tax household unless there is evidence to the contrary. C. Treatment of Other Household Members The eligibility of other household members must be re -evaluated, and changes made with timely notice if the incarcerated adult is removed from the Non -MAGI Medi-Cal household due to no longer living in the home. Incarceration does not necessarily mean that the customer is removed from the MAGI household as the Internal Revenue Service ( IRS) considers them temporarily absent and expected to return unless there is evidence to the contrary. MAGI Tax Household rules apply. D. Reinstatement Upon release from the correctional facility, follow the suspension lift policies in MPG 06.02.05.D and procedures in Processing Guide 13, section 5. Procedure: Procedures for processing suspensions are in Processing Guide 13.
