title: Section 3 - Institution for Mental Diseases
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageInstitution for Mental Diseases (IMD) 6.3 1 of 2 Revision Date: April 9, 2020 Background: An IMD is defined as a hospital, nursing facility, or other institution with more than 16 beds that is primarily engaged in providing diagnosis, treatment, or care of people with mental diseases. If a facility functions primarily as a facility established and maintained for the care and treatment of people with mental diseases, then it is an IMD; it does not have to be licensed as such. An institution for the developmentally disabled is not an IMD. Purpose: This section has been written in the current format; the rules for people age 22 have been corrected to match the State rules. The prior section stated that people age 22 could no longer get Medi-Cal in an IMD, which conflicted with the rest of the section. Policy: IMD Eligibility: People between 21 and 65 years of age in IMDs can receive Medi-Cal if otherwise eligible. Note: There is no federal financial participation for these people. Medi-Cal Covered Services in an IMD: Services covered for people 21 to 65 years of age in an IMD include the following: •Facility charges (the daily bed rate) •Medi-Cal covered physician services •Prescription drugs •Laboratory services •X-ray services •Dental services •Vision services •Psychiatrist services •Psychologist services Note: Services not related to the IMD (for example, hospital, emergency room, etc.) would be covered. Disability Determination: Determine the Medi-Cal eligibility of a person admitted to an IMD or who is a resident of an IMD as shown in the table below: If disability … Then … Has not been established, Initiate a referral to Disability Determination Services Division (DDSD) for a disability determination. Place the person in Aid Code 53 until a determination has been completed (See MPG 5.4 for instructions on DDSD referrals). Has been established, Place the individual in the appropriate disability aid code. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageInstitution for Mental Diseases (IMD) 6.3 2 of 2 Individuals 21 and 22 Years of Age in an IMD: If a Medi-Cal beneficiary in an IMD has been receiving psychiatric inpatient hospital services prior to his/her 21st birthday and continues to receive these services until age 22, he/she remains entitled to receive Medi-Cal benefits. Use Aid Code 82 (Medically Indigent Child). A Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS) hold and an alert will be generated at age 21 indicating that a special Eligibility Status Action Code (ESAC) is required for this age group and age. Submit an on-line request to the Family Resource Center (FRC) MEDS clerk to reactivate the person on MEDS using aid code 82 and assigning a special ESAC code of “4” or “9.” Set a Case Alert for when the person turns 22 to evaluate for other Medi-Cal programs. At age 22, the above person can no longer receive Medi-Cal in Aid Code 82, and their Medi-Cal eligibility must be reevaluated. If determined eligible, activate them in the appropriate aid code. Procedure: See above. Program Impacts: None. References: MEPM 6E Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by March 31, 2023 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations

title: Section 4 - Fleeing Felons
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageFleeing Felons 6.4 1 of 1 Revision Date: August 1, 2020 Background: Fleeing felons are not eligible for CalWORKs, Supplemental Security Income/State Supplemental Program (SSI/SSP), CalFresh, or General Relief (GR). However, if otherwise eligible, fleeing felons are eligible to receive Medi-Cal benefits. Purpose: This section has been written in the current format; all references to drug felons, which is a separate status than fleeing felons, have been removed because the programs listed above no longer deny benefits to drug felons. Policy: Under federal regulations, a fleeing felon is defined as an individual who is “fleeing to avoid prosecution or custody or confinement after conviction … for a crime … which is a felony under the laws of the place from which the individual flees, or … (who is) violating a condition of probation or parole under Federal or State law.” To receive Medi-Cal, fleeing felons are subject to all the eligibility requirements of the program. If otherwise eligible, fleeing felons are eligible to receive Medi-Cal benefits until they have been booked, sentenced, or incarcerated. When any of these occur, Medi-Cal eligibility is suspended (see MPG 6.2.5, Suspending Benefits for Inmates). Procedure: None. Program Impacts: None. References: MEPM 6G Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by July 31, 2023 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Eligibility Operations

title: Section 5 - Juveniles in Public Institutions
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageIncarcerated Juveniles 06.05.01 1 of 2 Effective/Revision Date: 8/1/2024 Background: In determining the Medi-Cal eligibility of a juvenile (under the age of 18) in a facility, staff must consider both the disposition status of the juvenile and the type of facility they are in. Customers incarcerated in a correctional facility who apply for Medi-Cal must be evaluated. Residence in a correctional facility does not disqualify applicants from Medi-Cal, however if otherwise eligible their eligibility must be suspended until they are no longer considered incarcerated. Incarcerated individuals receiving inpatient or mental health services outside of the correctional facility may be eligible to limited scope coverage that pays only for the inpatient or mental health services. This section was updated to include suspense language. Purpose: This section provides staff with policy guidance for how to determine Medi-Cal eligibility for Juveniles in correctional facilities. Policy: A. Disposition Disposition is the decision made by the court for the juvenile’s welfare. A disposition order is the court decision that the minor will be placed in foster care, sentenced, placed on probation, or released either temporarily or permanently. When the juvenile is determined a “Ward of the Court” and is awaiting foster care placement and not awaiting sentencing for a criminal violation of law, the juvenile is eligible for Medi-Cal. (See MPG Article 5, Section 12 for information on Foster Care). B. Status Prior to Disposition •If a juvenile is in a detention center due to criminal activity, they are considered incarcerated must have their eligibility suspended, if currently active. •If they are in a detention center for care, protection and/or in the best interest of the child and there is a specific plan that makes the stay temporary (1 to 2 months) then they are not considered incarcerated. C. Status After Disposition •Juveniles on intensive probation with a plan of release, which includes residence in a correctional facility, are considered incarcerated and must have Medi-Cal benefits suspended until released. •Juveniles placed or awaiting placement, on intensive probation in a residential facility, are not considered incarcerated if the facility is not part of the criminal justice system. D. Facility Publicly operated community residences that serve no more than 16 residents are not considered correctional facilities, and juveniles in these facilities are entitled to Medi-Cal if otherwise eligible. These facilities may be psychiatric nursing facilities licensed by the Department of Mental Health or other community care facilities. Example A juvenile is detained for criminal activity and is placed on probation with specific conditions of release, including a stay of 30 days or longer at a correctional facility. The facility is identified as a juvenile detention center, not a treatment center. Upon release from this detention center, they would be placed on probation with their parent or guardian. The juvenile is considered an incarcerated individual and must have their benefits suspended until release. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageIncarcerated Juveniles 06.05.01 2 of 2 References: ACWDL 13-18, 22-27, 24-04 MEM Letter 241 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 8/31/2027 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageSuspension of Benefits for Incarcerated Juveniles 06.05.02 1 of 1 Effective/Revision Date: 8/1/2024 Background: Medi-Cal eligibility must be suspended for incarcerated individual in correctional facilities under the age 21 who were Medi-Cal eligible at the time of incarceration. This section was updated to include the extension of juvenile suspension past one year. Purpose: This section provides requirements for suspending benefits for incarcerated juveniles. Policy: Juveniles incarcerated in a correctional facility must have their benefits suspended and not discontinued until their release. Suspense only ends on the release date, death, or if they are no longer considered juveniles (under age 21 or age 26 if former foster youth). Annual and change in circumstances redeterminations are not required for the juvenile while incarcerated, but the worker shall update to the appropriate aid code if notified of a change such as aging out of a specific aid type. An ex parte redetermination is only required at release if one hasn’t been completed in the past year. Incarcerated juveniles are considered temporarily absent from the home and still part of the tax household unless there is evidence to the contrary. Procedure: Refer to Processing Guide 13 – Incarcerated Customers for suspension procedures. References: ACWDLs 10-06, 14-26, 21-22, and 24-04 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 8/31/2027 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageIncarcerated Juvenile Pre-Release Application Process 06.05.03 1 of 1 Effective/Revision Date: 8/1/2024 Background: Juveniles incarcerated in county correctional facilities (Juvenile Hall, a camp or ranch) for more than 30 days may begin the Medi-Cal application process while incarcerated so that they may have Medi-Cal eligibility immediately upon release, if possible. This section was revised to include direction to grant and immediately suspend eligibility when there is no release date on the referral form. Purpose: To provide staff with policy guidance for the juvenile pre-release application process. Policy: A. Notification The County of San Diego Department of Probation will notify the incarcerated individual’s parents during intake that they intend to obtain Medi-Cal for the incarcerated individual. If the parent requests an application or there is no response within 30 days, the Department will send referral form 14-88 to HHSA to Self-Sufficiency services to evaluate at the time of intake. B. Evaluation If there is an active case, suspense procedures apply. If there is no active case, it should be treated as a mailin application request with the referral date serving as the date of application and the release date as the beginning date of aid. Juveniles with no release date on the referral shall be evaluated and if eligible, granted and immediately suspended until a release date is communicated by the Department of Probation. C. Communication with Department of Probation Use form 14-88 HHSA to communicate to the San Diego County Probation Department the outcome of the eligibility determination or if the determination cannot be completed prior to the release date, at least ten days prior to the scheduled release via secure email to the probation contact on the form. D. Release Date Changes When a release date changes, the Probation Department will send a modified referral form with the new date. Change the beginning date of aid to the new release date. NOTE: Some individuals may have shorter incarcerations and the referral form will reach the HSS very close to the release date. The HSS must make every effort to grant the case prior to release. E. Notice of Action When notifying the incarcerated juvenile’s family of granting or suspense of benefits, send a copy of all notices to the youth in the county correctional facility as well if the address is known. Send notices for incarcerated juveniles in cases by themselves or adults incarcerated in a juvenile facility to the correctional facility if known, if not then use the last known address. Procedure: Suspension procedures are in the Incarcerated Customers Processing Guide section 9. References: ACWDL 07-34 and 24-04 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 8/31/2027 County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageIncarcerated Juvenile Pre-Release Application Process 06.05.03 1 of 1 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: Section 1 - Citizenship
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageCitizenship 07.01.01 1 of 4 Revision Date: 05/01/2022 Background: The DRA of 2005 requires citizens of the United States to provide acceptable evidence of citizenship status and identity to receive full-scope Medi-Cal benefits. With the implementation of ACA, electronic verification of citizenship status through the federal data hub via the California Healthcare Eligibility Enrollment and Retention System (CalHEERS) is acceptable evidence of citizenship status and no other documentation is required. DRA requirements were changed to allow issuance of full-scope Medi-Cal benefits to otherwise eligible U.S. citizen applicants during their Reasonable Opportunity Period (ROP) while they obtain the required citizenship and identity documents. Note: Any reference to “U.S. citizens” should be interpreted as including both U.S. citizens and U.S. nationals for the purpose of this section. Purpose: This section has been revised to incorporate updates Medi-Cal eligibility for customers of the member sovereign states of the Compact of Free Association (COFA). Policy: A customer who is attesting to be a U.S. citizen and has their citizenship electronically verified is eligible to receive full-scope Medi-Cal benefits. See Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 04.02.09 Statement of Citizenship/Non-Citizen Status for more information. A. Definitions for U.S. Citizens: Persons who fall within one of the following categories shall be considered U.S. citizens for Medi-Cal purposes. Category Description People born in one of the fifty United States or the District of Columbia (D.C.)U.S. Citizens/ Nationals People born in the following areas are treated the same as U.S. citizens for Medi- Cal purposes: •American Samoa •Swain’s Island Collectively Naturalized People born in the following areas are treated the same as U.S. citizens for Medi- Cal purposes, if conditions specified in MPG 07.02 Appendix A are met. •Puerto Rico •Guam •U.S. Virgin Islands (St. John, St. Croix, and St. Thomas) •Northern Mariana Islands County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageCitizenship 07.01.01 2 of 4 Acquired Citizenship People born in another country may have acquired citizenship if one or both of their parents were U.S. citizens at the time of birth, and the parent(s) met the requirements for transmitting citizenship. INS must act favorably on an application for Certificate of Citizenship, INS Form N-600, before acquired citizenship is approved. INS Form N-600 is not documentation of acquired citizenship as it merely shows the person has applied for acquired citizenship. Derived Citizenship A child may have derived citizenship if one or both child’s parents become citizens through naturalization before the child’s eighteenth birthday. The child would have to have been a legal permanent resident to obtain derived citizenship through their parent’s naturalized citizenship. Naturalized Citizenship Naturalized U.S. citizens are persons who were born abroad and have since obtained U.S. citizenship through the naturalization process. Many conditions must be met before a person may obtain U.S. citizenship through this process, including: •Legal permanent resident status for at least five years; or •Marriage to a U.S. citizen for at least three years B. Compact Free Association Act (COFA) of 1985: In accordance with the COFA of 1985, citizens of the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM) and the Republic of the Marshall Islands (MIS) may live, work or study in the U.S. without restrictions. They may also qualify for full-scope Medi-Cal benefits if otherwise eligible. As proof that they are citizens of independent nations “freely associated” with the U.S., these “permanent non-immigrants” must present Arrival-Departure Records (Form I-94) annotated either CFA/FSM or CFA/MIS. Effective December 27, 2020, the federal Consolidated Appropriation Act states that individuals from any of the member sovereign states of the COFA are considered Qualified Non-Citizens (QNC) who are exempt from the federal five-year bar on full-scope Medi-Cal eligibility. Customers are eligible for federal funded full-scope Medi-Cal retroactive to December 1, 2020, regardless of age or pregnancy status if they meet all other Medi-Cal eligibility requirements. Verification The most common immigration documents provided from COFA states are: •I-94, Arrival-Departure Records annotated either: oCFA/FSM (Compact of Free Association/Federated States of Micronesia). oCFA/MIS (Compact of Free Association/Republic of the Marshall Islands). oPAL (Republic of Palau). •I-766 Employment Authorization Document (EAD) with a category code of A08 (Citizen of Micronesia, The Marshall Islands, or Palau admitted as a nonimmigrant). Note: A SAVE response for a customer from any of the COFA states may return a COA code of “PI”, which identifies persons from the Pacific Trust Territories. Customers with this COA may or may not be from a COFA state. In these cases, initiate additional SAVE verification steps to confirm whether the customer as a COFA immigration status. When the SAVE verification confirms a customer has COFA immigration status, send a transaction to MEDS to update the Citizen/Alien Indicator code to a “4”. C. American Indians Born in Canada American Indians born in Canada have the right to freely enter and reside in the U.S. if they are at least one-half American Indian ancestry. These persons may qualify for full-scope Medi-Cal benefits if otherwise eligible. Spouses or children of Canadian-born Indians and individuals, whose membership in an Indian tribe or family is created by adoption, may not qualify for this special immigration status unless they are at least fifty percent American Indian ancestry. The requirement does not have to be met at the time of application for the applicant to receive full-scope benefits. This section was updated with directions for when children and young adults up to 26 years of age and adults aged 50 and older fail to provide citizenship or identity documents. Purpose This section provides guidance for verifying Citizenship and Identity. Policy: A customer attesting to be a U.S. citizen (see MPG 04.02.09) and has their citizenship electronically verified is eligible to receive full-scope Medi-Cal benefits. A. Verification Requirements for Applicants Issuance of full-scope or limited-scope benefits is based on the following circumstances at application: If an otherwise eligible U.S. citizen applicant… Then… has CIT/ID status electronically verified provides the required CIT/ID documents issue full-scope benefits is attempting to gather the required CIT/ID documents •establish a ROP •issue full-scope benefits during the ROP •set case alert to review case at the end of the ROP indicates that they will not present the required CIT/ID documents issue limited scope benefits the first of the following month provided that the ten-day notice requirement is met Exception: Grant full-scope benefits to children and young adults up to the age of 26 and adults age of 50 and older. has not met the DRA CIT/ID requirements at the end of the ROP reduce from full-scope to limited-scope with timely notice effective the first of the future month Exception: Grant full-scope benefits to children and young adults up to the age of 26 and adults age of 50 and older. Verification of citizenship AND identity is a one-time activity in that once the verification is requested and provided, it may not be requested again. This would apply to any customer who: •Moves from one county to another. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageVerification Requirements 07.01.02 2 of 4 •Has a break in aid. •Presents evidence that they have met the citizenship and identity requirements in another state’s Medicaid program. Non-citizens are not subject to the citizenship and identity verification requirements specified under DRA. An otherwise eligible non-citizen continues to be evaluated for Medi-Cal using existing procedures regarding acceptable evidence of non-citizen status and identity as specified in MPG 04.07 and 07.03A and 07.03B. B. Exemption from Requirements Medi-Cal customers in any of the following groups are exempt from the citizenship and identity verification requirements as long as they remain recipients of these programs: •Current Supplemental Security Income (SSI) - Title XVI beneficiaries. •Current Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI)-Title II beneficiaries. •Current Medicare - Title XVIII beneficiaries (Parts A, B, C, or D). •Current Social Security Retirement and Survivors Insurance (RSI) Title II beneficiaries who receive those benefits based on their own disability. •Minor Consent Medi-Cal applicants and beneficiaries (Aid Code 7M, 7N, 7P, 7R). •Children who are recipients of Title IV-E or Title IV-B foster care assistance, Foster Care 45 aid code, adoptions assistance, Kinship Guardianship Assistance Payments (KIN-GAP). •Children who are in receipt of Former Foster Youth (FFY) 4M aid code. •Customers who are receiving Medi-Cal Dialysis Only and Dialysis Supplement Program (Aid Code 71). •Customers who are receiving Total Parenteral Nutrition (Aid Code 73). •Customers Indigent Long-Term Care (Aid Code 53). EXCEPTIONS: The following groups are exempt from the citizenship and identity verification requirements indefinitely. •Deemed eligible infants who are born in the U.S. and are therefore citizens (includes children born to non-citizen mothers whose delivery was covered by Medi-Cal). •Children covered under the Abandoned Baby Program who are born in the U.S. and have no documentation. Change in Citizenship Status Medi-Cal beneficiaries who report a change in their citizenship status, such as a legal permanent resident who became a U.S. Citizen, are required to provide acceptable documentation of citizenship AND identity only after ex parte review of all information available, including databases and citizenship status cannot be electronically verified. These beneficiaries, if otherwise eligible, continue to receive the same level of benefits if they are making a good faith effort to provide the required CIT/ID documents. When a beneficiary reports a change in their citizenship status at annual redetermination, certify the redetermination as complete with no reduction in benefits if both of the following conditions are met: •The only outstanding verifications are for citizenship and/or identity. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageVerification Requirements 07.01.02 3 of 4 •The beneficiary is otherwise eligible and is making a good faith effort to provide the required documents. C. Presumptive Eligibility (PE)/Accelerated Enrollment (AE) for Children The requirement to provide verifications of citizenship and identity does not apply to customers at the time presumptive eligibility or accelerated enrollment is established. These programs include: •Presumptive Eligibility for Pregnant Women. •Child Health and Disability Prevention (CHDP) Gateway. •Accelerated Enrollment at the Single Point of Entry. •School Lunch Program. •Presumptive MC eligibility under the Breast and Cervical Cancer Treatment Program (BCCTP). Customers receiving Medi-Cal coverage under one of the above PE or AE program will be placed in the appropriate aid code for on-going eligibility as soon as it is determined that they are otherwise eligible. Issuance of full-scope or limited-scope aid code is based on the customer’s circumstances at application as stated above, MPG 7.2.2B. Note: Presumptive disability relates to one Medi-Cal eligibility requirement and is not the same as Presumptive Eligibility. Customers who are presumptively disabled are not exempt from the DRA citizenship/identity verification requirements. D. CalWORKs The CalWORKs citizenship and identity documentation requirements fulfill the DRA requirements. Therefore, CalWORKs recipients would have met the citizenship and identity verification requirements from the beginning date of their CalWORKs aid and will not be required to provide documentation of their citizenship and identity for on-going Medi-Cal eligibility. This would include customers discontinued from CalWORKs and transitioned to either Transitional Medi-Cal (TMC), Edwards v Kizer (Aid Code 38) or any other Medi-Cal program. NOTE: CalWORKs beneficiaries who receive CalWORKs during the initial 90 days in which they must provide the documents and then lose CalWORKs eligibility for failure to provide the required citizenship document will be subject to electronic verification. If citizenship status cannot be electronically verified, then the beneficiary will: •Be required to provide documentation of citizenship prior to their redetermination date. •Continue to receive full-scope benefits during their ROP if otherwise eligible. Document Standards Citizenship Verification of U.S. citizenship must meet the following conditions: •Show a U.S. place of birth or that the individual is a U.S. citizen or national; AND •Fall within those identified in Desk Aid 119. References: ACWDL 07-12, 08-03, 08-23, 08-19, 08-54, 09-27, 09-65 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 05/31/2025 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAutomated Birth Record Matches 07.01.04 1 of 3 Revision Date: 05/01/2022 Background: Individuals who are born in California and who are not exempt from the citizenship/identity (CIT/ID) verification requirements may have their citizenship verified by an automated data match against state birth records. The data match compares the California birth records against information in the Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS), the Statewide Client Index (SCI), and California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids Information Network (CalWIN). Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide staff with guidance on requesting and processing automated birth record matches. This section has been reformatted as part of a sunset review. Policy: A request for a birth record match can be initiated at the State or County levels. When a successful match occurs, citizenship information is automatically populated to the MEDS INQE screen for the matched individual. Electronic birth records are considered secondary level evidence of citizenship. See Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 07.02.03D for more information on levels of evidence for citizenship. A. State-Run Matches Automated birth record matches are performed by the Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) for existing MC applicants or beneficiaries already known to MEDS. Customers for whom a match was found are not required to provide evidence of citizenship however they are still required to provide evidence of identity. B. Requesting a Birth Record Match When a customer’s citizenship cannot be verified using the Federal Hub via the California Healthcare Eligibility, Enrollment, and Retention System (CalHEERS), a birth record match may be requested to attempt to verify the customer’s citizenship. Submitting a request in CalWIN Human Services Specialists (HSSs) may request a birth record match in CalWIN by submitting an AP19 Transaction. See MPG 07.02.Appendix D for guidance on submitting a birth record match request via CalWIN. Submitting a manual request Staff may submit a manual request for a birth records match by completing form 14-28 and submitting it to the office MEDS operator. The following information must be included in the request: •Individual’s birth name. •Date of birth. •City and/or County of birth. •Mother’s maiden name (optional). •Father’s name (optional). C. Processing Matched Birth Records When a valid birth record match is found, the HSS must mail form DHCS 0006 Proof of Citizenship or Identity Needed for Medi-Cal Applicants and Beneficiaries Who Are U.S. Citizens or Nationals to inform the individual of the result and whether verification of identity is still required. Note: Verification of identity is still required unless the valid birth record match is for a child under 16 years of age. For additional information on verifying identity of an individual under 18 years of age, see MPG 07.02.03F Special Identity Rules for Children Under 18 years Old. D. Processing Unmatched Records When a valid birth record match is not found, HSS must inform the customer born in California of the result and provide the following forms: •DHCS 0006: Proof of Citizenship or Identity Needed for Medi-Cal Applicants and Beneficiaries Who Are U.S. Citizens or Nationals. oIf boxes 3, 4, or 5 are checked on form DHCS 0006, HSS must also provide form DHCS 0004 Request for California Birth Record. Upon receiving additional information from the customer, HSS must submit a new birth record match request. Note: Form DHCS 0004 may be completed telephonically with the customer. If an HSS can complete the form over the phone with the customer, the DHCS 0004 does not need to be mailed to the customer when mailing form DHCS 0006. E. Validating Questionable Copies of California Birth Certificates When a customer presents a questionable copy of a California birth certificate, HSS may use the information contained in the copy to request a birth record match. A successful SSA CIT/ID verification match indicates that the customer’s citizenship and identity have been verified fulfilling DRA CIT/ID verification requirements. SSA CIT/ID verification match is considered secondary level evidence of citizenship and identity. Purpose: The purpose of this section is to provide guidance regarding the use of SSA CIT/ID verification matches to confirm citizenship and identity when completing an ex parte review for a customer who has not met DRA CIT/ID verification requirements. This section has been revised as part of a sunset review. Policy: As part of the ex parte review process, Human Services Specialists (HSSs) must attempt to verify a customer’s citizenship and identity through the SSA CIT/ID verification match before requesting documents from the customer. See Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) section 04.07.11 for more information on completing the ex parte process. A. Overview of SSA CIT/ID Verification Match An automated SSA CIT/ID verification match is performed once a customer’s social security number (SSN) is validated by SSA daily as part of the Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS) SSN validation process and the SSN belongs to a customer who has not met the DRA requirements or who has provided third or fourth level citizenship documents. Once the SSN validation process is complete, if there is a successful SSA CIT/ID match, verification will display on MEDS within two business days from when SSA receives the data from MEDS. Results will be displayed in MEDs in one of the following ways: •A new DRA document type (2Z) will populate in the MEDS INQE screen for customers whose citizenship and identity are verified by the SSA. •MEDS will generate additional alerts. Note: Having a validated SSN does not guarantee that citizenship or identity would be verified through SSA. It is possible that in some cases, SSA may not be able to verify citizenship or identity based on information in their database. B. Who is Subject to Verification Match? The SSA CIT/ID verification match is performed on customers who meet one of the following criteria: •Declared a U.S. Citizen or National status. •Has an SSN that has been validated by SSA through the daily MEDS SSN validation process and has not met the DRA CIT/ID verification requirement or provided a 3 rd or 4 th level of evidence for citizenship. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAutomated Social Security Administration (SSA) Citizenship/Identity (CIT/ID) Verification Matches 07.01.05 2 of 8 It is possible for MEDS to request a SSA CIT/ID verification match on a customer who is exempt from DRA requirements. No further action is needed by either the customer or the HSS unless the customer loses their DRA exemption status. The SSA CIT/ID verification match will not be performed for customers who have met the DRA verification requirements by submitting a secondary level of evidence document. C. Triggering a Verification Match For customers who fall within the criteria outlined on MPG 07.02.05B, MEDS will automatically request a SSA CIT/ID verification match when one of the following conditions are met: •A new SSN is reported. •A key data change, such as a change in name, SSN, or date of birth, is made to an existing unvalidated SSN. •There has been no prior SSA CIT/ID verification match result for the SSN provided. D. Notification of Match Results HSSs will be notified of SSA CIT/ID verification match results through MEDS alerts. MEDS alerts 9044 through 9054 are generated based on whether the customer’s citizenship and identity are verified through SSA. Below is a description of each alert, message, and action needed if any. Alert Number Message Action Needed 9044 SSA Citizenship Verified Via SSA Data Match, Posted to MEDS •Confirms citizenship is verified through SSA. •No further documentation is needed from the customer to comply with DRA requirements. 9045 SSA Citizenship Verified, Updated to MEDS as Higher Status •SSA CIT/ID verification match supersedes lower-level documentation. •No further documentation is needed from the customer to comply with DRA requirements. 9046 Not Applicable This alert is currently suppressed from distribution. 9047 SSA Identity Verified Via SSA Data Match, Posted to MEDS •Identity is verified through SSA. •No further documentation is needed from the customer to comply with DRA requirements. 9048 SSA Identity Verified, Updated to MEDS as Higher Status •SSA CIT/ID verification match supersedes lower-level documentation. •No further documentation is needed from the customer to comply with DRA requirements. 9049 Not Applicable This alert is currently suppressed from distribution. 9050 Citizenship/Identity Not Verified Via SSA Data Match •Refer to 07.02.05I for detailed instructions. 9051 SSA Did Not Attempt Citizenship/Identity Data Match •Refer to 07.02.05I for detailed instructions. E. Impact to MEDS INQE Screen A successful SSA CIT/ID verification match may trigger updates to the MEDS INQE screen based on the customer’s circumstances. If the non-exempt customer… Then a successful SSA CIT/ID verification match will… Has submitted primary or secondary level CIT/ID documents, Not change the existing values that are on the MEDS INQE screen. For unsuccessful matches, no changes will be made to the MEDS INQE screen and any existing DRA document type code and source in the citizenship and identity fields will remain unchanged. F. Processing a Successful Match When a customer’s citizenship and identity are verified through the SSA CIT/ID verification match, the customer is no longer required to provide documents to meet the DRA requirements and the customer will be eligible for full-scope MC benefits if otherwise eligible. For customers who are not exempt from the DRA requirement and their citizenship and identity are verified through SSA, the HSS will update the DRA tab located in the “Collect Individual Demographics Detail” screen as follows: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageAutomated Social Security Administration (SSA) Citizenship/Identity (CIT/ID) Verification Matches 07.01.05 4 of 8 Field Entry DRA US Citizen (Y/N) •Select “Yes” from the dropdown menu. •Mark the verification as received. •Select source “Citizenship is verified by the SSA” from the dropdown. HSSs will be notified of the SSA CIT/ID verification status removal via MEDS alert 9054. Upon receiving MEDS alert 9054, the HSS will take the following actions: Step Action 1 Review and determine if the customer is exempt from the DRA requirement. If the customer is… Then… exempt, no further action is needed. not exempt, proceed to Step 2. Processing Unsuccessful Matches An unsuccessful match, or a mismatch, occurs when SSA is unable to verify a customer’s citizenship and identity. When an unsuccessful match occurs, the customer is still required to meet the DRA citizenship and identity verification requirements. Before attempting to resolve the mismatch, HSSs must verify that the customer is not exempt from or has not yet complied with the DRA CIT/ID verification requirements as follows: If the customer is… And they have… Then… Exempt from DRA, No further action is needed unless the customer loses their exemption status. Reason(s) for Possible Mismatches Various factors may contribute to mismatches where citizenship and identity of a customer cannot be verified through the SSA CIT/ID verification matching process. Contributing factors include the following: •Inaccurate reporting of a customer’s SSN, full name (first, middle, and last name), or the date of birth associated with the reported SSN. •Lack of citizenship information for the reported SSN within SSA’s record. oSSA is more likely to have citizenship information for more recently issued SSNs than for those issued to older customers. •SSA may not have the most current information for the customer. oThe SSA CIT/ID verification match only verifies whether a customer’s reported citizenship status is consistent with SSA’s records. ▪A customer who was a Legal Permanent Resident (LPR) and becomes a naturalized citizen may not have their information correctly reflected by the SSA database. I. sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageCitizenship 07.01.01 1 of 4 Revision Date: 05/01/2022 Background: The DRA of 2005 requires citizens of the United States to provide acceptable evidence of citizenship status and identity to receive full-scope Medi-Cal benefits. With the implementation of ACA, electronic verification of citizenship status through the federal data hub via the California Healthcare Eligibility Enrollment and Retention System (CalHEERS) is acceptable evidence of citizenship status and no other documentation is required. DRA requirements were changed to allow issuance of full-scope Medi-Cal benefits to otherwise eligible U.S. citizen applicants during their Reasonable Opportunity Period (ROP) while they obtain the required citizenship and identity documents. Note: Any reference to “U.S. citizens” should be interpreted as including both U.S. citizens and U.S. nationals for the purpose of this section. Purpose: This section has been revised to incorporate updates Medi-Cal eligibility for customers of the member sovereign states of the Compact of Free Association (COFA). Policy: A customer who is attesting to be a U.S. citizen and has their citizenship electronically verified is eligible to receive full-scope Medi-Cal benefits. See Medi-Cal Program Guide (MPG) 04.02.09 Statement of Citizenship/Non-Citizen Status for more information. A. Definitions for U.S. Citizens: Persons who fall within one of the following categories shall be considered U.S. citizens for Medi-Cal purposes. Category Description People born in one of the fifty United States or the District of Columbia (D.C.)U.S. Citizens/ Nationals People born in the following areas are treated the same as U.S. citizens for Medi- Cal purposes: •American Samoa •Swain’s Island Collectively Naturalized People born in the following areas are treated the same as U.S. citizens for Medi- Cal purposes, if conditions specified in MPG 07.02 Appendix A are met. •Puerto Rico •Guam •U.S. Virgin Islands (St. John, St. Croix, and St. Thomas) •Northern Mariana Islands County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageCitizenship 07.01.01 2 of 4 Acquired Citizenship People born in another country may have acquired citizenship if one or both of their parents were U.S. citizens at the time of birth, and the parent(s) met the requirements for transmitting citizenship. INS must act favorably on an application for Certificate of Citizenship, INS Form N-600, before acquired citizenship is approved. INS Form N-600 is not documentation of acquired citizenship as it merely shows the person has applied for acquired citizenship. Derived Citizenship A child may have derived citizenship if one or both child’s parents become citizens through naturalization before the child’s eighteenth birthday. The child would have to have been a legal permanent resident to obtain derived citizenship through their parent’s naturalized citizenship. Naturalized Citizenship Naturalized U.S. citizens are persons who were born abroad and have since obtained U.S. citizenship through the naturalization process. Many conditions must be met before a person may obtain U.S. citizenship through this process, including: •Legal permanent resident status for at least five years; or •Marriage to a U.S. citizen for at least three years B. Compact Free Association Act (COFA) of 1985: In accordance with the COFA of 1985, citizens of the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM) and the Republic of the Marshall Islands (MIS) may live, work or study in the U.S. without restrictions. They may also qualify for full-scope Medi-Cal benefits if otherwise eligible. As proof that they are citizens of independent nations “freely associated” with the U.S., these “permanent non-immigrants” must present Arrival-Departure Records (Form I-94) annotated either CFA/FSM or CFA/MIS. title: Section 2 - Non-Citizens
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageNon-Citizen Categories 07.02.01 1 of 3 Revision Date: December 1, 2025 Background: Non-citizens fall under multiple categories that impact Medi-Cal eligibility and the level of benefits they are entitled to. Purpose: This section describes the non-citizen categories and provides guidance on determining residency for those who possess a Border Crossing Card or non-immigrant visa. Policy: A. Qualified Non-Citizens (QNC) QNC in the following categories are eligible for full scope Medi-Cal coverage. Legal Permanent Residents (LPR) LPR who were admitted into the United States (U.S.) on a permanent basis or for an indefinite period are entitled to full scope Medi-Cal if otherwise eligible. Refer to Medi-Cal Desk Aid 78 for U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) documentation types. Battered Non-citizens Non-citizens who were battered or subjected to extreme cruelty are considered QNC and eligible to full scope Medi-Cal benefits under federal law if they meet each of the four requirements below. 1. The customer has been approved or has a petition pending under one of the Immigration and Nationality Act provisions. Note: Pending adjudication for one of the provisions may be verified with a Notice of Prima Facie Case is valid until USCIS has made a determination. 2. The customer, their child, and/or the parent of a non-citizen child applicant were battered or subjected to extreme cruelty. 3. The battered non-citizen has provided verification that there is a substantial connection between the battery and the need for benefits. Acceptable verification includes a sworn statement from the customer that describes any one of the following circumstances: •The non-citizen or their child is receiving cash assistance based on battery or extreme cruelty •Loss of financial support resulting from the non-citizen and/or their child’s separation from the abuser •The non-citizen or their child requires medical attention, mental health counseling, or has become disabled because of the battery/cruelty •Unwanted pregnancy or children resulting from the abuser’s sexual assault or abusive relationship with the non-citizen or their child •Needs to replace coverage the customer/child had while living with the abuser If the customer presents different facts than those above and claims a connection between the battery and the need for benefits, an elevation must be submitted to the Medi-Cal Program team using the proper channels. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageNon-Citizen Categories 07.02.01 2 of 3 4. The customer must no longer live in the same household as the abuser. Permanently Residing Under Color of Law (PRUCOL) Non-citizens in the PRUCOL category are entitled to full scope Medi-Cal benefits if otherwise eligible. Non-citizen Medi-Cal applicants may claim any one of the PRUCOL categories listed on the Statement of Citizenship, Alienage and Immigration Status (MC 13). Refer to Medi-Cal Desk Aid 78 for PRUCOL categories and documentation required. B. Non-Citizens with Unsatisfactory Immigration Status (UIS) Non-Citizens with UIS will receive full or restricted benefits based on which of the following categories they fall under: •Non-citizens with UIS who apply for Medi-Cal on or after January 1, 2026 will receive restricted scope Medi-Cal if otherwise eligible. •Non-citizens with UIS who were active prior to January 1, 2026 will continue to receive full scope Medi-Cal as long as they do not experience a break in aid. C. Residency for Border Crossing Card (BCC) or Non-Immigrant Visa Holders USCIS issues BCC and non-immigrant visas to non-citizens who reside in another country and provide documentation that they intend to enter the United States for only a temporary period. Border Crossing Card Due the requirements for receipt of a BCC, possession of a valid and current card is compelling evidence that the holder is not a resident of the state of California. A non-citizen with a BCC may establish residency by presenting persuasive evidence that they have taken steps consistent with their stated intent to live in California permanently, or indefinitely, or have entered the state for employment reasons. The claim of California residency must be evaluated using all available information with the results clearly detailed in a journal entry. If unable to determine California residency, staff must initiate a fraud referral as indicated in Medi-Cal Processing Guide 19 Fraud Prevention. Non-Immigrant Visa A valid and current non-immigrant visa, including but not limited to B-1 and B-2 visas, which allows entry for a period of less than one year constitutes strong evidence that the bearer is not a resident of California and is not eligible for any Medi-Cal benefits, unless they present persuasive evidence to the contrary. People with non-immigrant visas are permitted entry into the United States for personal or business purposes. At the port of entry, USCIS frequently stamps the I-94 with permission for the person to stay for a period of six months or less. If after considering all available information, the HSS is unable to determine the customer’s claim of California residence, then initiate a fraud referral due to inconsistent or questionable information, that cannot be resolved. Clearly narrate all facts in case comments if it is determined that the customer is not a resident of the state. Program Impacts: Automation Staff must complete the appropriate citizen and non-citizen fields in California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) so customers receive the correct level of benefits. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageNon-Citizen Categories 07.02.01 3 of 3 References: ACWDL 88-66, 89-34, 89-59, 90-31, 90-67, 93-14, 93-29, 93-49, 95-47, 96-27, 97-42, 98-55, 12-19, 21-13, 22-04, 25-13 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance November 30, 2028. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageLevel of Benefits 07.02.02 1 of 2 Revision Date: December 1, 2025 Background: Medi-Cal customers are potentially eligible for either full or restricted scope benefits. The level of benefits they are entitled to is determined by their citizenship or immigration status and whether the verification requirements of their status are met. Purpose: This section was updated to reflect the elimination of full scope Medi-Cal for new applicants ages 19 years and older with Unsatisfactory Immigration Status (UIS) who apply on or after January 1, 2026. Policy: Full Scope Benefits Full scope benefits include all medical services covered by the Medi-Cal program. To be eligible for full scope benefits, a customer must be a/an: •United States (U.S.) citizen who has provided the required citizenship/identity documents or is making a good faith effort to provide •Non-citizen who was lawfully admitted into the U.S. permanently or for an indefinite period •Non-citizen who is Permanently Residing Under Color of Law (PRUCOL) •Pregnant individual regardless of citizenship status (12 months postpartum included) •Child under 19 regardless of immigration status •An adult aged 19 and older with UIS who was active prior to January 1, 2026 and has maintained coverage without interruption 90-day Expansion Grace Period After discontinuance for any reason, including over income and failure to provide the annual renewal, individuals who are 19 and older with UIS active full scope Medi-Cal at the time of discontinuance are entitled to a 90 day grace period to reenroll in full scope if eligibility conditions are met. Note: Children with UIS and active Medi-Cal who turn 19 years old after January 1, 2026 will continue on full scope coverage as long as they maintain eligibility without interruption. Permanently Residing Under Color of Law (PRUCOL) A non-citizen may request full scope benefits and claim PRUCOL on the basis that United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) is aware of their presence in the U.S. but does not intend to deport them due to their status or individual circumstances. The customer may claim PRUCOL by checking the last category on the Statement of Citizenship, Alienage and Immigration Status (MC 13). USCIS Policy: •USCIS does not recognize PRUCOL as a legal immigration status. Individuals receive no immigration benefits because of a PRUCOL determination. •USCIS will not deport non-citizens on the basis that they claim PRUCOL or apply for/receive Medi-Cal. These non-citizens may be deported for reasons unrelated to Medi-Cal, such as providing false information to USCIS or having an open warrant for their arrest. •PRUCOL can be requested for a deceased person. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageLevel of Benefits 07.02.02 2 of 2 For applicants who claim the last PRUCOL category on the MC 13: •Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) verification or other documents related to immigration status will not be requested. •Full scope Medi-Cal will be approved, if otherwise eligible. •PRUCOL status will not be reverified at annual renewal. •An elevation to Medi-Cal Program is required when conflicting information is reported (e.g. applicant claiming last PRUCOL category with immigration documentation on file). Program will initiate a review by the State Medi-Cal Eligibility Division (MCED) who will evaluate whether the individual is receiving the appropriate level of benefits based on their known immigration status or other relevant factors such as domestic violence, trafficking or other serious crimes. Restricted Scope Benefits Restricted scope benefits cover only emergency medical conditions which if not treated, would seriously endanger a customer’s health or impair use of limbs, organs, or bodily functions. Customers are not required to have an emergency medical condition to be eligible for restricted scope benefits. Individuals who apply on or after January 1, 2026 and are unable to establish Satisfactory Immigration Status (SIS) will receive restricted scope Medi-Cal, if they meet all other eligibility requirements. Presumptive Eligibility Customers who claim SIS have a Reasonable Opportunity Period (ROP) of 90 days from the date of application (or the time it takes to determine eligibility, whichever is longer) to provide documentation of their immigration status. These individuals will be given full scope Medi-Cal if otherwise eligible. If SIS documentation is not received within the ROP, their level of benefits will be reduced to restricted. Note: When a customer later provides documentation of SIS that was valid during the months they received restricted Medi-Cal, full scope benefits will be issued retroactively. Program Impacts: Automation Staff must complete the appropriate citizen and non-citizen fields in California Statewide Automated Welfare (CalSAWS) so customers receive the correct level of benefits. References: ACWDL 90-31, 90-40, 92-48, 93-14, 07-12, 09-27, 12-19, 16-12, 17-01, 19-23, 21-13, 21-15, 25-13 MEDIL I 17-14 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by November 30, 2028 Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageSystematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) 07.02.03 1 of 2 Revision Date: December 1, 2025 Background: The Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) electronic verification process is used to verify immigration status when required for official purposes of a government agency. Purpose: This section provides instructions to County staff on using SAVE to verify Satisfactory Immigration Status (SIS). The section was revised for the sunset review; no policies or procedures were changed. Policy: When to use SAVE SAVE must be used to verify the documentation of SIS provided by a Qualified Non-Citizen: •At application •When documentation of SIS is provided by a Qualified Non-Citizen (QNC) who was granted fullscope benefits presumptively during a Reasonable Opportunity Period (ROP) •When there’s a change of immigration status •When a QNC who is receiving restricted benefits provides documentation of SIS SAVE is not to be used when: •SIS was electronically verified •A non-citizen claims SIS but provides documentation that does not support it (e.g. Form I-94) indicates the non-citizen was admitted to the United States (U.S.) for temporary residence) •A non-citizen is claiming the last Permanently Residing Under Color of Law (PRUCOL) category on the Statement of Citizenship, Alienage and Immigration Status (MC 13) The approval of full scope benefits must not be delayed pending verification of the customer’s immigration status through SAVE. If the SAVE response indicates the documentation is not valid, benefits will be reduced to restricted with timely notice. A potential overpayment may exist for the months that the non-citizen received full scope Medi-Cal. Refer to Medi-Cal Processing Guide 19 for guidance. SAVE Primary Verification System Under the SAVE Primary System, CalSAWS will initiate a SAVE abstract using the QNC’s A-number. The abstract must be compared to information provided by the customer. If there is a question regarding the identity or immigration status of the customer, a secondary verification must be obtained. The SAVE abstract will indicate one of these responses from USCIS: •Asylee •Conditional Resident •Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) •Lawful Permanent Resident (LPR) •Non-Immigrant •Parolee •Refugee •Temporary Protected Status (TPS) County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageSystematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) 07.02.03 2 of 2 •U.S. Citizen •Institute Secondary Verification All but the final response indicate SIS. Individuals without SIS may receive full scope benefits only if they are under 19 years of age or have applied for and received Medi-Cal prior to January 1, 2026 without a break in aid exceeding the 90-day grace period. SAVE Secondary Verification System The SAVE Secondary Verification System is an automated process completed by United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS). It is required when the SAVE primary response is “Institute Secondary Verification,” when there are doubts about the identity/immigration status of the non-citizen, or when discrepancies exist such as the following: •The document appears counterfeit, altered, or unfamiliar •The document does not have an A-number but it notes an immigration status •The A-number is in the 60000000 or 70000000 series, which was never officially issued by USCIS •The document is a USCIS receipt •The customer presents a foreign passport containing an I-94 form which is over one year old with the statement “Processed for I-551, Temporary evidence of Lawful Permanent Residence” Exception for new refugees: A federal waiver allows the county to delay secondary verification of immigration status for newly arrived refugees for 12 months from their arrival date or until the first redetermination, whichever comes first, even if the SAVE primary response indicates “Institute Secondary Verification.” If the SAVE database does not contain information on these refugees at the time of application, the A-number must be submitted for primary verification at the annual renewal, or within 12 months of their arrival date. A secondary verification will be initiated at this time, if necessary. SAVE Secondary and Third-Level System Procedures Refer to Eligibility Operations Processing Guide (EOPG) - Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) Secondary Verification for these procedures. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageStatement of Citizenship/Non-Citizen Status 07.02.04 1 of 2 Revision Date: December 1, 2025 Background: United States (U.S.) citizenship and non-citizen status is used to determine the level of ben efits a Medi- Cal applicant is potentially eligible for. Purpose: This section is revised for the sunset review; no policies or procedures were changed. Policy: Applicants who claim to be U.S. citizens/nationals or to have satisfactory immigration status (SIS) will have their status electronically verified via the California Healthcare Eligibility Enrollment, and Retention System (CalHEERS) through the Federal Data Services Hub. Self-attestation of citizenship is acceptable via telephonic and electronic signature for applications submitted online. Refer to MPG section 04.07. Medi-Cal eligibility should not be delayed, denied, or discontinued solely for failure to respond to a request for the Statement of Citizenship, Alienage, and Immigration Status form (MC 13). Procedure: When Documentation is Not Required The MC 13 form or any additional citizenship/immigration status documentation is not required when the applicant: •Claims to be a U.S. citizen/national or to have SIS AND whose status is verified via electronic means, including a California birth record match or the Social Security Administration (SSA) citizenship verification process. •Is the secondary adult on a case who did not sign the application and the primary applicant attests the individual is a U.S. citizen/national AND their citizenship/immigration status is verified via electronic means, including a California birth record match, or the SSA citizenship verification process. •The applicant is not claiming U.S. citizenship or SIS Verbal Attestation An MC 13 is not required for immigrants who verbally attest to an immigration status and have associated documentation that is sufficient to request verification via electronic means or the Systemic Alien Verification for Entitlement (SAVE) verification process. The MC 13 form will only be completed: •At application when it is unclear, or staff are unable to determine from the application or verbal statement if the individual is claiming U.S. citizenship or SIS. •At renewal or Change in Circumstances (CIC) redetermination when unable to determine if the individual is claiming U.S. citizenship or SIS after an ex parte review of all available information. •When the applicant wants to claim the last category of Permanently Residing Under Color of Law (PRUCOL). Individuals who claim this status are not required to provide additional documentation. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageStatement of Citizenship/Non-Citizen Status 07.02.04 1 of 2 Reasonable Opportunity Period (ROP) Individuals who claim citizenship or SIS at application will be given a 90-day ROP to provide the MC 13/other verifications during which they will receive full scope Medi-Cal if otherwise eligible. If verification is … Then … submitted that confirms citizenship or SIS full scope Medi-Cal will continue. provided or final determination is received that does not prove SIS, not submitted, Medi-Cal will be reduced to restricted scope. Program Impacts: None References: ACWDL 14-41, 15-32, 16-12 17-01, 18-16, 19-23, 20-17 MEDIL I 14-21 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by November 30, 2028 Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services

sections.text: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageNon-Citizen Categories 07.02.01 1 of 3 Revision Date: December 1, 2025 Background: Non-citizens fall under multiple categories that impact Medi-Cal eligibility and the level of benefits they are entitled to. Purpose: This section describes the non-citizen categories and provides guidance on determining residency for those who possess a Border Crossing Card or non-immigrant visa. Policy: A. Qualified Non-Citizens (QNC) QNC in the following categories are eligible for full scope Medi-Cal coverage. Legal Permanent Residents (LPR) LPR who were admitted into the United States (U.S.) on a permanent basis or for an indefinite period are entitled to full scope Medi-Cal if otherwise eligible. Refer to Medi-Cal Desk Aid 78 for U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) documentation types. Battered Non-citizens Non-citizens who were battered or subjected to extreme cruelty are considered QNC and eligible to full scope Medi-Cal benefits under federal law if they meet each of the four requirements below. 1. The customer has been approved or has a petition pending under one of the Immigration and Nationality Act provisions. Note: Pending adjudication for one of the provisions may be verified with a Notice of Prima Facie Case is valid until USCIS has made a determination. 2. The customer, their child, and/or the parent of a non-citizen child applicant were battered or subjected to extreme cruelty. 3. The battered non-citizen has provided verification that there is a substantial connection between the battery and the need for benefits. Acceptable verification includes a sworn statement from the customer that describes any one of the following circumstances: •The non-citizen or their child is receiving cash assistance based on battery or extreme cruelty •Loss of financial support resulting from the non-citizen and/or their child’s separation from the abuser •The non-citizen or their child requires medical attention, mental health counseling, or has become disabled because of the battery/cruelty •Unwanted pregnancy or children resulting from the abuser’s sexual assault or abusive relationship with the non-citizen or their child •Needs to replace coverage the customer/child had while living with the abuser If the customer presents different facts than those above and claims a connection between the battery and the need for benefits, an elevation must be submitted to the Medi-Cal Program team using the proper channels. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageNon-Citizen Categories 07.02.01 2 of 3 4. The customer must no longer live in the same household as the abuser. Permanently Residing Under Color of Law (PRUCOL) Non-citizens in the PRUCOL category are entitled to full scope Medi-Cal benefits if otherwise eligible. Non-citizen Medi-Cal applicants may claim any one of the PRUCOL categories listed on the Statement of Citizenship, Alienage and Immigration Status (MC 13). Refer to Medi-Cal Desk Aid 78 for PRUCOL categories and documentation required. B. Non-Citizens with Unsatisfactory Immigration Status (UIS) Non-Citizens with UIS will receive full or restricted benefits based on which of the following categories they fall under: •Non-citizens with UIS who apply for Medi-Cal on or after January 1, 2026 will receive restricted scope Medi-Cal if otherwise eligible. •Non-citizens with UIS who were active prior to January 1, 2026 will continue to receive full scope Medi-Cal as long as they do not experience a break in aid. C. Residency for Border Crossing Card (BCC) or Non-Immigrant Visa Holders USCIS issues BCC and non-immigrant visas to non-citizens who reside in another country and provide documentation that they intend to enter the United States for only a temporary period. title: Section 1 - Medi-Cal Family Budget Unit
content: Article 8, Section 1 – Medi-Cal Family Budget Unit (MFBU) Table of Contents TITLE MPG CITE General 08.01.01 Responsible Relatives 08.01.02 Medi-Cal Family Budget Unit (MFBU) 08.01.03 Status of Family Members 08.01.04 MFBU Composition Appendix A Treatment of MFBU Members Appendix B Questions and Answers Regarding Responsible Relatives Appendix C 08.01.01 - General ACA Information For information about determining household composition for Modified Adjusted Gross Income based Medi-Cal and Advanced Premium Tax Credits, please see Special Notice 13-09 Addendum A. A. General This section: •contains regulations for determining the Medi-Cal Family Budget Unit (MFBU); •describes responsible relative criteria; •identifies eligible and ineligible members of the MFBU; and •specifies who may be excluded from the MFBU. MPG LTR 16 (4/88) 08.01.02 – Responsible Relatives A. Introduction The responsibility of a relative to contribute to the cost of health care services of a Medi-Cal applicant or beneficiary shall be limited to spouse for spouse and parent for child. A caretaker relative as defined in Article 8, Section 5 is not considered to be a responsible relative. MPG LTR 16 (4/88) MEM 50351 B. Spouse for Spouse Spouses are responsible for each other when: •Both spouses live together in the home; or •One or both spouses are in LTC/B&C and both are MI or AFDC-MN. Spouse for spouse responsibility is for the month of admission to LTC/B&C only, when one or both spouses are in LTC/B&C and one or both are ABD. In this situation, spouse for spouse responsibility ends on the last day of the month of admission. MPG LTR 16 (4/88) C. Parent for Child A parent is responsible for a child when the child: •Lives in the parent’s home •Lives out of the parent’s home and the child is: A tax dependent of the parent 18 to 21 years old 14 to 18 years old and the parent is handling some or all of his/her financial affairs under 14 years old •Is married even if the child is a parent and the child is both: A tax dependent of the parent 18 to 21 years old EXCEPTION: Parents of a child have no responsibility when the child is applying for Minor Consent services. MPG LTR 16 (4/88) MEPM 8C 08.01.03 – Medi-Cal Family Budget Unit (MFBU) A. Introduction The MFBU is the basic unit of persons considered in determining a person’s or family’s Medi-Cal eligibility and share of cost (SOC). MPG LTR 241 (3/94) B. Family Members Family members for Medi-Cal purposes are: •A child or sibling children, including an unborn. (Verification of pregnancy must be on file for full-scope coverage. See MPG 04.07.08.) •The parents, married or unmarried, of the sibling child(ren). •The stepparents of the sibling child(ren). •The separate child(ren) of either unmarried parent or the parent or stepparent. •If there are no children, family members mean a single person or a married couple. MPG LTR 241 (3/94) MEM 50041 C. Persons Temporarily Absent from the Home People temporarily absent from the home because of hospitalization, visiting, vacation, trips in connection with work, or for similar reasons, are considered living in the home. MPG LTR 241 (3/94) MEM 50371 D. Public Assistance (PA) Recipients Family members who are PA or Other PA recipients are eligible to receive Medi-Cal benefits under the PA or Other PA program. Therefore, they will not be part of the Medically Needy Only (MNO) MFBU. Family members who are eligible for Four-Month Continuing, TMC, or Edwards shall be included in the MFBU. MPG LTR 241 (3/94) MEM 50373 ACWDL 92-65 08.01.04 – Status of Family Members A. Introduction Family members may be eligible or ineligible members of the MFBU or may be excluded from the MFBU per F, below. MPG LTR 411 (3/01) B. Eligible MFBU Members Eligible MFBU members are entitled to receive Medi-Cal benefits. Their income and property are included for eligibility and SOC determinations. MPG LTR 411 (3/01) C. Reasons for Ineligibility People are considered ineligible members of the MFBU when they: •Refuse to apply for a Social Security number. •Refuse to apply for Medicare. •Refuse to apply for and accept unconditionally available income. •Are unable to meet the basic eligibility criteria for any of the Medi-Cal programs. •Refuse to cooperate with the Medical Support Enforcement Program without good cause. MPG LTR 411 (3/01) MEM 50379 MEM 50771.5 D. Circumstance s of Ineligibility People in the following circumstances are ineligible members of the MFBU. •People receiving Medi-Cal as Four-Month Continuing, Edwards, or TMC eligible. •People 21 or over and under 65 who are not blind, disabled, pregnant, and are not linked to AFDC. •Minor parents living with their parents are ineligible members of the MFBU that includes the minor parent’s child(ren) (except when the minor parent wishes to receive only Minor Consent services). Minor parents, who wish to receive Medi-Cal, other than Minor Consent services, shall be included in the MFBU with their parents. •Parents who reside outside the state and who claim their child(ren) residing in the state as dependent(s) in order to receive a tax credit or deduction for state or federal income tax purposes are ineligible members of their child(ren)’s MFBU. •The following people shall be ineligible members of the MFBU when a person 18 to 21 years old is claimed by his/her parent as a dependent in order to receive a tax credit or deduction for state or ACWDL 92-65 MEM 50379 federal income tax: The spouse, child(ren) and parent(s) of the married child claimed as a tax dependent are ineligible members of the MFBU which includes the tax dependent. The person 18 to 21 years old claimed as a tax dependent is an ineligible member of the MFBUs which include either his/her parent(s) or his/her spouse and child(ren). •An infant under age of one year receiving benefits through the Income Disregard or Asset Waiver programs (see MPG Article 5, Section 12). These infants are treated as ineligible members of the MI/MN MFBU. Although treated as ineligible members of the MFBU, they are able to link parents to Medi-Cal as AFDC-MN. •Children age one up to age six receiving benefits through the 133% federal poverty level (FPL) Program. These children are treated as ineligible members of the MI/MN MFBU. They are able to link parents to Medi-Cal as AFDC-MN. •Children age six up to age 19 receiving benefits through the 100% FPL Program. These children are treated as ineligible members of the MI/MN MFBU. They are able to link parents to Medi-Cal as AFDC-MN. •Children receiving State-only AAP-AAC are ineligible members of the MFBU. They are considered to be medically indigent; not medically needy. MPG LTR 411 (3/01) ACWDL 89-50 89-103 ACWDL 90-61 E. Special Consideration s A child who is otherwise eligible or ineligible for any of the reasons listed in C or D, above, may be treated as an ineligible member of the MFBU or may be excluded from the MFBU. This choice is the option of the person who has legal responsibility for the child. In either case, the child may not link parents to Medi-Cal as AFDC-MN. To treat an otherwise eligible person as ineligible, obtain all forms and verifications as required for an eligible person, but select ‘Y’ in the “Ignore Eligibility Determination” on the Collect Case Individual Detail window. Ineligible members will: •Have their income included in eligibility and SOC determinations •Have their property counted in eligibility computations •Have their medical expenses used to meet the SOC for the MFBU; •Not be considered in determining the program for which persons included in the MFBU are eligible MPG LTR 471 (11/01) MEM 50205 F. Excluded MFBU Members The only family members that may be excluded from the MFBU are: •A child of any age (for example, from one day old to 21 years old) who either: Refuses to provide information about his/her own income or property Chooses not to receive Medi-Cal. Whenever a child is excluded from the MFBU, the parent or caretaker relative must be provided the excluded child statement, form MC 239 SN-3. The worker is required to provide the form to the parent or caretaker relative; however, if the form is not returned, notate in the Case Comments that the form was provided and not returned. Continue to exclude the child from the MFBU as requested, but do not deny or discontinue other family members based on non-receipt of the MC 239 SN-3. Send informing notice MC 239 SN-2 to the applicant. •Members of a stepparent unit other than the parent of the child requesting Medi-Cal shall be excluded from the MFBU. •The unmarried father of an unborn when the unmarried father lives with the pregnant woman and she wants Medi-Cal only for herself and/or her separate children. •Children receiving federal AAP with or without a cash grant are excluded from the MFBU because they are receiving PA or Other PA. MPG LTR 471 (11/01) MEM 50381 MEPM 8F-14 MEM 50381 G. Excluded Members Restrictions Excluded members are not eligible to Medi-Cal benefits. Excluded members may not: •Apply separately, except for Minor Consent services, for which they may receive benefits •Be included in the MFBU for eligibility or SOC determinations •Have their medical expenses used to meet the MFBU’s SOC •Be considered in determining the program for which persons included in the MFBU are eligible. MPG LTR 471 (11/01) MEM 50205 H. Property of Excluded Members The property of excluded family members will not be counted in determining the eligibility of the MFBU. MPG LTR 471 (11/01) I. Income of Excluded The income of excluded MFBU members will be treated as follows: •The income of an excluded child(ren) will not be counted in determining the SOC for the MFBU. An allocation of income may be Members made to an excluded child(ren), but not when the child is excluded because the parents refuse to provide information. See MPG Article 10, Section 5 for instructions on calculating the allocation to an excluded child. •The income of the members of a stepparent unit will be treated in accordance with the Sneede v. Kizer lawsuit described in MPG Article 5, Section 14. MPG LTR 471 (11/01) ACWDL 04-25 J. Changes in the MFBU Changes in the MFBU may be made at the request of the applicant/beneficiary. Changes may be reflected in the month the changes are reported if it is to the beneficiary’s advantage. Any advantage shall be explained to the beneficiary. The beneficiary shall determine whether the change shall be reflected in the month it is reported. MPG Article 12, Section 1 describes how to make changes and adjustments. MPG LTR 562 (9/04) MEM 50371 Appendix A.
