title: Section 3 - MAGI Medi-Cal Tax Household Composition
chapter: ARTICLE 21 - MAGI APTC and Health Care Reform
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageMAGI Medi-Cal Tax Household Composition 21.03 1 of 4 Revision Date: 7/1/2021 Background: The Affordable Care act (ACA) was signed into law in March of 2010. The law enacted comprehensive health insurance reforms through the expansion of Medi-Cal, Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) based Medi- Cal, creation of the Health Insurance Exchange, and new regulations for health insurance plans. MAGI Medi- Cal household composition is based on the federal tax filing rules. Purpose: To provide guidance for determining MAGI Medi-Cal tax household (HH) composition. Policy The tax filing status is based on the current year. Every customer in the case will have their own household composition which may be different for every person in the home depending on the tax filing status. Individuals do not need to file taxes to qualify for MAGI based Medi-Cal, but all individuals need to provide information on how they plan to file or not file taxes for the year they are seeking coverage. The following tax information is required for all individuals at application and redetermination: •Who is the primary tax filer (the first name on the tax return) •If the individual intends to file taxes •If the individual expects to be required to file taxes •The individual’s tax filing status (Married filing jointly, head of household, etc.) •If claimed as a dependent, the name of the tax filer claiming them as a dependent A. Tax Filing Status The MAGI Medi-Cal household composition is based on whether the individual is a: •Tax filer •Tax dependent •Tax dependent with exceptions •Non-filer Tax dependents can sometimes file their own taxes but are counted as tax dependents if also claimed by someone as a dependent. B. Tax Filer Household Composition The household composition of a tax filer not claimed as a dependent on someone’s else’s taxes includes: •The tax filer •Their spouse who lives in the home •Their spouse who lives outside the home if they file “married filing jointly” •The tax filer’s claimed dependents regardless of where they live •The unborn children of the above Tax dependents do not have to live in the home to be counted in the tax filer’s household composition. C. Tax Dependent Household Composition The household composition of tax dependent who does not meet any of the tax dependent exceptions (see section D below for exceptions) will be the dependent, the tax filer claiming the dependent, and the rest of the people claimed by the tax filer. Generally, this is the same as the household of the tax filer who claimed the dependent, however it can sometimes vary because the general rules for married couples applies when a tax dependent is married. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageMAGI Medi-Cal Tax Household Composition 21.03 2 of 4 D. Tax Dependent Exceptions The household composition of tax dependent will generally be the same as the tax filer unless they meet one of the tax dependent exceptions. Use the non-filer rules when a tax dependent meets one of the below exceptions: •A dependent any age who is not the spouse or child of the tax filer •A child (under 19 or under 21 and a full-time student) and the parents do not expect to file a joint return •A child (under 19 or under 21 and a full-time student) and is claimed by a parent outside of the home E. Non-Filer Household Composition The household composition for a person who does not expect to file taxes or a tax dependent who meets one of the above exceptions includes: •For adults over 19 and not a full-time student oThe non-filer oThe non-filer’s spouse who lives in the home oThe non-filer’s children (under age 19 or under age 21 and a full-time student) living in the home including adopted and stepchildren •For children under age 19 or adults under age 21 oThe non-filer oThe non-filer’s spouse who lives in the home oThe non-filer’s children (under age 19 or under age 21 and a full-time student) living in the home including adopted and stepchildren oThe non-filer’s biological, step, or adoptive parents if living in the home oThe non-filer’s siblings living in the home including adopted and stepsiblings Use the non-filer rules when an applicant is unsure of how they will file taxes. F. Establishing Family Size Family size is the number of persons counted as members of an individual’s Medi-Cal HH, with the following adjustments: •A pregnant person is counted as one plus the number of children she is expected to deliver. •For another individual whose HH incudes a pregnant person, include the number of children expected by the pregnant person. G. Rules for Married Couples Married couples will be included in each other’s household no matter how they file. The exception to this rule is married couples who file separately and do not live together. Those who file “Married Filing Jointly” must be in each other’s household and income from both spouses must be evaluated. If a spouse filing “Married Filing Jointly” fails to provide income verification, the application for both spouses can be denied for failure to provide unless inclusion of the spouse who failed to provide would not affect the outcome of the determination (for example, a couple living separately claiming “Married Filing Jointly” but is unmarried). H. Future Changes When the customer reasonably predicts a future change in their tax filing status and living situation (for example a married couple filing as “Married Filing Jointly” this year but is separating and plans to file separately next year), use the next year’s tax filing status to redetermine their household composition. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageMAGI Medi-Cal Tax Household Composition 21.03 3 of 4 I. Ways to Report Tax Filing Information Tax filing information may be reported over the phone, in-person, online, or the customer’s preferred method of communication. Customers are not required to submit any supporting documentation. Ex parte applies to obtaining tax filing information. Human Services Specialists (HSS) must review the case file prior to requesting the information. If the customer fails to provide the information, the regular denial and discontinuance timelines and notification requirements apply. J. Self-Attestation of Tax Filing Status The Federal Data Services Hub does not electronically verify tax household composition. Accept a customer’s self-attestation of their plans to file taxes, their expectation to be required to file taxes, and the effect on the MAGI Medi-Cal HH determination. The self-attested answers shall be accepted as true, regardless of other information provided within the application that may appear to conflict with the customer’s statements, such as the amount of income and/or deductions. This is because there may be circumstances known to the Internal Revenue Service or to the customer that are not included or reported on the applications. Note: Tax filing status does not expire and should not be changed unless the customer reports a change. K. Conflicting Tax Filing Status Use the non-filer rules when unmarried individuals report filing “Married Filing Jointly,” or the applicant is unsure of their tax filing status. L. Victims of Domestic Violence The tax household for victims of domestic violence can change depending on how they plan to file taxes depending on their situation: •If the individual files “Married Filing Jointly” in the current year, but self-attest that they will file separately next year, base the tax household on how the applicant intends to file in the future and the spouse would not be included. •If the individuals attest that they will file “Married Filing Separately”, the spouse would not be included. •If they are unsure of how they will file in the future because they are in a transitional state, apply the non-filer rules. M. Institutionalized Children Institutionalized Children residing outside the parent’s home in an institution such as a psychiatric hospital, penal institution, or children’s home that are claimed as tax dependents will use the tax dependent rules to determine household composition. If the child is ineligible for MAGI Medi-Cal based on income, they can be evaluated for non-MAGI and the parent’s income excluded. Use the non-filer rules to determine household composition for Institutionalized children not claimed as tax dependents or that are unsure of their status. N. Joint Custody When there is joint custody of a child and one or both parents request Medi-Cal, determine the custodial parent or primary caregiver. The custodial parent or primary caregiver is the parent with whom the child spends most nights. When parents apply separately for the same child and claim to have the child for equal nights, the child will be in the home of the parent who applied first. In joint custody situations where the child is primarily with the parent who does not claim them on their taxes, use the non-filer rules to determine household composition. O. Child Tax Filer Living with Parents A child (under 19 or under 21 if a full-time student) who files their own taxes and is not claimed by their parent will use the Tax Filer rules to determine household composition. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Number PageMAGI Medi-Cal Tax Household Composition 21.03 4 of 4 P. Homeless Children The household composition of homeless children living outside the parent’s home depends on whether they are claimed as tax dependents. If they are claimed, the tax dependent rules apply. If the child cannot provide parent income and tax information, they can be evaluated for non-MAGI Medi-Cal and the parent’s income excluded. If the homeless child is not claimed by their parents or unsure about their tax filing status, apply the non-filer rules to determine household composition. Q. Household Composition for Covered California (CA) Financial Assistance The tax household for Covered CA includes: •The primary tax filer •The spouse of the primary tax filer •Any tax dependents Additionally, the following rules apply to the Covered CA tax household: •Married couples must attest to intend to file a joint tax return to be eligible to Covered CA financial assistance. •Legally separated and divorced spouses are not included. •The tax filer does not have to include their spouse if they are a victim of domestic violence or spousal abandonment. •Dependent children are included regardless of age. •Non-dependent children under age 26 are included if they are to be covered under the Covered CA plan. Program Impacts: Automation Enter appropriate fields in CalWIN to receive the appropriate MAGI eligibility determination. Do not enter any individuals into CalWIN if they are not part of any applicant’s tax household or requesting (for example the absent parent). Do not mark tax dependents who live outside of the home as in the home. Desk Aids The following desk aids are available in Eligibility Essentials to assist HSSs with determining household composition: •Desk aid 67 – Determining Household Composition •Desk aid 68 – Magi Medi-Cal Household Composition Examples •Desk aid 70 – MAGI Medi-Cal Individual Household Flow Chart References: MEDIL 13-12, 19-24 ACWDL 17-16, 20-10, 20-21 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 7/31/2024. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

Non-Filer Household Composition The household composition for a person who does not expect to file taxes or a tax dependent who meets one of the above exceptions includes: •For adults over 19 and not a full-time student oThe non-filer oThe non-filer’s spouse who lives in the home oThe non-filer’s children (under age 19 or under age 21 and a full-time student) living in the home including adopted and stepchildren •For children under age 19 or adults under age 21 oThe non-filer oThe non-filer’s spouse who lives in the home oThe non-filer’s child

title: Section 4 - MAGI Income and Deductions
chapter: ARTICLE 21 - MAGI APTC and Health Care Reform
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Modified Adjusted Gross Income and Deductions Number Page 21.04 1 of 7 Revision Date: October 1, 2026 Background: The Affordable Care Act (ACA) of 2010 introduced Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) methodology-based Medi-Cal which uses federal tax filing rules. Purpose: This section provides guidance on how income is addressed under MAGI regulations. The section was updated to replace references to Projected Annual Income (PAI) with System Calculated Annual Income (SCAI). California Healthcare Enrollment, Eligibility and Retention System (CalHEERS ) functionality information for the Reasonably Projected Annual Income (RPAI) budget period has been incorporated. Policy: A. Countable Income MAGI Medi -Cal follows Internal Revenue Services (IRS) tax rules when determining treatment of income. MAGI income methodology requires the use of Adjusted Gross Income (AGI), which is federal taxable income minus any allowable deductions, for eligibility determinations. Refer to Medi-Cal Desk Aid 56 MAGI Income and Deduction Types to determine applicable and exempt income types. In addition to federal taxable income, the following income types are also included as countable income for MAGI Medi-Cal: • Non-taxable Title II Social Security Administration (SSA) benefits not included in the gross income, such as Retirement, Survivors and Disability (RSDI) benefits. • Tax-exempt interest. • Foreign earned income and housing expenses for Americans living abroad. • L ump sum income (non-recurring) is counted only in the month of receipt and calculated as part of the individual’s annual income. Some income types such as scholarships, awards, education- based fellowship grants , and certain American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) income may be taxable but are excluded from MAGI. B. Deductions The same deductions used when filing taxes to reduce overall taxable income to determine the AGI on the 1040 tax form are applied. This means that certain pre-tax deductions are subtracted from the gross income by an employer or other income source outside of the MAGI determination. Refer to Medi-Cal Desk Aid 56 MAGI Income and Deduction Types to determine allowable deductions. C. Whose Income Counts Eligibility for MAGI Medi- Cal is determined at an individual level . The tax household composition identifies who should be considered part of an individual’s MAGI household to determine whose income County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Modified Adjusted Gross Income and Deductions Number Page 21.04 2 of 7 counts. The sum of the individual’s countable MAGI income, and the countable income of all other persons in their MAGI household must be included. The following rules apply when determining whose income counts and is based on self-attestation from the tax household: If the individual is… then the countable income is… an adult in the tax household that is not claimed as a tax dependent, the MAGI-based income of the individual only. an adult in a tax household that is claimed as a tax dependent, the MAGI-based income of the adult tax dependent when at least one of the following apply: − The tax filer who claims the adult is not included in the household composition under evaluation. − The adult tax dependent is expected to be required to file a tax return. The MAGI-based income of the adult tax dependent is not counted when the tax filer who claims them is included in their household composition and is not expected to file taxes. a child in the household (under the age of 19 or under the of age 21, if they are a full-time student). the MAGI-based income of the child when one of the following applies: − The tax filer who is claiming the child is someone other than a parent and the child’s parent (natural, adopted, or step) is not included in the child’s household composition. − The child is expected to be required to file a tax return. The MAGI-based income is not counted for a child when the parent(s) who are included in the household composition, and the child is not expected to be required to file taxes. Note: Members of the same family may have different MAGI household compositions, and the income of a child or tax dependent may count for one household member but not another. D. Obtaining Household Income Customers can report their household income or any changes to the county by phone, in person, by mail, online via BenefitsCal or the Covered California website. They can also use any form such as the Single Streamlined Application (SSApp), SAWS2Plus, the Renewal (RE) form, or written attestation. Reported income must be verified prior to determining eligibility. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Modified Adjusted Gross Income and Deductions Number Page 21.04 3 of 7 E. Verifications When evaluating MAGI eligibility, electronic verification of self -attested income must be attempted to determine if the income is reasonably compatible prior to requesting documents from the customer. To determine reasonable compatibility, CalHEERS compares the individual’s self -attested MAGI household income to information received from the Federal Data Service Hub ( FDSH). CalHEERS identifies income that passes the reasonable compatibility rules as electronically verified ( e-verified). CalHEERS evaluates the data returned from the following four sources: • IRS. • Franchise Tax Board (FTB). • Employment Development Department (EDD). • SSA. An individual’s MAGI household income is reasonably compatible when both self-attested income and information from the FDSH are below the MAGI income limit for the household size. If the self-attested income is over the MAGI income limit, the income will not be checked for reasonable compatibility through the FDSH but will be used to determine eligibility for other Insurance Affordability Programs (IAPs) through Covered California. Since e-verification for MAGI Medi -Cal is determined on an individual level, the income of some household members may be reasonably compatible while others may not. In cases where verification status does not automatically transfer to other household members, manual verification may be needed for those members whose income is not reasonably compatible. Note: Reasonable compatibility of income does not apply to Former Foster Youth (FFY) as they do not have an income eligibility requirement. F. Manual Verification When self -attested income is not e- verified and a reasonable explanation does not clarify income discrepancies, manual verification is required. Verification of income may include, but is not limited to: • Paystubs. • Letters from employers. • Tax statements. When an individual household member fails to provide verification and their income cannot be verified, the individual must be denied or discontinued. G. Verification of No Income When an individual reports zero income or self-attests that they no longer receive income and the report is not reasonably compatible with the FDSH, additional verification is required. This also applies to Non- MAGI individuals who are included in the household composition. H. Verifying Income with a Sworn Statement When all attempts to verify self -attested income are exhausted, eligibility staff may obtain a sworn statement from the individual as verification of income. The signed statement must include the following information: • The name of the individual whose income is being verified. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Modified Adjusted Gross Income and Deductions Number Page 21.04 4 of 7 • The income details such as the gross amount, frequency of pay, and source of income. • A signature with a penalty of perjury statement. • The date that the statement was signed. An affidavit may also be signed by: • A parent or caretaker relative for a child. • An individual with power of attorney for another individual. • A spouse or Registered Domestic Partner (RDP). • An Authorized Representative (AR), if they have been authorized to do so. Note: The affidavit is only valid for 90 days from the signature date. I. Income Budget Periods There are three different budget periods that may be used when determining MAGI eligibility. Eligibility staff must use the budget period with the lowest income calculation as it is the most beneficial for the household. Current Monthly Income (CMI) The CMI is the amount of income a customer expects to receive in the month of evaluation. It is the default budget period when determining MAGI eligibility and is used when a customer does not provide enough income information to use a different budget period that may be more beneficial. Reasonably Projected Annual Income (RPAI) The RPAI is the total amount of income that a customer expects to receive in a 12- month period, beginning with the month of application, annual renewal, or reported Change in Circumstances ( CIC). The RPAI budget period is an option for households with fluctuating income whose CMI exceeds the MAGI income limit. When a customer reports fluctuating income to the county, eligibility staff must determine if the income meets RPAI criteria by obtaining enough information to answer the following questions: • What reasonably predictable future changes in income will occur during the next 12 months? • Why will the change in income occur (i.e. seasonal work, job loss, new employment)? • Does the individual have other reasonably predictable income changes that will occur in the next 12 months? Verification of RPAI is required if the self-attested income information is not reasonably compatible with the FDSH. Some methods to verify fluctuating income include: • A signed contract for employment. • Clear proof of a history of predictable fluctuations in income. • Prior year’s tax return. • Other clear documentation of predicted future changes in income (such as the remaining balance of unemployment benefits). • A reasonable explanation. • A sworn statement, as a last resort. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Modified Adjusted Gross Income and Deductions Number Page 21.04 5 of 7 Eligibility staff must document all verification used in detail when using the RPAI budget period. Anticipated income changes are entered in the California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) to compare the customer’s CMI and RPAI budget periods. CalSAWS will use whichever budget period has the lowest monthly income amount. System Calculated Annual Income (SCAI) The SCAI budget period is used for current beneficiaries whose income exceeds the CMI limit but their total income over the calendar year (from January 1 to December 31 of the year reported) is under the MAGI income limit. SCAI is only used when all of the following conditions apply: • The individual’s income does not fluctuate. • The individual’s CMI and RPAI are over the MAGI income limit. • The individual’s SCAI amount is under the MAGI income limit. The annual renewal date will not change when the SCAI budget is used. The individual must have a redetermination before the end of the calendar year in which SCAI is applied. CalSAWS will initiate the annual SCAI renewal process by transmitting a batch job to CalHEERS in December to evaluate eligibility for the following year. Soft Pause and Consumer Protection Programs (CPPs) The SCAI budget period does not affect CPPs and cases that are in Soft Pause. If the customer no longer qualifies for MAGI at the mandatory end of the year SCAI redetermination but is protected under any CPP, they must remain enrolled until the CPP period has ended. If a customer is over the income limit for MAGI and is not eligible under a CPP, they remain in Soft Pause until they are evaluated for all Medi-Cal programs and referred to Covered California before they are discontinued. For more information on Soft Pause and CPP s, refer to Medi -Cal Program Guide (M PG) 04.15.05A and 04.15.02I. J. Reasonably Compatible Income for Budget Periods Reasonable compatibility is also determined on an individual level using the household’s income and may be different for all three budget periods. When an individual’s income is reasonably compatible for themselves or another household member for at least one of the budget periods, no further verification of income is required. If reasonable compatibility cannot be established for any budget period that their income applies to, a request for reasonable explanation or manual verification must be made. K. Retroactive Determinations The CMI and RPAI budget periods may be used to determine retroactive eligibility. SCAI methodology cannot be used w hen an individual requests retroactive eligibility prior to the month of application as they are considered applicants. L. Advanced Premium Tax Credit (APTC) and the Bounce Back Rule Household composition and countable income rules differ between MAGI and APTC. For APTC, only the income of the taxpayer and individuals in their tax filing household who are required to file a tax return, including dependents, is included in the budget calculation. Since federal regulations require that an individual’s annual income is above 100% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) to qualify for APTC, a gap in coverage may exist when their income is over the County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Modified Adjusted Gross Income and Deductions Number Page 21.04 6 of 7 MAGI limit. Exception rule 435.603(i), also known as the bounce back rule is applied to bridge the gap in coverage. When the Business Rule Engine (BRE) is called to evaluate a household for APTC, the Determination of Eligibility Response (DER) will apply the bounce back rule and return with a “MAGI Eligible” status if: • The household countable income is above the income limit for the corresponding MAGI coverage group (i.e.138% FPL for the adult group, or 266% FPL for a child) and; • The individual’s countable annual income is below 100% of the FPL. The bounce back rule does not apply to individuals who: • H ave other minimum essential coverage. • D o not plan on filing a tax return. • Are eligible for other public health coverage such as Medicare. • Are married but not filing taxes as Married Filing Jointly. • Do not have Satisfactory Immigration Status (SIS). The tables below provide examples: Example 1 - Bounce Back Rules Apply - Unmarried couple with mutual child, all living together Mom and Dad file taxes separately; Mom claims their child as a tax dependent: • Dad’s income exceeds the 266% FPL limit and is eligible to APTC. • Mom’s income is at 85% of the FPL and is eligible to MAGI. • In determining the child’s MAGI tax household composition, the countable income exceeds 266% of the FPL with both parent’s income counting in the budget. When MAGI is requested and the DER is received, the child is “bounced back” with the status of MAGI Eligible, because Mom’s income is below 100% of the FPL. Example 2 - Bounce Back Rule Does Not Apply - Unmarried Couple , with 3 common children, all living together. Dad does not have SIS. Mom and Dad file taxes separately; Mom claims children as tax dependents: • Dad’s income exceeds the 266% FPL limit. o He is ineligible for APTC because he does not have SIS. • Mom’s income is at 166% of the FPL exceeding the MAGI limit and is referred to APTC. The children’s countable income exceeds the MAGI limits for their age-appropriate program with both parents’ income counting making them ineligible for MAGI and they are referred to APTC. Since mom claims the children and her income exceeds the 100% FPL limit, the children and mom will be evaluated for APTC coverage and will not be bounced back. Program Impacts: Automation Staff must complete all appropriate fields in CalSAWS to establish the correct level of benefits. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Medi-Cal Program Guide Modified Adjusted Gross Income and Deductions Number Page 21.04 7 of 7 References: All County Welfare Directors Letters (ACWDLs) 20-10, 21-04, 25-21 Medi-Cal Eligibility Division Information Letters (MEDILs) I 26-10, I 26-11 Resources: MC Desk Aid 55 MAGI Medi-Cal Budget Periods Flowchart MC Desk Aid 56 MAGI Income and Deduction Types MC Desk Aid 67 Determining Household Composition MC Desk Aid 68 MAGI HH Composition Examples MC Desk Aid 70 MAGI Individual Household Flow Chart MC Desk Aid 71 Whose Income Counts for MAGI Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by September 30, 2029. Approval for Release: Alberto Banuelos, Ph.D., Interim Director Self-Sufficiency Services
